Remaining: rival logistics and third-party convoys (5.11), allies in battle, relation rules and trade effects, the full strategist, a play-through.

docs.title: The Interceptor campaign mod
docs.text: Status: design; authored across Stages 2–6, playable start to finish at the end of Stage 5. The existing interceptor pack grows into a kind: campaign mod that plays the whole original campaign from the player's CD. It is the primary test case of the engine: if a system of the original cannot be expressed, the format is incomplete.

docs.title: What the mod contains — and what it does not
docs.text:
The mod contains only this project's own work: rules that inherit original sections, definitions authored from the analysis, and references to original files. It never contains original text, art, audio or extracted tables of the original's content beyond the names and numbers needed to reference them (mesh names, section names, values the rules restate).

packs/interceptor/
  pack.yaml                    kind: campaign, requires_original: true, format: 2   (exists)
  campaign/
    campaign.yaml              campaign: (difficulty levels exist), starts:, endings
    doomsday.yaml              arcs: doomsday, plans: doomsday, warnings
    score.yaml                 scores: interceptor (MissionScores by name), reports
  strategy/
    map.yaml                   maps: frontier (generated); star_classes ×9; bodies; travel
    factions.yaml              xcom, alien, corporate (funding), pirates, cult, arms dealer, gsc
    economy.yaml               resources, incomes, expenses, markets, factories, deliveries, storage
    research.yaml              71 topics: inherit original:GameSettings.ini/R_*, + unlocks, appears
    salvage.yaml               13 sets: inherit the *Goodies sections
    bases.yaml                 base_types: xcom, alien; templates
    modules.yaml               68 modules: inherit M_*, + effects, on_destroyed, model sets
    items.yaml                 beams, launchers, missiles, mines, equipment: inherit originals
    pilots.yaml                pilots: ranks inherit RankAdvancement*, formulas authored
    strategist.yaml            strategists: alien — Think.ini values by reference + rules
  rules/                       combat rules (ships, weapons, systems, flight, cockpits, sounds;
                               exist as YAML today)
  models/
    modelsets.yaml             21 class model sets, 11 station sets, module sets with textures
    debris.yaml                the 28 debris sets
    effects.yaml               explosions, shock waves, shield rings
  behaviours/                  per-class AI with Beginner…Superhuman variants
  missions/                    27 mission types, simulator types, the final mission
  events/                      side missions, messages, news triggers, reports
  interface/                   screens laid out with original wrapper art; cockpits A/B/C
  text/en/                     imports: original:LangFile1.txt, starcorp1, Names1, news1, short1
  scenarios/                   testbed arenas (exist as YAML today, kept)

docs.title: Import, reference, author
docs.text: Kind of content How the mod gets it Numbers in GameSettings.ini, Think.ini, soundfx.ini, MPSettings.INI inherit: original:<file>/<section> (implemented; original keys map to field names by spelling, HitPoints → hit_points) and per-key references (think:<section>/<key>); never copied Text text: original:LangFile1.txt and the other text files, imported at load under orig.* keys; the mod's own text files only map ids to those keys Models, textures, images, sounds, music, video original: references and override paths (Stage 1) Tables the executable holds (class → mesh, debris sets, module texture triples, star visuals) Written as rules naming the original meshes and textures — facts needed to reference the data, recorded once in the mod Rules the executable holds (mission compositions, AI, story, yields, formulas) Authored from the analysis; each definition's comment cites its source (guide chapter, CD string, play-test) and confidence

docs.title: Id mapping
docs.text:
Original section names become readable ids, with the original name kept as the inheritance source:

research:
  tri_titanium:
    inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/R_<topic>   # level, file_size, prereq* (section name illustrative)
    size: "file_size * 1000"                 # the original's unit is k TQ
    requires: "research(wraith_examination)" # numeric Prereq ids resolved to readable ids
    unlocks: [items.tri_titanium_armor, hulls.firestar]   # AUTH: guide ch. 3
    name: "@orig.R_<topic>.found"            # from short1.txt

Numeric tech ids in prerequisite keys (Prereq1=12 in the original file) are translated by a mapping table in the mod (tech_ids:), checked by --check against the original file so a mistake is reported, not silently wrong.

As built (app 0.8.0)

The table is generated from the player's executable by tools/interceptor_strategy.py into packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml (derived: the executable's 12-byte entries of R_ name pointer, string id and tech id). --check checks that every research id the table gives is a defined topic once a condition uses it, but it does not compare the table with the original file again: a number the table does not list is left out of the condition silently (by design for the alien ids 75 and up). Research unlocks are not authored; items, hulls and modules are gated by their own TechRequired. See Strategy layer › the interceptor campaign.

docs.title: Fidelity process
docs.text:
1. Stage 2 — combat behaviours: each alien class's behaviour tuned against recorded play of the original (where possible) and the guide's descriptions; difficulty variants from the guide's list of what each level changes.
  2. Stage 3 — mission types: each of the 27 types authored; compositions from the guide's legible tables, else estimates marked derived; checked by playing each in the testbed.
  3. Stages 4–5 — the strategy layer, then the arc and the strategist; a full campaign play-through at Veteran is Stage 5's exit test, with a log comparing milestone dates (first message, first Firestar, Doomsday progress) against the guide's expectations.
  4. The open items are closed or documented as derived estimates in the mod.

docs.title: Interceptor Remastered
docs.text: Status: design; scheduled in Stage 7. The example of a campaign that extends another: parent: interceptor, plus sharper textures for modern screens and an upgraded X-1A Lightning II whose panel lines, vents and intakes — today only painted on — are real geometry.

docs.title: The constraint: nothing derived from the CD may be shipped
docs.text:
An upscaled original texture is a conversion of MicroProse's art, and so is a model built by editing the original Lightning mesh. Project rule: no original content, conversions included, enters the repository or a published mod. So the remastered mod ships recipes, and the engine produces the remastered assets on the player's machine from the player's own CD (generated assets). What is published is the mod's own work only: recipe files, patch instructions, and any art made from scratch.

mods/interceptor-remastered/
  pack.yaml                    kind: campaign, parent: interceptor, requires_original: true
  recipes/textures.yaml        upscale every original texture x4
  recipes/images.yaml          upscale the HUD and menu images x2 (cockpits: see below)
  recipes/lightning.yaml       build the enhanced Lightning from the original mesh
  patches/lightning.meshpatch  the face edits (this project's own work: numbers, no geometry)
  rules/models.yaml            point the Lightning's model set at the generated model

docs.title: Textures: the upscale generator
docs.text:
recipes:
  textures-x4:
    kind: upscale
    inputs: original:*.xtxr            # all 799 textures
    scale: 4
    method: edge-directed
    sharpen: 0.3
    output: "textures/{name}.png"      # = the texture override path, so it replaces the original

Method. The originals are 8-bit palettised and mostly 64–256 px: blocky edges and dithering are the problem, not a lack of high-frequency detail. The built-in, deterministic pipeline (all in-crate, no ML model, no dependency):

  1. Decode at full colour (palette 0; Stage 1 reader).
  2. De-dither: a small edge-preserving smoothing pass (a bilateral filter in a 3×3 window) removes the palette's ordered-dither noise without blurring panel edges.
  3. Edge-directed upscale ×2 per step (two steps for ×4): each new pixel is interpolated along the local edge direction (estimated from gradients) rather than across it — the idea behind NEDI/xBR-family scalers — so diagonal panel lines stay sharp and stair-free.
  4. Sharpen lightly (unsharp mask) and re-apply the colour key / alpha mask at the new resolution, with a 1-pixel feathered edge.
  5. Wrap-aware borders: the textures tile (Stage 1 found UVs outside 0..1), so filtering wraps around the edges instead of clamping, avoiding seams.

Each step is a pure function on an image buffer with unit tests on synthetic images (a hard diagonal edge stays a single sharp edge at ×4; a checkerboard dither becomes flat colour; a tiling texture stays seamless). Output quality is judged by a manual test with side-by-side screenshots in the viewer.

Cockpits are a special case: they are large hand-painted images with text. The recipe upscales them ×2 the same way, and the mod documents the HD-repaint path (overrides) for anyone who wants hand-made art.

docs.title: The enhanced Lightning: the mesh-patch generator
docs.text:
The X-1A Lightning II (INTTYPEA, 198 faces at LOD 0) is the smallest playable hull and the one seen most, so it is the showcase. Its textures paint raised panels, recessed intakes, vents and a canopy frame on flat faces. A mesh patch is a list of geometric edits addressed by the original face numbers that the viewer shows (W, [ ], I):

# patches/lightning.meshpatch — edits to INTTYPEA LOD 0
# Face numbers come from the model viewer. Units are metres. Texture coordinates of new faces
# are derived from the face they came from, so the original paint lines up with the new shape.

inset    face 41  by 0.12               # intake rim
extrude  face 41  by -0.35              # recess the intake
inset    face 42  by 0.12
extrude  face 42  by -0.35
bevel    edges of faces 10-17 by 0.04   # rounded nose panels
extrude  face 63  by 0.06  taper 0.9    # raised spine panel
cut      face 88  along uv-line (0.31,0.10)-(0.31,0.92) then extrude by -0.02   # panel seam
subdivide faces 20-27 smooth 0.5        # canopy curvature
relief   face 70  from texture height scale 0.03 grid 8   # vents: displacement from the paint
lod      keep 1-3                        # leave the far LODs as they are
Operation Effect inset face N by d Shrinks a face inwards, creating a ring of new faces (a rim). extrude face N by d [taper t] Moves a face along its normal (negative = into the hull), building side walls. bevel edges of faces … by d Chamfers sharp edges. cut face N along uv-line a-b Splits a face along a line given in texture space, so a painted seam can become a real one. subdivide faces … smooth s Splits faces and moves new vertices towards a smooth surface. relief face N from texture height scale h grid g Displaces a grid of new vertices by the texture's brightness (a height map from the paint). lod keep … Copies other LODs unchanged.

All operations keep the one-sided, counter-clockwise convention and the overlay layers (Stage 1), produce new texture coordinates by interpolation from the source face, and are deterministic. Each is a pure function on the engine's Model type with unit tests on small synthetic meshes (a cube face extruded by −1 gives the expected volume; a cut along a UV line produces two faces whose UVs meet on the line).

The patch file contains no original geometry — only face numbers and distances chosen by the author — so it can be published. Applied to someone else's mesh it simply fails the recipe's check (face count and a checksum of the source mesh are recorded in the recipe):

recipes:
  lightning:
    kind: mesh-patch
    input: original:INTTYPEA
    input_faces: 198                # refuse to patch an unexpected mesh
    patch: patches/lightning.meshpatch
    output: models/inttypea.obj     # = the model override path: replaces the Lightning everywhere

Authoring workflow: open the mesh in the viewer (--model INTTYPEA, W, [ ], I), note face numbers, write the patch, and the viewer reloads it on save (Stage 7 adds patch hot-reload) to show the result next to the original.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
# rules/models.yaml — nothing else changes: the parent campaign's rules all apply
modelsets:
  lightning:
    intact: models/inttypea.obj     # generated by recipes.lightning

Every other model set keeps pointing at the originals, and because the upscaled textures land on the texture override paths, every model in the game picks them up without a rule change.

Exit of Stage 4 (both campaigns run 6 months; save/load round trips; a manual long run): both strategy layers run six months headless (--strategy-soak 180: default 12 of 14 topics, interceptor 4 of 71), and the default campaign's run is a unit test with a save round trip (the_default_campaign_runs_six_months). Outstanding: the manual long run, the interceptor play-test and balance, and the open items above.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
OpenInterceptor is a library crate (src/lib.rs, crate openinterceptor) with a thin binary on top (src/main.rs, program openinterceptor). Almost all code lives in the library, so every module can be unit-tested with cargo test. The engine is built in layers: each layer uses only the layers below it.

Status

Updated to the code as built in Stage 1, build 0.2.0 (main 909d687): Newtonian flight, settings and data discovery, per-asset overrides, the extractor, HD/3D cockpits, the asset browser and the macOS app bundle. No specification exists yet, so plan stages are cited instead of requirement IDs.

app::flight::FlightSession::frame:

    A["next_frame().await"] --> B["app::devices::Devices::read → RawInput"]

docs.title: Event flow
docs.text:
The simulation reports what happened as sim::SimEvent values in world.events (cleared at the start of every World::step). Three consumers read them, none of which can change the simulation:

flowchart LR
    W["World::step"] --> EV["world.events: Vec<SimEvent>"]
    EV --> FX["render::effects::Effects::on_events<br/>explosions, sparks, debris"]
    EV --> SB["audio::event_sound → SoundBank::play"]
    EV --> MS["app::flight::event_messages → hud::MessageLog"]

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol Where What it is, in plain words main src/main.rs Parses the command line; runs --help/--list/--check without a window, otherwise opens one with macroquad::Window::from_config and runs app::run. Content src/content/mod.rs Everything loaded: packs, the original data, the Ruleset, the scenarios; plus asset loaders. Ruleset src/content/rules.rs Every ship, beam, missile, faction, system and cockpit, plus the flight, power and damage rules, after all packs of the chosen campaign are layered. Model src/model.rs A format-neutral 3D model (from XMSH or OBJ): right-handed, −Z forward, LODs, per-texture triangle groups. World src/sim/mod.rs The battle: ships, bolts, missiles, events. Changed only by World::step. Renderer src/render/mod.rs Owns shaders and GPU caches; draws a World from a SpaceCamera. FlightSession src/app/flight.rs One running scenario: world, camera view, HUD state, accumulator. Campaign src/campaign/mod.rs One strategy-layer game: map, bases, research, craft, pilots, contacts; advanced an hour at a time, saved as YAML (Campaign). ConsoleServer src/remote/server.rs The tablet console's server threads, seen from the game: poll events, broadcast messages (Remote console).

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text: Each layer's public API is on its own page: Formats, Packs, VFS and rules, Assets and GPU cache, Simulation, Conditions, Missions, Campaign, Rendering, HUD, Input, Audio, Presentation, Platform, Remote console, Testbed. cargo doc --open renders the /// comments of every item.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --check [--data <original data>] loads and validates everything without a window and prints each error with the file and section it came from. --list prints packs, playable ships and scenarios.
  • openinterceptor --data <original data> --scenario flight-test --ship lightning --view chase starts a scenario directly, skipping the launcher.
  • OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 prints the name of every key pressed (the name to use in bindings.yaml).
  • Load problems that do not stop the program (missing texture, bad sound) are printed to standard error as warning: / sound: lines.
  • RUST_BACKTRACE=1 for a panic's stack trace. Panics are bugs: bad data must produce an error.
  • Planned (not built): a developer overlay and a --verbose load trace.

docs.title: Assets and GPU cache
docs.text:
Two steps turn a file into something drawable:

  1. src/model.rs converts an XmshMesh or ObjMesh into the format-neutral Model, once, at load time (pure CPU data, unit-tested).
  2. src/render/gpu.rs splits each LOD into per-texture chunks with u16 indices (split_lod, pure, tested) and uploads them as macroquad Meshes with their textures (ModelCache).

Plan: Stage 1.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    X["xmsh::XmshMesh<br/>D3D: left-handed, +Z forward"] -->|"Model::from_xmsh<br/>negate Z, reverse winding,<br/>fan-triangulate, group by texture"| M["model::Model"]
    O["obj::ObjMesh + materials"] -->|"Model::from_obj<br/>scale, flip v, face normals"| M
    M -->|"gpu::split_lod"| CH["Chunk<br/>texture, vertices, u16 indices"]
    CH -->|"ModelCache::upload"| G["GpuModel<br/>GpuLod { switch_distance, meshes }"]
    T["Content::load_texture"] --> TX["Texture2D cache"] --> G

Engine coordinates everywhere above the formats layer: right-handed, +Y up, −Z forward, metres. The original models use Direct3D's left-handed system with +Z forward, so from_xmsh negates Z and swaps two indices of every triangle so faces still point outwards (a unit test checks the winding).

Collision shapes come from the same data: Model::collision_lod() (the cheapest LOD) gives triangles for station meshes in app::flight::FlightSession::start.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is model::Model name, radius, bounds_min/max, lods: Vec<ModelLod> (never empty), attachments. model::ModelLod switch_distance, vertices: Vec<ModelVertex>, groups: Vec<MaterialGroup>. model::MaterialGroup texture: Option<String> and triangle indices: Vec<u32>. model::Attachment A point and facing from an original manipulator (e.g. engine exhaust). render::gpu::Chunk CPU-side chunk ready to become a Mesh (≤ MAX_CHUNK_VERTICES = 16 000). render::gpu::GpuModel GPU LODs plus the CPU Model (kept for stats and collision). render::gpu::ModelCache (reference, pack) → Option<Rc<GpuModel>> and texture caches; failures recorded in errors.

docs.text:
• Model::from_xmsh(&XmshMesh), Model::from_obj(name, &ObjMesh, scale, &[ObjMaterial]).
  • model.lod_for_distance(d), model.collision_lod(), lod.triangle_count(), lod.triangles() -> impl Iterator<Item = [Vec3; 3]>.
  • gpu::split_lod(&ModelLod) -> Vec<Chunk>.
  • ModelCache::get(&Content, reference, pack, scale) -> Option<Rc<GpuModel>>; GpuModel::lod(distance).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• The model viewer (launcher → Model viewer) shows each model's LOD triangle counts and switch distances, forces a LOD with L, and draws attachment points as RGB axes.
  • A model drawn inside-out or mirrored points at the handedness conversion; a model that is missing shows "could not load" with the ModelCache error underneath.
  • Textures that fail to load leave the group white (macroquad's default texture).

docs.title: Audio
docs.text: src/audio.rs: sound effects driven by simulation events, radio voice clips and interactive music. Plan: Stage 1 (event sounds); radio voices Stage 3.7 (app 0.6.2); interactive music Stage 6.4 (app 0.11.0) with the volumes of app 0.12.1; CD audio tracks are not built.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    R["Ruleset: sounds, beam sound, missile sound,<br/>voice_clips"] --> L["SoundBank::load (async)<br/>Content::load_sound → wav::decode (PCM / MS ADPCM / IMA ADPCM)<br/>→ Pcm::to_wav_bytes → load_sound_from_bytes"]
    EV["world.events"] --> ES["event_sound(world, event, listener, ear)<br/>→ (SoundKey, volume)"]
    ES --> P["SoundBank::play"]
    L --> P
    FS["app::flight: wing order, wingman lost,<br/>MissionRun::voices, debrief"] -->|"SoundKey::Voice(i),<br/>Named(mission_accomplished / failed)"| P

event_sound is pure and tested: beam and missile sounds use the firing ship's weapon; hits use shield_hit or hull_hit; destruction uses big_explosion for objects with radius over 100 m, else explosion (always at least 15 % volume); lock and denied only for the listener; since Stage 2, system_damage when one of the listener's systems is damaged (SystemChanged, not repairs), tractor / cloak / ecm when a switchable system goes on or off (Switched; quieter when switching off, attenuated for other ships) and hyperspace when a ship jumps out (Departed), point_defence for each point-defence shot (PointDefence, at 40 % of the distance volume); a destruction whose model set's destroyed_effect, or a missile blast whose explosion effect, has a sound plays that sound instead of the usual event; everything else is attenuated by distance (attenuate: full within 50 m, half at about 350 m).

Cue table (Stage 2, item 2.12). Sound references are resolved when the rules load (rules::build_at): a reference written cue:<Name> is looked up in the table named by audio.cue_table — original:<file>/<section> of an original INI file, the original game's soundfx.ini — whose entry's file name becomes original:<file>.wav. By the time SoundBank loads, every reference is an ordinary asset, so cues need no run-time code. Unknown cues and a missing table are load errors.

Radio voices (Stage 3.7, app 0.6.2). The rules collect every voice clip in one list, Ruleset::voice_clips ((reference, pack) pairs): first each voice set's clips (voices: {<set>: {<line>: clip or [clips]}}, kept as VoiceSet { id, lines } with the clip indices), then each mission chatter line's voice:. SoundBank::load loads clip i as SoundKey::Voice(i), beside the named sounds. The audio layer does not decide when a voice speaks: the flight screen (app::flight) does —

  • a wing order plays acknowledge and a status request status, from the first living wingman of the player whose ship has a voice set with that line (flight::wingman_voice; the clip is picked from the line's list by the battle time);
  • when one of the player's wingmen is destroyed, another wingman says down;
  • chatter clips are queued by the mission (MissionRun::voices) as their lines are said, and the screen plays and clears them each frame;
  • when the debrief appears, the named sound mission_accomplished (a win) or mission_failed (any other result) plays — the computer voice.

A ship's voice is resolved to an index when the ship spawns (Ship::voice); an unknown set named by a ship is a rules error. Voice lines without a clip, and ships without a voice, are simply silent.

docs.title: Music (app 0.11.0)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    MD["rules: music.<set><br/>content::music::MusicSet"] --> BL["SoundBank::load<br/>SoundKey::Music(set, state, seg),<br/>Stinger(set, k) + their lengths"]
    FL["app::flight each frame:<br/>set = seed mod sets;<br/>battle_state(nearest hostile)"] --> MP
    SG["app::strategy each frame:<br/>set 0, state strategy;<br/>app::menu: menu, else strategy"] --> MP
    MP["MusicPlayer::frame(bank, rules, set, state, now)"] -->|"segment ended?<br/>next_segment(set, state, count)"| PL["SoundBank::play(key, set.volume × music volume)"]
    RES["flight: result decided"] --> STG["MusicPlayer::stinger(victory | death)"] --> PL
    APP["app::run: any other screen"] --> STOP["MusicPlayer::stop"]

content::music parses a set (states — each a list of asset references, or one — stingers, threat_range 12 km, battle_range 4 km and volume 60 % by default) and holds the pure rule battle_state(set, distances): battle within battle_range of the nearest live hostile, threat within threat_range, else cruise. MusicSet::segments(state) falls back to cruise, then the first state.

SoundBank::load loads every segment and stinger beside the other sounds, and keeps each one's length (Pcm::duration) in SoundBank::lengths, because macroquad's audio cannot say when a sound has finished. MusicPlayer (owned by AppContext::music) is called every frame by the screens that have music with the set and state they want. It does nothing while the current segment has time left (to 20 ms before its end); then it plays the next segment — next_segment(set, set_index, state, count) picks the wanted state's segment count mod n, so each state walks its list in turn — and records its end time. Changing set stops the playing segment and restarts the count. This is the original's segment_end transition; its .wtl transition tables are not read (DEV-053).

  • Which set: a battle uses set seed mod sets (FlightSession::frame), so a battle always has the same music; the strategy screen uses set 0 with the strategy state.
  • Stingers: when a mission's result is decided, victory for a win and death otherwise, with the computer voice. good and bad are loaded but not played.
  • Silence: app::run stops the music on every screen other than Screen::Flight, Screen::Strategy and (app 0.14.0) Screen::Menu, and before a video.

Volumes (app 0.12.1). settings.yaml audio: {music, effects} (0 – 100 %, default 70 % and 100 %) is read at start-up: MusicPlayer::volume multiplies each set's own volume, and SoundBank::effects_volume multiplies every other key in SoundBank::play (music and stinger keys already carry the music volume). The launcher's M and V keys step them by quarters and save them (app::remember_audio). A reload (Tab) re-reads the effects volume for the new bank. Video soundtracks are played by app::video directly, at 0.9 × the effects volume (app 0.14.1).

Playback uses macroquad's audio feature (quad-snd: CoreAudio on macOS, ALSA on Linux).

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is SoundKey Named(&'static str), Beam(u16), Missile(u16), Effect(u16), since app 0.6.2 Voice(u32) (an index into Ruleset::voice_clips), and since app 0.11.0 Music(set, state, segment) and Stinger(set, stinger) (indices into Ruleset::music). content::music::MusicSet, battle_state A music set (states, stingers, ranges, volume, pack); the battle state from the hostiles' distances (pure, tested). MusicPlayer, next_segment Plays one segment at a time and changes state only at a segment's end; the next segment's key (pure, tested). volume is the player's music volume. NAMED The eighteen named sounds: since app 0.6.2 mission_accomplished and mission_failed (the computer voice at the debrief), and the event names explosion, big_explosion, shield_hit, hull_hit, lock, missile_launch, afterburner, target, denied, collision, and since Stage 2 system_damage, tractor, cloak, ecm, hyperspace, point_defence. SoundKey::Effect(i) The sound of effect i (an event name from sounds: or an asset in the effect's pack), loaded with the bank. rules::VoiceSet, VoiceSet::clips(line) A voice set: id and lines (line name → clip indices); clips is empty for a line the voice lacks. Ruleset::voices, Ruleset::voice_clips The voice sets, and every voice clip (sets first, then chatter) as (reference, pack). flight::wingman_voice(&World, player, except, line, pick) A clip of line from the first living wingman of player (not except) with a voice that has it (pure, tested). SoundBank Decoded sounds by key, music lengths, effects_volume (app 0.12.1), and errors for sounds that failed.

docs.text:
• SoundBank::load(&Content).await, bank.play(&SoundKey, volume), bank.play_events(&World, listener, ear); since app 0.11.0 – 0.13.0 bank.play_named(name, volume) (a cutscene's sounds), bank.length(&SoundKey), bank.stop(&SoundKey).
  • MusicPlayer::new(volume), player.frame(&SoundBank, &Ruleset, set, state, now), player.stinger(&SoundBank, &Ruleset, name), player.stop(&SoundBank); next_segment(&MusicSet, set_index, state, count) -> Option<SoundKey>; content::music::battle_state(&MusicSet, distances) -> &'static str.
  • event_sound(&World, &SimEvent, ShipId, Vec3) -> Option<(SoundKey, f32)>, attenuate(distance).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Sounds that fail to load are printed at start-up as sound: … lines; --check loads every referenced sound too.
  • A wingman that says nothing: its ship class needs voice: <set>, the set needs the line (acknowledge, status, down), and the clip must load (a failed clip prints a sound: … line). Only the player's own wingmen (AI wingman led by the player) speak.
  • No music: the campaign needs a music: section, the screen must be a flight or the strategy screen, audio.music must be above 0, and the segment files must load (a failure prints a sound: … line). The default campaign's music WAVs are committed since main 16a9954 (before that the *.wav ignore rule kept them out of Git).
  • The music does not change when an enemy closes in: it changes at the end of the segment playing, by design; check threat_range and battle_range against the battle's distances.
  • No sound at all on Linux: the build needs the ALSA development package (libasound2-dev).
  • A cue: sound that is silent: --check names unknown cues (sounds.x: unknown sound cue 'Y'); if the cue resolves, the asset browser shows whether the original file (or its override) loads.

docs.title: Campaign (strategy layer)
docs.text: src/campaign/ (mod.rs, logistics.rs, story.rs, save.rs) with its data in src/content/strategy.rs, src/content/logistics.rs and src/content/story.rs, its expression context in src/script/campaign.rs, its story actions in src/script/action.rs and its screen in src/app/strategy.rs: the real-time strategy game around the battles (Stage 4, app 0.7.0 – 0.9.2, filled in by app 0.16.1 – 0.16.14) and the story on top of it (Stage 5, app 0.10.0 – 0.10.3; its testbed tools in 0.16.13). The modder's view is Strategy layer and Story layer; the player's is User guide › Campaign. Requirements: R-STR-001 – R-STR-027 on Strategy & logistics, R-CPN-007 – R-CPN-010 on Campaigns.

docs.title: Where it sits
docs.text:
The campaign is a simulation layer beside sim: deterministic, plain data, no macroquad, no rendering, no input. It reads the content layer (StrategyDef) and the script layer (it is a script::Context), and the application layer drives it.

flowchart TB
    subgraph APP["7 · Application"]
        ST["app::strategy::StrategyScreen<br/>top bar, map, info, lists, prompts"]
        FL["app::flight::FlightSession<br/>(campaign_battle)"]
        AM["app::run<br/>Screen, Next, AppContext"]
    end
    subgraph SIM["4 · Simulation"]
        CA["campaign::Campaign<br/>advance, orders, battle_result"]
        LG["campaign::logistics<br/>step, Logistics, convoy_result"]
        STO["campaign::story<br/>step, check_end, StoryState"]
        SV["campaign::save<br/>write / read"]
        W["sim::World"]
    end
    subgraph CON["3 · Content"]
        SD["content::strategy::StrategyDef"]
        LD["content::logistics::LogisticsDef<br/>(StrategyDef::logistics)"]
        SC["script::campaign<br/>QUERIES, schema"]
        SYD["content::story::StoryDef<br/>(StrategyDef::story)"]
        EA["script::action::EVENT_ACTIONS"]
    end
    ST --> CA & SV
    AM --> ST & FL
    FL --> W
    CA --> SD & SC & LG & STO
    LG --> LD
    STO --> SYD
    SYD --> SC & EA
    SV --> CA & SD
    SD --> SC & LD

campaign never calls sim: a battle is handed to the app, which flies it in an ordinary FlightSession and hands the debrief back. The two simulations meet only through strings (the mission id, the result, the outcome's action texts), a kill count, the share of cargo still aboard (app 0.9.2) and, going in, the factions' stances (app 0.10.3).

docs.title: Data flow: from YAML to the screen
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Y[("<pack>/strategy/*.yaml<br/>start, maps, research, items, hulls,<br/>base_modules, base_types, raids, …")] --> RS["content::rules::build<br/>resolved definitions + globals"]
    RS --> B["StrategyDef::build<br/>name table → script::campaign::schema<br/>expressions parsed and checked"]
    B --> X["StrategyDef::check<br/>start, templates, unlocks exist"]
    X --> RU["Ruleset::strategy: Option<StrategyDef><br/>(None without start:)"]
    RU --> N["Campaign::new(def, difficulty, seed)<br/>or save::read(text, def, packs)"]
    N --> SCR["StrategyScreen { campaign, … }"]
    SCR -->|"orders"| N
    SCR -->|"F5, Esc"| SAVE[("<user data>/saves/<campaign>.yaml")]
  1. Rules. The strategy sections are ordinary rules sections: definition sections (maps, star_classes, research, items, hulls, base_modules, base_types, raids, incomes, expenses: content::strategy::DEF_SECTIONS) layer across packs like ships do; globals (start, research_model, pilots, scores, economy, flags, tech_ids, logistics) are read once; the logistics definitions (content::logistics::DEF_SECTIONS: resources, components, recipes, facility_types, research_sites) layer like the others (app 0.9.0). start.money_from: original:<file>/<key> is resolved here, while the original's files are at hand: content::rules::build_at reads the key from the section named after the difficulty level and merges it into start as money (app 0.8.0). Their schema (content::strategy::sections) joins the rules file schema, so --check and the editor JSON Schema know every key.
  2. Names. StrategyDef::build first collects every id it defines, plus factions, ship classes, missions and the flags missions set, into one sorted table (names). That table becomes the constants of script::campaign::schema, so research(heat_rays) compiles to query 0 with argument 7 and a misspelling is a load error.
  3. The original's numbers (app 0.8.0). Data inherited from the original names prerequisites by number (prereq1 – prereq3 on topics, tech_required, tech_required2 on items, hulls and modules). When a definition has no requires: and the campaign has a tech_ids table, StrategyDef::build turns the numbers it lists into research(<id>) and … text before parsing it like any written condition, so the result is checked the same way. Costs, prices, upkeep and maintenance are multiplied by economy.cost_scale; with economy.module_time: days, a module's prod_time becomes its build time in days.
  4. Logistics (app 0.9.0). LogisticsDef::build reads the logistics definitions, the start map's systems (their deposits and features), each hull's components and each topic's lab, site and start_cost — into vectors in the same order as the map's systems, the hulls and the topics, so a hull index or topic index finds its logistics data directly. It returns None when no facility type is defined: StrategyDef::logistics is an Option, and everything downstream starts with let Some(l) = def.logistics.as_ref() else { return }.
  5. Check. Cross-references (start bases, systems, craft, templates, unlocks) are checked; content::rules adds the outside ones (a raid's mission and faction, a hull's ship class).
  6. Play. Campaign::new builds the starting state: the map's systems (generated now for a generated map), the starting bases with finished modules, craft, pilots who take the craft in order, recruits, the first times for every income, expense and raid roll; with logistics, an empty Logistics with every system unsurveyed and each deposit's full reserve.

docs.title: Logic flow: the hour step
docs.text:
Campaign::advance(def, hours) loops step in slices of at most one hour, and returns as soon as a step produced an event, so the screen can stop the clock. The order inside step is fixed, which is what makes a campaign replay exactly from a save:

flowchart TD
    A["hours += dt"] --> B["construction finished → Notice"]
    B --> C["research: each base, rate = eval(research_model.rate, base)<br/>topic done → known, Notice"]
    C --> D["manufacture: first job first; a unit not yet started is paid (cost)<br/>or, a hull with components, waits for logistics;<br/>production_rate × dt; finished unit → receive (item or craft)"]
    D --> E["deliveries due → receive<br/>(or lost: roll < economy.delivery_loss → Notice)"]
    E --> F["incomes and expenses due → money ± eval(amount);<br/>pilots in training: stats += gain × dt/24, money −= cost × dt/24"]
    F --> G{"month boundary<br/>(720 h)?"}
    G -->|yes| H["maintenance + upkeep + salaries;<br/>evaluations: first that holds → its actions, rating;<br/>monthly report → Notice; recruits refreshed"]
    G -->|no| I
    H --> I["injured pilots heal"]
    I --> J["raids: roll each due raid (requires, chance) → launch contact"]
    J --> K["contacts move; within a base's sensor range → detected, Notice;<br/>hidden systems in range revealed"]
    K --> L["interceptions fly to their contacts → Event::Battle"]
    L --> M["contacts that arrived unopposed → score(undefended), Notice;<br/>roll < 1 − 0.85^defence → driven off, else module lost"]
    M --> N["logistics::step (app 0.9.0; campaigns with logistics):<br/>construction strikes → Event::Strike (0.16.4);<br/>demand, mining, recipes, stations, convoys, surveys"]
    N --> O["story::step (app 0.10.0): events, plans,<br/>monthly drift and aggression, the end conditions"]

Since app 0.10.0 a raid's roll uses chance × story.aggression, and is skipped while raids_allowed says its faction is no longer hostile. The evaluation (app 0.16.8), training (0.16.7), delivery losses (0.16.11) and the defence roll (0.16.10) joined the step later; each is skipped when its data is absent, so an older pack plays as before.

Notices outside the clock (app 0.16.2). advance returns its events, but some changes happen in a debrief, outside advance — a relation(…) outcome that changes a stance, a lose(<facility>), a construction strike's result — and a save loaded with a changed pack version. These push their text onto Campaign::notices: Vec<String> (not saved: the screen shows them before the next save is possible); the strategy screen pops one into its Report prompt whenever no other prompt is up, and stops the clock.

Every roll (raids, launch points, pilots, recruits, generated maps, random(p)) draws from one xorshift generator stored in the campaign (Campaign::rng), so same_seed_same_campaign can assert that two campaigns from one seed are equal after the same time.

docs.title: Expressions: the campaign as a script::Context
docs.text: Campaign answers the 29 queries of script::campaign::QUERIES (16 until app 0.9.2; arc, plan, relation, fired and battles_won came with the story; the eight logistics queries with app 0.16.3, answered by Campaign::logistics_query — lane_distance by Campaign::lane_hops, a breadth-first search counting lanes, not distance) through a small context struct (Cx) that holds &Campaign, an optional base (so module_count in a research rate counts the base being evaluated) and the generator in a Cell<u64> — Context::query takes &self, but random(p) must advance the generator, the same interior-mutability trick as sim::ai::ObjectContext (Conditions). After evaluating, Campaign::eval copies the advanced generator back.

docs.title: The battle hand-off
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant S as StrategyScreen
    participant A as app::run
    participant C as AppContext
    participant F as FlightSession
    S->>S: advance → Event::Battle{contact} | Convoy{convoy} | Mission{mission}; banner
    S-->>A: Enter → flying = PendingBattle::Contact | Convoy | Story;<br/>Next::CampaignBattle{mission, ship, loadout, stances}
    A->>C: mem::replace(screen, Launcher); ctx.campaign = Some(strategy screen)
    A->>F: start_mission(mission, ship); apply_loadout(loadout);<br/>apply_stances(stances); campaign_battle = true
    F-->>C: debrief + Enter/Esc → ctx.battle_report = {result, actions, kills, cargo}
    F-->>A: Next::Strategy
    A->>C: ctx.campaign.take(), ctx.battle_report.take()
    A->>S: battle_done(report) → battle_result | convoy_result | mission_result;<br/>story::check_end

Four kinds of campaign battle (app 0.9.2 – 0.16.4). StrategyScreen::flying is an enum, PendingBattle, saying what the battle was for, so that the one report coming back is routed to the right place:

PendingBattle Started by The report goes to Contact(id) Event::Battle — an interception reached its contact Campaign::battle_result(def, id, …) Convoy(v) Event::Convoy — an ambushed convoy (with logistics.ambush_mission) Campaign::convoy_result(def, v, share): lose → Some(0.0), retreat → None (fights on alone), anything else → Some(report.cargo.unwrap_or(1.0)) Story Event::Mission — a story event's mission(x) offer Campaign::mission_result(def, …): battle_result with an id no contact has, so the outcome's actions and the win apply Strike(f) (app 0.16.4) Event::Strike { facility } — a construction strike, flown with logistics.construction_strikes.mission Campaign::strike_result(def, f, won): win → Some(true) (beaten off), lose → Some(false) (the site removed), anything else → None (set back); then mission_result for the outcome's actions

A flown convoy escort also runs mission_result since app 0.16.3, so its outcome's score and actions apply like any battle's. Auto-resolve (app 0.16.12) never leaves the screen: the Interception prompt's second button calls balance::win_chance(rules, mission, hull ids), rolls Campaign::roll against it and hands battle_result the mission's own outcome actions for the rolled win or lose (rendered back to text with Action::display), with the hostile roles' minimum counts as kills on a win. Prizes (app 0.16.3): the flight screen adds captured(<class id>) to the report's actions for each prize the player's tractor brought home; battle_result keeps them as salvage only when the outcome also says capture.

After any of them story::check_end runs, because a battle (a flag set by a finale's win, a last base lost) can end the campaign.

  • The strategy screen cannot stay the current Screen while a flight runs, and it must not be dropped (it owns the campaign). app::run moves it out of screen with std::mem::replace and parks it in AppContext::campaign (Option<Box<StrategyScreen>>). Next::Strategy takes it back with Option::take (Learn Rust › Ownership).
  • The loadout (app 0.7.2). Campaign::loadout(def, craft) turns the first craft's fit into beam ids (one per fitted beam slot) and missile ids with rounds. flight::apply_loadout sets them on the player's class — but beams belong to a ship class in the shared Ruleset, which every other screen also reads. The battle's World holds the rules as an Arc<Ruleset>, so Arc::make_mut gives the battle its own copy the first time it is changed (copy-on-write) and the shared content stays untouched. Ids that are not weapons of the campaign are skipped; with no beams fitted the class's own are kept. Since app 0.15.0 the loadout is a campaign::Loadout struct — beams, missiles, and shields / armor as Option<f32>: the strongest fitted shield item's protection and the sum of the fitted armor items' (None: keep the class's own). apply_loadout(world, player, &Loadout) writes them into the battle's copy of the class and fills the player's facings and armour. An item's protection is content::strategy::protection_of(kind, Get): its protection: key, else, for an item inheriting the original's equipment, Special (shield) or HitPoints (armour) — derived. The same function serves fitted: on ship classes, applied while the rules are resolved (rules::apply_fitted, on each definition once its inherit: chain is merged; a shields / armor already present, own or inherited, wins), so a class names its default equipment instead of copying numbers (Strategy layer › items).
  • The stances (app 0.10.3). With dynamic relations, StrategyScreen::stances lists every faction with a standing as (faction, hostile) — hostile when its stance is hostile. flight::apply_stances calls Ruleset::set_hostile(player_faction, faction, hostile) for each (never for the player's own faction), which edits both factions' hostile lists — in the battle's own copy of the rules through Arc::make_mut, exactly like the loadout. Without dynamic relations the list is empty and the factions' own hostility stands.
  • The flight screen fills AppContext::battle_report (BattleReport {result, actions, kills, cargo}) from the debrief: the result, the outcome's campaign actions as written (score(x), money(n), salvage, set_flag(x), …), the kill count and — when the mission names a cargo: role — the share of its cargo still aboard (mission::cargo_share). Leaving from the pause menu is retreat; a mission that cannot start is counted as retreat too, with the error printed.
  • Campaign::battle_result applies the actions it knows (score, money, set_flag, salvage, since app 0.12.1 relation(f, n) through change_standing — since 0.16.2 a stance change it causes becomes a notice; since 0.16.3 capture / captured(<class>), lose(<facility type>) through Campaign::remove_facility — which removes the facility's orders and inbound convoys and moves every later facility index down by one — and cargo_lost / cargo_captured, logged), marks a battle for after_battle events, counts a win for the story, credits the party's pilots, removes a killed leader's craft (re-indexing pilots' craft handles), sends the rest home, and removes the contact on win or draw.

Fixed in app 0.9.0: salvaged(x) and manufacture costs

Until app 0.9.0 salvage recorded the raid's display name while salvaged(x) compared the id, so the default campaign's saucer_hulls and robot_brains could never start; battle_result now records def.raids[contact.raid].id. Manufacture was free; each Job now has a started flag, and the hour step takes the unit's cost when it starts (or waits for the money). campaign::tests::manufacture_is_paid_per_unit_and_salvage_names_the_raid_by_id covers both.

docs.title: Travel on the map
docs.text: Positions are map units and everything moves in straight hops at its speed per hour (travel). On a travel: lanes map (app 0.7.3) contacts and craft carry a route: the system positions still to pass, consumed one by one before the final leg. Campaign::lane_route(def, from, to) finds the shortest way along the lanes with Dijkstra's algorithm — repeatedly settle the unsettled system with the shortest known distance and relax its lanes, then walk the prev links back. With seven systems a linear scan for the minimum is simpler than a heap and fast enough. A raid enters at the free system farthest from its target; an interception flies the lanes to the system nearest the contact (nearest_system), then straight to it, and home along the lanes. Routes are part of the saved state.

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text: campaign::logistics (app 0.9.0, plan items 4.14 – 4.17) is the runtime of content::logistics::LogisticsDef. Its state is one more plain struct inside the campaign, Campaign::logistics: Logistics — facilities, open orders, convoys and survey ships in flight, which systems are surveyed, what each deposit has left, and each base's store of components — and logistics::step(campaign, def, dt, events) runs one slice of it at the end of the hour step. The modder's view is Strategy layer › Logistics.

docs.title: Data flow: demand pulls, convoys carry
docs.text:
flowchart RL
    subgraph BASE["Main base"]
        J["hull job (not started)<br/>needs hulls.x.components"]
        BS[("base_goods[b]")]
    end
    subgraph MC["Manufacturing center"]
        MO["orders it must fill"]
        LN["lines: recipe runs<br/>(≤ lines at once)"]
        MS[("store")]
    end
    subgraph MF["Mining facility"]
        DP["system deposits<br/>rate / 24 per hour, reserve"]
        FS[("store ≤ storage")]
    end
    subgraph RS["Research station"]
        PR["project: station-only topic<br/>start_cost once, then research_rate"]
        RSS[("store")]
    end
    J -- "want(component, short)<br/>Order → nearest ready center" --> MO
    MO -- "inputs short:<br/>want(resource) → nearest mine with a deposit" --> FS
    PR -- "want(start_cost)" --> FS
    DP --> FS
    MO --> LN
    LN -- "output" --> MS
    MS -- "filled order → Convoy<br/>(vessels, lane route, ambush roll)" --> BS
    FS -- "filled order → Convoy" --> MS
    FS -- "filled order → Convoy" --> RSS
    BS -- "all components in store →<br/>job.started = true" --> J
    RSS --> PR

An order is {goods, amount, to: Dest, source}: amount of goods wanted at to (a base or a facility, the Dest enum of two index variants), to be filled by facility source. Campaign::want(l, goods, amount, to) tops up the open orders for that destination and goods to amount; the shortfall is computed by the caller as needed − in store − already in convoys (inbound), so the same demand never produces two orders. A resource goes to the nearest ready mining facility whose system has a deposit of it, a component to the nearest ready manufacturing center (Campaign::supplier, by straight-line distance between systems). No supplier means no order: the demand waits and is asked again next hour.

docs.title: Logic flow: logistics::step
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    A["facilities whose ready_at fell in this slice → Notice;<br/>construction_strikes: first site past from, its system under max,<br/>roll < chance × dt/24 → attacks += 1, Event::Strike (one at a time)"] --> B["1 · demand: each base's unstarted hull jobs<br/>→ want(component, need − store − inbound)"]
    B --> C{"2 · each ready facility, by role"}
    C -->|mining| M["each deposit: min(rate/24 × dt, room, reserve) → store; reserve −="]
    C -->|manufacturing| P["finished lines → output to store;<br/>per order it fills: store + running ≥ amount? else<br/>free line and inputs in store → start recipe (inputs used)<br/>inputs short → want(inputs)"]
    C -->|research| R["project not started: start_cost in store? use it : want(start_cost)<br/>started: progress[topic] += research_rate × dt → known, Notice"]
    M & P & R --> D["3 · orders whose source store holds the amount →<br/>Convoy {cargo, to, route = lane_route, vessels, ambush_in = roll < ambush_chance ? roll × length}"]
    D --> E["4 · convoys travel convoy_speed × dt along the route;<br/>ambush_in reaches 0 → each vessel lost with ambush_loss, Notice;<br/>at the end → deliver cargo × surviving / vessels"]
    E --> F["5 · hull jobs whose components are in base_goods → use them, started = true"]
    F --> G["6 · survey ships travel survey_speed × dt;<br/>arrived: attacked and roll < 0.5 → lost, else surveyed;<br/>Notice with deposits (rate, reserve), features and sites"]

Design points worth noticing:

  • Everything is an index. Facilities refer to their type and system by index, orders to their source facility, Dest to a base or facility, Line to a recipe; stores are short Vec<(String, f32)> lists of goods and amounts (logistics::amount, add). A save is then a direct walk, and the borrow checker never sees two live references into the campaign.
  • Copy out, then mutate. step takes &mut Campaign and often needs to read one part while changing another (an order's amount while changing the source facility's store). It clones the small thing it reads first — let o = c.logistics.orders[k].clone();, the list of (goods, amount) a center must fill — and then mutates freely. With a few dozen orders the clones cost nothing, and the code stays free of RefCell and of index juggling.
  • Rolls are made when something launches, not when it arrives: the ambush and its point along the route, and a survey ship's attack. The outcome is then part of the saved state (Convoy::ambush_in, Survey::attacked), so a save loaded before the ambush replays it the same way.
  • An ambush waits for the player (app 0.9.2). With logistics.ambush_mission set, a convoy reaching its ambush point is marked held (saved), a message names its cargo, and Event::Convoy { convoy } goes to the screen; a held convoy does not move. The screen either flies the ambush mission (PendingBattle::Convoy) or calls Campaign::convoy_result(def, convoy, None), which auto-resolves it per vessel as before. convoy_result(…, Some(share)) scales every cargo amount by the share that got through. Without an ambush mission the ambush is auto-resolved on the spot, as in app 0.9.0.
  • Fixed placement rules (Campaign::facility_allowed): mining needs a surveyed system with deposits, research a surveyed research site, manufacturing at most two lanes (lane_route(...).len() <= 2) from a base; one facility of each type per system. The design's placement: expressions are not built (DEV-049).
  • Hulls with components are not paid in money: the manufacture step in Campaign::advance sees hull_components and leaves the job for logistics::step to start once its components are in the base's store.
  • Construction strikes (app 0.16.4, R-STR-023): LogisticsDef::strikes: Option<Strikes> (from, max, chance, mission, setback). The roll is per hour for each site whose progress 1 − (ready_at − now) / time has passed from and whose system's facilities have suffered fewer than max strikes in all (Facility::attacks, saved); the first hit raises Event::Strike and stops the loop, so strikes come one at a time. strike_result settles it: beaten off, destroyed (remove_facility), or set back (ready_at += time × setback), with a message and a notice. The automatic player lets every strike be.
  • Station-only topics (station_topics[t] is Some) are filtered out of Campaign::researchable, so bases never offer them; start_station_research starts one at a research station of the right lab type on the right site.

docs.title: The story (app 0.10.0)
docs.text: campaign::story is the runtime of content::story::StoryDef (StrategyDef::story, always present, empty for a campaign without story sections). Its state is one more plain struct, Campaign::story: StoryState — per event the times fired and the hour it last fired, per arc the steps done, per plan whether it has started, components done, the next roll's hour and the warnings given, the standings, the aggression, battles won (in all and this month), two "something happened" latches for after_battle and on_research, and the ending reached. As everywhere in the campaign these are vectors parallel to the definitions, indexed by position.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    Y[("strategy/story.yaml<br/>events, arcs, plans, endings,<br/>encyclopaedia; relations,<br/>strategist, campaign_end")] --> R["content::rules::build_at<br/>story::DEF_SECTIONS layer;<br/>globals read once"]
    R --> N["StrategyDef::build<br/>story ids join the name table"]
    N --> B["StoryDef::build<br/>conditions parsed (campaign schema);<br/>actions checked (EVENT_ACTIONS);<br/>arcs, raids, endings resolved to indices"]
    B --> T["content::resolve_text<br/>@keys in names, messages, choices,<br/>endings, entries resolved"]
    T --> ST["StoryState::new<br/>(Campaign::new, save::read)"]

The story ids are added to the strategy layer's name table before any expression is parsed, so arc(serial), plan(eclipse_engine) and fired(ch07) compile to checked constants like every other name. Actions are parsed with script::action::parse(text, EVENT_ACTIONS); a single-text action (message, news) keeps its whole argument, commas included, while every other action splits on commas.

docs.title: Logic flow: story::step
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Z{"ending reached?"} -->|yes| END["nothing more happens"]
    Z -->|no| A["1 · events in order: due by check period<br/>(day / week / month boundary crossed, or a battle / topic since last)<br/>not spent (once), not cooling down, next step of its arc,<br/>when holds, roll < chance → fired, arc step +1,<br/>apply_actions(do); choices → Event::Choice"]
    A --> B["2 · plans: not started and start_when → started, log;<br/>started, not complete, next roll due → roll < chance and a base →<br/>launch(raid), contact.plan = Some(p)"]
    B --> C{"3 · month boundary?"}
    C -->|yes| D["standings drift towards 0;<br/>aggression −down if month_wins ≥ calm_after_wins else +up;<br/>month_wins = 0"]
    C -->|no| E
    D --> E["4 · day boundary or an ending event →<br/>check_end: defeats, then victories; first that holds → Event::Ending"]
  • One place changes the campaign. Campaign::apply_actions(def, actions, events) is the only code that turns story actions into changes — money, flags, standings, research, raids, plan progress, aggression, endings — and into events for the screen (Notice, Mission, Ending, and since app 0.11.1 – 0.13.0 Card { title, text }, Video { reference } and Cutscene { id }, which change nothing in the campaign: card only logs its title). Events, choices (Campaign::choose), plan warnings and completion all call it.
  • Shipments reuse raids. A plan's shipment is an ordinary Contact with plan: Some(p), so detection, interception and the battle need nothing new. Only the arrival differs: Campaign::unopposed sees plan and calls shipment_arrived (one more component) instead of striking. A shipment destroyed or driven off is simply removed with its contact.
  • Relations reach two places. Campaign::raids_allowed stops a non-hostile faction's raids in the hour step; StrategyScreen::stances carries the stances into battle (above). A change of stance is announced in change_standing.
  • Arc order by data, not code. An event's arc index is set from the arc's steps while building, so the step check is one comparison: arcs[a].steps.get(arc_step[a]) == Some(&e).

The screen (app::strategy) holds what is waiting for the player — convoy, choice, offer, ending — as Options on StrategyScreen, checked in that order before normal input: an ending takes Enter/Esc to leave, a choice takes the number keys, an offer and a convoy take Enter (fly) or Esc (decline); a title card (card, app 0.11.1) waits for Enter, Esc or a click. A video or cutscene event makes the screen return Next::Video / Next::Cutscene and the app parks it until the film is over (Presentation). An ending's video plays before its banner; loading a save whose story has ended sets StrategyScreen::ending again, so a finished campaign shows its ending (app 0.12.1). The automatic player (autoplay_from) ignores the three presentation events. The Archive tab (Tab::Archive) lists the started plans, the standings with their stances, the aggression and battles won, and Campaign::encyclopaedia's unlocked entries.

docs.title: The X-COM data (app 0.8.0)
docs.text: tools/interceptor_strategy.py (Python, standard library) is a build-time helper, not part of the engine: it reads the player's GameSettings.ini and Interceptor.exe and writes packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml — the tech_ids: table and inherit: references to the original's sections, with no values. The engine then treats the X-COM campaign like any other: inheritance reads the values from the player's file at load, tech_ids turns the numeric prerequisites into conditions (above), and cost_scale, module_time and money_from adapt the original's units. The executable's table layout (12-byte entries: a pointer to the R_ section name, a string id, the tech id) is derived; see Strategy layer › the interceptor campaign.

docs.title: The economy's later rules (app 0.16.6 – 0.16.11)
docs.text:
• Hidden and either-or research (0.16.6): Topic::hidden filters a topic out of researchable until the flag discovered.<topic> exists, which the story action discover sets (with a notice). requires_any: [a, b] is not a new mechanism: while the rules are built it becomes the text research(a) or research(b), joined to requires: as (…) and (…), and is parsed like any condition — so a misspelt topic is reported at research.<id>.requires.
  • Training and dismissal (0.16.7): Pilot::training (saved as yes/no; older saves read as not training); PilotRules::train_gain / train_cost from pilots.training. Campaign::dismiss(p) removes the pilot; no other structure holds a pilot index (a craft's pilot is the Pilot::craft back-reference), so nothing needs renumbering.
  • Evaluations (0.16.8): StrategyDef::evaluations: Vec<Evaluation {rating, when, actions}>; at the month the first whose when holds runs its actions through apply_actions (the story's action runner) and names the rating in the report. evaluations must be in the rules' list of strategy globals (rules::build_at) to reach StrategyDef at all — it was missing until 0.16.9, which the unit test did not catch because it builds the strategy layer directly.
  • Base effects (0.16.10): Campaign::quarters(def) (all bases' type quarters plus quarters effects; 0 = no limit) checked by hire; Campaign::storage(def, base) -> (Option<capacity>, used) — None when no module in the campaign has storage — checked by buy for items; the raid's defence roll in the unopposed-strike code; Campaign::dismantle_module(def, base, m) refunding StrategyDef::dismantle_refund. On the screen Row::default_act keeps Dismantle, Dismiss and (0.16.11) CancelJob off Enter and the double click.
  • Queues and deliveries (0.16.11): Campaign::raise_job(base, j) swaps a job with the one above; cancel_job(base, j) removes an unstarted job, or cuts a started one to its paid unit; StrategyDef::delivery_loss rolls each arriving delivery.

docs.title: Testbed cheats (app 0.8.1)
docs.text:
Campaign::cheat_payday, cheat_knowitall, cheat_quickbase and cheat_jump(contact) are the original's own cheat list as plain methods on the campaign (so they are unit-tested like any order); app::strategy binds them to Ctrl+M, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+B and Ctrl+J. cheat_jump puts the first ready craft with a ready pilot at the contact (away = Some((contact, pos)), route cleared), so the next step's interception check reports Event::Battle at once. Each cheat is logged in the message list.

The event debugger and start-at-chapter (app 0.16.13): Campaign::fire_event(def, e) -> Vec<Event> counts the event as fired, advances its arc only when it is the arc's next step, runs its actions and offers its choice — the same steps as story::step, minus the checks; campaign::autoplay_to_chapter(def, c, step, max_days) repeats autoplay_from five days at a time until story.arc_step[0] >= step or max_days pass (Testbed).

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
campaign::save writes the whole Campaign as a YAML document (write) and reads it back (read), using the engine's own YAML reader and writer (formats::yaml). Because the state holds only numbers, text and indices into the rules, the save is a direct walk:

# OpenInterceptor campaign save
save: 1
campaign: default
packs: [{id: default, version: 0.7.1}]
hours: 1234
money: 2150000
…

Reading checks the format version, then that every pack listed is loaded (else "this save needs packs that are not loaded: …"), then every index against the loaded rules (module, item, topic, income/expense/raid counts; else "save: … does not match the loaded rules (was a mod changed?)"). Since app 0.9.0 a logistics: block follows (write_logistics / read_logistics): facilities with their stores, lines and projects, orders, convoys with their routes, vessels and pending ambush and (app 0.9.2) whether it is held, survey ships, the surveyed flags, the reserves and the bases' stores; destinations are written base:<i> / facility:<i>. Its indices are checked like the rest, a campaign without logistics saves an empty block, and a save with facilities is refused by a campaign that has no logistics. Since app 0.10.0 a story: block follows too (write_story / read_story): events fired and when, arc steps, plan state, standings, aggression, battles won, the two latches and the ending; a contact's plan. Never-fired events hold -inf for their last firing, which YAML numbers cannot carry, so it is written as a very old hour (−10¹²) and read back as -inf. A save whose events, arcs or plans no longer match the rules is refused. A changed mod is refused with a message instead of crashing or silently changing the game. Since app 0.16.2 the pack versions are compared too: a pack still loaded at another version loads, with a notice per pack (Pack x is now version a (this save was made with b)) in Campaign::notices. Since 0.16.3 each facility saves its attacks, since 0.16.7 each pilot training; older saves read them as 0 and not training. The screen saves to <user data>/saves/<campaign id>.yaml (strategy::save_path, slot 0) on F5, when leaving with Esc and at the ending; Campaign: continue loads it. docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --check --campaign default reports every strategy-data error with where it came from (research.x.requires: unknown name 'y', raids.x: unknown mission 'y').
  • openinterceptor --no-original --strategy opens a new default campaign straight away.
  • A save is readable YAML: open <user data>/saves/default.yaml to see the whole state.
  • The message log (Messages tab) records every payment, arrival, research result, battle and report with its date; the Reports list (app 0.16.8) keeps the monthly reports with their ratings.
  • Ctrl+D on the strategy screen (app 0.16.13) lists every arc's step and every event's fired count and whether its condition holds now; Fire now fires one. --strategy --chapter N starts a new campaign played forward to chapter N.
  • openinterceptor --campaign <id> --strategy-soak 180 plays six months headless with campaign::autoplay and prints a one-line summary (app 0.8.0): the quickest check that a modded strategy layer runs — six-month results at app 0.8.0: interceptor 4 of 71 topics on one downlink, default 12 of 14. Since app 0.10.1 – 0.10.2 it also prints the last monthly report and a story line — story: arcs [serial 12/12], plans [eclipse_engine 61%], aggression 1.20, ending none (an example of the form) — so a story that stalls shows which arc stopped where.
  • The story: the Archive tab shows plan progress, standings and aggression; the message log records every chapter, choice (Chose: …), shipment that got through, stance change and the ending. An arc that never moves usually has a step whose when cannot hold (a flag nobody sets, a plan that never starts because its start_when is never true).
  • campaign::tests::the_default_campaign_runs_a_year_with_its_story_and_stays_consistent is the year-long consistency soak: it plays a month at a time with autoplay_from and checks after each month that every craft, pilot, base, contact and facility index is in range, money and score are finite, and arcs never go backwards.
  • Logistics: the Supply tab's last row counts open orders, convoys and survey ships; the message log records every survey, completed facility and ambush. An order that never appears usually means no ready facility can fill it (a resource no mined system has, or no manufacturing center); a hull job that never starts is waiting for its components.
  • The campaign is unit-testable without a window: campaign::autoplay plays any StrategyDef with a simple automatic player (keeps every base researching, builds a lab and a workshop when it can, intercepts every contact it sees, alternates battle results). The tests build small synthetic strategy layers from one YAML document (content::strategy::tests::build) and also play the real default campaign for six months.

docs.title: Extractor (--extract)
docs.text: src/extract.rs: converts the player's original data into formats every tool edits, writing each file at its override path so an edited copy dropped into a mod replaces the original. Plan: Stage 1 (first version); Stage 6 polishes the modding toolkit.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CD["OriginalData<br/>(the player's CD)"] --> M["XMSH → Model::from_xmsh → model_to_obj<br/>models/<name>.obj + .mtl"]
    CD --> T["XTXR → RGBA → png()<br/>textures/<name>.png"]
    CD --> I["TARG (TGA, incl. colour-mapped) → RGBA<br/>cockpit cyan → alpha → png()<br/>images/<dll>/<id>.png"]
    CD --> S["*.wav (MS/IMA ADPCM, PCM) → Pcm → to_wav_bytes<br/>sounds/<name>.wav"]
    CD --> R["*.ini, *.txt copied<br/>original-data/"]
    M & T & I & S & R --> OUT["<DIR>/ with pack.yaml (interceptor-extracted) and README.txt"]
  • Models: the most detailed LOD, in the engine's convention (metres, +Y up, nose along −Z), so positions are written unchanged; texture v is flipped back (1 − v) because Model::from_obj flips it on load — a round trip is exact (unit-tested). Textured groups get map_Kd ../textures/<tex>.png; untextured faces become flat_rrggbb materials with a Kd colour. Materials are kept in a BTreeMap so the output is identical run to run.
  • Images: the original cockpits mark see-through areas with cyan (0x03DF); for cockpit DLLs that becomes alpha 0. Sprites and menu art use colour-mapped TGA, also decoded.
  • On the full CD: 297 models, 799 textures, 3244 images, 792 sounds, 27 reference files, 0 errors, about 2.4 s and 195 MB.

The output is the player's own copy of copyrighted content: personal modding only, never to be shared or committed. The README written into the folder says so.

docs.title: Formats layer
docs.text: src/formats/: turns bytes into plain Rust data. Nothing here knows about windows, GPUs, rules or the simulation, so every reader is tested with small byte buffers built inside the test itself — never with original game files. Plan: Stage 1 (formats needed for flight).

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    B["&[u8]<br/>borrowed bytes"] --> RD["Reader<'a><br/>bounds-checked little-endian reads"]
    RD --> PE["pe::ResourceFile"]
    RD --> XM["xmsh::parse → XmshMesh"]
    RD --> XT["xtxr::parse → XTexture"]
    RD --> TG["tga::decode → Image"]
    RD --> WV["wav::decode → Pcm"]
    B --> SMK["smacker::Smacker::new → next_frame<br/>(Bits: LSB-first bit reader)"]
    B --> MPS["mpsrc::entries, mpsrc::member → &[u8]"]
    TXT["&str"] --> INI["ini::Ini::parse<br/>(original INI; legacy settings)"]
    TXT --> YML["yaml::parse → Node<br/>(mod files, settings, bindings)"]
    TXT --> OBJ["obj::parse → ObjMesh<br/>obj::parse_mtl"]
    RGBA["RGBA pixels"] --> PNG["png::downscale, png::encode_rgba → PNG bytes<br/>(encoding by the image crate since 2ed1149)"]

Logic flow of a typical reader: check the signature (BadMagic if wrong) → read the header with Reader (every read returns FResult, so ? propagates a Truncated error) → read the tables the header points to → validate cross-references (edge and vertex indices, palette indices) → return owned data.

Module Reads Notes formats::pe Win32 resource tables in the original DLLs Names are stored with quotes ("INTTYPEA"); ResId::name strips and upper-cases them. formats::xmsh XMSH meshes LODs, signed edge references, BSP walked with an explicit stack and a node budget. formats::xtxr XTXR palettised textures Palette 0 (full brightness) of 16 RGB555 shade palettes; top mip only. formats::tga TGA (16/24/32-bit, raw or RLE) Optional colour key (cockpit cyan 0x03DF) → transparent black. formats::wav RIFF WAVE: PCM 8/16, MS ADPCM, IMA ADPCM Re-encodes to PCM WAV in memory for playback. formats::ini INI text Case-insensitive sections/keys, ; comments, layered merge. Since Stage 2 used for the original CD's INI files (inherit: original:…) and to migrate old settings.ini / bindings.ini; mod files are YAML. formats::yaml A strict subset of YAML Block and flow mappings and sequences, plain/quoted scalars, | and > block text, # comments. Rejects tabs, anchors, aliases, tags, several documents, complex keys and multi-line plain scalars with a line number. Every scalar stays text (with a quoted flag); the schema layer gives it a type. Also writes YAML (to_yaml). Why hand-written: DEV-030. formats::png (writes) RGBA → PNG App 0.6.7, for the console's textured target model. Since main 2ed1149 encode_rgba(w, h, rgba) calls the image crate's PngEncoder — image is already a direct dependency for decoding (its png feature encodes too), so the in-crate writer of app 0.6.7 (stored deflate blocks, its own CRC-32 and Adler-32) was removed as a duplicate; a length mismatch gives an empty result rather than a panic. The module keeps what the console needs first: shrinking a texture by averaging blocks. Test: the encoded PNG decodes back to the same pixels (Dependency policy). formats::smacker Smacker video SMK2 / SMK4 App 0.12.0. A complete in-crate decoder (below): Huffman trees with the escape cache, the four block types, delta palettes, DPCM audio. formats::mpsrc MPSRC packs (.mps) Main 319a31b. The bundle mfdanim.mps (113 talking-head Smacker clips): below. formats::obj Wavefront OBJ + MTL The mod model format. Negative indices, v/vt/vn forms. Faces in a g/o named slot_<name> are not kept as geometry: each such group becomes an attachment point (name, centre of its faces, first face's normal) in ObjMesh::slots.

docs.title: Smacker (formats::smacker)
docs.text:
The original's films are Smacker files (format page). Smacker::new(&[u8]) reads the 104-byte header (signature, size, frame count, frame rate, flags, seven audio tracks' sizes and rates), the frame size and type tables and the four big Huffman trees, and keeps a borrow of the bytes. next_frame() then decodes one frame into the public pixels (palette indices) and palette and returns its audio, (track, samples) per track present; rgba() converts the current frame. The decoder keeps no history beyond those two buffers, so skip_to(n) can resume at frame n after a caller restores them — which is how app::video steps a decoder it cannot store (Presentation › Videos).

How it is built, layer by layer:

  • Bits. Bits<'a> reads bits least-significant first from a borrowed slice; running out is an error (bitstream ended early), never a panic.
  • Trees. A small tree (8-bit leaves) is an arena of Leaf/Node entries read recursively. A big tree (16-bit leaves) is built from two small trees (low and high byte) plus three escape values; a leaf equal to an escape returns one of a three-slot cache of recent values instead, and every decoded value is pushed into it. The caches are reset each frame.
  • Blocks. The type tree gives a block kind and a run length — SIZES, a 64-entry table built by a const block at compile time (1 – 59, then 128 … 2048) — over 4 × 4 blocks in raster order: mono (two colours from mclr, a 16-bit pattern from mmap), full (16 pixels from full; version 4 adds two half-resolution modes), skip (unchanged) and solid (one colour).
  • Palette. A frame may carry a palette chunk: runs that keep entries, copy a range from the previous palette, or set an entry from three 6-bit components (expanded to 8 bits).
  • Audio. Each track chunk is DPCM: per-channel Huffman trees of deltas from a first sample, 8- or 16-bit, mono or stereo (interleaved), or raw PCM; decode_audio returns 16-bit samples.
  • Line doubling. Files flagged as doubled or interlaced report out_height() = 2 × height.

Unit tests build bitstreams by hand (W, an LSB-first writer): trees with the cache, palettes (kept, copied and explicit entries), a one-frame file with a solid block, and 8-bit mono DPCM. The decoder was checked by hand against all eleven of the reference CD's videos — every frame and its audio decode — with the ignored test real_smacker_file_decodes, which reads a file named by OI_SMK. No original file is in the repository.

docs.title: MPSRC (formats::mpsrc)
docs.text: An MPSRC pack is a named-file bundle (format page): an 8-byte MPSRC signature, a u32 count and count 136-byte entries (a zero-padded 128-byte name, u32 size, u32 offset), then the files. entries(&[u8]) returns the table, checking every entry lies inside the data; member(&[u8], name) returns one file's bytes as a borrowed slice — no copy — matching the name without regard to case. Content::read_asset uses it for references written original:<pack>.mps#<member> (the # part, which for DLLs names a resource, names the member). Test: a_pack_lists_and_returns_its_members (a two-member pack built in the test: the table, a case-insensitive lookup, a missing member, a foreign file).

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is Reader<'a> A borrowed view of bytes with checked u16/i16/u32/i32/f32/name reads. The lifetime 'a ties it to the buffer, so it can never outlive the data. FormatError Why decoding failed: Truncated { offset, wanted, len }, BadMagic { expected }, Invalid(String), Unsupported(String). Implements Display and std::error::Error. FResult<T> Short for Result<T, FormatError>. pe::ResourceFile Owns a DLL's bytes and its resource index; find(kind, id) returns a borrowed slice. pe::ResId Num(u32) or Name(String) — a resource id. xmsh::XmshMesh, Lod, Polygon, XVertex, Manipulator The mesh exactly as stored (Direct3D coordinates). Polygons store a first/count range into one shared polygon_vertices vector. xtxr::XTexture Width, height, palette 0 and the top mip's indices; to_rgba(). tga::Image RGBA, rows top to bottom (also used as content::Image). wav::Pcm Interleaved i16 samples; to_wav_bytes(), duration(). ini::Ini, ini::Section Parsed INI; get, get_f32, get_bool, get_floats, merge_from. yaml::Node, yaml::Value, yaml::YamlError A YAML value with its 1-based line: Null, Scalar { text, quoted }, Seq, Map (entries in file order); an error with line and message. smacker::Smacker<'a>, AudioTrack, FrameAudio, SmkError A Smacker file being decoded (borrowing its bytes): width, height, frames, frame_time, tracks, the current pixels and palette; one audio track's rate and format; a frame's audio per track; a decoding error. mpsrc::Entry, mpsrc::entries, mpsrc::member One file in an MPSRC pack (name, offset, size); the table; one member's bytes. smacker::Bits<'a>, smacker::Big The LSB-first bit reader; a big Huffman tree with its escape cache. obj::ObjMesh, obj::ObjMaterial Positions, uvs, normals, faces (as corner ranges), material names, slots (attachment points).

docs.text:
• openinterceptor --check --data <cd> parses every original mesh and texture and reports each failure by resource name (1 096 resources, 0 errors on the reference CD).
  • A Truncated error names the offset and size requested: compare with the byte tables on the format pages.
