docs.title: Cockpit and HUD
docs.text: src/hud/: the 2D layer over the 3D view. hud/mod.rs holds the pure logic (tested); hud/draw.rs paints it with macroquad (verified by manual tests). hud/layout.rs holds the pure maths of 3D-cockpit anchors and the cockpit layout editor. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added the power and systems instruments, status flags, the MFD Systems page, text fitted to each instrument, instruments anchored in perspective on a 3D cockpit and the layout editor (F12). Stage 6.6 added the ship status display (ship_status, app 0.15.1).

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    W["World + player ShipId"] --> L["pure logic<br/>radar_point, gauge_values, gauge_angle,<br/>mfd_lines, MessageLog::visible,<br/>power_readout, system_lamps, status_flags,<br/>draw::shield_bands, draw::hull_color"]
    CK["CockpitDef.instruments + design<br/>(or default_instruments, 640×480)"] --> LY["Layout::new(screen, design)<br/>design space → pixels"]
    L --> D["draw::draw_targeting<br/>draw::draw_cockpit<br/>draw::draw_instruments<br/>(skips anchored ones)"]
    LY --> D
    AN["CockpitDef.anchors"] --> AC["layout::anchor_corners<br/>(+ model_offset)"]
    AC --> DA["app::flight::draw_anchored<br/>draw_instrument → RenderTarget<br/>→ grid mapped onto the corners"]
    L --> DA

Anchored instruments (3D cockpits). An anchor (at, normal, size, metres from the eye) is a rectangle lying on the cockpit model's surface. anchor_corners builds its four corners: "up" is world +Y with its component along the normal removed (Gram–Schmidt), "right" completes the frame. Each frame, draw_anchored (in app::flight) projects the corners to measure the instrument's on-screen footprint, draws the instrument with draw::draw_instrument into a RenderTarget at about twice that size (so lines stay sharp), and maps the texture onto the rectangle through a grid of small quads (anchor_point interpolates the corners), because one quad of two triangles would bend straight lines at its diagonal. The instrument then sits in its bezel at any window shape and field of view. HudFrame::anchored names the instruments drawn this way, and draw_instruments skips them.

Text fitted to instruments. Every instrument painter sizes its text to its box (fit_size: the longest line, measured once at a reference size, scaled to fit the width and the row count to fit the height, capped at a maximum). The MFD uses one size for every page, fitted to the longest page, so text does not jump when pages change. Lines and text also scale with an anchored instrument's texture.

Design space. Instruments are placed in a cockpit's design space (instruments: {mfd: [x, y, w, h]} in the rules). The original cockpits use 640×480, the default; a cockpit can declare its own with design: [w, h] (the default campaign's Guard cockpit uses 1280×720). Layout::new(screen, design) scales the design space as large as fits (min(screen.w / design.w, screen.h / design.h)) and centres it: a 4:3 cockpit fills the height of a 16:9 screen with space visible at the sides; a 16:9 design fills it exactly. The cockpit image is stretched to the whole design space (Layout::full), whatever its pixel size — which is why an HD repaint (e.g. 2560×1920 replacing a 640×480 original) keeps every instrument aligned without changing a rule.

Instruments (names used in cockpit rules):

Name Shows radar_front, radar_rear Contacts in the front / rear hemisphere; distance from the centre = angle off the axis (rim = 90°); rear scope mirrored left/right. Faction colours; stations drawn larger; the target boxed. Mobile contacts beyond [flight] RadarRange are hidden. mfd One of five pages (MfdPage): Target (name, faction, range, speed, shields, armour, hull, lock state), Weapons (beams, link mode, racks with the selected one marked >), Status (own shields with balance, armour/hull/energy, and the power line BEAM x SHLD y PWR used/budget), Systems (one line per fitted system: OK, ON, DMG n%, OUT, DESTROYED, * while being repaired), Nav. gauge1–gauge4 Needles for speed, energy, shields, hull (red below 25 %). ship_status The player's craft from above, tinted by hull_color(hull / class hull) (green → amber → red), inside a fore arc (centred ahead) and an aft arc (behind), each 140° wide with three bands; shield_bands(fraction) lights one band per third of that facing (none at or below 2 %), coloured by shield_ring_color (blinking when down), from power_readout's fore / aft fractions. The silhouette is three triangles (fuselage, wings, tail) — one generic shape, not the class's model. On the glass HUD it gets a ring outline. App 0.15.1; replaces gauge 3 in the glass layout and the default cockpit. message The newest message younger than 4 s. power B-<level> and S-<level> columns (charge settings), fore/aft shield bars with the favoured facing marked, used/budget in yellow when the budget is full (power_readout). systems A grid of lamps, one per fitted system with a three-letter label (system_abbrev): green OK, cyan switched on, amber damaged, red knocked out (blinking while repaired), grey destroyed (system_lamps, Lamp).

Fallback panels. A cockpit that does not place power or systems gets them as small panels at the top right of its own design space — x from 87.5 % of the design width, y from 9 % of its height — with a dark backdrop over cockpit art. The glass layout (default_instruments) places both along the bottom.

Ships without cockpit art, and the non-cockpit views, use glass instruments (default_instruments() with dark backgrounds). A throttle/speed/REV/BURN/VCT strip is drawn under the message line, extended with BRAKE while braking and HOLD n while the flight computer holds a speed, and the Stage 2 status flags (status_flags): DISABLED, CLOAKED, TRACTOR, ECM, JUMP n (hyperspace countdown).

Drift readout (app 0.3.1). The status line reads THR 60% 312 m/s X+45 Y-12: throttle, forward speed, then sideways (X, + right) and vertical (Y, + up) drift in whole metres per second, signed (drift_text). All three come from Ship::body_velocity(), the velocity turned into the ship's own axes (Simulation). In newtonian flight a turn changes the nose, not the motion, so after a hard turn X or Y shows how far the ship is sliding.

Atmosphere instruments (app 0.6.0). Over a ground, status_line (which now takes the World) appends ALT n VS ±n: draw::altitude(world, ship) — the height above World::ground_height under the craft, None in space — and the world vertical speed. In the forward views draw_targeting draws an artificial horizon: ladder_directions(camera_forward, angles) gives, for each pitch angle, a direction straight ahead in the camera's compass heading (its forward with the vertical part removed) tilted up by that angle. A point 1 km along it is projected, and a line is drawn across it along the camera's level right: 320 m long (at 1 km) for the horizon (0°), 120 m with a +10-style label for the rungs at −20°, −10°, +10°, +20°. Because the directions are built from the level heading, the horizon stays level on screen in world terms whatever the craft's pitch and roll.

Flight-path marker. draw_targeting projects a point 1 km along the ship's velocity (when faster than 5 m/s) and draws a circle with three ticks (left, right, up) there: where the craft is actually going. With no drift it sits on the crosshair; sideways drift slides it off to the side.

Targeting (forward views): a reticle; corner brackets sized by the target's angular size; name and range; a lead circle (where to aim beams); a lock-progress ring, then a red lock diamond and LOCK; an arrow on a ring when the target is off-screen. Nav points draw a blue diamond.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• No ALT/VS or horizon: they appear only when the battle has a ground (World::env.ground); in space and in physics: space environments they are hidden by design.
  • Power and systems panels appearing at the top right mean the cockpit has no instruments.power / instruments.systems rectangles; add them to place the instruments.
  • In a 3D cockpit, instruments that drift off their bezels on a narrow window point to a Design that does not match the proportions the bezels were measured at; the field of view widens to fit the design's width (app::flight::cockpit_fov), see Cockpits.
  • Press F12 in the cockpit view to move instruments with the mouse (layout editor, see Cockpits); S saves the result as an addon you can inspect.
  • An anchored instrument that looks mirrored or upside down has its normal pointing into the surface; the editor's ray pick always turns the normal towards the eye.
  • If instruments sit in the wrong place on a cockpit, adjust the instruments rectangles in the cockpit's rules section — no code change needed; positions are in the cockpit's design space (640×480 unless Design says otherwise), not in the image's pixels.
  • The original cockpits' cyan colour key becomes transparent black on load; a cyan halo means the key was not applied (load_image(.., colour_key = true)).
  • The ship status display shows three dim bands and a green craft at the start of a battle in a class with no shields: power_readout gives a zero fraction, which lights no band (by design). On X-COM art it may sit beside the round display: the rectangles were placed by eye; move them with F12 and save.

docs.title: Input and gamepads
docs.text: src/input/ turns device state into simulation Controls and one-shot Commands, using bindings from an editable YAML file (bindings.yaml). The device reading itself is in src/app/devices.rs (keyboard, mouse) and src/platform/ (gamepads). The in-game controls menu is modelled in src/input/editor.rs and drawn by src/app/controls.rs. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added the power, equipment and wingman actions, gamepad chords and the controls menu; app 0.3.1 the keys overlay (help, help_rows). The default layout is on Controls.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    KB["macroquad keys<br/>KeyCode → name"] --> RAW["RawInput<br/>held, pressed, shift,<br/>mouse_offset, buttons, pad, pad_previous"]
    MS["mouse"] --> RAW
    GP["platform::Gamepads::poll<br/>→ PadState"] --> RAW
    RAW --> T["Bindings::translate(&raw, mouse_flight)"]
    T --> C["Controls (sim)"]
    T --> CMD["Vec<Command> (app)"]
    T --> CH["ChaseInput (camera)"]
    TAB["ACTIONS table<br/>name, action, keys, pad, group, label"] --> B["Bindings::from_yaml<br/>(defaults + bindings.yaml)"]
    B --> T
    ED["editor::Editor<br/>(controls menu)"] -- "edits a copy;<br/>saved on leaving" --> B
  • One table. ACTIONS lists every action once: its bindings.yaml name, the Action, its default keys, its default pad chords, its menu Group and its label. Parsing, defaults, to_yaml_text, the controls menu and the Controls tables all come from it, so they cannot drift apart. Entries are built with a const fn a(…) so the whole table is a compile-time constant.
  • Keys overlay (app 0.3.1). help_rows(&Bindings) turns the table into the overlay's content: every Group in table order, each with (label, keys) rows showing the player's current keys, then pad buttons (pad A), or "unbound". The action help (? = Shift+Slash, and Shift+F1) toggles it; app::flight::draw_help paints it. A new action therefore appears in parsing, the defaults, the controls menu, the overlay and (later) the console without further work. F12 is not bound to it: in a custom cockpit F12 opens the layout editor (Cockpits).

  • Remote action sets (the control console, interlude C1, app 0.4.0). RawInput gains remote_held and remote_pressed (sets of Action) and remote_throttle. A remote surface — the tablet console, later a USB panel — fills them, and translate treats a held or tapped remote action exactly like a key bound to it, so the console needs no second path into the simulation. A remote throttle position sets Controls::throttle_set (clamped to 0–1). remote::RemoteInput fills the sets each frame from the console's events (one held set per console, released when it disconnects); see Remote console.

  • Key names are macroquad's KeyCode variant names, lower-cased (KeyCode::Kp7 → kp7), produced by app::devices::key_name. Every key macroquad knows is therefore bindable.

  • Held vs pressed: axes, fire beams and afterburner are held; throttle steps, missile, link mode, targeting, views, power and equipment switches fire once per press. A Shift+X chord fires only with Shift held; a plain X only without it, so both can be bound to different actions. While Shift is held, a key used in any Shift chord is ignored by held actions bound to the plain key (shifted_keys): Shift+E (wingmen evasive) does not also roll the ship on E.
  • Gamepad chords. A PadChord is a button with an optional modifier button (LeftShoulder+A). Any button used as a modifier somewhere (modifiers()) does nothing on its own, and a plain binding does not fire while another modifier is held — holding the modifier switches the pad to its second layer. The defaults use the left shoulder as the only modifier.
  • Gamepad presses are detected by comparing with last frame's PadState.
  • Sticks add to the keys and are clamped; a dead zone is applied and rescaled (input::dead). StickLayout::Space (default): left stick yaw and pitch, right stick roll and vertical slide; StickLayout::Aircraft swaps yaw and roll (the original's Alt+J). Stick forward = nose down unless invert_pitch.
  • Mouse flight (toggle C): cursor offset from the centre / mouse range gives yaw and pitch, cursor down = nose down (as the original readme states) unless mouse_invert; left button = beams, right button = missile.
  • Bindings file: bindings.yaml in the user data folder (macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ or ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/). Created with the defaults on first run (app::load_bindings); keys not mentioned keep their defaults; the controls menu rewrites it in full when it saves. A bindings.ini of an earlier build is read once with the legacy reader (Bindings::from_ini) and saved as bindings.yaml.
keyboard:
  fire_beams: [Enter, LeftControl]
  wing_fire_at_will: [Shift+F]
gamepad:
  fire_beams: [RightTrigger]
  hyperspace: [LeftShoulder+A]
options:
  dead_zone: 0.15
  invert_pitch: false
  stick_layout: space
  mouse_range: 200
  mouse_invert: false

docs.title: The controls menu
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    DEV["devices.read()<br/>RawInput"] --> CM["app::controls::ControlsMenu::frame"]
    CM -- "keys, d-pad, A/B/X/Y" --> ED["editor::Editor<br/>rows, selection, capture"]
    ED --> PAINT["paint rows, cells, message"]
    CM -- "on leaving" --> AP["ctx.bindings = editor.bindings<br/>write bindings.yaml"]

Editor holds a working copy of the Bindings and the list of Rows: a Header per Group, an Action row per action, then a Setting row per device option (dead zone, invert pitch, stick layout, mouse range, mouse invert). Each action row has four cells (COLUMNS): two key slots and two pad slots. activate starts a Capture:

  • Capture::Key — capture_key(key, shift) binds the next key with Shift as a chord; a lone Shift is ignored (waiting for its key), Escape cancels.
  • Capture::Pad { first } — the capture cannot tell from the first button whether it is a plain press or a chord, so it waits: a second button pressed while the first is held makes first+second; the first released alone makes a plain binding.

assign_key / assign_pad remove the chord from every other action before setting it (the status line names the actions that lost it), so a chord is bound to at most one action. clear, reset_selected and reset_all restore defaults. The screen is a component with a frame method so the launcher and the in-flight pause menu (K) can both host it; it gives up a capture after 8 s (CAPTURE_TIMEOUT).

docs.title: Keys held when a battle starts (app 0.4.10)
docs.text: Enter starts a mission from the launcher, the restart prompt and the debrief, and Enter is also a fire key; the pad's A button both starts and acts in flight. input::StartGuard, applied first in the flight screen's frame right after the devices are read, records the keys, pad buttons, triggers and mouse button held on the battle's first frame and filters each out of every later frame until it is released; a fresh press then works normally (R-CON-025; test keys_held_when_a_battle_starts_are_ignored_until_released).

docs.text: Symbol What it is Action Every bindable action (65, with Help). ACTIONS, ActionInfo, info(action) The single table: name, action, keys, pad, group, label — one source for parsing, defaults, the menu and docs. Group Flight, Throttle, Weapons, Targeting, Power, Wingmen, Views, Camera, Interface; title(). KeyChord A key name plus optional Shift; parse, text. PadChord A button plus optional modifier button; plain, parse, text. StickLayout Space or Aircraft. Bindings keys: HashMap<Action, Vec<KeyChord>>, pad: HashMap<Action, Vec<PadChord>>, dead_zone, mouse_range, pad_invert_pitch, stick_layout, mouse_invert; from_yaml, to_yaml_text, legacy from_ini, translate. Power and equipment presses go to Controls::requests instead. View Cockpit, Forward, Left, Right, RearLeft, RearRight, Chase, ChaseManual; View::parse for --view. docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 openinterceptor … prints the names of keys as they are pressed.
  • One-shot inputs pressed in a frame that runs no simulation tick are carried over by Controls::carry_unconsumed, so a press is never lost on high-refresh displays.
  • An action that "does nothing": open the controls menu and look at its cells — a chord moved to another action is removed from the old one, and the status line said which. A pad button that does nothing on its own is probably used as a modifier in some chord.
  • A broken bindings.yaml cannot lock you out (a file that does not parse is reported and the defaults are used): Shift+D in the controls menu restores every default, and deleting the file recreates it on the next run.
  • A gamepad that does nothing on Linux: check /dev/input/js0 exists and is readable by your user (often the input group).

docs.title: Missions
docs.text: src/content/mission.rs (definitions) and src/mission/ (the runtime): battles described by roles, waves, objectives and outcomes, refereed on top of the simulation. The battle conditions are src/script/battle.rs, the outcome actions src/script/action.rs. Plan: Stage 3 part 1 (app 0.3.0). The modder's view is Missions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Y["missions/*.yaml<br/>(any rules folder)"] --> RB["rules::build_at<br/>validate (files::mission), inherit, variants, per_level"]
    RB --> MP["MissionDef::parse(id, Get, pack, classes, levels)<br/>roles, waves, objectives, optional, timer,<br/>outcomes, chatter, debrief"]
    BS["script::battle::schema(role names, levels)"] --> MP
    AC["script::action::MISSION_ACTIONS"] --> MP
    MP --> TX["Content: @keys resolved<br/>(name, briefing, debrief, chatter, message args)"]
    TX --> RU["Ruleset::missions (sorted by order)"]
    RU --> ST["MissionRun::start(def, rules, shapes, player class)<br/>environment first → player + roles arriving at the start<br/>→ hazards last → World"]
    ST --> W["World"]

Layering. mission sits between sim and app: it reads and spawns into a World (through World::spawn_placement, the same path scenario objects take), but the simulation knows nothing about missions, so sim stays testable on its own.

Start order (Stage 3). MissionRun::start sets the mission's environment: on the new World first (World::set_environment), so that ground installations among the roles are set down on its terrain (app 0.6.1); then places the player and the roles that arrive at the start; and applies hazards: last (World::apply_hazards), so asteroids and mines keep 300 m clear of every craft already placed. World::from_scenario follows the same order for scenarios. See Simulation.

docs.title: One frame of a mission
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    FS["FlightSession::frame"] --> STEP["World::step() × n ticks"]
    STEP --> UP["MissionRun::update(&mut World)<br/>after every tick"]
    UP --> L1["1. losses per role from member state<br/>(destroyed, departed, captured events)"]
    L1 --> L2["2. arrive: conditions → spawn_role;<br/>waves (once); chatter (once) → message lines<br/>(and its voice clip → voices);<br/>optional objectives latched"]
    L2 --> L3["3. end: retreat (player departed) →<br/>killed (player destroyed) →<br/>lose → win → draw → timer"]
    L3 -->|result| DB["Debrief: result, text, optional (met?),<br/>campaign actions, kills, losses, seconds;<br/>battle actions (message) run"]
    DB --> OV["debrief overlay over the frozen battle<br/>Enter: again · Esc/L: launcher"]
  • Placement (spawn_role): the count is rolled from [min, max], each member's class from the role's list; the arrival point is distance along bearing (yaw, pitch; [0, 0] = −Z from the player's start; random within ±20° pitch when absent) from the player's start or the centre of the from role's survivors; members stand side by side spread apart across the line of sight and face the player's start. Placed members get the role's faction, AI role, behaviour, protect flag, state, hull, destroyed systems and speed.
  • Counting: a member that has left the world is departed (hyperspace) if its slot still holds it (World::same_slot) and it departed, otherwise destroyed; captures come from Captured events. Kills are hostile losses, losses the player's own faction's.
  • Determinism: the mission's random choices come from its own generator seeded by starfield_seed, and condition random(p) from the same stream, so a mission replays identically with the same inputs.
  • Chatter voices (app 0.6.2): a chatter line with voice: also pushes its clip (an index into Ruleset::voice_clips) onto MissionRun::voices when it is said; the flight screen plays and clears that list every frame, and plays the computer voice (mission_accomplished or mission_failed) when the debrief appears (Audio).
  • Spawning over a ground (app 0.6.4): over a terrain, World::spawn lifts any craft placed less than 300 m above the ground to 300 m (ground installations are still set down on it). A role placed from a ground installation would otherwise start inside a hill.
  • Conditions are evaluated through BattleCx, which implements the script language's Context for this battle; role names are constants of the battle schema, compiled to indices.

docs.title: The killed result (app 0.3.1)
docs.text:
When the player's craft is destroyed — its slot no longer holds it (!World::same_slot, the slot may have been reused) or it is not alive — the result is killed, checked before the mission's own conditions. Before 0.3.1 a mission whose lose condition included not player_alive reported the player's death as a loss, and the debrief showed the lose text, which usually describes the objective failing ("the base was destroyed"). Measured with the idle soak pilot, that was what players of xcom_base_defense saw on veteran: the base was fine, the player had been killed in 15–18 s.

killed takes the mission's own outcomes: {killed: …} if it has any, else its lose outcomes; the debrief text is debrief: {killed: …} if given, else empty. The debrief panel's headline is "YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED".

docs.title: Launcher, --mission, soak
docs.text: The launcher lists missions after the scenarios (Mission: name, the briefing as the description, the ship choice when player.class is choose) and scrolls the list to keep the selection near the middle (launcher::Menu::first_visible, "^ more" / "v more" markers). Selecting one returns Next::Mission { mission, ship }; --mission <id> starts one directly. soak::run_mission plays a mission headless with the passive, AI or idle pilot and reports the result (--soak <mission id>). A unit test holds the balance promise of R-MSN-011: in the default campaign at cadet, defend_station with the idle pilot is still running after 150 s. Since app 0.6.4 the soak report counts kills while the mission is still running (MissionRun::kills()); before, a mission that ran out of time read 0 kills.

docs.title: The simulator (app 0.6.3)
docs.text: The simulator (app::simulator, Testbed) flies a modified copy of a mission: simulator::apply returns a new MissionDef with the chosen environment and hazards and its enemy roles and waves scaled, and FlightSession::start_custom starts it through the same MissionRun as any other mission. Nothing in mission knows it is a simulation.

docs.title: Cargo, escorts and repeating waves (app 0.9.2)
docs.text:
• cargo(role) and the debrief's cargo share come from mission::cargo_share(world, role): the cargo containers (modules of a cargo: true class) still mounted on a live member — or departed with a departed member — over every cargo slot of the members' classes. A container torn off has no mount; a destroyed one is neither alive nor departed. Debrief::cargo is Some(share) when the mission names a cargo: role, and it reaches the campaign in the BattleReport.
  • Escorts: when a role with escort: spawns, each member's AI gets the newest live member of the escorted role as its leader and a slot of its formation (sim::ai's escort manoeuvre flies it).
  • Repeating waves: MissionRun::waves_again holds, per wave with every:, the battle time it may come again; a wave that has come is skipped unless that time has passed and its when still holds.

docs.title: AI changes made with missions
docs.text: Enemies now launch missiles only when closing in (within 2.5 × their attack range, at least 2 km); the first launch comes 3 s plus a random part of one interval into the attack, and each interval varies by ±25 %. Every AI pilot's random sequence is seeded per ship in World::spawn, so pilots that start together do not act together.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is content::mission::MissionDef A parsed mission: id, name, briefing, order, player_class, player_position, roles, waves, win/lose/draw, optional, timer, outcomes, chatter, debrief, starfield_seed. RoleDef, Arrival, WaveDef, ChatterDef A role (classes, count range, faction, AI, behaviour, protect, state, hull, destroyed systems, speed, at, arrive); an arrival (distance, bearing, from, spread); a wave; a radio line (when, line, and since app 0.6.2 voice with its voice_clip index, filled in by the rules). mission::MissionRun The running mission: its definition, the player's id, per-role RoleRuns, wave/chatter/optional latches, its generator, kills, losses, debrief, and voices (chatter clips said and not yet played). kills() reads the kills so far, also while the battle runs; evaluate answers the condition console (app 0.16.5). mission::RoleRun members, arrived, destroyed, retreated, captured. mission::Debrief result (win, lose, draw, retreat, killed), text, optional: Vec<(name, met)>, campaign actions (as text), kills, losses, seconds. mission::BattleCx The battle Context for conditions. script::battle::QUERIES, schema(roles, levels) The battle context's queries. script::action::{ActionDef, Action, Scope, MISSION_ACTIONS} Outcome actions with Battle or Campaign scope. schema::Ty::Either A schema type with two accepted forms (count, bearing, class). World::spawn_placement, World::same_slot Spawn one placed object; whether an id's slot still holds its ship. app::Next::Mission, FlightSession::start_mission Starting a mission from the launcher or --mission. app::Next::Simulate, FlightSession::start_custom Starting a simulator mission: a ready-made, modified MissionDef (app 0.6.3).

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
• MissionDef::parse(id, Get, pack, classes, levels) -> Result<MissionDef, String>; def.outcome(result) -> &[Action].

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• --check reports every mission problem with file, line and path (missions.x: roles.y…, unknown roles in conditions, unknown actions).
  • --mission <id> --ship <id> jumps straight in; --soak <id> --difficulty <level> [--soak-pilot ai|idle] plays it headless and prints soak mission <id> (<level>, <pilot>): <result> after <n> s; <k> kills — the quickest way to check that a mission can be both won and lost.
  • A role that never appears: its arrive: condition never held, or its at.from role has no survivors (it then appears at the player's start). arrived(role) in a chatter line makes arrivals visible in play.
  • A "MISSION ERROR: …" message line means a role could not be spawned (an unknown slot in a station's modules, for example).
  • Press ` in the battle to type any condition and see its value now — arrived(raiders), count(foes), the win: expression itself (app 0.16.5). The battle pauses meanwhile.

docs.title: Packs, VFS and rules
docs.text:
src/content/: answers "what is in the game?". Chooses the campaign and its active set of packs, loads them in dependency order, indexes the player's original data, builds the typed Ruleset (including ship systems, power and damage rules from content::equipment), parses scenarios, and loads individual assets on demand as plain CPU data. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added mod kinds, the active set, equipment, behaviours and difficulty, and moved every mod file to YAML checked against schemas (mod format 2: formats::yaml, content::schema, content::files). The user-facing side is in Modding.

Where packs come from (app 0.4.2). ContentConfig::pack_dirs lists folders whose sub-folders with a pack.yaml are packs, in load order: resources/ (what ships with the game: the default campaign in resources/default) then packs/ (bundled mods such as interceptor); mods_dir (the user's mods) comes last. A later pack overrides an earlier one, so mods override resources. cli::content_dirs builds the list; --packs replaces only packs/. The player's original data in resources/xcom/ or resources/xcom-cd/ has no pack.yaml, so discovery skips it; it reaches the engine as ContentConfig::original (Settings and data discovery).

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    CFG["ContentConfig<br/>pack_dirs, mods_dir, original, no_original,<br/>disabled, campaign"] --> D["pack::discover<br/>folders with pack.yaml<br/>(kind, parent, targets, format)"]
    D --> CA{"which campaign?<br/>cfg.campaign if available,<br/>else preferred_campaign"}
    CA --> AS["pack::active_set<br/>parent chain + targeting addons<br/>+ their depends"]
    AS --> DIS{"disabled in<br/>settings.yaml?"}
    DIS -->|skip + warning| W
    DIS -->|keep| SK{"requires_original<br/>and no data?"}
    SK -->|skip + warning| W["warnings"]
    SK -->|keep| O["pack::order<br/>stable topological sort"]
    CFG --> OD["vfs::OriginalData::open<br/>index files by name, open DLLs"]
    O --> RS["rules/, campaign/ and missions/*.yaml of every pack<br/>yaml::parse → Node trees"]
    RS --> B["rules::build_at(level)<br/>validate → merge → levels → inherit/variants/per_level → typed structs"]
    OD -->|"original:File.ini/Section<br/>(still INI)"| B
    B --> RU["Ruleset<br/>incl. behaviours, difficulty"]
    O --> SC["scenarios/*.yaml → validate → Scenario<br/>later pack replaces same id"]
    O --> TX["text/<language>/*.yaml (else text/en/)<br/>+ imports of original LangFile*.txt<br/>→ TextTable"]
    TX -->|"@key resolved"| B
    TX -->|"@key resolved"| SC

docs.title: From YAML text to typed rules
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T["file text"] --> Y["formats::yaml::parse<br/>strict subset → Node<br/>(every value a string + line)"]
    Y --> V["schema::validate(node, files::rules())<br/>unknown keys (did you mean), types, units"]
    V --> M["merge_into, pack by pack<br/>maps merge, lists replace,<br/>empty removes, key+ / key- edit lists"]
    M --> L["campaign.difficulty →<br/>level index"]
    L --> I["resolve inherit (ids, original: INI)<br/>apply variants[level]<br/>pick per_level[level]"]
    I --> TY["typed structs via schema::Get<br/>(num, qty with unit, list, …)"]
    I -.-> SCH["behaviours: script::parse_condition<br/>checked against the object schema"]

Logic flow of rules::build_at(sources, original, level):

  1. Validate every file against files::rules(); each problem becomes <file>:<line>: <key path>: <message>.
  2. Merge the files in load order (merge_into): definitions of the eight definition sections by (section, id), global sections by name; mappings merge recursively, values and lists are replaced, an empty value removes a key, key+ / key- edit a list (kept until there is a list to edit, so they also work on an inherited list). Each entry remembers the pack and file:line that last wrote it.
  3. Difficulty: the campaign section's difficulty list and the level asked for (else default_difficulty, else the middle level) give a level index.
  4. Resolve each definition: inherit chains (same section, section.id, or original:<file>/<section> read through the OriginalLookup and renamed by snake_case; depth limit 16 catches cycles) → variants[level] merged over it → every {per_level: […]} replaced by its entry → dropped if delete: true.
  5. Type: factions, beams, missiles (guidance, damage mode, cluster submunitions resolved by id), systems (built-ins of every SystemKind first), damage and power, the sound cue table (audio.cue_table; every cue:<Name> reference resolved), behaviours (with prefer selectors), looks — effects (the engine's explosion added if none), debris sets, model sets (texture swaps, damage levels, states) — (conditions parsed and checked against the object schema with the level names as constants; builtin_attack added if no pack defines it), then ships and objects (which refer to the others by id; model_set, or a model set made from the shorthand model/debris; class_systems resolves systems, systems+, systems-, vct; modules as (slot, class)), then missions (MissionDef::parse against the battle schema of their role names; their hazards: through content::hazards), terrains (TerrainDef::parse; a generated heightfield is built here, once), environments (EnvironmentDef::parse, each terrain: checked against the terrains), cockpits (with anchors), flight, sounds, and since app 0.6.2 voices: each voices: set becomes a VoiceSet whose lines hold indices into one list of every voice clip, Ruleset::voice_clips (the sets' clips first, then each mission chatter line's voice:, whose index is written back into its ChatterDef::voice_clip); a ship naming an unknown voice set is an error. environments, terrains and voices are definition sections like ships (DEF_SECTIONS), so inherit, delete and variants work on them.

Every problem is collected; a broken definition is skipped, the rest still load. Scenarios go through the same parse and files::scenario() validation (Scenario::from_yaml), and manifests through files::pack() (PackInfo::parse).

Heightmaps (app 0.6.0): after the rules and text, Content::load reads each terrain with a heightmap: image from its pack (load_image) and builds its Heightfield::from_image; a failure is a content error naming the terrain. Generated terrains need no files, so they are built with the rules; heightmaps need the pack's files, so they wait for content loading. Either way the heightfield is stored once in TerrainDef::field (an Arc) and shared by every battle.

Text (content::text, Stage 2): before the rules are typed, every active pack's text/<language>/*.yaml (falling back to text/en/ for a pack without the language) is read into one TextTable, later packs replacing keys; imports: read the original's language files from the original data by reference (formats::langfile) under a prefix (orig.<KEY>). TextTable::resolve turns @key values into strings in names, descriptions and scenario titles; a missing key is an error and shows as the key.

The schemas are data (schema::Ty trees built in files.rs), so one description drives validation, the JSON Schema export (files::json_schemas, --write-schemas; the committed schemas/*.schema.json are checked by the gate) and the Mod file reference.

docs.title: Mod kinds and the active set
docs.text:
pack::PackInfo carries kind (Campaign, Addon, Library), parent (campaigns only), targets (addons) and format (newer than pack::FORMAT = 2 is refused; a folder with only a format-1 pack.ini is refused with a pointer to the docs). The player plays one campaign; Content::load picks it from ContentConfig.campaign (command line --campaign or settings.yaml game.campaign), and the difficulty from ContentConfig.difficulty, falling back with a warning to preferred_campaign: interceptor when available, else default, else the first campaign found.

flowchart LR
    ID["campaign id"] --> CH["pack::chain<br/>follow parent links,<br/>root first; error on cycle"]
    CH --> AD["+ addons whose targets<br/>name a chain campaign, *, or nothing"]
    AD --> DP["+ everything they depend on<br/>(transitively)"]
    DP --> OR["pack::order<br/>parents and depends first"]

--check and the gate run once per campaign, each with its own active set. When no pack is a campaign (a Stage 1 setup) every pack loads, as before.

docs.title: Asset loading and per-asset overrides
docs.text:
Content::load_* parses an AssetRef. Pack-relative paths resolve in the pack that defined them. An original: reference first asks find_override: every active pack is searched, highest priority (latest in load order) first, for a file at the asset's override path (vfs::override_paths); only if none exists is the original data read.

flowchart LR
    R["original:CockpitA.dll#12000"] --> OP["override_paths(Image, 'CockpitA.dll', '12000')<br/>images/cockpita/12000.png | .tga"]
    OP --> FO{"find_override:<br/>latest pack with the file?"}
    FO -->|yes| PF["decode the pack file<br/>(PNG alpha, no colour key)"]
    FO -->|no| CD["OriginalData → TARG resource<br/>(cyan colour key applied)"]
Original asset Override path in a pack mesh INTTYPEA models/inttypea.obj texture CUBETOP (named by a model) textures/cubetop.png or .tga image CockpitA.dll#12000 images/cockpita/12000.png or .tga loose image file images/<file stem>.png sound Xwinder.wav sounds/xwinder.wav

Paths are lower-case. These are exactly the paths --extract writes (Extractor), so an extracted, edited file dropped into a mod replaces the original. Whole packs can be switched off with packs.disabled in settings.yaml (Settings); a disabled pack contributes no rules, scenarios or overrides.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• --check prints every file problem as file:line: key.path: message and every rules error as file:line: section.id: message, plus model, texture, image, sound and scenario failures, per campaign. --list shows the campaigns (* = loaded) and what loaded. --check --campaign <id> checks one campaign.
  • "campaign 'x' is not available; using the default" — the id is wrong, the pack is disabled, or it needs original data that was not found. "only a campaign may have a parent", "unknown pack kind", and "needs mod format n" come from PackInfo::parse.
  • An addon that seems ignored: check its targets names the campaign being played (or the campaign's parent).
  • "pack 'x' skipped" means it needs --data (or a dependency was skipped); "pack 'x' is disabled in settings" means settings.yaml switched it off.
  • An original file that "is not found" although it is on the disc: the original-data index (vfs::index_files) reaches eight folder levels below the data folder (four before app 0.6.2; the CD's computer-voice clips sit six deep, under Game/ProgramFiles/SoundFX/Chatter/ComputerVoice). A copy nested deeper than that is not indexed.
  • Is my override used? Open the launcher's Asset browser: overridden textures, images and sounds are marked [overridden by <pack>].
  • A key that "does nothing": check the section id prefix (ship: vs object:) and that a later pack does not override it; keys are case-insensitive, values are not.
  • A YAML error such as "tabs are not allowed" or "anchors are not supported" names the line; see the supported subset on Rulesets.
  • A value that "does nothing" may be at the wrong level: {per_level: …} and variants are resolved before typing, so check which difficulty is loaded (the launcher header shows it).

docs.title: Platform layer
docs.text:
src/platform/: the only operating-system-specific code. #[cfg(target_os = "…")] chooses at compile time which implementation is built. Plan: Stage 1 (gamepads); Stage 7 (packaging).

Platform Gamepads Window / GL / audio macOS GameController.framework via the Objective-C shim macos/shim/oi_platform.m macroquad (Cocoa, OpenGL, CoreAudio) Linux kernel joystick API /dev/input/js0, std only (linux.rs) macroquad (X11, OpenGL, ALSA) other none yet (Windows XInput planned) macroquad

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A["app::devices::Devices::read"] --> G["platform::Gamepads::poll"]
    G -->|macOS| M["macos::pad_state(0)<br/>unsafe extern \"C\" oi_pad_state(index, *mut OiPad)"]
    G -->|Linux| J["linux::JoystickReader::poll<br/>non-blocking read of 8-byte js events"]
    M --> P["input::gamepad::PadState"]
    J --> P
  • macOS: build.rs compiles oi_platform.m with xcrun clang and ar (no extra crates) and links GameController and Foundation. The shim reports the first controller with an extended-gamepad profile (Xbox, PlayStation, Switch Pro, MFi) in XInput layout. Adapted from the Looking Glass macOS port's shim (MIT).
  • Linux: the device is opened with O_NONBLOCK; each read applies all pending events (apply_event): buttons 0–10 and axes 0–7 in the common xpad layout, stick Y inverted to XInput's "up is positive", triggers rescaled to 0–255. If no device exists it retries about every two seconds; unplugging drops the device and retries.

docs.title: Presentation: skins, videos and cutscenes
docs.text:
src/app/ui.rs, src/app/video.rs, src/app/cutscene.rs, src/app/comms.rs, with their data in src/content/skin.rs, src/content/cutscene.rs and the voice sets of src/content/rules.rs. Plan: Stage 6.1 (skins, app 0.11.1), 6.8 (title cards), 6.3 (videos, app 0.12.0), MD2 (cutscenes, app 0.13.0), 6.6 (the comms panel, app 0.13.1) and 6.2 (the main menu and credits, src/app/menu.rs, src/app/credits.rs, src/content/front.rs, app 0.14.0), and the widgets and screen layouts (src/app/widgets.rs, src/content/screens.rs, app 0.16.0). Music is on Audio; the Smacker decoder on Formats.

These are application-layer screens and helpers: they read Content and draw with macroquad, and the cutscene player drives a sim::World the same way a flight session does. Nothing in content, sim or formats knows they exist.

docs.title: Skins (app::ui)
docs.text:
Ui::load(&Content) takes rules.skins[0] — rules::build_at has already swapped the skin named by campaign.skin to the front — and loads its panel image (Content::load_image, linear filtering) and its font (Content::read_pack_file → load_ttf_font_from_bytes). A failure of either is printed and left out, so a skin never stops a screen from drawing. With no skins the fallback Skin::fallback() reproduces the colours the screens had before skins.

AppContext::ui holds the result. It is built once at start-up, before content moves into the context, and rebuilt when the launcher switches campaign (Next::Reload). Screens draw through three helpers:

Helper Draws Ui::colour(role) A macroquad Color from the skin's role (background, panel, border, text, dim, accent, highlight; an unknown role gets text). Ui::panel(x, y, w, h) The nine-slice frame, or the panel colour with a border line when the skin has no image. Ui::text(s, x, y, size, role), Ui::text_in(…, Color), Ui::measure(s, size) Text in the skin's font (or the built-in one).

Nine-slice maths is the pure function nine_slice(iw, ih, s, scale, rect) -> Vec<Piece>: the source and destination rectangles of the nine pieces. Corners keep their size (shrunk if the rectangle is smaller than two corners), edges stretch one way, the centre both — tested by app::ui::tests::nine_slices_keep_corners_and_stretch_the_rest.

The launcher and the strategy screen draw through ctx.ui. The strategy screen's title card (StrategyScreen::card, set by Event::Card) is a 70 % × 50 % panel over a dimmed screen: the title in the border colour, the text word-wrapped beneath; Enter, Esc or a click clears it.

docs.title: Videos (app::video)
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant R as app::run
    participant V as VideoPlayer
    participant S as formats::smacker::Smacker
    R->>V: open(&Content, reference, pack).await
    V->>S: Smacker::new(&bytes)
    loop every frame of the file
        V->>S: next_frame() (audio of track 0 kept)
    end
    V->>V: Pcm → WAV bytes → load_sound_from_bytes().await
    loop each app frame (sync)
        R->>V: frame()
        V->>V: due = elapsed / frame_time + 1
        V->>S: rebuild, restore pixels and palette, skip_to(shown), decode up to due
        V->>V: Texture2D::update(rgba), draw letterboxed
    end
    V-->>R: true when ended or skipped

VideoPlayer::open is async: it reads the bytes (Content::read_asset), decodes the whole file once to collect the first audio track's samples, and turns them into a macroquad Sound (which needs .await). VideoPlayer::frame is an ordinary function: it starts the sound on its first call, then shows whatever frame the clock has reached — a slow frame is skipped, the film never slows — so picture and sound stay together. The decoder borrows the file's bytes, so it cannot be stored beside them in the same struct; instead each step rebuilds a Smacker from data, restores the previous frame's pixels and palette, skips to the next frame and decodes forward (Learn Rust › Async).

The picture is scaled to fit the window, centred, on black. Enter, Esc, a left click or a gamepad's Start, A or B skips; at the end (or on a skip) the sound is stopped. The soundtrack plays at 0.9 × the effects volume (VideoPlayer::frame(volume, skip), app 0.14.1). Since app 0.16.2 the player no longer reads the keys itself: app::skip_pressed(ctx) decides for both players — Esc, Enter, a left click, or a pad button newly pressed this frame (raw.pad against raw.pad_previous, so a button held from the menu does not skip at once) — and app::run passes the answer in as skip. open tries the given pack first, then every pack, latest first, for a pack path.

docs.title: Cutscenes (app::cutscene)
docs.text:
flowchart TB
    N["CutscenePlayer::new(ctx, id)<br/>World::new(rules, shapes, starfield_seed)<br/>set_environment"] --> F
    F["frame(): skip_pressed → done<br/>accumulator += frame time"] --> T
    T["tick() at 60 Hz"] --> E1["each entity: spawn at enter (Pilot::External),<br/>remove at leave"]
    E1 --> E2["place on catmull_rom(path, t),<br/>velocity from the path, path_rotation;<br/>fire_beams while firing_until"]
    E2 --> E3["timed actions: FireBeams, Missile (target + fire),<br/>Destroy (combat::apply_damage)"]
    E3 --> E4["sounds due → SoundBank::play_named"]
    E4 --> E5["World::step → Effects::on_events → play_events"]
    E5 --> F
    F --> D["draw: environment sky, Renderer::draw_sky / draw_world / draw_glows,<br/>letterbox bars, captions (ctx.ui)"]

A CutscenePlayer owns its own World (built like a battle's: the rules, collision shapes from the models, the scene's star-field seed as the world's seed, the environment by id) and its own Effects. Every tick each entity that is in the scene is placed on its path rather than flown: position, velocity (from the path one tick ahead), rotation (path_rotation: nose along the path, banked by the sideways acceleration, at most 60°), zero angular velocity and cleared controls. So the scene is deterministic without depending on the flight model; the simulation still moves bolts and missiles, resolves hits and makes the events that drive effects and sounds — which is why a cutscene looks and sounds exactly like a battle.

Timed actions call the battle's code: holding controls.fire_beams, setting a target and controls.fire_missile, or combat::apply_damage with an overwhelming amount after zeroing shields and armour. A harmless entity's ship id goes into World::harmless when it spawns; sim::combat gives its bolts and missiles zero damage (app 0.14.1), so their hits, flashes and sounds still play. The camera at time t is the cut in force (Cutscene::camera_at): a fixed camera on its spline looking at an entity or a point with a level horizon, or an attached camera behind its entity at the keyed distance, rotated by the entity's rotation then the keyed yaw and pitch.

The path maths is pure and in content::cutscene: catmull_rom (centripetal, α = ½, evaluated with the Barry–Goldman pyramid of lerps, clamped at the ends), path_rotation and scalar (linear keys). Tests: catmull_rom_passes_through_keys_without_overshoot, cutscenes_parse_and_check_their_references.

finish clears the sky, planet and nebula it set on the renderer, so the next screen starts clean.

docs.title: The comms panel (app::comms)
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    W["app::flight: a wing order's acknowledge / status,<br/>a wingman lost (down)"] -->|"voice_of_clip(clip)"| SP
    M["MissionRun::voices: (clip, speaker_set)"] -->|"speaker, else voice_of_clip"| SP
    SP["Comms::speak(content, rules, speaker, length, battle time)<br/>first time: load_face"] --> F["Face: Still(texture) | Clip(frames, frame_time) | Signal"]
    SP --> D["Comms::draw(rules, battle time)<br/>top left, until clip length + 0.6 s (≥ 2.5 s)"]

Comms lives on the FlightSession. Every place the flight screen plays a voice clip also calls Comms::speak with the speaker's voice set — a chatter line's speaker (resolved to ChatterDef::speaker_set when the rules load), else the set whose lines contain the clip (Ruleset::voice_of_clip) — and the clip's length (SoundBank::length, which since app 0.13.1 records voice clips as well as music). showing_for(length) is the clip clamped to 0.5 – 30 s plus 0.6 s, at least 2.5 s (3 s when the length is unknown); the time is in battle seconds, so a paused battle keeps the panel up.

A voice's face is loaded the first time it speaks (load_face): a .smk reference is read with Content::read_asset — which since main 319a31b also opens a member of an MPSRC pack, original:<pack>.mps#<member> (Formats › MPSRC) — and every frame becomes a texture, played in a loop from when the voice started; any other reference is a still picture; no face, or a failure (printed once), is the signal graphic. signal_bars(n, t) — a pulse moving across the bars — is pure and tested with showing_for in app::comms::tests::the_panel_lasts_the_clip_and_the_signal_moves. The name is the set's name (else its id) in capitals, or COMMS for a clip with no speaker.

docs.title: Widgets and screen layouts (app::widgets, content::screens)
docs.text:
App 0.16.0, main ac7ae62. The strategy screen is built from immediate-mode widgets: a screen calls widgets::button(ui, input, rect, label, enabled) every frame with where the button is and what it says, and the call draws it and returns whether it was clicked this frame. No widget objects live between frames, so there is nothing to keep in step with the campaign's own state: the rows, labels and enabled flags are recomputed from the campaign each frame. The little state that must persist — a list's scroll position and selected row — is a plain ListView the screen owns. (Learn Rust › Immediate-mode UI explains the pattern and why it suits Rust's borrowing rules.)

Widget What it is Input::read() The frame's mouse position, left click, wheel, Enter and Esc, read once and passed to every widget — so a prompt can hand the screen beneath an empty Input::default() and the screen takes no input. button, button_row, grid A button in the skin's colours (filled with panel, highlight under the mouse, outlined in border, centred text, dim when disabled); a row of buttons of one width; equal cells for a grid of buttons. ListView {first, selected}, fit, scroll, step A list's scroll and selection: step moves the selection and scrolls just enough to keep it in view; scroll moves the view and clamps it to the last screenful; fit pulls both in when the list shrinks. wrap(text, width, measure) Word wrapping by a measuring function (a giant word is cut; newlines kept). modal(ui, input, title, body, buttons) A prompt over a dimmed screen: title, wrapped body, a row of buttons; Enter picks the first, Esc the last.

wrap, ListView, grid and contains are pure and tested (text_wraps_between_words_and_cuts_only_giant_words, lists_keep_the_selection_in_view, grids_and_hits), with a fake 10-pixels-a-character measure so no font or window is needed.

Screen layouts. content::screens::ScreenLayout {id, design, background, widgets, pack} is screens.<id> from the rules. rules::build_at starts from the engine's default_starmap() (1280 × 720: top, map, nav, info, panel) and lets each pack's entry override only the widgets it names (ScreenLayout::parse, which rejects names outside STARMAP_WIDGETS; tested by a_layout_moves_only_what_it_names). Ruleset::screens always holds a starmap. Since app 0.16.2 the strategy screen draws the layout's background over the whole window before the map: the image is loaded on the first frame into StrategyScreen::background: Option<Option<Texture2D>> — the outer Option says "tried yet", the inner "found" — so a missing file is reported once and never retried.

One frame of the strategy screen (StrategyScreen::frame):

flowchart TD
    A["Input::read()"] --> B["layout = rules.screens['starmap']<br/>sx = window w / design w, sy = window h / design h<br/>k = min(sx, sy), at least 0.5"]
    B --> C["draw_map(map rect, zoom, pan)<br/>lanes, systems, contacts, convoys, craft,<br/>selection, hover label, legend"]
    C --> P{"a prompt is up?<br/>card, battle, ending, choice,<br/>offer, convoy, banner"}
    P -- yes --> Q["the widgets get Input::default()<br/>(no clicks reach them)"]
    P -- no --> R["the widgets get this frame's Input"]
    Q --> W["draw_top · draw_nav · draw_info · draw_panel<br/>each returns an Act or a Next when clicked"]
    R --> W
    W --> X["act(Act) → a Campaign order<br/>flash the answer"]
    X --> Y{"prompt?"}
    Y -- yes --> Z["prompts(): widgets::modal → choose,<br/>fly (Next::CampaignBattle), leave"]
    Y -- no --> M["map input: wheel zoom about the cursor,<br/>right/middle drag pan, click → pick()"]
    M --> K["keys(): Space, 1–4, Tab, Up/Down, Enter,<br/>Left/Right, F5, Esc, cheats"]
    K --> T["advance the clock (SPEEDS[speed]);<br/>events → prompts, Next::Video / Cutscene"]
  • Stretch, not fit. A cockpit keeps its proportions and is centred (hud::Layout); a screen scales x and y separately (sx, sy) so its panels reach the window's edges, and sizes text and button heights by k.
  • Map transform. map_transform fits the systems into the map rectangle (tested by the_map_fits_its_rectangle_centred); map_view applies the zoom about the rectangle's centre and the pan in map units. Zooming about the cursor keeps the map point under the cursor fixed: the pan is corrected by the difference between that point before and after the zoom. Zoom is clamped to ×0.5 – ×12.
  • Picking. pick(point, scale, origin, reach) returns the nearest system, detected contact, convoy, survey ship or craft in flight within reach pixels (22 for a click, 18 for the hover label); moving things are favoured by 4 pixels because they are smaller targets.
  • Rows carry their actions. A list row is Row {text, acts: Vec<(&'static str, Act)>}; the first action is the default (Enter, a double click within 0.4 s), and all of them are the buttons under the selected row. The info panel builds its own (label, Act) list for the selection (info()), at most four buttons.

docs.title: The main menu and credits (app::menu, app::credits)
docs.text:
Since app 0.14.0 app::run opens Screen::Menu(MainMenu) instead of the launcher when the campaign has a strategy layer (rules.strategy.is_some()); Next::Menu — from the launcher's Esc, from leaving the strategy screen, from the end of a film or cutscene with no campaign parked, and from the credits — goes there too, or to the launcher for a campaign without one.

  • Data: content::front::MenuDef (campaign.menu: title, subtitle, showcase, starfield_seed, default 7) and CreditsDef (campaign.credits: lines, video), on Ruleset::menu and Ruleset::credits. CreditsDef::roll() is the campaign's lines, two blank lines, then ENGINE_CREDITS.
  • Menu: three pages. The pure functions items(has_save, has_slots) (Continue only with the automatic save; New campaign; Load game only when a numbered slot holds a save, app 0.16.14; then Battles & tools, Options, Credits, Quit) and settings(campaigns, simple_allowed) (Campaign only with more than one, Difficulty, Physics only where Simple is allowed, Music, Effects, Full screen and Controls since app 0.16.14, Back) build the rows. The load page (MainMenu::load: Option<usize>) lists slot 0 (Automatic save) and slots 1 – strategy::SLOTS with menu::age_text(seconds) of each file's modification time (just now, n minutes/hours/days ago) or empty, then Back; Enter on a slot that exists returns Next::LoadSlot { slot }. The slot ages are read from the file system each frame the page is shown (slot_ages). Full screen calls macroquad's set_fullscreen and remember_fullscreen (graphics.fullscreen in settings.yaml); Controls returns Next::Controls, and the controls screen now always returns Next::Menu; step_volume(v, up) moves a volume a quarter and clamps. Items return Next::LoadCampaign, NewCampaign, Launcher, Credits or Quit; a campaign or difficulty change returns Next::Reload, after which app::run reopens the menu on its options page (MainMenu::on_options). Volumes and physics are saved at once (remember_audio, remember_physics). The screen draws the starfield, the showcase ship turning off to the right, the title, and the rows in a skin panel; it keeps the music playing (the first set's menu state, else strategy).
  • Credits: Next::Credits plays credits.video through the video player when there is one, else Screen::Credits: the roll rises from below the screen at a fixed speed (line_y), headings in the skin's accent, and ends when its last line passes the top (finished) or on Esc or Enter. --credits opens on it.
  • Save slots (app 0.16.14): strategy::slot_path(campaign, slot) — slot 0 is the automatic save <user data>/saves/<campaign>.yaml (F5, leaving the map, the ending), slot n is <campaign>-<n>.yaml beside it. The strategy screen's Save button sets StrategyScreen::saving, a modal with Slot 1 – Slot 3 and Cancel; save_slot / load_slot read and write through campaign::save as before, so a slot is an ordinary save.
  • The ending screen (app 0.16.14): while StrategyScreen::ending is set the screen draws, over the darkened map, a panel 70 % of the window with VICTORY (the skin's border colour) or DEFEAT (accent), the ending's text wrapped, and the record — Campaign::date, the score, story.battles_won, bases and craft — with a button_row of Credits (Next::Credits) and Main menu (Next::Menu); Enter and Esc take Main menu. Each saves to slot 0 first.

docs.title: Who plays what: the app's routing
docs.text:
Trigger Path --video <ref> / --cutscene <id> app::run opens Screen::Video / Screen::Cutscene instead of the launcher. A new campaign (Next::NewCampaign) The strategy screen is built and parked in AppContext::campaign; rules.intro plays as a cutscene, else rules.intro_video as a video; otherwise the strategy screen opens at once. A story event's card Event::Card → StrategyScreen::card (drawn by the strategy screen itself). A story event's video / play_cutscene, an ending's video Event::Video / Event::Cutscene / the ending → the strategy screen returns Next::Video / Next::Cutscene; app::run parks the screen in AppContext::campaign and opens the player. An ending reached after a battle is held in StrategyScreen::pending_video and handed over on the next frame. The end of a video or cutscene Back to Next::Strategy when a campaign is parked, else Next::Menu (the launcher before app 0.14.0). A player that fails to open prints the error and returns to the parked campaign.

Music is stopped on every screen except flights and the strategy screen, so videos and cutscenes play without it.
