docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --no-original --cutscene intro plays the default intro on its own; openinterceptor --video original:alientrans1.smk plays one of the player's films. Each returns to the launcher.
  • A cutscene or video that does not start prints cutscene <id>: …, intro: …, video <ref>: … or intro video <ref>: … on standard error, and the game carries on.
  • Cutscene file mistakes are load errors (--check), with the file and key.
  • A skin whose image or font does not load prints skin <id>: panel: … / skin <id>: font: ….
  • A Smacker file that will not decode: run the ignored test against it — OI_SMK=<file> OI_SMK_OUT=/tmp/f.png cargo test --lib real_smacker -- --ignored --nocapture prints its size, frame count, frame time and audio tracks and writes the middle frame.
  • A comms panel showing signal bars instead of a face: the set has no face, or it failed to load (voices.<id>: face … on standard error). COMMS instead of a name: the chatter line has no speaker and its clip is not one of a set's lines.
  • A video pack path not found: open looks in every active pack (latest first, app 0.14.1); the error names the first pack's path.
  • A strategy screen whose panels overlap or leave gaps: a pack's screens.starmap changed design without restating every widget (the rest keep the engine's 1280 × 720 numbers, read in the new space). --check lists the layout errors; there is no on-screen layout editor yet.
  • A button that does not respond: a prompt is up (the screen beneath gets an empty Input), or the button is outside its widget's rectangle on a very small window.
  • A layout background that does not show: standard error has screens.starmap.background <file>: … once (it is loaded on the screen's first frame and not retried).
  • A cutscene caption that shows a key: the key is missing for the language (--check reports text: missing key … (cutscenes/<id>)).

docs.title: Remote console
docs.text:
src/remote/: the tablet control console (interlude item C1, app 0.4.0, main dfff71b; pairing from any screen in 0.4.7, main c42d773; keeping the tablet awake in 0.4.8, main f1c8be8; the two layouts and tiles, C2, in 0.4.11, main db2f264; the target viewport, C3, in 0.4.14, main e51eca9; the map, contacts and events, C4, in 0.4.15, main e2b5012; campaign themes, C2b, in 0.5.0, main 0a1c340). Console items C1 – C4 are complete; only the serial panel (C5) remains. The game serves a web page and a WebSocket to a tablet on the local network; the tablet shows the craft's condition live and sends the pilot's button presses back. Requirements R-CON-009 – R-CON-026; the wire format is the Console protocol; the player's guide is Tablet console.

Everything — HTTP, the WebSocket handshake and frames, SHA-1, base64 and JSON — is written in the crate: no dependency was added (dependency policy). The page in web/console/ is plain HTML, CSS and custom elements, plus a 2 KB video clip, built into the binary with include_bytes! (which embeds a file's bytes at compile time).

remote sits in the application layer: it uses threads and sockets, and reads the world only to describe it. sim knows nothing about it.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    subgraph Tablet["Tablet browser"]
        PG["web/console<br/>All-in-one: oi-telemetry · oi-throttle · oi-actions<br/>Cockpit: oi-hud-strip · oi-shields · oi-display<br/>(oi-target-view · oi-map) · oi-power · oi-tiles"]
    end
    subgraph Threads["Server threads (remote::server)"]
        AC["accept loop<br/>is_local(peer)?"]
        CN["one thread per connection<br/>http::parse_request →<br/>file or ws upgrade;<br/>ws::decode → protocol::decode"]
    end
    subgraph Game["Game loop (app::flight)"]
        CI["app::console_idle<br/>(launcher)"]
        CF["FlightSession::console_frame"]
        RI["remote::RemoteInput"]
        RW["RawInput<br/>remote_held · remote_pressed · remote_throttle"]
        BT["Bindings::translate"]
        W["sim::World"]
        PR["protocol::catalogue · telemetry<br/>contacts · model · theme · event"]
        RU["rules.console<br/>ConsoleTheme::for_cockpit"]
        ML["hud::MessageLog::since"]
    end
    PG -- "GET / · /console.js · /console.css · /keepawake.mp4 (Range)" --> CN
    PG -- "hello · action · throttle<br/>power · target · ping<br/>(masked frames)" --> CN
    AC --> CN
    CN -- "Event (mpsc channel)" --> CF
    CN -- "Event" --> CI
    CI -- "catalogue_idle · telemetry_idle" --> CN
    CN -- "welcome (at once, on the right code)" --> PG
    CF --> RI --> RW --> BT --> W
    W --> PR --> CF
    RU --> PR
    ML --> PR
    CF -- "broadcast / send<br/>(per-client channel)" --> CN
    CN -- "welcome · catalogue · telemetry · denied<br/>theme · model · contacts · event" --> PG

The game loop must never wait on the network, so the server runs on its own threads and talks to the game only through channels (std::sync::mpsc). The game calls ConsoleServer::poll once a frame (it never blocks) and broadcast / send to queue outgoing frames; each connection thread drains its own queue between reads. The only lock guards the short list of connected clients.

docs.title: A connection's life
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant T as Tablet
    participant S as Connection thread
    participant G as Game loop
    T->>S: GET / (HTTP/1.1)
    S->>T: 200 index.html (connection closes)
    T->>S: GET /ws, Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Key
    S->>T: 101 Switching Protocols, Sec-WebSocket-Accept
    T->>S: hello {code}
    alt wrong code
        S->>T: denied (third wrong code: connection closed)
    else right code
        S->>T: welcome {version} (the connection thread, at once)
        S->>G: Event::Paired(id)
        alt launcher (app::console_idle)
            G->>T: catalogue_idle (every action available)
            G->>T: telemetry {alive: false, state: "launcher"} (twice a second)
        else flight (FlightSession::console_frame)
            G->>T: welcome {version, campaign}, catalogue
        end
        loop every frame
            T->>S: action / throttle
            S->>G: Event::Input(id, Inbound)
            G->>T: telemetry (every 0.05 s)
        end
    end
    T--xS: socket closes
    S->>G: Event::Left(id): its held actions are released

docs.title: Pairing on any screen (app 0.4.7)
docs.text:
Before 0.4.7 only FlightSession::console_frame answered Event::Paired, so a tablet paired while the launcher was open waited for ever. Now:

  • the connection thread writes welcome {version} straight onto its own socket the moment the code is right (remote::server::serve), so the page knows it is paired whatever the game is doing;
  • the launcher calls app::console_idle(ctx, "launcher") each frame: on Event::Paired it broadcasts protocol::catalogue_idle() (every action of input::ACTIONS, all available, as there is no craft yet), and twice a second protocol::telemetry_idle("launcher") ({alive: false, state: "launcher"}), counted by AppContext::console_idle_tick. Console input is ignored until a battle starts;
  • in a battle the flight screen still sends welcome {version, campaign} and the real catalogue.

The page (web/console/console.js, OiPairing) pairs as soon as the sixth digit is typed (iPad number pads have no Enter key), shows Connecting… and errors (Could not reach the game, the denied reason, Disconnected), takes ?code=123456 from the address, and switches to the console on welcome rather than catalogue. console.css has [hidden] { display: none !important; }: the custom elements' own display: grid rules had beaten the hidden attribute, so the pairing screen could not hide.

docs.title: Keeping the tablet awake
docs.text:
keepAwake() in console.js (app 0.4.8, R-CON-022):

  1. navigator.wakeLock.request("screen") where the browser allows it. Safari allows it only on secure (https) pages, and the console is plain http on the local network, so on an iPad this usually fails.
  2. Otherwise a hidden <video> (1 px, almost transparent) plays keepawake.mp4 muted, inline (playsinline) and looping: browsers do not let the screen sleep during video playback. iOS allows muted inline playback reliably only after a tap, so it is started from the pairing tap and retried on every pointerdown until it runs.

Both are released by the browser when the page is hidden, so visibilitychange takes them again. The state is shown in the telemetry grid's Tablet cell. The clip (black, 2 KB) is made by tools/console_assets/make_keepawake.swift with AVFoundation — the project's own output, not a third-party file.

iOS Safari fetches video in byte ranges and will not play it from a server that ignores them, so remote::http::file_response answers Range: bytes=a-b, bytes=a- and bytes=-n with 206 Partial Content and a Content-Range header, and every whole-file answer carries Accept-Ranges: bytes. Several ranges at once, or a range outside the file, get the whole file.

docs.title: Press feedback and hit static (app 0.4.9)
docs.text: Every button shows its pressed state — background filled with its border colour, black text — while held, or for at least 150 ms after a tap (R-CON-023). telemetry carries running counts hits and hull_hits for the player's craft; when either rises the page plays about 0.4 s of fading static, stronger for a hull hit (R-CON-024). Counts rather than one-off events mean a dropped or merged telemetry message never loses a hit.

docs.title: Two layouts and tiles (C2, app 0.4.11)
docs.text:
index.html holds both layouts in one page; oi-mode switches between them, remembers the choice per tablet (localStorage) and accepts ?mode= in the address (R-CON-026):

  • All-in-one (#allinone): the C1 elements, oi-telemetry, oi-throttle, oi-actions.
  • Cockpit (#cockpit): oi-hud-strip (the exterior-view HUD figures), oi-shields (shield rings and the balance buttons), oi-display (the display console, with Target and Map tabs), oi-power (beam and shield charge sliders) and oi-tiles (one status card per catalogue group; tapping one opens a full-width strip of its buttons and folds the rest).

Every element listens to the same link event target (one EventTarget that re-dispatches each message by its type), so both layouts stay live and switching costs nothing. The power sliders send power {beam, shield, balance}; the game applies them with sim::systems::set_level and the balance request, within the power budget, and telemetry carries balance.

docs.title: Target viewport (C3, app 0.4.14)
docs.text:
oi-target-view in the Target tab draws the target's model with WebGL 1, written by hand (no library; a 4×4 projection and a quaternion-to-matrix in a few lines, R-CON-015):

  1. Game side. FlightSession::console_frame remembers the class the consoles last received (console_target). When the player's target has another class — or a tablet pairs, which clears it — it loads the class's model (Content::load_model), takes each material group's colour (protocol::average_color of its texture, or the vertex colour if untextured) and builds protocol::model: the most detailed LOD with at most protocol::MODEL_TRIANGLE_BUDGET (3000) triangles, normalised to radius 1, positions rounded to 3 decimals. The text is cached per class in console_models (HashMap<ShipClassId, Rc<String>>), so retargeting a class costs one broadcast.
  2. Page side. Each group becomes a vertex buffer of un-indexed triangles with a face normal per triangle (flat shading). The light comes from the upper left; the model is turned by telemetry.target.rotation, already the target's orientation in the player's body axes, so the page needs nothing else. The clear colour is transparent, so the themed panel shows through.

Textures (app 0.6.7, from the user's playtest). Each textured group is now sent with its image and uvs: the flight screen loads the group's texture, protocol::texture_url shrinks it to at most 128 pixels a side (formats::png::downscale, averaging blocks) and encodes it as an uncompressed PNG (formats::png::encode_rgba) in a base64 data: URL; protocol::model adds texture and uvs (two per vertex) to that group. On the page, each group is a draw range of one vertex buffer ([x y z nx ny nz r g b u v] per corner); a textured group's image is loaded into an Image, redrawn onto a 128 × 128 canvas — WebGL 1 repeats a texture only when its sides are powers of two, and the original models' uvs run past 0..1 — and uploaded with REPEAT wrapping. The fragment shader samples it when textured is set, else uses the group's colour, which also shows until the image has loaded. A model message grows from tens to a few hundred kilobytes, once per class. The ignored helper serve_for_a_browser now sends a checkerboard-textured sample so the image path can be tried in a browser; it was checked in headless Chrome. A video stream of the game's own rendering stays on GitHub issue #3 as a possible later upgrade.

docs.title: Map (C4, app 0.4.15)
docs.text:
R-CON-016, R-CON-014:

  • contacts every 0.2 s (console_contacts_clock): protocol::contacts(&World, player) lists every live craft for which sim::systems::on_radar is true, with relative position and velocity turned into the player's axes by the conjugate of the player's rotation (and z negated so that z is ahead). The id is "slot:generation".
  • event: MessageLog counts every line ever pushed (total); since(seen) returns the lines after a count, as many as are still kept. The flight screen sends each new line as event {text} and remembers console_messages_seen, so no line is sent twice and none is lost between frames.
  • target {id} decodes to Inbound::Target { index, generation }; the flight screen sets the player's target only if that ship still exists and is on the player's radar, so a console cannot target what the pilot could not.

oi-map is a 2D canvas with its own small perspective projection: the player's axes are rotated by the orbit's yaw and pitch, then projected from a camera 2.2 units back (positions scaled by the radar range and the zoom). Per frame it draws range rings at ¼, ½ and 1 × the radar range and spokes on the plane at the player's height, then the contacts sorted far to near, each with a height stalk to that plane, a relation-coloured mark, a label with name and range, and a tick to where it will be in 2 seconds. Presets Behind, Top, Side; pointer drag orbits, two pointers pinch-zoom, the wheel zooms (0.5 × – 8 ×). A pointer-up that moved less than 8 px is a tap, and targets the nearest drawn contact within 28 px. The list beside the map shows the nearest 14 contacts by range; tapping a row targets it. The map skips drawing while its tab is hidden. oi-display also keeps the last four event lines under the target data.

docs.title: Themes (C2b, app 0.5.0)
docs.text:
R-CON-020, R-CON-021:

flowchart LR
    Y["rules/console.yaml<br/>console: {theme, cockpits}"] --> L["content::rules::load<br/>ConsoleTheme {base, cockpits}"]
    L --> B["launcher (app::console_idle):<br/>theme(base) on pairing"]
    L --> F["flight: theme(for_cockpit(class.cockpit))<br/>with every catalogue"]
    B --> P["page: root style.setProperty(--bg …)"]
    F --> P
    P --> C["console.css: var(--line), color-mix(…)"]
  • rules::ConsoleTheme holds the campaign's base ThemeLayer and one layer per cockpit id (lower-cased). ThemeLayer is colors: Vec<(String, [f32; 3])> plus optional font and corner; unknown colour names are load errors listing rules::CONSOLE_COLORS.
  • ConsoleTheme::for_cockpit(Some("A")) clones the base and lays the cockpit's values over it.
  • protocol::theme turns a layer into CSS variables (#rrggbb, --font, --corner in px).
  • The page removes the variables of the previous theme before setting the new ones, so a cockpit without an override returns to the base, and an empty theme to the page's defaults. console.css derives every colour from about nine variables, mixing tints with color-mix(in srgb, var(--line) 25%, var(--panel)), so a pack sets a whole look with a few values.

docs.title: Input path
docs.text:
A console button reaches the simulation the same way a key does:

  1. The connection thread decodes {"type":"action","name":"fire_beams","value":1} into Inbound::Action { action: Action::FireBeams, down: true } (protocol::decode; a name outside input::ACTIONS is refused) and sends Event::Input(id, …) to the game.
  2. RemoteInput::apply keeps held actions (protocol::HELD: turns, slides, afterburner, brake, fire beams, chase camera) in a set per console until the matching value: 0; any other action is a one-frame tap. A throttle message sets a one-frame throttle position.
  3. RemoteInput::merge_into(&mut raw) adds them to this frame's RawInput (remote_held, remote_pressed, remote_throttle) and clears the taps.
  4. Bindings::translate treats remote_held like a held key bound to the action and remote_pressed like a pressed one; remote_throttle sets Controls::throttle_set. From here on nothing knows the input came from a tablet.

Event::Left removes that console's held set, so a tablet that drops off the Wi-Fi in the middle of a turn does not leave the craft turning. Each console has its own held set, so one letting go does not release another's buttons.

docs.title: Safety (R-CON-009)
docs.text:
• Off by default: --console, --console-port N or console: {enabled: true}.
  • Local network only: accept_loop checks every peer with is_local: IPv4 private (10/8, 172.16/12, 192.168/16), link-local (169.254/16) and loopback; IPv6 loopback, unique-local (fc00::/7) and link-local (fe80::/10); IPv4-mapped IPv6 by its IPv4 address. Anything else is dropped without an answer.
  • Pairing: a 6-digit code from the clock at start-up (pairing_code, xorshift). Until a connection sends the right hello, its other messages are ignored; three wrong codes close it. The code only has to be unguessable to someone on the same network who cannot see the screen.
  • Limits: a request head over 16 KB (http::MAX_HEAD) and a WebSocket frame over 64 KB (ws::MAX_FRAME) are protocol errors that end the connection; unmasked client frames and unknown opcodes too. Only the three embedded files are served; any other path is a 404.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is remote::server::ConsoleServer The running server as the game sees it: port, code, url (e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8765), the event receiver and the client list. Dropping it stops the accept loop. remote::server::Event What the server tells the game: Paired(id), Input(id, Inbound), Left(id). remote::server::DEFAULT_PORT 8765. remote::RemoteInput The consoles' input state: held actions per console, this frame's taps and throttle. remote::protocol::Inbound A decoded console message: Hello { code }, Action { action, down }, Throttle(f32), Ping, Power { beam, shield, balance }, Target { index, generation }. remote::protocol::MODEL_TRIANGLE_BUDGET 3000: the most triangles in a model message; the most detailed LOD under it is sent. content::rules::ConsoleTheme, ThemeLayer, CONSOLE_COLORS The console: rules section: the base layer and per-cockpit layers; the nine colour names. hud::MessageLog::total, since Lines pushed in all; the lines after a count. The console's event source. FlightSession::console_target, console_models The target class the consoles have; the cached model messages per class. FlightSession::console_contacts_clock, console_messages_seen The 5 Hz contacts timer; how many log lines were sent as events. remote::protocol::HELD The actions that act while held; every other action is a tap. remote::protocol::VERSION The protocol version sent in welcome (1). remote::ws::Frame, ws::Opcode One WebSocket frame: fin, opcode (Text, Binary, Close, Ping, Pong, Continuation), unmasked payload. remote::http::Request A parsed request head: method, path (no query), lower-cased headers. remote::json::Json A parsed JSON value (Null, Bool, Num, Str, Arr, Obj with key order kept). remote::json::Obj A builder that writes a JSON object straight into a String (the 20 Hz telemetry costs one allocation). AppContext::console, AppContext::remote The server (when on) and the RemoteInput, owned by the app and passed to each screen. FlightSession::console_frame One frame of console work in flight: poll, apply (including target), welcome {version, campaign}, (re)send the catalogue and theme, the target's model, 20 Hz telemetry, 5 Hz contacts, new log lines as events, merge input. app::console_idle One frame of console work outside a battle (the launcher): the idle catalogue on pairing, idle telemetry twice a second; input ignored. AppContext::console_idle_tick The half-second count of the last idle telemetry. remote::server::FILES The embedded page files (&[u8]): index.html, console.js, console.css, keepawake.mp4. Page elements oi-pairing, oi-mode, oi-telemetry, oi-throttle, oi-actions, oi-hud-strip, oi-shields, oi-display, oi-target-view, oi-map, oi-power, oi-tiles, oi-static (web/console/console.js).

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
• Server (remote::server): ConsoleServer::start(port, seed) -> Result<ConsoleServer, String> (binds 0.0.0.0:port; the error names the port and the settings key); poll(&self) -> Vec<Event>; broadcast(&self, text) (every paired console; forgets clients whose thread has ended); send(&self, id, text); paired(&self) -> usize. Helpers: pairing_code(seed) -> String, is_local(IpAddr) -> bool, local_address() -> Option<IpAddr> (asks the OS which interface would route to a documentation address; nothing is sent).
  • Protocol (remote::protocol): decode(text) -> Result<Inbound, String>; catalogue(&Ruleset, &World, ShipId) -> String; catalogue_idle() -> String (every action, all available: no craft yet); telemetry(&World, ShipId, time) -> String; telemetry_idle(screen) -> String ({alive: false, state: screen}); model(name, &Model, colors: &[[f32; 3]]) -> String; average_color(rgba: &[u8]) -> [f32; 3]; contacts(&World, ShipId) -> String; event(text) -> String; theme(&ThemeLayer) -> String; available(&Ruleset, &World, ShipId, Action) -> bool (cloak, ECM, tractor need the system fitted; VCT slides need vct; missiles need missiles aboard; beam actions need beams).
  • WebSocket (remote::ws): sha1(&[u8]) -> [u8; 20], base64(&[u8]) -> String, accept_key(client_key) -> String, decode(&[u8]) -> Result<Option<(Frame, usize)>, String> (Ok(None) = wait for more bytes), encode(Opcode, payload) -> Vec<u8> (unmasked, final).
  • HTTP (remote::http): parse_request(&[u8]) -> Result<Option<(Request, usize)>, String>, Request::header, Request::is_websocket, response(status, content_type, body), file_response(content_type, body, range: Option<&str>) (206 Partial Content for one byte range, else 200 with Accept-Ranges: bytes), upgrade_response(accept), content_type(path).
  • JSON (remote::json): parse(text) -> Result<Json, String> (recursive descent; nesting deeper than 32 levels is an error, so hostile input cannot overflow the stack), Json::get, as_str, as_f64; Obj::new().str(k, v).num(k, v).bool(k, v).nums(k, &[..]).raw(k, json).end(), array(&[String]).
  • Input (remote): RemoteInput::apply(&Event), RemoteInput::merge_into(&mut RawInput).
  • Themes (content::rules): ConsoleTheme::for_cockpit(Option<&str>) -> ThemeLayer; the rules field Ruleset::console.

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Without a tablet: tools/console_client.py (Python standard library only) pairs, prints the catalogue summary (including what is not fitted) and a few telemetry messages, and can send actions:

    target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --console --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet
# in another terminal, with the code the game printed:
tools/console_client.py 127.0.0.1:8765 123456 --tap next_target --hold fire_beams:1.5 --throttle 0.8

    --telemetry N sets how many telemetry lines to print (default 3). denied: wrong pairing code means the code is not the current run's. - The port is in use: start-up prints console: port 8765 is not available (…); set console.port in settings.yaml and the game runs without the console. Find the other program with lsof -i :8765 (macOS/Linux), or set console.port / --console-port. - Wrong code: each wrong hello gets {"type":"denied","reason":"wrong pairing code"}; the third closes the connection (reload the page). The code changes every run; the terminal and the bottom-left hint show the current one. - Refused from outside the local network: a peer that is not private, link-local or loopback is dropped silently, so the browser just reports that the connection closed. A phone on mobile data, a guest Wi-Fi with client isolation, or a VPN that gives the tablet a public-looking address (for example carrier-grade NAT, 100.64/10) are refused by design. Test from the same machine with 127.0.0.1. - The URL shows this-computer: local_address found no route; use the machine's address from the system's network settings. - The page loads but nothing pairs: the WebSocket is opened on the page's own host and port (ws://<host>/ws). Check the browser console; a macOS firewall prompt may need answering. - Buttons do nothing in flight: they act exactly like keys, so whatever stops a key (pause, menu, keys overlay, a dead craft) stops them too. An unavailable action (not fitted) does nothing by design. - Tests: remote::server::serves_the_page_pairs_and_relays_actions_over_a_real_socket runs the whole path over a real localhost socket on a port derived from the process id, and checks that welcome comes from the server at once. - The real page in a browser, without the game: the ignored helper test remote::server::tests::serve_for_a_browser serves the page on 127.0.0.1:8790 (pairing code from seed 7) for 60 s and prints a …/?code=NNNNNN address to open. On pairing it sends the idle catalogue, a sample target model (a wedge) and the default campaign's theme; twice a second a sample in-flight telemetry, four sample contacts and an event, so every panel, the target view and the map have something to show:

    cargo test serve_for_a_browser -- --ignored --nocapture

  • The page waits after the code (before app 0.4.7): pairing from the launcher was never answered; update. If the pairing screen stays on top after Connecting…, check that console.css still has the [hidden] rule.

  • The target view stays empty: the page needs WebGL; check the browser console for webgl errors. A class whose model failed to load sends a model with no groups. With no target, the view is blank by design.
  • The map is empty: contacts lists only craft on the player's radar; check the range rings' scale (range) and zoom out. A tap that does nothing targeted a contact no longer on radar.
  • The theme does not change: the base theme comes on pairing from the launcher; in a battle the cockpit's layer comes with each catalogue (pairing, or a craft of another class). A rules error (an unknown colour name) is reported at load and by --check.
  • The tablet still goes to sleep: look at the Tablet cell. tap the screen to keep it awake means the clip could not start without a gesture: tap once. If it says screen kept awake and the tablet still sleeps, check that /keepawake.mp4 is served with 206 to a Range request (curl -r 0-1 -i http://<address>:8765/keepawake.mp4); as a last resort set the iPad's Auto-Lock to Never.

docs.title: Rendering
docs.text: src/render/: draws one frame of the 3D scene with macroquad. It only reads the simulation. Plan: Stage 1; Stage 2 added looks (model sets with texture swaps), debris sets, effects with shock waves, station modules and their wrecks; app 0.3.1 lighting from the rules (rim light), a brightness gamma, distant dots and viewer-relative bolt streaks; Stage 3 the black hole (app 0.5.1) and the battle environment — terrain, sky dome, distance fog and a planet backdrop (app 0.6.0).

docs.title: Frame structure
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    CL["clear_background<br/>(black, or the sky's horizon colour)"] --> SKY["draw_sky<br/>sky dome (atmosphere), 2 500 stars (dimmed by sky.stars),<br/>planet disc (backdrop), sun<br/>sky material: no depth, additive"]
    SKY --> SOL["draw_world<br/>terrain mesh, black-hole core,<br/>ships, stations, debris<br/>lit material: depth test + write, fog"]
    SOL --> GLO["draw_glows<br/>engines, bolts, missiles, sparks, explosions,<br/>distant dots, black-hole accretion ring<br/>glow material: depth test, no write, additive"]
    GLO --> CP["draw_cockpit_model (3D cockpit, cockpit view only)<br/>flush + clear depth; 5 cm near plane"]
    CP --> HUD["2D HUD (hud::draw)"]

docs.title: Looks: which model to draw
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    SH["ship (class, hull fraction)"] --> MS["ruleset.model_set(class.model_set)"]
    MS --> SW["ModelSet::swaps_for(hull, state)<br/>set swaps → damage levels below → state"]
    SW --> MC["ModelCache::get_variant(intact, pack, scale, swaps)<br/>loaded once per distinct swap list"]
    MC --> DRAW["draw_world"]
    WR["World::wrecks"] --> WS["swaps_for(0, 'destroyed')<br/>placed at hub × offset"] --> DRAW

Renderer::ship_look picks the model a ship shows now: its model set's intact model with the texture swaps for its hull fraction (content::looks::ModelSet::swaps_for). Swaps match the model's textures by looks::texture_key (file name without folder or extension, lower-case). ModelCache::get_variant keys the cache by model, scale and swap list, so each damage level is built once and drawing it per frame costs nothing extra. Destroyed station modules with a destroyed state are drawn from World::wrecks on their hubs. OBJ slot_<name> groups are not part of the drawn mesh at all (the OBJ reader sets them aside as attachment points).

Effects (render::effects). On a Destroyed event, Effects::on_events starts an Explosion with the model set's destroyed_effect (size × radius, duration, colour, and a shock wave — a ring of glows racing outwards in the wreck's plane — when shockwave is set), and throws the debris set: pick distinct pieces chosen with the effects' generator, each starting at its place in the object's model space with the object's velocity plus a random outward push and tumble, plus the generic chunks; wreckage darkens as it cools over its last third and disappears after the set's life. Missile detonations draw the missile's explosion effect (SimEvent::MissileExploded { position, effect }; size in metres), else a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball. Point-defence tracers (SimEvent::PointDefence) are short streaks in the glow pass.

docs.title: The 3D cockpit pass
docs.text:
A cockpit definition may name a model (see Cockpits). It must always appear in front of the world and may sit centimetres from the pilot's eye, which the normal 1 m near plane would clip. So Renderer::draw_cockpit_model:

  1. flushes macroquad's batched draws (InternalGlContext::flush) so the world is on the GPU;
  2. clears only the depth buffer (quad_context.clear(None, Some(1.0), None)) — the world's colour stays, but nothing in it can hide the cockpit;
  3. draws the model with the lit material using SpaceCamera::with_near(0.05), placed at the eye plus ModelOffset (in the eye's frame), always at LOD 0.

This and the model-matrix stack are the only uses of macroquad's internal GL state (unsafe_gl_context, one documented unsafe block).

docs.title: Camera-relative rendering
docs.text: f32 loses precision far from the origin, and GPUs lose more. So no absolute world position reaches the GPU: each object's model matrix is built from position − camera.position (SpaceCamera::model_matrix), and the camera's view matrix is rotation-only (SpaceCamera::view_projection). Near plane 1 m, far plane 200 km.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
Material Shader GPU state Used for lit vertex lighting: ambient + sun × max(n·sun, 0) + rim × edge³ × vertex colour × texture, plus a Tint uniform (hit flash); gamma 1 / brightness in the fragment shader; overlay depth bias depth test ≤, depth write, back faces culled (counter-clockwise = front) ships, stations, debris sky unlit depth always, no write, additive stars, sun glow unlit depth test ≤, no write, SrcAlpha + One engines, bolts, missiles, sparks, explosions

Normals reach the shader through macroquad's spare normal vertex attribute. Per-object transforms use macroquad's model-matrix stack (push_model_matrix), which breaks batches per object and snapshots uniforms per draw call — so the hit Tint is per ship.

docs.title: One-sided faces (back-face culling)
docs.text: Models are one-sided, as in the original game: the lit pipeline sets cull_face: Back with counter-clockwise front faces. The original data winds every polygon counter-clockwise around its outward plane normal, and models a surface seen from both sides as two polygons back to back (shield rings, fins). Without culling both copies drew at the same depth and flickered (z-fighting). Model::from_xmsh mirrors Z and reverses winding, so engine triangles stay counter-clockwise seen from outside; mod OBJ models follow the same rule (Models).

docs.title: Overlay layers and the depth bias
docs.text:
A decal lying exactly on another face (station panels, alien hull markings) has the same depth values as the face under it, so the depth test picks a winner at random per pixel — flicker. At load, model::assign_overlay_layers compares every pair of faces in a LOD: faces in the same plane (normals within 0.999, plane offsets within 1e-4 × radius), facing the same way, that overlap by the separating-axis test get stacked layers. Which is on top: faces flagged POLY_OVERLAY, then POLY_TRANSLUCENT, then ordinary faces; among equals the later face in the file (the original painted in that order). OBJ models use file order only. The pass takes about 8 ms for all 297 CD meshes; 119 of 17,284 LOD-0 faces get a layer above 0.

The layer travels per vertex in the spare w of the normal attribute (ModelVertex::layer). The lit vertex shader does

gl_Position.z -= normal.w * LAYER_BIAS * gl_Position.w;

which moves the face towards the camera in depth only (the image does not shift). LAYER_DEPTH_BIAS = 2⁻¹⁸ in normalised device coordinates, about 32 steps of a 24-bit depth buffer — the same idea as glPolygonOffset, done per vertex because a model is one draw call. Multiplying by w keeps the shift constant after the perspective divide. GLSL cannot read a Rust constant, so lit_vertex_source() pastes the number into the shader text at start-up.

Overlay-flagged faces are kept in their own material groups (MaterialGroup::overlay, GpuLod::overlay), so Renderer::show_overlays = false hides them (the model viewer's O).

docs.title: Texture addressing
docs.text: Original texture coordinates run outside 0..1 to tile a texture across a big face. Model textures are set to repeat (render::set_repeat, via texture_set_wrap on the internal GL context) instead of macroquad's default clamp, which smeared edge pixels across such faces (the "incomplete" Patton, the asteroids, many debris chunks). The UV varying is mediump, not lowp, so tiled coordinates keep their precision on GL ES devices.

docs.title: Lighting, rim and brightness (app 0.3.1)
docs.text: The lit shader's light comes from the Light uniform, a mediump vec4 declared identically in both stages (see Debugging): x = ambient, y = sun, z = rim, w = gamma. Renderer::lighting is the campaign's flight: {lighting: …} (content::rules::Lighting, defaults 0.30 / 0.85 / 0 / 4 px, which reproduce the earlier fixed lighting); the flight screen copies it in each frame. In the vertex shader the model matrix already places the vertex relative to the camera, so its position is also the view ray; edge = 1 − |n·ray| is 1 where a face is seen edge-on, and rim × edge³ lights a thin outline around a hull against black space. Renderer::brightness is the player's graphics.brightness (1 = as authored, clamped 0.25–4 here, 0.5–2 by the settings reader), read at start-up; the fragment shader raises the colour to the power 1 / brightness, which lifts dark tones more than bright ones.

docs.title: Distant dots
docs.text: push_distant_dots (inside draw_glows) draws each ship that is on the player's radar (systems::on_radar, so cloaked ships stay hidden) and smaller on screen than lighting.distant_dot pixels as a glow billboard of that size in its radar colour (hostile, friendly, neutral; the objective colour when protected). The on-screen size is 2 × radius / (distance × metres per pixel), where one pixel covers 2 tan(fov / 2) / screen height metres at unit distance. The dot fades in as the ship shrinks, so there is no pop at the threshold. distant_dot: 0 turns it off.

docs.title: Bolt streaks
docs.text:
A bolt is drawn as a streak trailing behind its head. Bolt::streak_length() is min(muzzle_speed × 0.025 s, 80 m, muzzle_speed × age): never longer than the distance the bolt has flown from the gun. Without the last term, a bolt fired this frame trailed up to 80 m back past the muzzle, so in the chase view fire seemed to come from behind the ship.

The streak points along the bolt's velocity relative to the viewer, bolt.velocity − cam.velocity (SpaceCamera::velocity, set from the player's ship with with_velocity). That is what the eye sees: a bolt from a drifting ship shares the drift, so relative to the pilot it streaks straight out of the guns, while a stationary observer would see it slanted.

docs.title: Battle environments (app 0.6.0)
docs.text:
The flight screen sets Renderer::env_sky and Renderer::planet from the battle's environment before drawing each frame, and clears them after, so the launcher, viewer and other screens still draw plain space. With a sky, the background is cleared to the horizon colour instead of black.

  • Sky dome (draw_sky_dome, drawn first in draw_sky): a dome of 8 rings × 24 segments around the camera, from 30° below the horizon to the zenith, coloured from horizon to top by √max(sin(elevation), 0) — the square root keeps the horizon band narrow. Stars are then drawn with their colour scaled by sky.stars.
  • Planet (draw_planet): a disc facing the camera at 80 % of the sky distance, its radius set by the angular size. Each vertex is shaded as if it were on a sphere (the normal is rebuilt from the disc position), lit by the sun with a darker limb, so one flat mesh reads as a lit globe.
  • Nebula (nebula_sphere, app 0.9.1): a latitude/longitude sphere (24 rings × 48 segments) at 85 % of the sky distance, each vertex coloured and made more or less transparent by Nebula::color(direction) — two fields of smooth 3D value noise (fbm: four octaves of a hashed lattice, smoothstep-interpolated), one for how much cloud and one for its tint between the two colours, stretched back to 0..1 and thresholded so thin areas vanish. The GPU blends between vertices. The mesh is built once per nebula and kept in Renderer::nebula_mesh with the Nebula it was built for; each frame its vectors are moved into a Mesh for draw_mesh and moved back, as the star field does — no per-frame allocation. Stars are dimmed by up to 60 % × density. content::environment::nebula_tests checks the colours stay in range, vary, and repeat for a seed.
  • Terrain (render::terrain::terrain_model): the heightfield becomes an ordinary Model — one vertex per grid point, two triangles per square, wound counter-clockwise seen from above so the fronts face up for back-face culling. Vertex colours run from low to high by height, blended to slope where the normal tips more than about 0.08 from vertical (full at 0.38), with a fixed ±8 % per-vertex variation. It is uploaded once per terrain id through ModelCache::upload_model and kept in Renderer::terrain, then drawn with draw_model like any ship: lit by the sun, depth-tested, fogged.
  • Ground to the horizon (app 0.6.7, from the user's playtest). Past its square the ground continues as mirror-image tiles (Heightfield::fold): tile (i, j) is the field reflected across each odd index, so neighbours meet without seams and height_at — used by collision and the AI — answers everywhere. A tile reflected in X alone cannot be drawn by rotating the normal mesh, so two meshes are uploaded: the field and its X-mirror (terrain_model(def, field, mirror_x), with the triangles' winding swapped so they still face up). A tile reflected in both X and Z is the normal mesh turned 180° about Y; one reflected in Z alone is the mirrored mesh turned 180° (render::terrain::tile_placement). Each frame the renderer draws the tiles within the fog distance × 1.1 (else three field sizes), at most 7 × 7 around the tile under the camera, skipping those whose nearest part is beyond reach. The test tiles_match_the_folded_ground_heights checks every vertex of every placed tile against the folded height.
  • Fog in the lit shader: the vertex stage computes fog = clamp(d / FogDistance.x, 0, 1)² from the camera-relative position; the fragment stage mixes the colour towards FogColor. FogDistance.x = 0 (space) turns it off. See the precision note under Debugging.

docs.title: Black hole
docs.text:
A black hole (World::hazards.black_hole, app 0.5.1) is drawn in two parts: in draw_world a black sphere of the hole's radius that hides the stars and anything behind it, and in draw_glows an accretion ring of 48 additive orange glows at 1.6 – 1.85 × the radius, turning slowly with the battle time and bobbing a little out of plane, with fixed per-glow heat variations.

LOD choice: GpuModel::lod(distance) picks the first LOD whose switch_distance exceeds the camera distance (the original values: e.g. 75 / 150 / 450 m / ∞ for the Lightning II). Objects entirely behind the camera are skipped.

docs.text:
• Renderer::new() -> Result<Renderer, String> (fails only if a shader is rejected).
  • draw_sky(&cam, seed, sun), begin_solid(&cam, sun), draw_model(&cam, &GpuModel, pos, rot, tint), draw_model_lod(.., force_lod: Option<usize>), draw_world(&Content, &World, &Effects, &cam, sun, hide), draw_glows(&Content, &World, &Effects, &cam, hide, player) (player for distant dots), draw_cockpit_model(&cam, &GpuModel, offset, sun), draw_axes, ship_model, ship_look(&Content, &World, &Ship).

docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• Ships too dark or invisible: raise rim or ambient in the campaign's flight.lighting, or graphics.brightness in settings.yaml; dots missing for far ships: check distant_dot is not 0 and that the ship is on the radar (beyond radar_range, or cloaked, it is not).

  • Reused buffers: draw_glows and draw_sky move their Vecs into a Mesh with std::mem::take, draw, then move them back — no allocation after the first frame.

  • If a scene is black except the HUD, check the shader compile error returned by Renderer::new (shown on the start-up error screen).
  • "Shader error" at start-up, program fails to link (fixed in app 0.4.1, main 42716d1): in GLSL ES a uniform declared in both the vertex and the fragment shader must have the same type and precision, or the program does not link. The lit shader's Light uniform is used by both; the vertex shader's default float precision is highp and the fragment shader's precision mediump float makes it mediump there, so a bare uniform vec4 Light; in both had two different precisions. Both now declare uniform mediump vec4 Light;. Some desktop drivers accept the mismatch, so it can pass on one machine and fail on another. The test render::tests::uniforms_shared_by_both_lit_shaders_match_exactly compares every uniform the two lit shaders share and requires an explicit precision, so a new shared uniform cannot reintroduce the problem.
  • Fog distance is computed in the vertex shader (app 0.6.0). Battle distances reach tens of kilometres, and the fragment shader's precision mediump float only guarantees about ±16 384 with a 10-bit mantissa, so d / FogDistance computed there would be coarse or overflow on some GPUs. The vertex stage (highp by default) computes the fog factor, already in 0..1, and passes it down as a mediump varying. Each uniform is declared in one stage only (FogDistance in the vertex shader, FogColor in the fragment shader), which also sidesteps the shared-uniform precision rule above.
  • An atmospheric battle with no visible ground: check the player starts above the terrain's height range, and that fog_distance is not so short that the ground is fogged out; the heightfield is cached per terrain id, so a changed terrain needs a new battle (not a new frame).
  • Engine glows come from rear-facing model attachments, else the back of the bounding box; GpuModel::engines is computed once at load, so drawing glows allocates nothing per frame.
  • A face that vanishes from one side is a back face: wind it the other way, or add a second face back to back if it must be seen from both sides. The viewer's wireframe (W) shows the missing face's outline.
  • Flicker on a flat area means coplanar faces facing the same way that the overlay pass did not pair (they are not in the same plane within tolerance); select them with [ ] in the viewer and compare their layer.
  • Stretched or single-colour faces on original models: check that the texture repeats (the face info line shows UVs beyond 0..1).
  • A 3D cockpit that is invisible usually sits behind the eye: check ModelOffset and that the model's front faces −Z.
  • A damage texture that never appears: the swap's key must be the model's texture name (no folder, no extension); open the class in the model viewer and press D to step through its looks, and --check reports swapped textures that fail to load.
  • Debris that flies from the wrong place was modelled away from the object: pieces must be in the object's own model space. The viewer's debris look pulls them apart from where they sit.

docs.title: Conditions (script)
docs.text: src/script/: the condition language that behaviours (and, from Stage 3, missions and events) use to decide things — hull < 25% and not system_damaged(engines). A complete little language implementation in four classic steps: lexing, recursive-descent parsing, type checking against a schema, and evaluation. Plan: Stage 2 item 2.9 (object context); Stage 3 adds the mission and event contexts and actions. The modder's view is on Behaviours and conditions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    T["condition text<br/>(from a rules file)"] --> L["lex<br/>tokens: Num (units applied),<br/>Name, Sym"]
    L --> P["Parser (recursive descent)<br/>or → and → not → comparison<br/>→ sum → term → unary → primary"]
    S["Schema<br/>queries (QueryDef) +<br/>constants (level names)"] --> P
    P -->|"type-checked at load"| E["Expr tree<br/>(queries by index)"]
    E --> EV["Expr::eval / test<br/>at run time"]
    CX["Context::query(id, args)<br/>sim::ai::ObjectContext"] --> EV
  • Lexing (lex): whitespace-separated numbers, names and symbols. A unit written straight after a number is applied at once (1.5km → 1500, 25% → 0.25; m, km, s, min, h, day, %). Names are lower-cased.
  • Parsing (Parser): one method per precedence level, lowest first — or, and, not, comparison (< <= > >= == !=, not chained), sum (+ -), term (* /), unary (-), primary (number, true/false, constant, query with arguments, brackets). Each method returns the sub-tree and its type (Num or Bool).
  • Checking happens while parsing, against the Schema: unknown names, wrong argument counts or kinds (system_damaged(warp)), and type errors (hull and 3, a comparison of booleans) are errors with a message; parse_condition also requires the whole expression to be true/false. Behaviours call it when the rules load, so a bad condition never reaches play.
  • Evaluation (Expr::eval) walks the tree. and/or short-circuit; == and != compare within 1e-6; division by zero gives 0. Queries are answered by a Context; arguments are evaluated first and passed as numbers (a name argument such as engines is resolved to its index while parsing).

There is no assignment, loop or user function, so evaluation cannot change the game and always finishes. random(p) draws from the asking pilot's seeded generator, so runs are deterministic.

docs.title: The object context
docs.text: script::object declares the queries a behaviour may use (QUERIES, with doc strings that the docs table is made from) and schema(levels) adds the campaign's difficulty level ids as numeric constants. sim::ai::ObjectContext implements Context for one ship: it holds &World, the ship's id, the time in its current state and the pilot's random state in a Cell<u64> — Context::query takes &self, but random must advance the generator, and a Cell allows that for a Copy value without &mut (interior mutability).

docs.title: The campaign context (app 0.6.7)
docs.text:
script::campaign declares the strategy layer's 16 queries (research, researching, has, module_count, bases, money, day, month, difficulty, pilots, score, month_score, random, flag, salvaged, craft; ids in campaign::id). campaign::schema(names, levels) makes every id the campaign's data defines a constant — its index in StrategyDef::names — so a topic, item or module is passed as a bare word (research(heat_rays) compiles to query 0 with that index) and a misspelt name is a load error. Difficulty level ids are constants too, unless an id already has that name. The context is answered by campaign::Campaign (Campaign). Time quantities accept d (days) since app 0.6.7, for every: 30d.

The story added five queries in app 0.10.0 (arc, plan, relation, fired, battles_won) and logistics eight in app 0.16.3 (deposit, feature, research_site, survey_known, owned, lane_distance, facility_progress, construction_attacks; ids 21 – 28, R-MOD-014): 29 in all. A logistics query's arguments are names like any other — the map's system ids and their feature tags, resource, component, facility-type and research-site ids were added to StrategyDef::names for them — and its first argument is always a system. Arg::Num carries the constant's index; the campaign looks the name up again (Campaign::logistics_query), so a name that is not a system answers 0 instead of failing.

docs.title: The condition console (app 0.16.5)
docs.text: The testbed's backquote console evaluates typed text in the battle context: MissionRun::evaluate(&World, text, levels) builds battle::schema from the mission's own role names and the difficulty levels, parses, and evaluates against a BattleCx whose generator is a Cell copy of the mission's (Cell::new(self.rng)), so random(p) reads the dice without moving them — looking never changes the battle (unit-tested). The value comes back as text; a parse error as the Err string the flight screen shows in orange.

docs.title: Key Symbols
docs.text: Symbol What it is Token Num(f32), Name(String), Sym(&'static str). Expr Num, Bool, Query(u16, Vec<Expr>), Not, Neg, Binary(Op, …). Op Or, And, Lt, Le, Gt, Ge, Eq, Ne, Add, Sub, Mul, Div. Type, Value Num / Bool at check time; Value::Num(f32) / Value::Bool(bool) at run time. QueryDef, Arg A query: name, args (Arg::Num or Arg::Name(&[..])), result type, doc. Schema The queries and named constants available in one context. Context The trait a game context implements: query(id, &[f32]) -> Value. object::QUERIES, object::id, object::SYSTEM_NAMES, object::schema The object context (21 queries). campaign::QUERIES, campaign::id, campaign::schema The campaign context (16 queries in app 0.6.7; 29 since app 0.16.3). mission::MissionRun::evaluate The condition console's evaluation (app 0.16.5). sim::ai::ObjectContext The simulation's answer to object queries.
