docs.title: Debugging
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --data <cd> --scenario flight-test --ship firestar --view chase jumps straight into a scenario; add --campaign default (or interceptor) to pick the campaign.
  • openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --screenshot shot.png saves the cockpit view after 120 frames. The window opens at 1280×960 (4:3), so this shows the widened 3D-cockpit field of view; compare with a manual run in a 16:9 window (MT-2-14).
  • Scenario errors (unknown class, faction or leader) are shown in orange on the launcher and printed to standard error.
  • openinterceptor --campaign default --soak rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --difficulty cadet plays the scenario headless and prints the player's fate (src/soak.rs): how long a passive ship survives, or whether an AI-flown one wins (--soak-pilot ai), per difficulty level. --soak-pilot idle leaves the player's craft sitting still: in a defence mission it measures how long the defended object holds on its own (SoakPilot::Idle).
  • A layout saved by F12 that seems ignored: the addon targets the campaign that was loaded when it was saved; check --list shows <campaign>-cockpit-<id> and that it is not disabled.
  • A simulator row that does nothing: the campaign has no asteroid class (no id containing asteroid) or no kind: mine class; the row says "(none in this campaign)". A Fly that does nothing: read the orange line under the rows (a ship that cannot enter an atmosphere).
  • openinterceptor --mission defend_station --ship comet starts a mission directly; --soak defend_station --soak-pilot ai --seconds 400 plays it headless and prints the result.
  • In any mission battle press ` to type a condition and see its value (app 0.16.5); the battle waits.
  • openinterceptor --no-original --strategy --chapter 6 opens the default campaign at chapter 6; Ctrl+D on the strategy screen shows the story's state and fires events (app 0.16.13).

docs.title: Packaging
docs.text:
Game data is never inside a build

The app contains the engine, the default campaign (resources/default) and the bundled mods (packs/), none of which hold original content. The player's original data (an installed copy or the CD), settings and mods live in the user data folder; the checkout's resources/xcom* folders are never copied into the app.

docs.title: Plain build
docs.text: cargo build --release produces target/release/openinterceptor. It finds the original data automatically (Settings and data discovery).

docs.title: macOS app
docs.text:
python3 tools/build_bundle.py                    # app + settings.yaml pointing at ./resources/xcom(-cd)
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --data /Volumes/CD # settings point at another copy
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --install-data     # clone the data into <user data>/original
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --no-settings      # leave settings.yaml alone
python3 tools/build_bundle.py --skip-build       # reuse the last release build

tools/build_bundle.py (standard-library Python) builds the release binary, assembles dist/OpenInterceptor-<version>.app (dist/ is git-ignored), and signs it ad hoc:

OpenInterceptor-0.4.2.app/Contents/
  Info.plist                   identifier io.github.bbogovich.openinterceptor, version, game category
  MacOS/openinterceptor        (the console page is built into the binary)
  Resources/resources/default/ the default campaign
  Resources/packs/             the bundled mods (interceptor)
  Resources/LICENSE            the MIT licence

Then it prepares the user data folder ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/: settings.yaml paths.original is set to the checkout's resources/xcom/ if it holds files, else resources/xcom-cd/ (or --data), keeping any other settings; --install-data instead clones that data into original/ (an APFS clone costs almost no disk) and points the settings there; mods/ is created. The program finds ../Resources/resources and ../Resources/packs relative to the executable, so it works when Finder starts it with / as the working directory (verified at app 0.3.x with the old layout: the bundled binary run from / loaded both packs and the CD, --check 0 errors; to re-verify with resources/ in MT-1-30).

docs.title: Build numbers
docs.text:
Like ArenaVM's per-phase apps, versions follow the implementation stages: 0.<stage + 1>.<build>. The version is Cargo.toml's; bump the last number for each new build of a stage. From Stage 2 on, a stage's in-progress deliveries continue the previous stage's numbering and the stage's own 0.<stage + 1>.0 marks it complete: the first Stage 2 delivery is 0.2.2, and 0.3.0 marks Stage 2 complete (it also carries Stage 3 part 1). The Stage 3 interlude departs from this: its console delivery took 0.4.0 although Stage 3 is not complete, so 0.4.x builds are Stage 3 work in progress (see the implementation status).

Stage Versions Builds 0 Foundation 0.1.x (no app; analysis, formats, docs) 1 Flight simulator 0.2.x 0.2.0 — first app: newtonian flight, overrides, --extract, HD/3D cockpits, asset browser; 0.2.1 — mesh rendering fixes (tiled textures, back-face culling, overlay layers), viewer mesh tools and --model, bolt streaks, radar alignment 2 Combat, objects and behaviours 0.3.x 0.2.2 — mod kinds and campaign choice, ship systems, power, damage and repair, tractor, cloak, ECM, hyperspace, wingman orders, controls menu and gamepad chords, power/systems instruments, default campaign Perils of the Void, --screenshot, then YAML mod files, behaviours, looks, guidance, modules, probes, text keys; 0.3.0 — Stage 2 complete, plus Stage 3 part 1 (missions) 3 Missions, environments and conditions 0.4.x part 1 shipped in 0.3.0; 0.3.1 — interlude playtest fixes: shot physics, drift readout and flight-path marker, lighting and brightness, the killed result, keys overlay; 0.4.0 — tablet console C1 (in-crate HTTP/WebSocket server, protocol v1, pairing, telemetry, console actions); 0.4.1 — lit shader link fix (Light uniform precision); 0.4.2 — resources/ layout (resources/default, resources/xcom, resources/xcom-cd) 4 Strategy layer 0.5.x — 5 Campaigns 0.6.x — 6 Presentation 0.7.x — 7 Modding toolkit and Remastered 0.8.x — 8 Platforms and release 1.0.0 —

docs.title: Linux (Stage 8)
docs.text: A tarball with the binary, resources/default, packs/ and a .desktop file. AppImage is under consideration.

docs.title: Windows
docs.text: Kept buildable; gamepad (XInput) and packaging are planned for Stage 8.

docs.title: Toolchain
docs.text: Tool Version Notes Rust ≥ 1.86 (rust-version in Cargo.toml) Checked with 1.99 stable. Install with rustup. macOS 11+ on Apple silicon Xcode command line tools: build.rs compiles the gamepad shim with xcrun clang. Linux any with OpenGL 3 + X11 Packages for miniquad: libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev (Debian/Ubuntu names); libasound2-dev for audio. Python 3 for the docs site only ./docs.sh creates its own .venv.

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: Three crates, pinned exactly: macroquad =0.4.14 with the audio feature (the version ArenaVM and Looking Glass use), plus glam =0.27.0 and image =0.24.9 (png), both already part of macroquad's tree. Everything else is in the crate. See the dependency policy.

docs.title: Layout of a checkout
docs.text:
OpenInterceptor/
  Cargo.toml  Cargo.lock  build.rs
  src/                 the engine (see Architecture)
  resources/default/   the default campaign, Perils of the Void: everything the game
                       ships, in editable formats (YAML, OBJ, PNG, WAV)
  resources/xcom/      your installed copy of Interceptor (optional, git-ignored)
  resources/xcom-cd/   your CD copy (optional, git-ignored)
  packs/interceptor/   bundled mod: rules + scenarios binding the original data
  web/console/         the tablet console page (embedded in the binary)
  tools/               default_assets/ (generates the default campaign's models, textures
                       and sounds into resources/default:
                       python3 tools/default_assets/make_all.py [--check]),
                       build_bundle.py (macOS app bundle),
                       console_client.py (console test client)
  macos/shim/          the Objective-C gamepad shim (oi_platform.m)
  CLAUDE.md            project rules (objectives, no original content, quality bar)
  rustfmt.toml         formatting (width 120)
  scripts/check.sh     the quality gate
  engine-docs/         worktree of the docs branch (git-ignored on main)

docs.title: Day to day
docs.text:
cargo run --release                         # launcher (original data found in resources/xcom*)
cargo test                                  # unit tests
cargo clippy --all-targets                  # lints (kept at zero warnings)
cargo fmt                                   # formatting
scripts/check.sh                            # everything the gate runs
cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu   # type-check the Linux paths from macOS

The gate (scripts/check.sh) runs the original-data checks on OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA if set, else on the first of resources/xcom/ and resources/xcom-cd/ that holds files, and skips them when there is none. It fails if any file under resources/xcom* (or the old game/) is tracked by Git. A checkout from before app 0.4.2 that kept its data in game/ should move it to resources/xcom-cd/ (a CD copy) or resources/xcom/ (an installed copy).

docs.title: Deviations
docs.text:
Where OpenInterceptor knowingly differs from the original game, or uses an engine value where the original's is unknown, and why. A deviation on the record is a decision; an undocumented one looks like a bug.

ID Deviation Why Stage DEV-001 Default keys for actions the original left undocumented: M match speed, W cycle missile, Kp4/6/8/2 VCT slides, Q/E roll, LeftControl also fires beams, C mouse flight. These actions exist in the original's bindable list but their release defaults are not documented anywhere found; Q/E and LeftControl help keyboards without a keypad. 1 DEV-002 Navigation points in scenarios (nav: {<name>: …}), cycled with N, shown on the MFD Nav page and as an on-screen marker. The original has no in-mission nav points (travel happens on the strategy map). Mods need them; the test arenas use them to find the alien and pirate groups. 1 DEV-003 Gamepad support with an XInput-style layout. The original supported DirectInput joysticks and rudders only. 1 DEV-004 Mouse controls are rebindable (beams/missile via the bindings; steering range via mouse_range in bindings.yaml) and mouse flight is a toggle (C). The original fixed them; a toggle avoids the mouse fighting the menus. Steering direction follows the readme (cursor down = nose down). 1 DEV-005 Hardware 3D with per-vertex lighting instead of the 16 shade palettes. The shade palettes served the 1998 software renderer; palette 0 (full brightness) gives the texture colours. 1 DEV-006 Wide-screen: a cockpit's design space (640×480 for the originals) is scaled as large as fits and centred; the 3D view fills the window. Cockpits may declare their own design (e.g. 1920×1080) and may be 3D models. Modern displays are not 4:3; modders replace cockpits with HD, widescreen or 3D ones. 1 DEV-007 Multiplayer deferred, possibly never implemented. Not needed for single player or modding. 7 DEV-008 Original beam Range read as kilometres (Range=4 in GameSettings.ini → 4 000 m, when inherited through inherit: original:…). Since mod format 2 a mod's range takes a unit (2.4km, 350m; a plain number is metres), replacing the Stage 1 RangeMetres key. The original's 1–6 values have no documented unit; kilometres matches the documented sensor ranges (3–5 km). 1 DEV-009 Missile TurnRate and LockTime are engine values set in the Interceptor pack. The original stores no turn rate per missile; lock time depends on the targeting system (Stage 4 equipment). 1 DEV-010 Proximity fuse fires on a near miss: inside ProximityRadius and moving away from the target. A hit inside the target's collision shape deals ImpactDamage. Firing as soon as the radius was entered meant impacts never happened. 1 DEV-011 Hull Shields, Armor, Energy, EnergyRecharge, Acceleration are engine values per hull in the Interceptor pack. In the original they come from fitted equipment (ShieldType, ArmorType, EngineType*), which arrives with the equipment system. 1 → 4 DEV-012 Alien, freighter and capital flight values are estimates (MaxSpeed, turn rates, acceleration). The original file has flight values only for the three X-COM hulls; the others were coded per class. 1 → 2 DEV-013 Missile lock cone is 10° (flight.lock_angle). The original's SensorsSetting LockAngle units are not decoded. 1 DEV-014 Cockpit ↔ hull mapping A = Lightning II, B = Firestar, C = Super Avenger. Derived (one cockpit per hull), not confirmed. 1 DEV-015 One-shot inputs are carried across frames that run no simulation tick (Controls::carry_unconsumed). On high-refresh displays some frames run no tick; a key press would otherwise be lost. Not an original behaviour, an engine correctness fix. 1 DEV-016 Esc opens a pause menu (resume, restart, back to launcher) instead of resetting the MFD. The testbed needs a way back to the launcher; MFD pages cycle with </>. 1 DEV-017 Keyed cockpit pixels become transparent black, not transparent cyan. Filtering would otherwise blend cyan into the edges of the art. Visual result matches the original. 1 DEV-018 ~~"Ignore my target" and "retreat" wingman orders both mean "form on me"; "evasive" is not bound.~~ Resolved in Stage 2: every wingman order has its own behaviour (formation, attack my target, fire at will, 10 s evasive weave, retreat and hyperspace out) and evasive is bound (Shift+E). Distinct behaviours arrived with the Stage 2 AI. 1 → 2 DEV-019 Newtonian flight model by default: throttle is thrust, ships coast at zero throttle, Z reverses thrust, a held brake (B) retro-thrusts to a stop, MaxSpeed caps speed, turning does not steer the velocity. flight: {model: assisted} restores the arcade model (throttle = target speed, automatic slowing, drift damped). The original's flight model is not documented and felt arcade-like; the project owner chose physics where deceleration only comes from thrust. Keeping both as data lets each campaign choose. 1 DEV-020 Flight computer (speed hold): match speed (M) and every AI pilot fly a held forward speed through hold_speed, which thrusts and brakes within the hull's own acceleration and also cancels sideways drift. Under newtonian physics AI pilots need a way to manage speed that obeys the same limits as the player; cancelling drift keeps AI dogfights readable. 1 → 2 DEV-021 Arena edge: ships reaching flight.arena_radius (default 60 km) are halted against it ("ARENA BOUNDARY"). Under newtonian physics a coasting ship would otherwise drift away for ever; outside testing this should rarely be reached. 1 DEV-023 Overlay polygons are depth-biased instead of drawn in BSP order; coplanar overlapping faces are found geometrically, the original overlay flag only decides which is on top. Translucent-flagged polygons are drawn opaque for now. A depth-buffered renderer cannot use painter's order per model; the same pass then also serves mod OBJ decals, which have no flag. The opacity meaning of the flag is not confirmed. 1 DEV-022 Per-asset overrides and --extract: any original model, texture, image or sound is replaced by a pack file at its override path; the extractor writes every original asset at those paths in OBJ/PNG/WAV. The modding objective: HD and 3D replacements without touching or redistributing the originals (compare XWVM, Modding). 1 DEV-024 Power budget and start levels are engine values: the beam and shield charge settings plus switched-on equipment share power.budget: 6 steps; ships start at beam D / shield C (interceptor) or C / C (default); tractor, cloak and ECM use 2, 3 and 1 steps. The original's charge-rate tables are verified (BeamRechargeRate, ShieldRechargeRate), but how many levels may be high at once and what equipment costs is not in the data (derived). All are power / systems data. 2 DEV-025 Firing drops the cloak (beams or a missile), with the message "CLOAK DROPPED". Prevents an invisible ship from attacking with impunity; the original's exact rule is unknown. Cloak lock-break by difficulty level waits for 2.8. 2 DEV-026 Hyperspace countdown of flight.hyperspace_time seconds (10 in interceptor, 8 in default), doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged; pressing H again aborts. The original's countdown length is not documented (derived). 2 DEV-027 Default keys for tractor, cloak and ECM: Shift+T, Shift+C, Shift+J. The original's key list has no documented default for these; Shift chords keep the plain T, C and J free. Rebindable in the controls menu. 2 DEV-028 Gamepad modifier layer: holding the left shoulder (LeftShoulder) switches the pad to a second layer (LeftShoulder+A hyperspace, LeftShoulder+DpadUp power to beams, …); a button used as a modifier does nothing on its own. A controller has far fewer buttons than the keyboard has keys; chords make every action reachable from the pad (extends DEV-003). 2 DEV-029 System condition thresholds: above half its hit points a system works fully, at half or below at half effect, at zero it stops until repaired back to 25 %, below −destroy_below × hit_points (−50 %) it is destroyed for the battle. Repair takes the worst system first. The original shows damaged / inoperative / destroyed systems and repairs them, but its thresholds and repair order are not in the data (derived). Thresholds below zero and the repair rate are damage data. 2 DEV-030 Mod files are a strict subset of YAML, read by an in-crate reader (formats::yaml): no tabs, anchors (&a), aliases (*a), tags (!!str), multiple documents, complex keys (?) or plain scalars continued over several lines — each rejected with its line number. Every scalar stays text until the schema types it. Mod files moved from INI (format 1, no longer read) to YAML (format 2). YAML gives modders nesting, lists and comments that INI lacked, and is what OpenXcom modders know. A full YAML library was not taken: the project's dependency policy avoids dependencies for what the codebase can do, serde_yaml is unmaintained, and full YAML's implicit typing (no → false, 1.10 → 1.1) and anchors surprise modders. The subset covers every construct the mod files need; the original game's own INI files are still read as INI. 2 DEV-031 AI skill model: enemies aim with an error of up to (1 − aim) × 8°, re-picked every reaction seconds, fire in burst/pause cycles inside a fire_cone, and check behaviour transitions 4 times a second. The original's AI is hard-coded and its accuracy model unknown; this model is data, so each campaign tunes it per difficulty level. 2 DEV-032 Interceptor enemy behaviours and per-level values are derived (Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm, Shade, Harbinger, drones, pirates, corporates, X-COM wingmen; skill, bursts, missile intervals and flee thresholds for beginner … superhuman). The original's AI code is not data; the behaviours follow the strategy guide's descriptions of each class and were tuned in the testbed (and with --soak). What each original difficulty level changes in combat is unknown. 2 DEV-033 3D cockpit instruments drawn in perspective on the dashboard (anchors) and an in-game cockpit layout editor (F12) that saves an addon. Engine extensions for modding: the original has only 2D cockpits. XWVM's 3D cockpits show instruments on in-cockpit screens the same way. 2 DEV-034 Explosions are engine fireballs (size, duration, colour, optional shock-wave ring per effect) instead of the original's XSPT sprite animations; which original wreck set each class uses follows the set names. XSPT pixel runs are not decoded yet; the 28 wreck sets' names and chunk meshes are verified from Interceptor.exe, the class mapping is derived. Effects are data, so sprite explosions can replace the fireballs later without rule changes. 2 DEV-035 Module placement on the original bases is derived: which of the X-COM base's 33 and the alien base's 28 attachment points carries a turret, shield generator, hangar or pod. Hit points come from the original M_XCOM* / M_ALIEN* sections (verified); a station's shields fail once all its shield-generator modules are destroyed, and destroying the hub destroys its modules. The original assembles bases on the strategy layer (Stage 4), so their battle layout is not stored; the shield and cascade rules follow the strategy guide's descriptions (derived). Placement is modules: [{slot, class}] data. 2 DEV-036 Special missile behaviours are engine models of the original's descriptions: Sidestep turns twice as hard inside 600 m and weaves; Parallax decoys lure at 80 % per second within 2.5 km; Passive Cloaking waits for prey within 800 m; Doppelganger copies are fragile and short-lived; mines blast four times their fuse radius. The original's guidance code is not data; names and one-line descriptions are all that is known (derived). Every number is a missile key or an engine constant documented on Missiles and mines. 2 DEV-037 Shield rings on the radar scopes (front scope = fore shield, rear = aft; green / amber / red, blinking when down), top-bar text placement in the interceptor cockpits (message in the lit band, throttle line, power and systems in the two strips below), and since app 0.15.1 the ship status display (ship_status): the craft from above tinted by hull, inside fore and aft arcs of up to three shield bands each, in the round ship display of cockpits A, B and C. The rectangles are measured from the cockpit art (verified pixel bounds); what the original showed in each strip and the ring thresholds are derived from the player's description of the original HUD. The ship status display is a user request after a playtest (the round display showed nothing): its look follows X-Wing's shield display, not the original's (what the original drew there is unknown), and its rectangles in A, B and C were placed by eye (derived). 2, 6 DEV-038 Point-defence data is derived: which ships carry point defence (the Patton, the X-COM freighter, the bases; the dreadnought and the stations) and its numbers (range 900 m–1.2 km, 3–4 shots/s, 35–40 % kill chance, 3–4 energy per shot). Point defence also shoots at decoys. The original's point-defence behaviour is not data; the values are engine estimates tuned in the testbed. All are point_defence keys. 2 DEV-039 Probes act in battle: a sensor probe extends its side's radar to 8 km around it; an ECM / jamming probe halves hostile radar range and missile-lock speed within 2.5 km. The original launches probes from the strategy map; their battle effects and numbers are derived (mesh names SENSPROB, ECMPROB verified). Data: probe: {sensors, jamming}. 2 DEV-040 Mission arrivals belong to the role (at: {distance, bearing, from, spread} and arrive: <condition>) instead of a separate arrivals: map as first designed. One place per group keeps a role's composition, position and timing together; a role without arrive: enters at the start. Waves add members later. 3 DEV-041 Interceptor mission compositions are derived: the five implemented mission types (xcom_base_defense, defend_freighter_convoy, deep_space_encounter, attack_alien_outpost, destroy_alien_probe) use the original's own names, briefings and debriefs by key (@orig.*, read from the CD), but which classes appear, how many, where and in what waves are estimates, sized early-war so every level is winnable and losable (checked with --soak). The original composes battles in code and grows them with campaign progress (Stage 4); compositions are missions: data. %s in original briefings awaits the strategy layer. 3 DEV-042 Process: Rapid Prototyping run as an implementation project. The project follows the Rapid Prototyping workflow (SpecItOut proposal P65), but until sio supports a prototype kind the manifest declares kind: implementation, with spec pointing at this worktree's docs/specification (Definition and Specification 1.0.0). The sio client does not yet support the prototype kind; the implementation kind lets issues cite requirement IDs now. Process DEV-043 Interceptor shots use plain physics (flight: {bolt_frame: world}): a bolt leaves with the ship's velocity plus the muzzle's turn velocity plus its muzzle speed, then flies straight. Engine value: how the original moves its shots has not been observed side by side; physics is the default by decision D1 (R-CMB-021). bolt_frame: ship is the arcade alternative, one rules line away. 3 DEV-044 Interceptor lighting adds a rim light and distant dots (flight: {lighting: {ambient: 0.30, sun: 0.85, rim: 0.35, distant_dot: 4}}): hulls seen edge-on are outlined, and craft smaller than 4 px on screen that are on the radar are drawn as a dot in their radar colour. An engine choice for visibility (F-HUD-007: "it is difficult to see other fighters"). Ambient and sun match the engine's earlier fixed lighting; the original's look is otherwise unchanged and the keys are data. 3 DEV-045 Interceptor hazards are engine models with derived numbers: the black hole pulls with 1/d² (pull at 1 km, capped at 20 ×) and destroys craft inside its radius; the ion storm keeps a fraction of radar range and halves lock speed; asteroid fields are scattered, slowly turning objects. The interceptor testbed scenarios use pull: 12, radius: 450 and sensors: 40%. The original's belt and black-hole battles are built in code; their pull law, numbers and sensor effects have not been measured. All are hazards: data (R-MSN-009). 3 DEV-046 The strategy format as built is a simpler subset of its design: one start: section instead of starts; base_types.max_distance (map units) instead of a placement expression; plain numbers for upkeep, maintenance, salary and costs (only incomes, expenses, the research rate and prerequisites are expressions); raids: with fixed missions instead of squadrons, flight plans and generated missions; pilot ranks by experience thresholds; fitting is best available from the store (app 0.7.2) without fitting rules. Stage 4 first makes every rule playable end to end with the default campaign; the richer keys of Format: strategy layer are added when the interceptor strategy data (4.12) and logistics (4.14 – 4.17) need them. 4 DEV-047 The default campaign's strategy texts are plain English in resources/default/strategy/*.yaml, not text keys. The strategy layer was written ahead of its translation; moving the names and descriptions to text/en/ keys is a data change for a later pass (R-STR-010 Open note). 4 DEV-048 A battle runs on after its result: the verdict and computer voice come at once, and the debrief waits flight.debrief_delay (30 s by default; Enter skips it; a retreat shows it at once). User request (playtest, app 0.7.4): to watch the final explosion. An engine choice: the original's own timing is not measured here (unknown); the delay is rules data, so a campaign can set 0s. 3 DEV-049 Logistics as built simplifies its design: facility placement is a fixed rule per role (mining: a surveyed system with deposits; research: a surveyed research site; manufacturing: at most two lanes from a base; one facility of each type per system) instead of the design's placement: expressions; the nearest supplier is measured in a straight line between systems, not by lane (R-STR-013); convoy ambushes are auto-resolved as per-vessel losses (since app 0.9.2 only when the campaign has no logistics.ambush_mission or the player declines to fly the escort), and an attacked survey ship is lost on a fixed 50 % roll, instead of generating battles; storage limits only mining facilities. App 0.9.0 (ff9d8fc): the smallest version of the design that plays the whole chain. Expressions over the campaign context and flown ambushes (convoy_ambush exists) are the next steps; the survey loss chance should become data. Default campaign only; the interceptor campaign has no logistics. 4 DEV-050 The interceptor strategy layer's estimates are derived: the start (date, pilots, craft, stock), the generated map's number of systems, delivery and salvage, hull speeds, missile rounds, module groups and effects, the X-COM base type's cost and hub sensor range, corporate funding and the raid rolls and targets are authored in packs/interceptor/strategy/campaign.yaml, each marked DERIVED; the pilot rules and mission score points are authored there too, from the design analysis, without the mark. The tech-id table in references.yaml is read from the player's executable by a layout that is itself derived (12-byte entries: R_ name pointer, string id, tech id); ids 75 and up are not in it and are left out of conditions; research unlocks are not authored (items, hulls and modules are gated by their own TechRequired). App 0.8.0 (c64d178, plan item 4.12): research sizes and prerequisites, costs, production times and maintenance are inherited from the player's GameSettings.ini (verified as data, no values in the pack); what the original keeps in code or its manual describes only loosely is estimated, from the design analysis. Not play-tested: a six-month automatic run researches 4 of 71 topics on one downlink. The original's monthly evaluation per outpost and the strategist replace the funding and raid estimates in Stage 5. 4 DEV-051 The story format as built is a simpler subset of its design (app 0.10.0): arc: <id> names the arc (the step is its place in steps) instead of {id, step}; the actions are the fourteen of EVENT_ACTIONS (seventeen since app 0.13.0, with card, video and play_cutscene) — mission(x) offers a mission now (no start_mission with a place and an expiry, no offer_mission, no reward:), no map changes; plans have stages of {name, count}, a shipment chance instead of ship_visibility, warnings as a list of {at, do}, no budget, grant_if_missed or plan_stage(x); relations are the player's standing with each faction only (no pairs between other factions, no relation_rules, no scale), and a stance change is a notice, not an on_stance_change event; of the stance effects only hostile or not acts (raids and battle hostility) — no allies in battle, no trade effects; the strategist is aggression only (strategist: with aggression and calm_after_wins, not strategists.<id> with budgets, expansion and an offence ladder); endings have text and victory (and since app 0.12.1 video; no image, music or continue). Stage 5 first makes the story playable end to end in both campaigns with the smallest format that expresses their arcs, plans and endings; the rest of the design stays the target (R-CPN-007 – R-CPN-010 notes). 5 DEV-052 The story content is incomplete and partly derived (app 0.10.1 – 0.10.2): the default campaign's chapters fly the nearest existing mission where their bespoke special mission is not built (only the finale eclipse_assault is its own); the interceptor arc's gates use the type_1/2/3_saucer_examination topics for the guide's Wraith, Spectre and Phantasm examinations (derived, unconfirmed), its later first-message day, middle-level plan counts, shipment interval, side-mission triggers and strategist values are derived, and only two of the seven side missions exist. The arcs, plans and endings are what the engine needed to prove; the missing missions are content work, recorded on R-CPN-004 and R-CPN-005. 5 DEV-053 Music changes state only at a segment's end, chosen by a fixed rule: the battle state is battle within battle_range of the nearest live hostile, threat within threat_range, else cruise; the set is the battle's seed modulo the number of sets; the interceptor strategy screen plays each set's cruise segments. The original's transition tables (Loops/*.wtl) are not read, and there is no switch: list. App 0.11.0: the smallest interactive-music model that plays the original's loop sets without cutting a phrase. The .wtl format is not decoded (unknown), and what the original plays on its strategy screens is derived. Ranges and sets are music: data. 6 DEV-054 The cutscene format as built is a subset of its design (MD2, app 0.13.0): scripted entities only, placed on centripetal Catmull-Rom position paths each tick (no rotation or speed keys; they face along the path and bank); actions fire_beams, missile, destroy; cameras' keys sit directly on the camera; cuts are instant; sounds are named event sounds; captions are plain text; harmless is per entity only (since app 0.14.1 its bolts and missiles do no damage; in 0.13.0 it kept the entity's own hull up instead). No formations, autopilot, chase, capture or jump, mission intros and outros, or video: in a cutscene. The engine side first plays the default campaign's intro end to end; the rest of the design (Mod designer §3.4) stays the target (R-MOD-033 – R-MOD-046 notes). 6 DEV-055 The interceptor films as built: animation1.smk opens a new campaign (derived: which of the CD's films is the original's opening), the five alien transmissions play full screen as each message arrives (alientrans1 – 5), and the victory plays credits_sm2a.smk. Films play letterboxed in the window, skippable with Enter, Esc or a click. App 0.12.0 – 0.13.0. How and where the original showed each film has not been compared side by side (unknown); every choice is a line of story or campaign data. 6 DEV-056 The interceptor craft's protection is derived from the original's equipment (app 0.15.0): the three player craft and several alien classes name their default shield and/or armour (fitted: → an original ShieldType* / ArmorType* section, chosen per class — derived); a shield's protection is read as its Special key and armour's as its HitPoints key (derived); the X-COM hulls get one shield and one armor slot (derived); alien classes with no known fit carry three times their former engine values (derived); stations that inherit an original hit-point chart (HP1 – HP4) take the four summed as their hull (derived: what each part protects in the original is unknown). In battle a craft flies the strongest fitted shield and the sum of its armour. Playtest: ships and stations were destroyed too easily — the X-COM craft flew placeholder Stage 2 values. Naming the original's equipment reads the player's own numbers instead of copying them into the pack. Which section each class carries, and what the keys mean, are not documented by the original; --balance shows the result. The default campaign (original-free) was toughened in its own data at the same time: fighters ×4, capital ships, stations and ground installations ×3. 4 DEV-057 Auto-resolved interceptions use an engine strength model (app 0.16.12): each craft's power is √(effective hit points × sustained beam damage per second) from its class (balance::power), a side's power the sum, and the player wins with p = P² / (P² + E²) against the mission's hostile roles at their average counts; the mission's own outcome actions for the rolled result apply. Fitted items, pilots and wingmen are not counted, and a lost auto-resolve does not damage craft or pilots. The original's auto-resolution is code, not data (unknown). The square makes a clear superiority nearly certain, like Lanchester's square law; it reuses the --balance numbers so a modder can predict it. 4 DEV-058 Base effects as built (app 0.16.10): quarters is a campaign-wide pilot limit (every base's type and modules added up; none anywhere = no limit), storage limits only purchases at a base (item sizes; no storage module anywhere in the campaign = no limit), and each point of a base's defence turns away 15 % of unopposed raids on that base on its own (1 − 0.85^points in all); income stays a tag that incomes: formulas count. Dismantling refunds economy.dismantle (50 %) of a module's cost. The original's numbers are not data (unknown). These are the simplest readings of the design's effect names that a modder can reason about; the refund and the module values are data. 4 DEV-059 The good and bad stingers' occasions are derived (app 0.16.2): good on a won battle (as the map returns), a finished research topic and a victory; bad on any other battle result and a defeat. The interceptor sets map them to the CD's loops by name (goodre1.wav / badre1.wav, gudrein2.wav / badrein2.wav, …). When the original played these loops is not recorded (derived from their names); the occasions are engine code, the clips are music: data. 6

docs.title: Implementation plan
docs.text:
An iterative, staged plan. Each stage ends with a playable build of the testbed: a launcher listing live test environments (scenarios) that show the stage's features and let a tester playtest one component at a time. Later stages add scenarios; none are removed.

Stage Version Delivers Status 0 Foundation 0.1.0 Repository, SpecItOut, docs site, format analysis, feasibility Done 1 Flight simulator 0.2.0 Packs and rules, model loading, rendering, cockpits and HUD, controls, flight model, weapons, targeting, wingmen, testbed Done (signed off 2026-11-10) 2 Combat, objects and behaviours 0.3.0 Mod kinds and parent; model sets (damage, construction states, debris); full damage, power and special systems; behaviours with difficulty variants; missiles, mines, probes, stations; effects, sound Done (deferred items listed) 3 Missions, environments and conditions 0.4.0 Condition/action language; mission types; space and atmospheric/ground environments with terrain; comms; hyperspace; debrief; Tier 2 script decision In progress 3 interlude: feedback and control console 0.4.0 Drift display, shot physics, visibility, base-defence balance, action catalogue and overlay; the tablet control console (server, protocol, components, target viewport, map; Arduino later) Planned 4 Strategy layer 0.5.0 Interactive star map, squadrons and sensors, economy, research, bases and modules, logistics (mining, research and manufacturing facilities, supply convoys, surveys — default campaign), ships and loadouts, pilots, functional screens, saves; shared formations (MD1) Planned 5 Campaigns 0.6.0 Events, arcs, rival plans, strategist, dynamic relations, endings: both campaigns playable start to finish Planned 6 Presentation 0.7.0 Screen layouts and skins, menus, video, interactive music, voices; cutscenes and video cutscenes (MD2, MD3) Planned 7 Modding toolkit and Remastered 0.8.0 Full validator, recipes (upscale, mesh patch), interceptor-remastered, modding guide; the Mod Designer and Cutscene Designer (MD4–MD6) Planned 8 Platforms and release 1.0.0 macOS app, Linux packages, Windows, release process; game bundling (MD7) Planned

Items MD1–MD7 come from the mod designer, cutscene designer and game bundling design.

docs.title: Three campaigns
docs.text:
The plan delivers three campaign mods, designed in Game design and mod format:

Campaign Grows in stages Complete interceptor: the full original campaign from the player's CD — the primary test case 2–6 Playable start to finish at Stage 5; presentation at Stage 6 default: Perils of the Void, a 1950s film-serial campaign with original content — runs without a CD 2–7 Playable start to finish at Stage 5; finished at Stage 7 interceptor-remastered: extends interceptor with locally generated upscaled textures and an enhanced Lightning 7 Stage 7

Every stage's features must work in both interceptor and default before the stage is done (the project's modding-first rule), so neither campaign can fall behind.

docs.title: Feasibility
docs.text: Confident. Every asset type stages 1–2 need was decoded and checked against the data: all 297 meshes parse; hulls and a saucer rendered correctly with their own textures; textures, cockpit images, sound effects and music loops are understood; all balance data is plain INI. The remaining unknowns (XSPT pixel runs, a few mesh fields, the CD audio codec; mfdanim.mps was read in Stage 6) have fallbacks and do not block any stage. The original simulator is far simpler than an id Tech 3 game: no levels, no skeletal animation, no scripting VM to reproduce.

docs.title: Ground rules
docs.text: Rule In practice The player supplies the game Original data is read from the player's own CD copy at run time. No original content in the repository game/, dist/ and every original asset type are git-ignored; the gate fails if one is tracked. Engine, not game Nothing Interceptor-specific is hard-coded: it lives in the interceptor pack as rules and scenarios. Original programs are data Interceptor.exe and the DLLs are parsed, never executed. Modding first Each feature is reachable from a pack before it is called done; the original-free default campaign (the sample pack in Stage 1) exercises it without original data. Tests before done Unit tests for every module; manual cases for what only a playtest shows (testing policy).

docs.title: Checks for every stage
docs.text:
• scripts/check.sh (unit tests, release build, --check on all packs, asset-tracking guard).
  • The stage's manual test cases, recorded as passed.

docs.title: Delivered
docs.text:
• Repository OpenInterceptor (MIT) with the SpecItOut manifest (implementation, specVersion: null), labels, .gitignore safety net, README and scripts/check.sh.
  • This site on the docs branch, with docs.sh.
  • Analysis of the CD: layout and formats.
  • Prototype decoders (outside the repository) that parsed all meshes and rendered models with their textures, used to confirm the formats before engine code was written.
  • Research into the original's gameplay and controls.
  • The architecture, the dependency decision (macroquad only) and this plan.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Decision Why Rust, one crate, macroquad 0.4.14 Proven in ArenaVM and Looking Glass on this machine; OpenGL 3 on macOS and Linux; small. All format readers in-crate Each is a few hundred lines; no crate exists for these formats anyway. INI for rules The original uses INI, so original sections import directly; no parser dependency. Revised in Stage 2: mod files moved to a YAML subset with schemas (DEV-030); original INI sections are still imported through inherit: original:…. OBJ + PNG/TGA for mod art Universal export targets; OBJ is trivial to parse. Gamepad without a crate macOS GameController shim (pattern from Looking Glass) and Linux joystick API with std.

docs.title: Stage 1 — Flight simulator
docs.text: Version 0.2.0. Status: done — signed off by the developer's playtest on 2026-11-10 (status). The core of the application: fly any playable ship in a live arena with the original's cockpit, controls, navigation, speed management and weapons.

docs.title: Exit scenario
docs.text: The testbed scenario Flight test: station patrol (flight-test) contains: the player's ship (any of the three playable hulls, chosen in the launcher), an X-COM base, two wingmen in formation, and one of each enemy type (Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm, Shade, Harbinger with its container, Spirit, Drone; pirate Lightning, Firestar and Super Avenger, Rogue Freighter) flying practice circles, plus nav points base, aliens, pirates. combat-test is the same arena with hostile AI. The player can fly with the cockpit controls, manage speed, target, and fire beams and missiles that damage and destroy targets.

docs.text:
# Item Module 1.1 PE resource reader; XMSH, XTXR, TGA, WAV (PCM, MS and IMA ADPCM), INI, OBJ readers, each with unit tests formats 1.2 Packs, VFS (pack files + original DLL resources), rules with inherit and layering, scenarios content 1.3 Asset cache: original/OBJ models to GPU meshes per texture, all LODs; textures with colour key model, render::gpu 1.4 Rendering: camera-relative transform, per-vertex sun lighting, LOD selection, starfield, sun render 1.5 Flight model from hull rules: newtonian default (thrust, coasting, reverse, brake, speed cap) and assisted option; afterburner; speed-hold flight computer (match speed, AI); VCT; arena edge sim::flight 1.6 Beams (energy, rate of fire, link modes) and missiles (lock time and cone, homing) sim::combat 1.7 Targeting (next/prev/closest/in-sights), collisions, damage, destruction sim 1.8 Wingmen formation; basic enemy pursuit; idle objects sim::ai 1.9 Cockpits A/B/C, reticle, radar, target MFD, gauges, message line; views F1–F8 hud, render::camera 1.10 Keyboard, mouse, gamepad (macOS shim, Linux joystick API), bindings.ini input, platform 1.11 Testbed launcher: scenario list, ship selection, model viewer app 1.12 sample pack with original-free models and a scenario packs/sample 1.13 --check headless validation check 1.14 Settings and data discovery: user data folder, settings.ini, automatic CD discovery settings, cli 1.15 Per-asset overrides of original models, textures, images and sounds; pack switch-off content 1.16 --extract: original assets → OBJ/PNG/WAV at their override paths extract 1.17 Cockpits with their own design space, HD art and 3D cockpit models; a 3D cockpit in the sample pack hud, render, packs/sample 1.18 Asset browser in the testbed app::assets 1.19 macOS app bundle with stage build numbers (0.2.x) tools/build_bundle.py

Items 1.14–1.19 were added at the project owner's request after the first playtest: the CD was not found without --data, the arcade flight model slowed ships without thrust, and modding needed extraction and per-asset replacement (HD and 3D cockpits) in the XWVM manner.

Launcher entry Id Shows Model viewer — Every ship class's model and every original mesh; orbit camera, LOD forcing, attachment points Asset browser — Every original texture, image and sound, with pack overrides marked; sounds play Flight test: station patrol flight-test The exit scenario above Combat test: hostile arena combat-test The same arena with every alien and pirate hostile Gunnery range gunnery-range Six drones circling ahead: beams, link modes, energy, missile lock Station tour station-tour Every station type, a Patton cruiser and a freighter: models, LODs, station collision Sample pack arena (no original data) sample-arena Original-free ships and station from the sample pack, a 3D cockpit, hostile raiders

docs.title: Stage 2 — Combat, objects and behaviours
docs.text:
Version 0.3.0. Status: complete (app 0.3.0, main d7553f5, 2026-11-11), except the deferred items below — XSPT sprite explosions and the model-set extras — and the manual passes, which are still to be recorded. Stage 3 part 1 (missions) ships in the same build. Every craft, station and weapon of both campaigns fights correctly, looks right in every state, and is driven by data: model sets, debris, behaviours with difficulty variants. The mod structure (campaign/addon/library, parent) lands here because every later stage loads content through it.

Design: mod structure, objects and models, behaviours.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Dependencies. The server (HTTP, WebSocket framing, SHA-1, base64, JSON) and the console page are written in-crate and with plain web components (C1): no dependency was added.
  • Settings. console: {enabled, port} in settings.yaml, --console and --console-port N (C1; R-CON-009 resolved).
  • Also in this period. App 0.4.1 fixed a start-up shader error (the lit shader's Light uniform needs the same precision in both stages; Rendering), and app 0.4.2 moved the default campaign to resources/default with the player's original data in resources/xcom or resources/xcom-cd (F-CMP-005).
  • F1. The request named F1 for the overlay, which selects cockpit view 1. Resolved: F1 stays the original's view key (no deviation); the overlay is on ? (Shift+Slash) and Shift+F1. F12 is the cockpit layout editor's key in custom cockpits, so it is not used (R-CON-008).

Exit: unit tests for the drift components, shot velocity, the catalogue and the protocol messages; manual test cases for the drift display, visibility, the overlay, base defence at the lowest level and the console on an iPad.

docs.title: Stage 3 — Missions, environments and the condition language
docs.text:
Version 0.4.0. Status: in progress — part 1 (missions as data) shipped in app 0.3.0, main d7553f5, 2026-11-11; hazards in app 0.5.1 (main 70d68e2); environments, atmospheric flight, terrain and the atmosphere HUD in app 0.6.0 (main af003f6); ground installations in app 0.6.1 (main de417df); radio voices in app 0.6.2 (main 5bdb47f); the simulator in app 0.6.3 (main 1d13b59, c3fb959); five more default missions in app 0.6.4 (main 3866c34, 90653b9); the remaining interceptor mission types in app 0.6.5 (main b1f57ab); playtest fixes (ground to the horizon, the textured console target, AI collision avoidance) in app 0.6.7 (main c0e2516) and the battle running on after its result in app 0.7.4 (main 9295707); the condition console in app 0.16.5 (main f227494). Missions become data: roles, waves, objectives and outcomes, in space and — new to this engine — on planet surfaces with atmospheric flight.

Design: missions and events, behaviours and scripting.

docs.title: Work items
docs.text:
# Item Module Status 3.1 The condition and action language: lexer, parser, type checker, interpreter; units; contexts (object, battle, campaign); load-time validation with file/section/key messages script Done: conditions (Stage 2) and actions (checked calls with battle/campaign scope); the battle context; the campaign context (app 0.6.7; logistics queries 0.16.3); the campaign outcome actions capture, lose, cargo_lost, cargo_captured act since app 0.16.3. 3.2 Mission types: roles (from situation, class lists per difficulty, player craft), arrivals and waves, objectives (win/draw/lose, optional), outcomes as action lists, timers, hazards (asteroids, black-hole pull, minefields, ion storm) mission (new), sim Done except hazards: roles (class lists, counts per level, faction, AI, behaviour, protect, state, hull, systems, speed), arrivals (at:, arrive:; DEV-040), waves, objectives, optional objectives, timers, outcomes. Hazards done (app 0.5.1, main 70d68e2): asteroid fields and minefields as scattered objects, black hole (pull, swallow, look, AI escape), ion storm (content::hazards, sim::hazards); GitHub #9. 3.3 Battle environments: space, orbit, pocket; backdrops from the map location render, sim Done (app 0.6.0, main af003f6): environments: data, environment: <id> on missions and scenarios, arena, planet backdrop, sky; default orbit, pocket, moon_surface, dusk_hills. Backdrops from the map location wait for Stage 4. GitHub #10. 3.4 Atmospheric flight: drag, gravity, lift, hover, ground collision and landing, ceiling escape; per-ship DragArea, Lift, Hover, AtmosphereMaxSpeed, Atmospheric sim::env Done (app 0.6.0): drag from atmosphere_max_speed, gravity, lift, hover, landing below 25 m/s upright, crash damage, ceiling exit, AI ground avoidance; ship keys atmosphere_max_speed, lift, hover, atmospheric (drag_area not adopted; atmospheric not yet acted on). GitHub #11. 3.5 Terrain: heightfield from an image or a generator (craters, hills), texturing with detail maps, scattered objects, sky gradient, fog; ground installations (kind: ground) and anti-air turrets render::terrain (new), sim Partial: heightfields generated (hills, craters) or from a heightmap, the coloured terrain mesh, sky dome and distance fog (app 0.6.0); ground installations, kind: ground, and anti-air batteries as ground turrets (app 0.6.1, main de417df). To do: detail-map texturing and scattered objects (deferred). GitHub #12. 3.6 HUD for atmosphere: altitude, vertical speed, horizon hud Done (app 0.6.0): ALT n VS ±n on the status line, artificial horizon and pitch ladder. GitHub #13. 3.7 Wingman comms menu and orders; radio chatter by trigger; voices sim, audio, hud Done (voices app 0.6.2, main 5bdb47f): wingman comms menu and orders (Stage 2); radio chatter by condition (missions); voices: sets and ship voice: — wingmen answer orders (acknowledge) and status requests (status), another reports a wingman lost (down); chatter voice: clips; the computer voice at the debrief (mission_accomplished, mission_failed). Default: synthesised guard_pilot clips; interceptor: computer voice from the cue table, pilot clips not mapped until their lines are identified (Open note, R-MSN-007). GitHub #14. 3.8 Hyperspace out with countdown; retreat outcomes; debrief screen (results, salvage, score) mission, app Partial: hyperspace out with countdown (Stage 2) — the player jumping out is the retreat result; the debrief screen (result, text, kills, losses, time, optional objectives, campaign actions). Salvage and score are applied by the strategy layer (Stage 4). 3.9 Simulator missions with a setup screen app Done (app 0.6.3, main 1d13b59, c3fb959): the launcher's Simulator — mission, ship, environment, asteroids, minefield, black hole, ion storm, enemy force (×0.5 – ×2), Fly; a modified copy of the mission (simulator::apply) flown by the ordinary mission code; "again" flies the same setup; atmospheric: false refused in an atmosphere. GitHub #15. 3.10 Tier 2 script language decision: dependency evaluation recorded on the dependency page, then hooks (do: script, do: ["script(...)"]) and the sandboxed API script Evaluation recorded; awaiting the user's decision. Tier 2 scripting, evaluated compares (a) mlua (Lua 5.4), (b) rhai and (c) growing script::* into a small statement language; the evaluator recommends (c) as the default under the dependency policy, with (a) as the fallback if mods need a full general-purpose language. Hooks and the API follow the decision. GitHub #16. 3.11 interceptor: the 27 mission types, the simulator types and the final mission's two parts as mission definitions (compositions from the guide, else derived estimates) packs/interceptor Done (app 0.6.5, main b1f57ab): 26 mission types — the first five and 21 more (original types 3 – 5, 7 – 9, 12 – 14, 16, 18 – 23, 25 – 27, 29, 30: base, corporate outpost, OPP and science-station defence; freighter convoys against aliens and pirates; deep-space ambush and encounter; the pirate squadron ambush; alien freighter ambushes; attacks on alien mining platforms, outposts and bases; the doomsday weapon). Original names, briefings and debriefs by @orig key; compositions derived, growing with the level, variants escalating (DEV-041). Soaked with the AI pilot at beginner, and at veteran for the hardest. Open: the earlier count was 27; briefing types 2, 6, 10 and 17 have no definition (whether they exist is unknown), and the simulator types and the final mission's two parts are not separate entries (R-CPN-005). GitHub #17 (closed). 3.12 default: the 11 generated mission types (2 on surfaces) and chapter missions 1, 2, 4, 5 playable from the testbed; terrain and sky assets generated resources/default, tools Done for Stage 3 (app 0.6.4, main 3866c34, 90653b9): nine missions — defend_station, convoy_ambush, construction_defence, intercept_scouts, and colony_defence (moon_surface, protect guard_colony), ground_strike (dusk_hills, dominion_flak, a timer draw), outpost_raid (orbit, dominion_outpost, wingmen), asteroid_hunt (asteroid hazard), pocket_ambush (pocket, 65 % ion storm, hot-rods) — each with briefing, chatter and debriefs including killed. Craft spawned below 300 m over a ground are lifted to 300 m. Terrain and sky are generated by the environments (no separate assets). Moved: the chapter story missions go with the arc (Stage 5); generating the mission types from the campaign is the strategy layer (Stage 4). GitHub #18. 3.13 Logistics missions (default campaign, design): convoy_ambush (generated when a supply convoy reaches the attack point chosen at random at its launch; protect it; cargo lost if destroyed, stored by the enemy if captured) and construction_defence (from 50 % construction, at most three per location; the facility in its construction-stage state); roles from the strategy situation; auto-resolve when the player does not fly; the campaign context queries they need mission, script Done (app 0.9.2, 0.16.3 – 0.16.4): convoy_ambush is generated by an ambushed supply convoy (logistics.ambush_mission, app 0.9.2) and construction_defence by a construction strike (logistics.construction_strikes, app 0.16.4, main d300642); both are auto-resolved when the player does not fly; the eight logistics queries of the campaign context (app 0.16.3, main a45331a). The struck facility is shown by the mission's own site (a research station at 60 %), not by the struck facility's type and stage (R-STR-022).

Testbed adds (so far: missions on the launcher with scrolling, --mission, --soak <mission>; the simulator as the mission browser (app 0.6.3; every mission of the loaded campaign, the force on its screen, the difficulty from the launcher) and, with its environments, the terrain sandbox; hazard scenarios hazard-asteroids, hazard-black-hole, hazard-minefield and environment scenarios env-orbit, env-pocket, surface-moon, surface-hills, surface-colony, surface-strike; and since app 0.16.5 (main f227494, GitHub #20) the condition console: backquote over any mission battle, a condition or expression typed and its value shown live (or the parse error), the battle paused, evaluated on a copy of the mission's generator (MissionRun::evaluate; MT-3-66). Planned originally: a mission browser (every mission type of both campaigns, with difficulty and force choices — done as the simulator), a terrain flight sandbox (atmospheric handling on several worlds — done through the simulator and the surface scenarios), and a condition-language console.

Exit: every mission type winnable and losable in the testbed; atmospheric flight feels distinct from space (manual test); the language fully unit-tested (parser, types, evaluation, error messages).

docs.text:
Version 0.5.0. Status: in progress — MD1 formations in app 0.6.6 (main 6d390d7); the campaign context in 0.6.7 (65141dc); the core (strategy data, the campaign runtime, saves) in 0.7.0 (77d6c9f); the default campaign's strategy data and the strategy screen in 0.7.1 (10f7fce); fitting in 0.7.2 (94d66c1); lane travel in 0.7.3 (076203e); the interceptor strategy layer from the player's data in 0.8.0 (c64d178); the testbed cheats in 0.8.1 (8e96338); logistics in 0.9.0 (ff9d8fc); playtest changes in 0.9.1 (3b19dea) and flown supply-convoy battles in 0.9.2 (0d1c522, 146195b); fitted shields and armour and --balance in 0.15.0 (1ff754b); the strategy screen rebuilt for the mouse in 0.16.0 (ac7ae62); the issue-audit gaps in 0.16.1 – 0.16.14 (f82a6ab … de30c2a). Design: strategy layer, interface.

From the mod designer, cutscene designer and game bundling design (decisions D1–D5 made 2026-11-11). The design places MD1 at "Stage 3 / 4"; it is planned here, in Stage 4. It comes first because it also serves wingmen: battles use it before any cutscene does.

Mission outcomes' relation(…) moves standings since app 0.12.1 (main 563c93f). #40. 5.6 Victory, defeat and endings (total/partial victories) campaign Done for the engine (0.10.0): endings, campaign_end victory and defeat conditions (defeats first), victory(x)/defeat(x) actions; the ending shown as a banner, saved — since 0.16.14 an ending screen (Stage 6.2). Neither campaign defines a partial victory yet. Since app 0.12.1 (main 87b04f3) an ending may play a video (the X-COM victory plays the credits), and continuing a finished campaign shows its ending again. #41. 5.7 Encyclopaedia (functional) with unlock conditions app Done (0.10.0): encyclopaedia.<id> with unlock, listed on the Archive tab. #42. 5.8 interceptor: the Doomsday arc (five messages and their gates), the Doomsday plan per difficulty, MacArthur and the final mission, the seven side missions, the alien strategist from Think.ini and the guide, news and report triggers packs/interceptor Partial (0.10.2): the arc (five messages with the guide's date, research and plan gates, MacArthur, the final mission), the plan by difficulty with its convoys and three warnings, endings using the original's own text keys, a strategist with DERIVED values; two of the seven side missions. Not built: the other five, the Think.ini strategist, report triggers. The saucer-examination topics in the gates are derived (unconfirmed). Not play-tested. #43. 5.9 default: the 12-chapter serial arc with progress-based triggers, the Eclipse Engine plan, the Dominion strategist, dynamic relations among the six factions (Senate, Cartel, Prospectors, raiders), chapter title cards (plain), narrator text resources/default Partial (0.10.1): the twelve chapters as messages with progress-based triggers, the Cartel's choice, side events, the Eclipse Engine plan, dynamic relations (the Senate stipend follows its standing), the strategist, four endings, the encyclopaedia, the finale eclipse_assault. Chapters whose bespoke special mission is not built fly the nearest existing mission. Relations are the player's with each faction, not among all six. Not play-tested. #44. 5.10 Fidelity: the open items closed or recorded as derived packs/interceptor, docs Not started beyond the story's own DERIVED marks. #45. 5.11 Rival logistics (default campaign): the Dominion's mines, cosmium shipments (the Eclipse Engine's convoys) and supply depots storing captured cargo (the player seizes a destroyed depot's stock); raids on the Guard's lanes and strikes on facilities under construction; third-party convoys: Prospector expeditions (to a system under investigation, pause, home) and Cartel runs to random destinations, with relation effects campaign::strategist, resources/default Not built. The Eclipse Engine's shipments exist as plan contacts (5.3) and the Guard's own convoys can be ambushed and escorted (app 0.9.2, Stage 4.15); the Dominion's mines and depots, seizing them, lane raids by the rival's logistics, construction strikes and third-party convoys are not. #46.

Testbed adds — Done (app 0.16.13, main 52e9e7f, #47): the event and arc debugger — Ctrl+D on the strategy screen shows a Debug list with each arc's step and every story event with its fired count and whether its condition holds now; Fire now fires one (Campaign::fire_event: its arc advances only if it is the next step, its actions run, its choice is offered) — and start-at-chapter: --strategy --chapter N plays a new campaign forward headless (campaign::autoplay_to_chapter, up to 1500 days) until its first arc reaches step N. Not built: setting flags and plan progress directly (fire an event that does it). --strategy-soak reports the story (arcs, plans, aggression, ending; 0.10.1) and the Archive tab shows plans, standings and aggression. MT-5-12, MT-5-13.

Exit: a full play-through of each campaign at a middle difficulty (manual tests, with a log of milestone dates); automated soak test running each campaign for a simulated year with the player's battles auto-resolved, checking invariants (money accounting, no orphan references, arc progress monotonic).

Exit status at app 0.10.3

The automated soak is built for the default campaign: campaign::tests::the_default_campaign_runs_a_year_with_its_story_and_stays_consistent plays a year a month at a time (campaign::autoplay_from), checking every reference, that money and score stay finite and that arcs only move forward, and that the serial and the Engine progress. Money accounting is checked only as finite. The interceptor story needs the player's data, so it has no unit test; --strategy-soak 365 --campaign interceptor runs it by hand. No play-through of either campaign has been done yet (MT-5-01 – MT-5-10).

docs.title: 6.9 Original-style strategy screens
docs.text:
Status: not started — specified in Definition and Specification 1.19.0 from the user's request (2026-11-12): "Critically missing from the game and requirements is the strategy UI from Interceptor. The gridded layout currently present is fine for testing, but we need to support the interface style the original game has. It broke up functionality across multiple screens as opposed to a single grid like currently present." — "there are additional screens, these are just a subset."

Requirements: Strategy interface (R-UI-001 – R-UI-040); features F-UI-001 – F-UI-006; format: Screen sets. Parent issue #112.

A campaign defines a screen set: full screens and dialogs, each a background plus engine widgets placed by rectangle in its design space (640 × 480 for interceptor, its art read by original:WrappersDLL.dll#<id> reference), linked to one another by actions. The engine owns each screen's function; the set owns the layout. A set may be partial — a screen it lacks opens the built-in version — so the interceptor set grows as the WrappersDLL mapping proceeds and no step waits on it. Every step works in the default campaign too, and adds unit tests for its logic and manual tests MT-6-xx for what must be played.

# Step Delivers Requirements Issue 6.9.1 Framework screens.<id> sets, the campaign interface keys, navigation and dialogs, the core widgets (button, toggle and radio groups, label, value, list, text, image, frame), uniform scaling with bands, keyboard and gamepad focus, validation, the partial-set fallback, custom screens, interface sounds, original:…@[x, y, w, h] image parts R-UI-001 – R-UI-009, R-UI-012, R-UI-014 – R-UI-017, R-UI-019, R-UI-021, R-UI-039, R-UI-040 #98 6.9.2 CSD The round map with its hover box, minimap, globe and lamps, clock, date, money, speeds, the screen buttons R-UI-010, R-UI-023 #99 6.9.3 Dialogs Interceptor Orders, Launch Mission, notices and Alien Transmission, event choices R-UI-004, R-UI-024, R-UI-029, R-UI-030 #100 6.9.4 Bases The 3D base view (model_view) with slots, overlays, rotate pad and module dial R-UI-011, R-UI-025 #101 6.9.5 Purchase / manufacture market (categories, item list with quantities, cargo and hangar space) and factory (queue) R-UI-026, R-UI-027 #102 6.9.6 Pilots portraits sockets, the stat panel, docked ships with pilot assignment R-UI-013, R-UI-028 #103 6.9.7 Research Topics, current work, progress and rate R-UI-033 #104 6.9.8 Hangar Equip ship: the craft in 3D, slots and items, pilot R-UI-034 #105 6.9.9 Reports Four report panels by period R-UI-035 #106 6.9.10 Encyclopaedia Categories, entries, model or picture, text, stats R-UI-036 #107 6.9.11 Briefing / debriefing The formation grid_view and text; recovery, items, score, rating; return to the launching screen R-UI-031, R-UI-032 #108 6.9.12 Options Keyboard configuration, audio, graphics, the layout switch; messages, simulator and title screens R-UI-037, R-UI-038 #109 6.9.13 Default-campaign art The default set in art-deco style, art generated by tools/default_assets R-UI-022 #110 6.9.14 Testbed-layout switch testbed_layout, the Options switch per campaign, the fallback for packs without a set R-UI-018 #111

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: See the testing policy for what must be tested and how.

docs.title: The gate
docs.text:
scripts/check.sh on main runs every automated check:

  1. cargo test --release — all unit tests (269 on macOS at main d7553f5).
  2. cargo build --release.
  3. openinterceptor --check --no-original — the original-free default campaign loads and validates. Since Stage 2 --check validates every campaign separately, each with its own active set of packs.
  4. openinterceptor --data <data> --check — when the player's data is found (OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA, else the first of ./resources/xcom and ./resources/xcom-cd that holds files): every rule, ship model, debris model, texture, cockpit image, sound and scenario loads, and every original mesh and texture decodes (reference CD at build 0.2.0: 2 packs, 34 ship classes, 100 models incl. the then sample pack's 3D cockpit, 272 textures, 3 images, 20 sounds, 5 scenarios, 1 096 original resources, 0 errors; the Stage 2 counts are per campaign). Skipped with a message otherwise.
  5. The committed JSON Schemas (schemas/*.schema.json) must equal what --write-schemas produces, so editors always see the engine's current schema.
  6. A guard that fails if any original asset file type (exe dll cab smk aif aiff wav mps) is tracked by git — except resources/default/sounds/*.wav, the default campaign's own generated sounds.
  7. A guard that fails if any file under resources/xcom/, resources/xcom-cd/ or the old game/ is tracked by git (app 0.4.2).

Also kept clean before every commit (project rule): cargo clippy --all-targets with no warnings and cargo fmt --check (settings in rustfmt.toml: width 120).

scripts/check.sh                                 # everything
openinterceptor --extract /tmp/x                 # also exercises every reader (not in the gate)
cargo test                                       # unit tests only
cargo test xmsh                                  # tests whose name contains "xmsh"
OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA=~/Games/Interceptor scripts/check.sh

docs.title: Pages
docs.text:
• Unit tests: what each module's tests cover.
  • Manual tests: playtest cases, per stage, with results.

docs.title: Cross-platform check
docs.text: From macOS, cargo check --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu type-checks the Linux code paths (platform::linux) without a Linux machine; running needs Linux (manual case MT-1-21).

docs.title: Manual tests
docs.text:
Playtest cases for behaviour that unit tests cannot show (what is drawn, how it feels, sound, real devices). Each stage's cases must be run and recorded as passed before the stage is complete. Record results in the table (date, tester, platform, result, notes); keep earlier rows when re-running a case.

How to run: cargo build --release, then target/release/openinterceptor (original data — an installed copy in resources/xcom/ or a CD copy in resources/xcom-cd/ — is found automatically; see Settings), or open dist/OpenInterceptor-<version>.app built by python3 tools/build_bundle.py. Every case names its launcher entry; to jump straight in use --scenario <id> --ship <id> (and --view chase for an outside view). Ship ids: lightning, firestar, avenger (interceptor campaign); comet, meteor, thunderbolt (default campaign — add --campaign default, or --no-original). Keys are the defaults on Controls.
