docs.title: MT-1-01 — Launcher lists scenarios
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher Preconditions Original data available. Steps 1. Run openinterceptor --data game.2. Look at the list; move with Up/Down; read each description.3. Quit (Esc) and run openinterceptor --no-original. Expected With data: Model viewer, Flight test: station patrol, Combat test: hostile arena, Gunnery range, Station tour, Sample pack arena (no original data) — since Stage 2 one campaign's scenarios at a time (see MT-2-12). The packs line names both packs. With --no-original: Model viewer and the Sample pack arena only, and an orange note that the Interceptor pack was skipped. Clicking a line selects it; clicking it again starts it.

docs.title: MT-1-02 — Ship selection: all three hulls
docs.text: Field Scenario Flight test: station patrol Steps 1. Select the scenario.2. Press Left/Right repeatedly.3. For each hull press Enter, fly briefly, Esc → L back. Expected A turning model, name, description and stats for X-1A Lightning II, S-2 Firestar and M-3 Super Avenger, wrapping round. Each starts the scenario in that hull (the MFD Status page shows its name). Scenarios with a fixed ship (Sample arena) show no choice.

docs.title: MT-1-03 — Model viewer
docs.text: Field Scenario Model viewer Steps 1. Open it. 2. PgDn/PgUp (or N/B) through the list. 3. Arrows or mouse drag to orbit; +/− or wheel to zoom. 4. L several times. 5. Space. 6. Esc. Expected Ship classes first (name and id), then every original mesh (mesh NAME). Each model is framed fully and textured; zoom never enters the model and does not run away. L cycles auto → LOD 0 → 1 → 2 → 3 → auto with visibly simpler models and the info line showing the forced LOD. Attachment points show as small RGB axes. Space stops/starts the spin. Esc returns to the launcher.

docs.title: MT-1-04 — Keyboard flight: attitude
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test, Lightning II Steps 1. Press Up, then Down. 2. Left, Right. 3. Kp7/Q and Kp9/E. 4. Repeat at full throttle. Expected Up lowers the nose, Down raises it; Left/Right turn; Kp7/Q roll left, Kp9/E roll right. Response builds up smoothly and stops smoothly. At full throttle pitch and yaw are noticeably slower than at rest (roll is not). The Avenger turns more slowly than the Lightning.

docs.title: MT-1-05 — Keyboard flight: throttle and afterburner
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test, any hull Steps 1. Press = (or keypad +) three times, - once. 2. Backspace. 3. Hold Tab, release. Expected THR reads 30 %, 20 %, then 100 %; each press changes the throttle exactly once. At 100 % speed climbs to the hull's MaxSpeed (600 m/s) and stops there. Tab: BURN shown, speed rises to MaxSpeed + Boost, energy gauge falls; released (or out of energy) the extra speed bleeds off back to MaxSpeed. (Coasting, reverse and braking: MT-1-22.)

docs.title: MT-1-06 — Mouse flight
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Steps 1. Press C. 2. Move the cursor up, down, left, right of centre. 3. Left button, right button. 4. Press C again. Expected The cursor hides and is confined; the caption says "mouse flight (C)". Cursor down = nose down, up = nose up, left/right turn, proportional to the distance from centre. Left button fires beams; right button fires a missile. C again restores the cursor.

docs.title: MT-1-07 — Gamepad flight
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test; Xbox/PlayStation-style controller connected before starting Steps Use the left stick, right stick, triggers, shoulders, A/B/X/Y, D-pad, Back, Start; in the launcher use the D-pad and A. Expected Per Controls → gamepad: left stick forward = nose down, sideways = yaw; right stick = roll and vertical slide (VCT hulls); RT beams, LT missile; RB/LB next/previous target; A afterburner; B nearest enemy; X match speed; Y chase view; D-pad throttle and MFD pages; Back link mode; Start pause. Small stick movements inside the dead zone do nothing.

docs.title: MT-1-08 — Cockpit per hull
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Steps Start once with each hull; stay in F1. Expected Lightning II → cockpit A, Firestar → B, Avenger → C, centred and scaled to the window height with no cyan fringe. Both radar scopes, the MFD, the four gauges (speed, energy, shields, hull) and the message line sit inside the art's instrument faces.

docs.title: MT-1-09 — Views F1–F8
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Steps Press F1 … F8; in F8 use Insert/Delete, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End, Kp5. Expected F1 cockpit art; F2 full forward with glass instruments; F3/F4 look left/right; F5/F6 rear-left/rear-right; F7 chase camera behind and above showing the ship with its engine glow; F8 orbit camera that moves with the keys and resets with Kp5. The caption names the view. Target brackets show only in F1, F2 and F7.

docs.title: MT-1-10 — Targeting, brackets and target MFD
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range Steps 1. T several times, Y. 2. R. 3. Point the nose at a drone, G. 4. Turn away so the target leaves the screen. 5. . and , to cycle MFD pages. Expected Each target change shows "TARGET: NAME" and a click; brackets in the faction colour sized to the target, with name and range and a lead circle. R picks the nearest hostile; G picks the one nearest the reticle. Off screen, an arrow on a ring points to it. MFD pages: Target (name, faction, range, speed, shields, armour, hull, lock state), Weapons, Status, Nav. On the radar the target is boxed.

docs.title: MT-1-11 — Beams, energy and link modes
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range, Firestar (four beams) Steps 1. Hold Enter (or LeftControl) at a drone. 2. Press X three times, firing in each mode. 3. Fire until energy runs out. Expected Coloured bolts leave the guns with sound and travel to their range. "WEAPONS FULL", "WEAPONS UNLINKED", "WEAPONS LINKED" messages; Linked fires pairs, Full all mounts, Unlinked one at a time. The energy gauge falls while firing and refills when not. At low energy "INSUFFICIENT POWER" and a denied sound; firing resumes once energy recovers. Hits flash the target and show sparks (blue on shields, orange on hull).

docs.title: MT-1-12 — Missile lock and hit
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range Steps 1. R, keep the drone near the reticle. 2. Watch the lock ring. 3. Space when locked. 4. W to change missile type; fire one without a lock. Expected A red ring closes in on the target, then a red diamond with "LOCK" and "MISSILE LOCK" plus a lock tone; the MFD shows "locking", then "LOCKED". A locked missile homes in and explodes on the drone. W moves the > marker on the Weapons page. An unlocked missile flies straight and expires after its duration. Rack counts go down; an empty rack reports "NO MISSILES".

docs.title: MT-1-13 — Destroying enemies, debris
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Steps Destroy one of each kind of enemy (beams and missiles). Expected Shields, then armour, then hull fall on the target MFD. At zero hull: an explosion (bigger for bigger ships), a sound, tumbling debris chunks of that ship that fade after about 12 s, "NAME DESTROYED", and the target is cleared.

docs.title: MT-1-14 — Wingmen formation and orders
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test (two Lightning wingmen, alpha2/alpha3) Steps 1. Fly turns at several throttles; F7 to watch. 2. Shift+F near the aliens. 3. Shift+I. 4. Target an enemy, Shift+A. Expected Wingmen hold slots beside and slightly behind the player, match speed and catch up with afterburner when far. Messages "WINGMEN: FIRE AT WILL", "WINGMEN: FORM ON ME", "WINGMEN: ATTACK MY TARGET"; they attack accordingly and return to formation.

docs.title: MT-1-15 — Station collision
docs.text: Field Scenario station-tour Steps Fly past each station; then fly slowly into the X-COM base's arms and hull. Expected Every station type renders textured with plausible LOD changes as you approach. Flying into the structure (not just its bounding sphere) bounces the ship back with a collision sound and hull damage; flying through the gaps between arms does not collide.

docs.title: MT-1-16 — Hostile AI
docs.text: Field Scenario combat-test Steps Fly towards the aliens and pirates; dogfight. Expected Enemies close in, lead their shots, fire beams and missiles, break off when about to ram, and jink sideways when targeted (VCT ships). The player can be destroyed (MT-1-20).

docs.title: MT-1-17 — Nav points
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Steps Press N three times; MFD Nav page (,/.). Expected "NAV BASE", "NAV ALIENS", "NAV PIRATES" cycle; a blue diamond with the name marks the point on screen; the Nav page shows its name and range.

docs.title: MT-1-18 — Sound effects
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range Steps Fire each weapon, get a lock, hit and destroy a drone, collide gently, run out of energy, change target. Expected Original sounds play: beam sounds per weapon, missile launch, lock tone, shield/hull hits, explosions, collision, denied, target click. Distant events are quieter.

docs.title: MT-1-19 — Original-free sample pack
docs.text: Field Scenario Sample pack arena (retired in Stage 2 — see MT-2-13) Steps Run openinterceptor --no-original (or without --data); start the arena; fight. Expected The Dart (3D cockpit, see MT-1-26), two Dart wingmen, the textured ring station and three red raiders that attack. Everything works without any original file. The Model viewer lists only dart, raider and ring station.

docs.title: MT-1-20 — Pause, menu, restart, death
docs.text: Field Scenario combat-test Steps 1. P, P. 2. Esc, Esc. 3. Esc, R. 4. Get destroyed; press Enter. 5. Esc, L. Expected P freezes the simulation ("PAUSED (P)"). Esc dims the screen with the menu and a key summary; Esc resumes; R restarts the scenario with the same ship. On death: "SHIP DESTROYED", the camera orbits the wreck, Enter restarts. L returns to the launcher.

docs.title: MT-1-21 — Linux build and run
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test Preconditions Linux with libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev; an Xbox-style pad at /dev/input/js0 if available. Steps scripts/check.sh, then run MT-1-01, 04, 07, 08, 18. Expected The gate passes; the cases behave as on macOS; bindings.yaml is created under ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/.

docs.title: MT-1-22 — Newtonian flight: coast, reverse, brake
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test, any hull, cockpit view Steps 1. Backspace (full throttle) until 600 m/s. 2. \ (zero throttle). 3. Yaw hard right for two seconds, release. 4. Z (reverse) and Backspace. 5. Hold B. 6. Release B, Z again. Expected 2: speed stays at 600 m/s — the ship coasts. 3: the nose turns but the ship keeps travelling the old way (stars and targets slide sideways); the forward-speed reading falls as the nose turns away from the motion. 4: REV shown; the ship slows, stops and then backs up. 5: BRAKE shown; the ship comes to a full stop (0 m/s) and stays there. 6: thrust forward again. Repeat with flight: {model: assisted} in a test mod: zero throttle then slows the ship to a stop and turning carries the velocity round.

docs.title: MT-1-23 — Match speed hold
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range Steps Target a drone (R); press M; fly behind it; then press =. Expected M shows HOLD n with the drone's speed; the ship settles at that speed and stops drifting sideways. Any throttle key (or B, Z) clears HOLD and returns to manual thrust.

docs.title: MT-1-24 — Arena edge
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer (arena_radius 30 000 m; was sample-arena) Steps Full throttle with afterburner in one direction for about a minute (or use a test mod with arena_radius: 3000). Expected "ARENA BOUNDARY" appears once on the message line; the ship stops moving outwards at the edge but can still slide along it and fly back in.

docs.title: MT-1-25 — HD cockpit override
docs.text: Field Preconditions An extracted CD (MT-1-27). Steps 1. Scale images/cockpita/12000.png from the extraction to 2560×1920 and tint it (any image editor). 2. Save it as <user data>/mods/hd-cockpit-test/images/cockpita/12000.png with a pack.yaml (id: hd-cockpit-test, kind: addon, targets: [interceptor], requires_original: true, format: 2; the Stage 1 run used the equivalent pack.ini). 3. openinterceptor --check. 4. Fly flight-test in the Lightning II. 5. Add hd-cockpit-test to packs: {disabled: […]} in settings.yaml; fly again. Expected 3: 0 errors, 3 packs. 4: the tinted, sharper cockpit replaces the original; windows are transparent; radars, MFD, gauges and message line sit exactly where they did. 5: the original cockpit is back. Recorded 2026-11-10, macOS: pass (steps 1–4).

docs.title: MT-1-26 — 3D cockpit (sample Dart)
docs.text: Field Scenario sample-arena (retired in Stage 2; the 3D cockpit is now tested by MT-2-14) Steps Start the arena; look around the cockpit view (F1); fly towards the ring station; switch to F7 and back. Expected A 3D cockpit around the pilot: dashboard slab, side consoles, canopy struts meeting above the nose, an overhead hoop, two green screens. It never disappears behind or into world objects (the station, other ships), struts directly ahead are not clipped, and it turns with the ship. Instruments are drawn in the 1280×720 layout along the bottom (radars at the corners, MFD left of centre, gauges right). F7 shows the Dart from outside without the cockpit.

docs.title: MT-1-27 — Extract the CD
docs.text: Field Steps openinterceptor --extract ~/interceptor-extracted; open a few files: a model in Blender (models/inttypea.obj), a texture, images/cockpita/12000.png, a sound. Expected A summary with 0 errors; the model imports with its textures (nose along −Z, metres); the cockpit PNG has transparent windows; sounds play in any player. Recorded 2026-11-10, macOS: pass for the run and counts (297 models, 799 textures, 3244 images, 792 sounds, 27 files, 0 errors); files not yet opened in Blender.

docs.title: MT-1-28 — Asset browser and override marking
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher → Asset browser Steps Browse textures, Tab to images (find cockpita.dll #12000), Tab to sounds and press Enter on a few; with the MT-1-25 mod installed, look at cockpita.dll #12000 again. Expected Textures and images draw over a checkerboard at their size; sounds play; with the mod, the entry reads [overridden by hd-cockpit-test] and shows the repaint.

docs.title: MT-1-29 — Disable a pack
docs.text: Field Steps With any mod installed, add its id to packs: {disabled: […]} in settings.yaml; run --list and fly. Expected --list omits the pack; a warning "pack '' is disabled in settings" is printed; the originals are used again.

docs.title: MT-1-30 — App bundle from Finder
docs.text: Field Steps python3 tools/build_bundle.py; double-click dist/OpenInterceptor-0.2.0.app in Finder. Expected The launcher opens with both packs listed (the CD found through settings.yaml); Finder shows the build's version in Get Info; bindings.yaml and mods/ exist in ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/.

docs.title: MT-1-31 — Original meshes render correctly
docs.text: Field Scenario Model viewer (--model <NAME> opens it on a mesh) Preconditions Original data available Steps Open each of XBASE7, CPAT, ROID100, ALIENC7, 1ASHB, AVENGER16, AL-OPP7, A-FRT3, A-SHIPA5; orbit all the way round (arrows/drag) and zoom in close (+/wheel). Expected No flickering on flat areas (station panels, saucer underside circles, shield ring, Avenger fin); every textured face shows texture detail — no single-colour faces and no smeared stripes (the Patton's hull is fully textured, the asteroid is rock all over); faces seen only from outside, never inside-out. Known, not bugs A-BMOD01, ALCLAW2, A-FRT4 (and other debris/parts) are open shells in the original data: looking into the opening shows no inside faces. A-SHIPA4's stretched texture on one side matches its original UVs (unconfirmed against the original game). Faces flagged translucent are drawn opaque (the flag is not used yet).

docs.title: MT-1-32 — Viewer wireframe and face selection
docs.text: Field Scenario Model viewer, --model A-SHIPA5 Steps Press W three times; press ] several times, Shift+], [; press I; press PgDn to the next model. Expected W cycles solid → solid + green face outlines with yellow vertex dots → outlines only (all edges visible) → solid; the info line names the mode. ] selects face 0, 1, …; Shift jumps 10; [ goes back and wraps; the selected face is outlined in yellow with its number, and the info line shows its corners, texture, flags, layer and UVs. I numbers every face towards the camera. Changing model clears the selection.

docs.title: MT-1-33 — Overlay toggle
docs.text: Field Scenario Model viewer, --model XBASE7 Steps Zoom in to the station's flat panels; press O twice; press Esc and fly any scenario. Expected O hides the overlay-flagged panels (the base surface under them shows) and shows them again; the info line says "overlays hidden/shown". After Esc, stations in flight have their overlays (the setting is restored).

docs.title: MT-1-34 — Bolts leave from the nose (chase view)
docs.text: Field Scenario gunnery-range, --view chase Steps Fire beams (Space) while stationary, then at full throttle and with afterburner. Expected Every bolt streak starts at the front of the ship and grows forward; no streak reaches back past the ship.

docs.title: MT-1-35 — Radar scopes aligned with cockpit art
docs.text: Field Scenario combat-test, cockpit view, once with each hull (--ship lightning, firestar, avenger) Steps Look at both radar scopes; turn so contacts move to the edge of each scope. Expected Contacts stay inside the painted round glass, centred on the painted crosshair; no extra engine-drawn rings or F/R letters over the art; the glass HUD (F2 or a non-cockpit view) still shows rings and labels.

docs.title: MT-1-36 — Sample models one-sided
docs.text: Field Scenario sample-arena, --no-original, chase view (retired with the sample pack) Steps Fly around the ring station and past the wingmen's Darts; open the model viewer on ring and dart. Expected The ring is solid from every side (no missing walls); the Dart's canopy fin shows from both sides; the 3D cockpit is unchanged.

docs.title: Stage 2 results
docs.text:
First delivery: build 0.2.2. Cases run in both campaigns where a scenario exists in both: systems-trial. Fitted equipment — interceptor: tractor on the Firestar and Super Avenger, cloak on the Super Avenger, ECM on all three (advanced ECM on the Avenger); default: tractor on the Meteor and Thunderbolt, cloak on the Thunderbolt, ECM on all three rockets.

ID Case Scenario Result Date Tester / platform Notes MT-2-01 Power keys and the power instrument systems-trial not run MT-2-02 Shield balance systems-trial not run MT-2-03 System damage and repair: messages and lamps rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-04 Tractor tow and capture systems-trial not run MT-2-05 Cloak and enemy sensors systems-trial not run MT-2-06 ECM against missiles dominion-raid not run MT-2-07 Hyperspace countdown and abort systems-trial not run MT-2-08 Wingman menu and orders rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-09 Controls menu: keyboard rebinding and saving Launcher → Controls not run MT-2-10 Gamepad chord capture and modifier layer Launcher → Controls not run Needs a physical controller MT-2-11 Stick layout and mouse invert rocket-vs-saucer not run Gamepad part needs a controller MT-2-12 Campaign switch Launcher not run MT-2-13 Default campaign look: cockpit and ships rocket-vs-saucer, dominion-raid, black-comet-ambush not run Replaces MT-1-19 MT-2-14 3D cockpit on 4:3 and 16:9 windows rocket-vs-saucer not run Replaces MT-1-26 MT-2-15 Anchored 3D-cockpit instruments rocket-vs-saucer not run Build dd92045 MT-2-16 Cockpit layout editor: 2D instruments flight-test (cockpit A) or any 2D cockpit not run MT-2-17 Cockpit layout editor: 3D placement and saving rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-18 YAML mistakes reported with file and line --check not run MT-2-19 Difficulty switch Launcher not run MT-2-20 Enemy accuracy by difficulty rocket-vs-saucer not run Also --soak numbers MT-2-21 HUD text fits the instruments any not run MT-2-22 Station modules close up outpost-strike, base-assault not run Build a062822 MT-2-23 Shield modules and hub cascade outpost-strike, base-assault not run MT-2-24 Missile guidance kinds and mines combat-test (Super Avenger), dominion-raid not run MT-2-25 Debris and damage showcase; viewer looks debris-showcase, model viewer not run MT-2-26 Original sound cues gunnery-range, systems-trial not run Needs original data MT-2-27 Duels and target preferences duel-*, mixed-dogfight, escort, rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-28 Protected objectives and radar colours systems-trial, rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-29 Cockpit text legibility rocket-vs-saucer, systems-trial (default) not run MT-2-30 Top display bar and shield rings any interceptor duel, each hull; rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-31 Point defence base-assault, outpost-strike, duel-dreadnought not run Build a08c8bf MT-2-32 Sensor and jamming probes probe-net (both campaigns) not run MT-2-33 AI pilots use cloak, ECM and power duel-raider-saucer, duel-shade, rocket-vs-saucer not run MT-2-34 Text keys and a translation addon Launcher, --language not run

docs.title: MT-2-01 — Power keys and the power instrument
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial (either campaign), cockpit view Steps 1. Press F9 five times, watching the message line and the power instrument. 2. Press F10 five times. 3. Press ' (power to beams) until it refuses, then ; (power to shields) until it refuses. 4. Open the MFD Status page (. / ,). 5. Fly from a cockpit without power rectangles (any interceptor hull). Expected 1–2: each press shows "BEAMS x n% SHIELDS y n%" and steps the B-<level> / S-<level> column; after E it wraps to A. 3: raising one setting lowers the other once the budget is full; at the top it says "BEAM/SHIELD CHARGE AT MAXIMUM", and "INSUFFICIENT POWER" when the budget cannot be met; used/budget shows in yellow when the budget is full. 4: Status shows BEAM x SHLD y PWR used/budget. Beam capacitor and shield recharge visibly slow at A. 5: the power and systems panels appear at the top right of the cockpit's design space with a dark backdrop.

docs.title: MT-2-02 — Shield balance
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial, cockpit view, shields full Steps Press S three times, waiting a few seconds after each; watch the F and A bars of the power instrument. Expected "SHIELDS FULL FORWARD": the F label turns white, points flow from aft to fore and the fore bar can grow above the aft. "SHIELDS FULL AFT": the reverse. "SHIELDS BALANCED": both settle at equal capacity. The MFD Status line shows FWD, AFT or EVEN.

docs.title: MT-2-03 — System damage and repair: messages and lamps
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer, cockpit view; let the saucers hit you after your shields are down Steps 1. Take hull hits; watch the message line, the systems lamps and the MFD Systems page. 2. Break away and wait. 3. Press L after a message has faded. Expected 1: a hit past the armour plays the system-damage sound and shows "… DAMAGED: HALF EFFICIENCY" (amber lamp, DMG n%) or "… INOPERATIVE: REPAIRS UNDERWAY" (red lamp, OUT); a damaged engine slows acceleration, damaged manoeuvring slows turns. 2: one system at a time is repaired, worst first (its red lamp blinks, * on the Systems page); an inoperative system comes "BACK ON-LINE" only after some repair, later "… REPAIRED" (green). 3: the last message is shown again. If engines and manoeuvring both go out: "ENGINES AND THRUSTERS OUT: SHIP DISABLED" and DISABLED in the status strip.

docs.title: MT-2-04 — Tractor tow and capture
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial; default: Meteor or Thunderbolt; interceptor: Super Avenger or Firestar Steps 1. Target the crippled ship (T) and press Shift+T from far away. 2. Close to within 250 m and press Shift+T. 3. Fly around for a while; try to fire beams. 4. Press H and wait for the jump. 5. Restart, tow the prize, then press Shift+T again. Expected 1: "NO TARGET IN TRACTOR RANGE". 2: "TRACTOR BEAM ON", the tractor sound, TRACTOR in the status strip and a cyan TRC lamp; the target follows at a fixed distance. 3: "BEAMS OFF-LINE: TRACTOR BEAM ON". 4: countdown, then "JUMPED TO HYPERSPACE" with "Captured: " on the end screen. 5: "TRACTOR BEAM OFF"; the prize drifts. A ship without a tractor gets "NO TRACTOR BEAM FITTED".

docs.title: MT-2-05 — Cloak and enemy sensors
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial; default: Thunderbolt; interceptor: Super Avenger Steps 1. Press Shift+C with the budget full, then lower a setting and press it again. 2. Fly away from the enemies, then close in. 3. Fire beams. 4. Watch an enemy cloaker (the Shade or a raider saucer) from a distance and close. Expected 1: "INSUFFICIENT POWER FOR …", then "… ON", the cloak sound and CLOAKED. 2: beyond the cloak's range enemies lose you ("TARGET LOST" on their side; they stop attacking); close in they find you again. 3: "CLOAK DROPPED". 4: a cloaked enemy vanishes from your radar and target cycling beyond its range and reappears nearer.

docs.title: MT-2-06 — ECM against missiles
docs.text: Field Scenario dominion-raid in a Comet (ECM fitted), or combat-test in any interceptor hull Steps 1. Let enemies lock and fire missiles with ECM off; note how often they hit. 2. Press Shift+J and repeat. 3. Watch your own lock time on an enemy with ECM on (if any). Expected 2: "… ON", the ECM sound and ECM in the status strip; incoming missiles more often lose their lock and fly past. 3: locking onto a jamming ship takes about twice as long.

docs.title: MT-2-07 — Hyperspace countdown and abort
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial Steps 1. Press H; press H again after two seconds. 2. Press H and wait. 3. (If possible) start a countdown with a damaged hyperdrive. Expected 1: "HYPERDRIVE ACTIVATED: JUMP IN n S", JUMP n in the status strip, then "HYPERJUMP ABORTED". 2: "JUMP IN 5" … "JUMP IN 1", the hyperspace sound, "HYPERJUMP COMPLETE" and the "JUMPED TO HYPERSPACE" end screen (Enter flies again, Esc menu). Countdown: 10 s in interceptor, 8 s in default. 3: twice as long; a hyperdrive knocked out during the countdown aborts it ("HYPERJUMP ABORTED: HYPERDRIVE DAMAGED").

docs.title: MT-2-08 — Wingman menu and orders
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer (two wingmen) Steps 1. Press ]; choose 6 (status report). 2. ], 2 (attack my target) with a saucer targeted. 3. Shift+F (fire at will). 4. Shift+E (evasive). 5. Shift+I (ignore my target). 6. Shift+R (retreat). 7. With a gamepad: LB + left stick click, d-pad, A. Expected 1: a menu of six entries; one status line per wingman (name, hull %, shields %, order). 2: "WINGMEN: ATTACK MY TARGET"; both attack your target. 3: they engage saucers near you. 4: they weave unpredictably for about 10 s, then form up. 5: they return to formation and ignore your target. 6: they run and jump out ("… JUMPED OUT"). 7: the d-pad moves the highlight and A chooses; while the menu is open the d-pad does not change throttle or MFD; B closes it. Pressing E (roll) alone still rolls; Shift+E does not roll.

docs.title: MT-2-09 — Controls menu: keyboard rebinding and saving
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher → Controls (keyboard, gamepad, mouse); later the pause menu (Esc, K) in any scenario Steps 1. Select Fire missile, Key column, Enter, press V. 2. Select Cloaking device, Alt key column, Enter, press Shift+B. 3. Select Brake, Key column, Enter, press V. 4. Delete on a cell; D on an action; Shift+D. 5. Change Mouse flight range with Left/Right. 6. Esc; fly; open bindings.yaml. 7. Restart the game. Expected 1: the cell shows V; the status line confirms. 2: the cell shows Shift+B. 3: V moves to Brake and the status line says it was taken from Fire missile (whose cell is now empty). 4: the cell clears; D restores that action's defaults; Shift+D restores all. 6: the new bindings work at once; bindings.yaml contains them. 7: they persist. Esc during a capture cancels it; a capture with no input gives up after 8 s.

docs.title: MT-2-10 — Gamepad chord capture and modifier layer
docs.text: Field Preconditions An XInput-style controller. Scenario Launcher → Controls; then systems-trial Steps 1. On ECM, Gamepad column, press A (pad) to capture, then hold RB and press Y. 2. On Next MFD page, Alt gamepad column, capture a plain X (press and release). 3. Fly: hold LB and press each of A, B, X, Y, Back and the d-pad. 4. Press LB alone. 5. Press RB alone, then RB + Y. Expected 1: the cell shows the RB+Y chord. 2: plain X. 3: LB + A hyperspace, LB + B shield balance, LB + X tractor, LB + Y cloak, LB + Back ECM, LB + d-pad power controls (see Controls). 4: nothing happens (LB is a modifier). 5: RB is now a modifier too, so RB alone no longer cycles targets; RB + Y switches the ECM. Restore defaults with Y in the menu.

docs.title: MT-2-11 — Stick layout and mouse invert
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher → Controls, then rocket-vs-saucer Steps 1. Set Gamepad stick layout to aircraft; fly with the left stick. 2. Set it back to space. 3. Toggle Mouse flight: up = nose down; press C in flight and move the mouse up and down. Expected 1: left stick X rolls, right stick X yaws. 2: left stick X yaws, right stick X rolls. 3: with the option off, moving the cursor down lowers the nose; with it on, moving it up lowers the nose.

docs.title: MT-2-12 — Campaign switch
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher, with original data available Steps 1. Start the game; read the header. 2. Press Tab (pad Y). 3. Quit and start again. 4. Run openinterceptor --list, then --campaign interceptor. 5. Run with --no-original. Expected 1: "Campaign: X-COM: Interceptor (original data) (Tab: switch campaign)" (or the last campaign chosen). 2: content reloads; the header says Perils of the Void and the scenario list shows the default campaign's scenarios only. 3: the last choice is remembered (settings.yaml game.campaign). 4: --list marks the loaded campaign with *; --campaign overrides the remembered choice. 5: only Perils of the Void; no Tab hint.

docs.title: MT-2-13 — Default campaign look: cockpit and ships
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer, dominion-raid, black-comet-ambush; the model viewer; --no-original Steps 1. Fly each scenario in each rocket (Comet, Meteor, Thunderbolt), cockpit view and chase view. 2. Open the model viewer and step through every default-campaign class. 3. Destroy a few ships. 4. Listen. Expected 1: the art-deco Guard cockpit around the pilot with instruments in its bezels; rockets, flying saucers, robot sentinels, freighters and stations read as a 1950s film serial; faction colours on the radar. 2: every model solid from all sides, textured, no missing faces. 3: debris pieces and explosions. 4: the generated sounds (weapons, explosions, hits, tractor, cloak, ECM, hyperspace). No original file is needed.

docs.title: MT-2-14 — 3D cockpit on 4:3 and 16:9 windows
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer, cockpit view (F1) Steps 1. Start in the default 1280×960 (4:3) window. 2. Resize the window to 16:9 (or go full screen on a 16:9 display). 3. Optionally: openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --screenshot pit.png. Expected 1: the whole dashboard is visible, side to side; radars, MFD, gauges, message bar, power and systems sit inside their bezels (the view widens to fit the 16:9 design). 2: the normal 60° field; instruments still in their bezels. The cockpit never disappears into world objects and turns with the ship; F7 shows the rocket without the cockpit. 3: the PNG matches what step 1 shows.

docs.title: MT-2-15 — Anchored 3D-cockpit instruments
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer in a Comet, cockpit view (F1) Steps 1. Fly in the default 4:3 window. 2. Resize to 16:9, then to a tall narrow window and a very wide one. 3. Look at the radars, MFD, gauges, message bar, power and systems close up while turning and firing. Expected Every instrument lies on the dashboard inside its bezel, in perspective (tilted with the dashboard surface), at every window shape; nothing floats over the bezels or drifts when the window changes. Lines and text stay sharp and readable; radar contacts, needles and lamps update live. In the chase view (F7) the instruments return to their 2D places.

docs.title: MT-2-16 — Cockpit layout editor: 2D instruments
docs.text: Field Scenario flight-test in the Lightning II (cockpit A, 2D art), cockpit view Steps 1. Press F12. 2. Tab to the MFD; drag it; drag its bottom-right corner; nudge with the arrows (and Shift+arrows); use the wheel and +/-. 3. Shift+Tab back. 4. Press S. 5. Esc; fly; then quit and fly again. Expected 1: the battle pauses; "COCKPIT LAYOUT: " and a key summary at the top. 2: the rectangle moves and resizes with the mouse, nudges 1 or 10 design pixels, grows and shrinks by 5 % about its centre; never below a minimum size. 4: "Saved as an addon: …/mods/interceptor-cockpit-a/rules/cockpit-layout.yaml". 5: the new layout is used now and after a restart; --list shows the addon; disabling it restores the original layout.

docs.title: MT-2-17 — Cockpit layout editor: 3D placement and saving
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer in a Comet, cockpit view Steps 1. F12; Tab to mfd. 2. Click a different spot on the dashboard; click empty space through the canopy. 3. Wheel up and down. 4. S, then Esc. 5. Open the saved rules/cockpit-layout.yaml; run openinterceptor --check --no-original. Expected 2: the MFD jumps to the clicked spot, lying flat on that surface and facing the pilot ("mfd placed at …"); clicking empty space says "No cockpit surface under the cursor". 3: it grows and shrinks keeping its shape. 4: saved under <user data>/mods/default-cockpit-guard/. 5: the file holds cockpits: guard: instruments and anchors in valid YAML; --check reports no errors.

docs.title: MT-2-18 — YAML mistakes reported with file and line
docs.text: Field Preconditions A test mod copied from resources/default (before app 0.4.2: packs/default) into the mods folder (id changed). Steps In the copy: 1. misspell a key (max_sped: 700); 2. give a bad unit (range: 2.4kn); 3. indent one line with a tab; 4. write a condition with a typo (when: "hul < 20%"); 5. put a format-1 pack.ini folder beside it. Run openinterceptor --check --no-original after each, then open the launcher. Expected Each problem is reported with the file, line and key path: 1: "unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?)"; 2: "unknown unit 'kn' … (use m, km)"; 3: a tab error with the line; 4: "unknown name 'hul'" for that behaviour; 5: "pack.ini is the old INI mod format (format 1) …". --check exits with status 1 for 1–4; the launcher shows the problems in orange and still offers the rest of the content.

docs.title: MT-2-19 — Difficulty switch
docs.text: Field Scenario Launcher, default campaign Steps 1. Read the header. 2. Press D repeatedly (pad X). 3. Quit and start again. 4. Run with --difficulty space_ace, then --difficulty nonsense. 5. Switch to the interceptor campaign (Tab) and press D. Expected 1: "Difficulty: ranger (D: change)". 2: cadet → ranger → captain → space ace → cadet, content reloading each time. 3: the last level is remembered (settings.yaml game.difficulty). 4: space ace is used; an unknown level is reported and the middle level used. 5: beginner, experienced, veteran (default), genius, superhuman.

docs.title: MT-2-20 — Enemy accuracy by difficulty
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer in a Comet, at cadet and at space ace Steps 1. At each level, fly straight towards the saucers without firing for 30 s; watch their bolts. 2. Fight normally. 3. Optionally run openinterceptor --campaign default --soak rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --difficulty cadet and again with space_ace. Expected 1: at cadet most bolts miss wide, saucers fire short bursts with long pauses and no seeker rockets; at space ace bolts land close, bursts are long and rockets come. 2: cadet is clearly easier. Hurt saucers at captain and above sometimes flee. 3: the passive ship survives clearly longer at cadet than at space ace.

docs.title: MT-2-21 — HUD text fits the instruments
docs.text: Field Scenario Any, in a 2D cockpit, the 3D Guard cockpit and the glass HUD (F2); small and large windows Steps Page through every MFD page; trigger long messages (system damage, wingman status); watch the gauges, power and systems. Expected All text stays inside its instrument box at every window size; the MFD text size does not change between pages; nothing overlaps the next instrument.

docs.title: MT-2-22 — Station modules close up
docs.text: Field Scenario outpost-strike (default) and base-assault (interceptor); chase view (F7/F8) and cockpit Steps 1. Fly slowly round the station within a few hundred metres. 2. Watch the turrets/pods while the station turns. 3. Destroy one gun module. Expected 1: every module sits on the hull at its place, standing out from the surface (not sunk in, not floating, not upside down); no slot squares are visible anywhere. 2: modules stay locked to the hull as it turns; gun modules swivel and fire at you in bursts. 3: the module explodes with debris; on the default stations its blackened wreck stays mounted (wrecked texture); interceptor modules (no destroyed state) disappear.

docs.title: MT-2-23 — Shield modules and hub cascade
docs.text: Field Scenario outpost-strike, then base-assault Steps 1. Target the hub (T/R) and fire: watch the Target MFD's shields. 2. Destroy the shield pod (every shield module on the alien base). 3. Fire at the hub again. 4. Destroy the hub while some gun pods still live. Expected 1: hits land on the hub's shields first. 2: "STATION SHIELDS DOWN"; the hub's shields read 0 and stay at 0. 3: hits go to armour and hull at once. 4: the hub explodes and every remaining module and wreck goes with it, each with its own explosion.

docs.title: MT-2-24 — Missile guidance kinds and mines
docs.text: Field Scenario combat-test in the Super Avenger (--ship avenger; one of each special missile), and dominion-raid (default; mines) in the Meteor and the Thunderbolt Steps Cycle missiles (W) and fire each at a locked target: X-Winder, Sidestep, Permeator, Enveloping, Parallax, Passive Cloaking, Doppelganger; in the default campaign the cluster rocket (Thunderbolt) and the decoy rocket (Meteor). Let an enemy lock and fire at you after launching a parallax / decoy rocket. Fly near a Dominion space mine. Expected Sidestep weaves and turns hard near the target. Permeator's damage skips the target's shields; Enveloping drains both shield facings. Parallax/decoy: two decoys fly off; enemy missiles often chase them. Passive Cloaking: drops behind you, stops and waits; it strikes an enemy passing within about 800 m. Doppelganger: a copy of your ship flies off; enemies sometimes chase it; it vanishes after a while. Cluster: splits into six seekers before reaching the target. Mine: explodes when you come within ~100–160 m (by difficulty), damaging everything nearby, and is gone.

docs.title: MT-2-25 — Debris and damage showcase; viewer looks
docs.text: Field Scenario debris-showcase in both campaigns; the model viewer Steps 1. Look along the row of ships before firing. 2. Destroy them one by one with a single shot each, in cockpit and chase views. 3. In the model viewer, select a class and press D repeatedly. Expected 1: every ship already shows its worst damage textures (scorched/burnt). 2: each explodes with its effect (size, colour; a shock-wave ring on large ships and aliens), its debris pieces fly apart from where they belonged and tumble, rubble chunks scatter; pieces darken and vanish after their life. Interceptor wrecks use the original chunk meshes and, for aliens, floating body parts. 3: intact → each damage level → each state → debris pulled apart, with the look's name on the info line.

docs.title: MT-2-26 — Original sound cues
docs.text: Field Preconditions Original data. Scenario gunnery-range, systems-trial (interceptor) Steps Fire beams and missiles, lock on, take hits, destroy a drone, cycle targets, switch tractor/cloak/ECM, jump out (H). Run --check. Expected Each event plays the original's sound for its cue (laser Beam1, X-Winder Missile1, target lock, shield hit, small explosion, warp-out on the hyperjump …). --check reports no unknown cues. A test mod with sounds: {lock: cue:Nope} is reported as "unknown sound cue 'Nope'".

docs.title: MT-2-27 — Duels and target preferences
docs.text: Field Scenario Each duel-<enemy> arena of both campaigns; mixed-dogfight; escort (interceptor); rocket-vs-saucer (default) Steps 1. Fly each duel at the lowest and highest difficulty. 2. In mixed-dogfight, watch who attacks whom. 3. In escort, defend the freighter. 4. In rocket-vs-saucer, hang back behind your two wingmen. Expected 1: each enemy type flies and fights distinctly (saucers dart and dodge, the dreadnought's turrets track, the grappler/harbinger tries to tow disabled ships, robots are reckless); clearly harder at the top level. 2: several factions fight each other, not only the player. 3: the freighter is attacked and can be lost. 4: the saucers (prefer: {player: …}) still come for you, past wingmen up to about 1.3–1.5 times nearer; with no behaviour preference they would take the nearest ship. Station turrets (station_turret) shoot fighters before larger ships.

docs.title: MT-2-28 — Protected objectives and radar colours
docs.text: Field Scenario systems-trial (either campaign); rocket-vs-saucer (default) Steps 1. In systems-trial, look at the radar. 2. Press R (nearest enemy) repeatedly. 3. Press T until the prize is selected; read the MFD target page and the target brackets. 4. In rocket-vs-saucer, compare your wingmen's and the saucers' radar blips. Expected 1: the crippled saucer is cyan with a ring; enemies red; the asteroid yellow (neutral). 2: R never selects the prize while an enemy is detectable. 3: T reaches it; the MFD shows OBJECTIVE: PROTECT under its name and the bracket label starts PROTECT. 4: wingmen and your station green, saucers red.

docs.title: MT-2-29 — Cockpit text legibility
docs.text: Field Scenario rocket-vs-saucer and systems-trial (default), cockpit (3D) view and exterior view, at full screen and in a small window Steps 1. Read the throttle/speed line at the top left. 2. Read the dial labels (SPD NRG SHD HUL), the power labels and the system lamps. 3. Select a target and read the MFD. Expected All text is readable in both views; dials carry labels in the cockpit; the lamps rearrange into rows that fit their panel; long MFD lines end in .. rather than shrinking the page.

docs.title: MT-2-30 — Top display bar and shield rings
docs.text: Field Scenario duel-wraith (interceptor) flown in a Lightning, Firestar and Avenger (the three cockpits); rocket-vs-saucer (default), cockpit view Steps 1. Read the top bar at start. 2. Throttle up, use afterburner. 3. Let the Wraith shoot your nose, then your tail. 4. Lower shield power (F10) and watch the power strip. Expected 1: the message sits in the lit band; THR … m/s in the left strip; B-x S-x F100 A100 and SYSTEMS OK in the right strip; nothing overlaps the bar's dividers. 2: the throttle line updates and shows BURN. 3: the front scope's ring turns amber/red as the fore shield drops, then the rear's; a downed facing blinks red. 4: the power strip's letters change; a damaged system appears in the systems strip in amber/red.

docs.title: MT-2-31 — Point defence
docs.text: Field Scenario outpost-strike / base-assault (stations), duel-dreadnought (default) Steps 1. Lock a missile on the station or dreadnought from about 3 km and fire several. 2. Fire a parallax / decoy rocket near it. 3. Watch its energy on the Target MFD while it shoots. Expected 1: short tracers flash from the target towards your missiles inside about 1 km with the point_defence sound; roughly a third to two-fifths of shots destroy a missile, so some missiles still get through. 2: the guns also shoot at decoys. 3: each shot costs a little energy. Missile blasts show their own explosion effect (and sound, where the effect has one).

docs.title: MT-2-32 — Sensor and jamming probes
docs.text: Field Scenario probe-net in both campaigns Steps 1. At the start, look at the radar. 2. Fly towards the hostile jamming probe; watch the radar and try a missile lock inside 2.5 km of it. 3. Destroy the jamming probe and lock again. 4. Destroy your own sensor probe (or let the enemy do it). 5. Have a cloaked enemy in range (duel-shade / duel-raider-saucer). Expected 1: enemies around your sensor probe, 7 km ahead, already show on the radar, beyond your own radar range. 2: inside the jamming radius distant contacts disappear (half range) and the lock takes about twice as long. 3: normal again. 4: the far contacts vanish. 5: a cloaked enemy beyond its cloak range does not show on the radar, probe or not.

docs.title: MT-2-33 — AI pilots use cloak, ECM and power
docs.text: Field Scenario duel-raider-saucer (default), duel-shade (interceptor), rocket-vs-saucer Steps 1. Watch the raider saucers / Shade as they close in. 2. Fire missiles at enemies (and at the dreadnought or Guard pilots). 3. Damage an enemy below half hull and watch its shots. Expected 1: they stay cloaked (off the radar) until about 2 km from their target, then decloak to fire. 2: ships with ECM switch it on while your missiles are coming (your missiles lose lock more often). 3: hurt pilots favour shields: their shields recover faster and their beam fire slackens (slower capacitor recharge).

docs.title: MT-2-34 — Text keys and a translation addon
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Run the default campaign and read ship and scenario names. 2. Create mods/default-de/ with pack.yaml (kind: addon, targets: [default]) and text/de/ships.yaml renaming ship.comet.name. 3. Run with --language de, then set game: {language: de} in settings.yaml and run without the option. 4. Add a rule with name: "@ship.nope.name" and run --check. 5. With the CD: --check in the interceptor campaign. Expected 1: names read normally (no @ keys showing). 2–3: the Comet has the new name; every other string stays English (fallback to text/en/). 4: --check reports the missing key; in game it shows as the key. 5: the summary counts the texts, including the 3 645 imported orig.* strings.
