docs.title: The debrief (every mission case)
docs.text: Expected When the mission ends the battle freezes behind a panel: the headline for the result (MISSION ACCOMPLISHED / MISSION FAILED / MISSION ENDED / LEFT THE BATTLE, and YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED when the player died), the mission's debrief text for it (original text by key for interceptor), Kills n Losses n Time m:ss, each optional objective ticked or not, and "Campaign effects (applied by the strategy layer)" listing the outcome's campaign actions. Enter (pad A) flies the mission again; Esc or L returns to the launcher. Jumping out (H) before the end gives RETREAT; being destroyed gives YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED with the mission's killed text or none (never the lose text).

docs.title: MT-3-01 — defend_station
docs.text: Field Steps Win: defend the Guard station with your two Comet wingmen until all raiders and the late robot sentinels are destroyed. Lose: let the saucers destroy the station (dying gives killed, MT-3-17). Expected Raiders arrive from a random bearing 6 km beyond the station; "saucers inbound" chatter; robots arrive after 75 s ("robots" chatter); reinforcements when fewer than two raiders remain; "station hurt" chatter below 50 % hull. Win: debrief WIN with optional station untouched / no losses; campaign effects score(station_defended), salvage, relation(guard, +5). Lose: LOSE with lose(guard_station), score(station_lost).

docs.title: MT-3-02 — convoy_ambush
docs.text: Field Steps Win: protect the two cargo clippers until the hot-rods and the saucer (arrives after 40 s) are destroyed, or survive 4 minutes. Lose: let both clippers die. Expected Clippers are marked PROTECT; "ambush" chatter; "clipper lost" when one dies. Win after 4 min even with enemies left (timer). Lose: cargo_lost, score(convoy_lost); optional both clippers.

docs.title: MT-3-03 — construction_defence
docs.text: Field Steps Win: keep the research station at 60 % (scaffolding, no guns) alive; destroy the raiders and the wave after 90 s. Lose: let it fall. Expected The station shows its build_60 model, has no turrets or point defence; win needs all raiders destroyed and more than 95 s elapsed. Lose: lose(construction_site).

docs.title: MT-3-04 — intercept_scouts
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy every scout saucer. Draw: let 3 minutes pass with scouts alive. Lose: die. Expected Scouts ahead at 5 km (count by difficulty: 2 cadet … 4 space ace). After 3 min: DRAW with the draw debrief.

docs.title: MT-3-05 — xcom_base_defense
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy all Wraiths/Spectres attacking the X-COM base (a wave after 2 min). Lose: let the base fall. Expected Launcher name and briefing are the original's text (from LangFile1.txt, %s shown as written). Debriefs are the original's win/lose texts.

docs.title: MT-3-06 — defend_freighter_convoy
docs.text: Field Steps Win: protect two X-COM freighters until the Wraiths are destroyed or 4 minutes pass. Lose: let both freighters die. Expected Original texts; win by timer possible; lose lists cargo_lost.

docs.title: MT-3-07 — deep_space_encounter
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy every alien. Lose: die. Expected Original texts; campaign effects score(aliens_destroyed), salvage on a win.

docs.title: MT-3-08 — attack_alien_outpost
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy the alien outpost (4 km ahead, below) through its defenders. Lose: die. Expected Original texts; the defenders fight back; win as soon as the outpost is destroyed.

docs.title: MT-3-09 — destroy_alien_probe
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy the alien probe (drone) moving away at 5 km; from experienced up a Wraith escorts it. Draw: let 3 minutes pass. Lose: die. Expected Original win, draw and lose debriefs.

docs.title: MT-3-10 — Launcher mission list and scrolling
docs.text: Field Steps Open the launcher in each campaign; move down the whole list with the arrows and back up; click visible entries; select a mission. Expected After the scenarios come Mission: … entries in their order, each with its briefing as the description and the ship choice when the player chooses. The list scrolls to keep the selection near the middle, with "^ more" / "v more" markers when entries are hidden; clicking a visible entry selects it, clicking again starts it.

docs.title: MT-3-11 — --mission and retry from the debrief
docs.text: Field Steps openinterceptor --no-original --mission defend_station --ship meteor; finish the mission; press Enter; finish again; press Esc. Also try the pause menu's R during a mission, and an unknown id. Expected The mission starts directly in the Meteor; Enter restarts the same mission with the same ship; Esc returns to the launcher; R in the pause menu restarts; an unknown id shows an error.

docs.title: MT-3-12 — Soak baseline
docs.text: Field Steps For each mission: openinterceptor --campaign <c> --soak <mission> --soak-pilot ai --seconds 400 --difficulty <level> (interceptor with --ship avenger); then the passive pilot; for the defence missions also --soak-pilot idle. Expected (baseline at d7553f5) Default, ranger, AI pilot: defend_station lose at 132 s; convoy_ambush win at 64 s; construction_defence win at 97 s; intercept_scouts win at 72 s. Passive pilots lose or draw. Interceptor, Super Avenger: beginner wins all five; veteran: base defence lose, convoy win, deep space lose, outpost win, probe lose; superhuman mostly lose (three elerium torpedoes kill an Avenger: the original values 400 impact against 250 armour + 200 shield + 400 hull). Re-run after balance changes; a mission that only ever wins or only ever loses at every level needs attention. Expected (AI pilot, cadet, app 0.6.4, main 3866c34) colony_defence win at 43 s; outpost_raid win at 99 s; ground_strike, asteroid_hunt and pocket_ambush make kills (counted while running since 0.6.4) but are still running at 300 s. Expected (idle pilot, c583659) Default, defend_station: cadet still running at 400 s (the unit test holds ≥ 150 s); ranger lose at 140 s; space ace killed at 8 s. Interceptor, xcom_base_defense, beginner: the base still has about 2 390 of 6 000 hull at 400 s; the AI pilot wins in about 75 s with the base untouched. On veteran the result is killed at 15–18 s (elerium torpedoes), not lose.

docs.title: MT-3-13 — Drift readout and flight-path marker
docs.text: Field Steps openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --view chase (glass HUD); full throttle until about 300 m/s; throttle to 0; yaw 90° right and hold the nose there; then pitch up. Repeat in the cockpit view and with --campaign interceptor --ship avenger. Expected The status line reads THR n% <forward> m/s X<±n> Y<±n>. Flying straight: X and Y near 0 and the flight-path marker (a circle with ticks left, right and up) on the crosshair. After the yaw right the forward speed falls towards 0 and X becomes about −300 (drifting to the ship's left), and the marker slides to the left edge or off screen; pitching up makes Y negative. Brake (B) or match speed brings X and Y back to 0.

docs.title: MT-3-14 — Shot streaks while drifting and turning
docs.text: Field Steps As MT-3-13: set up a sideways drift (X about ±200), then fire beams (Enter) in the cockpit and chase views; then fire while yawing hard. Then make an addon with flight: {bolt_frame: ship, bolt_carry: 0.5s} and repeat. Expected Physics (default): drifting, shots streak straight out of the guns from the pilot's view (they share the drift) and do not slant across the screen. While yawing, shots leave straight from the muzzles and then stay on their line: the nose turns away from them. With bolt_frame: ship the shots swing round with the nose for about half a second, then fly straight.

docs.title: MT-3-15 — Distant dots and rim light
docs.text: Field Steps rocket-vs-saucer (default) and combat-test (interceptor, needs original data): let the enemies close from beyond 5 km, and fly away from them; look at them against the stars and against the sun. Fly a mission with a protected object (defend_station). Expected Far craft on the radar show as a dot in their radar colour (red hostile, green friendly, cyan for the protected station) that fades into the model as they come near, without a pop. Hulls seen side-on have a bright outline, dark alien hulls included. A cloaked enemy beyond sensor range shows no dot.

docs.title: MT-3-16 — Brightness setting
docs.text: Field Steps Quit; in settings.yaml set graphics: {brightness: 2}, start and look at a ship in shadow; then 0.5; then 9; then delete the key. Expected 2: shadowed hull areas clearly lighter, lit faces not washed out. 0.5: darker. 9 behaves as 2 (clamped). Without the key: as authored (1). The HUD and cockpit art are not affected.

docs.title: MT-3-17 — The killed debrief
docs.text: Field Steps --no-original --mission defend_station --ship comet --difficulty space_ace: fly at the raiders and let them kill you. Then --mission xcom_base_defense --ship lightning --difficulty veteran (needs original data) and do the same. Then let the station fall while you survive. Expected When the player dies: headline YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED, no base-lost text (or the mission's own killed text), campaign effects those of the mission's lose outcomes. When the station falls with the player alive: MISSION FAILED with the lose text.

docs.title: MT-3-18 — Keys overlay
docs.text: Field Steps In any flight press ? (Shift+/); look through the list; press ? again. Open it with Shift+F1 and close it with Esc. Rebind afterburner in the controls menu (Esc, K) to another key and clear its pad button, then open the overlay again. Press F1 (no Shift) in flight. Open the pause menu (Esc). Expected The battle pauses under a dark panel titled KEYS listing every action under its group (Flight, Throttle and speed, Weapons, Targeting, Power and systems, Wingmen and comms, Views, Chase camera, Interface), in several columns if needed, each with its current keys then pad buttons. After the rebinding the afterburner row shows the new key and no pad button (or "unbound" with neither). ?, Shift+F1 and Esc close it and the battle resumes. Plain F1 still selects the cockpit view. The pause menu shows a line pointing to ? instead of a key list. In a custom cockpit F12 still opens the layout editor.

docs.title: MT-3-19 — Console: pairing from an iPad
docs.text: Field Preconditions The computer and an iPad on the same Wi-Fi (not a guest network). App 0.4.7 or later. Steps 1. Start openinterceptor --console --no-original and stay on the launcher; read the terminal line and the launcher's console status. 2. On the iPad open the URL in Safari. 3. Type a wrong code three times. 4. Reload, and type the right code without pressing anything after the sixth digit. 5. Start rocket-vs-saucer with the Comet from the launcher; watch the telemetry while flying; open the menu (Esc) in the game. 6. Quit; start again with console: {enabled: true, port: 9000} in settings.yaml and no --console; open http://<address>:9000/?code=<code> directly. 7. Quit the game with the page open, then type a code. 8. Start a second program on the same port first (for example python3 -m http.server 9000), then the game. Expected 1: the terminal prints console: open http://<address>:8765 on the tablet; pairing code NNNNNN, and the launcher shows the console's address and code. 2: the pairing page asks for the code, with the number pad. 3: each wrong code shows wrong pairing code; after the third the page shows Disconnected. 4: Connecting… shows as the sixth digit is typed, then the console appears at once (no Enter needed), on the launcher; the craft cell reads Not flying (launcher) and every group and button is shown. 5: when the battle starts the buttons reflect the Comet (not fitted where it lacks equipment); craft, speed, drift, hull, energy, shields, missile and target update smoothly (about 20 times a second); the bottom-left hint shows again while the menu is open. 6: the page pairs from the address alone, on port 9000, without --console. 7: Could not reach the game. Is it still running? 8: the game reports that the port is not available and runs normally without the console.

docs.title: MT-3-20 — Console: hold and tap buttons
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired. Steps 1. Hold Yaw left (or another turn) on the iPad for two seconds, then lift the finger. 2. Hold Afterburner; slide the finger off the button while still touching the screen. 3. Hold Fire beams with an enemy ahead. 4. Tap Next target several times; tap a view button (cockpit, chase). 5. Hold a turn on the iPad and the opposite turn on the keyboard at the same time. Expected 1: the craft turns for as long as the button is held and stops when it is released, exactly as with the key. 2: the afterburner lights while held and goes out when the finger leaves the button. 3: beams fire continuously while held. 4: each tap moves the target once and changes the view once (no repeats). 5: the two inputs combine as two keys would; nothing sticks afterwards.

docs.title: MT-3-21 — Console: features not fitted
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired. Steps 1. In rocket-vs-saucer with the Comet, look at the Power and systems and Weapons groups. 2. Tap a disabled button. 3. Fly systems-trial (default) with the Thunderbolt, then with the Meteor, re-pairing if needed. 4. Run tools/console_client.py <address> <code> from the computer for each craft. Expected 1: every group is shown; actions the craft has no equipment for (for example cloak, ECM, tractor, the VCT slides, missiles or beams, whichever the craft lacks) are greyed and labelled not fitted; all other buttons are active. 2: nothing happens. 3: the Thunderbolt's cloak button is active; the list changes with the craft (the catalogue is resent when the craft class changes). 4: the client's not fitted: list matches the greyed buttons.

docs.title: MT-3-22 — Console: reconnecting and letting go
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired. Steps 1. Hold Yaw left and, while holding, close the Safari tab with the other hand. 1b. Open the page again, pair, hold Yaw left and turn the iPad's Wi-Fi off; time how long the craft keeps turning. 2. Turn Wi-Fi back on and reload the page. 3. Quit the game with the page open; start it again; enter the new code. 4. Pair a second device (a phone or a laptop browser) at the same time; hold a turn on one and release on the other. Expected 1: the craft stops turning as soon as the tab closes (the console's held actions are released). 1b: the craft stops turning once the game notices the connection is gone; record the delay in the notes. C1 has no keep-alive or write timeout, so after a Wi-Fi drop this may take as long as the system's TCP timeout: a delay of more than a few seconds is a finding to file. 2: the page reconnects with the remembered code and the console returns. 3: the page shows Disconnected. Enter the code to reconnect.; the old code is refused (wrong pairing code), the new one pairs. 4: both devices show telemetry; one device releasing does not release the other's held button.

docs.title: MT-3-23 — Console: throttle slider
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired. Steps 1. Drag the throttle slider from 0 to 100 % and back, slowly and then quickly. 2. Change the throttle from the keyboard (or stick) while not touching the slider. 3. Set 50 % on the slider, then hold the keyboard's throttle-up key. Expected 1: the craft's throttle (HUD THR) follows the slider and the percentage label; no lag beyond a frame or two. 2: the slider moves to follow the game's throttle. 3: the keyboard changes the throttle from 50 % and the slider follows; the slider does not fight it while untouched.

docs.title: MT-3-24 — Original data from resources/xcom or resources/xcom-cd; start-up without a shader error
docs.text: Field Preconditions A checkout at app 0.4.2 or later. For steps 2–4, your own original data. Steps 1. With resources/xcom/ and resources/xcom-cd/ empty and no other data configured, start the game and run --list. 2. Put a CD copy in resources/xcom-cd/; run --list and the launcher. 3. Also put an installed copy in resources/xcom/; run --list. 4. Run scripts/check.sh; git status. 5. Build the app with python3 tools/build_bundle.py and open it from Finder. Expected Every start shows no shader error (the lit shader links; app 0.4.1) and ships are lit. 1: only the default campaign loads, with no error. 2: interceptor loads from the CD copy. 3: the installed copy is used (it is tried first). 4: the gate runs the original-data checks on the folder found and passes; git status shows nothing under resources/xcom*. 5: the app opens with the default campaign (Contents/Resources/resources/default) and the bundled mods, and finds the original data through settings.yaml.

docs.title: MT-3-25 — Simple physics for beginners
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.4.6 or later. Steps 1. Start openinterceptor --no-original; on the launcher set difficulty (D) to the first level and press P until it reads Physics: Simple. 2. Start rocket-vs-saucer with the Comet. Full throttle, then yaw 90° and hold the nose there; throttle down to 0; collide gently with the saucer. 3. Back on the launcher, press P to Realistic and repeat step 2. 4. Step D through the levels to the fourth (space_ace in the default campaign) and press P. 5. Back on the first level, quit and start again. Expected 1: the launcher's campaign line reads Physics: Simple (P: change); settings.yaml gets game: {physics: simple}. 2: the HUD status line shows SIMPLE; the craft always travels where its nose points — after the yaw the velocity turns with the nose and the drift readout stays X 0 Y 0; at throttle 0 the craft slows to a stop; after the collision any sideways drift is gone at once. Enemy craft behave as before. 3: no SIMPLE on the HUD; the craft drifts after the yaw, as in MT-3-13. 4: on the second and third levels Simple is still offered; on the fourth the line reads Physics: Realistic (always, at this level), P does nothing and the HUD shows no SIMPLE. 5: the choice is remembered.

docs.title: MT-3-26 — Console: the tablet stays awake
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired, on an iPad over plain http. iPad Auto-Lock set to its shortest time (for example 30 seconds). App 0.4.8 or later. Steps 1. Pair, then leave the iPad untouched on the console page for three times the Auto-Lock time, on the launcher and then in a battle. 2. Read the telemetry's Tablet cell. 3. Switch to another app and back to Safari; wait again. 4. Lock the iPad, unlock it and return to the page; tap once if the cell asks. 5. Repeat step 1 in a desktop browser opened on http://127.0.0.1:8765 on the game's computer. Expected 1: the iPad's screen does not dim or lock while the page is open. 2: the cell reads screen kept awake (the silent video; Safari offers no wake lock over http). No video is visible and no sound plays. 3 and 4: after returning, the cell again reads screen kept awake (at most after one tap, when it says tap the screen to keep it awake), and the screen stays on. 5: the cell reads screen kept awake (wake lock). If the iPad still sleeps, record it as a finding; the user-guide fallback is Settings › Display & Brightness › Auto-Lock.

docs.title: MT-3-27 — Console: press feedback and hit static
docs.text:
Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired, in rocket-vs-saucer with the Comet. App 0.4.9 or later. Steps 1. Hold Yaw left for two seconds, then release. 2. Tap Next target quickly, several times. 3. Let the saucer shoot you while your shields are up. 4. Let it keep shooting until hits reach the hull. 5. Fly clear and watch the console for a while without being hit. Expected 1: the button fills with its border colour and its text turns black for the whole hold, and returns to normal on release. 2: every tap visibly lights the button (at least about 0.15 s), even a very quick one. 3: each shield hit shows a light burst of static on the console, about 0.4 s, fading out. 4: hull hits show a stronger static burst. 5: no static without hits; the buttons stay readable during the effect.

Hit static (steps 3–5): confirmed by the user, 2026-11-11 — "Hit static - correct, works well now". The full case is still to be recorded as run.

docs.title: MT-3-28 — No shot from the start key
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.4.10 or later. Steps 1. In the launcher choose defend_station (default) and press Enter, holding it for a second. 2. Release Enter, then press it again. 3. Open the menu (Esc) and restart (R); then end the mission and press Enter on the debrief, holding it. 4. With a gamepad, start a mission with A and keep it held; release it and press again. 5. Start a mission while holding the fire mouse button (mouse flight on). Expected 1: no beam fires at the start, however long Enter is held. 2: the second press fires normally. 3: the retried mission starts without a shot. 4: no A action in flight until A is released and pressed again. 5: no shot until the mouse button is released and pressed again.

docs.title: MT-3-29 — Console: two layouts and function-group tiles
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired, on an iPad in landscape, in systems-trial (default) with a craft that lacks some equipment (for example no cloak or no missiles). App 0.4.11 or later. Steps 1. Tap All-in-one, then Cockpit at the top. 2. Reload the page. 3. Open the address with ?mode=allinone. 4. In Cockpit: read the HUD strip, the shield rings and the display console while flying, firing and taking hits. 5. Tap the shield balance buttons Fore, Equal, Aft. 6. Drag the beam and shield power sliders. 7. Tap the Weapons tile, then its title again, then the Flight tile's title while Weapons is open. 8. Look at the tiles' status cards. Expected 1: the layout switches at once; both show live values. 2: the last layout chosen comes back. 3: All-in-one is shown. 4: the strip shows speed, drift, throttle, hull, energy, target and status; the rings fill and colour with the shields; the display console shows the target's data. 5: the game's shield balance changes, and the button that matches it is lit. 6: the levels change in the game's power readout within the budget; a slider moves back if the budget does not allow it. 7: Weapons opens a full-width strip of its buttons and the other tiles fold to their titles; tapping its title closes the strip and all cards show; tapping Flight switches the strip to Flight. 8: a group with missing equipment says how many controls are not fitted; those buttons are greyed and cannot be pressed. Everything fits the iPad screen without scrolling sideways.

docs.title: MT-3-30 — Console: the target view
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired, Cockpit layout, Target tab, in mixed-dogfight (default). App 0.4.14 or later. Steps 1. Without a target, look at the view. 2. Target a scout saucer (next_target until one is selected). 3. Turn so that it flies across your nose, then fly behind it, then let it come at you head-on. 4. Cycle to a craft of another class (a hotrod, then the hauler). 5. Reload the page and pair again while a target is selected. Expected 1: the view is empty; the data reads No target. 2: within a moment the saucer's model appears, flat-shaded in a few colours that match its look, lit from the upper left. 3: the model turns as its true orientation relative to your craft changes: side-on when crossing, tail towards you when you are behind it, nose towards you head-on; the motion is smooth (20 updates a second). 4: the model changes to the new class each time; switching back to an earlier class is immediate. 5: the model appears again after pairing. No stutter in the game while a model is sent.

docs.title: MT-3-31 — Console: map views, gestures and tap to target
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired, Cockpit layout, Map tab, in mixed-dogfight (default). App 0.4.15 or later. Steps 1. Look at the map in the Behind view, then Top, then Side. 2. Drag with one finger left, right, up and down. 3. Pinch in and out. 4. Fly so that enemies are above and below you. 5. Tap an enemy's mark on the map. 6. Tap a row of the list beside the map. 7. Tap a contact just as it leaves radar range (fly away from a distant one). 8. Switch to the Target tab and watch the message lines while fighting. Expected 1: range rings at a quarter, half and full radar range on a grid at your height; your craft at the centre; in Top, ahead is up the screen. 2: the view orbits around you smoothly. 3: the map zooms in and out (within limits). 4: each contact has a stalk to the grid, up or down; colours: green friendly (your wingman), red hostile, yellow neutral, blue an objective; stations are squares; labels show name and range in km; a short tick points where each will be in two seconds. 5 and 6: the game's target changes to that craft at once (the HUD and the Target tab show it, and the contact is ringed on the map and highlighted in the list). 7: a contact no longer on radar is not targeted. 8: the last four lines of the game's message log appear under the target data, in step with the cockpit's message line.

docs.title: MT-3-32 — Console: themes per campaign and per cockpit
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-19 paired on an iPad. App 0.5.0 or later. For steps 4–6, original data for the interceptor campaign. Steps 1. Start the game with the default campaign and pair from the launcher. 2. Start rocket-vs-saucer (default). 3. Press a few buttons, open a tile, look at the map and the shield rings. 4. Start the game with the interceptor campaign and pair again from the launcher. 5. Fly combat-test in the Lightning (cockpit A), then the Firestar (cockpit B), then the Avenger (cockpit C). 6. Return to the launcher. Expected 1–3: the art-deco look: brass lines on midnight panels, cream text, amber values, a Futura-like font, small corners; a pressed button fills with brass; every control keeps its label and stays readable. 4: the green instrument look on a dark background. 5: the frames and highlights take each cockpit's tint — olive bronze for A, steel blue for B, red for C — as each battle starts. 6: the base look of the current campaign. No original image appears anywhere on the console.

docs.title: MT-3-33 — Hazard: asteroid field
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.5.1 or later; --no-original is enough. Steps 1. Start hazard-asteroids (default) in any craft. 2. Fly into the field; watch the radar as you approach. 3. Shoot an asteroid until it breaks up. 4. Fly into one at moderate speed. 5. Quit and start the scenario again. Expected 1: 45 asteroids tumble slowly ahead, none near your start. 2: asteroids appear on the radar only once within radar range, not from the start; the two saucers fly among them. 3: hits land and the asteroid is destroyed with its explosion and debris. 4: a collision with its sound and damage. 5: the field is laid out the same way every time.

docs.title: MT-3-34 — Hazard: black hole
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.5.1 or later. Steps 1. Start hazard-black-hole (default). 2. Look towards the hole (ahead and slightly below). 3. Cut the throttle and let it pull you in, watching the speed. 4. Before the core, turn away and burn out with the afterburner. 5. Watch the saucers for a few minutes. 6. Finally, fly into the black core. Expected 2: a black sphere hides the stars behind it, ringed by a slowly turning ring of orange glows. 3: the speed towards it grows, faster the closer you get. 4: you can still escape outside the core with full thrust. 5: the saucers fight but veer away from the hole; none falls in. 6: your craft is destroyed as it crosses the core's edge, and missiles fired near it curve towards it.

docs.title: MT-3-35 — Hazard: minefield in an ion storm
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.5.1 or later. Steps 1. Start hazard-minefield (default). 2. Read the first message. 3. Watch the radar while flying towards the hauler ahead. 4. Try a missile lock on a mine or on the hauler. 5. Fly close to a mine. Expected 2: ION STORM: SENSORS AT 50% at the start. 3: contacts appear at about half the usual radar range, so the mines show up late. 4: the lock builds visibly slower than in rocket-vs-saucer. 5: the mine goes off as in the Stage 2 mine cases.

docs.title: MT-3-36 — Hazards in the interceptor campaign
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.5.1 or later; original data for the interceptor campaign. Steps 1. Start hazard-asteroids (interceptor). 2. Read the first message and watch the radar. 3. Start hazard-black-hole (interceptor) and fight the Wraith and the Spectre. Expected 1: the original's asteroid model fills the belt and tumbles. 2: ION STORM: SENSORS AT 40%; the radar range is short. 3: the black core and accretion ring as in MT-3-34; the aliens steer clear of the hole.

docs.title: MT-3-37 — Orbit: the planet backdrop
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. Start env-orbit (default). 2. Look around, down and to the right. 3. Fight the two saucers. 4. Return to the launcher. Expected 2: a large blue planet below and ahead, lit on the sun's side with a darker limb, behind the stars and all craft. Flight is ordinary space flight. 4: the launcher and any other scenario show plain black space (no planet carried over).

docs.title: MT-3-38 — Pocket: the small arena
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. Start env-pocket (default). 2. Note the purple planet behind you. 3. Fly straight out at full speed. Expected 2: a purple planet fills a large part of the sky behind the start. 3: within about 12 km of the centre the flight is halted with ARENA BOUNDARY (much sooner than in other scenarios).

docs.title: MT-3-39 — Moon surface: sky, stars, fog and cratered terrain
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. Start surface-moon (default). 2. Look at the sky up, at the horizon and down. 3. Fly low over the ground towards the far edge. 4. Look at a distant crater and fly towards it. Expected 2: a dark violet sky shading to a lighter mauve horizon, stars showing faintly through; grey, cratered ground below, lit by the sun, with darker steep crater walls and raised rims. 3: the ground fades into the fog colour with distance; no hard terrain edge is visible before the fog. 4: the crater gains detail and colour as you near it; no seams or holes in the ground; no flicker.

docs.title: MT-3-40 — Dusk hills: sky, fog and hill terrain
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. Start surface-hills (default). 2. Look around. 3. Fly low through the valleys. Expected 2: a warm dusk sky — deep blue above, orange at the horizon — with almost no stars; rolling green-brown hills with darker slopes. 3: hills ahead fade in out of an orange haze; the hills block the view of craft behind them.

docs.title: MT-3-41 — Atmospheric flight feels distinct from space (Stage 3 exit)
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later; Realistic physics (MT-3-25). Steps 1. In surface-hills with a Comet, fly level at full throttle, note the top speed; then cut the throttle. 2. Slow to under 120 m/s and hold the nose level. 3. Bank to 60° and pull. 4. Repeat 1 – 3 in surface-moon. 5. Compare with the same manoeuvres in rocket-vs-saucer (space). 6. Watch a saucer in surface-hills. Expected 1: the top speed is lower than in space; with the throttle cut the craft slows down by itself. 2: below the stall speed the craft sinks (VS negative) even with the nose level. 3: the craft turns by banking and loses some height if not pulled harder. 4: on the moon the top speed is higher, stalling needs more speed but the sink is slow (low gravity). 5: in space nothing slows or pulls the craft — the difference is plain. 6: saucers hover and do not sink. Record the developer's verdict on "feels distinct from space".

docs.title: MT-3-42 — Landing and crashing
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. In surface-moon, descend to a flat crater floor and touch down gently (under 25 m/s of sink), wings level. 2. Take off again. 3. Dive into the ground steeply at speed. 4. Touch down gently but rolled over 60°. Expected 1: the craft lands: it stops sinking, slides to a halt, no damage, no collision sound. 2: it can climb away. 3: a crash: collision sound, heavy damage (or destruction at high speed), a bounce. 4: a crash, although slow, because the craft is not upright.

docs.title: MT-3-43 — The ceiling exit
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. In surface-hills, climb steeply at full throttle, watching ALT. 2. Pass a height of 7 km (ALT plus the ground's height; the hills reach 1.4 km). Expected 2: the battle ends for you as by a hyperspace jump, with LEFT THE ATMOSPHERE in the message log (the retreat path in a mission).

docs.title: MT-3-44 — ALT / VS and the artificial horizon
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.0 or later. Steps 1. In surface-moon, read the status line while climbing and diving. 2. Fly over a crater rim and down into the crater at constant height. 3. Look at the forward view while pitching up and down and rolling. 4. Switch to chase and cockpit views. 5. Start env-orbit. Expected 1: ALT n VS ±n after the speed: VS positive climbing, negative diving. 2: ALT changes with the ground below although your height does not. 3: a level horizon line ahead with rungs at ±10° and ±20°, labelled; the horizon line stays level with the real horizon as you roll, and the rungs move as you pitch. 4: the instruments stay readable in each view. 5: no ALT, VS or horizon in space.

docs.title: MT-3-45 — Ground installation: defend the colony
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.1 or later. Steps 1. Start surface-colony (default). 2. Find the colony (protected) on the ground ahead. 3. Fight off the two raider saucers. 4. Let a saucer attack the colony. Expected 2: the colony sits on the moon's surface — neither floating above it nor buried — in the objective colour with a PROTECT label and radar ring. 3 – 4: the saucers attack it; hits on it are shown; it does not move or fall.

docs.title: MT-3-46 — Ground installations: flak strike
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.1 or later. Steps 1. Start surface-strike (default). 2. Locate the three flak batteries on the hillside ahead. 3. Fly low and slow past one. 4. Attack fast and keep moving; destroy all three. Expected 2: each battery sits on the ground where it stands, at different heights on the slope. 3: the batteries turn and fire death rays at you across a wide arc. 4: each can be destroyed; the turret stops firing when destroyed.

docs.title: MT-3-47 — Voices: wingmen answer orders and status requests
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.2 or later; default campaign; sound on. Steps 1. Start rocket-vs-saucer in any ship (your two Comet wingmen have the guard_pilot voice). 2. Open the comms menu (]) and give each order in turn: 1 fire at will, 2 attack my target, 3 ignore my target, 4 evasive, 5 retreat. 3. Ask for a status report (6). 4. Repeat a few orders. Expected 2: each order plays the short acknowledge radio chirp, as well as the order's message line. 3: the status request plays the different status chirp, with one message line per wingman. 4: the radio answers every time; nothing plays when no wingman is alive.

docs.title: MT-3-48 — Voices: a wingman lost
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.2 or later; default campaign. Steps 1. Start rocket-vs-saucer. 2. Order the wingmen to attack (], 2) and let the saucers destroy one (stay back). 3. Let the second be destroyed too. Expected 2: when the first wingman is destroyed, the down clip plays (said by the surviving wingman). 3: when the last one is destroyed, nothing is said — nobody is left to say it.

docs.title: MT-3-49 — Voices: spoken chatter
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.2 or later (the mission from 0.6.4). Steps 1. Start Mission: Colony defence. 2. Wait for the first chatter line (about 3 s). 3. Let the colony fall below half hull. Expected 2: "Colony control: saucers on the horizon, coming in low!" on the message line, with a radio clip playing at the same moment. 3: "we're taking hits" appears with no clip (that line has no voice:).

docs.title: MT-3-50 — Voices: the computer voice at the debrief
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.2 or later. Step 3 needs original data. Steps 1. Win any default mission (intercept_scouts is quick). 2. Lose one, or be shot down, or jump out (H). 3. In the interceptor campaign, win and lose xcom_base_defense. 4. In the interceptor campaign, give wing orders in flight-test. Expected 1: the mission win sting plays once as the debrief appears. 2: the mission fail sting plays once for lose, killed, draw or retreat. 3: the original computer voice says the mission was accomplished, or failed. 4: the wingmen answer silently (their pilot clips are not mapped yet; R-MSN-007 Open note).

docs.title: MT-3-51 — Simulator: the setup rows
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.3 or later. Steps 1. Open the launcher (default campaign); the selection starts on the first scenario. Move up to Simulator (set up a mission and fly it) and press Enter. 2. Move through every row with Up/Down; change each with Left and Right. 3. Choose a mission whose player craft is fixed, if the campaign has one. 4. Esc. 5. Tab to interceptor (original data) and open the simulator again. Expected 1: the SIMULATOR screen, rows Mission, Ship, Environment, Asteroids, Minefield, Black hole, Ion storm, Enemy force, Fly; the chosen row highlighted; the mission's briefing below. 2: Mission cycles every mission (briefing follows); Ship the playable ships; Environment " (the mission's)" or "open space", then each environment; the four hazards on/off; Enemy force x0.5, x1, x1.5, x2; all wrap. 3: Ship shows "(the mission's own)". 4: back to the launcher. 5: the interceptor's missions; a hazard the campaign has no class for reads "(none in this campaign)" and does not change.

docs.title: MT-3-52 — Simulator: Fly with environment, hazards and force
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.3 or later; default campaign. Steps 1. Simulator: Defend the station, Comet, defaults; Fly. 2. Again with Environment moon_surface, all four hazards on, force x2. 3. Again with force x0.5 and orbit. Expected 1: the mission exactly as from the launcher. 2: the battle is over the moon (sky, craters, ALT/VS); asteroids and mines ahead, a black hole far ahead and below whose pull you feel when you approach, "ION STORM: SENSORS AT 40%" at the start; about twice the raiders (and robots) of a normal run, while your two wingmen and the station are unchanged. Note where the station sits: static objects other than ground installations are neither lifted nor set down over a terrain, so a space mission's station may sit partly inside a hill or crater rim — record what you see. 3: a planet in the sky; about half the raiders, never none.

docs.title: MT-3-53 — Simulator: again with the same setup
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.3 or later. Steps 1. Fly a simulator setup with a non-default environment and a hazard. 2. Finish the battle (win, lose or die) and press Enter at the debrief. 3. During that battle, open the pause menu and press R. 4. Esc or L from the debrief. Expected 2 – 3: the same mission starts again with the same ship, environment, hazards and force (not the unmodified mission). 4: back to the launcher.

docs.title: MT-3-54 — Simulator: a ship that cannot enter an atmosphere
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.3 or later. A test addon mods/default-noair/ with pack.yaml (kind: addon, targets: [default]) and rules/ships.yaml setting ships: {meteor: {atmospheric: false}}. Steps 1. Simulator: a mission that lets you choose, Ship Meteor, Environment dusk_hills; Fly. 2. Change any row. 3. Environment orbit; Fly. 4. Remove the addon. Expected 1: nothing starts; "The Meteor cannot enter an atmosphere: choose another ship or environment." in orange under the rows. 2: the message clears. 3: the battle starts (space is fine).

docs.title: MT-3-55 — colony_defence
docs.text: Field Steps Win: keep the Guard colony on the moon alive and destroy every raider and the reinforcements that come after 90 s. Lose: let the saucers destroy the colony. Also be shot down once. Expected Over moon_surface; the colony 3 km ahead, set down on the ground, marked PROTECT; raiders 7 km beyond it, starting at least 300 m above the ground; "Colony control: saucers on the horizon" with a radio clip; "taking hits" below 50 %. Win: score(colony_defended), relation(guard, +5), optional colony untouched. Lose: lose(guard_colony), score(colony_lost). Killed: "Your rocket was shot down."

docs.title: MT-3-56 — ground_strike
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy every flak battery in the hills (3 at cadet … 6 at space ace). Draw: let 6 minutes pass. Also be shot down once. Expected Over dusk_hills; the batteries spread along the slopes 4 km ahead, on the ground, firing at you; two scout saucers arrive after 60 s ("saucers inbound"); "Flak batteries ahead" at the start. Win: score(flak_destroyed), the flak win text. After 6 min: DRAW with "Some batteries still stand".

docs.title: MT-3-57 — outpost_raid
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy the Dominion outpost with your two Meteor wingmen. Also be shot down once, and jump out once. Expected In orbit (planet backdrop); the outpost 5 km ahead with guards (raider saucers, robot sentinels) around it; win when the outpost is destroyed, whatever guards remain: score(outpost_destroyed), salvage. Killed and retreat show their own texts.

docs.title: MT-3-58 — asteroid_hunt
docs.text: Field Steps Win: find and destroy every scout among the asteroids. Draw: let 5 minutes pass. Expected Open space with 50 turning cosmium asteroids in a 5 km field ahead, shown on radar only within range; the scouts spread among them. Win: score(scouts_destroyed); after 5 min: DRAW.

docs.title: MT-3-59 — pocket_ambush
docs.text: Field Steps Win: destroy every hot-rod. Also be shot down once. Expected The pocket environment (a 12 km arena under a purple planet); "ION STORM: SENSORS AT 65%" at the start and a shorter radar range; hot-rods 3 km away. Win: score(raiders_destroyed), relation(raiders, -5).

docs.title: MT-3-60 — Ground to the horizon
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.7 or later. Steps 1. Start surface-strike (default). 2. Climb to 3 km and look all round, then to the edge of the fog. 3. Fly straight in one direction for well over 15 km (past the field's edge), low over the ground. 4. Fly into a hill beyond the edge. Expected 1–2: ground everywhere up to the fog; no edge, gap or wall where the field ends. 3: the hills continue as a mirror image of the field; no seam, no step and no flicker where tiles meet; the frame rate stays smooth. 4: a hill beyond the edge is solid: the craft crashes or lands exactly where the drawn ground is (collision and drawing agree).

docs.title: MT-3-61 — Console: the textured target
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-3-30 passes. App 0.6.7 or later. Steps 1. Default campaign, mixed-dogfight: target a scout saucer, then a hot-rod. 2. interceptor campaign (original data), combat-test: target an alien fighter and a station. 3. Cycle quickly between classes. Expected 1–2: the Target view shows the craft with its own textures, not flat colours: markings and panels where they are in the game, wrapped correctly (no stretched or smeared faces); for a moment after a class change the flat colours may show, then the textures appear. 3: no stutter in the game; each class's model appears within about a second.

docs.title: MT-3-62 — AI avoidance: wingmen do not ram
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.7 or later. Steps 1. Start rocket-vs-saucer (default) with wingmen. 2. Fly straight, then brake hard and turn sharply across their path. 3. Order attack my target (Shift+A), then form up (Shift+I), several times. 4. Fly head-on at a wingman as it forms up. Expected 1–3: wingmen break away and ease off instead of flying into you or each other; they return to their slots. 4: the wingman swerves well before contact. No collisions caused by the AI in several minutes.

docs.title: MT-3-63 — AI avoidance: enemies do not ram, firing passes go on
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.7 or later. Steps 1. Start mixed-dogfight (default); fly among the enemies, sometimes head-on at one. 2. Watch enemies attacking you and each other's paths crossing. 3. Fly defend_station at cadet without fighting (idle) and watch the raiders' runs on the station. Expected 1: an enemy on a collision course swerves late but in time; it still fires on its pass (firing passes are not broken off early). 2: enemies do not collide with each other. 3: raiders press their attacks close to the station without flying into it; the station holds at least 150 s (R-MSN-011).

docs.title: MT-3-64 — The battle runs on before the debrief
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.7.4 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. Win defend_station (or any mission). 2. Win again and press Enter during the countdown. 3. Be shot down in a mission. 4. Leave a mission from the pause menu (L). 5. In an addon set flight: {debrief_delay: 0s} and win once more. Expected 1: "MISSION ACCOMPLISHED" at once with the computer voice; the battle keeps running (the last explosion plays out, wingmen fly on); "Debrief in 30 s (Enter: now)" counts down; the debrief appears at 0. 2: the debrief appears at once. 3: "YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED", the camera on the wreck, then the debrief after the countdown. 4: the debrief at once (retreat). 5: the debrief at once.

docs.title: MT-3-65 — Action descriptions: keys overlay and tablet
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.1 or later (main bb04952). Default campaign. A tablet paired for steps 3 – 4 (Tablet console). Steps 1. In a wide window start any mission and press ?. 2. Make the window small (or the display narrow) and press ? again. 3. On the paired tablet, open the Cockpit layout and a tile's strip; read the buttons. 4. Hover (or long-press) a button. 5. Leave the battle to the launcher and look at the tablet again. Expected 1: under each action's name and keys a dimmer one-sentence description (for example what the afterburner does); groups and columns as before. 2: one line per action, no descriptions, every action still listed (more columns if needed). 3: each button has its label and, beneath it, a small caption of at most two lines. 4: the full sentence as the button's tooltip. 5: the idle catalogue (every action available) shows the same captions. No caption overlaps the next button.

docs.title: MT-3-66 — Condition console in battle
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.5 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --mission colony_defence --ship comet. 2. After a few seconds press the backquote key (`). 3. Type count(raiders). 4. Change it to alive(colony) and time > 10s, then to hull(colony). 5. Type count(friends). 6. Clear the line with Backspace. 7. Type random(0.5) and watch it for a few seconds. 8. Press Esc (or ` again). 9. Start any scenario (--scenario rocket-vs-saucer) and press `. Expected 2: a dark panel along the bottom with a sky-blue frame: *CONDITION CONSOLE (or Esc to close; the battle is paused)*, a prompt> _with a blinking caret and the hint *(type a condition, e.g. alive(player) and time > 30s)*; the battle stops (ships, missiles and the clock). The backquote itself is not typed. 3:= 2(or the level's count of raiders) in green. 4:= trueor= false, changing as you type; then a number. 5: an orange error naming the unknown role. 6: the hint again. 7: a steadytrueorfalse` — it does not flicker, because the console evaluates on a copy of the battle's random generator. 8: the console closes and the battle carries on from where it stopped. 9: no mission: conditions belong to missions in orange.
