docs.title: Stage 4 cases
docs.text: How to start: the launcher with the default campaign (--no-original, or Tab to it) selects Campaign: continue first; Campaign: new game is next. Or --no-original --strategy. Keys: User guide › Campaign. Since app 0.16.0 every row action is also a button and the S and F keys are gone: in MT-4-06 sell with Sell 1, in MT-4-12 fit with Fit best (MT-4-29 – MT-4-34 cover the new screen).

docs.title: MT-4-01 — Formations: Shift+O
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.6.6 or later. Steps 1. Start rocket-vs-saucer (default) with wingmen, chase view (F-key for chase or --view chase). 2. Press Shift+O five times, waiting a few seconds each time. 3. Press Shift+O once more. 4. Order evasive (Shift+E), wait 10 s. 5. Fly outpost_raid (two Meteor wingmen). 6. Interceptor campaign: repeat 2 in a scenario with wingmen. 7. A scenario with no wingmen: Shift+O. Expected 1: wingmen in a vee behind you. 2: each press shows WINGMEN: FORM LINE ABREAST, ECHELON, BOX, DIAMOND, VEE in turn, and the wingmen move into that shape: level beside you; a diagonal back and right; rows of two behind you; left, right and behind. 3: wraps to LINE ABREAST. 4: after evasive they return to the last formation ordered. 5: both wingmen in slots of a vee, not on top of each other. 6: the same shapes. 7: NO WINGMEN.

docs.title: MT-4-02 — Campaign: a new game and the map
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Launcher (default): note the first two entries. 2. Campaign: new game. 3. Look at the map and the Bases tab. 4. Click Ajax on the map; look at the Bases tab. 5. Click the far east of the map, where nothing is drawn. Expected 1: Campaign: continue, Campaign: new game, selection on continue. 2: the strategy screen, paused, dated 2084-03-01, funds 2,500,000, score 0. 3: six systems and seven lanes; the Gatehouse at Mercury Gate with its sensor circle; no dark moon. Bases tab: * Gatehouse - Mercury Gate: 3 modules (0 building); researching nothing. 4: a row Build a Guard base at Ajax (1,800,000). 5: nothing is chosen (hidden systems cannot be clicked).

docs.title: MT-4-03 — Campaign: the clock, speeds and auto-pause
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Press 1, 2, 3 and 4 in turn, watching the date. 2. Space twice. 3. Leave it at 4 until something happens. 4. Dismiss the banner with Enter, Esc and a click on three occasions. Expected 1: the top line shows 1 hour/s, 6 hours/s, 1 day/s, 5 days/s and the date advances at that pace. 2: paused, then 1 day/s. 3: the clock stops by itself with a banner (a contact, research complete, a module finished or the monthly report) and the speed reads paused. 4: each dismisses it; the clock stays paused until a speed is chosen.

docs.title: MT-4-04 — Campaign: interception → battle → back
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Run the clock until Contact: Dominion scouts (or another raid). 2. Contacts tab: Enter on the contact. 3. Run the clock; watch the craft fly. 4. At the banner, Enter. 5. Fly the battle and win; at the debrief press Enter. 6. Repeat with another contact; in the battle open the pause menu and press L. Expected 1: the banner, and the contact drawn on the map. 2: Done.; the craft leave the base on the map. 3: when they meet the contact the clock stops with a fly-or-break-off banner. 4: the raid's mission starts (for scouts intercept_scouts) with the first craft's hull (a Comet) as your ship. 5: after the debrief delay and Enter, back on the map with Battle result: WIN (n destroyed); the contact is gone; score and funds changed by the outcome; the craft fly home; the pilot's kills and missions grew (Hangar). 6: back on the map at once, result RETREAT; the contact still flies.

docs.title: MT-4-05 — Campaign: breaking off, and an unopposed raid
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Intercept a contact; at the fly-or-break-off banner press Esc. 2. Let a saucer raid heading for the Gatehouse arrive without intercepting it. Expected 1: Broke off the interception.; the contact flies on; the craft fly home. 2: a banner Saucer raid struck Gatehouse unopposed; Build tab: the newest finished module is gone; Messages: the module destroyed; the score drops by 100.

docs.title: MT-4-06 — Campaign: Bases, Build, Market and Factory tabs
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Build tab: Enter on Laboratory; Enter on it again until refused. 2. Market: Enter on Buy Blaster; S on a Blaster row. 3. Factory: Enter on Make Seeker rocket several times; run the clock. 4. Choose Ajax on the map; Bases tab: Enter on Build a Guard base at Ajax; run the clock 21 days. 5. Left/Right; Build a module at the new base. Expected 1: funds drop by 300,000; the lab shows building, 12.0 days, later working; past the research limit (3) the message says the base already has the most research modules. 2: funds drop by 40,000; 48 hours later Messages: Gatehouse: 1 x Blaster arrived; S sells one for 20,000. 3: Production: 0 units an hour until a workshop is built — then the queue shows units left, and seekers arrive in store. (Known issue: funds do not drop for manufacture.) 4: Ajax Station under construction, complete after 21 days (banner). 5: the current base changes (marked *); orders apply to it.

docs.title: MT-4-07 — Campaign: the Research tab
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Research tab: Enter on Heat rays. 2. Run at 5 days/s until complete. 3. Look at the Market and the list of topics. 4. Switch the base to another topic midway and back. Expected 1: Gatehouse is researching: Heat rays; the percentage grows with time (6 + 12 per lab work units an hour). 2: banner Research complete: Heat rays. 3: Buy Heat ray appears in the Market; Ion rays is now researchable. 4: progress is kept (keep_progress). Known issue: Saucer hull analysis and Robot brains never appear, even after salvage.

docs.title: MT-4-08 — Campaign: the Hangar tab, pilots and recruits
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Hangar tab: read the craft, pilots and recruits. 2. Enter on a recruit. 3. Buy a Comet; when it is ready, Enter on it. 4. Get a pilot shot down in a campaign battle. Expected 1: three Comets with pilots; four pilots with rank cadet, kills, missions, ready; five recruits with stats and the fee 40,000. 2: funds drop by 40,000; the pilot joins the roster. 3: the new Comet gets the free pilot (or no free pilot). 4: back on the map, the craft is gone and the pilot reads injured, 12 days (or killed); after 12 days ready.

docs.title: MT-4-09 — Campaign: the monthly report and messages
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Run the clock past 30 days. 2. Messages tab. Expected 1: banner Monthly report: score … this month (… in all); costs … (modules …, craft …, salaries …); funds …; a new set of recruits. 2: the newest lines first, dated: stipend, fuel, arrivals, battles.

docs.title: MT-4-10 — Campaign: save and continue
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Mid-campaign press F5. 2. Note date, funds, research progress and contacts; Esc. 3. Quit the program, start it, Campaign: continue. 4. Disable an addon the campaign was started with (if any) and continue. 5. Campaign: new game. Expected 1: Saved to …/saves/default.yaml. 2: back to the launcher. 3: the same date, funds, bases, modules (with build progress), research, craft (also those in flight), pilots and contacts. 4: the launcher shows this save needs packs that are not loaded: …. 5: a fresh campaign (the save is overwritten on the next save).

docs.title: MT-4-11 — Campaign: lane travel
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Run until a raid is detected; look at its line on the map. 2. Intercept a contact far from Mercury Gate; watch the craft. 3. Let the contact be destroyed or leave; watch the craft return. Expected 1: the raid enters at a system without a base (often the far east) and its way ahead is drawn along the lanes. 2: the craft follow the lanes from system to system to the one nearest the contact, then fly straight to it. 3: they come home along the lanes.

docs.title: MT-4-12 — Campaign: fitting a craft and flying its fit
docs.text: Field Steps 1. Hangar tab: on a Comet press F. 2. Press F on a second Comet. 3. Research Heat rays, buy two, press F on the first Comet again. 4. Intercept with that Comet and fly the battle; look at the weapons. Expected 1: … fitted: Blaster, Blaster, Seeker rocket, …; the row shows the fit; the store has fewer blasters and seekers. 2: what is left is fitted, or nothing in store fits this craft. 3: the better beams replace the blasters, which go back into the store. 4: the battle's craft fires the fitted beams and carries the fitted missiles with their rounds; other battles (launcher missions) keep the class's own weapons.

docs.title: MT-4-13 — Supply: surveying a system
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.0 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Open the Supply tab with no system chosen. 2. Click a system inside the Gatehouse's radar circle (or Mercury Gate itself); on the Supply tab choose Survey  from Gatehouse. 3. Run the clock until the survey reports. 4. Choose the same row again. 5. Click a system outside every radar circle and try to survey it. Expected 1: (choose a system on the map to survey it or build there) and 0 orders open, 0 convoys under way, 0 survey ships out. 2: Done.; a sky-blue ring leaves the base on the map; the count says 1 survey ships out. 3: the clock stops with Survey of : ; research site: … (or, after an attack roll, (after fighting off an attack), or Survey ship attacked and lost on the way to  — then survey again). 4: the Survey row is gone. 5:  is outside Gatehouse's radar range.

docs.title: MT-4-14 — Supply: building facilities and the placement rules
docs.text: Field Preconditions MT-4-13 done for a system with deposits; Ctrl+M once or twice for funds. Steps 1. Choose an unsurveyed system: read the three Build rows. 2. Choose the surveyed system: build a Mining facility. 3. Build a second Mining facility there. 4. Choose Mercury Gate: build a Manufacturing center. 5. Choose a system that is not a research site: read the Research station row. 6. Run the clock until the facilities are complete. Expected 1: Mining and Research station rows end (… has not been surveyed). 2: Done.; funds drop by its cost (400,000); a grey diamond beside the system; the Supply tab lists Mining facility at : building, 10.0 days. 3: there is already one in this system. 4: allowed (a base's system); a system more than two lanes away says is more than two lanes from your bases. 5: (… is not a research site). 6: Mining facility at  is complete stops the clock; the diamond turns orange; the facility's row lists its store filling (… Iron).

docs.title: MT-4-15 — Supply: a hull built from components (the whole chain)
docs.text: Field Preconditions A Workshop at the Gatehouse (Build tab; Ctrl+B finishes it) for a production rate. A Manufacturing center within two lanes of the Gatehouse and Mining facilities on systems with iron, cosmium, gold and dilithium (the Comet needs hull plating, rocket motors and ray emitters). Ctrl+M for funds. Steps 1. Factory tab: queue one Comet. 2. Watch the Supply tab and the map at speed 3 – 4. 3. Wait until the Comet is built. Expected 1: the job is queued; no money is taken for it. 2: n orders open rises; gold dots (convoys) travel along the lanes from the mines to the center and from the center to the Gatehouse; the center's store shows iron, cosmium, … and then hull plating, rocket motors, ray emitters; the base's store row appears (Gatehouse store: …). 3: once the base holds 8 hull plating, 2 rocket motors and 2 ray emitters they disappear from its store, the job runs, and a Comet joins the Hangar. No goods move without an order.

docs.title: MT-4-16 — Supply: convoys, ambushes and short deliveries
docs.text: Field Preconditions An addon for the default campaign with logistics: {ambush_chance: 100%, ambush_loss: 50%}; the chain of MT-4-15 set up. Steps 1. Queue a Comet and watch the messages while convoys travel. 2. Look at the store the convoy was heading for when it arrives. 3. Wait for the Comet. Expected 1: every convoy stops the clock somewhere along its route with Supply convoy ( ) ambushed: k of 3 vessels lost. 2: the delivery is the surviving share (for 1 of 3 lost, two thirds). 3: further orders make up the difference; the Comet is still built, later. With 3 of 3 lost nothing arrives and the goods are ordered again.

docs.title: MT-4-17 — Supply: a research station and a station-only topic
docs.text: Field Preconditions Default campaign. Deep radar researched (Research tab; or wait). Tycho Drift surveyed (it has gold and the pulsar_near feature) — build a base nearer if it is out of radar range. Ctrl+M for funds. Steps 1. Research tab: look for Pulsar navigation and Theremin shielding. 2. Supply tab at Tycho Drift: build a Mining facility and a Research station; wait until both are complete. 3. Choose Research Theremin shielding here. 4. Choose Research Pulsar navigation here. 5. Run the clock. Expected 1: neither station-only topic is offered at a base. 2: under the station's row, Research Theremin shielding here and Research Pulsar navigation here (every station-only topic of this facility type not yet known). 3: this station is not on a nebula_lab site. 4: Research station at Tycho Drift: …; researching Pulsar navigation (awaiting materials); an order for gold is opened. 5: a convoy delivers the gold; (awaiting materials) disappears; later Research complete: Pulsar navigation.

docs.title: MT-4-18 — Supply: save and continue with logistics under way
docs.text: Field Preconditions A default campaign with facilities, at least one convoy and one survey ship in flight. Steps 1. Note the Supply tab and the map. 2. F5; Esc to the launcher. 3. Campaign: continue. 4. Run the clock. Expected 3: the same facilities, stores, orders, convoys and survey ships, in the same places. 4: they carry on: convoys arrive (or are ambushed where they were going to be) and surveys report as before saving.

docs.title: MT-4-19 — Fixes: manufacture is paid; salvage topics open
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.0 or later. Default campaign with a Workshop at the Gatehouse (Build tab; Ctrl+B finishes it). Steps 1. Factory tab: queue two of an item (not a hull: hulls are paid in components); note the funds before and after the clock runs one hour, and when the second unit starts. 2. Set funds below an item's cost (spend them) and queue one. 3. Intercept and win a saucer raid whose outcome salvages; then open the Research tab. Expected 1: nothing is taken when queued; the first unit's cost is taken when it starts, the second's when it starts. 2: the job waits until money comes in. 3: Saucer hull analysis is offered (and, after a robot raid is salvaged, Robot brains).

docs.title: MT-4-20 — Testbed cheats: payday, knowitall, quickbase
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.8.1 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Ctrl+M. 2. Build tab: order a module; Bases tab: order a new base. 3. Ctrl+B. 4. Ctrl+K; open the Research tab and the Market tab. 5. Build a facility (Supply tab) and press Ctrl+B. Expected 1: banner Cheat: payday; funds up by 1,000,000; a line in Messages. 2: both building. 3: Cheat: quickbase; the module and the base are finished at once. 4: Cheat: knowitall; nothing left to research; every item and hull on sale. 5: the facility keeps building (quickbase finishes bases and modules only).

docs.title: MT-4-21 — Testbed cheat: jump to battle
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.8.1 or later. A default campaign with a detected contact (wait at speed 4). Steps 1. Press Ctrl+J on the Bases tab. 2. Contacts tab: choose the contact; Ctrl+J. 3. Enter; fly or leave the battle. 4. Send every craft away (or lose them), choose a contact and press Ctrl+J. Expected 1: Choose a contact on the Contacts tab first. 2: the fly-or-break-off banner at once, without the craft flying there. 3: the raid's mission starts with that craft's hull; the debrief returns to the map as usual. 4: no ready craft with a pilot.

docs.title: MT-4-22 — interceptor: a new campaign from the player's data
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.8.0 or later with the player's data (resources/xcom or resources/xcom-cd). Steps 1. Launcher: Tab to interceptor; note the first entries. 2. Campaign: new game at two difficulty levels in turn (D in the launcher). 3. Look at the map, the Bases, Research, Build and Hangar tabs. 4. openinterceptor --check --campaign interceptor. Expected 1: Campaign: continue, Campaign: new game. 2: the starting funds differ by level (read from the level's section of GameSettings.ini). 3: a generated map of 30 – 45 systems; Frontier Base One with its template modules and a hangar; three craft; research offered only where its prerequisites are known; module costs and build times in the original's scale (thousands, days). 4: no errors. Compare against the original game where you can; note anything that feels wrong — every estimate is DERIVED.

docs.title: MT-4-23 — interceptor: research, prerequisites and a six-month soak
docs.text: Field Preconditions As MT-4-22. Steps 1. openinterceptor --campaign interceptor --strategy-soak 180. 2. The same with --campaign default. 3. In a new interceptor campaign research a topic; see which topics and items appear once it is done. 4. Build a second downlink; compare the research speed. Expected 1: one line after 180 days — about 4 of 71 topics on one downlink at app 0.8.0, funds, score, battles. 2: about 12 of 14 topics. 3: the topics whose Prereq ids name it, and the items whose TechRequired names it, become available. 4: faster research (the rate counts every downlink type). Whether the pace matches the original is the play-test's question.

docs.title: MT-4-24 — Playtest: the nebula pocket
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.1 or later. openinterceptor --no-original --mission pocket_ambush (or the launcher). Steps 1. Look all round with the chase view and the cockpit view. 2. Fly a full circle at the arena's edge. 3. Compare the stars with an open-space mission (rocket-vs-saucer). Expected 1: soft violet and blue clouds all around, with gaps; no planet. 2: the clouds stay put as you move (they are a backdrop) and no seams or flicker show. 3: the stars are dimmer behind the clouds. The frame rate is the same as in open space.

docs.title: MT-4-25 — Playtest: bulbous fighters and the bigger dreadnought
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.1 or later, default campaign. Steps 1. Model viewer: the Comet, Meteor and Thunderbolt, and their debris. 2. Fly rocket-vs-saucer and shoot at a Guard wingman's shape from behind (or watch the AI fight). 3. Model viewer: the dreadnought; then fly eclipse_assault to the dreadnought's arrival (90 s). Expected 1: each is a teardrop "bullet with fins", widest about 40 % back, in the Flash Gordon / Captain Proton style; the Meteor's booster pylons start wide and thick at the hull and taper to the boosters; debris pieces match. 2: they are visibly bigger targets and easier to hit than before. 3: the dreadnought is a quarter larger, and shots and collisions meet its hull where it is drawn (its collision shape follows the scale).

docs.title: MT-4-26 — Convoy ambush: tugs, torn-off pods and escorts
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.2 or later. openinterceptor --no-original --mission convoy_ambush; chase view helps. Steps 1. Watch the clippers from the start. 2. At about 45 s, find the grappler and its saucers; do not attack yet. 3. Let the tug reach a clipper. 4. Attack the tug's escorts from 3 km, then from 1 km of the tug. 5. Destroy a tug while it hauls a pod. 6. Fire a missile at a clipper's escort fighter near the clipper (or watch enemy missiles near a clipper). Expected 1: two clippers, each with pods along its body and a laser turret on top, flying slowly and straight; the pods stay on as they move (no juddering). 2: Grapplers inbound with escorts on the radio; the saucers fly a vee around the tug. 3: the tug tractors a pod: CARGO CONTAINER TORN AWAY; the pod leaves the clipper and is hauled away about 3 km, then the tug jumps out with it. 4: the escorts stay in formation while you are far, and break off to attack once you come within about 1.5 km of the tug or of them. 5: the pod is left drifting (not captured). 6: the clipper's laser fires slowly at missiles and close fighters. More tugs keep arriving about every two minutes.

docs.title: MT-4-27 — Convoy ambush: winning, losing and the 15-minute draw
docs.text: Field Preconditions As MT-4-26. Steps 1. Defend well until the clippers jump (about ten minutes; one minute to the jump point is said near the end). 2. Fly again; do nothing and let the tugs work. 3. Fly again; help the raiders cripple one clipper (or wait until one is disabled) and keep the tugs off it for 15 minutes. Expected 1: the clippers go into hyperspace with their remaining pods; win, the debrief shows the cargo share and the optional objectives all_cargo / both_clippers. 2: Convoy: we've lost a quarter of the cargo! as pods go; lose when a clipper is captured or every pod is gone. 3: after 15 minutes a draw, with the convoy draw debrief text.

docs.title: MT-4-28 — Campaign: flying an ambushed convoy's escort
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.9.2 or later. A default campaign with a supply chain under way (MT-4-15), so convoys are moving; speed 4 until one is ambushed (30 % of convoys). Steps 1. When the clock stops with Supply convoy ambushed! Enter: fly its escort Esc: let it fight through, look at the map. 2. Press Enter; fly the battle to a win with part of the cargo lost; return to the map. 3. At the next ambush press Esc. 4. At another, leave the battle early from the pause menu (L). 5. Send every craft away (or have no pilot) and wait for an ambush; press Enter. Expected 1: the convoy's gold dot has stopped and stays put while the banner is up; the message names its cargo. 2: the battle is convoy_ambush with the first ready craft; back on the map Convoy escort: WIN - NN% of the cargo got through; the delivery is that share. 3: The convoy fought through alone: N of M vessels lost. 4: the same as Esc. 5: No ready craft: the convoy fights through alone.

docs.title: MT-4-29 — Strategy screen: top bar, clock and base switcher
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A new default campaign (--no-original --strategy); build or cheat a second base for step 3 (Ctrl+M, then a base from a system's info panel). Steps 1. Read the top bar. 2. Click ||, 1h, 6h, 1d, 5d in turn; then press Space and 1 – 4. 3. Click < and > beside the base name; press Left / Right. 4. Click Save. 5. Click Menu; choose Continue. 6. Resize the window to a tall narrow shape, then a very wide one; then full screen. Expected 1: date, Funds with thousands separators, Score; the current base's name between < and > (dimmed with one base); the speed buttons, Save, Menu. 2: the clock stops / runs at that speed; the running speed is outlined in the accent colour; the keys do the same. 3: the base name changes and orders (Build, Research) apply to it. 4: a yellow Saved to … line at the bottom of the map. 5: the main menu; Continue returns to the map as saved. 6: the top bar, map and panels always reach the window's edges (stretched, no black bars); text stays readable on a small window.

docs.title: MT-4-30 — Strategy map: zoom, pan, hover and select
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A default campaign with a detected contact and a convoy or craft in flight (speed 4 until one appears; Ctrl+J needs a contact). Steps 1. Put the pointer on a system near the map's edge and roll the wheel forward several times; then back. 2. Drag with the right button; then with the middle button. 3. Hover over systems, a contact, a convoy, a survey ship, a craft in flight. 4. Click a system; a system with your base; a contact; a convoy. 5. Click empty space. 6. Read the legend. Expected 1: the map zooms in about the pointer — the system under it stays under it — up to a limit, and out to half size. 2: the map follows the drag; release stops it; dragging that starts outside the map does nothing. 3: a dark label with the name follows the pointer (Supply convoy, Survey ship, the craft's name). 4: each is selected (the info panel changes); clicking a system with a base makes that base current in the top bar. A contact beside a system is chosen over the system when they are about as close. 5: the selection stays. 6: square: base, red: hostile, gold: convoy, blue: survey/craft, diamond: facility, wheel: zoom, right-drag: pan.

docs.title: MT-4-31 — Strategy info panel: the selection's actions
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A default campaign; Ctrl+M for money. Steps 1. With nothing selected, read the info panel. 2. Select a system without a base; press a Build  () button. 3. Select an unsurveyed system within radar range; press Survey. 4. After the survey, select a system where a facility may be built; press its Build  button. 5. Select a system with a base that is not current; press Make  current. 6. Select a detected contact; press Intercept. 7. Select a convoy, a survey ship and a craft in flight. Expected 1: Nothing selected and a hint on clicking, the wheel and right-drag. 2: the base is ordered (funds drop) or a yellow line says why not. 3: a survey ship leaves (sky-blue ring). 4: the facility is ordered (grey diamond). 5: the top bar shows that base. 6: the contact's name, where it is heading and how many craft are ready; Intercept sends them (they appear on the map). 7: a one-line description and no buttons. The text wraps inside the panel and never overlaps the buttons; at most four buttons.

docs.title: MT-4-32 — Strategy lists: scrolling, the selected row, double click, keys
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A default campaign some months in (many messages and research topics); Ctrl+K optional. Steps 1. Click each of the ten list buttons. 2. Open Messages; roll the wheel over the list; drag nothing, just watch the scroll bar. 3. Use Up / Down past the visible rows; Tab / Shift+Tab. 4. Click a long row. 5. Double-click a Research topic. 6. Press Enter on another topic. 7. Click a grey (information) row. Expected 1: the list's title changes and the open button is outlined. 2: the list scrolls two rows per notch and stops at the ends; the bar's thumb shows the position and size of the view. 3: the selection moves and the list scrolls just enough to keep it in view; Tab moves to the next list. 4: rows too wide end in ...; the selected row is shown in full (two lines) below the separator. 5: the base researches it (a second click within about half a second acts). 6: the same. 7: it is selected, shows in full, and has no buttons.

docs.title: MT-4-33 — Strategy lists: the row buttons
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A default campaign; Ctrl+M for money; a craft without a pilot and a free pilot for step 4 (hire a recruit). Steps 1. Market: select an item; press Buy 1, Buy 5. 2. After delivery press Sell 1. 3. Factory: Make 1, Make 5. 4. Hangar: on a craft press Assign pilot, then Fit best; on a recruit press Hire. 5. Research: Research; Build: Build; Bases: Select; Contacts: Intercept; Supply on a station topic: Start. 6. Press a button you cannot afford. Expected 1: funds drop by one and five prices; deliveries arrive at the current base. 2: the stock falls by one and funds rise by the sell price. 3: one and five jobs in the base's queue. 4: the craft gets the pilot (or no free pilot); its fit changes from standard fit to the items fitted; the recruit joins the roster. 5: each order takes effect with Done. in the yellow line. 6: the yellow line says why (not enough money, …). No order needs a key.

docs.title: MT-4-34 — Strategy prompts: modals with buttons
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A default campaign (a chapter's title card and offered mission come in the first weeks); a contact for step 2 (Ctrl+J). Steps 1. Wait for a report (a module finished, the monthly report); press OK. 2. Ctrl+J on a selected contact: Interception; press Break off; again, Fly the battle and return. 3. A title card: Continue; another: click anywhere. 4. Mission offered: Decline; at the next, Fly it. 5. A story choice: click an option; at another press its number key. 6. A convoy ambush: Let it fight. 7. While any prompt is up, click the map, the list buttons and the top bar; roll the wheel; press Enter and Esc on a two-button prompt. Expected 1: the clock stopped; the prompt over a dimmed screen with the text wrapped; OK closes it. 2: break off — Broke off the interception.; fly — the battle, then the map. 3: both dismiss. 4: declined — Declined.; fly — the mission with the first ready craft. 5: the choice applies (messages, money). 6: the convoy fights on alone. 7: nothing beneath reacts (no selection, no zoom, no speed change); Enter chooses the first button, Esc the last.

docs.title: MT-4-35 — Fitted shields and armour in battle
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.0 or later. Either the interceptor campaign with the player's data (its hulls have one shield and one armour slot; items shield_type1 – 4, armor_type1 – 3), or the default campaign with a test addon mods/default-armour/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) whose strategy/items.yaml adds items: {test_shield: {name: Test shield, kind: shield, cost: 1000, protection: 900}, test_armour: {name: Test armour, kind: armor, cost: 1000, protection: 700}} and gives hulls.comet slots: {beam: 2, missile: 2, special: 1, shield: 1, armor: 1}. Steps 1. Before fitting, fly a campaign battle with a craft (standard fit); open the MFD Status page. 2. Buy a shield and an armour item for the craft's base; Hangar › Fit best on the craft. 3. Fly the next campaign battle with it (Ctrl+J); read the MFD Status page and the ship status display. 4. Take hits until the shield bands drop. 5. Fly a plain --mission of the same class. Expected 1: the class's own shields and armour (interceptor: those of its fitted: equipment from your data). 2: the Hangar row lists the fitted items. 3: the shields per facing and the armour are the fitted items' protection (addon: 900 per facing, 700 armour), both full at the start. 4: the bands go out one third at a time. 5: the class's own values again — the fit applies only to the campaign craft's battle.

docs.title: MT-4-36 — --balance report
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.0 or later; the player's data for step 3. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --balance. 2. Again with --difficulty cadet and --difficulty space_ace. 3. openinterceptor --campaign interceptor --balance. Expected 1: balance at difficulty : …, a header (class, shield, armour, hull, eff.hp, dps, then one column per playable ship id: comet, meteor, thunderbolt), then one row per class from the weakest to the toughest by effective hit points (shield + armour + hull): the seconds of perfect fire each playable ship needs to destroy it, - where the ship has no beams; the program exits without a window. Stations and capital ships take many times longer than fighters. 2: the numbers change with the level's variants. 3: the X-COM classes, with the craft's protection from their fitted: equipment and stations' hull from their HP charts — no zeros where your data has values.

docs.title: MT-4-37 — Durability: ships and stations last longer
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.0 or later. Default campaign; the player's data for step 3. Steps 1. Fly mixed-dogfight (default) at the middle level and count the bursts needed to kill a saucer; note how long your own craft survives. 2. Fly defend_station idle (do not fight) and time the station. 3. Fly an interceptor raid mission with the Lightning; attack an alien base or outpost in a later mission. 4. Compare with --balance. Expected 1: fighters take noticeably longer to destroy than before 0.15.0 (about four times the punishment), on both sides. 2: the station holds well beyond its old time (at least R-MSN-011's 150 s). 3: the Lightning survives a sustained exchange; stations take minutes of fire, not seconds. 4: the order of toughness matches the report. Judge the feel: is anything now too hard to kill? Record findings for a balance pass.

docs.title: MT-4-38 — Default shields and armour: buy, research, fit and fly
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.1 or later. A new default campaign (--no-original --strategy). Steps 1. Bases or Market: look at the opening store and the Market list. 2. Hangar › a Comet › Fit best. 3. Fly a battle with it (select a contact, Ctrl+J, Fly the battle) and open the MFD Status page. 4. Research list: look for Force fields and Saucer alloys; then Ctrl+K and the Market again. 5. Buy a force field and saucer-alloy plating, wait for the delivery, Fit best again and fly another battle. Expected 1: the store holds 3 deflector screens and 3 steel platings besides the blasters and seeker rockets; the Market offers Deflector screen (60,000) and Steel plating (30,000) but not yet the better two. 2: the Hangar row lists a deflector screen and steel plating. 3: shields 300 per facing and armour 180, full at the start. 4: Force fields opens after Heat rays, Saucer alloys after Saucer hull analysis; after Ctrl+K the Market adds Force field (140,000) and Saucer-alloy plating (110,000). 5: the better items are fitted (the old ones go back to the store); in battle shields 480 per facing, armour 380.

docs.title: MT-4-39 — Survey report names reserves and features
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Survey Ajax from the Gatehouse (select Ajax, Survey). 2. Run the clock until the report. 3. Survey Cinder the same way. Expected 2: Survey of Ajax: cosmium 6/day (1800 in reserve), iron 20/day (unlimited); features: none; research site: none (resource names as the data spells them; (after fighting off an attack) after the name when the ship was attacked). 3: iron 30/day (unlimited) and gold 3/day (600 in reserve); features none. A system with features (Nebula Haven, Tycho Drift) names them, e.g. features: nebula; research site: nebula_lab.

docs.title: MT-4-40 — A save from another pack version loads with a notice
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. A test addon mods/default-ver/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with version: 1.0.0 and no other files. Steps 1. With the addon active, start a default campaign, play a day and leave with Menu (it saves). 2. Change the addon's version: to 1.1.0. 3. Main menu › Continue. 4. Remove the addon and Continue again. Expected 3: the campaign loads and a Report says Pack default-ver is now version 1.1.0 (this save was made with 1.0.0), with the clock stopped; after OK play goes on. 4: refused, with this save needs packs that are not loaded: default-ver in the menu.

docs.title: MT-4-41 — Construction strikes: fly the defence or let it be
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.4 or later. A new default campaign; Ctrl+M for money. Strikes are a 12 % daily roll in the second half of a build, so build several facilities (mining 10 days, manufacturing center 15) to see every branch. Steps 1. Survey Ajax and Cinder; build a mining facility at each and a manufacturing center. 2. Run at 1d; watch for the first Construction under attack prompt. 3. Let it be. 4. At the next strike, Fly the defence and win. 5. At another, fly and lose (let the site be destroyed). 6. Keep the facilities building to completion and count the strikes per system. 7. With no ready craft (all away, or no pilot), press Fly the defence. Expected 2: no strike before a site is half built; the prompt Enemy craft are striking the  at  under construction. Fly its defence, or let the strike set the work back. with Fly the defence and Let it be; the clock stopped. 3: a report  at  was struck: construction set back N days (a quarter of its build time) and the site finishes that much later. 4: the Construction defence battle (a research station at 60 % and raiders); back on the map Construction defence: WIN and …: the strike was beaten off. 5: … was destroyed under construction; its diamond is gone from the map. 6: at most three strikes per system. 7: No ready craft: the strike goes unopposed. and the set-back report.

docs.title: MT-4-42 — Mission outcomes: capture, losing a facility, the escort's outcome
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.3 or later (and 0.16.13 for the Debug list). A test addon mods/default-outcomes/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with missions/outcome_test.yaml: missions: {outcome_test: {name: Outcome test, player: {class: choose}, roles: {prize: {class: scout_saucer, count: 1, ai: idle, at: {distance: 2km, bearing: [0, 0]}}}, objectives: {win: destroyed_all(prize)}, outcomes: {win: ["lose(mining_facility)"], retreat: [capture]}}} and strategy/story.yaml: events: {outcome_test: {when: day >= 99999, do: ["mission(outcome_test)"]}}. A Meteor or Thunderbolt (tractor beam) as the first ready craft: Ctrl+K, buy one, give it a pilot. Steps 1. Order a mining facility at a surveyed system. 2. Ctrl+D › outcome_test › Fire now; fly it and destroy the scout. 3. Fire it again; disable the scout, tow it with Shift+T and jump out with H (as in MT-2-04). 4. Research list. 5. Fly an ambushed convoy's escort (MT-4-28) once to a win and once to a loss; read the score and Messages. Expected 2: back on the map a report Mining facility at lost; the facility is gone and its orders with it; Lost: Mining facility at in the log. 3: Captured: scout_saucer in the log; the prize counts as salvage, so a topic with requires: salvaged(scout_saucer) could start. Without capture in the outcome nothing is kept. 4: nothing new: the default topics name raids in salvaged(…), not classes. 5: the win adds the mission's convoy_delivered score; the loss records Convoy cargo lost and the convoy_lost score, as well as delivering nothing.

docs.title: MT-4-43 — Research: requires_any, hidden topics and discover
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.6 or later (0.16.13 for the Debug list). A test addon mods/default-research/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with strategy/research.yaml: research: {either_way: {name: Either way, size: 500, requires_any: [heat_rays, rocketry]}, both_ways: {name: Both ways, size: 500, requires: research(rocketry), requires_any: [heat_rays, ion_rays]}, secret_lab: {name: Secret lab, size: 500, hidden: true}} and strategy/story.yaml: events: {find_secret: {when: day >= 99999, do: ["discover(secret_lab)"]}}. Steps 1. A new default campaign (rocketry known): Research list. 2. Ctrl+D › find_secret › Fire now. 3. Research list. 4. Research Heat rays (or Ctrl+K) and look again. 5. Misspell heat_rays in requires_any and run --check. Expected 1: Either way is offered (one of the two is enough); Both ways is not; Secret lab is not listed. 2: a report New research possible: Secret lab. 3: Secret lab offered. 4: Both ways offered. 5: an error at research.either_way.requires naming the unknown topic.

docs.title: MT-4-44 — Pilot training and dismissal
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.7 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Hangar: select a pilot row. 2. Press Train; note the funds; run five days at 1d; save (Save › a slot) and open the save in a text editor. 3. Select the pilot again: Stop training. 4. Press Enter, then double-click a pilot row. 5. Dismiss a pilot without a craft, then one assigned to a craft. 6. Save, leave and load the slot: is training kept? Expected 2: the row ends , training and the button reads Stop training; funds fall by 400 a day for the pilot (beyond other costs); in the save the pilot's stats are about 2 points higher (0.4 a day), never above a stat's maximum (the pilots list shows no stats). 3: training stops. 4: Enter and a double click toggle training (the row's first action); they never dismiss. 5: the pilot leaves the roster; Dismissed:  in the log; the craft is without a pilot. 6: a pilot in training is still training.

docs.title: MT-4-45 — The monthly evaluation and the Reports list
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.9 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Open the Reports list at once. 2. Run to the first monthly report, breaking off every interception. 3. Reports again. 4. Play a month winning battles (Ctrl+J), so the month scores 400 or more. 5. openinterceptor --no-original --strategy-soak 90. Expected 1: Funds 2,500,000 - score 0 (+0 this month) - 1 bases, 3 craft, 4 pilots and No monthly report yet. 2: the report ends ; rated : Satisfactory for a score of 0 or more, Poor (−50,000) from −300, else Unacceptable (−150,000 and the news The Senate cuts the Guard's funding). 3: each report dated, newest first, without its Monthly report: prefix. 4: rated Outstanding, +150,000 and the news The Senate commends the Guard's month. 5: the last monthly report printed ends rated ….

docs.title: MT-4-46 — Base effects: quarters and defence; dismantling
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.10 or later. A new default campaign; Ctrl+M. Steps 1. Bases list: read the rows under the Gatehouse. 2. Hangar: hire a recruit. 3. Build › Crew quarters; Ctrl+B; hire again until refused. 4. Bases list: select a module row; press Enter and double-click it; then press Dismantle. 5. Build two Ray batteries (Ctrl+B) and let several raids reach the Gatehouse unopposed (Break off). 6. Market: buy many items. Expected 1: each module row has Dismantle; a line Quarters: room for 4 pilots. 2: refused with no quarters: room for 4 pilots (the four starting pilots fill it). 3: room for 10 pilots; hiring works until ten living pilots. 4: Enter and the double click do nothing; Dismantle removes the module and logs Gatehouse:  dismantled ( back). 5: about one raid in four on the Gatehouse is driven off — 's defences drove the raid off — and loses nothing; the others destroy the newest finished module as before. 6: no store limit (the default campaign has no storage modules).

docs.title: MT-4-47 — Factory queue: Move up and Cancel; delivery losses
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.11 or later. A new default campaign; Ctrl+M, Ctrl+K. For step 5 a test addon mods/default-losses/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with strategy/economy.yaml: economy: {delivery_loss: 50%}. Steps 1. Factory: Make 5 of one item, then Make 1 of two others. 2. Select the third queued row: Move up. 3. Select the first row (being worked on): Cancel; again Cancel; then cancel a job not yet started. 4. Press Enter, then double-click a queued row. 5. With the addon: Buy 1 five times and wait for the deliveries. Expected 1: rows queued: 5 x (… units left on this one) with Cancel; every row but the first also has Move up. 2: it swaps with the row above. 3: the job at work drops to one unit (the paid one) and finishes; the second Cancel says the last unit is already under way; a job not yet started disappears, costing nothing. 4: Enter and the double click move a row up, never cancel. 5: about half arrive; each lost one gives a report A delivery of 1 x to Gatehouse was lost, paid all the same.

docs.title: MT-4-48 — Auto-resolve an interception
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.12 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Intercept a contact with three Comets; at the Interception prompt press Auto-resolve. 2. Repeat with one craft against a larger raid (Ctrl+J with a single ready craft). 3. After a win and after a loss read the map, the score and Messages. 4. At another prompt press Enter, then at another Esc. Expected 1: the prompt has Fly the battle, Auto-resolve and Break off; Auto-resolve flies nothing and reports Auto-resolved (NN% odds): WIN or LOSE. 2: lower odds. 3: a win removes the contact and applies the mission's win outcome (score, money, salvage); a loss leaves it flying and applies the lose outcome. 4: Enter flies the battle, Esc breaks off.

docs.title: MT-4-49 — Logistics conditions in the Debug list
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.13 or later. A test addon mods/default-queries/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with strategy/story.yaml: events: q_survey: {when: survey_known(ajax), chance: 0%, do: ["news(q)"]}, q_deposit: {when: deposit(ajax, cosmium) > 5, …}, q_feature: {when: feature(nebula_haven, nebula) and research_site(nebula_haven, nebula_lab), …}, q_owned: {when: owned(ajax), …}, q_lanes: {when: lane_distance(mercury_gate, vesta_reach) == 2, …}, q_building: {when: facility_progress(ajax) < 1, …}, q_strikes: {when: construction_attacks(ajax) >= 1, …} (each with chance: 0% and the same do). Steps 1. A new default campaign; Ctrl+D; read the q_ rows. 2. Survey Ajax; read again. 3. Build a mining facility at Ajax; read. 4. After a strike on it (MT-4-41); read. 5. When it is finished; read. 6. Change ajax to atlantis in one condition and run --check. Expected 1: q_feature and q_lanes condition holds, the others false; all fired 0. 2: q_survey and q_deposit hold. 3: q_owned and q_building hold. 4: q_strikes holds. 5: q_building false again. 6: an error naming the unknown name atlantis.

docs.title: Stage 5 cases
docs.text: How to start: as for Stage 4 (Campaign: new game, or --no-original --strategy). Speed 4 (5 days a second) and the cheats (Ctrl+M, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+B) shorten the waits. Keys: User guide › Campaign › The story.

docs.title: MT-5-01 — Story: chapter messages and the arc's order
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.1 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Start the clock. 2. Decline the offered mission (Esc). 3. Run to day 15; then to day 30. 4. Look at Messages. Expected 1: within the first day the clock stops with Chapter 1 - The Shadow Falls… and a mission is offered. 2: Declined.; the clock can run on. 3: Chapter 2 about day 15 and Chapter 3 about day 30 (or earlier, if both heat rays and deep radar are researched), never out of order. 4: each chapter in the log with its date.

docs.title: MT-5-02 — Story: a choice
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.1 or later. A default campaign about to reach chapter 7 (the Cartel), or past month 2 with the raiders still hostile (the truce event may come with 30 % a month). Steps 1. When Your choice - 1: … 2: … appears, press another key (Space, 3). 2. Press 1. 3. In a later campaign (or the next offer) press 2. 4. Open the Archive tab after each. Expected 1: nothing happens; the clock stays stopped. 2: Chose: … in the log; money and the faction's standing change as the option says; a stance change, if any, is announced (Relations: … are now … (were …)). 3: the other option's effects. 4: the standings reflect the choice.

docs.title: MT-5-03 — Story: an offered mission, flown and declined
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.0 or later. A default campaign with a ready craft and pilot. Steps 1. At a chapter's offer press Enter; fly and win. 2. At the next offer press Enter and lose or retreat. 3. Send every craft away and wait for an offer; press Enter. Expected 1: the chapter's mission starts with that craft's hull and fit; back on the map Mission: WIN (N destroyed); the outcome's score and money apply; Archive: battles won +1. 2: Mission: LOSE / RETREAT; no win counted. 3: No ready craft to fly it., and the offer is gone.

docs.title: MT-5-04 — Story: the Eclipse Engine's shipments and warnings
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.1 or later. A default campaign past chapter 3 (regent_revealed). Steps 1. Look in Messages for Intelligence: the rival's eclipse_engine has begun. 2. Wait for an Eclipse Engine shipment contact; intercept it and win. 3. Let the next one through. 4. Watch the Archive tab over several shipments. Expected 1: present. 2: the battle is intercept_scouts; Archive progress unchanged. 3: A shipment for the rival's eclipse_engine got through; progress +1/18. 4: warnings at a third, two-thirds and 90 %; chapters 4, 8, 10 and 11 follow the progress. If it reaches 100 %, the campaign ends in defeat (engine_lit).

docs.title: MT-5-05 — Relations: stances, raids and who fights whom
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.3 or later. A default campaign where the Black Comet truce is offered (month 2 or later); Ctrl+M for the money. Steps 1. Archive: note the raiders' stance (hostile). 2. Accept the truce (pay). 3. Archive again; run a month. 4. Fly any battle in which raiders' craft appear (a story mission with hot-rods, e.g. pocket_ambush if offered). 5. In another campaign refuse the truce and fly the same battle. Expected 1: raiders: hostile (−70) or so. 2: Relations: raiders are now neutral (were hostile). 3: neutral; no Black Comet ambush raids appear; drift moves the standing towards 0 each month. 4: the raiders' craft do not attack you (and you are not hostile to them). 5: they attack as before.

docs.title: MT-5-06 — The Archive tab and the encyclopaedia
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.0 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Open the Archive tab on day 0. 2. After chapter 3, and after chapter 7, open it again. 3. Win battles three months running; then sit three months without fighting; read the aggression each month. Expected 1: every faction with its stance and standing; Rival aggression x1.00; battles won 0; entries for the Guard, the Dominion and cosmium. 2: the Engine's progress row and the Eclipse Engine entry after chapter 3; the Cartel entry after chapter 7. 3: aggression falls by 0.1 a month while you win three or more battles a month, rises by 0.1 while you do not (between 0.6 and 1.8); raids come more often as it rises.

docs.title: MT-5-07 — Endings: defeat and victory
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.1 or later. Default campaigns. Steps 1. Let the Eclipse Engine be completed: let its shipments through (Ctrl+M keeps you solvent). 2. Press Enter; then choose Campaign: continue. 3. Reach chapter 12 (research victory_design — Ctrl+K — after chapter 10) and fly eclipse_assault to a win; return to the map. Expected 1: DEFEAT. with the ending's text; the clock stops. 2: Enter saves and leaves to the launcher; continue shows the ending again (since app 0.12.1; see MT-6-11). 3: the nebula battle with the Engine, a guard fleet that keeps coming and a dreadnought after 90 s; on return VICTORY. with the Engine's ending.

docs.title: MT-5-08 — The default campaign played through
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.3 or later. A new default campaign at the second difficulty level; no cheats. Steps Play to an ending. Record the date of each chapter, the Cartel choice, each Engine warning and the ending. Note chapters whose mission did not fit their message (they fly existing missions). Expected All twelve chapters in order; the campaign ends in one of the four endings. The log of milestone dates is the Stage 5 exit record.

docs.title: MT-5-09 — interceptor: the Doomsday arc
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.2 or later with the player's data. A new interceptor campaign. Steps 1. Fly battles after 1 February until the first alien message. 2. Research the saucer examinations; watch for messages 2 – 5. 3. Watch the Archive tab for the Doomsday plan and its convoys; let some through. 4. With Ctrl+K, check MacArthur's message and the final mission's offer a week later; win it. Expected 1: the first message after a battle, not before 1 February. 2: each later message only after its date, its examination and (for 4 and 5) the plan's progress. 3: Doomsday convoys as contacts (ambush_alien_freighters_escorted); warnings shown with the original's own texts. 4: the original's MacArthur prompt; the final mission; on its win the victory ending. Note anything that differs from the original — the gates' topics are derived.

docs.title: MT-5-10 — --strategy-soak reports the story
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.10.1 or later. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --strategy-soak 365. 2. With the player's data: openinterceptor --campaign interceptor --strategy-soak 365. Expected 1: the summary line, the last monthly report, and story: arcs [serial N/12], plans [eclipse_engine NN%], aggression X.XX, ending … with the serial well advanced. 2: the same form with doomsday and the Doomsday plan.

docs.title: MT-5-11 — A stance changed by a mission is announced
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later (0.16.13 for the Debug list). A test addon mods/default-stance/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with missions/stance_test.yaml: missions: {stance_test: {name: Stance test, player: {class: choose}, roles: {foes: {class: scout_saucer, count: 1, at: {distance: 3km}}}, objectives: {win: destroyed_all(foes)}, outcomes: {win: ["relation(prospectors, +60)"]}}} and strategy/story.yaml: events: {stance_offer: {when: day >= 99999, do: ["mission(stance_test)"]}}. Steps 1. A new default campaign; Archive: the prospectors' standing and stance. 2. Ctrl+D › stance_offer › Fire now; Fly it; destroy the scout. 3. Back on the map: OK the mission report. Expected 1: 15, neutral. 3: at once a second report Relations: prospectors are now allied (were neutral), with the clock stopped; the Archive shows 75, allied. (Until 0.16.2 the change was only logged.)

docs.title: MT-5-12 — Event debugger: Ctrl+D and Fire now
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.13 or later. A new default campaign, past chapter 1's title card and mission offer. Steps 1. Press Ctrl+D. 2. Read the Debug list. 3. Fire now on ch03 (not the arc's next step). 4. Fire now on ch02 (the next step). 5. Fire now on raider_bribe. 6. Press Tab through the lists; press Ctrl+D again. Expected 1: a Debug button joins the list buttons and its list opens. 2: Arc serial: step 1 of 12, then every event as - fired n, condition holds (or false). 3: ch03's actions run — its title card, the mission offer, the flag regent_revealed — and Debug: fired event ch03 is logged, but the arc stays at step 1. 4: the arc moves to step 2, with ch02's card and offer. 5: the truce choice with both options. 6: Tab passes through Debug while it is shown; Ctrl+D hides the button and opens Bases.

docs.title: MT-5-13 — Start at a chapter: --strategy --chapter N
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.13 or later. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --strategy --chapter 6. 2. Ctrl+D; Archive; Messages. 3. --strategy --chapter 99. 4. --strategy --chapter six. 5. --chapter 3 without --strategy. Expected 1: after a pause (the campaign is played forward headless) the strategy screen opens months into the campaign, with no intro cutscene. 2: Arc serial: step 6 of 12 or later; the log shows the earlier chapters and auto-played battles. 3: it stops after at most 1500 days or at an ending and opens there (record how long it takes). 4: --chapter: expected a number. 5: ignored: the main menu opens as usual.

docs.title: Stage 6 cases
docs.text: How to start: the launcher, or --no-original for the default campaign. References: Music, Skins, Cutscenes, Radio voices › Faces.

docs.title: MT-6-01 — Music in a battle: states and stingers
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.11.0 or later. Default campaign (--no-original). Music volume above 0. Steps 1. Start a mission and hold position away from the enemy. 2. Fly towards the enemy until it is on radar within 10 km. 3. Close to under 3.5 km. 4. Win the mission; in another run lose or retreat. Expected 1: calm cruise music, two segments alternating. 2: at the end of the segment playing, the threat music (pulsing bass, theremin). 3: at the next segment end, the battle music (snare, brass stabs). Changes never cut a phrase. 4: a rising fanfare with the computer voice on a win; a falling figure on any other result.

docs.title: MT-6-02 — Music on the strategy screen, silence elsewhere
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.11.0 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. Sit in the launcher. 2. Campaign: new game (skip the intro). 3. Fly an offered mission and return. 4. Open the model viewer. Expected 1: silence. 2: slow strategy music (pads, glockenspiel). 3: battle music during the battle, strategy music again on the map. 4: silence.

docs.title: MT-6-03 — interceptor music from the player's data
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.11.0 or later with the player's data. Steps 1. Fly several different missions; note the music in each. 2. Fly the same mission twice. 3. Open the strategy screen. Expected 1: the original's loop sets; different battles may use different sets. 2: the same set both times (chosen by the battle's seed). 3: cruise loops. No sound: … lines for cruise*, threat*, battle* or the stingers at start-up.

docs.title: MT-6-04 — Volumes: the launcher's M and V keys
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.12.1 or later. Steps 1. Read the packs line. 2. Press M repeatedly; then V. 3. Quit and look in settings.yaml. 4. With music 0 % and effects 100 % fly a mission; then music 100 % and effects 25 %. Expected 1: Music 70% (M) Effects 100% (V). 2: M goes 100, 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 %; V likewise from 100 to 0, 25 … Each change shows at once. 3: audio: {music: …%, effects: …%} with the last values. 4: silent music with full effects; then loud music and quiet weapons, explosions and voices.

docs.title: MT-6-05 — Skins: art deco and X-COM
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.11.1 or later; the player's data for step 3. Steps 1. Open the launcher with the default campaign. 2. Campaign: new game; look at the map and the tab panel. 3. Press Tab in the launcher to switch to interceptor; open its strategy screen. Expected 1: dark navy background, cream text, a dark-gold selection bar. 2: the map and the tab panel framed in gold with stepped corner ornaments that do not stretch; the active tab highlighted. 3: green-on-steel colours and plain bordered panels (no frame art).

docs.title: MT-6-06 — Title cards
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.11.1 or later. A new default campaign. Steps 1. Start the clock. 2. Press Enter on the card. 3. Run to about day 15. 4. Open Messages. Expected 1: within the first day a card fills the middle of the screen in the gold frame: Chapter 1 - The Shadow Falls large, its hook beneath, (Enter) bottom right; the clock stopped. 2: the card goes; the chapter's mission is offered. 3: the chapter 2 card. 4: each chapter title in the log.

docs.title: MT-6-07 — A Smacker video from the command line
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.12.0 or later with the player's data. Steps 1. openinterceptor --video original:alientrans1.smk. 2. Resize the window during playback. 3. Again, and press Esc half-way. 4. --video original:mfdanim.mps#<member> with a member name from the pack. Expected 1: the film plays centred and letterboxed, its sound in step with the picture; at the end the launcher. 2: the picture stays fitted. 3: picture and sound stop at once; the launcher. 4: a short talking-head clip plays (main 319a31b).

docs.title: MT-6-08 — interceptor: the alien transmissions
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.12.0 or later with the player's data. An interceptor campaign about to receive the first alien message (fly battles after 1 February). Steps 1. Fly battles until the first message. 2. Let the film run to its end. 3. Look at the map. Expected 1: the message, then the transmission film fills the screen. 2: back to the strategy screen where it was, clock stopped, the message in the log. 3: no music during the film; strategy music again after it.

docs.title: MT-6-09 — The default campaign's intro cutscene
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.13.0 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. Campaign: new game; watch to the end. 2. Again, press Esc after a few seconds. 3. openinterceptor --no-original --cutscene intro. Expected 1: black bars top and bottom; three Comets fly past the camera in the orbit environment; the camera cuts to a chase view behind the leader, which fires; the saucer explodes with debris and sound; a cut to the Gatehouse station; three captions in the bottom bar in the skin's font; then the strategy screen. 2: the strategy screen at once. 3: the same scene; then the launcher.

docs.title: MT-6-10 — interceptor: the opening film
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.13.0 or later with the player's data. Steps 1. Campaign: new game. 2. Skip with Enter. Expected 1: the original's opening film (animation1; derived that it is the opening) before the strategy screen. 2: the strategy screen. Note whether the film matches what the original shows first.

docs.title: MT-6-11 — Endings: a film, and the ending shown again
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.12.1 or later. An interceptor campaign at the final mission (Ctrl+K helps), and any campaign that has ended. Steps 1. Win the final mission. 2. Press Enter on the ending. 3. Campaign: continue. Expected 1: the credits film, then VICTORY. with the ending's text. 2: saved; the launcher. 3: the ending's banner again, not a stopped map.

docs.title: MT-6-12 — A mission outcome moves a standing
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.12.1 or later. A default campaign where pocket_ambush is offered (chapter 4, or the Cartel raid choice). Steps 1. Archive tab: note the raiders' standing. 2. Fly pocket_ambush and win. 3. Archive again; Messages. Expected 3: the raiders' standing 5 lower than before (beyond any monthly drift). A stance change, if one happens, is in the log; it does not stop the clock.

docs.title: MT-6-13 — The comms panel
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.13.1 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. --no-original --mission colony_defence; wait. 2. Give a wing order (], then 1 – 6) in a mission with wingmen. Expected 1: about 3 s in, with the radio clip, a green-framed panel at the top left shows the generated CRT portrait of Colony Control and COLONY CONTROL beneath, for about 2.5 s. 2: the Guard Wing portrait and GUARD WING while the wingman answers. With a voice set that has no face, animated signal bars instead; with a chatter clip of no speaker, COMMS.

docs.title: MT-6-14 — Main menu: navigation
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.14.0 or later. Default campaign; first with no save, then with one. Steps 1. Start openinterceptor --no-original with no save. 2. Move through the items with Up/Down (and the pad's D-pad); press Enter on Battles & tools, then Esc. 3. New campaign; skip the intro; Esc on the map. 4. Look at the items again. 5. Continue; Esc. 6. Esc on the main page. Expected 1: the menu, not the launcher: Perils of the Void and its subtitle over a starfield, a Comet turning to the right, the items in the gold-framed panel, the strategy music (the default set has no menu state); no Continue. 2: the selection wraps; the launcher opens; Esc returns to the menu. 3: the intro, then the map; Esc saves and returns to the menu. 4: Continue now first. 5: the map as saved; Esc back to the menu. 6: the game quits.

docs.title: MT-6-15 — Main menu: options round trip
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.14.0 or later. Default campaign; the player's data for the campaign row. Steps 1. Options; Left/Right on Music and Effects; listen in a battle. 2. Change Physics (on a level that allows Simple). 3. Change Difficulty. 4. Change Campaign (with interceptor available). 5. Quit and restart; open Options; look at settings.yaml. Expected 1: each press moves a quarter and stops at 0 % and 100 %; the volumes apply at once. 2: Simple / Realistic toggles. 3: the campaign reloads and the menu reopens on Options with the new level. 4: the other campaign's menu, on Options, in its skin. 5: every choice kept; settings.yaml has audio, game.physics, game.difficulty and game.campaign to match. Physics is not listed on levels that do not allow Simple; Campaign only with more than one campaign.

docs.title: MT-6-16 — Credits
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.14.0 or later; the player's data for step 3. Steps 1. Default campaign: Credits; watch to the end. 2. Again, press Esc part-way. 3. interceptor: Credits. 4. openinterceptor --no-original --credits. Expected 1: the lines rise from below over the stars, headings (Perils of the Void, Music, …) in the skin's accent colour, then Engine, OpenInterceptor and the rest; back to the menu when the last line leaves the top. 2: the menu at once. 3: the CD's credits film plays, then the menu. 4: the roll at start-up, then the menu.

docs.title: MT-6-17 — Ship status display: the default cockpit and the glass HUD
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.1 or later. Default campaign. Steps 1. Start mixed-dogfight with the Comet in the cockpit view; look at the third gauge bezel right of the MFD. 2. Let enemies hit you from ahead, then from behind; watch the arcs. 3. Shift the shield balance forward and aft. 4. Let the hull take damage. 5. Lose one facing entirely. 6. Switch to the chase view (glass HUD). 7. Open the layout editor (F12) and Tab through the instruments. Expected 1: a round display with a small top-down craft in the middle, a three-band arc ahead and one behind, all lit green. 2: hits ahead put out fore bands one third at a time (green, then amber, then red); hits behind the aft. 3: the bands follow each facing's share. 4: the craft's colour moves from green through amber to red. 5: that arc blinks red. 6: the same display where gauge 3 (the shield needle) used to be, with a thin ring around it. 7: ship_status is one of the instruments and can be moved.

docs.title: MT-6-18 — Ship status display: X-COM cockpits A, B and C
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.15.1 or later; the player's data. Steps 1. Fly an interceptor scenario in the Lightning (cockpit A), cockpit view; look at the round ship display in the art. 2. The same in the Firestar (B) and the Avenger (C). 3. Take shield and hull damage. 4. Where the display sits off-centre, press F12, move ship_status onto the art's display, save; restart and check. Expected 1 – 2: the craft and its arcs sit inside the art's round display, centred, not spilling onto the panel around it (placed by eye: note any offset in pixels). 3: as MT-6-17. 4: the saved addon moves it; report the corrected rectangles so the pack's values can be updated. Gauges 1 – 4 still work.

docs.title: MT-6-19 — Main menu: long option values fit
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.14.2 or later; the player's data, so both campaigns are available. A small window for step 3. Steps 1. Main menu › Options; step the Campaign row to the X-COM campaign. 2. Step through the other rows. 3. Make the window small and look again. 4. The launcher's campaign line. Expected 1: the value reads X-COM: Interceptor (no (original data) suffix) and fits beside its label, drawn smaller if needed, never over the label. 2: short values keep the normal size. 3: a long value shrinks, but never below half size; it stays legible. 4: the campaign is named X-COM: Interceptor.

docs.title: MT-6-20 — Screen layouts: moving the strategy screen's widgets
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.0 or later. A test addon mods/default-layout/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with rules/screens.yaml: screens: {starmap: {widgets: {map: [482, 52, 790, 660], nav: [8, 52, 466, 72], info: [8, 132, 466, 212], panel: [8, 352, 466, 360]}}}. Steps 1. Open the default campaign's strategy screen. 2. Use the map, the lists and a prompt. 3. Change the addon to name a widget radar; run --check. 4. Change map to three numbers; run --check. 5. Remove the addon. Expected 1: the map on the right and the list buttons, info and list panels on the left; the top bar unchanged. 2: everything works as in MT-4-29 – MT-4-34 in the new places (clicks land on what is drawn). 3: an error naming the file and widgets.radar: not one of top, map, nav, info, panel. 4: widgets.map: expected [x, y, w, h]. 5: the engine's layout again.

docs.title: MT-6-21 — Good and bad stingers
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. The interceptor campaign with the player's data: only its music sets have good and bad stingers (goodre1.wav, badre1.wav, …); the default campaign's music has only victory and death. Steps 1. On the strategy screen, let a research topic finish. 2. Fly a battle and win; return to the map. 3. Fly one and lose or retreat. 4. Reach an ending (MT-6-26). 5. The same in the default campaign. Expected 1: with the Research complete report a short upbeat sting plays over the strategy music. 2: the good sting as the map returns (after the battle's own victory sting). 3: the bad sting (any result but a win). 4: a victory plays the good sting, a defeat the bad. 5: no sting on the map (record it: the default music defines none).

docs.title: MT-6-22 — A screen layout's background picture
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. A test addon mods/default-backdrop/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with rules/screens.yaml: screens: {starmap: {background: textures/backdrop.png}} and a picture of your own at textures/backdrop.png. Steps 1. Open the strategy screen. 2. Resize the window. 3. Point background at a file that does not exist; start from a terminal. Expected 1: the picture fills the window behind the map and the panels (they draw over it). 2: it stretches to the new size. 3: the screen draws without a picture, and standard error has screens.starmap.background textures/: … once.

docs.title: MT-6-23 — Cutscene text keys; skipping with a click or the gamepad
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. A gamepad for steps 4 – 5; the player's data for step 5. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --cutscene intro; watch it to the end. 2. Again; click the left mouse button. 3. A test addon mods/default-de/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with text/de/cutscenes.yaml giving cutscene.intro.line1 – line3 your own words; run step 1 with --language de. 4. Again; press the pad's A (then B, then Start in later runs). 5. --campaign interceptor --video original:alientrans1.smk; press the pad's Start. 6. In a copy of intro.yaml in an addon, change a caption to @cutscene.intro.nothing; run --check. Expected 1: the captions The frontier, 2084., Regent Vexor's saucers prowl the cosmium belts..., Only the Interplanetary Guard stands in their way. as before. 2: skipped at once. 3: your words. 4: skipped by each button. 5: the film is skipped. 6: an error text: missing key … naming the key and cutscenes/intro.

docs.title: MT-6-24 — --check loads voices, music and faces
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.2 or later. A test addon mods/default-media/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with rules/media.yaml: music: {serial: {stingers: {good: music/missing.wav}}} and voices: {colony_control: {face: faces/nobody.png}}. Steps 1. openinterceptor --no-original --check without the addon. 2. With the addon. 3. With the player's data: --check --campaign interceptor. Expected 1: passes. 2: errors naming music/missing.wav and voices.colony_control.face faces/nobody.png: …; exit status 1. 3: passes when the data is complete (every loop, stinger and voice clip found).

docs.title: MT-6-25 — Save slots and the Load game page
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.14 or later. No saves/default-*.yaml in the user data folder. Steps 1. A new default campaign; play a day; press Save in the top bar. 2. Slot 2. 3. Save again; Cancel (or Esc). 4. Play on a few days; Menu. 5. Main menu › Load game. 6. Enter on an empty slot; on Slot 2; then (from the menu again) on Automatic save. 7. Delete saves/default-2.yaml and restart. Expected 1: a Save game prompt — Choose a slot. (F5 and leaving the map save automatically.) — with Slot 1, Slot 2, Slot 3, Cancel; the clock stopped. 2: Saved to slot 2; the file saves/default-2.yaml. 3: nothing saved. 4: the menu lists Continue, New campaign, Load game, … 5: Automatic save and Slot 1 – Slot 3, each empty or how long ago it was written (just now, 5 minutes ago, 2 hours ago, 3 days ago), then Back; hint Enter: load Esc: back. 6: an empty slot does nothing; Slot 2 opens on the day it was saved; Automatic save on the later day. 7: no Load game item.

docs.title: MT-6-26 — The ending screen
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.14 or later. A test addon mods/default-end/ (pack.yaml: kind: addon, targets: [default]) with strategy/story.yaml: events: {end_win: {when: day >= 99999, do: ["victory(engine_destroyed)"]}, end_lose: {when: day >= 99999, do: ["defeat(last_base)"]}}. (Or reach an ending as in MT-5-07.) Steps 1. A new default campaign; Ctrl+D › end_win › Fire now. 2. Read the screen. 3. Credits. 4. Main menu › Continue. 5. A new campaign; fire end_lose; press Enter (another time Esc, another Main menu). Expected 2: the map darkened; a large panel with VICTORY in the skin's border colour, the ending's text wrapped beneath, the record - final score N - n battles won - n bases, n craft, and the buttons Credits and Main menu. 3: the credits, then the main menu; the campaign was saved. 4: the ending screen again. 5: DEFEAT in the accent colour; Enter, Esc and Main menu all save and go to the menu.

docs.title: MT-6-27 — Options: Full screen and Controls
docs.text: Field Preconditions App 0.16.14 or later. Steps 1. Options › Full screen: Left, Right or Enter. 2. Quit and start again. 3. Start with --windowed. 4. Set Full screen Off; restart. 5. Options › Controls...; Esc. 6. Battles & tools › the launcher's controls entry; Esc. Expected 1: the window goes full screen at once; the row reads On; settings.yaml has graphics: fullscreen: true. 2: starts full screen. 3: starts in a window (the setting stays on). 4: Off; starts in a window. 5: the controls screen; leaving it returns to the main menu. 6: since 0.16.14 leaving it also returns to the main menu, not the launcher (record whether that is wanted).

platform::linux has a test too (joystick event mapping); it is compiled and run only on Linux, so it is not in the count from macOS.

newtonian: acceleration to the cap and coasting, half throttle, reverse thrust, brake stops exactly, turning keeps the velocity, speed hold and drift cancelling, afterburner cap and bleed-off, VCT thrust; Systems), power readout and system lamps, message expiry; the message log reports what is new since a count (the console's events, kept-lines limit) hud::layout 4 Anchor corners lie on the surface with world up; music segments cycle within the wanted state and a missing state plays cruise (app 0.11.0) app::assets 2 Tab cycling; empty lists without original data app::devices 2 Key names match the bindings vocabulary app::flight 10 Camera pose for every view, 3D cockpit field of view widens only on narrow screens, chase orbit, targeting and wing-order commands, pilot messages from events (incl. system, disabled, jump and capture messages), a wingman answers in its own voice (only the player's wingmen, only with the line, never the lost one); looks cover damage levels, states and debris check 2 The default campaign passes; broken definitions become errors extract 3 OBJ export round-trips through the mod loader (positions, triangles, uvs, materials, flat colours), PNG encoding round trip, a full extraction of a synthetic CD writes every override path (incl. cockpit cyan → alpha) cli 4 Every option incl. --extract, --view, --model, --campaign, --screenshot, --frames, environment variable precedence, unknown/incomplete options; content folders are resources/ then packs/, and --packs replaces only the mods folder remote 1 Console input: held actions last until released, taps fire once, the throttle is one-shot, the bindings see a console-held action like a held key, a console that leaves lets go remote::ws 3 SHA-1 and base64 match the published vectors (FIPS 180 and RFC 4648; the RFC 6455 handshake example), masked frames decode (the RFC 6455 §5.7 examples), partial frames wait for more bytes, back-to-back frames, 16-bit lengths, unmasked server frames with 16- and 64-bit lengths; protocol violations are errors (unmasked, unknown opcode, too large) remote::json 3 Objects, arrays, strings with escapes, numbers with exponents; bad and hostile input is an error (unclosed, trailing commas, trailing text, nesting deeper than 32); the writer's compact objects (numbers to 3 decimals, NaN as null) parse back remote::http 3 A WebSocket upgrade parses and the parser waits for the blank line; bad requests are errors (incl. an oversized head) and responses are well formed; byte ranges are served as 206 Partial Content (a-b, a-, -n, clamped end; no range or out of range gives the whole file with Accept-Ranges) remote::protocol 7 Console messages decode (incl. power), unknown actions and types are refused, throttle clamped; pairing codes are six digits and vary with the seed; end to end over a real localhost socket: page served, 404, handshake accept key, unpaired action dropped, wrong code denied, pairing, action relayed, broadcast received; welcome answered at once by the server (0.4.7).
