docs.text: Version Date Change 1.9.1 2026-11-11 Page created: the 3D cockpit workflow with original art referenced from materials (app 0.4.13)

docs.title: Behaviours and conditions
docs.text: How AI ships fly and fight is data: a behaviour in a pack's behaviours: section, named by a ship class (behaviour: saucer_scout) or by one scenario object (behaviour: … on the object). This is the Tier 1 design of Format: behaviours and scripting, implemented in Stage 2 (src/content/behaviour.rs, src/script/, src/sim/ai.rs).

docs.title: A behaviour
docs.text:
A behaviour is a small state machine. Each state runs one built-in manoeuvre with parameters; transitions move between states when a condition becomes true; skill sets how well the pilot aims and how fast it reacts.

behaviours:
  saucer_raider:
    start: engage
    states:
      engage:
        do: attack
        range: 1.8km
        fire_cone: 3
        burst: {per_level: [0.8s, 1s, 1.2s, 1.5s]}
        pause: {per_level: [1.8s, 1.4s, 1.1s, 0.8s]}
        missiles: {per_level: [0, 14s, 11s, 8s]}      # 0 = no missiles at cadet
      dodge: {do: evade, duration: 2s}
      flee: {do: retreat, jump: true}
    transitions:
      - {from: engage, to: dodge, when: "hit_recently(0.3s) and random(0.25)"}
      - {from: dodge, to: engage, when: "time_in_state > 2s"}
      - {from: "*", to: flee, when: "hull < 20% and difficulty >= ranger"}
    skill:
      aim: {per_level: [0.2, 0.35, 0.5, 0.65]}
      reaction: {per_level: [1.2s, 0.9s, 0.7s, 0.5s]}

ships:
  raider_saucer:
    behaviour: saucer_raider

stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> engage
    engage --> dodge: hit_recently(0.3s) and random(0.25)
    dodge --> engage: time_in_state > 2s
    engage --> flee: hull < 20% and difficulty >= ranger
    dodge --> flee: hull < 20% and difficulty >= ranger
  • The ship starts in start (default: the first state listed).
  • Transitions are checked 4 times a second (ai::CHECKS_PER_SECOND), tried in order; the first whose from matches the current state ("*" matches any) and whose condition holds wins. A transition to the state the ship is already in is skipped. time_in_state restarts at 0 on every change.
  • Every condition is parsed and type-checked when the rules load: a misspelt query, a wrong argument or hull and 3 is a load error naming the behaviour, not a surprise in flight.

All keys with types and defaults: Mod file reference › behaviours.

docs.title: Manoeuvres
docs.text: do: What it does Parameters it reads idle Nothing (parked ships, unarmed stations). — circle A slow circle at 35 % of top speed; never shoots (practice targets). — patrol Circles its spawn point. range (radius), speed attack Pursues the target (its current one, else the nearest visible hostile within 8 km) with lead and aim error; fires in bursts inside fire_cone and range (and 95 % of its first beam's reach); launches a missile every missiles seconds when locked; breaks off for 2 s when about to ram; VCT hulls strafe when the target faces them. Without a target it cruises at half speed. range, fire_cone, burst, pause, missiles, speed evade Weaves unpredictably at top speed (VCT hulls also slide). Leave it with a transition on time_in_state. duration retreat Runs from the nearest hostile at top speed, afterburning while energy lasts. jump: true also starts the hyperdrive turret Stays put; beams that can swivel (turret_arc on the ship class) track hostiles within range (and 95 % of the first beam's reach) and fire in bursts. range, burst, pause mine Waits; when a hostile is within range, detonates its first missile rack as an area blast and is gone (Missiles and mines). range (trigger distance) tow Finds a disabled, capturable hostile ship — or, failing one, the nearest towable hostile object (a cargo container, app 0.9.2) — that no one else is towing; closes in, tractors it, hauls it escape from where it took it and jumps out with it (tugs; needs a tractor beam fitted). A towable module is torn off its hub by the tractor. range (search radius, at least 5 km), escape (default 2.5 km) escort Flies in formation on its leader — the newest live member of the role named by the mission role's escort: — and attacks any hostile that comes within range of the leader or of itself, returning to its slot when the threat is gone; without a leader it just fights (app 0.9.2). range, and the attack parameters travel Flies straight on at speed × top speed for range from where the state began, then starts the hyperdrive (a supply ship making for its jump point; app 0.9.2). range, speed

docs.title: Using the ship's systems
docs.text:
systems: tells the pilot when to use its ship's equipment and power. Each entry is a condition, checked with the transitions (4 times a second):

behaviours:
  saucer_raider:
    systems:
      cloak: target_distance > 2km          # stay cloaked until 2 km from the target
      ecm: missiles_incoming(3km) > 0       # jam when missiles are coming
      shields_first: hull < 50%             # hurt: favour shields
Key While the condition holds Otherwise cloak The cloak is switched on (if fitted, working and powered). Switched off. ecm ECM on. ECM off. shields_first Power moves one step at a time towards shields (;), up to the top level. — beams_first Power moves towards beams ('), unless shields_first also holds. —

The requests are exactly the player's keys, so the same power budget and fitting rules apply (a ship without a cloak cannot cloak), and firing still drops a cloak. Both campaigns' pilots run ECM against incoming missiles and favour shields when hurt; the raider saucer and the Shade stay cloaked until 2 km from their target.

docs.title: Target preferences
docs.text:
By default an attacker picks the nearest visible hostile (within 8 km for attack, range for turret). prefer: weights that choice: a hostile matching a selector counts as if it were weight times nearer, so {player: 1.5} chases the player over a wingman up to 1.5 times closer. When several selectors match one ship their weights multiply.

behaviours:
  saucer_raider:
    prefer: {player: 1.5}          # go for the player
  station_turret:
    prefer: {fighter: 1.5}         # shoot fighters before freighters and stations
  wraith:
    prefer: {freighter: 3, class:lightning: 1.2}
Selector Matches player The ship the player flies. a ship kind fighter, freighter, capital, drone, station, probe, mine, debris. class:<id> Ships of that class. faction:<id> Ships of that faction.

Weights must be above 0 (below 1 makes a match less attractive). Preferences only apply when the AI picks a new target: it keeps attacking its current one while that stays alive and visible. An unknown selector is a load error ("prefer: 'x' is not player, a ship kind, class: or faction:").

Wingmen keep the role and orders of Simulation › AI; when they engage they fly attack with the parameters and skill of their class's behaviour (its first attack state).

Fallback. An enemy whose class names no behaviour flies the engine's builtin_attack: engage (attack with default parameters) and evade for 2.5 s, entered on hit_recently(0.3s) and random(0.2) and left on time_in_state > 2.5s, with skill aim 0.5, reaction 0.7 s. A pack may define its own builtin_attack to change it.

docs.title: Skill and fire discipline
docs.text:
Setting Effect skill.aim (0 … 1) Every reaction seconds the pilot picks a fresh aim error of up to (1 − aim) × 8° (ai::MAX_AIM_ERROR). At 0.2 the error is up to 6.4°, enough to miss a fighter at a kilometre; at 1 the pilot leads perfectly. skill.reaction Seconds between the pilot's looks at its target: between looks the pilot assumes the target flies straight on from its last sighting, so a slow pilot leads where the target was going. Lead uses the target's velocity relative to the shooter (bolts carry the shooter's velocity). burst, pause Fire for burst seconds, then hold for pause: pilots do not hose a target continuously. fire_cone Only fire when the aim point is within this angle of the nose.

Together with per-level values these make difficulty. Both campaigns ship behaviours for every enemy type in rules/behaviours.yaml — the default campaign's saucers, robots, gun platforms, tugs, hot-rods and Guard pilots; the interceptor Wraith, Spectre, Phantasm, Shade, Harbinger (tow), drones, pirate and corporate pilots and X-COM wingmen (derived from the strategy guide's descriptions; the original's AI is hard-coded). In the default campaign a cadet-level saucer aims within about 6–7°, looks every 1.2–1.4 s and fires short bursts with long pauses; at space ace it aims within about 3°, looks every 0.5 s and fires long bursts.

docs.title: The condition language
docs.text:
Transitions use conditions — small expressions that are true or false:

hull < 25% and not system_damaged(engines)
target_distance < 1.5km or hit_recently(2s)
difficulty >= captain and random(0.3)
Element Written as Numbers 3, 0.25, .5; with a unit straight after: 1.5km, 350m, 2s, 2min, 1h, 1day, 25% (= 0.25) Logic and, or, not, brackets ( … ); and and or stop early (has_target and target_distance < 1km never asks for a distance without a target) Comparisons <, <=, >, >=, ==, != — between numbers, giving true/false Arithmetic +, -, *, /, unary - Constants true, false; the campaign's difficulty level ids stand for their index (captain = 2 in the default campaign) Queries names from the context below, some with arguments: hit_recently(2s)

Precedence, lowest first: or, and, not, comparisons, + -, * /, then numbers, names and brackets. Names are case-insensitive. Types are checked when the rules load: and, or, not and the whole condition need true/false; comparisons and arithmetic need numbers. There is no assignment, loop or user function, so a condition cannot change the game and always finishes; random draws from the pilot's seeded generator, so a battle replays exactly.

docs.title: Object context: what a behaviour can ask
docs.text:
The queries a behaviour's transitions may use, about the ship flying it (src/script/object.rs). Fractions are 0..1 (write 25% or 0.25), distances metres, times seconds.

Query Type Meaning hull number Hull as a fraction of its maximum. shields number Fore + aft shields as a fraction of full. energy number Beam capacitor as a fraction of full. speed number Speed, m/s. has_target true/false The ship has a target. target_distance number Distance to the target, m (very large without one). target_hull number The target's hull fraction (1 without one). target_disabled true/false The target is disabled. target_is_player true/false The target is flown by the player. time_in_state number Seconds since the behaviour entered its state. hit_recently(t) true/false Hit within the last t seconds: hit_recently(2s). random(p) true/false True with probability p per check (seeded): random(0.3). system_damaged(kind) true/false The system is damaged, knocked out or destroyed: system_damaged(engines). kind is one of engines, manoeuvring, sensors, shields, hyperdrive, vct, tractor, cloak, ecm, damage_control. threats(d) number Hostile ships within distance d: threats(2km). allies(d) number Friendly ships within distance d. missiles number Missiles left in all racks. difficulty number The difficulty level's index; compare with level ids: difficulty >= captain. disabled true/false This ship is disabled. towing true/false This ship's tractor beam holds something. missiles_incoming(d) number Hostile missiles homing on this ship within distance d: missiles_incoming(3km). prize_near(d) true/false A disabled, capturable hostile ship is within distance d.

Missions and events (Stage 3) will add their own contexts with the same language.

docs.title: Difficulty
docs.text: Any number in a behaviour may be {per_level: […]}, a behaviour may have variants per level, and conditions can test difficulty — see Rulesets › Difficulty levels. Cloak lock-break chance by difficulty (Stage 2 item 2.7) is still a fixed strength per system.

docs.title: Errors you may see
docs.text: Message (in --check or on the launcher) Cause states.x: say what it does (do: attack, …) A state without do:. states.x: unknown manoeuvre 'y' do: is not one of the nine manoeuvres. start: no state 'b' / transitions[2]: no state 'b' A name that is not a state. unknown name 'hul' … A query or constant that the object context does not have. 'hull' is a number, not a condition (compare it: 'hull > 0') The condition is not true/false. variants: unknown difficulty level 'x' A level id the campaign does not define.

docs.title: Campaigns (design)
docs.text:
Campaigns — the star map, factions and relations, economy, research, bases, pilots, the story and the rival's plan — are designed in full in Game design and mod format:

  • Mod structure: campaign, addon and library mods; parent.
  • Campaign and game flow: start state, difficulty, arcs, rival plans, score, endings.
  • Strategy layer: map, relations, economy, research, bases, ships, pilots, strategist.
  • Missions, environments and events.

Built so far

The strategy layer's first part is built (app 0.7.0 – 0.7.3): every key a mod can write today is on Strategy layer, with the default campaign as the example.

They are implemented in Stages 4 and 5 (plan). The default campaign will be the worked example for modders.

docs.title: Cockpits (HD and 3D)
docs.text:
A cockpit is an entry of the cockpits: section of a pack's rules; a ship uses it with cockpit: <id>. It can be 2D art, a 3D model, or both, and it says where the instruments go — as rectangles in a 2D design space, and for a 3D cockpit optionally as anchors on the model's surface, drawn in perspective.

cockpits:
  a:
    image: original:CockpitA.dll#12000   # 2D art: original, a pack image, or none
    design: [640, 480]                   # coordinate space of instruments (default 640, 480)
    model: models/cockpit.obj            # optional 3D cockpit around the pilot's eye
    model_offset: [0, 0, 0]              # metres from the eye (x right, y up, -z ahead)
    model_scale: 1
    instruments:
      message: [118, 12, 410, 24]
      radar_front: [111, 332, 60, 60]    # the round glass of the scope
      radar_rear: [473, 332, 60, 60]
      mfd: [246, 338, 156, 82]
      gauge1: [243, 299, 26, 26]         # speed
      gauge2: [288, 299, 26, 26]         # energy
      gauge3: [333, 299, 26, 26]         # shields
      gauge4: [378, 299, 26, 26]         # hull
      ship_status: [111, 407, 58, 58]    # the craft and its shields (app 0.15.1)
Key Default Meaning image — Asset reference of the 2D art, drawn over the whole design space; none for no 2D art. design [640, 480] The size of the coordinate space the instruments use. The art is stretched to it whatever its pixel size. model none Asset reference of a 3D cockpit model. model_offset [0, 0, 0] Where the model's origin sits relative to the pilot's eye, in metres. model_scale 1 Model units → metres. instruments — name: [x, y, w, h] in design space. Names: message, radar_front, radar_rear, mfd, gauge1–gauge4, power, systems, status (the throttle/speed line; without it the line is plain screen text at the top left), ship_status (below, app 0.15.1). A rectangle more than five times wider than tall is a strip and gets the instrument's one-line form (below). anchors none 3D cockpits: name: {at, normal, size} — the instrument drawn in perspective on the model (below). wide none Wide screens: side bands beside 4:3 art: {blackout: true, color: [0,0,0], from: 305, left: images/left.png, right: images/right.png}. The X-COM cockpits black out the dashboard sides from the height where each image's edges become solid (A 305, B 382, C 352) (R-HUD-013).

All instrument text — MFD pages, the message line, gauge labels, the power and systems labels — is sized to fit its instrument's box, so a small rectangle gets small text rather than text spilling out of it.

A cockpit's id also selects the tablet console's per-cockpit colours (console.cockpits.<id>; Console themes).

docs.title: Shield rings
docs.text: Each radar scope carries a ring just inside its edge showing a shield facing: the front scope the fore shield, the rear scope the aft. Green above 66 %, amber above 33 %, red below, blinking red when the facing is down. Size the radar_front / radar_rear rectangles to the scope glass and the ring sits on its rim.

docs.title: The ship status display
docs.text:
ship_status (app 0.15.1, R-HUD-005) shows your craft from above in the middle of a round instrument, in the manner of X-Wing:

  • the craft is a small top-down silhouette tinted by the hull left — green when whole, turning amber, then red as it nears destruction;
  • an arc ahead is the fore shield and an arc behind the aft shield. Each has up to three bands, one per third of that facing's shield: three lit above two thirds, two above one third, one above 2 %, none below. The lit bands take the shield rings' colours (green, amber, red) and blink when the facing is down; unlit bands are dim.

Give it a square rectangle: the display is drawn in the largest circle that fits. On the glass HUD it gets a thin ring of its own; over cockpit art it draws only the bands and the craft, so put it over a round display in the art.

Cockpit Where it is Glass HUD (no cockpit) Where gauge 3 was, beside the other gauges. default campaign's 3D cockpit The third gauge bezel (in place of gauge 3, the summed shield needle). interceptor A, B, C The round ship display in each cockpit's art, placed by eye (derived). If yours sits off, adjust it with the layout editor (F12) and save the result as an addon.

Gauge 3 is still an instrument: a cockpit that wants the needle as well can place both.

docs.title: The power and systems instruments (Stage 2)
docs.text:
Instrument Shows power Four columns: B-<level> and S-<level> (beam and shield charge setting, A–E, one cell lit per level), then F and A bars for the fore and aft shields as a fraction of their balanced capacity (red below 25 %; the favoured facing's label is white). When the power budget is fully used, used/budget appears in yellow. status The throttle, speed and drive/system flags line (THR 20% -274 m/s VCT BURN …), fitted to the rectangle and clipped with .. when long. strips In a strip, power reads B-<level> S-<level> F<fore %> A<aft %> (red when a facing is below 25 %), and systems lists only the systems that are not plain OK in their lamp colours, or SYSTEMS OK. The interceptor cockpits put status, power and systems in the two strips of the top display bar. systems One lamp per fitted system with a three-letter label (ENG, MAN, SEN, SHD, HYP, VCT, TRC, CLK, ECM, DCC): green working, bright cyan switched on, amber damaged, red knocked out (blinking while being repaired), dark destroyed.

A cockpit that does not place them still gets them: small panels at the top right of the cockpit's own design space (from 87.5 % of the design width, 9 % of its height down), with a dark backdrop over cockpit art. The original cockpits and the interceptor pack do not place them, so they appear there; the default campaign's 3D cockpit has bezels for both.

Radar rectangles enclose the scope's glass. Contacts are placed in the circle inscribed in the rectangle, so draw it tight around the round glass (centre on the painted crosshair). Over cockpit art the engine draws only the contacts — the art supplies the scope rings; on the glass HUD (no art) the engine adds two rings and an F/R label. The interceptor pack's values were measured from the original art to ±1 px.

A cockpit needs an image, a model, or both. Without a cockpit (or in the non-cockpit views) the HUD uses glass instruments in a default layout.

docs.title: How the screen is fitted
docs.text:
The design space is scaled as large as fits the window and centred (Layout::new(screen, design)): a 640×480 cockpit fills the height of a 16:9 window with space visible either side; a 1920×1080 design fills it exactly. So:

  • An HD repaint at the same proportions (2560×1920 for 640×480) needs no rule changes at all: just override the image.
  • A widescreen redesign sets design: [1920, 1080] and new instruments rectangles.

docs.title: A 3D cockpit instead of the overlay
docs.text:
With model, the cockpit is a 3D model drawn around the pilot's eye in the cockpit view (F1). It is drawn after the world with a fresh depth buffer, so the world never pokes through it, and with a 5 cm near plane, so struts right in front of the eye are not clipped. Model it in metres around the eye at the origin, +Y up, looking along −Z.

Its instruments can be placed two ways:

2D rectangle (instruments) Anchor (anchors) Drawn flat, over the view, at its design-space position into a texture, then mapped onto a rectangle on the model's surface, in perspective Window shape depends on the field of view matching the design (below) sits in its bezel at any window shape and field of view Used for 2D cockpits; any instrument without an anchor 3D cockpits with screens or bezels on the dashboard

An anchor is {at: [x, y, z], normal: [x, y, z], size: [w, h]} in metres from the eye: the centre of the instrument on the model, the surface's outward normal, and the instrument's width and height on the surface. Its "up" is world up projected onto the surface. An instrument with an anchor is drawn only on the surface in the cockpit view; its 2D rectangle still serves the other views and the fallback.

Field of view. The 3D view normally has a 60° vertical field. On a window narrower than the cockpit's design proportions (a 4:3 window with a 16:9 cockpit), that would cut off the cockpit's sides and misplace 2D instruments relative to their bezels, so the field widens until the design's full width fits (app::flight::cockpit_fov). Windows as wide as the design or wider keep 60°. Measure 2D rectangles for the camera they will be seen with: eye at the origin, looking −Z, 60° vertical field, at the design aspect. Anchored instruments do not need this.

The default campaign's Guard rockets fly from one, an art-deco dashboard (original-free, generated by tools/default_assets/models.py). The generator writes both placements, measured from the bezels it builds, to models/guard_cockpit.instruments.yaml, from which they are copied into the rules:

cockpits:
  guard:
    image: none
    model: models/guard_cockpit.obj
    model_offset: [0, 0, 0]
    design: [1280, 720]
    instruments:
      message: [404, 474, 472, 26]
      radar_front: [101, 540, 155, 156]
      mfd: [548, 514, 184, 186]
      power: [292, 628, 196, 64]
      systems: [792, 632, 196, 32]
      # … radar_rear, gauge1–gauge4
    anchors:
      message: {at: [0, -0.1729, -0.8497], normal: [0, 0.342, 0.9397], size: [0.6449, 0.0351]}
      mfd: {at: [0, -0.311, -0.7995], normal: [0, 0.342, 0.9397], size: [0.2445, 0.2218]}
      # … one per instrument
ships:
  comet:
    cockpit: guard

To give an original ship a 3D cockpit, a mod adds only:

cockpits:
  a:
    image: none                    # or keep the art and add the model on top
    model: models/lightning_pit.obj
    design: [1280, 720]
    # … new instruments in 1280×720, and anchors (or place them with F12, below)

Using your own X-COM cockpit art on a 3D model: a model's material can name the original art directly (map_Kd original:CockpitA.dll#12000), so the mod ships no copy of it. See Tutorial: a 3D X-COM cockpit.

docs.title: The cockpit layout editor (F12)
docs.text:
In the cockpit view of any ship with a cockpit, F12 opens the layout editor; the battle pauses while it is open.

Key / mouse Effect Tab / Shift+Tab Select the next / previous instrument (its name is shown at the top). 2D instrument: drag inside Move it. 2D instrument: drag the corner Resize it. 2D instrument: arrow keys Nudge 1 design pixel (Shift: 10). 3D (anchored) instrument: click the dashboard Place it there: a ray from the eye through the cursor is intersected with the cockpit model; the hit point becomes the anchor's centre and the hit face's normal its facing. Mouse wheel, + / - Grow / shrink the selected instrument by 5 % (2D about its centre; 3D keeps its proportions). S Save. F12 or Esc Leave the editor (unsaved changes stay for this flight only).

Save writes a small addon into the user's mods folder, <user data>/mods/<campaign>-cockpit-<cockpit id>/, with a pack.yaml (kind: addon, targets: [<campaign>]) and rules/cockpit-layout.yaml holding the cockpit's instruments and anchors. It loads with that campaign from then on and overrides the original layout key by key; delete the folder (or disable the pack) to go back. To ship a layout with your own mod, copy cockpit-layout.yaml into its rules/.

Status: the 3D cockpit path, anchors and the editor are implemented; the on-screen checks are manual tests MT-2-14 to MT-2-17.

Planned (Mod Designer, MD8 – MD9): drag each instrument over the cockpit model with a live preview on the face below the cursor, and Create 3D cockpit, which starts from the parent's model or a generic base cockpit in resources/default (design).

Open a model straight in the viewer: openinterceptor --model <ship id or mesh name>. In the viewer, W cycles solid / solid + wireframe / wireframe, [ ] select faces (Shift: ten at a time) and show each face's number, corner count, texture, flags, overlay layer and UVs, I labels every face towards the camera, and O hides overlay-flagged faces.

docs.title: Console themes
docs.text: The tablet console takes its look from the active campaign, and while flying, from the cockpit of the player's craft (app 0.5.0, R-CON-020). A theme is a few colours, a font and a corner radius in a console: section of a pack's rules. It needs no images and no code: the console page derives every tint, border and highlight from these values.

docs.title: The console section
docs.text:
Put it in any rules file; by convention rules/console.yaml:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/rules.schema.json
console:
  theme:                       # the campaign's base look
    colors:
      bg: [0.05, 0.04, 0.08]   # page background (RGB 0..1)
      panel: [0.10, 0.08, 0.14]
      line: [0.79, 0.64, 0.29] # borders, and the fill of a pressed button
      ink: [0.95, 0.90, 0.78]  # text
      hot: [1.00, 0.81, 0.35]  # values and highlights
    font: "Futura, 'Avenir Next', 'Trebuchet MS', sans-serif"
    corner: 2                  # panel corner radius, pixels
  cockpits:                    # optional: changes while flying a craft with this cockpit
    a:
      colors: {line: [0.55, 0.47, 0.27]}
Key Type Meaning theme layer The campaign's base theme, used on the launcher and for every craft. cockpits mapping cockpit id: layer Overrides while flying a craft whose cockpit: is that id (ids ignore case). Only the keys given change; the rest come from theme.

A layer has:

Key Type Meaning colors mapping name: RGB Any of the nine colour names below. font text A CSS font list. The tablet uses the first font it has, so end with a generic family (sans-serif, serif, monospace). corner number The panels' corner radius in pixels. Colour Used for bg The page background. panel Panel and button backgrounds. line Borders and frames, and the fill of a pressed button. ink Text. dim Labels and secondary text. hot Values and highlights. warn Warnings (amber in both bundled themes). danger Danger (red). off Controls the craft does not have (not fitted).

Anything a theme leaves out keeps the page's own default (the green instrument look). A pack with no console section gets that default unchanged. An unknown colour name is a load error that lists the valid ones, and --check reports it. The editor schema schemas/rules.schema.json completes and checks the keys.

docs.title: Layering with other packs
docs.text:
console is a global section: like flight or power, a later pack merges key by key into an earlier one (Rulesets). A mod that only wants a different highlight colour for the default campaign writes just that:

console:
  theme:
    colors: {hot: [0.4, 0.9, 1.0]}

docs.title: How the console receives it
docs.text:
• On pairing (from the launcher), the game sends the campaign's base theme.
  • In a battle, with each action catalogue (on pairing, and when the player switches to a craft of another class), it sends the base with that craft's cockpit layer applied.

Each is a theme {vars} message of CSS variables (--bg … --off, --font, --corner) (Console protocol). To try a theme without a tablet, open the console in a desktop browser on the same computer (http://127.0.0.1:8765).

docs.title: The bundled themes
docs.text:
Campaign File Look default resources/default/rules/console.yaml Art-deco, after the campaign's retro HUD and menus: brass lines on midnight panels, cream text, amber values, Futura, corner 2. interceptor packs/interceptor/rules/console.yaml The page's green instrument look on a darker background, tinted per cockpit with each cockpit's accent colour: A olive bronze, B steel blue, C red.

The interceptor colours were measured from the player's cockpit art and written down as numbers; nothing of the art itself is copied or shipped (R-CON-021). A theme for your own campaign should follow the same rule: your own colours, and every control keeps its text label.

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.10.0 2026-11-11 Page created: the console rules section (app 0.5.0)

docs.title: Cutscenes
docs.text:
A cutscene is a short film the engine plays with its own ships, effects and sounds: craft that fly keyframed paths, fire and explode on cue, cameras that follow them with cuts between, and captions (app 0.13.0, plan item MD2). It is a pack file, cutscenes/<id>.yaml, written by hand until the Cutscene Designer (MD6) edits it. It runs on the ordinary battle simulation at the fixed 60 Hz tick with a fixed seed, so it looks exactly like a battle and plays the same way every time.

Requirements: R-MOD-033 – R-MOD-045 (several partly met; see Not built yet). Design (the full planned format, of which this page is the built part): Mod designer › The Cutscene Designer. Editor schema: schemas/cutscene.schema.json. How it plays: Architecture › Presentation › Cutscenes.

For films made in another program, the original's Smacker videos play through the video(…) action and campaign.intro_video (below); other video files are plan item MD3.

docs.title: Where cutscenes play
docs.text:
How Where it is set Then A new campaign's introduction campaign: {intro: <id>} The strategy screen. A story event the action play_cutscene(<id>) in any story action list (Story layer) Back to the strategy screen; the clock stays stopped. From the command line openinterceptor --cutscene <id> The launcher.

The player skips a cutscene with Esc or Enter. Music stops while one plays.

docs.title: A worked example: the default campaign's intro
docs.text:
A Guard patrol of three Comets meets a Dominion saucer over the Gatehouse station; the leader fires and the saucer explodes; the camera ends on the station.

# resources/default/cutscenes/intro.yaml
id: intro
title: "@cutscene.intro.title"     # text keys since app 0.16.2: text/en/cutscenes.yaml
length: 20s
environment: {starfield_seed: 31, sun: [-0.4, 0.45, -0.8], environment: orbit}
entities:
  gatehouse: {class: guard_station, keys: {position: [[0s, [0, -150, -3200]]]}}
  lead:
    class: comet
    keys: {position: [[0s, [-260, 40, 900]], [5s, [-80, 60, -400]], [10s, [60, 90, -1500]], [16s, [300, 160, -2600]]]}
    actions: [[9s, fire_beams, 2.5s]]
  # left and right: two more Comets on parallel paths
  saucer:
    class: raider_saucer
    enter: 6s
    keys: {position: [[6s, [1800, 400, -3800]], [9s, [700, 180, -2400]], [11s, [260, 110, -1900]]]}
    destroy_at: 11s
cameras:
  wide: {position: [[0s, [-120, 70, 780]], [6s, [60, 110, -260]]], look_at: lead, fov: 50}
  chase: {attach: lead, distance: [[6s, 70], [10s, 40]], orbit: [[6s, [25, 10]], [10s, [10, 6]]], fov: 60}
  station: {position: [[11s, [-500, 260, -1200]], [20s, [-700, 320, -900]]], look_at: gatehouse, fov: 45}
cuts: [[0s, wide], [6.5s, chase], [11.2s, station]]
captions:
  - [1s, 5s, "@cutscene.intro.line1"]       # "The frontier, 2084."
  - [5.5s, 9.5s, "@cutscene.intro.line2"]   # "Regent Vexor's saucers prowl the cosmium belts..."
  - [14s, 19.5s, "@cutscene.intro.line3"]   # "Only the Interplanetary Guard stands in their way."

# resources/default/campaign/campaign.yaml
campaign:
  intro: intro

Play it on its own with openinterceptor --no-original --cutscene intro.

docs.title: Coordinates and times
docs.text:
• Positions are metres in the battle's world: X right, Y up, −Z forward (the direction a craft with no rotation faces). The origin is arbitrary; keep the scene within a few kilometres of it, as a battle would.
  • Times are seconds from the start, with a unit or without: 9s, 2.5s, 1min, 12.
  • Keys are [time, value] pairs; they are sorted by time when the file loads.

docs.title: The file
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning id id required The cutscene's id (named by campaign.intro, play_cutscene, --cutscene). A later pack's file with the same id replaces it. title text the id Its title (for the designer and listings; not shown during play). May be a text key, "@cutscene.intro.title" (app 0.16.2). length time 10s When it ends. environment.starfield_seed number 1 The stars, and the seed of the scene's simulation. environment.sun three numbers [-0.4, 0.45, -0.8] The direction of the sun. environment.environment id none (deep space) A battle environment: its sky, planet, nebula and lighting. entities map none The craft and objects, by id (below). cameras map none The cameras, by id (below). cuts [[time, camera], …] required with cameras Which camera is in use from each time on. sounds [[time, sound, volume], …] none Named event sounds (below). captions [[from, to, text], …] none Caption lines and when they show. The text may be a text key (app 0.16.2).

docs.title: Entities
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning class id required Any ship or object class of the loaded packs (fighters, saucers, stations, asteroids). An unknown class is a load error. faction id the class's Its faction (this decides its radar colour and who its weapons may hit). enter time its first key's time When it appears, at its place on the path. leave time never When it disappears (quietly, without exploding). keys.position [[time, [x, y, z]], …] required (at least one) Its path. One key holds it still. actions list none Timed actions (below). destroy_at time never Shorthand for [time, destroy]. harmless bool false Its bolts and missiles fire, hit and show their effects but do no damage (app 0.14.1).

Paths. The keys are joined by a centripetal Catmull-Rom spline: the path passes through every key exactly at its time, curves smoothly between them, and — unlike a plain Catmull-Rom spline — never overshoots or loops at a sharp corner. Before the first key and after the last the entity holds its position. The speed follows from the keys: far-apart keys close in time make it fast.

Facing. An entity faces along its path and banks into its turns (up to 60°, from how sharply the path bends). An entity with a single key faces straight ahead (−Z).

How entities move. An entity is placed on its path every tick: the simulation never steers it, so the flight model (Realistic or Simple) and the AI do not apply. Its velocity is the path's, so bolts it fires and its engine glow look right.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Action Written Does Fire beams [time, fire_beams, seconds] (default 1s) Holds its beam trigger for that long: its own beams fire as in a battle. Missile [time, missile, <entity>] Targets that entity and fires its missile, as the battle does (the class needs a missile). Destroy [time, destroy] Explodes with the class's explosion, debris and sound.

Each action calls the battle's own code, so bolts, hits, shield flashes, explosions, debris and their sounds are the battle's. Beams and missiles do real damage: a craft caught in another's fire may be destroyed before its own destroy_at. Mark the shooter harmless: true for a show of fire that hurts nothing (since app 0.14.1: its hits land, with their flashes and sounds, but do no damage), and use destroy for kills.

docs.title: Cameras
docs.text:
A camera is fixed (keyframed positions) or attached to an entity.

Key Camera Default Meaning position fixed required [[time, [x, y, z]], …], joined by the same spline as entity paths. look_at fixed the origin An entity id, or a point [x, y, z]. The horizon is kept level. attach attached — The entity it follows. distance attached — [[time, metres], …] behind the entity, linear between keys. orbit attached [0, 0] [[time, [yaw, pitch]], …] degrees around the entity, in the entity's frame (yaw 0, pitch 0 is straight behind). fov both 60 Vertical field of view in degrees (10 – 120).

cuts switch cameras instantly. Before the first cut the first cut's camera is used; with no cameras at all, a fixed view from [0, 50, 300] looking ahead.

docs.title: Sounds and captions
docs.text:
• sounds: [[time, name, volume]] plays one of the campaign's named event sounds — the sounds: section's explosion, big_explosion, shield_hit, hyperspace, mission_accomplished and the rest (Mod file reference › sounds) — at that volume (0 – 1, default 1). The entities' own weapons and explosions make their sounds anyway.
  • captions: [[from, to, text]] shows a line at the bottom of the screen, centred in the letterbox bar, in the skin's font, from from until to. Quote a caption that contains a colon or a comma.
  • Text keys (app 0.16.2): a caption — and the title — may be "@<key>", resolved from the packs' text/<language>/ files like any other text (Text and translation), so a translation addon can give a cutscene its own words. The default intro's are in resources/default/text/en/cutscenes.yaml:
# text/en/cutscenes.yaml
text:
  cutscene.intro.title: "Perils of the Void"
  cutscene.intro.line1: "The frontier, 2084."

# cutscenes/intro.yaml
title: "@cutscene.intro.title"
captions:
  - [1s, 5s, "@cutscene.intro.line1"]

A missing key is a load error (text: missing key … (cutscenes/<id>)) and shows as the key.

docs.title: What the player sees
docs.text: Black letterbox bars cover the top and bottom tenth of the screen; captions sit in the bottom bar. Esc, Enter, a mouse click or a gamepad's Start, A or B skips it (the click and the pad since app 0.16.2). When the cutscene ends (or is skipped) the next screen draws its own sky again.

docs.title: Videos
docs.text:
The original's films are Smacker videos, played full screen and letterboxed (app 0.12.0):

How Written A story event the action video(original:<file>.smk) (Story layer) A new campaign's introduction campaign: {intro_video: original:<file>.smk} — used when the campaign has no intro cutscene An ending endings: {<id>: {video: …}} (Story layer) From the command line openinterceptor --video <ref>

A video reference may also be a pack path (video/<file>.smk); only Smacker files play. A pack path is looked for in every active pack, latest first (app 0.14.1). Enter, Esc, a click or a gamepad's Start, A or B (app 0.16.2) skips a video; its soundtrack follows the effects volume (app 0.14.1).

docs.title: Validating
docs.text: Cutscene files are read with every other pack file when the game or --check loads: a mistake is reported with the file and the key, for example default/cutscenes/intro.yaml: cameras.chase: no entity 'leed'. The editor schema schemas/cutscene.schema.json checks keys and types as you type. A campaign.intro that names no cutscene is a load error (campaign.intro: no cutscene 'x' (cutscenes/<id>.yaml), app 0.14.1). A play_cutscene id that does not exist is still reported only when it would play (cutscene x: no cutscene 'x' on standard error), and the game carries on without it.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
From the design, not in app 0.16.14:

  • Rotation keys (slerp) and speed keys; entities only face along their paths.
  • Autopilot entities flown by the AI (aggressive), switching between scripted and autopilot, and formations of a group following a leader.
  • The actions chase, capture (tractor) and jump (hyperspace); harmless on a single action (it is per entity).
  • Sound files at times with fades, positions and music ducking. (Captions take text keys since app 0.16.2.)
  • Camera height and look-offset keys, keyframed field of view, blended cuts.
  • Cutscenes as a mission's intro and outro; skipping from the tablet console (the pad skips since app 0.16.2).
  • A video: file in place of a cutscene, and video files other than Smacker (MD3).
  • Scrubbing and snapshots (the designer's seeking, MD6).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Message Cause …/cutscenes/x.yaml: needs an id No id. entities.e: needs keys: {position: [[time, [x, y, z]], …]} An entity without position keys. entities.e: needs a class / …/cutscenes/x.yaml: unknown class 'y' No class, or one the packs do not define. entities.e: actions[i]: 'y' is not fire_beams, missile or destroy An unknown action. entities.e: key i: expected [time, value] (also bad time, bad value) A malformed key. cameras.c: no entity 'y' attach or look_at names no entity. cameras.c: needs position keys (or attach:) A fixed camera without positions. cuts: no camera 'y' / cuts: needs at least one [time, camera] A cut naming no camera, or cameras without cuts. sounds: expected [time, sound, volume], captions: expected [from, to, text] Malformed lists. campaign.intro: no cutscene 'x' (cutscenes/<id>.yaml) campaign.intro names no cutscene (app 0.14.1). text: missing key '…' (cutscenes/<id>) A cutscene's title or caption names a text key no pack defines (app 0.16.2).

docs.title: Environments and terrain
docs.text:
Where a battle happens: deep space, in orbit over a planet, in a small "pocket", or in the air above a planet's surface with ground installations on it. Environments and terrains are rules data (app 0.6.0; ground installations 0.6.1), so a mod adds worlds without code. A mission or scenario picks one with environment: <id>; without it the battle is in open space, exactly as before.

Every key with its type and default: Mod file reference › environments and terrains. Requirements: R-MSN-008, R-FLT-011, R-FLT-012, R-HUD-012. Hazards (asteroids, mines, black holes, ion storms) are separate and combine with any environment: Missions › Hazards.

docs.title: A worked example
docs.text:
The default campaign's resources/default/rules/environments.yaml defines four environments and two terrains:

environments:
  orbit:
    # High orbit over a blue world: open-space physics, a planet in the sky.
    backdrop: {planet: {color: [0.30, 0.52, 0.95], size: 48, direction: [0.25, -0.55, -1]}}
  pocket:
    # A small, enclosed arena: tight, close-quarters fights.
    arena: 12km
    backdrop: {planet: {color: [0.55, 0.25, 0.60], size: 90, direction: [-0.3, 0.2, 1]}}
  moon_surface:
    # A cratered moon: thin air, low gravity, a dark violet sky with stars showing.
    physics: atmosphere
    gravity: 3.7
    air_density: 0.35
    ceiling: 9km
    terrain: craters
    sky: {top: [0.03, 0.02, 0.08], horizon: [0.32, 0.24, 0.34], fog: [0.30, 0.23, 0.32], fog_distance: 14km, stars: 0.6}
  dusk_hills:
    # Rolling hills at dusk: thick air, full gravity, a warm sky. Rockets need speed to fly.
    physics: atmosphere
    gravity: 9.8
    air_density: 1.0
    ceiling: 7km
    terrain: hills
    sky: {top: [0.10, 0.12, 0.30], horizon: [0.95, 0.55, 0.35], fog: [0.80, 0.50, 0.38], fog_distance: 10km, stars: 0.1}

terrains:
  craters:
    generate: {kind: craters, seed: 7}
    size: 30km
    height: [0, 1600]
    colors: {low: [0.30, 0.27, 0.26], high: [0.62, 0.58, 0.55], slope: [0.20, 0.18, 0.18]}
  hills:
    generate: {kind: hills, seed: 3}
    size: 30km
    height: [0, 1400]
    colors: {low: [0.22, 0.33, 0.16], high: [0.55, 0.50, 0.32], slope: [0.36, 0.30, 0.22]}

A scenario on the moon:

# resources/default/scenarios/surface-moon.yaml (abridged)
id: surface-moon
player: choose
environment: moon_surface
player_position: [0, 2600, 6000]     # 2.6 km up: start well above the highest ground
objects:
  raider1: {class: raider_saucer, ai: enemy, position: [-800, 2400, 1000], speed: 200}

docs.title: Space environments
docs.text:
With physics: space (the default) the campaign's flight model is unchanged. Two keys change the battle:

  • arena: the arena radius for battles here, replacing flight.arena_radius — a pocket is a small arena with its edge close by ("ARENA BOUNDARY").
  • backdrop: {planet: {color, size, direction}}: a planet hanging in the sky, size degrees across, in direction, lit from the sun's side with a darker limb. It is drawn behind everything, like the stars.
  • backdrop: {nebula: {color, second_color, density, seed}} (app 0.9.1): soft clouds of two colours all around the battle, the stars dimmed behind them — the inside of a nebula. color is the clouds' main colour and second_color the colour they shade into (defaults a violet and a blue); density (0..1, default 0.8) is how thick they are, and also how much they hide the stars (by up to 60 %); seed (default 1) picks a different cloud pattern. The pattern is smooth 3D value noise sampled on a sky sphere, built once per nebula, so it costs nothing per frame. The default campaign's pocket uses one (it showed a large purple planet until the user's playtest asked for a nebula):
pocket:
  arena: 12km
  backdrop: {nebula: {color: [0.60, 0.22, 0.62], second_color: [0.20, 0.40, 0.85], density: 0.85, seed: 7}}

docs.title: Atmospheric flight
docs.text:
With physics: atmosphere every craft that can move feels, each tick (ρ = air_density, g = gravity):

Force Rule Effect Drag a = −k · ρ · |v| · v, with k = acceleration / atmosphere_max_speed² Full thrust balances drag at atmosphere_max_speed in air of density 1. Without thrust a craft slows down. Thinner air (ρ < 1) lets it go faster. Gravity g along −Y, except for hover: true craft A winged craft must hold altitude with lift; a hovering saucer stays up on its drive. Lift g · ρ · (forward speed / lift)² along the craft's own up, capped at 2g At the lift speed the wings carry the weight exactly; slower the craft sinks, faster it climbs. Banking tilts the lift, which is how a winged craft turns. Ground the terrain's height under the craft A touchdown at no more than 25 m/s into the ground while upright is a landing: the craft stops sinking and slides to a halt. Faster, or not upright (up more than about 45° off the ground's normal), is a crash: damage of (impact speed)² × 0.5, a collision sound and a bounce that keeps half the speed. Ceiling the environment's ceiling Climbing above it leaves the battle, as a hyperspace jump does ("LEFT THE ATMOSPHERE").

Ship keys that tune it (every ship class; reference):

Key Default Meaning atmosphere_max_speed 60 % of max_speed Top speed in air of density 1, m/s. lift 120 for fighter, 0 for every other kind The wing speed that carries the weight, m/s; 0 = no wings. hover false Gravity does not pull it down. The default campaign's saucers, dreadnought, robot sentinel, grappler and cargo orb hover; the rockets fly on wings. atmospheric true Can enter an atmosphere. false (a craft without heat shields or wings, say) is refused in an atmosphere environment by the Simulator (app 0.6.3); the strategy layer will also keep it out of surface missions (Stage 4).

Choosing numbers. A craft's stall speed is its lift speed scaled by the air: level flight needs forward speed = lift / √ρ. In dusk_hills (ρ = 1) a fighter with lift: 120 must fly at 120 m/s or more to hold height; on the moon (ρ = 0.35, g = 3.7) the same wings need about 203 m/s, but gravity is weak, so sinking is slow. Its top speed in the moon's thin air is atmosphere_max_speed / √ρ ≈ 1.7 × as fast as in thick air.

Simple physics (R-FLT-013) keeps its arcade handling in an atmosphere: the forces act, but the craft's velocity is still set along its nose each tick.

AI pilots pull up to a climb at a speed their wings can fly when they are below 150 m, or when their vertical speed would take them below 100 m within 3 s.

docs.title: Terrains
docs.text:
A terrain is a square heightfield: a grid of resolution × resolution heights (default 129, 17 – 257), size metres across (default 30 km), centred on the origin. Beyond the square the edge heights continue. The heights span height: [low, high] metres. They come from exactly one of:

  • generate: {kind, seed} — hills: smooth value noise summed over five octaves (rolling hills); craters: a gently rolling plain with about sixty bowl-shaped craters with raised rims, a few large and many small. The same seed always gives the same ground. Built once, while the rules are read.
  • heightmap: textures/terrain/my_world.png — a greyscale PNG or TGA from your pack: black is low, white is high (the red channel is read). Any size; it is resampled to resolution. Built once, when the content loads.

The ground height under a craft is interpolated between the four grid points around it (bilinear), so it has no steps. The terrain is drawn as one mesh, coloured from colors: {low, high, slope}: from low to high by height, blended towards slope where the ground is steep, with a slight per-point variation so wide flats do not look painted. It is lit by the sun and fades into the fog with distance.

Higher resolution means more detail and a heavier mesh: 129 points per side is about 32 000 triangles; 257 is about 131 000.

Not built yet: detail textures (texture: {base, detail}) and scattered objects such as rocks (objects:) — the design is on Format: missions, environments, events.

docs.title: Sky and fog
docs.text:
sky: replaces black space:

  • a dome around the camera coloured from top (straight up) to horizon (at and below the horizon), drawn behind everything; the screen is cleared to the horizon colour;
  • stars (0–1) dims the starfield seen through the sky (0 = no stars, the default);
  • distant things fade into fog (default: the horizon colour). The fade grows with the square of the distance: a quarter at half fog_distance, complete at fog_distance (default 15 km). Make fog_distance shorter than half the terrain's size, so its edge stays hidden.

docs.title: Ground installations
docs.text:
An object class of kind: ground is a ground installation: it never moves, and it is set down on the terrain wherever it is placed, at the ground height plus a quarter of its collision radius — the y of its position is replaced. The environment is set before anything is placed, so this works for scenario objects and mission roles alike. In space a ground object stays where it is placed.

Anti-air is simply a turret on the ground: a kind: ground class with beams, a turret_arc and a turret behaviour. The default campaign's resources/default/rules/ground.yaml:

objects:
  guard_colony:
    name: "@object.guard_colony.name"
    model_set: mining_facility
    kind: ground
    faction: guard
    hit_points: 6000
    shields: 800
    armor: 300
  dominion_flak:                 # an anti-air battery
    name: "@object.dominion_flak.name"
    model_set: dominion_turret_pod
    kind: ground
    faction: dominion
    hit_points: 400
    armor: 120
    beams: [death_ray]
    turret_arc: 180
    behaviour: station_turret

docs.title: The HUD in an atmosphere
docs.text: Over a ground the status line adds ALT 1240 VS -35: height above the terrain directly below, and vertical speed (+ up). The forward view shows an artificial horizon — a level line straight ahead in your compass direction, whatever your pitch and roll — and a pitch ladder with labelled rungs at −20°, −10°, +10° and +20°. In space neither is shown.

docs.title: Testbed scenarios
docs.text:
Scenario (default campaign) Environment What to try env-orbit orbit The planet backdrop; a dogfight with two scout saucers. env-pocket pocket The 12 km arena edge; two Black Comet hot-rods. surface-moon moon_surface Low gravity, thin air, craters, the violet sky with stars; landing and crashing. surface-hills dusk_hills Full gravity and thick air: rockets need speed to stay up; the warm dusk sky and fog; the ceiling at 7 km. surface-colony moon_surface Defend a Guard colony (protected) on the ground from two raider saucers. surface-strike dusk_hills Knock out three Dominion flak batteries in the hills; they track low fliers.

The first four were soaked with the AI pilot (app 0.6.0). The interceptor campaign stays in space, as the original did.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Cause environments.x: an atmosphere needs a terrain physics: atmosphere without terrain:. environments.x: unknown terrain 'y' terrain: names no terrains: entry. environments.x: physics: 'y' is not space or atmosphere A misspelled physics. terrains.x: needs generate or heightmap / give generate or heightmap, not both A terrain must have exactly one source. terrains.x: generate.kind: 'y' is not hills or craters An unknown generator. terrains.x: heightmap <file>: … The heightmap image could not be loaded. mission x: unknown environment 'y' (--check) A mission names an environment no pack defines (a scenario fails to start with unknown environment 'y').

docs.title: Make your first mod
docs.text: A walkthrough that builds a new, original-free campaign from the default campaign (Perils of the Void). No programming and no X-COM data needed.

docs.title: 1. Copy the default campaign
docs.text:
MODS="$HOME/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/mods"   # Linux: ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/mods
mkdir -p "$MODS"
cp -R resources/default "$MODS/frontier"   # from a checkout; in the macOS app: Contents/Resources/resources/default

The default campaign lives in resources/default/ (before app 0.4.2: packs/default/). Your mods folder is loaded after resources/ and packs/, so a mod always wins over what ships with the game.

docs.title: 2. Give it its own id
docs.text:
Edit frontier/pack.yaml:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../schemas/pack.schema.json
id: frontier
name: Frontier
version: "0.1"
description: My first OpenInterceptor mod
kind: campaign
format: 2
requires_original: false

The copy is a campaign of its own: on the launcher, Tab switches between Perils of the Void and Frontier (or start with --campaign frontier). Only one campaign loads at a time, so the copy's ship ids do not clash with the original's. To change a few values of the default campaign instead of copying all of it, make a small addon (kind: addon, targets: [default]) that only contains the changed keys — see Packs.

Editor help. The first line of every file names its JSON Schema. The copied files point at the repository's schemas/ folder. In your mods folder, run openinterceptor --write-schemas "$MODS/schemas" once and change the first lines to ../schemas/pack.schema.json (in pack.yaml) and ../../schemas/rules.schema.json or ../../schemas/scenario.schema.json (in rules/ and scenarios/): your editor then offers completion, hover help and live checking.

docs.title: 3. Change a ship
docs.text:
In frontier/rules/ships.yaml, make the Comet faster, give it a third gun and fit a tractor ray:

ships:
  comet:
    name: Comet Mk II
    max_speed: 700
    beams: [blaster, blaster, heat_ray]
    systems+: [tractor]       # adds to the Comet's list (which already has ecm)

Only the keys you change need to appear if you edit the copy in place; a typo such as max_sped is reported with its file and line, with a suggestion. Power, systems and damage rules are in rules/systems.yaml — see Rulesets.

docs.title: 4. Make the enemy smarter (optional)
docs.text:
The saucers fly the behaviours in rules/behaviours.yaml. Make the scouts aim better and run away when badly hurt, at every difficulty level:

behaviours:
  saucer_scout:
    skill: {aim: 0.6, reaction: 0.6s}
    transitions:
      - {from: engage, to: dodge, when: "hit_recently(0.3s) and random(0.35)"}
      - {from: dodge, to: engage, when: "time_in_state > 2.5s"}
      - {from: "*", to: flee, when: "hull < 30%"}

See Behaviours and conditions.

docs.title: 5. Add a scenario
docs.text:
Create frontier/scenarios/patrol.yaml (see Scenarios):

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/scenario.schema.json
id: frontier-patrol
title: Frontier patrol
player: comet
order: 5
objects:
  station:
    class: guard_station
    position: [0, 0, -1500]
  r1:
    class: scout_saucer
    ai: enemy
    position: [0, 300, -5000]
    speed: 250

docs.title: 6. Bring your own model (optional)
docs.text: Export an OBJ + MTL from Blender (Forward −Z, Up Y, metres) into frontier/models/, then point a ship at it: model: models/hornet.obj. The default campaign's own models are generated by the Python scripts in tools/default_assets/, which are a worked example of building models in code. Textures referenced by map_Kd are relative to the .mtl file. See Models and textures.

docs.title: 7. Validate and play
docs.text:
openinterceptor --check --no-original                       # checks every campaign; fix anything it reports
openinterceptor --no-original --campaign frontier           # "Frontier patrol" is on the launcher

Use the Model viewer to inspect your models, then fly the scenario. D on the launcher changes the difficulty level (cadet … space ace).

docs.title: Looks: model sets, debris and effects
docs.text:
How an object looks in every state is kept apart from what it is. A ship or object class names a model set (model_set: comet); the model set names its model, the texture swaps for its damage levels and named states, the debris set it breaks into and the effect of its explosion. Several classes can share a look, and a remaster can replace a look without touching any class. Keys from src/content/looks.rs; every field with type and default: Mod file reference.

modelsets:
  comet:
    intact: models/comet.obj
    damage:                                   # texture swaps as the hull falls
      - {below: 66%, textures: {guard_hull: textures/guard_hull_scorched.png}}
      - {below: 33%, textures: {guard_hull: textures/guard_hull_burnt.png}}
    debris: comet                             # the debris set used when it explodes
    destroyed_effect: explosion_small
debris:
  comet:
    pieces: [models/comet_debris1.obj, models/comet_debris2.obj, models/comet_debris3.obj]
    pick: [2, 3]                              # how many pieces, chosen at random
    speed: [20, 60]                           # m/s, thrown outwards
    spin: [30, 120]                           # degrees per second
    life: 20s
    chunks: {models: [models/chunk1.obj], count: 6, speed: [40, 120]}
effects:
  explosion_small: {size: 2.5, duration: 1.2s, color: [1, 0.6, 0.2], shockwave: false}
ships:
  comet:
    model_set: comet

The Stage 1 keys still work: a class with model: (and debris: as a list of pieces) and no model_set gets a simple model set of its own.

docs.title: Model sets
Debris sets
docs.text:
Key Meaning pieces Piece models, in the object's own model space: placed at the object, they reassemble it. Each piece starts where it belongs and flies off with the object's velocity plus a random outward push. pick [min, max] pieces thrown, chosen at random without repeats (default: all of them). speed, spin [min, max] outward speed (m/s, default 20–60) and tumble (°/s, default 30–120). life How long the pieces last (default 15 s); wreckage darkens as it cools over its last third. chunks Generic rubble: {models: […], count, speed: [min, max]} scattered from the centre (default none).

The default campaign's generator (tools/default_assets/models.py) cuts each model into its pieces with planes, so they fit together exactly; the scorched, burnt and wrecked textures come from textures.py.

docs.title: Effects
docs.text:
Key Meaning size Fireball size: a multiple of the object's radius (for a missile's explosion, metres). duration How long it lasts. color Fireball colour. shockwave true adds an expanding ring of light in the wreck's plane. sound A sound event name (from sounds:) or asset, played with the effect.

Effects are used by model sets (destroyed_effect; without one, the effect named explosion — a pack may define it, otherwise the engine's: size 2.5, 1.6 s, orange) and by missiles (explosion, sized in metres; without one, a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball).

docs.title: The interceptor pack's looks
docs.text: packs/interceptor/rules/looks.yaml restates the original's wreck table: 28 named wreck sets of up to five chunk meshes each (sets with fewer chunks repeat the first), plus generic rubble, the alien body parts that float in alien wrecks, and the shock-wave meshes. The file holds only names and numbers — set names and original: mesh references read from Interceptor.exe (verified) — never the meshes; which class uses which set follows the names (derived). The original's explosions are XSPT sprite animations, not yet decoded, so the fireballs are the engine's (DEV-034).

docs.title: Checking looks
docs.text:
• Model viewer: D cycles a class's looks — intact, each damage level, each state, and the debris pieces pulled apart from the centre — with the look's name on the info line.
  • --check loads every swapped texture and every debris piece and chunk.
  • The debris-showcase scenario (both campaigns) lines up every class at 2 % hull: the damage textures show at once, and one shot each shows the explosion, shock wave and debris.

docs.title: Missions
docs.text:
A scenario places fixed objects. A mission describes a battle by roles — groups of craft whose classes, counts and arrivals vary — and says when it is won, lost or drawn, and what happens then. Implemented in Stage 3 (part 1, app 0.3.0): src/content/mission.rs (the definitions), src/mission/ (the runtime, architecture), src/script/battle.rs (the battle conditions) and src/script/action.rs (outcome actions).

Missions are a rules section, missions:, so they live in any rules folder (by convention missions/*.yaml) and get everything rules offer: inherit, variants per difficulty level and {per_level: […]} values. They appear on the launcher as Mission: … entries and start with --mission <id>; the strategy layer (Stage 4) will generate them from the campaign.

docs.title: A worked example
docs.text:
# missions/missions.yaml
missions:
  defend_station:
    name: "@mission.defend_station.name"
    briefing: "@mission.defend_station.brief"
    order: 1
    starfield_seed: 101
    player: {class: choose}
    roles:
      station: {class: guard_station, ai: idle, protect: true, at: {distance: 1.2km, bearing: [0, -8]}}
      wing: {class: comet, ai: wingman, count: 2, at: {distance: 0m, spread: 80m}}
      raiders:
        class: [scout_saucer, raider_saucer]          # each member picks one at random
        count: {per_level: [[2, 3], [3, 4], [4, 5], [5, 6]]}
        at: {distance: 6km, from: station, bearing: random}
      robots:                                          # a late arrival
        class: robot_sentinel
        count: 2
        arrive: "time > 75s and alive(station)"
        at: {distance: 5km, from: station, bearing: random}
    waves:
      - {role: raiders, when: "count(raiders) < 2 and time > 30s", count: [1, 2]}
    objectives:
      lose: destroyed(station) or not player_alive
      win: destroyed_all(raiders) and destroyed_all(robots)
    optional:
      station_untouched: hull(station) > 90%
      no_losses: count(wing) == 2
    outcomes:
      win: [score(station_defended), salvage, "relation(guard, +5)"]
      lose: [lose(guard_station), score(station_lost)]
      retreat: [score(station_abandoned)]
    chatter:
      - {when: "time > 3s", line: "@chat.saucers_inbound"}
      - {when: arrived(robots), line: "@chat.robots"}
      - {when: "hull(station) < 50%", line: "@chat.station_hurt"}
    debrief:
      win: "@debrief.defend_station.win"
      lose: "@debrief.defend_station.lose"
      retreat: "@debrief.retreat"

docs.title: The mission
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Shown in the launcher (usually a @key). briefing text empty The briefing, shown in the launcher. order number 100 Sort key among the launcher's missions. starfield_seed number 1 The star field; also seeds the mission's random choices (counts, classes, random bearings). sun 3 numbers default sun Direction towards the sun. player {class, position} choose, [0, 0, 0] The player's ship class (or choose: picked in the launcher, --ship) and start position. roles mapping name: role — Groups of craft (below). player is reserved. waves list none Reinforcements (below). objectives {win, lose, draw} none Conditions that end the battle (below). optional mapping name: condition none Optional objectives, latched when first met and reported on the debrief. timer {after, then} none A time limit: after after (a time) the result is then (win, lose, draw, retreat or killed; default draw). outcomes mapping result: list of actions none What each result does (below). Results: win, lose, draw, retreat, killed. A mission without killed outcomes uses its lose outcomes for it. chatter list of {when, line, voice, speaker} none Radio lines, each said once when its condition first holds. voice (optional, app 0.6.2) is a sound asset spoken on the radio with the line: voice: sounds/colony_control.wav, or a cue:<Name> (app 0.6.7). speaker (optional, app 0.13.1) is the voice set whose name and face the comms panel shows while the clip plays (Radio voices › Faces). debrief mapping result: text none The debrief text for each result (usually @keys). killed shows its own text if given, otherwise none: the lose text usually describes the objective failing, which is not what happened. The debrief appears flight.debrief_delay (30 s) after the result; the battle runs on meanwhile (app 0.7.4, reference). environment id open space Where the battle happens: an environment such as orbit or moon_surface. hazards mapping none Asteroid field, minefield, black hole, ion storm (below). cargo role name none The role whose cargo containers count for the campaign (app 0.9.2): the debrief reports the share still aboard (cargo(<role>) at the end), and a flown convoy escort delivers that share. An unknown role is a load error.

docs.title: Roles
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning class id, or list of ids required A class, or a list: each member picks one at random (repeat an id to weight it). count number or [min, max] 1 How many; a range is rolled when the role spawns. Per level: {per_level: [[2, 3], [3, 4], …]}. faction id the class's Side. ai enemy, wingman, target, idle enemy How it is flown (wingmen follow the player). behaviour id the class's A behaviour to fly instead of the class's. protect bool false An objective the player must keep alive (marked on the HUD, skipped by nearest-enemy targeting). state id none Model-set state, e.g. a construction stage (build_60): no modules or point defence. hull fraction 100 % Starting hull. destroyed_systems ids none Systems that start destroyed. speed number 0 Starting speed, m/s. formation id flight.formation (vee) Wingmen (ai: wingman): the formation they fly in (app 0.6.6). Wingmen of every wingman role take successive slots of it, so two roles never share a slot. An unknown formation is a load error. Escorts (below) use it too. escort role name none Escorts (app 0.9.2): each member flies in formation on the newest live member of that role (a tug), with a behaviour whose manoeuvre is escort. A role that is not defined is a load error (roles.x.escort: no role 'y'). at arrival the player's start Where it enters (below). arrive condition at the start When it enters: the role spawns the first time this holds.

Arrival (at:).

Key Type Default Meaning distance distance 0 m From the reference point. bearing [yaw, pitch] degrees, or random random Direction from the reference point; [0, 0] is straight ahead of the player's start (−Z), positive yaw to the left. Random picks any yaw and a pitch within ±20°. from role name the player's start Place it relative to a role (the centre of its surviving members). spread distance 120 m How far apart the members are, side by side across the line of sight.

Members face the player's start. A role placed from another role that has not arrived (or has no survivors) is placed relative to the player's start.

docs.title: Waves
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning role role name required The role that gets more craft (they count as members of that role). when condition required Fires once, the first time it holds (unless every). count number or [min, max] the role's count How many. at arrival the role's at Where. every time none A repeating wave (app 0.9.2): it comes again this long after it last came, for as long as when still holds (every: 120s).

docs.title: Objectives and results
docs.text:
Every tick after the simulation step the mission checks, in this order:

  1. the player jumped out (hyperspace) → retreat;
  2. the player's craft was destroyed → killed (set by the engine, before the mission's own conditions);
  3. lose → lose (checked first, so a simultaneous win and loss is a loss);
  4. win → win;
  5. draw → draw;
  6. the timer → its then.

killed is the player's death as its own result. Its debrief headline is "YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED"; it applies the mission's outcomes: {killed: […]} if there are any, else the lose outcomes, and shows debrief: {killed: …} if given, else no text. A lose condition such as destroyed(station) or not player_alive therefore no longer reports the player's death as the station falling: the station's text is shown only when the station falls.

    outcomes:
      lose: [lose(guard_station), score(station_lost)]
      killed: [score(pilot_lost)]          # optional; else the lose outcomes apply
    debrief:
      lose: "@debrief.defend_station.lose"
      killed: "@debrief.killed"            # optional; else no text

The battle then freezes behind the debrief: the result, the debrief text, kills, losses and time, the optional objectives (met or not), and the outcome's campaign actions. Enter (pad A) flies the mission again; Esc or L returns to the launcher.

docs.title: Hazards
docs.text:
hazards: (app 0.5.1) puts a battle in an asteroid belt, a minefield, next to a black hole or in an ion storm. It works the same in a mission and in a scenario. Each part is optional, and everything is deterministic for the mission's starfield_seed.

hazards:
  asteroids:  {class: cosmium_asteroid, count: 45, radius: 4km, center: [0, 0, -4500], spin: 8}
  minefield:  {class: space_mine, count: 24, radius: 2500m, center: [0, 0, -3500]}
  black_hole: {position: [0, -500, -7000], pull: 12, radius: 450}
  ion_storm:  {sensors: 50%}
Hazard Keys (defaults) What happens asteroids class (required), count (40), radius (5 km), center (origin), spin (4 °/s), faction count objects of class scattered uniformly through the sphere, never within 300 m of a craft already placed; each turns at a random rate up to spin. They are ordinary objects: they collide, stop shots and can be shot to pieces. Asteroids are scenery: they show on the radar only within radar range, so a field does not flood the scopes (stations still always show). minefield the same; count (20), radius (2 km) Mines of a kind: mine class (Missiles and mines), placed the same way, belonging to faction (default: the class's own). black_hole position (origin), pull (15 m/s²), radius (400 m) Every craft and missile that can move is pulled towards position: pull m/s² at 1 km, growing with 1/d² and capped at 20 × pull (so at 224 m and closer it pulls its hardest). A craft that crosses radius is destroyed. It is drawn as a black sphere of radius with a turning ring of orange glows. AI pilots turn away and burn out inside 4 × radius, or inside 10 × radius while heading in. ion_storm sensors (40 %, at least 5 %) Radar range is multiplied by sensors; missile locks build at half speed; the pilot is told ION STORM: SENSORS AT 50% as the battle starts.

Hazards are placed last, after every role (and in a scenario after every object), so the asteroids and mines keep clear of everyone. Stations and other objects that never move are not pulled by a black hole. Choosing numbers: a black hole's pull at distance d is pull × (1000 / d)². With pull: 12 and radius: 450, the pull at the edge of the radius is 12 × (1000 / 450)² ≈ 59 m/s², so a craft that accelerates at 150 m/s² can still climb out from anywhere outside it if it thrusts away in time; one that coasts is drawn in.

Testbed scenarios: hazard-asteroids, hazard-black-hole and hazard-minefield (default); hazard-asteroids (in an ion storm) and hazard-black-hole (interceptor).

docs.title: The battle context
docs.text:
Mission conditions (objectives, optional, waves.when, arrive, chatter.when) use the condition language with the battle context. The mission's role names are constants, so alive(raiders) is checked when the rules load — a misspelled role is an error with file and line. Difficulty level names are constants too.

Query Type Meaning time number Seconds since the battle began. alive(role) true/false Any of the role is still in the battle. count(role) number How many of the role are still in the battle. destroyed_all(role) true/false Every member that has arrived was destroyed. destroyed(role) true/false The same as destroyed_all (reads better for one object). destroyed_any(role) true/false At least one member was destroyed. retreated_all(role) true/false Every member has left the battle by hyperspace, none destroyed. captured_any(role) true/false A member was captured (towed out by a tractor beam). hull(role) number The lowest hull fraction among the role's survivors (1 if none). near(role, d) true/false A member is within distance d of the player: near(attackers, 2km). arrived(role) true/false The role has entered the battle. cargo(role) number The share (0..1) of the role's cargo containers still aboard (app 0.9.2): modules of a cargo: true class, alive and mounted on a live member — or gone into hyperspace with it — over every cargo slot the members' classes have. A container shot off, torn away by a tractor or captured is no longer aboard. 0 when the role has no cargo. player_alive true/false The player's ship is still in the battle. player_hull number The player's hull fraction. player_retreated true/false The player jumped out. difficulty number The difficulty level's index (compare with level names). random(p) true/false True with probability p per check (seeded).

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
outcomes lists actions, written as calls: score(station_defended), relation(guard, +5), or a bare name (salvage). They are checked when the rules load — an unknown action or a wrong argument is an error. Battle actions run in the battle; campaign actions are listed on the debrief now and will be applied by the strategy layer (Stage 4).

Action Arguments Scope Meaning message(text) text (a @key or words) battle Show a line on the message display. score(name) id campaign Add a mission score entry. money(n) number campaign Add (or take) money. relation(faction, n) id, number campaign Change the player's standing with a faction (applied by the strategy layer since app 0.12.1, campaigns with dynamic relations only; a faction not in relations.start starts from 0 — the default campaign's relation(guard, +5) gives the player's own faction a standing nothing reads). salvage — campaign Collect salvage from destroyed enemies. capture — campaign Keep the craft captured by tractor beam. lose(asset) id campaign The player loses an asset (an outpost, a facility). set_flag(name) id campaign Set a campaign flag. cargo_lost — campaign The convoy's cargo never arrives. cargo_captured — campaign The enemy takes the cargo to a supply depot.

Quote an action that contains a comma or a + sign in a YAML flow list: [score(x), "relation(guard, +5)"].

docs.title: The missions shipped
docs.text: Campaign Missions default defend_station, convoy_ambush, construction_defence, intercept_scouts, and since app 0.6.4 colony_defence, ground_strike, outpost_raid, asteroid_hunt, pocket_ambush; since app 0.10.1 the serial's finale eclipse_assault (Story layer) (missions/missions.yaml; text in text/en/missions.yaml). Construction defence and convoy ambush are the logistics missions; the convoy ambush is flown from the strategy map since app 0.9.2 (below), construction defence is not generated yet. The five from app 0.6.4 are worked examples of environments, hazards and ground installations (below). interceptor xcom_base_defense, defend_freighter_convoy, deep_space_encounter, attack_alien_outpost, destroy_alien_probe — five of the original's 27 types, with the original's own names, briefings and debriefs by key (@orig.BRIEFING_TYPE_1, @orig.DEBRIEF_XBASE_WIN …, read from the CD); the force compositions are derived (DEV-041). %s in an original briefing is filled by the strategy layer later and shows as written for now.

docs.title: Examples: environments, hazards and ground installations (app 0.6.4)
docs.text:
Five missions of the default campaign each show one feature a mission can use. Read them in resources/default/missions/missions.yaml; copy one as the start of your own.

Mission Shows How colony_defence A surface battle protecting a ground installation environment: moon_surface; the role colony: {class: guard_colony, ai: idle, protect: true} (a kind: ground class, set down on the terrain); raiders placed from: colony; a wave while the colony lives; lose: destroyed(colony); an optional colony_untouched: hull(colony) > 90%; a chatter line with a radio voice:. ground_strike Attacking ground turrets, with a time limit environment: dusk_hills; flak: {class: dominion_flak, ai: enemy, at: {…, spread: 1200m}} — anti-air batteries spread along the hills; an escort that arrives after 60 s (arrive:); timer: {after: 6min, then: draw}. outpost_raid A raid in orbit, with wingmen environment: orbit (the planet backdrop); a dominion_outpost with guards placed from: outpost; two Meteor wingmen; outcomes: {win: [score(outpost_destroyed), salvage]}. asteroid_hunt A hazard in open space No environment; hazards: {asteroids: {class: cosmium_asteroid, count: 50, radius: 5km, center: [0, 0, -5000], spin: 8}}; scouts spread among the rocks; a 5-minute timer to a draw. pocket_ambush A small arena with a sensor hazard environment: pocket (a 12 km arena); hazards: {ion_storm: {sensors: 65%}}; hot-rods close by.

Each has a killed debrief (@debrief.killed) so that being shot down never shows the text for the objective failing. Over a terrain, craft placed less than 300 m above the ground start at 300 m (app 0.6.4), so a role placed from a ground installation does not start inside a hill; installations themselves are set down on the ground, and other static objects (a station over a surface) float one radius clear of it (app 0.6.7).

Measured with --soak <mission> --soak-pilot ai --difficulty cadet (app 0.6.4): colony_defence win at 43 s, outpost_raid win at 99 s; ground_strike, asteroid_hunt and pocket_ambush make kills but are still running at 300 s — the AI pilot is a weaker pilot than a player, so these are not balance verdicts.

The launcher's Simulator flies any mission with another environment, added hazards and a larger or smaller enemy force, without editing its file (User guide › Simulator).

--soak <mission id> plays a mission without a window and prints its result (soak mission defend_station (ranger, ai): lose after 132 s; <n> kills); see Validating a mod. --soak-pilot chooses who flies the player's craft: passive (flies at the nearest enemy, never shoots), ai (its class's behaviour) or idle (sits still and does nothing).
