The idle pilot measures how long a defended object holds on its own — the balance check for a defence mission: at the lowest level an undefended station or base should hold for at least 150 s (R-MSN-011; the default campaign's defend_station is held to it by a unit test).

docs.title: The convoy ambush (app 0.9.2)
docs.text:
convoy_ambush was rebuilt to the user's design for supply-convoy battles, and is the worked example of cargo, tugs, escorts and repeating waves:

  • The convoy: two cargo clippers (supply_ship, role clippers, protect: true) making for their jump point at 47 m/s with the behaviour supply_run (manoeuvre travel, 24 km, then the hyperdrive: about ten minutes). Each clipper is built to take punishment and carries twelve cargo pods (supply_pod: cargo, towable, capturable) and one slow-recharging point-defence laser (supply_pd, a turret that shoots missiles and close fighters) as modules. cargo: clippers makes the pods count.
  • Grappler tugs (role tugs, behaviour tug: tow with range: 8km, escape: 3km) come 45 s in, then again every two minutes from 140 s (waves: … every: 120s) while a clipper lives. A tug goes for a disabled clipper if there is one, else the nearest pod; a tractored pod is torn off its clipper ("CARGO CONTAINER TORN AWAY"), hauled 3 km from where it was taken, and the tug jumps out with it — captured.
  • Escorts (role escorts, escort: tugs, formation: vee, behaviour tug_escort) arrive with each tug and fly in formation on it, breaking off to attack anything hostile within 1.5 km of the tug or of themselves.
  • Raiders (behaviour freighter_raider, prefer: {freighter: 4, player: 1.2}) go for the clippers to cripple them for the tugs; hot-rods go for the escort fighters.
  • Win and lose: lose: captured_any(clippers) or destroyed_all(clippers) or cargo(clippers) == 0 — the Dominion wins by taking a clipper or every pod; win: count(clippers) == 0 and cargo(clippers) > 0 — every clipper has left (jumped, or lost) with cargo still aboard. A crippled clipper that never makes its jump ends the battle after 15 minutes in a draw (timer: {after: 15min, then: draw}), and what is still aboard is delivered. Optional objectives: all_cargo and both_clippers.
  • Chatter marks the grapplers' arrival, a quarter of the cargo lost and a minute to the jump.

docs.title: Common errors
docs.text: Message Cause missions.x: roles.y.class: needed (a class id or a list) A role without class. roles: 'player' is reserved (the player's craft) A role named player. unknown name 'raider' (in a condition) A misspelled role or query; role names are checked. waves[0]: unknown role 'z' / at.from: unknown role 'z' A wave or arrival names a role that does not exist. roles.y.ai: 'x' is not enemy, wingman, target or idle A bad ai. timer.then: 'x' is not win, lose, draw, retreat or killed A bad timer result. outcomes.x: results are win, lose, draw, retreat and killed An unknown result name. outcomes.win: unknown action 'teleport' (known: …) An unknown action, or a wrong argument. chatter[2]: needs line: A chatter entry without its line. a chatter voice: clip that does not load The start-up sound: … line names it (--check does not load voice clips yet); the line is still shown, silently. hazards.minefield: needs a class A hazard without class. hazards: position needs [x, y, z] (or center) A position with the wrong number of values. mission x: hazards: unknown class 'y' (--check) A hazard class that the rules do not define. hazards.asteroids: unknown faction 'y' A bad faction (reported when the battle starts). mission x: unknown environment 'y' (--check) An environment: that no environments: entry defines.

docs.title: Models and textures
docs.text:
Asset Mod format Notes Model Wavefront OBJ + MTL v, vt, vn, f (forms 1, 1/2, 1//3, 1/2/3, negative indices), usemtl, mtllib. Polygons are fan-triangulated, so keep them convex. Groups and objects are ignored. Material MTL newmtl, Kd r g b (flat colour, 0–1), map_Kd file (texture, relative to the .mtl; options before the file name are allowed). Texture PNG or TGA Any size; RGBA honoured. Cockpit art PNG or TGA Any resolution; stretched over the cockpit's design space (640×480 unless design says otherwise). Use alpha for the window. See Cockpits. 3D cockpit OBJ + MTL Metres around the pilot's eye at the origin, +Y up, looking along −Z. Replacement of an original asset OBJ / PNG / WAV at its override path See Overrides and extraction; --extract produces starting files.

The original formats (XMSH meshes, XTXR textures, TGA cockpits) are read straight from the CD behind the same interfaces, so original and mod assets can be mixed freely.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Units: metres. Use model_scale in the ship's rules if your file uses other units.
  • Axes: right-handed, +Y up, the nose pointing along −Z (the engine's convention). Blender's OBJ exporter with "Forward: −Z, Up: Y" produces this.
  • Texture coordinates: standard OBJ (v up); the loader flips them for the engine.
  • Normals: used if present; otherwise each face gets a flat normal.
  • Faces are one-sided. A face is visible only from the side where its corners run counter-clockwise (the OBJ and Blender convention for an outward face); from behind it is culled, exactly like the original models. A surface that must be seen from both sides — a fin, a shield, a sign — needs two faces back to back, one wound each way. If a face vanishes when you orbit it in the model viewer, it is wound the wrong way (Blender: Mesh → Normals → Flip or Recalculate Outside).
  • Decals. To lay a marking over a hull face, put a second face exactly in the same plane, facing the same way, later in the file than the face it covers. The engine detects such overlapping coplanar faces and draws the later one on top (a tiny depth bias), so there is no flicker and no need to lift the decal off the surface. Original models mark their decals with a polygon flag instead (XMSH).
  • Texture coordinates repeat: a UV of 0..4 tiles the texture four times across the face.
  • One LOD per OBJ model in Stage 1 (original models keep their four LODs). Multiple LOD files are planned for Stage 6.
  • Attachment points. A group (or object) named slot_<name> is not drawn: it marks where a station module mounts — at the centre of its faces, facing along its first face's normal. One small square, wound counter-clockwise seen from where the module should point, is enough. Modules are turned so their −Z follows that normal; model a module standing on its base at the origin and extending along −Z. See Stations and modules. Original models' attachment points are their manipulators, addressed by index. OBJ models get one engine glow at the back of their bounding box.
  • Looks. Damage textures, named states, debris pieces and explosions belong to the model set, not the model: see Looks. Debris pieces are modelled in the object's own space so they reassemble it.
  • Collision: craft collide as spheres (bounding radius); stations (kind: station) collide against their triangles, so model the station's real shape.

docs.title: Re-skinning original models
docs.text: A model's textures are looked up by name in every pack's textures/ folder (<name>.png, then <name>.tga, newest pack first) before the original XTXR texture. To re-skin, export your image with the original texture's name — the model viewer lists the models, and --check reports texture names that fail to load.

docs.title: Textures from the player's original data
docs.text:
A material may name original data instead of a file, so a mod can use the player's own art without shipping it:

map_Kd original:CockpitA.dll#12000   # an original image (cockpit art); cyan becomes transparent
map_Kd original:INTTOP               # an original model texture, by name

Only lines starting with # are comments; the # in #12000 is part of the value. --check loads every such reference and reports one that does not exist. Walkthrough: Tutorial: a 3D X-COM cockpit. Status: new in app 0.4.13, being evaluated in practice.

docs.title: Checking a model
docs.text: Open it straight in the viewer: openinterceptor --model <ship id or mesh name>. In the viewer, W cycles solid / solid + wireframe / wireframe, D cycles the class's looks (intact, damage levels, states, debris pulled apart), [ ] select faces (Shift: ten at a time) and show each face's number, corner count, texture, flags, overlay layer and UVs, I labels every face towards the camera, and O hides overlay-flagged faces.

docs.title: Example
docs.text: Every model of the default campaign — rockets, saucers, the robot sentinel, freighters, stations, rubble, debris pieces and the Guard 3D cockpit — is written by the Python scripts in tools/default_assets/ (models.py, with textures.py for hull paint and its scorched and burnt damage variants — and wrecked for station modules — and sounds.py for synthesised effects). Run python3 tools/default_assets/make_all.py to rebuild them, or make_all.py --check to build twice and prove the output is byte-identical. The scripts use only the Python standard library, seed every random choice, and validate every model before writing it (closed solids wound counter-clockwise from outside, no degenerate faces, within a triangle budget). Look at them to see how a model, its .mtl materials and its textures are written programmatically.

docs.title: The generator's conventions
docs.text: Convention In tools/default_assets/ Debris Each model is cut by planes into its <name>_debris<n>.obj pieces, in the model's own space. Attachment points slot(name, at, normal) adds one small square face in a group slot_<name>, centred on at and wound so its normal is normal; slots are open parts, so the validator checks them for degeneracy only, and debris cutting leaves them out. Station modules Stand on their base at the origin and extend along −Z (the slot's normal), e.g. the Guard ray turret and force-field generator, the Dominion death-ray pod and shield pod. Damage textures <texture>_scorched.png, <texture>_burnt.png; modules also <texture>_wrecked.png for their destroyed state. Instrument placement The Guard cockpit's rectangles and anchors, written to models/guard_cockpit.instruments.yaml.

docs.title: Music
docs.text:
Battles and the strategy screen play interactive music (app 0.11.0, plan item 6.4): a music set has states — calm, threatened, fighting, the star map — each a list of segments, and stingers played once when a mission is won or lost. The music changes state only when a segment ends, so it never cuts off mid-phrase. Music is rules data: a campaign without a music: section is silent, and a mod can replace or add sets without code.

Requirement: R-CPN-012. Every key with its type: Mod file reference › music. How the engine plays it: Architecture › Audio › Music. The player sets the music volume in the launcher (User guide › Settings).

docs.title: The states
docs.text:
State When it plays cruise In a battle with no hostile craft within threat_range of the player. Also the fallback for any state a set does not define. threat A hostile craft is within threat_range (default 12 km), but none within battle_range. battle A hostile craft is within battle_range (default 4 km). strategy On the strategy screen; also on the main menu when the set has no menu state. menu On the main menu (app 0.14.0), when the first set defines it.

"Hostile" means a live ship of a faction hostile to the player's; stations and other static objects do not count. Only these state names are used by the engine; a set may define others, but nothing will ask for them.

Each state's segments play in turn (the first, the second, … then the first again). When a segment ends the player starts the next segment of whatever state is wanted now, so a fight that starts in the middle of a cruise segment brings in the battle music at the end of that segment.

docs.title: Stingers
docs.text:
Stinger When it plays victory A mission's result is decided as a win (with the computer voice, before the debrief). death Any other result (lose, draw, retreat, killed). good, bad On the strategy screen (app 0.16.2): good when a battle flown from the map was won (as the map returns), when research completes and when the campaign ends in a victory; bad after any other battle result and on a defeat (DEV-059). The interceptor sets map them to the CD's loops; the default campaign's music has none, so nothing plays there.

A stinger plays once, over the segment that is playing.

docs.title: Which set plays
docs.text:
• In a battle one of the campaign's sets is chosen by the battle's star-field seed (set seed mod number of sets), so the same battle always has the same music and different battles vary.
  • On the strategy screen the first set plays its strategy state (or its cruise).
  • On the main menu the first set plays its menu state, else its strategy state.
  • Every other screen — the launcher, the credits roll, the viewer, the asset browser, videos and cutscenes — is silent.

docs.title: A worked example: the default campaign
docs.text:
The default campaign's music is synthesised by tools/default_assets/music.py (Python standard library only, deterministic): four states of two seamless four-bar loops each, and two stingers, written as 16 kHz mono WAVs to resources/default/music/.

# resources/default/rules/music.yaml
music:
  serial:
    states:
      cruise: [music/cruise1.wav, music/cruise2.wav]
      threat: [music/threat1.wav, music/threat2.wav]
      battle: [music/battle1.wav, music/battle2.wav]
      strategy: [music/strategy1.wav, music/strategy2.wav]
    stingers: {victory: music/victory.wav, death: music/death.wav}
    threat_range: 10km
    battle_range: 3500m
    volume: 55%

The generated WAVs are committed (since main 16a9954, an exception to the repository's *.wav safety net); run music.py again only after changing its score.

docs.title: The interceptor campaign
docs.text:
packs/interceptor/rules/music.yaml maps the original's three loop sets by file name from the player's own data (Loops/ on the CD; original:<file>.wav finds a file by name in any layout): for each set, five cruise, five threat and five battle segments, and the death, victory, good and bad stingers. The strategy screen plays each set's cruise segments as its strategy state (derived: what the original plays on its strategy screens is not mapped).

The original also has transition tables (Loops/*.wtl) that say how one segment leads to another; they are not read. The engine always changes at the end of a segment (DEV-053).

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text:
1. Make loops that start and end at the same point in the bar, so a segment can follow itself or another state's segment without a click. Any WAV the engine reads works (PCM 8/16-bit, MS ADPCM, IMA ADPCM).
  2. Put them in your pack (music/…) and list them under states. A state may be a single file instead of a list: threat: music/threat.wav.
  3. Set threat_range and battle_range for your battles' scale, and volume for the set's level against the effects.
  4. --check validates the section; the sounds themselves are loaded when the game starts, and a file that fails prints a sound: … line.

Several sets in one campaign are allowed: a battle picks one by its seed. An addon can add a set or replace one by id like any other definition (Rulesets).

docs.title: Volume
docs.text: What you hear is volume (the set's) × the player's music volume (settings.yaml audio.music, 70 % by default). The player's effects volume scales every other sound — weapons, explosions, voices, the computer voice — but not the music or its stingers.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
• Switching rules as data (the design's switch: list with conditions); the states are chosen by the fixed nearest-hostile rule above.
  • The original's .wtl transition tables; CD audio tracks; good and bad stingers for the default campaign (the strategy screen plays them since app 0.16.2, but the default music has none).
  • Music in cutscenes (a cutscene's sounds are named event sounds) and over videos (a video's own soundtrack plays).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Message Cause music.x: a music set needs states (cruise, threat, battle, strategy) No states. music.x: states.y: no segments A state with an empty list. sound: <file>: … (at start-up; since app 0.16.2 also from --check) A segment or stinger file that is missing or does not decode.

docs.title: Overrides and extraction
docs.text:
Any original asset can be replaced one file at a time: put a file at the asset's override path inside an active pack, and the engine uses it instead of the original version. Everything you do not replace still comes from the original data (your installed copy or CD). The highest-priority pack wins (the last one in load order), so several mods can stack.

Original asset Override path in your pack Format mesh INTTYPEA (any original:NAME model) models/inttypea.obj (+ its .mtl) Wavefront OBJ, metres, +Y up, nose along −Z texture CUBETOP (named by an original model) textures/cubetop.png or .tga any size image CockpitA.dll#12000 (cockpits, HUD art, menus, sprites) images/cockpita/12000.png or .tga any size; alpha = see-through sound Xwinder.wav sounds/xwinder.wav WAV (PCM or ADPCM)

Names are lower-case; the image folder is the DLL's name without .dll. Replacement images are used as they are — the original cockpits' cyan colour key is not applied, so mark see-through areas with PNG alpha.

docs.title: Extracting the originals
docs.text:
You do not need to know the names: the engine converts all of your original data for you, writing every asset at its override path:

openinterceptor --extract ~/Desktop/interceptor-extracted
# extract: 297 models, 799 textures, 3244 images, 792 sounds, 27 reference files; 0 errors

interceptor-extracted/
  README.txt, pack.yaml     (id interceptor-extracted; personal use only)
  models/<name>.obj, .mtl   most detailed LOD; textures referenced as ../textures/<tex>.png
  textures/<name>.png
  images/<dll>/<id>.png     cockpit cyan already turned into transparency
  sounds/<name>.wav         16-bit PCM (sound effects and music loops)
  original-data/            the original INI and text files, for reference (read-only data)

The extracted files are converted copies of copyrighted content from your copy of the game: use them to make your own art, keep them to yourself, and never put them in a mod you share. A shared mod should contain only files you made.

To find which file you want, open the launcher's Asset browser: it lists every texture, image and sound under the same names, and marks the ones a pack already overrides.

docs.title: Walkthrough: repaint the cockpit in HD
docs.text:
The original Lightning II cockpit is 640×480. Here is how to replace it with a modern repaint, without touching any rule.

  1. Extract (once): openinterceptor --extract ~/interceptor-extracted.
  2. Find the image: the Lightning II uses cockpit a, whose rules say image: original:CockpitA.dll#12000. Its extracted copy is ~/interceptor-extracted/images/cockpita/12000.png.
  3. Paint a new version at any resolution with the same 4:3 proportions — for example 2560×1920. Keep the windows transparent (alpha 0) and keep the instruments' screens where they were, scaled up: the instrument rectangles are given in the 640×480 design space, so a 4× repaint lines up automatically.

  4. Make a mod:

    ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/mods/hd-cockpit/
  pack.yaml
  images/cockpita/12000.png      ← your repaint

    id: hd-cockpit
name: HD cockpit
kind: addon
targets: [interceptor]
requires_original: true
format: 2

  5. Check and fly: openinterceptor --check (no errors), then the Asset browser shows CockpitA.dll #12000 [overridden by hd-cockpit], and any flight with the Lightning II uses the new art.

This was verified with a 2560×1920 test repaint: it replaced the original in game and every instrument stayed in place. To compare with the original, add hd-cockpit to packs: {disabled: [...]} in settings.yaml.

A widescreen redesign (16:9 art rather than 4:3) needs new instrument positions too: add a cockpits: {a: …} entry to your mod with design: [1920, 1080] and new instruments rectangles in that space — only the keys you change; the rest is inherited by layering. For a 3D cockpit the in-game layout editor (F12) writes such an addon for you. See Cockpits.

docs.title: Other common overrides
docs.text:
• New ship model: export from Blender as OBJ (metres, +Y up, forward −Z) to models/<original mesh name>.obj — e.g. models/inttypea.obj — and every Lightning II uses it. For a ship of your own, add a ship under ships: instead, with model: models/....
  • Re-skin: textures/<texture name>.png changes that texture on every model using it.
  • Sounds: sounds/xwinder.wav replaces the X-Winder launch sound.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Nothing changed: the file name or folder does not match — compare with the extracted path or the Asset browser label (all lower-case). Is the pack disabled in settings.yaml, or does its targets miss the campaign being played?
  • Black or cyan edges: the image needs real alpha; the cyan key is only applied to the original files.
  • Model faces the wrong way: the engine's forward is −Z; rotate the model 180° before export.

docs.title: Packs
docs.text:
A pack is a folder of content with a pack.yaml manifest. The engine loads packs from three places, in this order (app 0.4.2):

  1. resources/ — what ships with the game: the default campaign in resources/default/;
  2. packs/ — the bundled mods, such as interceptor (--packs <dir> replaces this folder only);
  3. the user mods folder (or --mods <dir>).

Later packs override earlier ones, so a mod overrides resources. The player's original data (resources/xcom/, resources/xcom-cd/ or a folder given with --data) is not a pack: it has no pack.yaml and is read only through original: references. Within a folder, packs are found in folder-name order and then ordered so that every pack comes after the packs it depends on (otherwise keeping that order). Later packs override earlier ones, key by key.

Since Stage 2 not every pack found is loaded: the player plays one campaign, and only the packs that belong with it load — see Mod kinds and the active set.

Default mods folder: macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/mods/, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/mods/ (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/mods/), or settings.yaml paths: {mods: …} (Settings).

docs.title: Packs and mods
docs.text:
Packs and mods use the same format. The difference is where they come from and whether a build includes them:

  • packs are "baked into" the game on build: resources/ and the bundled packs/, which a product bundle includes;
  • mods are added externally, in the user's local mods folder.

A mod built on another pack, which adds to it or overrides its assets, is an extension of that pack (planned in the Mod Designer; R-MOD-023). Today it is written as a campaign with parent: or an addon with targets:, below.

Open

Where exactly the line between a pack and a mod falls is to be settled, for example whether a mod promoted into a product bundle becomes a pack; and whether extension becomes a manifest kind or maps onto addon (MD4).

docs.title: Mod kinds and the active set
docs.text:
Every pack is one of three kinds (kind: in pack.yaml; from src/content/pack.rs):

Kind What it is Extra keys campaign A complete, playable game (default, interceptor). parent — the campaign it extends. addon (the default) Changes to one or more campaigns: a balance mod, a new ship, an HD cockpit. targets — the campaign ids it applies to (["*"] = all; none = all). library Shared content, loaded only when another pack depends on it. —

When campaign C is played, the active set is:

  1. C's parent chain — its parent, that campaign's parent, and so on (root first);
  2. every addon whose targets names a campaign in the chain (or *, or nothing);
  3. every pack any of those depends on (libraries and others), transitively.

Everything else stays out. The active set then loads parents and dependencies first; later packs override earlier ones key by key, so a campaign with parent: interceptor is "the Interceptor campaign plus my changes".

flowchart LR
  subgraph found["Packs found"]
    D["default<br/>campaign"]
    I["interceptor<br/>campaign"]
    R["remaster<br/>campaign, parent: interceptor"]
    A1["hd-cockpits<br/>addon, targets: interceptor"]
    A2["faster-comet<br/>addon, targets: default"]
    L["shared-art<br/>library"]
  end
  A1 -. depends .-> L
  subgraph active["Active set when playing remaster"]
    direction LR
    L2["shared-art"] --> I2["interceptor"] --> R2["remaster"] --> A12["hd-cockpits"]
  end

docs.title: Choosing the campaign
docs.text:
Where How Launcher The header shows Campaign: …; Tab (pad Y) switches to the next campaign and reloads content. settings.yaml game: {campaign: default} — the launcher writes the last choice here. Command line --campaign <id>. None of these interceptor when the player's data makes it available, otherwise default, otherwise the first campaign found.

An unknown or unavailable campaign falls back to that default with a warning. --list lists the campaigns (* marks the loaded one); --check checks every campaign separately, each with its own active set, so an addon must pass with each campaign it targets. If no pack is a campaign at all (a Stage 1 set-up), every pack loads as before.

docs.title: Mod-format version
docs.text:
format: 2 records the mod-format version the pack was written for. A pack with a higher format than the engine reads (pack::FORMAT, currently 2) is refused with a message asking for a newer OpenInterceptor; a missing format means the current one.

Format Since Files 1 Stage 1 INI: pack.ini, rules/*.ini, scenarios/*.ini. No longer read: a folder with only a pack.ini is reported ("pack.ini is the old INI mod format (format 1) …") and skipped. 2 Stage 2 YAML: pack.yaml, rules/*.yaml, campaign/*.yaml, scenarios/*.yaml (Rulesets).

Converting a format-1 mod by hand: section [ship:comet] becomes ships: / comet:, keys become snake_case (MaxSpeed = 620 → max_speed: 620), comma lists become [a, b], yes/no become true/false, Systems.add = ecm becomes systems+: [ecm], and ; comments become #. The built-in packs in resources/default/ and packs/interceptor/ show the result for every section.

docs.title: Switching packs on and off
docs.text:
A pack in the active set loads unless its id is listed in settings.yaml:

packs:
  disabled: [hd-cockpit-test, balance-tweak]

A disabled pack contributes nothing — no rules, no scenarios, no asset overrides — so removing an id from the list restores the mod, and adding it restores the originals. Packs that depend on a disabled pack are skipped too. (XWVM offers the same whole-pack switch in its launcher's Game Content screen; a launcher screen for this is planned for Stage 5.)

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
my-campaign/
  pack.yaml             the manifest (required)
  rules/*.yaml          ships, beams, missiles, objects, factions, cockpits, systems,
                        behaviours, modelsets, debris, effects, flight, power, damage,
                        sounds, audio
                        (all files loaded, in file-name order)
  campaign/*.yaml       campaigns: the campaign ruleset (name, difficulty levels)
  text/<lang>/*.yaml    player-visible strings by key; imports of the original's text
  scenarios/*.yaml      playable arenas (all files loaded)
  models/*.obj, *.mtl   models (any folder works; paths are written in the rules)
  textures/*.png, *.tga textures; also how a pack re-skins a model texture by name
  images/<dll>/<id>.png replacement original images (cockpits, HUD art) — see Overrides
  sounds/*.wav          sounds; sounds/<name>.wav also replaces an original sound

Only pack.yaml is required; every folder is optional. Every rule file may live in any of rules/ or campaign/; the split is a convention.

docs.title: pack.yaml
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/pack.schema.json
id: my-campaign            # letters, digits, - and _ only; must be unique
name: My Campaign
version: "1.0"             # quoted: text, not a number
description: A new war on the frontier
kind: campaign             # campaign | addon (the default) | library
parent: default            # campaigns only: the campaign this one extends
# targets: [default]       # addons only: campaigns it applies to (["*"] = all)
depends: []                # ids that must load first
requires_original: false   # true = needs the player's Interceptor data (--data)
format: 2                  # mod-format version it was written for
Key Default Meaning id — (required) Unique id. name the id Shown on the launcher. version 0 Free text. description empty Free text. kind addon campaign, addon or library (above). Anything else is an error. parent none Campaigns only (an error on other kinds): the campaign this one extends. A missing parent or a parent cycle is an error. targets all Addons only: a list of campaign ids, or ["*"]. format current Mod-format version; newer than the engine's is an error. authors, licence — Informational. depends none Packs that must be installed and load first. A missing dependency is an error; a cycle is an error. requires_original false true skips the pack (with a warning) when no original data is loaded; packs depending on it are skipped too.

docs.title: Built-in packs
docs.text: Pack Folder Needs original data Contents default resources/default no Campaign Perils of the Void: the original-free default campaign — 1950s film-serial rocket ships of the Interplanetary Guard against the flying saucers of the Umbral Dominion. Seven factions, six beams and two missiles, playable rockets comet, meteor, thunderbolt flown from the 3D cockpit guard, saucers, a robot sentinel, freighters, stations, systems and power rules, behaviours with four difficulty levels, and the scenarios rocket-vs-saucer, dominion-raid, black-comet-ambush, systems-trial. Models, textures and sounds are generated by tools/default_assets/. Copy this to start a mod — see Make your first mod. interceptor packs/interceptor yes Campaign. Rules that inherit the original GameSettings.ini sections, the class → mesh mapping, cockpits, systems and power rules (rules/systems.yaml), the campaign ruleset with the original's five difficulty levels, event sounds, and the test scenarios flight-test, combat-test, gunnery-range, station-tour, systems-trial. No assets: every model, texture, image and sound is an original: reference into the player's original data (an installed copy or the CD).

docs.title: Asset references
docs.text:
Rules refer to assets with a reference string:

Written as Means models/scout.obj A file in the pack that wrote the reference. \ is accepted; . and .. are normalised inside the pack (models/../textures/a.png = textures/a.png); a path that would leave the pack, starts with / or contains : is refused. original:INTTYPEA A named resource in the original DLLs; the kind comes from the key (model → an XMSH mesh). original:CockpitA.dll#12000 Resource 12000 of a specific original DLL (cockpit image). original:GameSettings.ini, original:target lock.wav An original file, found by name anywhere in the data folder (any case).

Textures named inside a model are looked up as textures/<name>.png then .tga in every pack, latest pack first, before falling back to the original XTXR texture of that name. Dropping textures/cubetop.png into a mod therefore re-skins every original model that uses cubetop. The same rule covers every original asset — meshes, cockpit and HUD images, sounds — see Overrides and extraction.

docs.title: Mod file reference
docs.text:
Every key of every mod file type, from the schemas in src/content/files.rs (the same definitions produce the editor JSON Schemas in schemas/ and validate files on load). Types:

Type Written as number 620, 0.5; any number may also be {per_level: [a, b, …]} (difficulty) distance / time / angle / fraction a number with an optional unit: 2.4km, 1.5s, 12deg, 40% (plain = metres, seconds, degrees, 0..1) text free text; quote it if it contains : or starts with a symbol. Player-visible names and descriptions may instead be a text key, "@ship.comet.name", resolved from text/<language>/ (Text and translation) id a lower-case id (blaster) ids a list of ids: [a, b] asset an asset reference: models/comet.obj, original:INTTYPEA, none where allowed bool true / false RGB three numbers 0..1: [1.0, 0.55, 0.15] condition a condition in quotes

Every definition (an entry under ships, beams, behaviours, … and the global sections) may also use inherit, delete: true, variants: {<level>: {…}} and list edits <key>+: […] / <key>-: […] (Rulesets). "—" in the Default column means no default (the key is optional unless marked required).

docs.title: pack.yaml
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning id id required Unique id: a-z, 0-9, - and _. name text the id Shown in the launcher. version text 0 The pack's own version (quote it: "1.0"). description text empty One or two sentences for the launcher. kind campaign / addon / library addon See Packs. parent id — Campaigns: the campaign this one extends. targets ids all Addons: campaigns it applies to (["*"] = all; quote the *). depends ids none Packs that must load first. requires_original bool false true when the pack reads the player's Interceptor CD. format number current (2) Mod-format version the pack was written for. authors, licence text — Informational.

docs.title: Rules files (rules/*.yaml, campaign/*.yaml)
docs.text:
Top-level sections: factions, beams, missiles, ships, objects, systems, cockpits, behaviours, modelsets, debris, effects, voices, environments, terrains, formations, missions, and since app 0.11.0 – 0.11.1 music and skins and since app 0.16.0 screens (definitions by id), and flight, power, damage, sounds, audio, console, campaign (global). The strategy layer adds the definitions maps, star_classes, research, items, hulls, base_modules, base_types, raids, incomes, expenses and the globals start, research_model, pilots, scores, flags, economy, tech_ids (app 0.8.0), by convention in strategy/*.yaml — every key is on Strategy layer. Its optional logistics (app 0.9.0) adds the definitions resources, components, recipes, facility_types, research_sites, the global logistics, and keys on existing entries: map systems' deposits and features, hulls' components, topics' lab, site and start_cost (Strategy layer › Logistics). New strategy keys in app 0.8.0: start.money_from, economy.cost_scale, economy.module_time, and the original's numeric prereq1 – prereq3, tech_required, tech_required2 read through tech_ids (tech_ids); in app 0.9.2 logistics.ambush_mission. The story layer (app 0.10.0) adds the definitions events, arcs, plans, endings, encyclopaedia and the globals relations, strategist, campaign_end, by convention in strategy/story.yaml — every key is on Story layer. All of them are in the editor schema schemas/rules.schema.json.

Times take s, min, h and, since app 0.6.7, d (days): 10d.

docs.title: factions
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. color RGB 0.8, 0.8, 0.8 Radar and HUD colour. hostile ids none Faction ids this faction fights. Hostility is symmetric: either side declaring it is enough.

docs.title: beams
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. damage number 25 Damage per hit. energy_cost number 10 Energy per shot. rate_of_fire number 2 Shots per second per mount. speed number 2000 Bolt speed, m/s. range distance 3000 m Reach (2.4km, 2400m; a plain number is metres). An original Range inherited from GameSettings.ini is read as kilometres (DEV-008). color RGB 1, 0.2, 0.2 Bolt colour. sound asset none Firing sound.

docs.title: missiles
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. speed number 1000 Top speed, m/s. duration time 10 s Flight time before self-destruct. impact_damage number 300 Damage on a direct hit. proximity_damage number 200 Damage from the proximity fuse. proximity_radius distance 25 m Proximity fuse radius. turn_rate number 90 Degrees per second while homing. lock_time time 2 s Seconds in the lock cone to lock on. color RGB 1, 0.8, 0.4 Trail colour. sound asset none Launch sound (or cue:<Name>). explosion id a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball Effect of its detonation (effects); its size is in metres, and its sound, if any, plays instead of the explosion event sound. guidance homing, dumbfire, sidestep, parallax, cloaked_wait, cluster, doppelganger homing How it steers (Missiles and mines). damage normal, bypass_shields, enveloping normal How the warhead's damage lands. decoys number 2 parallax: decoys released at launch. cluster {missile, count, at} count 6, at 600 m cluster: the submunition missile id, how many, and how close to the target it splits. trigger_range distance 800 m cloaked_wait: it wakes when a hostile comes this close.

docs.title: ships and objects
docs.text:
The same keys; objects defaults to kind: station.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. description text empty One line for the launcher and viewer. kind fighter, freighter, capital, drone, station, probe, mine, debris, ground fighter / station What sort of object it is. station, mine and ground never move; a ground installation is set down on the terrain wherever it is placed (Environments and terrain). faction id neutral Owning faction; must exist. model_set id — The look: a model set. Either model_set or model is required. model asset — Shorthand for a model set of its own: models/x.obj or original:MESH. model_scale number 1 Model units to metres. playable bool false The player may fly it (offered in the launcher). cockpit id none Cockpit for the player's view; without one, glass instruments. voice id none The radio voice set its pilot speaks with (app 0.6.2). An unknown set is an error; without one the pilot is silent. hit_points number 100 Hull points. A class inheriting an original station's hit-point chart (HP1 – HP4, no HitPoints) gets the four summed (app 0.15.0, derived). armor number 0 Armour points, absorbed after shields. shields number 0 Shield points per facing (fore and aft). fitted {shield, armor} none The equipment the class carries by default (app 0.15.0): each a reference to a definition with a protection value — an original: section such as original:GameSettings.ini/ShieldType1, read by its Special key (shields) or HitPoints key (armour). Its protection fills shields / armor unless the class has them already — set by itself or by what it inherits. A key other than shield or armor, or a reference with no protection value, is a load error. A campaign craft's own fit replaces both in battle (Strategy layer › items). shield_recharge number 5 Shield points per second per facing at full charge. max_speed number 400 Top speed, m/s (0 for static kinds). acceleration number 150 m/s². roll_rate, pitch_rate, yaw_rate number 120, 70, 70 Degrees per second (pitch and yaw at rest). angular_damp number 3 0 tight … 10 loose. lock_speed number 1000 Speed at which pitch and yaw rates fall to zero, m/s. vct bool false Fitted with vector control thrusters (adds the vct system). atmosphere_max_speed number 60 % of max_speed Top speed in air of density 1, m/s: full thrust balances drag here (atmospheric flight). lift number 120 for fighter, else 0 The forward speed, m/s, at which the wings carry the craft's weight; 0 = no wings. hover bool false Hovers in an atmosphere: gravity does not pull it down (saucers). atmospheric bool true Can enter an atmosphere. false: the Simulator refuses the craft in an environment with physics: atmosphere ("The … cannot enter an atmosphere", app 0.6.3); Stage 4 will also hide it from surface missions. energy number 500 Beam capacitor. energy_recharge number 40 Capacitor recharge per second at full beam charge. beams ids none One beam id per mount: [laser, laser]. missiles mapping id: number none Racks: {xwinder: 5, sidestep: 4}. systems ids by kind Fitted systems, replacing the default list; usually edit it instead: systems+: [ecm], systems-: [vct]. repair_rate number damage.repair_rate Hit points per second the crew repairs. capturable bool true for fighter, drone, probe, debris Can be captured with a tractor beam when disabled. towable bool false Can be towed away even when not disabled — a cargo container; a mounted one is torn off its hub by the tractor (app 0.9.2, Stations and modules). cargo bool false A cargo container, counted by the mission query cargo(role) and the mission key cargo: (app 0.9.2). behaviour id none (armed AI ships fly builtin_attack) AI behaviour (Behaviours). turret_arc angle 0 Beams can aim this far off the nose (turrets). debris list of assets none Shorthand (with model): wreckage models. With a model set, its debris set is used instead. modules list of {slot, class} none Stations (and, since app 0.9.2, any ship — they move and jump out with it): modules mounted at the model's attachment points — slot is an OBJ slot_<name> group's name or an original mesh's attachment index (quoted: '0') (Stations and modules). shield_generator bool false Modules: while one survives, its station's shields work. point_defence {range, rate, chance, energy} none Guns that shoot down hostile missiles (and decoys): range (distance, default 800 m), rate (shots per second, default 3), chance (fraction a shot destroys the missile, default 35 %), energy (per shot, default 4). probe {sensors, jamming} none Probes: sensors (distance) — its side's radar sees every contact this close to the probe; jamming (distance) — hostile ships this close have half radar range and lock missiles at half speed. engine_color RGB 0.5, 0.7, 1.0 Engine glow colour.

docs.title: systems
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning kind engines, manoeuvring, sensors, shields, hyperdrive, vct, tractor, cloak, ecm, damage_control the id The built-in effect. Required when the id is not a kind name. name text built-in name Display name. hit_points number per kind Damage before it stops working. power number per kind Power steps while switched on. range distance per kind Tractor hold range, ECM radius, cloak detection range. strength number per kind Tractor pull m/s²; ECM and cloak: chance per second, in %, that a homing missile loses its target. repair_rate number per kind (4 for damage control) Damage control: repair speed multiplier.

Built-in values per kind: Rulesets.

docs.title: cockpits
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning image asset or none — 2D cockpit art, stretched over the design space. design 2 numbers 640, 480 Width and height of the instrument coordinate space. model asset none 3D cockpit model around the pilot's eye. model_offset 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres from the eye: x right, y up, −z ahead. model_scale number 1 Model units to metres. instruments mapping name: [x, y, w, h] — Instrument rectangles in the design space. Names: message, radar_front, radar_rear, mfd, gauge1–gauge4, power, systems, status, and since app 0.15.1 ship_status (the craft from above with its shield bands, Cockpits › The ship status display). anchors mapping name: {at, normal, size} none 3D cockpits: instruments drawn in perspective on the model's surface (below). wide {blackout, color, from, left, right} none Wide screens: the bands left and right of narrower 2D cockpit art. blackout: true fills them with color (default black), hiding the 3D view there; from (design-space y, default 0) starts them lower, e.g. at the dashboard's top so space still shows beside the canopy; left/right are your own images stretched over each band (R-HUD-013).

An anchor:

Key Type Meaning at 3 numbers Centre of the instrument on the cockpit model, metres. normal 3 numbers The surface's outward normal. size 2 numbers Width and height on the surface, metres.

A cockpit needs an image, a model, or both. Guide: Cockpits.

docs.title: behaviours
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning start id the first state The first state. states mapping state name: state required (at least one) Manoeuvre and parameters (below). systems {cloak, ecm, shields_first, beams_first} none When the pilot uses its ship's systems: each a condition, checked with the transitions. cloak / ecm on while it holds, off otherwise (if fitted); shields_first moves power to shields one step at a time while it holds; else beams_first moves it to beams. prefer mapping selector: weight none Target preferences: a hostile matching a selector counts as if weight times nearer when the AI picks a new target (several matches multiply). Selectors: player, a ship kind (fighter, freighter, station, …), class:<id>, faction:<id>; weights above 0. transitions list of {from, to, when} none Tried in order; the first whose from matches and whose condition holds wins. from is a state name or "*" (any, the default); when is a condition. skill {aim, reaction} aim 0.5, reaction 0.7 s aim: fraction, 0 wild … 1 perfect; reaction: time between looks at the target.

A state:

Key Type Default Meaning do idle, circle, patrol, attack, evade, retreat, turret, tow, escort, travel, mine required The manoeuvre (Manoeuvres; escort and travel app 0.9.2). range distance 2000 m Attack: open fire inside it (and inside 95 % of the first beam's reach); patrol: radius around the spawn point; turret: reach; tow: search radius (at least 5 km); escort: how close a hostile may come to the leader or the escort before it attacks; travel: how far to fly before jumping; mine: trigger distance. fire_cone angle 5° Fire when the aim point is within this angle of the nose. burst time 1.5 s Seconds of firing. pause time 1 s Seconds holding fire between bursts. duration time 3 s Evade: how long. speed fraction 100 % Fraction of top speed. missiles time 10 s Seconds between missile launches (0 = none). jump bool false Retreat: start the hyperdrive. escape distance 2.5 km Tow: haul the prize this far from where it was taken before jumping out (app 0.9.2).

docs.title: modelsets
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning intact asset required The normal model (all its LODs). scale number 1 Model units to metres. textures mapping texture name: asset none Swaps always applied. damage list of {below, textures} none Damage levels: while the hull is below below (a fraction), its swaps apply; cumulative, the worst level wins. states mapping state: {model, debris, textures} none Named conditions: construction stages (build_25 …), destroyed (a mounted module's wreck). model replaces the intact mesh in that state; debris is the debris set used when destroyed in that state; textures swaps. debris id none Debris set thrown when destroyed. destroyed_effect id explosion Effect of its explosion.

Texture names match a model's textures by file name without folder or extension, case-insensitively. Guide: Looks.

docs.title: debris
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning pieces list of assets none Piece models, in the object's own model space. pick [min, max] all pieces How many pieces are thrown, chosen at random. speed [min, max] 20, 60 Outward speed, m/s. spin [min, max] 30, 120 Tumble, degrees per second. life time 15 s How long the pieces last. chunks {models, count, speed} none Generic rubble: models, how many, [min, max] m/s (default 40, 120).

docs.title: effects
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning size number 2.5 Fireball size: × the object's radius (a missile's explosion: metres). duration time 1.6 s How long it lasts. color RGB 1, 0.6, 0.25 Fireball colour. shockwave bool false An expanding ring of light. sound text none Played with the effect: an event name from sounds: (big_explosion) or an asset. Without one, destructions play the explosion / big_explosion event sounds and missile blasts explosion.

docs.title: flight
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning model newtonian / assisted newtonian Flight model (Simulation). arena_radius distance 60 km Ships are halted at this distance from the centre (0 = none). boost number 150 Afterburner speed bonus, m/s. cost number 50 Afterburner energy per second. lock_angle angle 10° Missile lock cone half-angle. radar_range distance 6000 m Mobile contacts beyond it are hidden from the radar. hyperspace_time time 10 s Hyperdrive countdown (doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged). bolt_frame world / ship world How a beam shot moves once fired. world is physics: it leaves with the ship's velocity plus the muzzle's turn velocity plus its muzzle speed, then flies straight. ship (arcade): for bolt_carry it moves in the ship's frame, turning with the nose, then flies straight (Simulation). bolt_carry time 0.3 s With bolt_frame: ship, how long a shot stays in the ship's frame. lighting map see below How ships are lit: ambient (light everywhere, 0.30), sun (extra light on faces towards the sun, 0.85), rim (extra light on edges seen side-on, outlining hulls against space, 0), distant_dot (pixels: a ship on the player's radar smaller than this on screen is drawn as a dot in its radar colour, 4; 0 = off). Keys left out keep their defaults (Rendering). collision map see below How collisions feel: restitution (bounciness, 0 = the ships stop together … 1 = a perfect bounce; 0.5), spin (how strongly the angle of impact spins a ship; 1), tumble (time: the longest a hard hit leaves the pilot with reduced control; 2.5 s). Ships pressed together make one impact (sound and damage), not one per tick (R-FLT-009). formation id vee The formation wingmen fly in when their mission role names none (formations, app 0.6.6). debrief_delay time 30 s After a mission's result the verdict shows and the computer voice speaks at once; the battle runs on this long before the debrief, with a countdown (Enter shows it now; a retreat shows it at once). 0s = at once (app 0.7.4). formation_gap number 3 A wingman's formation slot is at least this many × the two ships' combined radii from its leader; tighter slots in scenarios and missions are pushed out (R-CMB-022). radar_colors map see below Radar blip and target-marker colours by relation to the player: friendly (own faction, default green), hostile (either side hostile, red), neutral (yellow), objective (objects with protect: true, cyan). Each is [r, g, b], 0..1.

docs.title: formations
docs.text:
Named shapes for groups of craft (MD1, app 0.6.6): wingmen in battle now, cutscene formations later. A definition section: formations: {<id>: {…}}. Both campaigns ship vee, line_abreast, echelon, box and diamond in rules/formations.yaml.

Key Type Default Meaning shape vee / line_abreast / echelon / box / diamond — A built-in shape that gives a slot for any number of followers: vee alternates left and right, each pair one rank further back; line_abreast alternates left and right level with the leader; echelon is a diagonal back and to the right; box is rows of two behind the leader (the leader is the front-left corner); diamond is left, right, then behind (more trail behind). slots list of [x, y, z] — A custom shape instead of shape (not both): slots in the leader's frame, +x right, +y up, +z behind, in units of spacing. Followers beyond the list continue as a vee behind the deepest slot. spacing distance 60 m Metres per slot unit: one number opens or closes the whole formation.

A mission role of wingmen picks one with formation: <id>; otherwise flight.formation applies. Slots are still pushed out to flight.formation_gap × the combined radii. A campaign with no formations uses a built-in 60 m vee. In flight, Shift+O (Wingmen: next formation) moves your wingmen into the next formation of the list. Errors: formations.x: give shape or slots, not both; shape: 'y' is not vee, line_abreast, echelon, box or diamond; missions.m.roles.r: unknown formation 'y' (and flight.formation: …).

formations:
  vee: {shape: vee, spacing: 60m}
  staggered: {slots: [[-1, 0, 1], [1, 0, 2], [-1, 0, 3]], spacing: 50m}

docs.title: power
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning beam_recharge list of numbers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 Per level A, B, …: fraction of the ship's energy_recharge. 1 to 26 levels. shield_recharge list of numbers 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1 Per level: fraction of the ship's shield_recharge. As many levels as beam_recharge. budget number 6 Power steps shared by both settings (level index, A = 0) and switched-on systems. start_beam number 3 Starting beam level (0 = A). start_shield number 3 Starting shield level. balance_shift fraction 50 % With shields balanced forward the fore shield holds 1 + shift times its normal capacity and the aft 1 − shift.

docs.title: damage
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning system_share fraction 100 % Share of the damage past the armour that also strikes one system. destroy_below fraction 50 % A system this far below zero hit points is destroyed for the battle. repair_rate number 2 Default crew repair rate, hit points per second.

docs.title: sounds
docs.text: <event>: <asset> for the events the engine plays: explosion, big_explosion, shield_hit, hull_hit, lock, missile_launch, afterburner, target, denied, collision, system_damage, tractor, cloak, ecm, hyperspace, point_defence (a point-defence shot), and since app 0.6.2 the computer voice at the end of a mission: mission_accomplished (a win) and mission_failed (any other result), played when the debrief appears. Beam and missile sounds are set on each weapon. Any sound reference may be cue:<Name>, a cue of the audio cue table.

docs.title: voices
docs.text:
Radio voice sets (app 0.6.2; guide: Radio voices). A definition section: voices: {<set id>: {<line>: clip or [clips]}}. Ships choose one with voice: <set id>. Since app 0.13.1 two more keys, which are not lines: name (text, the speaker shown on the comms panel; default the id) and face (asset: a picture or a .smk clip, also original:<pack>.mps#<member>) (Faces on the comms panel).

Line When it is said acknowledge A wingman answers a wing order (fire at will, attack my target, ignore my target, evasive, retreat). status A wingman answers a status request. down Another wingman, when one of the player's wingmen is destroyed. engaging, kill Reserved names; not yet said by the engine. Other line names are kept and ignored.

A clip is a sound asset (sounds/x.wav, original:<file>.wav); with a list, one is picked each time. Like the sounds: section, a clip may be cue:<Name> (app 0.6.7), and --check does not load them: a clip that fails to load is reported on start-up as a sound: … line.

docs.title: audio
docs.text: Key Type Meaning cue_table asset A table of named sound cues: original:<file>/<section> — the original's soundfx.ini (original:soundfx.ini/InterceptorSounds). Each entry Name = "path\file.wav" makes cue:Name mean original:file.wav. Cue names ignore case; an unknown cue, or a missing table, is a load error.

docs.title: music
docs.text:
Interactive music sets (app 0.11.0; guide: Music). A definition section: music: {<set id>: {…}}.

Key Type Default Meaning states map of state → asset or [assets] required Segments per state, played in turn: cruise, threat, battle (battles) and strategy (the strategy screen). A missing state falls back to cruise, then to the first. stingers map of name → asset none Played once: victory (a mission won), death (any other result); good and bad are loaded but not yet played. threat_range distance 12km A hostile craft this close to the player: threat. battle_range distance 4km This close: battle. volume fraction 60% The set's level (× the player's music volume).

docs.title: skins
docs.text:
Skins for the menu and strategy screens (app 0.11.1; guide: Skins). A definition section: skins: {<skin id>: {…}}; campaign.skin chooses one.

Key Type Default Meaning colours map of role → [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] the plain look Roles background, panel, border, text, dim, accent, highlight; an unknown role is an error. panel.image asset none A nine-slice frame image for panels and title cards. panel.slice number 16 Its corner size, pixels. font asset the built-in font A TrueType font for every skinned text.

docs.title: screens
docs.text:
Screen layouts (app 0.16.0; guide: Screen layouts). A definition section: screens: {<screen id>: {…}}. Only starmap (the strategy screen) is laid out so far.

Key Type Default Meaning design 2 numbers 1280, 720 The design space the rectangles are written in. It is stretched to the window. background asset none An image stretched over the whole window behind the screen's widgets (drawn since app 0.16.2; a file that cannot be loaded is reported on standard error once and left out). widgets mapping name: [x, y, w, h] the engine's places Where each widget goes, in the design space. starmap: top, map, nav, info, panel; another name is a load error. A widget left out keeps the engine's place.

docs.title: console
docs.text:
The tablet console's look (app 0.5.0; guide: Console themes). A global section.

Key Type Default Meaning theme layer none (the page's own look) The campaign's base theme. cockpits mapping cockpit id: layer none Overrides while flying a craft with that cockpit:; ids ignore case.

A layer:

Key Type Default Meaning colors mapping name: RGB none bg (page background), panel (panel background), line (borders; pressed-button fill), ink (text), dim (labels), hot (values, highlights), warn, danger, off (not fitted). Any other name is a load error. font text the page's A CSS font list, e.g. "Futura, 'Avenir Next', sans-serif". corner number the page's Panel corner radius in pixels.

docs.title: environments
docs.text:
Battle environments by id (app 0.6.0; guide: Environments and terrain). A mission or scenario picks one with environment: <id>; without it the battle is in open space.

Key Type Default Meaning physics space, atmosphere space space: the flight model unchanged. atmosphere: drag, gravity, lift, a ground and a ceiling. arena distance flight.arena_radius Arena radius for battles here (a pocket is small). gravity number 9.8 in an atmosphere, else 0 m/s², downwards (−Y). air_density number 1 in an atmosphere, else 0 Scales drag and lift; 0 = vacuum. ceiling distance none Climbing above this height leaves the battle ("LEFT THE ATMOSPHERE"). terrain id — The terrain under the battle; required with physics: atmosphere. sky {top, horizon, fog, fog_distance, stars} none (black space) top, horizon: RGB at the zenith and the horizon (defaults [0.05, 0.08, 0.2], [0.5, 0.6, 0.75]); fog: RGB (default the horizon); fog_distance: distance at which things have faded fully into the fog (default 15 km, at least 100 m); stars: how much of the starfield shows, 0–1 (default 0). backdrop {planet: {color, size, direction}} or {nebula: {color, second_color, density, seed}} none A planet in the sky: color RGB (default [0.3, 0.5, 0.9]), size its angular size in degrees (default 30, 1–170), direction where it lies (default [0, -0.5, -1]). Or nebula clouds all around (app 0.9.1): color and second_color RGB (defaults [0.55, 0.2, 0.6], [0.2, 0.35, 0.75]), density 0..1 (default 0.8; also dims the stars), seed (default 1) (Environments).

docs.title: terrains
docs.text:
Terrains (heightfields) by id (app 0.6.0; guide: Environments and terrain).

Key Type Default Meaning generate {kind, seed} — Generated heights: kind hills (default) or craters; seed a number (default 1). Give generate or heightmap, not both. heightmap asset — A greyscale image (PNG or TGA): black = lowest, white = highest (the red channel). size distance 30 km Side of the square terrain, centred on the origin (at least 1 km). height 2 numbers [0, 1500] Lowest and highest ground, metres (plain numbers). colors {low, high, slope} greys RGB of low ground, high ground and steep slopes. resolution number 129 Grid points per side, 17–257 (the mesh and the height lookup).

docs.title: campaign
docs.text: Key Type Default Meaning name text — Campaign title. difficulty ids none Difficulty level ids, easiest first. default_difficulty id the middle level The level a new game starts at. skin id the first skin defined The skin of the menu and strategy screens (app 0.11.1). An unknown id is an error. intro id none A cutscene played before a new campaign's strategy screen (app 0.13.0). menu.title text the campaign's name The main menu's title (app 0.14.0). menu.subtitle text none A line under the title. menu.showcase id the first playable ship A ship class turning behind the menu. menu.starfield_seed number 7 The menu's stars. credits.lines list of text none The credits roll (app 0.14.0): one line each, "" for a gap; a line starting # is a heading (drawn in the skin's accent colour). The engine's own credits follow. credits.video asset none A credits film played instead of the roll (interceptor: original:credits_sm2a.smk). intro_video asset none A video played before a new campaign (app 0.13.0), when there is no intro; Smacker only (Cutscenes › Videos).

docs.title: missions
docs.text:
Battles defined by roles, waves, objectives and outcomes. Rules folders: rules/, campaign/ and missions/ (the convention for missions). Full reference, battle-context queries and actions: Missions.

Key Type Default Meaning name, briefing text the id, empty Launcher title and briefing (@keys). order number 100 Launcher sort key. starfield_seed number 1 Star field and the mission's random choices. sun 3 numbers — Direction towards the sun. player {class, position} choose, origin The player's craft and start. roles mapping name: {class, count, faction, ai, behaviour, protect, state, hull, destroyed_systems, speed, formation, escort, at, arrive} — Groups of craft. class: an id or a list (random per member); count: n or [min, max]; at: {distance, bearing, from, spread}; arrive: a condition. waves list of {role, when, count, at, every} none Reinforcements, each once — or, with every (a time, app 0.9.2), again that long after it last came while when holds. objectives {win, lose, draw} none Conditions; lose is checked before win. optional mapping name: condition none Latched optional objectives. timer {after, then} none Time limit and its result. outcomes mapping result: actions none Results win, lose, draw, retreat, killed (the player's craft destroyed; without its own entry it takes the lose actions). chatter list of {when, line, voice} none Radio lines; voice is a clip spoken with the line (app 0.6.2), or a cue:<Name> (app 0.6.7). debrief mapping result: text none Debrief texts, by the same results (killed shows no text unless given). environment id open space The battle environment. hazards hazards none Asteroid field, minefield, black hole, ion storm. cargo role name none The role whose cargo containers count: the debrief reports the share still aboard (app 0.9.2).

docs.title: hazards
docs.text:
In missions and scenarios (app 0.5.1; guide: Missions › Hazards). Each part is optional.

Key Type Default Meaning asteroids {class, count, radius, center, spin, faction} — An asteroid field: count (40) objects of class (required) scattered uniformly in the sphere radius (distance, 5 km) around center (3 numbers, origin), none within 300 m of a craft; each turns at a random rate up to spin (°/s, 4); faction default the class's. Shown on the radar only within range. minefield the same — A minefield: count (20) mines of class (a kind: mine class) in radius (2 km). black_hole {position, pull, radius} — Pulls craft and missiles towards position (3 numbers): pull m/s² at 1 km (15), growing with 1/d², capped at 20 × pull; a craft inside radius (distance, 400 m) is destroyed. ion_storm {sensors} — Radar range × sensors (fraction, 40 %, at least 5 %); missile locks at half speed.

The schema type either (Ty::Either) lets a key take one of two forms: count: 3 or count: [2, 4]; bearing: [10, 5] or bearing: random; class: comet or class: [a, b].

docs.title: Cutscene files (cutscenes/*.yaml)
docs.text: One cutscene per file (app 0.13.0; editor schema schemas/cutscene.schema.json). The title and the captions may be text keys (app 0.16.2). Every key — id, title, length, environment, entities, cameras, cuts, sounds, captions — with its type and default is on Cutscenes › The file.

docs.title: Text files (text/<language>/*.yaml)
docs.text:
Key Type Meaning text mapping key: text The strings by key; "@<key>" in rules and scenarios refers to them. imports list of {file, prefix} The original's language files, read from the player's CD at run time: file (original:LangFile1.txt), prefix (default orig) — every original key K becomes <prefix>.K.

Schema: schemas/text.schema.json. Guide: Text and translation.

docs.title: Scenario files (scenarios/*.yaml)
docs.text:
Key Type Default Meaning id id required Unique scenario id; used by --scenario. A later pack's scenario with the same id replaces it. title text the id Launcher title. description text empty Launcher description. order number 100 Launcher sort key (lower first; ties by title). player text choose A ship id, or choose to let the launcher pick among playable classes. player_position 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres. player_rotation 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Yaw, pitch, roll in degrees (positive yaw turns left). sun 3 numbers −0.4, 0.5, −0.8 Direction towards the sun. starfield_seed number 1 Background stars; the same seed gives the same sky. music asset none Read but not played yet (Stage 5). objects mapping name: object none Placed objects (below). nav mapping name: {position: [x, y, z]} none Navigation points (engine extension, DEV-002). environment id open space The battle environment (app 0.6.0). hazards hazards none Asteroid field, minefield, black hole, ion storm (app 0.5.1).

An object:

Key Type Default Meaning class id required Ship or object id. faction id the class's Overrides the side. position 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Metres; −z is ahead of the player's start. rotation 3 numbers 0, 0, 0 Yaw, pitch, roll in degrees. ai wingman, enemy, idle, target idle How it is flown. leader id none Wingmen: the object to follow (player = the player). offset 3 numbers −60, 0, 30 Wingmen: formation slot relative to the leader (x right, y up, +z behind). speed number 0 Starting speed, m/s (also sets the throttle). destroyed_systems ids none Systems (kinds or ids) that start destroyed; [engines, manoeuvring] starts it disabled. protect bool false An objective the player must keep alive: drawn in the objective radar colour with a ring, labelled PROTECT on the target brackets and the MFD, and never picked by "nearest enemy" (R) for the player or the player's wingmen. T can still select it. hull fraction 100 % Starting hull. behaviour id the class's Behaviour to fly instead of the class's. state id none Model-set state to show it in (a construction stage such as build_60); an object placed in a state gets no modules or point defence.

docs.title: Rulesets and layering
docs.text:
Rules are YAML files in a pack's rules/ folder (and the campaign ruleset in campaign/). Every active pack's files are merged in load order into one ruleset; this page explains the format and how files from several packs combine. Every key of every section is listed in the Mod file reference; behaviours have their own page, Behaviours and conditions.

Since mod format 2 (Stage 2), mod files are YAML; the INI files of format 1 are no longer read. The player's original GameSettings.ini is still INI: a definition reuses one of its sections with inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/<section> (below).

docs.title: The YAML subset
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/rules.schema.json
# comments start with #
ships:                          # a section: definitions by id
  comet:                        # a definition (ids: lower case a-z, 0-9, _ and -)
    name: Comet                 # plain text
    description: "Quick: and nimble"   # quote text that contains ': ' or starts with a symbol
    beams: [blaster, blaster]   # a list on one line …
    debris:                     # … or one item per line
      - models/comet_debris1.obj
      - models/comet_debris2.obj
    missiles: {seeker: 4}       # a mapping on one line
    playable: true              # true / false
flight:                         # a global section (no ids)
  model: newtonian

The reader (src/formats/yaml.rs) accepts a strict subset of YAML and rejects the rest with an error naming the line: no tabs for indentation, no anchors (&a) or aliases (*a), no tags (!!str), one document per file, no complex keys (?), and plain text may not continue over several lines (use quotes, or | / > block text). Why a subset: DEV-030.

Values with units. Distances, times, angles and fractions may carry a unit; a plain number is in the base unit.

Kind of value Units Base unit Examples distance m, km metres 2.4km, 350m, 350 time s, min, h seconds 1.5s, 2min angle deg degrees 12deg, 12 fraction % 0..1 40%, 0.4

Checked on load. Every file is validated against its schema: an unknown key (with a "did you mean" suggestion), a wrong type or a bad value is reported with file, line and key path, for example rules/ships.yaml:12: ships.comet.max_sped: unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?). --check lists every such problem; see Validating a mod.

Editor support. A first line # yaml-language-server: $schema=<path>/rules.schema.json points editors that use the YAML language server (for example VS Code's YAML extension) at the JSON Schema of the file type, which gives completion, hover documentation and live checking. The schemas are in the repository's schemas/ folder (pack.schema.json, rules.schema.json, scenario.schema.json; the built-in packs point there with a relative path); openinterceptor --write-schemas <dir> writes them anywhere, for a mod kept elsewhere. The gate fails if the committed schemas differ from the engine's.

docs.title: Sections
docs.text:
Section Defines ships Craft by id (default kind: fighter). objects Stations and other large objects by id (default kind: station, never moves). beams Beam weapons. missiles Missiles and torpedoes. factions Sides. cockpits Cockpit art and/or 3D model, design space, instrument positions and anchors. systems Damageable ship systems and special equipment (Stage 2). behaviours AI state machines (Behaviours and conditions). modelsets Looks: model, damage-level texture swaps, states, debris set, explosion (Looks). debris Debris sets: pieces, how many, speed, spin, life, rubble. effects Explosions and other effects. flight Global flight and sensor settings. power Global power-sharing rules: beam and shield charge levels, budget. damage Global rules for damage to systems and repair. sounds Event sounds (assets, or cue:<Name> from the cue table). audio The sound cue table (cue_table: original:soundfx.ini/<section>). environments Battle environments: space or atmosphere, arena, gravity, air, ceiling, terrain, sky, planet (Environments and terrain). terrains Heightfields, generated or from an image, and their colours (Environments and terrain). console The tablet console's look: colours, font, corners, per cockpit (Console themes). campaign The campaign ruleset: name and difficulty levels (usually in campaign/campaign.yaml).

Any other top-level key is an error ("unknown key").

docs.title: Layering, inherit, delete and list edits
docs.text:
1. All packs' rules files are merged in load order. A later pack's definition with the same id merges key by key into the earlier one: mappings merge recursively, other values and lists are replaced, new keys and definitions are added. Global sections merge the same way.
  2. An empty value removes a key that an earlier pack set (cockpit: with nothing after it), so the engine default applies again.
  3. inherit: <id> copies another definition of the same section first, and the definition's own keys override; inherit: ships.<id> names another section. inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/Ship_IntType1 copies a section of the player's original INI file: original keys become field names by spelling (HitPoints → hit_points, RateOfFire → rate_of_fire), except Side → faction, a beam's Range (kilometres in the original, DEV-008) → range in km, and LockAngleDegrees → lock_angle. Chains are allowed; a cycle (or a chain deeper than 16) is an error.
  4. delete: true removes a definition (a mod removing a ship it does not want).
  5. List edits: <key>+: [items] appends to the inherited or earlier list and <key>-: [items] removes items from it, so a mod need not restate the list (systems+: [ecm], beams-: [laser_cannon]). For systems the edits apply to the default list when no pack sets one.

A definition with an error is skipped and reported; everything else still loads.

# mods/lightning-variants/rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  lightning:
    max_speed: 700            # every other key keeps the interceptor pack's value
    systems+: [tractor]       # fit a tractor beam as well
  lightning_mk3:
    inherit: lightning        # a variant: the Lightning plus changes
    name: Lightning Mk III
    hit_points: 140

docs.title: Difficulty levels
docs.text:
A campaign lists its difficulty levels, easiest first, in its campaign ruleset:

# resources/default/campaign/campaign.yaml
campaign:
  name: Perils of the Void
  difficulty: [cadet, ranger, captain, space_ace]
  default_difficulty: ranger

The game is played at one level, chosen on the launcher (D, pad X), with --difficulty <id>, or remembered in settings.yaml (game: {difficulty: …}); without a choice it is default_difficulty, else the middle level. Two things vary by level:

  • Per-level values: any number may be written {per_level: [80, 100, 120, 150]} — one entry per level, in order; a shorter list repeats its last entry.
  • Variants: a definition's variants: mapping gives, per level id, only the keys that differ at that level; they are merged over the definition when that level is played.
behaviours:
  saucer_scout:
    states:
      engage: {do: attack, burst: {per_level: [0.6s, 0.8s, 1s, 1.2s]}}
    skill: {aim: 0.4, reaction: 0.9s}
    variants:
      cadet: {skill: {aim: 0.2, reaction: 1.4s}}

Conditions can also test the level: difficulty >= captain (Behaviours). The levels of the two campaigns:

Campaign Levels (default bold) Source interceptor beginner, experienced, veteran, genius, superhuman the original's five levels (GameSettings.ini has a section per level; verified). What each level changes in the original beyond those sections is unknown. default cadet, ranger, captain, space_ace this project

An unknown level in variants, --difficulty or settings.yaml is reported (the middle level is then used). Both campaigns give their enemies behaviours with skill and fire discipline per level (rules/behaviours.yaml); the interceptor values are derived from the strategy guide's descriptions of each class and tuned in the testbed, since the original's AI is hard-coded.

docs.title: Ship systems and equipment
docs.text:
Every ship carries a list of systems. Each one has hit points and can be damaged; the switchable ones (tractor, cloak, ECM) draw power while on. What a system does is fixed by its kind (engine code); everything a modder tunes is data, so a mod can define any number of systems of one kind (ecm, advanced_ecm) with different numbers. Keys: reference.

Kind Effect Built-in hit_points / power / range / strength engines Thrust and afterburner scale with its efficiency. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 manoeuvring (or maneuvering) Turn rates scale with its efficiency. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 sensors Target lock builds at its efficiency's speed. 60 / 0 / 0 / 0 shields Shield recharge and the fore/aft transfer scale with it. 50 / 0 / 0 / 0 hyperdrive Leaving the battle (H); a damaged drive takes twice as long. 100 / 0 / 0 / 0 vct Vector-control slides. 150 / 0 / 0 / 0 tractor Holds and drags the target; beams cannot fire while it is on. 250 / 2 / 250 m / 60 cloak Hidden from enemy sensors beyond range; firing drops it. 100 / 3 / 400 m / 25 ecm Incoming missiles within range may lose their lock; halves enemy lock speed. 100 / 1 / 250 m / 10 damage_control Multiplies repair speed by repair_rate (default 4). 150 / 0 / 0 / 0

A kind that no pack defines under systems: uses its built-in definition. Built-in hit points follow the original equipment table (verified: EngineType1 100, SensorTargetingSystem1 60, ShieldType1 50, VectorControlThrusters 150, TractorBeam 250, ShipDamageControlComputer 150); ranges, strengths and power steps are engine estimates (derived; the ECM values echo ECMPodType1).

Without a systems key a class gets what any craft of its kind obviously contains: engines and manoeuvring (unless it is a static kind), sensors, shields (if shields > 0), and hyperdrive for fighters, freighters and capital ships. Special equipment is added with a list edit; vct: true (the Stage 1 key) still fits vector-control thrusters:

ships:
  meteor:
    systems+: [ecm, damage_control, tractor]
systems:
  advanced_ecm:                 # a second ECM with longer reach
    kind: ecm
    name: Advanced ECM pod
    range: 500m
    strength: 25

docs.title: How systems behave in flight
docs.text:
Condition When Efficiency OK above half its hit points 1 Damaged half its hit points or less 0.5 Inoperative hit points reached 0 — stays off until repaired back to 25 % 0 Destroyed hit points below −destroy_below × hit_points; for the rest of the battle 0
  • Damage that gets past the shields and armour also strikes one working system at random (times damage.system_share). A knocked-out switchable system switches off; a knocked-out hyperdrive aborts a countdown.
  • The crew repairs one system at a time, worst first, at the class's repair_rate; a working damage control computer multiplies it (by less when it is itself damaged).
  • A ship whose engines and manoeuvring are both out is disabled: it drifts, and if its class is capturable it can be towed away as a prize.

docs.title: Power and damage rules
docs.text:
Each ship has a beam charge and a shield charge setting, both chosen from the same list of levels (the original's A–E). The two settings plus every switched-on system may not use more than budget steps together: raising one setting can force the other down, and switching on a cloak needs free steps. Damage to systems and repair follow the damage section. Keys: reference.

power:
  beam_recharge: [0, 0.32, 0.45, 0.68, 1]    # fraction of the ship's energy_recharge per level
  shield_recharge: [0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1]
  budget: 6
  start_beam: 3                               # D
  start_shield: 2                             # C
  balance_shift: 50%
damage:
  system_share: 100%
  destroy_below: 50%
  repair_rate: 2

The interceptor campaign restates the original BeamRechargeRate (0, 7, 10, 15, 22) and ShieldRechargeRate (0, 1, 2, 3, 5) tables as fractions of their top level (verified from GameSettings.ini); its budget, start levels and system power steps are engine values (derived — the original data does not say how many levels may be high at once, see DEV-024).

docs.title: Example: a small balance addon
docs.text:
# mods/faster-lightning/pack.yaml
id: faster-lightning
kind: addon
targets: [interceptor]
requires_original: true
format: 2

# mods/faster-lightning/rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  lightning:
    max_speed: 700          # every other key keeps the interceptor pack's value

docs.title: Sounds and the cue table
docs.text:
sounds: maps the engine's event names to sounds; beams and missiles name their own sound. Any of these may be an asset (sounds/blaster.wav, original:Xwinder.wav) or a cue, cue:<Name>, looked up in a cue table — the original game's soundfx.ini, which names every sound effect:

audio:
  cue_table: original:soundfx.ini/InterceptorSounds
sounds:
  explosion: cue:SmallExplode
  hyperspace: cue:WarpOut
beams:
  laser_cannon: {sound: cue:Beam1}
