Each table entry's file name becomes an original: reference (sounds are found on the CD by name). Cue names ignore case; an unknown cue or a missing table is a load error naming the key. The interceptor pack uses the original's cue names throughout (Stage 2 item 2.12); a mod can replace any cue's sound by a file at its override path (Overrides).

docs.title: Scenarios and missions
docs.text: A scenario is a playable arena in a pack's scenarios/*.yaml. The testbed's live test environments are scenarios; Stage 3 missions extend the same format with objectives and scripts. A later pack's scenario with the same id replaces the earlier one. Every key, with type and default: Mod file reference › scenario files (from src/content/files.rs, read by src/content/scenario.rs).

docs.title: Top level
docs.text: Key Meaning id Unique id (required); used by --scenario. title, description, order Launcher title, text and sort key (lower first). player A ship class id, or choose (default) to let the launcher pick among playable classes. player_position, player_rotation Metres; yaw, pitch, roll in degrees (positive yaw turns left). sun Direction towards the sun. starfield_seed The same seed always gives the same sky. music Read but not played yet (Stage 5). objects Placed objects by name (below). nav Navigation points by name: {position: [x, y, z]} (an engine extension, DEV-002). N cycles them; the selected one shows on the MFD Nav page and as a blue diamond on screen. environment The battle environment by id (orbit, moon_surface, …); default open space. See Environments and terrain. hazards Asteroid field, minefield, black hole and ion storm, as in missions: Missions › Hazards.

docs.title: Objects
docs.text: Key Meaning class Ship or object class id (required). faction Override the side. position, rotation Metres (the player starts facing −Z, so negative Z is "ahead"); yaw, pitch, roll in degrees. ai wingman (formation on leader), enemy (flies its behaviour), target (slow circles, never fires), idle (default, does nothing). The player is set with player:, not on an object. leader Another object's name, or player. offset Formation slot relative to the leader, in the leader's frame (x right, y up, +z behind); default [-60, 0, 30]. speed Initial speed, m/s (also sets the throttle). destroyed_systems System kinds or ids that start destroyed. [engines, manoeuvring] starts the ship disabled — a capture target. protect true marks an objective to protect: shown in the objective colour with a radar ring and a PROTECT label, and skipped by nearest-enemy targeting. Use it on a capture target so it is not shot by accident. hull Starting hull fraction (40% or 0.4). behaviour A behaviour id to fly instead of the class's (Behaviours) — an ambush, a guard that only patrols. state Show the object in a model-set state, e.g. a construction stage (state: build_60); such an object has no modules or point defence (Looks).

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Using the default campaign's classes:

# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/scenario.schema.json
id: ambush
title: Ambush at the station
player: comet
starfield_seed: 4
objects:
  station:
    class: guard_station
    position: [0, 0, -2000]
  wing: {class: comet, ai: wingman, leader: player, offset: [50, 0, 30]}
  s1:
    class: scout_saucer
    ai: enemy
    position: [600, 200, -4000]
    speed: 300
  patrol:                       # a saucer that only circles until you come close
    class: scout_saucer
    ai: enemy
    behaviour: lurker           # defined in this mod's rules/behaviours.yaml
    position: [-800, 0, -3000]
  wreck:                        # a crippled saucer to tow home with the tractor ray
    class: raider_saucer
    position: [0, 0, -900]
    destroyed_systems: [engines, manoeuvring]
    hull: 50%
nav:
  station: {position: [0, 0, -2000]}

# rules/behaviours.yaml of the same mod
behaviours:
  lurker:
    start: wait
    states:
      wait: {do: patrol, range: 400m, speed: 30%}
      strike: {do: attack, range: 1.5km}
    transitions:
      - {from: wait, to: strike, when: "threats(2km) > 0 or hit_recently(1s)"}

--check spawns every scenario (with every playable ship when player: choose) and reports unknown classes, factions, leaders or behaviours.

docs.title: Screen layouts
docs.text:
A screen layout says where a screen's parts go. The engine owns what each screen does and what its parts are — the widgets — and gives each a default place; a pack moves the widgets it wants, one at a time (app 0.16.0, plan item 6.1). It is the companion of a skin: the skin decides how things look, the layout where they are.

Requirement: R-CPN-011. Every key with its type: Mod file reference › screens. How the screen reads it: Architecture › Presentation › Widgets and screen layouts.

So far one screen is laid out: the strategy screen, starmap.

docs.title: The strategy screen's widgets
docs.text:
Widget What it holds top The top bar: date, funds and score; the base switcher; pause and the four speeds; Save; Menu. map The star map, with the hover label and the legend along its bottom edge. nav The ten buttons that choose the list (two rows of five). info The selection on the map: its name, its details and up to four action buttons. panel The chosen list: its title, the rows, the selected row in full and its action buttons.

The engine's own layout, in a 1280 × 720 design space:

screens:
  starmap:
    design: [1280, 720]
    widgets:
      top: [0, 0, 1280, 44]        # x, y, width, height
      map: [8, 52, 790, 660]
      nav: [806, 52, 466, 72]
      info: [806, 132, 466, 212]
      panel: [806, 352, 466, 360]

docs.title: Moving a widget
docs.text:
Put a screens section in any rules file of your pack (for example rules/screens.yaml). Name only what you move; the rest keep the engine's places:

# rules/screens.yaml — the map on the right, the lists on the left
screens:
  starmap:
    widgets:
      map: [482, 52, 790, 660]
      nav: [8, 52, 466, 72]
      info: [8, 132, 466, 212]
      panel: [8, 352, 466, 360]

A later pack changes a layout the same way, so an addon can move one panel of a campaign's screen without restating the others.

docs.title: The design space and the window
docs.text:
The rectangles are written in the layout's design space. Unlike a cockpit, which keeps its proportions and is centred, a screen fills the window: the design space is stretched to the window's width and height separately, so a rectangle at the right edge stays at the right edge on any window shape. Text and button heights scale by the smaller of the two stretches (never below half size), so they stay legible on a small window.

Write a new design when you lay a screen out from scratch at another size:

screens:
  starmap:
    design: [1920, 1080]
    widgets:
      top: [0, 0, 1920, 60]
      map: [12, 72, 1200, 996]
      nav: [1224, 72, 684, 96]
      info: [1224, 180, 684, 320]
      panel: [1224, 512, 684, 556]

When you change design, give every widget a rectangle in the new space: one left out keeps the engine's 1280 × 720 numbers, which are then read in your space.

Keep the info and panel widgets at least about 300 × 200 design units: they leave room for a nine-slice frame's corners, the title, a few lines and a row of buttons.

docs.title: Background
docs.text: background: images/ui/starmap_frame.png names an image drawn over the whole window, stretched to fit, behind every widget (app 0.16.2; in 0.16.0 it was read but not drawn). It is loaded the first time the screen draws; an image that cannot be loaded is reported once on standard error (screens.starmap.background <file>: …) and the screen falls back to the skin's background colour. Leave room in the picture where the map and panels sit, since they draw over it.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
• Layouts for the other screens: the main menu, the launcher, the credits and the prompts are placed in code.
  • Other screen ids: screens.<id> with another id is read and checked, but no screen uses it yet.
  • Custom panels bound to campaign queries, and new widgets: a layout can move the engine's widgets, not add its own.
  • The interceptor wrapper screens at 640 × 480 from the original art (6.7).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Message Cause screens.starmap: widgets.x: not one of top, map, nav, info, panel A widget the screen does not have. screens.starmap: widgets.x: expected [x, y, w, h] A rectangle without four numbers. screens.starmap: design: expected [width, height] design is not two positive numbers.

Each message is prefixed by the file it came from; --check reports them without a window.

docs.title: Scripting (design)
docs.text:
Behaviour and logic are designed in Behaviours and scripting:

  • Tier 1 (Stages 2–3): behaviours as state machines, missions and events as definitions, and a small built-in condition and action language — enough for both shipped campaigns. Implemented in Stage 2: behaviours and the condition language in the object context — see Behaviours and conditions. Actions, and the mission and event contexts, come with Stage 3.
  • Tier 2 (Stage 3.10, awaiting the user's decision): optional scripts called through hooks. The evaluation compares Lua 5.4 via mlua, rhai, and growing the condition and action language into a small statement language (variables, if/else, bounded loops, functions); it recommends the last as the default, with Lua as the fallback. Until the decision, write Tier 1.

docs.title: Skins
docs.text:
A skin is the look of the menu and strategy screens: seven named colours, an optional nine-slice panel frame and an optional TrueType font (app 0.11.1, plan item 6.1). Skins are rules data, and a campaign chooses its own with campaign.skin, so the default campaign's art-deco screens and the X-COM green-on-steel are the same screens in two skins.

Requirement: R-CPN-011. Every key with its type: Mod file reference › skins. How the screens draw through it: Architecture › Presentation › Skins.

docs.title: What is skinned
docs.text:
Screen Skinned parts Main menu (app 0.14.0) Title, subtitle, the item list in a panel, the selection bar; the credits roll's headings. Launcher Background, title and every line of text, the selection bar, hints. Strategy screen Background, the top bar, the map frame, the info panel and the list panel (nine-slice panels), buttons, rows and the selection bar, the legend and hover label, the modal prompts and title cards.

Since app 0.16.0 the strategy screen's buttons, lists, info panel and prompts are drawn in the skin too: prompts and panels use the nine-slice frame; buttons are filled with the panel colour (highlight under the mouse) and outlined in border; the selected row is highlight, the current list and clock speed are outlined in accent. Where the strategy screen's parts go is a separate section, the screen layout (Screen layouts).

Not skinned yet: the cockpit and HUD (cockpits have their own art), the viewer, the asset browser, the controls menu and the simulator setup. Custom panels bound to queries are not built (below).

docs.title: The colours
docs.text:
Each colour is [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a], every number 0 to 1. A colour left out keeps the plain look's value.

Role Used for background The screen behind everything. panel A panel's fill when the skin has no panel image; inactive tabs. border A panel's outline when the skin has no panel image; a title card's title. text Ordinary text. dim Secondary text: hints, inactive tabs, rows that cannot be acted on. accent Reserved for highlights a screen wants to draw attention to. highlight The bar behind the selected row; the active tab.

docs.title: The nine-slice panel
docs.text:
panel: {image, slice} names an image and a corner size in pixels. The image is cut slice pixels in from each edge into nine pieces: the corners are drawn at their own size, the edges stretch along one direction and the centre stretches both ways — so a frame with ornate corners fits any rectangle without distorting them. A rectangle smaller than two corners shrinks the corners to fit.

 ┌────┬────────────┬────┐
 │ TL │   top →    │ TR │   corners: drawn as they are
 ├────┼────────────┼────┤
 │ ↕  │  centre ↔↕ │ ↕  │   edges: stretched along their length
 ├────┼────────────┼────┤
 │ BL │  bottom →  │ BR │   centre: stretched both ways
 └────┴────────────┴────┘

Draw the corners so that they still read when the edges stretch: ornaments in the corner squares, plain bands along the edges. The image is drawn as it is (its centre included), so paint the centre in the colour the panel should have.

docs.title: A worked example: the default campaign's art-deco skin
docs.text:
# resources/default/rules/skin.yaml
skins:
  deco:
    colours:
      background: [0.03, 0.03, 0.08]
      panel: [0.07, 0.08, 0.17, 0.95]
      border: [0.86, 0.70, 0.34]
      text: [0.96, 0.91, 0.78]
      dim: [0.62, 0.58, 0.48]
      accent: [0.85, 0.20, 0.15]
      highlight: [0.32, 0.22, 0.10]
    panel: {image: textures/deco_panel.png, slice: 24}

# resources/default/campaign/campaign.yaml
campaign:
  name: Perils of the Void
  skin: deco
  # …

textures/deco_panel.png (96 × 96, 24-pixel corners: a navy field, a gold frame with a pinstripe, stepped corner ornaments with a red jewel) is painted by tools/default_assets/textures.py (deco_panel()), like every default texture.

The interceptor campaign's skin, xcom in packs/interceptor/rules/skin.yaml, is colours only — the original's steel-grey and green palette. The original's wrapper art (its screens at 640 × 480, in WrappersDLL.dll) is plan item 6.7; the layouts of those screens have not been mapped yet.

docs.title: Choosing the skin
docs.text:
• campaign.skin: <id> picks the campaign's skin; an unknown id is a load error (campaign.skin: unknown skin 'x').
  • Without it, the first skin defined in load order is used; with no skins at all the screens keep the plain look (dark blue, pale green-grey text).
  • An addon can re-skin a campaign by redefining its skin id (skins: {deco: {inherit: …}}, or the whole entry), or by adding a skin and setting campaign.skin.
  • The skin is loaded when the game starts and again when the launcher switches campaign (Tab).

docs.title: The main menu and credits
docs.text:
Since app 0.14.0 a campaign with a strategy layer opens on a main menu drawn in its skin (the item list sits in a skin panel), and its Credits item rolls the campaign's credit lines. Both are set under campaign::

# resources/default/campaign/campaign.yaml
campaign:
  menu: {subtitle: "A serial of the space frontier, in twelve chapters", showcase: comet, starfield_seed: 31}
  credits:
    lines:
      - "# Perils of the Void"
      - the default campaign of OpenInterceptor
      - ""
      - "# Music"
      - synthesised by tools/default_assets/music.py
  • menu: title (default: the campaign's name), subtitle, showcase (a ship class turning behind the menu; default the first playable ship) and starfield_seed.
  • credits: lines — a line starting # is a heading in the skin's accent colour, "" leaves a gap — rolled up over the stars, followed by the engine's own credits; or video, a film played instead (interceptor uses the CD's credits film).
  • The menu plays the first music set's menu state, or its strategy state (Music).

Every key: Mod file reference › campaign. Try the roll with openinterceptor --no-original --credits.

docs.title: Fonts
docs.text:
font: fonts/<name>.ttf loads a TrueType font from the pack for every skinned text. Choose a font whose licence allows redistribution with your pack. A font or panel image that fails to load is reported on standard error (skin <id>: font: …, skin <id>: panel: …) and left out: the screens still draw, with colours and the built-in font.

The strategy screen clips each list row to its width by measuring it in the skin's font (app 0.16.0) and shows the selected row in full beneath the list, so a wide font costs only room.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text:
• Custom panels bound to queries, buttons with hover images, skin sounds, several fonts per skin. Screen layouts are built for the strategy screen only (Screen layouts).
  • Main menu option values too long for their room are drawn smaller (down to half size, app 0.14.2), not wrapped.
  • A full graphics options page (the menu has Full screen since app 0.16.14; brightness is in settings.yaml). The load page and the ending screen (app 0.16.14) are placed in code, in the skin.
  • The interceptor wrapper screens at 640 × 480 (6.7).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Message Cause skins.x: colours.y: not one of background, panel, border, text, dim, accent, highlight An unknown colour role. skins.x: colours.y: expected [r, g, b] or [r, g, b, a] A colour with the wrong number of values. campaign.skin: unknown skin 'x' campaign.skin names no defined skin.

docs.title: Stations and modules
docs.text:
A station can carry modules — turrets, shield generators, hangars, pods — each a separate object with its own hit points, weapons and behaviour, mounted at an attachment point of the station's model. Modules can be shot off one by one; destroying a station destroys its modules with it. Implemented in Stage 2 (item 2.11; src/sim/mod.rs, src/formats/obj.rs).

objects:
  dominion_outpost:
    model_set: dominion_outpost
    hit_points: 6000
    shields: 1200
    modules:
      - {slot: pod1, class: dominion_turret_pod}      # OBJ group slot_pod1
      - {slot: pod2, class: dominion_turret_pod}
      - {slot: shield1, class: dominion_shield_pod}
  dominion_turret_pod:
    name: Death-ray pod
    model_set: dominion_turret_pod
    hit_points: 280
    beams: [death_ray]
    turret_arc: 180            # its beams swivel up to 180° off its nose
    behaviour: station_turret  # a behaviour with do: turret
  dominion_shield_pod:
    name: Shield pod
    model_set: dominion_shield_pod
    hit_points: 450
    shield_generator: true     # while one survives, the hub's shields work

docs.title: Attachment points
docs.text:
Model Attachment points slot: written as Mod model (OBJ) Every group or object named slot_<name> (g slot_turret1). Its faces are not drawn; the slot sits at the centre of its faces and faces along its first face's normal (counter-clockwise winding seen from outside, as for any face). One small square per slot is enough. the name after slot_: turret1 Original mesh (XMSH) The mesh's manipulators (attachment points in its first LOD). They have no names. their index: '0', '1', … (quoted)

A module is turned so that its −Z axis (its front) follows the slot's normal, pointing out of the hull: model a module standing on its base at the origin and extending along −Z. A slot name or index that the model does not have is an error when the scenario spawns.

In the default-campaign generator (tools/default_assets/models.py) a slot is made with slot(name, at, normal): one small square face in a slot_<name> group, centred on at and wound so its normal is normal. Slots are left out of debris cutting and of the solid-model checks. The Guard station has slot_turret1–slot_turret6 and slot_shield1–slot_shield2; the Dominion outpost slot_pod1–slot_pod6 and slot_shield1. The module models (Guard ray turret, force-field generator, death-ray pod, shield pod) stand on their bases and extend along −Z, with debris pieces and scorched, burnt and wrecked textures.

docs.title: In battle
docs.text:
• Spawning. When a station is placed, each modules entry spawns its class at its slot, with the station's faction, named <station>.<n>. A module class with a behaviour fights (a turret behaviour aims its swivelling beams within turret_arc); one without sits idle. Modules may carry modules of their own (up to five levels deep).
  • Unfinished stations. A station placed with state: (a construction stage) spawns no modules and fires no point defence.
  • Following. Every tick each module is placed back on its hub's attachment point, so it moves and turns with the station.
  • Shield generators. A station with shield_generator modules keeps its shields only while at least one of them survives; when the last one goes, its shields drop to zero and stay down ("STATION SHIELDS DOWN").
  • Cascade. When the hub is destroyed, all its modules are destroyed with it (each with its own explosion and debris).
  • Wrecks. A destroyed module whose model set has a destroyed state stays on the station as a wreck drawn in that state (Looks); the wreck goes with the station.

docs.title: Cargo containers and moving hubs
docs.text:
Since app 0.9.2 a hub need not be a station: any ship class may carry modules, and they ride with it. The default campaign's cargo clipper (supply_ship) carries twelve cargo pods and a point-defence laser:

objects:
  supply_pod:
    kind: freighter
    hit_points: 400
    armor: 150
    cargo: true          # counted by the mission's cargo(role) query
    towable: true        # a tug may tow it away even when not disabled; a mounted one is torn off
    capturable: true
  supply_pd:
    beams: [blaster]
    turret_arc: 180
    behaviour: supply_pd                       # do: turret, a long pause between bursts
    point_defence: {range: 900m, rate: 0.5, chance: 60%, energy: 3}
ships:
  supply_ship:
    behaviour: supply_run                      # do: travel, 24 km, then jump
    modules:
      - {slot: pod1, class: supply_pod}
      # … pod2 – pod12
      - {slot: pd, class: supply_pd}
  • One craft. A module never collides with its own hub, nor with another module of the same hub (their hulls overlap by design; before app 0.9.2 the pods dragged on a moving clipper), and a craft's collision avoidance ignores its own modules.
  • Jumping out. When a hub leaves by hyperspace, every module still mounted goes with it.
  • towable (default false): a tug's tractor may take the object even when it is not disabled; tractoring a mounted one tears it off its hub ("CARGO CONTAINER TORN AWAY"), and the tug that jumps while holding it captures it.
  • cargo (default false): the object is a cargo container, counted by the cargo(role) query of the role whose craft carry it, and by a mission's cargo: key.

docs.title: The two campaigns
docs.text:
Campaign Station Modules default Guard station six ray turrets, two force-field generators default Dominion outpost six death-ray pods, a shield pod interceptor X-COM base (XBASE7, 33 attachment points) beam-defence turrets, shield generators, a hangar interceptor Alien base (AL-BASE01, 28 attachment points) plasma gun pods, shield pods

The interceptor modules' hit points come from the original module sections (M_XCOM*, M_ALIEN* in GameSettings.ini, verified); their meshes are the original turret and pod meshes; which attachment point holds which module is derived (the original builds bases from the strategy layer, Stage 4) — see DEV-035.

Testbed arenas: outpost-strike (default) and base-assault (interceptor) — knock out the shield modules to bring the hub's shields down, silence the guns, then destroy the hub.

docs.title: Mines
docs.text:
A kind: mine object flies the mine manoeuvre: it waits and, when a hostile comes within the state's range, detonates its first missile rack as the warhead. The blast reaches four times the warhead's proximity_radius (at least 100 m), deals the warhead's proximity_damage falling off linearly with distance, spread over both shield facings, and destroys the mine.

missiles:
  mine_warhead: {guidance: dumbfire, speed: 0, impact_damage: 0, proximity_damage: 250, proximity_radius: 40m}
objects:
  space_mine:
    kind: mine
    model_set: robot_sentinel
    hit_points: 30
    missiles: {mine_warhead: 1}
    behaviour: space_mine
behaviours:
  space_mine:
    states:
      wait: {do: mine, range: {per_level: [100m, 120m, 140m, 160m]}}

The default campaign's dominion-raid scenario lays Dominion space mines.

docs.title: Probes
docs.text:
An object with kind: probe and a probe: entry changes what the sides can see:

objects:
  sky_eye_probe:
    kind: probe
    faction: guard
    model_set: sky_eye_probe
    hit_points: 50
    probe: {sensors: 8km}       # the Guard's radar sees every contact within 8 km of it
  jammer_buoy:
    kind: probe
    faction: dominion
    model_set: jammer_buoy
    hit_points: 80
    probe: {jamming: 2.5km}     # hostile ships within 2.5 km: half radar range, half lock speed
  • Sensors. A side's radar shows every contact within any of its own probes' sensors range, however far from the ship looking.
  • Jamming. A ship within a hostile probe's jamming radius has half its radar range and locks missiles at half speed (on top of a target's ECM).
  • Cloaks still win. Since this change the radar also hides cloaked ships of other factions beyond their cloak's range — probes do not reveal them.
  • Stations and mines (objects that never move) always show on radar.

Probes are ordinary objects: they can be shot (they have hit points and a look) and placed in scenarios. The interceptor probes use the original SENSPROB and ECMPROB meshes (verified names); their battle effects and numbers are derived, because the original launches probes from the strategy map (DEV-039). The default campaign has the Guard's Sky-Eye sensor probe and the Dominion jamming buoy. Testbed arena: probe-net (both campaigns).

docs.title: Story layer
docs.text:
The story layer (app 0.10.0 – 0.10.3, plan items 5.1 – 5.9) is what turns a strategy layer into a campaign with a beginning, a middle and an end: events that fire on conditions and may offer the player a choice or a mission, arcs that put events in order, a rival's plans built from shipments the player can intercept, relations with the other factions, a strategist whose aggression answers the player, endings, and an encyclopaedia. All of it is pack data in the strategy files; a campaign without these sections plays exactly as before.

Requirements: R-CPN-007 – R-CPN-010. Design (the full planned format, of which this page is the built part): Format: campaign and game flow, Campaign events, Dynamic relations. How the engine runs it: Architecture › Campaign › The story. What the player sees: User guide › Campaign › The story.

docs.title: Where the files go
docs.text:
Like every strategy section the story sections may sit in any rules file; by convention they go in <pack>/strategy/story.yaml:

File What it holds resources/default/strategy/story.yaml The default campaign's twelve-chapter serial, side events, the Eclipse Engine plan, relations, the Dominion's strategist, four endings, five encyclopaedia entries (app 0.10.1) packs/interceptor/strategy/story.yaml The X-COM Doomsday arc, the Doomsday plan, two side missions, the alien strategist, three endings (app 0.10.2)

events, arcs, plans, endings and encyclopaedia are definition sections: they layer across packs like any other definitions, so an addon may add an event, inherit a plan or delete: true an ending (Rulesets). relations, strategist and campaign_end are global sections: the last pack to write one wins. Every id these sections define is a named constant in the campaign's conditions, so a misspelt event, arc, plan or ending id is a load error that names it.

The campaign's presentation keys sit beside the story: campaign.skin (Skins), campaign.intro and campaign.intro_video (Cutscenes), and the music sets (Music).

docs.title: A worked example
docs.text:
A three-step arc with a choice, a rival plan and two endings:

# mypack/strategy/story.yaml
flags: [rival_revealed, beacon_destroyed]   # every flag a condition reads; one flags: list per campaign

arcs:
  main: {steps: [opening, reveal, finale]}

events:
  opening:
    when: day >= 0
    do: ["message(The frontier is quiet. Too quiet.)"]
  reveal:
    when: day >= 30 or research(deep_radar)
    do: ["message(Their fleet is building a beacon!)", set_flag(rival_revealed)]
    choices:
      - {text: "Ask the Senate for funds", do: ["money(200000)", "relation(senate, -10)"]}
      - {text: "Go it alone", do: ["relation(senate, 5)"]}
  finale:
    when: plan(beacon) >= 0.5
    do: ["message(Strike the beacon now!)", "mission(beacon_assault)"]

plans:
  beacon:
    owner: dominion
    stages: [{name: Frame, count: 4}, {name: Core, count: 4}]
    start_when: flag(rival_revealed)
    every: 7d
    chance: 60%
    raid: beacon_shipment                # a raid with chance: 0%, launched only by the plan
    warnings: [{at: 75%, do: ["message(The beacon is nearly complete.)"]}]
    complete: ["defeat(beacon_lit)"]

endings:
  beacon_destroyed: {victory: true, text: "The beacon is gone."}
  beacon_lit: {text: "The beacon is lit, and the frontier is theirs."}

campaign_end:
  victory: [{when: "flag(beacon_destroyed)", ending: beacon_destroyed}]
  defeat: [{when: "bases == 0", ending: beacon_lit}]

The mission beacon_assault sets the flag in its win outcome (outcomes: {win: [set_flag(beacon_destroyed)]}), which the next daily check turns into the victory.

docs.title: events
docs.text:
An event is a condition, a chance, a list of actions and, optionally, choices for the player.

Key Type Default Meaning when condition always When it may fire, in the campaign context. check daily, weekly, monthly, after_battle, on_research daily How often it is checked: at each day, week (168 h) or month (720 h) boundary, after any battle the player flies, or after any research topic is finished. chance fraction 100 % The chance per check, once when holds. do list of actions (or one action) none What it does when it fires. choices list of {text, do} none A choice for the player, made after do has run: text is the option (a @key or words), do its actions. Up to five are offered on number keys. once bool true Fires only once. cooldown time 0 For a repeating event (once: false): the least time between firings (60d). arc arc id none The arc it is a step of. Not needed when the arc lists it in steps.

An event fires when, at a check, it is not spent (once) or cooling down, it is its arc's next step (if it belongs to an arc), when holds, and its chance comes up. Events are checked in the order they are defined.

docs.title: arcs
docs.text:
arcs:
  serial: {steps: [ch01, ch02, ch03]}

steps lists events in order. A step can fire only after the step before it has fired, so each step's when needs to say only what this step waits for; arc(serial) reads how many steps have fired. A campaign may run several arcs side by side. An event listed in steps belongs to that arc whether or not it says arc:; an unknown event in steps is an error.

docs.title: plans
docs.text:
A rival's project, built from shipments the player can intercept. A plan's completion usually loses the campaign.

Key Type Default Meaning owner faction id — Whose plan it is (shown in the Archive; not otherwise used yet). stages list of {name, count} — The plan's parts in order; count components each (at least 1; {per_level: …} allowed). The plan's size is the sum. start_when condition at once When work begins (logged: Intelligence: the rival's … has begun). every time 7d How often a shipment is rolled once work has begun. chance fraction 100 % The chance per roll that a shipment leaves ({per_level: …} allowed). raid raid id none The raid a shipment flies as: a contact on the map, detected, intercepted and fought like any raid. Without it the plan grows only through the plan(…) action. warnings list of {at, do} none Actions run once when progress passes at (a fraction), in order. complete actions none Actions run when the last component arrives (usually defeat(<ending>)).

A shipment that reaches its destination unopposed adds one component; one the player intercepts and wins (or draws) against is gone and adds nothing; one the player loses to or breaks off from flies on and may still arrive. A plan's shipments go only while the player has a base. Give the shipment raid chance: 0% so that the ordinary raid roll never launches it: only the plan does.

plan(<id>) in a condition reads the progress, 0 to 1.

docs.title: relations
docs.text:
The player's standing with each other faction, from −100 to 100 (a global section).

Key Type Default Meaning dynamic bool false Standings change: actions move them, they drift, and stances take effect. Without it standings are fixed and the factions' own hostile lists decide everything. start mapping faction: number none Starting standings; an unlisted faction is 0. drift number 0 Each month every standing moves this much towards 0. stances mapping stance: upper bound hostile −40, wary −10, neutral 20, friendly 60 Stance names and the highest standing each covers, sorted by bound; above the last bound a faction is allied.

With dynamic: true:

  • relation(faction, n) moves a standing; a change of stance stops the clock with Relations: X are now Y (were Z).
  • Raids stop: a raid of a faction that has a standing flies only while that faction is hostile.
  • Battles follow the stances (app 0.10.3): when a campaign battle starts, every faction with a standing is made hostile to the player's faction if its stance is hostile, and not hostile otherwise — in that battle's own copy of the rules. A faction befriended stops attacking; one turned hostile attacks.
  • relation(<faction>) in a condition reads the standing, and expressions may use it — the default campaign's Senate stipend adds relation(senate) * 3000.

Not built yet: allied factions fighting at the player's side, relation effects on prices and trade, the design's relation_rules, and standings between factions other than the player.

docs.title: strategist
docs.text:
The rival's mood (a global section). Its aggression multiplies the chance of every raid.

Key Type Default Meaning aggression.start number 1 Starting aggression. aggression.min, aggression.max number 0.5, 2 Its limits. aggression.up number 0.1 Monthly rise while the player wins fewer than calm_after_wins battles that month (sits back). aggression.down number 0.1 Monthly fall when the player wins at least that many. calm_after_wins number 2 Battles won in a month that count as winning.

Without a strategist section aggression stays at 1. The aggression(n) action moves it directly. The design's budgets, expansion, offence ladder and Think.ini values are not built.

docs.title: endings and campaign_end
docs.text:
endings:
  engine_destroyed: {victory: true, text: "…"}
  last_base: {text: "…"}
campaign_end:
  defeat: [{when: "bases == 0", ending: last_base}]
  victory: [{when: "flag(engine_destroyed)", ending: engine_destroyed}]

An ending has a text (a @key or words), victory (default false) and, since app 0.12.1, an optional video — an asset played full screen when the campaign ends this way, before its text (the X-COM victory plays the original's closing credits, original:credits_sm2a.smk). campaign_end lists conditions for each: they are checked every day and after every battle, defeats first, and the first that holds ends the campaign. The victory(<ending>) and defeat(<ending>) actions end it at once. Once ended, the campaign stops; the screen shows VICTORY. or DEFEAT. with the text, and Enter saves and leaves. Continuing a finished campaign shows its ending again (app 0.12.1). A partial victory is simply another ending with victory: true and its own condition.

docs.title: encyclopaedia
docs.text:
encyclopaedia:
  dominion: {title: The Umbral Dominion, text: "…", unlock: day >= 0}

Each entry has a title (default the id), a text and an unlock condition; entries whose condition holds are listed on the strategy screen's Archive tab.

docs.title: Actions
docs.text:
Every action list in the story — do, choices[].do, warnings[].do, complete — and the strategy layer's evaluations do lists are checked when the rules load against the eighteen event actions (script::action::EVENT_ACTIONS): an unknown action or a wrong argument is an error with its place.

Action Arguments Does message(text) text A message that stops the clock (and goes in the log). news(text) text A News: line in the log; the clock runs on. card(Title \| text) text A full-screen title card in the campaign's skin (app 0.11.1): the title large in the skin's border colour, the text after \| wrapped beneath. The clock stops; Enter, Esc or a click dismisses it. The title goes in the log. Made for chapter openings. video(ref) asset Play a video full screen (app 0.12.0): original:<file>.smk from the player's data, or a pack path; Smacker only. The strategy screen waits and comes back afterwards (Cutscenes › Videos). play_cutscene(id) cutscene Play the engine cutscene cutscenes/<id>.yaml (app 0.13.0, Cutscenes); back to the strategy screen afterwards. set_flag(x), clear_flag(x) flag Set or clear a campaign flag. money(n) number Add (or, negative, take) money. score(x) score id Add a score entry (scores). relation(faction, n) faction, number Change a standing (dynamic relations only). research(x) topic The topic becomes known. discover(x) topic A hidden topic is discovered: from now on it is offered once its prerequisites hold. A notice says New research possible: ; kept as the flag discovered.<x> (app 0.16.6). mission(x) mission Offer a mission to fly now: the player accepts with Enter (the first ready craft with a pilot flies it) or declines with Esc. The outcome's campaign actions (score, money, set_flag, salvage, relation, and since app 0.16.3 capture, lose, cargo_lost, cargo_captured) apply as for a raid's battle (Raids and battles), and a win counts towards battles_won. raid(x) raid Launch that raid's contact now. plan(x, n) plan, number Add n components to a plan (warnings and completion follow). aggression(n) number Change the rival's aggression, within its limits. victory(x), defeat(x) ending End the campaign in that ending.

When one day's events ask for several videos or cutscenes, the last video asked for plays, and a cutscene only when no video was asked for; a video and a cutscene in the same event's list do not both play. An unknown video or play_cutscene id is reported on standard error when it would play (video …: …, cutscene x: no cutscene 'x'), not when the rules load (campaign.intro is checked at load since app 0.14.1).

An action with a single text argument takes everything between the brackets, commas included: message(Hold on, Guardsman!) (app 0.10.1). In a YAML flow list, quote an action that contains a comma, a colon or a +.

Text keys. Message, news and card texts, choice texts, ending texts and encyclopaedia titles and texts may be @keys (app 0.10.2), resolved like any other text: @msg.chapter_1 from the pack's text/, or @orig.KEY from the player's original language files.

docs.title: Conditions
docs.text:
Story conditions — when, start_when, campaign_end and unlock — use the campaign context, including its logistics queries (deposit, feature, research_site, survey_known, owned, lane_distance, facility_progress, construction_attacks; app 0.16.3), with five more queries:

Query Result Meaning arc(x) number Steps of arc x fired so far. plan(x) number Rival plan x's progress, 0..1. relation(x) number Faction x's standing with the player (−100..100). fired(x) number Times event x has fired. battles_won number Battles the player has won, story missions included.

docs.title: The default campaign's serial
docs.text:
resources/default/strategy/story.yaml (app 0.10.1) is Perils of the Void's serial, as in the campaign definition:

  • Arc serial, twelve chapters ch01 – ch12, each a title card (card(Chapter N - Title | hook), app 0.11.1; a message before that) and a mission offer. Chapters are triggered by the Guard's progress (days, research, bases), its relations and the Eclipse Engine's progress (plan(eclipse_engine)). Chapter 3 sets regent_revealed, which starts the plan; chapter 7 is the Cartel's choice — escort the Cartel's shipment (the Cartel becomes an ally, money) or raid it (the Cartel turns hostile, the Dominion's aggression falls, a mission); chapter 10 sets engine_site_found; chapter 12 offers the finale eclipse_assault.
  • Chapters whose bespoke mission is not built yet fly the nearest existing mission (colony_defence, convoy_ambush, intercept_scouts, pocket_ambush, ground_strike, defend_station, outpost_raid); only the finale has its own.
  • Side events: the Cartel's offers (monthly, 40 %, once: false, cooldown: 60d), the Belt Prospectors' tithe to friends (monthly while relation(prospectors) >= 20) and the Black Comet's truce, a choice that can buy the raiders off (standing +70 → neutral, so they stop raiding and stop attacking in battle).
  • Plan eclipse_engine: Lens, Coils and Heart, six components each; starts with regent_revealed; a shipment every 9 days at 70 % as the raid eclipse_shipment (intercept_scouts, chance: 0%); warnings at 33 %, 66 % and 90 %; complete = defeat(engine_lit).
  • Relations: dynamic; Senate 40, Cartel −5, Prospectors 15, raiders −70, Dominion −100; drift 2 a month; the default stances. The Senate stipend follows the Senate's standing.
  • Strategist: aggression 1.0 (0.6 – 1.8, ±0.1 a month), calm after 3 wins.
  • Endings: engine_destroyed (victory, set by eclipse_assault's win), engine_lit, last_base (no bases left) and senate_recognises (relation(senate) <= -60).
  • Encyclopaedia: the Guard, the Dominion, cosmium, the Eclipse Engine (once the Regent is revealed) and the Cartel (once chapter 7 has fired).

The finale mission eclipse_assault (in missions/missions.yaml) is set in the pocket nebula: the Engine (a dominion_outpost), three Thunderbolt wingmen, a guard fleet that comes again every two minutes while the Engine stands, and a dreadnought after 90 s; its win scores engine_destroyed and sets the flag.

The unit test campaign::tests::the_default_campaign_runs_a_year_with_its_story_and_stays_consistent plays it for a year with the automatic player (which takes each choice's first option and alternates mission results), a month at a time, checking that nothing refers to something that is not there, that arcs only move forward, and that the serial and the Engine are under way.

docs.title: The interceptor campaign's Doomsday arc
docs.text:
packs/interceptor/strategy/story.yaml (app 0.10.2) expresses the original's story from the design analysis — the gate chain the strategy guide describes. Every estimate is marked DERIVED in the file.

  • Arc doomsday: alien_message_1 – alien_message_5, summon_macarthur, final_mission. The first message is checked after_battle from 1 February with a chance per battle by difficulty, or regardless later (the later day is derived); the next ones need their date, a saucer examination topic and the Doomsday plan's progress; MacArthur needs three research topics, and the final mission (destroy_doomsday_weapon, whose win now sets doomsday_destroyed) is offered about a week later.
  • Plan doomsday: three stages (Structural, Weapon, Drive) with {per_level: …} counts, shipments as the raid doomsday_convoy (the escorted alien freighter ambush) with a chance by difficulty, three warnings and defeat(doomsday_complete).
  • Side missions: two of the original's seven so far — a rogue freighter and Kabron pirates, both flying ambush_pirate_squadron on derived triggers.
  • Strategist: aggression with derived values (the original's Think.ini rules are not read yet).
  • Videos (app 0.12.0): each alien message also plays the original's transmission film, video(original:alientrans1.smk) – alientrans5.smk; the victory ending plays the credits film (video: original:credits_sm2a.smk, app 0.12.1); and a new campaign opens with campaign.intro_video: original:animation1.smk (app 0.13.0) — which of the CD's films is the original's opening is derived.
  • Endings: doomsday_destroyed (victory), doomsday_complete and last_base.
  • Texts from the original: the warnings, MacArthur's prompt and two endings use the original's own text keys — @orig.DD_WARNING1 – DD_WARNING3, @orig.MAC_PROMPT1, @orig.DD_TOOLATE, @orig.S_LASTBASEDEAD — read from the player's data at load.

Derived: the saucer examinations

The gates of messages 2 – 4 use the topics type_1_saucer_examination, type_2_saucer_examination and type_3_saucer_examination for the guide's Wraith, Spectre and Phantasm examinations. That mapping is derived and unconfirmed.

docs.title: Trying a story out
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --campaign <id> --strategy-soak 365 plays a year headless and now prints the last monthly report and a story line: each arc's steps (serial 12/12), each plan's progress, the aggression and the ending reached (or none).
  • --check --campaign <id> reports every story error below.
  • On the strategy screen the Archive tab shows the plans under way, every standing and stance, the aggression, battles won and the unlocked encyclopaedia.
  • The event debugger (app 0.16.13): Ctrl+D on the strategy screen adds a Debug list — Arc : step n of m for each arc, then every event as - fired n, condition holds (or false), evaluated now. Fire now on an event fires it whatever its condition (Campaign::fire_event): it counts as fired, its arc advances only if it is the arc's next step, its actions run and its choice is offered; the log records Debug: fired event . A test event with when: day >= 99999 is a handy way to run any action list by hand.
  • Start at a chapter (app 0.16.13): openinterceptor --campaign <id> --strategy --chapter <n> plays a new campaign forward headless with the automatic player (--strategy-soak's) until its first arc reaches step n, or for at most 1500 days, then opens the strategy screen there.

    • Not built yet: setting flags and plan progress directly (fire an event that does it).

docs.title: Errors
docs.text: Message Cause events.x.check: 'y' is not daily, weekly, monthly, after_battle or on_research A wrong check period. events.x.arc: unknown arc 'y' / arcs.x.steps: unknown event 'y' An arc or step that is not defined. events.x.do: unknown action 'y' (known: …) (also .choices, plans.x.warnings, plans.x.complete) An action that is not an event action, or a wrong argument. events.x.when: … (also plans.x.start_when, encyclopaedia.x.unlock, campaign_end.victory) A condition that does not parse, or names something not defined. plans.x.raid: unknown raid 'y' A plan shipping as a raid that is not defined. campaign_end.victory: unknown ending 'y' (or defeat) An end condition naming an ending that is not defined. save: the story's events or arcs do not match the loaded rules (was a mod changed?) (or plans) Continuing a save after events, arcs or plans were added or removed.

docs.title: Strategy layer
docs.text:
The campaign around the battles — the star map, bases, research, the economy, craft, pilots and the enemy raids that start battles — is pack data (app 0.7.0 – 0.7.3), and so is the optional logistics layer of mining, manufacturing, research stations and supply convoys (app 0.9.0, Logistics). The story on top of it — events, arcs, the rival's plans, relations, the strategist, endings and the encyclopaedia (app 0.10.0) — has its own page, Story layer. A campaign that has a start: section has a strategy layer: the launcher then leads with Campaign: continue and Campaign: new game (User guide › Campaign). A campaign without start: is battles only, as before.

Requirements: R-STR-001 – R-STR-027. Design (the full planned format, of which this page is the built part): Format: strategy layer. How the engine plays these rules: Architecture › Campaign.

docs.title: Where the files go
docs.text:
Strategy sections are ordinary rules sections, so they may sit in any rules file; by convention they go in <pack>/strategy/*.yaml, which the loader reads like rules/, campaign/ and missions/. The default campaign splits them by subject:

File Sections resources/default/strategy/start.yaml start, flags resources/default/strategy/map.yaml maps, star_classes resources/default/strategy/research.yaml research_model, research resources/default/strategy/economy.yaml economy, incomes, expenses, items, hulls, base_modules, base_types resources/default/strategy/raids.yaml raids resources/default/strategy/pilots.yaml pilots, scores resources/default/strategy/logistics.yaml resources, components, recipes, facility_types, research_sites, logistics; and, merged into the reach map, the hulls and the research tree: deposits, features, hull components, two station-only topics (app 0.9.0) resources/default/strategy/story.yaml events, arcs, plans, relations, strategist, endings, campaign_end, encyclopaedia (app 0.10.1; Story layer)

The interceptor campaign has two (app 0.8.0, below): packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml, generated from the player's own files, and packs/interceptor/strategy/campaign.yaml, written by hand; and since app 0.10.2 its story, packs/interceptor/strategy/story.yaml (Story layer).

Each file starts with # yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../schemas/rules.schema.json, so an editor offers every key below. Definition sections (maps, research, items, …) layer across packs like any other definitions: an addon may add a research topic, inherit an item or delete: true a raid (Rulesets).

docs.title: Units
docs.text:
• Times — build_time, every, delivery — take a time unit: 10d (days, new in app 0.6.7 for every time quantity), 36h, 90min; a plain number is hours in the strategy layer.
  • Map units — positions, speed, sensor_range, max_distance — are the map's own units; unit_ly says how many light years one is (for display). speed is map units per hour.
  • Money is a plain number. upkeep, maintenance and salary are per month (720 hours). economy.cost_scale multiplies every item, hull and module cost, sell price, upkeep and maintenance (app 0.8.0; for data in thousands, like the original's).
  • Work units — research size, prod_time — are consumed at a rate per hour: a base's research rate (research_model.rate) or production rate (module effect production_rate).

docs.title: Expressions: the campaign context
docs.text:
Prerequisites (requires:), amounts (incomes, expenses) and the research rate are written in the condition language with the campaign context (script::campaign, app 0.6.7). Plain numbers are expressions too. Every id the strategy layer defines — topics, items, hulls, modules, base types, raids, flags — and every faction, ship class and mission id is a named constant, so a misspelt name (research(lazers)) is a load error that names it. Difficulty level ids are constants as well (difficulty >= veteran).

Query Result Meaning research(x) true/false Topic x has been researched. researching(x) true/false A base is working on topic x. has(x) number Items x in store, all bases. module_count(x) number Working modules x — at the base being evaluated (in a research rate), else at all bases. bases number The player's bases. money number The player's money. day number Days since the campaign began. month number Whole months (30 days) since the campaign began. difficulty number The difficulty level (compare with level names). pilots number Pilots on the roster. score number The campaign score so far. month_score number Score gained since the last monthly report. random(p) true/false True with probability p (0..1), from the campaign's seeded generator. flag(x) true/false Campaign flag x is set (by a mission outcome's set_flag(x)). salvaged(x) true/false Something named x has been salvaged (see Battles). craft number The player's craft, all bases. arc(x), plan(x), relation(x), fired(x), battles_won number The story's queries (app 0.10.0): see Story layer › Conditions. deposit(s, r) number The daily rate of resource r in system s — 0 until the system is surveyed (logistics, app 0.16.3). feature(s, tag) true/false System s has the feature tag (known without a survey). research_site(s, site) true/false System s meets research site site's features. survey_known(s) true/false System s has been surveyed. owned(s) true/false The player has a base or a facility (finished or not) in system s. lane_distance(a, b) number Jumps along the map's lanes from a to b (breadth-first; each lane one jump); 0 for the same system, −1 when no route exists; on a map without lanes every pair is 1 apart. facility_progress(s) number The construction progress (0..1) of the least finished facility in system s; 1 when none is building (also when there is none). construction_attacks(s) number Construction strikes suffered by the facilities built in system s.

Systems are named by their map id (ajax, nebula_haven) and are checked names like everything else, as are resource ids, feature tags and research-site ids (app 0.16.3).

research(ion_rays) and research(saucer_hulls)
6 + module_count(laboratory) * 12
400000 + 60000 * bases + month_score * 200
survey_known(nebula_haven) and deposit(nebula_haven, dilithium) > 10
owned(ajax) and lane_distance(mercury_gate, tycho_drift) <= 3

docs.title: start
docs.text:
How a new campaign begins. Without start: the campaign has no strategy layer.

Key Type Default Meaning date text required The first day, YYYY-MM-DD (Gregorian calendar, leap years counted). A missing or malformed date is a load error. money number 0 Starting money. map id the first map The map (maps.<id>). bases list of {type, system, name, modules} none Bases the player starts with: a base type, the system it is in, its name, and modules beyond the type's template. Starting bases and their modules are finished. craft list of {hull, base, count} none Craft the player starts with; base is an index into bases (0 = the first). pilots number 0 Pilots on the starting roster; they take the starting craft in order. research ids none Topics already known. stock mapping item: count none Items in store at the first base. money_from original:<file>/<key> none The starting money read from the player's original file, from the section named after the difficulty level (its id with a capital first letter: veteran → [Veteran]); the key's name is matched without regard to case. Replaces money. Not found = load error (app 0.8.0).

docs.title: maps and star_classes
docs.text:
maps: {<id>: …} — the star map.

Key Type Default Meaning kind fixed / generated fixed Hand-made (the systems as written) or generated when a campaign starts. systems fixed: mapping id: {name, pos, class, hidden}; generated: [min, max] or a count — Fixed: each system's display name (default the id), pos: [x, y] (required), star class (default yellow) and hidden (not shown until a base's sensors reach it; default false). Generated: how many systems (default 30). lanes list of {between: [a, b]} none Lanes between two of the map's systems (drawn on the map). travel free / lanes free Straight lines anywhere (the original) or along the lanes (app 0.7.3; see Travel). size [w, h] [60000, 60000] Generated: the rectangle, map units. names list of text none Generated: system names to draw from (then numbered). seed number the campaign's Generated: a fixed seed, so every campaign gets the same map. black_holes number 1 Generated: how many systems are hidden black holes. unit_ly number 0.001 Light years per map unit (display only).

Fixed-map systems also take bodies (a list of planets, moons and belts; descriptive) and, for a campaign with logistics, deposits and features (app 0.9.0).

star_classes: {<id>: {color: [r, g, b], weight}} — how a star of that class is drawn, and (for generated maps) how often it appears relative to the others (weight, default 1; 0 = never rolled). Generated systems are scattered at least a little apart, take a class by weight and a name from names.

docs.title: research and research_model
docs.text:
research: {<id>: …} — the research tree.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. size number 1000 Work units to finish (also read from the original's file_size, in thousands, through inheritance). requires condition none Available to research only while this holds: research(x), salvaged(x), any campaign query. requires_any list of topic ids none Available once any one of these topics is known — shorthand for research(a) or research(b), joined to requires with and (app 0.16.6). hidden bool false Not offered at all until a story event's discover(<topic>) action has run (then its requires must still hold; a notice says New research possible: ). The discovery is kept as the campaign flag discovered.<topic> (app 0.16.6). unlocks list none What finishing it makes available: items.<id>, hulls.<id>, modules.<id> (or base_modules.<id>), base_types.<id>. Something a topic unlocks cannot be bought, made or built until the topic is known. description text empty Encyclopaedia text (Stage 5 shows it). prereq1, prereq2, prereq3 numbers none The original's numeric prerequisites, read through inheritance; with a tech_ids table and no requires, they become research(a) and research(b) (app 0.8.0). lab, site, start_cost none A station-only topic: see Logistics › research stations (app 0.9.0).

research_model: — how research progresses.

Key Type Default Meaning mode download / labs download How it is described: the original's downloads, or staff in labs. The rule is the same: each base works on one topic at a time. rate expression 10 Work units per hour at one base, evaluated per base (so module_count counts that base's modules). switching keep_progress / lose_progress keep_progress Whether switching a base to another topic keeps the work done on the old one (with lose_progress it is lost unless another base is still working on it).

A topic finishes when its work reaches size; every base working on it stops, and a message says so.

docs.title: items and hulls
docs.text:
items: {<id>: …} — equipment, ammunition and goods.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. kind id goods beam, launcher, missile, armor, shield, engine, sensor, special, probe, mine or goods; matched against hull slots. cost number 0 Purchase price; 0 = cannot be bought. sell_price number 0 What one fetches on the market. prod_time number 0 Work units to manufacture one; 0 = bought only. size number 1 Storage space: what one takes of a base's store when the campaign has storage modules (app 0.16.10). rounds number 1 Missiles: the rounds one missile slot holds; fitting a slot takes this many from the store (app 0.7.2). protection number 0 A shield: shield points per facing; an armor: armour points (app 0.15.0). An item that inherits the original's equipment and sets none takes the original's Special (shields) or HitPoints (armour) — derived. In battle a craft flies with the strongest fitted shield and the sum of its fitted armour, in place of its class's shields / armor; with none fitted it keeps the class's own (which fitted: on the ship class may supply). requires condition none Available only while this holds (as well as any topic that unlocks it). tech_required, tech_required2 numbers none The original's numeric tech ids, read through inheritance; with a tech_ids table and no requires, they become the prerequisite (app 0.8.0). Also on hulls and modules.

hulls: {<id>: …} — the strategy side of a ship class. The id must be a ship class's id (hulls.comet is ships.comet); another id is a load error.

Key Type Default Meaning cost number 0 Purchase price. prod_time number 0 Work units to manufacture one. upkeep number 0 Per month, per craft (also read from the original's maint_cost through inheritance). speed number 1000 Map units per hour on the star map. slots mapping kind: count none Equipment slots: {beam: 2, missile: 2, shield: 1, armor: 1} (also read from the original's mount counts through inheritance). beam, missile, shield and armor slots change the craft in battle; other kinds are filled but have no effect yet. The interceptor hulls have one shield and one armor slot (app 0.15.0, derived). requires condition none Available only while this holds. components mapping component: amount none With logistics: what a main base builds one from. A hull with components is not paid for in money when its manufacture starts; it waits until the components are in the base's store (app 0.9.0).

docs.title: base_modules and base_types
docs.text:
base_modules: {<id>: …} — what a base is built from.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. group id the id Its limits group (research, hangar, sensor, …): a base type's limits cap modules per group. cost number 0 Build price, paid when ordered. build_time time 72 h Time to build; the module works from then on. With economy.module_time: days, a module without build_time takes its prod_time (the original's key) in days (app 0.8.0). maintenance number 0 Per month. effects mapping name: number none Campaign quantities it adds while working: research_rate, production_rate, sensor_range, hangar (craft housed), quarters (pilots housed), storage (store capacity, in item sizes), defence (points), income. requires condition none Available only while this holds.

As built, the engine reads production_rate (manufacturing), sensor_range (detection and revealing hidden systems) and hangar (craft a base houses). research_rate is a number the research_model.rate expression may use through module_count. Since app 0.16.10:

  • quarters: the pilots the player can keep — every base type's quarters plus every working quarters module, all bases together. Hiring is refused at the limit (no quarters: room for n pilots). A campaign that gives no quarters anywhere has no limit.
  • storage: a base's store capacity from its working storage modules, counted in item sizes; buying more than fits is refused (no room in store: …). If no module in the campaign has storage, there is no limit — but once one does, a base without one has room for nothing (deliveries, manufacture and salvage are not checked).
  • defence: each point of a base's working modules' defence turns away 15 % of unopposed raids on that base on its own — 1 − 0.85^points in all (two points: 28 %, four: 48 %). A raid turned away is reported and destroys nothing.
  • income stays a tag: an incomes: formula counts the modules with module_count.

Dismantling (app 0.16.10): any module of a base can be dismantled from the Bases list; it is removed at once and economy.dismantle of its cost (50 %) is refunded.

base_types: {<id>: …} — kinds of base.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. cost number 0 Build price. build_time time 168 h Time to build the hub and its template modules; the base is under construction until then. max_bases number 8 The most bases of this type. limits mapping group: count none The most modules of each group. template ids none Modules a new base comes with. sensor_range number 0 The hub's own sensor range, map units (modules add to it). hangar, quarters number 0 Craft and pilots the hub alone houses. max_distance number 0 A new base must be within this many map units of one of yours (0 = anywhere).

docs.title: raids
docs.text:
raids: {<id>: …} — enemy flights the campaign launches now and then. Meeting one is a battle.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Shown on the map and in messages. mission id required The mission flown when it is intercepted (missions.<id>; unknown = load error). faction id required Who flies it (factions.<id>; unknown = load error). every time 72 h Time between rolls. chance fraction 50 % Chance per roll that a raid launches (45%). requires condition none Rolled only while this holds (day >= 10). target base / system base What it heads for: one of the player's bases, or any system. speed number 600 Map units per hour.

On a free-travel map a launched raid appears well outside the map, in a random direction, and flies straight for its target; on a lane map it enters at a system and follows the lanes (Travel). See Raids and battles.

docs.title: incomes and expenses
docs.text: incomes: {<id>: {name, every, amount}} and expenses: {<id>: {name, every, amount}} — an amount (an expression) added or taken every period (every, default 30 days). Each payment is a line in the message log. Module maintenance, hull upkeep and pilot salary are charged monthly on their own; use expenses for anything else.

docs.title: pilots and scores
docs.text:
pilots: — pilot rules.

Key Type Default Meaning stats mapping stat: [min, max] none Each pilot's stats, rolled in the range. Any names. ranks mapping rank: experience none Ranks in ascending order with the experience each needs. salary number 0 Per month, per living pilot. recruit_fee number 0 Cost to hire one. pool number 6 Recruits offered at a time (refreshed every month). names list of text none Names to draw from. heal_days number 14 Days an injured pilot is out. survive fraction 60 % Chance that a pilot shot down ejects (injured) rather than dies. training {gain, cost} none Pilot training (app 0.16.7): a ready pilot put into training gains gain points in every stat a day, up to the top of that stat's stats range, and costs cost money a day. Without it (or with gain: 0) the Hangar offers no Train button. Training continues until stopped; it is saved.

scores: {<name>: points} — mission score names. A mission outcome's score(<name>) adds the points to the campaign score and the month's score; the name undefended is used when a raid reaches its target unopposed.

docs.title: evaluations
docs.text:
evaluations: [{rating, when, do}] (app 0.16.8; a global section like scores) — the patron's monthly evaluation. At each monthly report the ratings are tried in order and the first whose when holds rates the month: its do actions run (the event actions: money(-50000), news(…), relation(…), set_flag(…), …) and the report ends rated . A rating without when always applies, so put a catch-all last. No rating holds: the report has none. Key Type Meaning rating text The month's rating, shown in the report and the Reports list. when condition When it applies (the campaign context; month_score is the month being rated). None: always. do list of actions Run when it rates the month. Checked when the rules load. 

evaluations:
  - {rating: Outstanding, when: month_score >= 400, do: ["money(150000)", "news(The Senate commends the Guard's month)"]}
  - {rating: Satisfactory, when: month_score >= 0}
  - {rating: Poor, when: month_score >= -300, do: ["money(-50000)"]}
  - {rating: Unacceptable, do: ["money(-150000)", "news(The Senate cuts the Guard's funding)"]}

Before app 0.16.9 the section was dropped when the rules were built (it was missing from the list of strategy globals), so a pack's ratings never reached the campaign.

docs.title: flags and economy
docs.text:
flags: [<id>, …] — campaign flags that conditions may test with flag(x) before any mission sets them (set_flag(x) names in mission outcomes are added automatically).

economy:

Key Type Default Meaning delivery time 48 h Time for a purchase to arrive. delivery_loss fraction 0 % Chance that a purchase is lost on the way (app 0.16.11): it is paid for all the same, and a notice says so. dismantle fraction 50 % The share of a module's cost refunded when it is dismantled (app 0.16.10). salvage_per_kill number 0 Money per enemy destroyed when an outcome says salvage. cost_scale number 1 Multiplies every item and hull cost, sell_price, hull upkeep and module cost and maintenance (app 0.8.0). The interceptor campaign sets 1000: the original's money is in thousands. module_time days — Modules without build_time take their prod_time in days (app 0.8.0; the original's module times are days).

docs.title: tech_ids
docs.text:
tech_ids: {<number>: <research id>} (app 0.8.0) — for data inherited from a game that names prerequisites by number. A topic's prereq1 – prereq3, and an item's, hull's or module's tech_required and tech_required2, are looked up in the table and become research(<id>) conditions joined with and. Rules:

  • A written requires: always wins; the numbers are used only when there is none.
  • A number the table does not list is left out of the condition (the original's ids for alien craft and installations, 75 and up, are not research topics).
  • Without a tech_ids table the numeric keys are ignored.
  • The research ids are checked like any other name: a table entry naming an unknown topic is a load error once a condition uses it.

docs.title: How a campaign plays the data
docs.text:
• Time passes an hour at a time (smaller at the end of a jump). Each hour: construction finishes, each base researches its topic at research_model.rate, each base manufactures its queue (first job first) at its production_rate, deliveries arrive, incomes and expenses pay, pilots heal, raids roll and move, sensors detect, interceptions fly.
  • The month (every 720 hours): maintenance, upkeep and salaries are charged; the first evaluation that holds rates the month and runs its actions (app 0.16.8); the monthly report gives the month's score, the total, the costs, the funds and the rating; a new pool of recruits is offered.
  • Training (app 0.16.7): every hour each ready pilot in training gains training.gain / 24 in every stat and the campaign pays training.cost / 24.
  • Bases. A new base is built in a system that has none, at most max_bases of a type, within max_distance of one of yours; it comes with its template modules and is finished after build_time. A module is refused beyond its group's limit or while not available.
  • Buying pays now and delivers to the current base after economy.delivery — unless the base's store is full (storage), and with the chance economy.delivery_loss the delivery is lost. Selling takes one item from the current base's store at sell_price. Manufacture queues at the base; finished units go into its store (hulls become craft there). The player can move a queued job up one place and cancel a job: a job not yet started goes without cost, a job at work keeps only the unit already paid for (app 0.16.11). Each unit is paid for as it starts (its cost); a job waits while the money is short (app 0.9.0; until then manufacture was free). With logistics, a hull that has components is paid in components instead: it starts when they are in the base's store.
  • Interception sends every craft of the current base that is at home and has a ready pilot.
  • Fitting (app 0.7.2): fit best fills each of the craft's hull slots with the costliest item of that kind in its base's store, as many as the hull has slots of that kind (a missile slot takes the item's rounds); what was fitted before goes back into the store first. A campaign battle flies the fit: fitted beam items become the player's class's beams and fitted missile items its racks, matched to beams: and missiles: of the same id (items.blaster ↔ beams.blaster); ids with no such weapon are skipped, and with no beams fitted the class keeps its own. The refit changes only that battle's copy of the rules (wingmen of the same class fly it too).

docs.title: Travel
docs.text:
On a travel: free map everything flies straight. On a travel: lanes map (app 0.7.3):

  • a raid enters at the system farthest from its target that has none of the player's bases, and follows the shortest way along the lanes to the system nearest its target;
  • an interception flies the lanes from its base to the system nearest the contact, then straight to the contact, and comes home along the lanes;
  • the map draws each contact's way ahead. Routes are kept in saves.

The shortest way is by distance along the lanes (Dijkstra's algorithm, Campaign::lane_route); systems no lane joins are reached in one straight hop. Endurance and stranding are not built.

docs.title: Raids and battles
docs.text:
1. A raid's roll succeeds: a contact starts outside the map and heads for its target.
  2. When a contact comes within a base's sensor range (hub plus sensor_range effects) it is detected — the clock stops with a message — and shows on the map.
  3. The player sends the current base's ready craft to intercept it. They fly at their hull's speed; when they reach it the clock stops and the player chooses: fly the raid's mission, with the first craft's hull as the player's ship, auto-resolve it (app 0.16.12), or break off (the contact flies on). Auto-resolve rolls the result from both sides' strength: each craft's power is √(effective hit points × sustained damage per second) of its class (the --balance numbers), a side's power the sum — the player's craft at the contact against the mission's hostile roles at their average counts — and the player wins with p = P² / (P² + E²). The mission's own outcome actions for the rolled win or lose apply as for a flown battle (DEV-057).
  4. The battle's debrief comes back to the campaign: the outcome's actions apply — score(<name>), money(<n>), set_flag(<id>), relation(<faction>, <n>), salvage (money: salvage_per_kill × kills, and the raid's id is recorded, so salvaged(<raid id>) holds from then on — fixed in app 0.9.0; before, the display name was recorded and never matched), and since app 0.16.3:
  5. capture — every prize the player's tractor beam brought home (the battle reports each as captured(<class>)) is kept as salvage, so salvaged(<class id>) holds and research can start from a capture; without capture in the outcome nothing is kept;
  6. lose(<facility type>) — the player's most recently built facility of that type is lost (its orders and the convoys bound for it go too; a notice says so); any other argument is only logged;
  7. cargo_lost, cargo_captured — recorded in the log (a convoy escort's own cargo: share settles the cargo).

A stance change that a relation(…) outcome causes is announced as soon as the map is back, and stops the clock (app 0.16.2). A flown convoy escort or construction defence applies its outcome's actions too (app 0.16.3, 0.16.4). The leader is credited the kills and experience (kills + 1); every pilot in the party a mission. A killed result loses the craft, and its pilot ejects injured (survive) or dies. win and draw remove the contact; lose and retreat leave it flying. Leaving a campaign battle early from the pause menu is a retreat. 5. A contact that reaches its target unopposed: a base target loses its newest finished module, and the undefended score applies — unless the base's defence turns it away (app 0.16.10).

docs.title: Logistics
docs.text:
App 0.9.0, plan items 4.14 – 4.17. An optional layer of the strategy game: raw resources are mined from deposits in star systems, manufacturing centers turn them into components by recipes, and main bases build hulls from components. Nothing is shipped on speculation: demand pulls supply up the chain, and automatic government supply convoys carry each filled order along the lanes. Survey ships find out what a system holds; research stations work on topics no ordinary base can. The design is Logistics: facilities and supply lines; requirements R-STR-012 – R-STR-027.

A campaign has logistics only if it defines at least one facility_types entry. Without one, every key below is ignored and the campaign plays as before (the interceptor campaign has none, deliberately). The definition sections (resources, components, recipes, facility_types, research_sites) layer across packs like any other definitions.

Amounts are plain numbers in the resource's unit. Mining rate is per day; everything else in time takes the usual units (24h, 10d).

docs.title: resources and components
docs.text: Section Key Type Default Meaning resources.<id> name text the id Display name of a raw resource (mined). unit text empty The unit shown after amounts (t, kg). components.<id> name text the id Display name of a manufactured component.

docs.title: recipes
docs.text:
recipes: {<id>: …} — what a manufacturing center makes.

Key Type Default Meaning component id the recipe's id The component made. One recipe per component is used (the first). inputs mapping resource or component: amount none What one run consumes, taken from the center's store when the run starts. time time 24 h How long one run takes (at least 0.1 h). output number 1 How much one run makes.

An input or output that is neither a resource nor a component is a load error.

docs.title: facility_types
docs.text:
facility_types: {<id>: …} — what the player may build in a star system.

Key Type Default Meaning name text the id Display name. role mining / manufacturing / research required What it does. Another value is a load error. cost number 0 Build price, paid when ordered. time time 10 d Time to build; it works from then on. storage number 500 Mining: the most goods its store holds; extraction stops when it is full. lines number 1 Manufacturing: recipes running at once. research_rate number 0 Research: work units an hour on its project. hub id none The battle object at the facility, with its construction-stage looks (read; not yet used — R-STR-022).

Where a facility may be built (fixed rules per role, app 0.9.0; the design's placement: expressions are not built — DEV-049). At most one facility of each type per system, and:

Role Needs mining A surveyed system with at least one deposit. research A surveyed system that meets at least one research site's features. manufacturing A system with one of the player's bases, or at most two lanes from one (a system no lane reaches counts as one straight hop).

docs.title: research_sites
docs.text: research_sites: {<id>: {features: [<tag>, …]}} — a site is any system whose features include all the listed tags. Station-only topics name the site they need (below).

docs.title: On the map, hulls and topics
docs.text: Where Key Type Meaning A map system (maps.<id>.systems.<id>) deposits mapping resource: {rate, reserve, body} What a mining facility there extracts: rate per day (default 1), reserve a number or unlimited (the default), body descriptive. An unknown resource is a load error. Only the start map's systems are read. features list of tags Matched against research_sites. A hull (hulls.<id>) components mapping component: amount What a main base builds one from (instead of money). An unknown component is a load error. A topic (research.<id>) lab facility type Only a facility of this type may research it; the topic is not offered to bases. Unknown = load error. site research site Only a station in a system meeting this site. Unknown = load error. start_cost mapping resource or component: amount Materials delivered once to begin; then research runs without further supply.

docs.title: logistics
docs.text:
The supply settings (a global section).

Key Type Default Meaning vessels number 3 Vessels in each supply convoy; each carries an even share of the cargo. ambush_chance fraction 30 % Chance, rolled when a convoy launches, that it will be attacked on its way; the point along its route is rolled then too. ambush_loss fraction 35 % Chance that each vessel of an ambushed convoy is lost when the ambush is auto-resolved (no ambush_mission, or the player lets it fight through). survey_attack_chance fraction 25 % Chance, rolled when a survey ship launches, that it is attacked on the way. survey_speed number 900 Survey ship speed, map units an hour. convoy_speed number 500 Convoy speed, map units an hour. construction_strikes {from, max, chance, mission, setback} none Enemy strikes on facilities under construction (below, app 0.16.4). Without it there are none. ambush_mission mission id none The battle flown when the player escorts an ambushed convoy (app 0.9.2). With it, an ambushed convoy waits where it is and the clock stops: the player flies its escort, and the share of the mission's cargo: role still aboard at the end is delivered — or lets it fight through (auto-resolved as below). Without it every ambush is auto-resolved. An unknown mission is a load error. The default campaign sets convoy_ambush.

docs.title: How the chain runs
docs.text:
Every hour, after the rest of the hour step (Architecture › Campaign):
