  1. Demand at bases. Each hull job not yet started needs its hull's components. What the base's store lacks, less what is already on its way, is ordered from the nearest ready manufacturing center (nearest by straight-line distance).
  2. Mining facilities extract each deposit of their system at rate / 24 an hour, until the store is full (storage) or the reserve runs out.
  3. Manufacturing centers finish runs (the output goes into the store), then look at the orders they must fill: when the store plus the runs under way do not cover an order, a free line starts the component's recipe if its inputs are in store; if they are not, the missing inputs are ordered from the nearest mining facility whose system has a deposit of them.
  4. Research stations with a project first order its start_cost; when it is in store it is used up, and from then on the station adds research_rate an hour to the topic.
  5. Filled orders leave as convoys. When a facility's store holds an order's amount, it is taken out and a convoy of vessels vessels leaves along the lanes for the order's base or facility. The ambush roll and point are decided now.
  6. Convoys travel at convoy_speed. At the ambush point each vessel may be lost (ambush_loss) and a message says how many; on arrival the surviving share of the cargo is delivered. A short delivery is simply wanted again: the next hour's demand orders the rest.
  7. Hull jobs whose components are in the base's store start, using them up; the factory then works on them as usual.
  8. Survey ships arrive. One that was attacked is lost half the time; otherwise the system is surveyed and a message lists its deposits (with rates a day and the reserve, or unlimited), its features and the research sites it meets (reserves and features since app 0.16.2).
  9. Construction strikes (app 0.16.4, with construction_strikes): see below.

An order is placed only when a facility exists that can fill it: a base without a reachable manufacturing center simply waits. Facilities report when they are complete.

docs.title: Construction strikes
docs.text:
logistics.construction_strikes (app 0.16.4, R-STR-023) lets the enemy strike a facility while it is being built:

Key Type Default Meaning from fraction 50 % Construction progress from which a site can be struck. max number 3 Strikes at most per location (all facilities in one system together). chance fraction 10 % Chance per day for each eligible site. mission mission id none The defence the player flies (construction_defence). None: every strike is let be. setback fraction 25 % A strike not flown sets construction back this share of the facility type's time. 
logistics:
  construction_strikes: {from: 50%, max: 3, chance: 12%, mission: construction_defence, setback: 25%}

Each hour every site past from whose system has had fewer than max strikes rolls chance (per day); one strike at a time stops the clock with a prompt:

  • Fly the defence — the mission with the first ready craft: a win beats the strike off; a loss destroys the site (removed with its orders); a retreat or draw counts as not flown. The mission's own outcome actions apply too.
  • Let it be — or no ready craft, or no mission — the strike sets the site back by setback × its build time.

Every strike counts towards construction_attacks(<system>) (saved).

docs.title: The player's orders
docs.text:
On the strategy screen's Supply tab (User guide › Campaign):

  • Survey the chosen system from the current base — it must be within that base's sensor range (hub plus sensor_range effects) and not already surveyed.
  • Build a facility of any type in the chosen system, paying its cost (the row says why not when it is not allowed).
  • Research here: on a finished research station, start a station-only topic whose lab is its type, whose site its system meets and whose requires holds.

docs.title: Research stations and station-only topics
docs.text:
research:
  theremin_shielding:
    name: Theremin shielding
    size: 24000
    requires: research(heat_rays)
    lab: research_station        # only this facility type researches it
    site: nebula_lab             # only in a system meeting this site
    start_cost: {cosmium: 20, dilithium: 2}

The topic's progress is shared with the rest of the tree: when it reaches size it is known, like any other topic, and its unlocks apply.

docs.title: The default campaign's logistics
docs.text: resources/default/strategy/logistics.yaml: four resources (iron, gold, cosmium, dilithium), three components (hull plating, rocket motors, ray emitters) with a recipe each, the three facility types (mining facility, manufacturing center, research station), two research sites (nebula_lab, pulsar_array), deposits in every one of the Reach's six systems and two features, the components of all four hulls, and two station-only topics (theremin_shielding, pulsar_navigation). Every hull of the default campaign is therefore built from components: a Guard player who wants more craft must survey, mine and manufacture first.

docs.title: Not built yet
docs.text: Convoy ambushes can be flown since app 0.9.2 (ambush_mission; the battle is described in Missions › The convoy ambush), and construction sites are struck since app 0.16.4 (above). Not built: facility fighter pools and escorts (R-STR-025), construction-stage looks on the map and in battle (R-STR-022: the construction_defence mission shows its own research station at 60 %, whatever was struck), captured cargo and enemy supply depots (R-STR-020), third-party convoys (R-STR-027), supply-vessel cargo capacity (R-STR-026), facility upgrades, and the design's placement: expressions (fixed rules per role instead). The manufacturing center's and research station's storage is not enforced.

docs.title: The interceptor campaign from the player's data
docs.text:
App 0.8.0, plan item 4.12. The X-COM campaign's strategy layer is built from the player's own GameSettings.ini and Interceptor.exe; the pack holds no values from them.

  • tools/interceptor_strategy.py (Python, standard library) reads the player's files and writes packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml: the tech-id table (tech_ids:) and inherit: original:GameSettings.ini/<section> references for 71 research topics, 55 items and 34 X-COM base modules — section names and ids only. Run it on the player's data and review the diff:
python3 tools/interceptor_strategy.py resources/xcom-cd/Game/ProgramFiles \
    > packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml
  • The tech-id table comes from the executable, which keeps it as 12-byte entries of a pointer to an R_ section name, a string id and the tech id; the tool finds the run of entries whose pointers lead to R_ names. Derived (the layout is inferred, not documented). With it, 67 of the 69 TechRequired values resolve to topics; eight Prereq links point to a topic of a higher Level; ids 75 and up (alien craft and installations) are not in it and are left out of conditions.
  • packs/interceptor/strategy/campaign.yaml is written by hand on top: a generated Frontier map, downlink research (research_model.rate from the three downlink module types, switching loses progress), hulls inheriting Ship_IntType1 – Ship_IntType3, missile rounds, module groups and effects, the X-COM base type, corporate funding, raids flying the original mission types, pilots and scores. economy.cost_scale: 1000 and economy.module_time: days adapt the original's units; start.money_from reads the starting treasury for the chosen difficulty. Every estimate is marked DERIVED in the file (DEV-050): the start, the map's size in systems, delivery, salvage, hull speeds, rounds, module groups and effects, the base type's cost and hub sensor range, funding and raids. Pilot rules and score points are authored values too.
  • Research has no authored unlocks: items, hulls and modules are gated by their own TechRequired through tech_ids.

It has not been play-tested. A six-month --strategy-soak with the automatic player researches 4 of the 71 topics on the starting base's one downlink (the default campaign: 12 of 14), so the research pace in particular needs the developer's judgement.

docs.title: Trying a campaign out
docs.text:
• openinterceptor --campaign <id> --strategy-soak <days> (app 0.8.0) plays the strategy layer without a window for that many days with a simple automatic player (campaign::autoplay: every base researches the first topic it can, a lab and a workshop are built when there is money, every detected contact is intercepted, battles alternate win, win, retreat) and prints one line: the date, funds, score, bases, craft, topics known, battles and messages.
  • On the strategy screen the testbed has the original's own cheats (app 0.8.1): Ctrl+M payday (a million), Ctrl+K knowitall (every topic known), Ctrl+B quickbase (every base and module under construction finished — not facilities) and Ctrl+J jump to battle from the contact chosen on the Contacts tab (User guide › Campaign).
  • Ctrl+D shows the Debug list (app 0.16.13): each arc's step and every story event with how often it has fired and whether its condition holds now — the quickest way to check a condition you have written (the logistics queries included); Fire now fires one (Story layer › Trying a story out).
  • openinterceptor --campaign <id> --strategy --chapter <n> (app 0.16.13) plays a new campaign forward headless with the automatic player until its first arc reaches step n (at most 1500 days), then opens the strategy screen there.

docs.title: The default campaign as the example
docs.text:
Perils of the Void (resources/default/strategy/) uses every section:

  • Start: 1 March 2084, 2 500 000 in funds, the Gatehouse base (guard_base) at Mercury Gate, three Comets, four pilots, rocketry known, six blasters, twelve seeker rockets, three deflector screens and three steel platings (app 0.16.1).
  • Map reach: fixed, lane travel, 1 unit = 0.001 ly; six systems — Mercury Gate, Ajax, Cinder, Vesta Reach, Tycho Drift, Nebula Haven — joined by seven lanes, and The Dark Moon, a hidden black hole far to the east, found only when a base's sensors reach it.
  • Research: labs (6 + module_count(laboratory) * 12 per hour, keep_progress); twelve topics from rocketry through heat_rays, ion_rays, saucer_hulls (requires salvaged(saucer_raid) or salvaged(scout_probe)), saucer_propulsion, disintegrators, deep_radar, shipyards, thunderbolt_design, robot_brains (salvaged(robot_raid)), victory_design and regents_engine, plus force_fields (after heat_rays) and saucer_alloys (after saucer_hulls) since app 0.16.1 — fourteen in all — unlocking beams, missiles, the force field and saucer-alloy plating, the Meteor, Thunderbolt and Victory hulls and the deep-radar and shipyard modules; and two station-only topics, theremin_shielding and pulsar_navigation (app 0.9.0, Logistics).
  • Economy: delivery 48 h, salvage 15 000 a kill; the Senate stipend every 30 days, 400000 + 60000 * bases + month_score * 200 + relation(senate) * 3000 (the standing term since app 0.10.1); cosmium sales every 7 days, 12000 * module_count(cosmium_refinery); fuel and stores 4000 * craft a week. Twelve items (four beams, three missiles, cosmium, and since app 0.16.1 two shields — deflector screen 300, force field 480 — and two armours — steel plating 180, saucer-alloy plating 380), four hulls (each with a shield and an armor slot since 0.16.1), nine module kinds (hangar, quarters, radar, deep radar, laboratory, workshop, shipyard, cosmium refinery, ray battery) and the guard_base type (template hangar, radar, laboratory; at most 6 bases, 3500 units apart).
  • Raids: Dominion scouts (intercept_scouts), saucer raids (defend_station, from day 10), colony raids (colony_defence, day 20), robot assaults (outpost_raid, day 45) and the Black Comet ambush by raiders (pocket_ambush, day 15) — each a mission of the default campaign (Missions); and since app 0.10.1 the Eclipse Engine's shipments (eclipse_shipment, chance: 0%: launched only by the plan).
  • Pilots: flying, gunnery and nerve; five ranks from cadet to commander; salary 6000, recruit fee 40 000, five recruits a month, 12 days to heal, 70 % survive; training 0.4 points and 400 a day (app 0.16.7); twelve mission scores. The Gatehouse's guard_base houses four pilots — the four you start with — so hiring needs a Crew quarters module first (app 0.16.10).
  • Evaluations (app 0.16.8): the Senate rates each month Outstanding (a month's score of 400 or more: +150 000 and praise), Satisfactory (0 or more), Poor (−300 or more: −50 000) or Unacceptable (−150 000 and a funding-cut notice).
  • Logistics: construction strikes at 12 % a day from half-built, three at most per system, flown as construction_defence, a quarter of the build time set back when let be (app 0.16.4).

The unit test campaign::tests::the_default_campaign_runs_six_months plays it for six months with an automatic player: it stays solvent, researches at least four topics, fights raids and round-trips through a save. --strategy-soak 180 with the same player (app 0.8.0) reached 12 of the 14 topics — the automatic player builds no facilities, so the two station-only topics stay unknown.

docs.title: Limits in app 0.16.14
docs.text:
• No endurance or stranding on the map; no fitting rules (fits), power draw or stock designs — fitting is best available only, and slots of kinds other than beam, missile and (since app 0.15.0) shield and armor are filled but have no effect in battle.
  • cargo_lost and cargo_captured are only recorded: captured cargo goes to no enemy depot. lose(<x>) acts only on a facility type; a base type or anything else is logged.
  • Logistics: see Not built yet — fighter pools, construction stages, depots, third-party convoys, cargo capacity, facility upgrades and placement: expressions are not built.
  • No designs, bravery, stat effects in battle, on_destroyed or repair, or the 3D base view yet. Auto-resolve counts hull classes only (not fitted items or pilots) and does not damage the player's craft (DEV-057).
  • storage limits purchases only, and as soon as any module in the campaign has it, a base without a storage module can buy nothing (an interceptor base needs its cargo module).
  • Names and descriptions in the default campaign's strategy files are plain English, not text keys, so they are not yet translatable.
  • The interceptor strategy layer is built but not play-tested, and its estimates are DERIVED (above).
  • A save made with another version of a loaded pack loads with a notice naming the versions (app 0.16.2); its rules may differ.
  • Fixed in app 0.9.0: manufacture is paid per unit as each starts (it was free), and salvaged(<raid id>) now holds after a salvage (it compared the display name).

docs.title: Text and translation
docs.text:
Player-visible strings are named by text key in the rules and scenarios, and the strings themselves live in text/<language>/*.yaml in any pack. A translation, a rename or a re-voiced campaign is then an addon with only the keys it changes. Stage 2 item 2.1 (src/content/text.rs, src/formats/langfile.rs).

# rules/ships.yaml
ships:
  comet:
    name: "@ship.comet.name"
    description: "@ship.comet.desc"

# text/en/ships.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../../../schemas/text.schema.json
text:
  ship.comet.name: "Comet"
  ship.comet.desc: "Light interceptor rocket: quick, nimble and lightly armed."

docs.title: How keys resolve
docs.text:
• A value that starts with @ is a key; anything else is used as written, so a small mod can skip text files entirely.
  • Keys work in the names of ships, objects, beams, missiles, factions and systems, ship and object descriptions, and scenario titles and descriptions; also mission, story and strategy texts, and since app 0.16.2 cutscene titles and captions (the default intro's are in text/en/cutscenes.yaml). They are resolved when the content loads.
  • Packs load in order and a later pack's key replaces an earlier one's.
  • The game reads each pack's text/<language>/ folder for the chosen language, falling back to text/en/ for a pack that has no folder for it.
  • A missing key shows as the key itself and is a --check error. --check also counts the strings loaded ("… texts").

The language is chosen with --language <code> (the folder name: en, de, fr …) or settings.yaml game: {language: …}; the default is en. Editors check text files against schemas/text.schema.json.

docs.title: The original's text, by reference
docs.text:
The interceptor pack does not copy any of the original game's text. Its text/en/original.yaml imports the original language file from the player's CD at run time:

imports:
  - {file: "original:LangFile1.txt", prefix: orig}

Every string of LangFile1.txt (3 645 on the reference CD) becomes available as @orig.<KEY> — for example @orig.S_XCOM. The original format is plain text, one string per line: a key, whitespace, then the text between the first and last double quote; ~ is a line break and lines starting with / are comments (original formats).

docs.title: A translation addon
docs.text:
# mods/default-de/pack.yaml
id: default-de
name: Perils of the Void — Deutsch
kind: addon
targets: [default]
format: 2

# mods/default-de/text/de/ships.yaml
text:
  ship.comet.name: "Komet"
  ship.comet.desc: "Leichte Abfangrakete: schnell, wendig und leicht bewaffnet."

Run with --language de: translated keys come from the addon, every other key falls back to the default campaign's English. To rename a ship without translating, put the key in the addon's text/en/ instead.

The default campaign keeps all its player-visible names and descriptions in text/en/ (factions, objects, scenarios, ships, systems, weapons).

docs.title: Validating a mod
docs.text:
openinterceptor --check --mods ~/my-mods            # original-free mods
openinterceptor --check --mods ~/my-mods --data /path/to/interceptor   # an installed copy or the CD
openinterceptor --list  --mods ~/my-mods            # what loaded: packs, playable ships, scenarios

--check loads everything without opening a window and reports:

  • every file that is not valid YAML or does not match its schema, with file, line and key path: rules/ships.yaml:12: ships.comet.max_sped: unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?), scenarios/t.yaml:2: unbalanced …, a wrong type or unit (range: 2.4kn → "unknown unit 'kn' … (use m, km)");
  • every rules definition that failed (ships.x: unknown beam 'y', bad inherit, unknown faction or kind, missing model, cockpit without image or model, a behaviour whose condition does not check, an unknown difficulty level in variants);
  • every ship model, debris model and texture that does not load, and unknown cockpit ids;
  • every cockpit image and every referenced sound that does not load — since app 0.16.2 also the radio voice and chatter clips, the music's segments and stingers, and the voice sets' faces (voices.<id>.face <file>: …);
  • every scenario that cannot spawn (with each playable ship for player: choose), including unknown object behaviours;
  • with original data, every original mesh and texture that does not decode.

It ends with a summary line and exits with status 1 if there were errors, so it can run in a script or CI. Warnings (such as a pack skipped for lack of original data) do not fail it.

The repository's own gate (scripts/check.sh) runs --check --no-original on every build, so the default campaign — the template for mods — always validates. --check checks every campaign separately, each with its own active set of packs (its parent chain, the addons that target it and their dependencies), so an addon is validated with each campaign it applies to; --check --campaign <id> checks just one.

Validation happens at the difficulty level being loaded (the default unless --difficulty is given), so a typo inside one level's variants entry is reported whichever level is played. For balance across levels, --soak <scenario> --difficulty <level> plays a battle without a window and reports the player's fate; --soak-pilot passive | ai | idle chooses who flies the player's craft (idle sits still: how long a defended object holds on its own).

In your editor. Point each file at its JSON Schema (# yaml-language-server: $schema=…, see Rulesets) and most of these mistakes are underlined as you type.

docs.title: Radio voices
docs.text:
Pilots answer on the radio, chatter lines can be spoken, and a computer voice announces the end of a mission (app 0.6.2). Voices are rules data: a mod gives its pilots voices without code, and a campaign without any recorded speech is simply quiet.

Requirement: R-MSN-007. Every key with its type: Mod file reference › voices, the ship key voice, the sounds names mission_accomplished and mission_failed, and chatter in Missions.

docs.title: Three kinds of voice
docs.text:
What Where it is set When it is heard A pilot's voice voices: {<set>: {<line>: clips}}, and voice: <set> on the ship class A wingman answers your orders and status requests; another wingman reports one lost. A spoken chatter line voice: <clip> on a mission's chatter entry With the line, when its condition first holds. The computer voice sounds: {mission_accomplished, mission_failed} When the debrief appears: mission_accomplished for a win, mission_failed for any other result (lose, draw, retreat, killed).

Since app 0.13.1 whoever speaks also appears on the cockpit's comms panel (below).

docs.title: A worked example
docs.text:
The default campaign has no recorded speech yet. Its Guard pilots answer with short synthesised radio chirps, generated by tools/default_assets/sounds.py like every other default sound:

# resources/default/rules/voices.yaml
voices:
  guard_pilot:
    acknowledge: [sounds/radio_ack.wav]
    status: [sounds/radio_status.wav]
    down: [sounds/radio_down.wav]

# resources/default/rules/ships.yaml (each of comet, meteor, thunderbolt, victory)
ships:
  comet:
    voice: guard_pilot
    # …

# resources/default/rules/flight.yaml
sounds:
  mission_accomplished: sounds/mission_win.wav
  mission_failed: sounds/mission_fail.wav

# a chatter line spoken on the radio (resources/default/missions/missions.yaml, colony_defence)
chatter:
  - {when: "time > 3s", line: "@chat.colony_inbound", voice: sounds/radio_status.wav}

docs.title: Lines a voice can say
docs.text:
Line Said by When acknowledge the first of your wingmen whose voice has the line You give a wing order: fire at will, attack my target, ignore my target, evasive, retreat. status the same You ask for a status report. down another of your wingmen (never the one lost) One of your wingmen is destroyed. engaging, kill — Reserved names, not yet said by the engine.
  • A line may list several clips; one is chosen each time, so the radio does not repeat itself.
  • Only your own wingmen speak: AI pilots with the wingman role led by you. Enemies and other friendly craft are silent.
  • A ship without voice:, or a voice without the line, says nothing; the message line still shows the order's text.
  • Line names are lower-cased; a line the engine does not know is kept and ignored, so a mod can prepare lines for later.

docs.title: Faces on the comms panel
docs.text:
App 0.13.1, plan item 6.6. While a voice clip plays, a small panel at the top left of the screen shows who is speaking: the voice set's face and name, framed in green, for the clip's length plus 0.6 s (at least 2.5 s, so a short chirp still leaves time to read the name).

Key On Meaning name a voice set The speaker's name, shown in capitals under the face (default: the set's id). Not a line. face a voice set A picture (PNG/TGA, any asset reference), or a Smacker clip (.smk) that loops while the voice speaks — also a member of an MPSRC pack, original:mfdanim.mps#<member>. Not a line. speaker a mission chatter entry The voice set that says the line (an unknown set is a load error). Without it, a chatter clip that belongs to a set's lines is that set's; otherwise the panel reads COMMS.
  • A voice set with no face (or one that fails to load) shows animated signal bars instead, so a campaign without portrait art still shows that someone is on the air. A failed face is reported once on standard error (voices.<id>: face …: …).
  • Faces load the first time their voice speaks, not with the battle: a talking-head clip is a few megabytes once decoded, and most voices never speak in a given battle.
  • A voice set may have only name and face and no lines — a speaker for chatter, such as the default campaign's Colony Control.
# resources/default/rules/voices.yaml
voices:
  guard_pilot:
    name: Guard Wing
    face: textures/portrait_guard.png
    acknowledge: [sounds/radio_ack.wav]
    status: [sounds/radio_status.wav]
    down: [sounds/radio_down.wav]
  colony_control:
    name: Colony Control
    face: textures/portrait_colony.png

# resources/default/missions/missions.yaml, colony_defence
chatter:
  - {when: "time > 3s", line: "@chat.colony_inbound", voice: sounds/radio_status.wav, speaker: colony_control}

The two portraits are generated CRT-style images, painted by tools/default_assets/textures.py.

The interceptor campaign has no faces yet: the original's 113 talking-head clips are read from mfdanim.mps (MPSRC packs), but which clip prefix (at_, as_, e_, w_) belongs to which speaker is unknown. Play a member with --video original:mfdanim.mps#<member> to look at it; once identified, a voice set's face: original:mfdanim.mps#<member> shows it.

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text:
1. Record or generate short clips (WAV; the engine reads PCM and ADPCM WAV). Radio speech reads best when band-limited (roughly 300 – 3 000 Hz) with a little noise.
  2. Put them in your pack's sounds/ folder and list them under a voice set in any rules file.
  3. Give your ship classes voice: <set>. Different factions or squadrons can have different sets.
  4. For the computer voice, set mission_accomplished and mission_failed under sounds:.
  5. Run the game and give your wingmen orders (], then 1 – 6). A clip that fails to load is reported on start-up as a sound: … line.

docs.title: Using the player's original voices
docs.text:
The interceptor campaign maps the original's computer voice through its sound cue table:

# packs/interceptor/rules/flight.yaml
sounds:
  mission_accomplished: cue:Comp_MissionAccomplished
  mission_failed: cue:Comp_MissionFailed

These clips sit six folders deep on the CD; since app 0.6.2 the original-data index reaches eight levels, so they are found in an installed copy or a CD copy alike.

The original's pilot chatter clips (the numbered FPilot1xx and MPilotxxx files) are not mapped yet: which line each clip says is not known, and a wrong mapping would have a wingman say the wrong thing. Until they are identified (see the Open note on R-MSN-007), interceptor pilots are silent. A personal addon can map them for its own use with original:<file>.wav references once the lines are known.

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
Message Cause ships.x: unknown voice 'y' voice: names a set that no voices: entry defines. missions.x.chatter: no voice set 'y' (speaker) A chatter speaker: names no voice set. sound: … on start-up A clip that could not be loaded (a wrong path, or original data missing). Since app 0.16.2 --check loads every voice and chatter clip, and every voice set's face (a picture, or a Smacker clip checked as an asset that exists): voices.<id>.face <file>: ….

Fixed in app 0.6.7

cue:<Name> references now resolve inside voices: and chatter voice: too, through the same cue table as sounds: (main 65141dc). In app 0.6.2 – 0.6.6 they did not; use the asset path (original:<file>.wav) for those versions.

docs.title: Missiles and mines
docs.text:
Every missile class chooses how it steers (guidance) and how its warhead's damage lands (damage). Both are fixed engine behaviours (src/sim/guidance.rs); everything else — speeds, turn rates, damage, decoy counts, split distances — is data. Stage 2 item 2.10. Every key: Mod file reference › missiles.

missiles:
  cluster_rocket:
    name: Cluster rocket
    guidance: cluster          # splits into six seekers near the target
    cluster: {missile: seeker, count: 6, at: 700m}
    impact_damage: 120
    proximity_damage: 50
  decoy_rocket:
    guidance: parallax         # two flares that draw enemy rockets
    decoys: 2
  permeator:
    damage: bypass_shields     # straight to armour and hull

docs.title: Guidance
docs.text:
guidance: Behaviour homing (default) Turns towards its locked target at turn_rate. dumbfire Never steers. sidestep Its own thrusters: turns twice as hard inside 600 m of the target and weaves, so it is hard to dodge. parallax Homing; at launch releases decoys (default 2) that enemy missiles may chase instead of the launcher. cloaked_wait Dropped behind the launcher; drifts to a stop and waits, hidden, until a hostile comes within trigger_range (default 800 m), then strikes. cluster Homing; near the target (cluster.at, default 600 m — or when half its fuel is spent) it splits into cluster.count (default 6) submunitions of cluster.missile, which carry on to the target. doppelganger Launches a decoy copy of the launcher's ship: a short-lived, fragile double that enemy ships and missiles may chase instead.

Decoys. A decoy is a harmless missile flying away from its launcher. An enemy missile homing on the launcher, within 2.5 km of one of its decoys, may become lured (80 % chance per second) and from then on chases the nearest decoy; when the decoys are gone it returns to its target.

Every missile still detonates on impact, on a near miss (the proximity fuse: inside proximity_radius and moving away) or when its fuel (duration) runs out. Its blast is the explosion effect it names (Looks) — size in metres, with the effect's sound — or a 25 m, 0.8 s fireball.

docs.title: Damage modes
docs.text: damage: How the warhead's damage lands normal (default) On the shield facing that was hit, then armour, then hull. bypass_shields Ignores shields: straight to armour and hull (the original's Permeator). enveloping Spread over both shield facings, as if the whole surface were hit.

docs.title: Point defence
docs.text:
A ship or object with point_defence carries automatic guns that shoot at the nearest hostile missile in range — decoys included, since the guns cannot tell them apart:

objects:
  guard_station:
    point_defence: {range: 1.2km, rate: 4, chance: 40%, energy: 3}
Key Default Meaning range 800 m Reach. rate 3 Shots per second. chance 35 % Chance a shot destroys the missile, rolled on the world's seeded generator (battles replay identically). energy 4 Energy per shot, from the ship's capacitor; no energy, no shot.

Each shot draws a tracer and plays the point_defence event sound. Point defence is fitted to the Patton, the X-COM freighter and the bases (interceptor), and to the dreadnought and the stations (default); the numbers are derived (DEV-038).

docs.title: Mines
docs.text: An object with kind: mine and a behaviour whose state does do: mine waits until a hostile is within the state's range, then detonates its first missile rack as the warhead: an area blast reaching four times the warhead's proximity_radius (at least 100 m), dealing its proximity_damage falling off linearly with distance, enveloping — and the mine is gone. See Stations and modules › Mines for a complete example.

docs.title: In the two campaigns
docs.text: Campaign Missiles interceptor X-Winder (homing), Sidestep, Permeator (bypass_shields), Fusion, Enveloping torpedo, Parallax torpedo (2 decoys), Passive Cloaking torpedo (cloaked_wait), Doppelganger — the special behaviours follow the original's descriptions (derived); the Super Avenger's testbed load carries one of each. default Seeker rockets, atomic torpedoes, cluster rockets (Thunderbolt), decoy rockets (Meteor), Dominion space-mine warheads (dominion-raid).

docs.title: The original game
docs.text:
X-COM: Interceptor (MicroProse, May 1998) combines a real-time strategy layer, where the player runs X-COM's bases on a frontier of star systems, with a 3D space-combat simulator, where the player flies one ship with AI wingmen.

This section records what the engine has to reproduce and how the data on the CD is stored. Facts carry a source and, where they were worked out rather than read, a confidence:

Mark Meaning verified Checked against the data (parsed, rendered, or counted) derived Reasoned from strings, field names or values; not yet proven in play unknown Not yet determined

Sources: the release Readme.txt, the INI files and the string tables on the CD (read as data, never reproduced here), the 1998 demo readme, a published walkthrough, Wikipedia and MobyGames. UFOpaedia's Interceptor pages were not reachable by automated tools and remain to be checked.

  • Gameplay: ships, stations, weapons, missions, strategy layer.
  • Controls: the original key, mouse and joystick layout.
  • CD layout: what every file holds.
  • Formats: how each file type is read.

docs.title: CD layout
docs.text:
What is on the CD and what the engine reads. Paths are relative to the Game/ folder of a CD copy. Sizes are approximate.

Path Holds Read by the engine Resources/xobjects1.dll, xobjects2.dll All 3D models (XMSH), their textures (XTXR) and effect sprites (XSPT), as Win32 resources Yes (Stage 1) Resources/CockpitA.dll, CockpitB.dll, CockpitC.dll Cockpit art per hull (TARG = TGA): the 640×480 frame and instrument parts Yes (Stage 1) Resources/CockpitMisc.dll Shared cockpit/HUD parts (TARG) Yes (Stage 1–2) Resources/SpritesDLL.dll ~1,700 small TGA sprites: icons, HUD elements Stage 2–5 Resources/WrappersDLL.dll Full-screen menu and strategy screens (TARG) Stage 5 ProgramFiles/Interceptor.exe The original program. Read only for its string tables (object names) Strings only ProgramFiles/xcgen.dll The original 3D engine ("XCGEN") Never run ProgramFiles/GameSettings.ini Balance data: weapons, equipment, hulls, tech tree, modules, stations, scores Yes (Stage 1) ProgramFiles/Think.ini Alien strategic AI Stage 4 ProgramFiles/soundfx.ini Sound-effect table Stage 2 ProgramFiles/MPSettings.INI, NetSettings.ini Multiplayer arenas and network settings Deferred ProgramFiles/3DObjects/*.tga Lens flares, reticles, sun and star sprites Yes (Stage 1) ProgramFiles/Animations/mfdanim.mps MFD talking heads: an MPSRC pack of 113 Smacker clips (MPSRC packs) Read since main 319a31b; shown on the comms panel (app 0.13.1) once mapped to speakers ProgramFiles/SoundFX/{SpaceFlight,Chatter,Gadgets,Wrappers}/ Sound effects and radio chatter, MS-ADPCM WAV Stage 1–3 ProgramFiles/Loops/*.wav Music loops (cruise, battle, …) as PCM WAV Stage 5 ProgramFiles/Text/*.txt UI strings, encyclopedia, names, news, credits Stage 3–5 Animations/*.smk Cut-scenes, Smacker video Stage 5 ../CD Audio/*.aiff Red Book music tracks, extracted by the player as AIFF-C Stage 5 SETUP.EXE, *.cab, DirectX/, IE4_0Setup/, EReg/ Installer, DirectX 5, Internet Explorer 4, registration Never

The CD's ProgramFiles/ folder is already an installed layout, so the engine reads the CD copy directly; no installer step is needed.

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: Two tables: what the original game used (sources: the 1998 demo readme for keys, the release Readme.txt for mouse and joystick, the game's bindable-action list), and what OpenInterceptor binds by default (from the single ACTIONS table in src/input/mod.rs, which also drives the controls menu, so the tables below cannot drift from the game). Every engine binding can be changed in the in-game Controls menu or in bindings.yaml.

docs.title: Original keyboard defaults
docs.text:
Action Key Nose down / up Up / Down arrow Turn (yaw) left / right Left / Right arrow Roll left / right NumPad 7 / NumPad 9 Throttle up / down 10 % + / - Full throttle / zero throttle Backspace / \ Reverse throttle toggle Z Afterburner (hold) Tab Hyperspace out H Next / previous target T / Y Closest enemy / target in sights R / G Fire beams / fire missile Enter / Space Beam link mode (link / full / unlink) X Next / previous / default MFD mode > / < / Esc Beam / shield charge rate F9 / F10 Shield balance S Power to shields / to weapons ; / ' Wingman menu, repeat last message ], L Wingmen: fire at will / attack my target / ignore / evasive / retreat Shift+F / A / I / E / R Views: cockpit, full forward, left, right, rear-left, rear-right F1 – F6 Chase camera auto / manual F7 / F8 Chase camera move Ins/Del, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End (zoom), NumPad 5 (reset) Pause / quit P / Alt+Q

The original also had bindable actions with no documented default: slide left/right/up/down (VCT), tractor, cloak, ECM, match speed, cycle beam, cycle missile, letterbox, include base modules.

Mouse (release readme, not remappable in the original): "Nose Down = Mouse Back, Nose Up = Mouse Up", left/right = turn, left button = beams, right button = missiles.

Joystick and rudder: stick left/right yaws and the rudder rolls; Alt+J swaps to an aircraft layout. The hat switch drives the VCT.

docs.title: OpenInterceptor defaults
docs.text: Key and button names are those used in bindings.yaml (case does not matter). Shift+F is a keyboard chord; LeftShoulder+A is a gamepad chord (hold the left shoulder, press A). Since Stage 2 every action of the original has a default except letterbox, include base modules and quit (Alt+Q), which are still unbound (they arrive with the views and the strategy layer; the pause menu quits).

docs.title: Interface
docs.text:
Action (bindings.yaml name) Label Default keys Default gamepad Notes mfd_next Next MFD page Period DpadRight the > key; pages Target, Weapons, Status, Systems, Nav mfd_prev Previous MFD page Comma DpadLeft the < key next_nav Next nav point N — engine extension (DEV-002) pause Pause P Start menu Menu Escape LeftShoulder+Start pause menu: Esc resume, R restart, K controls, L back to launcher; points to ? for the keys mouse_flight Mouse flight on/off C — toggles mouse flight (hides and confines the cursor) help Keys help (this list) Shift+Slash, Shift+F1 — the keys overlay (?): every action by group with its current keys; pauses the battle; Esc also closes it (Controls). Engine extension; F1 stays the cockpit view

Shift chords and held keys. A Shift+ chord only fires with Shift held, and a plain key only fires without it, so F and Shift+F can do different things. While Shift is held, a key that belongs to some Shift chord is ignored by the held actions bound to it: Shift+E orders the wingmen to evade without also rolling the ship on E.

Mouse flight (after C): cursor offset from the screen centre steers — moving the cursor down lowers the nose (the readme's "Nose Down = Mouse Back"), right turns right. Left button fires beams, right button fires a missile. mouse_range (pixels for full deflection, default 200) and mouse_invert (true = moving up lowers the nose) are in bindings.yaml and the controls menu.

docs.title: OpenInterceptor gamepad defaults
docs.text:
XInput layout on every platform (Platform layer). The pad has two layers: the buttons on their own, and the same buttons while the left shoulder (LB) is held. A button used as a modifier in any chord does nothing on its own while held — that is why previous target, alone among the Stage 1 pad bindings, moved to LB + RB (DEV-028).

Control On its own With LB held Left stick Yaw (X) and pitch (Y; forward = nose down) — or roll and pitch in the aircraft layout Right stick Roll (X) and vertical VCT slide (Y) — or yaw and slide in the aircraft layout Right trigger / left trigger Fire beams (hold) / fire missile Right shoulder (RB) Next target Previous target A Afterburner (hold) Hyperspace out / abort B Brake (hold) Shield balance X Match speed Tractor beam Y Chase view Cloaking device D-pad up / down Throttle up / down 10 % Power to beams / power to shields D-pad left / right Previous / next MFD page Beam charge / shield charge rate Back Beam link mode ECM Start Pause Menu Left stick click Next missile type Wingman menu Right stick click Nearest enemy Target in sights

Wingman orders other than the menu have no default pad chord: open the menu with LB + left stick click, then choose with the d-pad and A (B closes it). Stick options (in the controls menu or options: in bindings.yaml): stick_layout: space (default, as the original joystick) or aircraft (the original's Alt+J swap: left stick rolls, right stick yaws), invert_pitch, dead_zone.

In the launcher: D-pad chooses, A or Start starts, Y switches campaign, Back quits.

docs.title: The controls menu
docs.text:
Reached from the launcher (Controls (keyboard, gamepad, mouse)) and from the in-flight pause menu (Esc, then K). The model is input::editor::Editor; the screen is app::controls (Input architecture).

  • Rows are the actions, grouped as in the tables above, followed by the device settings: stick dead zone, pull back to dive, stick layout, mouse flight range and mouse invert.
  • Each action has four cells: Key, Alt key, Gamepad, Alt gamepad.
  • Enter (pad A) on a key cell waits for a key — Shift may be held for a chord; on a pad cell it waits for a button, or for a modifier held and a second button pressed (a chord). Esc cancels; a capture gives up after 8 seconds. On a setting, Enter (or Left/Right) changes it.
  • Delete or Backspace (pad X) clears the cell; D (pad Y) restores the action's defaults; Shift+D restores every default.
  • Binding a key or chord that another action used takes it away from that action; the status line names the action that lost it.
  • Up/Down (d-pad) select, Left/Right or Tab move between cells, PageUp/PageDown (LB/RB) page. Esc (pad B) leaves: the bindings apply at once and are saved to bindings.yaml.

docs.title: bindings.yaml
docs.text:
Created with every default on first run in the user data folder — macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/bindings.yaml, Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/bindings.yaml (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/), and rewritten in full whenever the controls menu saves. Anything not mentioned keeps its default. A bindings.ini from an earlier build is read once, and its bindings are saved as bindings.yaml.

keyboard:
  fire_beams: [Enter, LeftControl]    # a list: several keys per action
  tractor: [Shift+T]                  # Shift+ makes a chord
  ecm: []                             # an empty list unbinds the action
gamepad:
  hyperspace: [LeftShoulder+A]        # Modifier+Button chord
  fire_beams: [RightTrigger]
options:
  dead_zone: 0.15
  invert_pitch: false
  stick_layout: space                 # space | aircraft
  mouse_range: 200
  mouse_invert: false

Run with OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 to print the name of each key you press.

docs.title: The space simulator
docs.text: Each battle is one 3D arena. The player flies one ship; the other X-COM ships are AI wingmen. There are no in-mission navigation points: travel between systems happens on the strategy map, and the player leaves a battle by hyperspace (H, with an abortable countdown). (derived from the bindable action list and the walkthrough)

docs.title: Damage model
docs.text:
Three layers: shields (fore and aft facings), then armour, then hull. The cockpit reports per-system damage and repair (shield generator, manoeuvring, sensors, engines, hyperdrive, tractor, cloak, VCT, damage control, ECM). (derived from cockpit strings)

In OpenInterceptor (Stage 2, implemented): every fitted system has hit points; damage past the armour also strikes one system at random; systems work at full, half or no effect, can be destroyed for the battle, and are repaired worst first (faster with a damage control computer). Engines and manoeuvring both out leaves a ship disabled. The thresholds are engine values (DEV-029). Rules: Rulesets › systems; behaviour: Simulation › systems.

docs.title: Power
docs.text:
One power supply feeds beam weapons and shields. Each has a recharge setting with five steps (A–E) cycled with F9 / F10; ; and ' move power between them; S cycles shield balance (equal / full forward / full aft). Tractor, cloak and ECM also draw power; beams cannot fire while the tractor is on. (GameSettings.ini BeamRechargeRate, ShieldRechargeRate; strings)

In OpenInterceptor (Stage 2, implemented): all of the above, with the original's keys (Controls). The charge tables are the original's (verified); how many steps may be high at once — the power budget — and the start levels are engine values (DEV-024). The tractor beam tows a target and a disabled ship held at the moment of a hyperjump is captured; the cloak hides the ship from enemy sensors beyond its range and is dropped by firing (DEV-025); ECM and the cloak make homing missiles lose their target; the hyperdrive counts down and can be aborted (DEV-026). Wingmen obey all five orders of the comms menu plus a status report.

docs.title: Flight model
docs.text:
Per hull, GameSettings.ini gives roll, yaw and pitch rates, an angular damping value ("0 tight – 10 loose"), a LockSpeed ("speed at which pitch and yaw rates are zero") and a MaxSpeed. Turn rate therefore falls as speed rises: the central handling idea. Speeds are in metres per second (weapon speeds are commented in m/s). The afterburner has Boost and Cost values whose units are not yet confirmed (derived: +150 m/s for 50 energy per second).

VCT (Vector Control Thrusters) is fitted equipment that lets a ship slide sideways and vertically. Alien ships have it, which is why they out-turn missiles.

docs.title: Missile lock
docs.text: Three sensor settings give a lock time and a lock cone: A 2.5 s, B 2.0 s, C 1.5 s, with widening cones. They correspond (derived) to the three targeting systems: Standard, Emissions and AATS. Some missiles need a minimum targeting system.

docs.title: Others
docs.text: Pirates (the Kabron) and corporations fly the same three human hulls in their own colours, plus freighters. The Patton-class research cruiser is an unarmed former warship.

docs.title: Stations
docs.text: X-COM bases are modular (hub plus hangar, personnel, medical, training, cargo, communications, downlinks, sensors, shield generators, ECM, tractor, probe launch, damage control, and beam/missile defence modules). Also: corporate outposts, Ore Processing Plants (OPPs), alien bases (a hub with pods; destroy the hub to destroy the base), alien outposts and mining platforms, pirate bases, the arms dealer, the science station, the Nova science station, the alien Doomsday weapon and the portal.

docs.title: Weapons
docs.text:
Beams: Laser Cannon, Heavy Laser, Gatling Laser, Tracer Cannon (continuous), Tracking Tracer, Phase Cannon (anti-shield), and alien Plasma Cannon, Tachyon Pulser (shields and engines only, for capture) and Psi Blaster. Beams can be linked, fired fully, or unlinked (X).

Missiles: X-winder (basic heat seeker), Elerium Torpedo, Permeator (bypasses shields), Sidestep (own thrusters), Enveloping Fusion Torpedo (damage spread over the surface), Parallax Torpedo (two decoys), Passive Cloaking Torpedo (dropped; waits cloaked), Doppelganger (a decoy copy of your ship), Fusion Missile (anti-station) and the Nova Bomb.

Defensive equipment: ECM pods, cloaking device, tractor beam (0.25 km), damage control computer.

docs.title: Missions
docs.text: Defend outpost / OPP / base, defend freighter convoys, defend probe or fleet, attack alien fleet, attack freighter or tug convoys, attack alien OPP / outpost / base / probe, attack the portal fleet, patrol, and the two-part final mission. Side missions: rogue freighter, pirate raiders, defend a pirate base, the hijacked Nova Bomb prototype, the arms dealer, survey a system. After a battle: debrief and score (MissionScores). Disabled ships can be tractored home for salvage.

docs.title: Strategy layer
docs.text: A star map of the Frontier with time compression; bases and modules; research done on Earth and sent via downlinks; manufacturing and purchase; pilots; probes; money from corporate protection payments and salvage; an alien strategic AI with its own budget split between research, goods and the Doomsday project (Think.ini). The tech tree is the R_* sections of GameSettings.ini.

docs.title: Multiplayer
docs.text: Dogfight arenas (deep space, asteroids, black hole, around each station type) and team modes (MPSettings.INI, NetSettings.ini). Deferred: see deviations.

docs.title: Specification
docs.text:
The specification states how OpenInterceptor behaves, precisely enough to build and test against. It has three parts:

  • Requirements, grouped by area, each implementing one or more features;
  • the mod formats and design pages, normative for the files a modder writes;
  • the original data formats, normative for reading the player's original data (an installed copy or the CD).

Specification version 1.19.0 (257 requirements). Changes are listed in the change history.

docs.title: Reading a requirement
docs.text:
Each requirement is a heading R-<AREA>-NNN Title with:

  • the behaviour in MUST / SHOULD / MAY terms and a one-line rationale;
  • Implements: the feature(s) it serves;
  • Status: implemented or planned;
  • Verified by: unit-test names (module::test_name) and manual test IDs (MT-…) where implemented;
  • Reverse-engineered: yes when it was written from the existing code rather than ahead of it;
  • See: the normative format page or architecture page;
  • an Open box where the material is thin and a decision is still needed.

Requirement IDs are permanent. In the Rapid Prototyping workflow the specification moves before the code: a request becomes a feature, then requirements, then issues.

docs.title: Console protocol
docs.text:
Status: version 1 implemented (C1, app 0.4.0; power with C2 in 0.4.11; model with C3 in 0.4.14; contacts, event and target with C4 in 0.4.15; theme with C2b in 0.5.0). Only the serial transport (C5) is still planned. The messages the game and a control console exchange. The console is the tablet page served by the game (F-CON-004); later, a physical panel over USB serial (F-CON-007). Requirements: R-CON-009 – R-CON-021. How it is built: Remote console.

Protocol version 1 below is as built (src/remote/protocol.rs): from the console hello, action, throttle, power, target and ping; from the game welcome, denied, catalogue, telemetry, theme, model, contacts and event. The additions since C1 kept the version at 1: each is a new message type, and a page that does not know a type ignores it.

docs.title: Transport
docs.text:
• Each message is one JSON object with a type field, sent as one WebSocket text frame.
  • WebSocket (first transport, built): the game serves the console page (/, /console.js, /console.css and /keepawake.mp4, built into the program; files honour HTTP Range requests with 206 Partial Content since app 0.4.8) and the socket (a WebSocket upgrade on any path; the page uses /ws) over HTTP/1.1 on port 8765 by default (console.port in settings.yaml, --console-port). The console is off by default (decision D2): --console or console.enabled turns it on.
  • Local network only: connections from addresses that are not private, link-local, unique-local or loopback are dropped without an answer.
  • Pairing from the address (app 0.4.7): /?code=123456 pairs straight away with that code, for a future QR code shown by the game.
  • USB serial (later, for an Arduino panel): the same messages, one per line. The protocol never depends on the transport.

docs.title: Session
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant C as Console
    participant G as Game
    C->>G: hello {code}
    alt wrong code
        G->>C: denied {reason}
        Note over C,G: the third wrong code closes the connection
    else right code
        G->>C: welcome {version} (server, at once)
        alt no battle running (launcher)
            G->>C: theme {vars} (the campaign's base)
            G->>C: catalogue (every action available)
            loop twice a second
                G-->>C: telemetry {alive: false, state: "launcher"}
            end
        else in a battle
            G->>C: welcome {version, campaign} (flight screen)
            G->>C: catalogue {groups, actions}, theme {vars}
            loop while paired
                G-->>C: telemetry (20 Hz)
                G-->>C: contacts (5 Hz)
                G-->>C: model (when the target's class changes)
                G-->>C: event {text} (each new message-log line)
                G-->>C: catalogue, theme (again when the craft class changes)
                C->>G: action {name, value}
                C->>G: throttle {value} · power {beam, shield, balance}
                C->>G: target {id}
            end
        end
    end

Since app 0.4.7 (main c42d773) the server answers a right code itself: its connection thread sends welcome {version} at once, so the page knows it is paired on any screen. Before, only the flight screen answered, and a tablet paired from the launcher waited for ever. During a battle the flight screen also sends welcome {version, campaign}. The page switches from the pairing screen to the console on welcome (not on catalogue).

Until a console has paired, every message other than hello is ignored, as is any message that does not decode. When the connection closes, everything that console was holding is released.

docs.title: Console → game
Game → console
docs.text:
Message When Fields welcome Right code: from the server at once with version only; during a battle the flight screen sends it again with campaign version (1), campaign (the active campaign's id, empty if none; flight screen only). denied Wrong code reason ("wrong pairing code"). catalogue After welcome; again whenever the player's craft class changes. Outside a battle (the launcher) a catalogue with every action marked available, since there is no craft yet; the battle sends the real one when it starts groups: [{id, title}] in menu order (flight, throttle, weapons, targeting, power, wingmen, views, camera, interface). actions: [{name, group, label, description, kind, available}] for every action of the catalogue (R-CON-007): name as in bindings.yaml, group one of the ids above, label the display name (the button text), description one player-facing sentence on what the action does (since app 0.15.1; the page shows it under the label), kind "hold" or "tap", available false when the craft has no equipment for it (R-CON-019). telemetry 20 Hz while paired in a battle; twice a second outside one See below. Outside a battle: {alive: false, state} only, with state the screen ("launcher"). theme On pairing (the campaign's base theme, from the launcher); in a battle with each catalogue (the base with the craft's cockpit layered on) vars: an object of CSS custom properties: --bg, --panel, --line, --ink, --dim, --hot, --warn, --danger, --off as #rrggbb; --font (a CSS font list); --corner (e.g. "2px"). Only what the theme sets is sent; vars: {} means the page's own look. See Theme. model When the target's class changes, and again when a tablet pairs name (class name), groups: [{color, positions, indices, uvs?, texture?}]. See Model. contacts 5 Hz while paired in a battle range (the radar range, metres), list: [{id, name, relation, station, target, pos, vel}]. See Contacts. event Each new line of the pilot's message log text: the line as the message line shows it.

Availability. An action is unavailable when the current craft lacks what it needs: cloak, ecm and tractor need that system fitted; the four VCT slides need a class with vct; missile firing and cycling need missiles aboard; beam firing, link cycling, beam charge and power-to-beams need a class with beams. Every other action is always available. Unavailable actions are still listed, so the console shows them disabled, never hidden.

telemetry fields. Fractions are 0 – 1; distances in metres, speeds in m/s.

Field Type Meaning time number Mission time, seconds. alive bool False once the player's craft is gone, or when no battle is running; then no other field is sent except state. hits, hull_hits number Running counts, since the battle began, of weapon hits on the player's craft and of those that struck the hull (app 0.4.9). The page plays a brief static effect when either rises: lighter for a shield hit, stronger for a hull hit (R-CON-024). state string Only when no battle is running: the screen the game is on ("launcher"). The page shows Not flying (launcher); alive: false without state is shown as DESTROYED. craft string The craft class's name. velocity [x, y, z] Velocity in the craft's body axes: x right, y up, z forward (so z is forward speed and x, y are the drift). throttle number Throttle position, 0 – 1. hull, energy number Fractions of the class's maximum. shields [fore, aft] Shield fractions. power [beam, shield, levels, used, budget] The power distribution, as on the HUD's power readout. link string The beam link mode, lower case. afterburner, braking bool Afterburner lit; brake held. missile {name, count} The selected missile rack; absent when the craft carries none. systems [{kind, health, destroyed, on}] Each fitted system: its kind (lower case), health fraction, destroyed, switched on. target object Absent without a target. name (class name), relation (friendly, hostile, neutral), protect (the target is protected by the player's faction), distance, closing (closing speed, positive while the gap shrinks), hull, shields [fore, aft], and rotation [x, y, z, w]: the target's orientation in the player's body axes (the conjugate of the player's rotation times the target's), for the target viewport (R-CON-015). 
{"type": "telemetry", "time": 12.5, "alive": true, "craft": "…", "velocity": [20, 0, 100],
 "throttle": 0.6, "hull": 1, "energy": 0.8, "shields": [1, 0.7], "power": [2, 2, 4, 4, 6],
 "link": "…", "afterburner": false, "braking": false, "missile": {"name": "…", "count": 4},
 "systems": [{"kind": "cloak", "health": 1, "destroyed": false, "on": false}],
 "target": {"name": "…", "relation": "hostile", "protect": false, "distance": 1000,
            "closing": 35, "hull": 0.5, "shields": [0, 1], "rotation": [0, 0.707, 0, 0.707]}}

Values in the examples are illustrative.

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
Built by protocol::theme from a rules::ThemeLayer (R-CON-020): the campaign's console.theme, with console.cockpits.<id> layered on by ConsoleTheme::for_cockpit while flying a craft with that cockpit. Colours are written as #rrggbb from the rules' RGB 0 – 1. The page sets each variable on the document root and removes variables a later theme leaves out, so they fall back to console.css. The keys a pack writes are on Console themes.

{"type": "theme", "vars": {"--bg": "#0d0a14", "--line": "#c9a34a", "--hot": "#ffcf59",
 "--font": "Futura, 'Avenir Next', sans-serif", "--corner": "2px"}}

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
For the target viewport (R-CON-015), built by protocol::model:

  • the most detailed level of detail with at most 3000 triangles (protocol::MODEL_TRIANGLE_BUDGET), or the coarsest if every level is larger;
  • normalised to radius 1 (positions divided by the model's radius, rounded to 3 decimals);
  • one entry per material group: positions (flat [x, y, z, …], only the vertices that group uses, renumbered from 0), indices (triangles, three per face) and color (RGB 0 – 1): a textured group's colour is its texture's average (protocol::average_color, transparent pixels ignored), an untextured group's is its vertex colour;
  • a textured group also carries texture, its image shrunk to at most 128 pixels a side and sent as a PNG data:image/png;base64,… URL (protocol::texture_url, written by the in-crate formats::png), and uvs (flat [u, v, …], two per vertex, in the same order as positions) — app 0.6.7. The page shows color until the image has loaded. Untextured groups have neither key.

Axes are the model's own (x right, y up, −z ahead, as in the engine); the page turns it by telemetry.target.rotation. The flight screen builds each class's message once and caches it. A model that fails to load gives {type: "model", name} with no groups.

{"type": "model", "name": "…", "groups": [{"color": [0.6, 0.75, 0.6],
 "positions": [0, 0, -1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 0.5, 0, 0.5], "indices": [0, 2, 1]}]}

docs.title: Contacts
docs.text:
For the map (R-CON-014, R-CON-016), built by protocol::contacts: every live craft on the player's radar (sim::systems::on_radar), the player excluded.

Field Type Meaning id string "slot:generation" of the ship handle; send it back in target. A reused slot gets a new generation, so a stale id never targets a newcomer. name string The class name. relation string friendly, hostile, neutral, or objective (a craft the player's faction protects). station bool A static object (station, base, module). target bool The player's current target. pos [x, y, z] Position relative to the player, metres, in the player's own axes: x right, y up, z ahead. vel [x, y, z] Velocity relative to the player, m/s, in the same axes.

range at the top level is the radar range (flight.radar_range), which the map's rings use. Because positions are already in the player's axes, the page needs no orientation to draw the map around the player.

{"type": "contacts", "range": 6000, "list": [
 {"id": "3:0", "name": "…", "relation": "hostile", "station": false, "target": true,
  "pos": [-400, 300, 2100], "vel": [40, 0, -90]}]}
{"type": "event", "text": "…"}

docs.title: Keeping the tablet awake
docs.text:
Not a message: the page itself keeps the tablet's screen on while it is open (app 0.4.8, main f1c8be8, R-CON-022).

  1. The Screen Wake Lock API (navigator.wakeLock.request("screen")) where the browser allows it. Safari allows it only on secure (https) pages, so it does not apply to an iPad on the plain-http console.
  2. Otherwise a tiny black clip, /keepawake.mp4 (2 KB, generated by tools/console_assets/make_keepawake.swift with AVFoundation; the project's own output), played muted, inline and looping, out of sight: browsers do not let the screen sleep while a video plays. iOS Safari plays video only from a server that honours Range requests, hence 206 Partial Content.

It starts on the pairing tap, again on any tap until it runs (iOS needs a user gesture for media), and again whenever the page becomes visible (the browser releases both when it is hidden). The telemetry grid's Tablet cell shows screen kept awake, screen kept awake (wake lock) or tap the screen to keep it awake.

docs.title: Still planned
docs.text:
• The serial transport (C5, R-CON-017): the same messages, one per line, for an Arduino panel.
  • Nav points in contacts (the map shows craft only).

docs.title: Open
docs.text:
• The QR code that would carry ?code= (the page accepts it since app 0.4.7; the game does not show one yet).
  • The pairing code's lifetime: in version 1 it is chosen when the game starts and lasts for the run. Whether it should change after a pairing, or time out, is open.
  • A client name and protocol version in hello (version 1 sends neither); how a version mismatch is reported.
  • Line framing and the message subset for the serial transport.
  • Theme images (frames, backgrounds): version 1 themes are colours, a font and a corner radius.

Status: design check, 2026-11-10. The second table goes the other way: features the default campaign adds, and what they mean for interceptor. A row with no construct would be a gap in the format. docs.title: Open items (data the original keeps in code)
docs.text:
These need the strategy guide, careful play of the original, or both; each becomes a work item in Stage 5 with its source recorded (verified/derived) in the mod's comments:

  1. The meaning of each MissionScores index (values are data, indices are code).
  2. Exact squadron compositions per mission type, tech level and difficulty (the guide's tables are partly illegible).
  3. Star count, planet size and sensor-radius tables for map generation.
  4. Salary, recruitment and psionics-by-rank modifiers.
  5. The alien tech-level cost mapping and the Doomsday cost/time columns.
  6. Station hit-point chart meaning (HP1..HP4, SD).
  7. The three-ring effect meshes (1ASH* etc.): shield flash or jump effect.
  8. Whether overlay-face low bits on station hubs are state groups.

Each is a data question with a reasonable fallback (the guide's legible values, or a documented estimate marked derived), so none blocks the format or the stages.
