Force Rule Effect Drag F = −½ · ρ · Cd · A · v·|v| (ρ = air_density, per-ship drag_area = Cd·A) A ship slows down without thrust; top speed is where thrust equals drag (much lower than in space) Gravity gravity along −Y A ship must hold altitude with lift or thrust; a stalled or disabled ship falls and crashes Lift lift (per ship) × ρ × v² × angle of attack, perpendicular to velocity; zero for ships without wings Winged craft bank to turn and glide; wingless saucers hover on thrust (hover: true with a power cost) Ground Collision with the heightfield; impact_speed below which a ship lands instead of crashing Landing pads, crashes, terrain masking Ceiling Above ceiling the battle ends for that ship (escape to orbit = retreat) Replaces hyperspace-out

Ship rules gain drag_area, lift, hover, atmosphere_max_speed (a cap) and atmospheric: false for craft that cannot enter an atmosphere (the mission screen hides them). Missiles get drag_area too. flight: {model: newtonian} (or assisted; implemented) stays the default for space; an environment's physics overrides it for its battles.

As built (app 0.6.0)

The forces were simplified so that each is set by one number a modder can reason about (R-FLT-011):

  • drag a = −k·ρ·|v|·v with k = acceleration / atmosphere_max_speed² — full thrust balances drag at atmosphere_max_speed (default 60 % of max_speed); there is no drag_area, and missiles feel no drag;
  • lift g·ρ·(forward speed / lift)² along the craft's up, capped at 2g, where lift is the speed at which the wings carry the weight (default 120 m/s for fighters, 0 otherwise); no angle-of-attack term;
  • hover: true cancels gravity, with no power cost yet;
  • a landing is any touchdown at no more than 25 m/s into the ground while upright (a fixed LANDING_SPEED, not a per-ship impact_speed); a crash does (speed)² × 0.5 damage;
  • above ceiling the craft leaves the battle (Departed, "LEFT THE ATMOSPHERE");
  • atmospheric is read but not yet acted on (the mission screen comes with Stage 4).

docs.title: Ground installations
docs.text:
Ground bases are object classes with kind: ground (static, placed on the terrain at a surface point: position: {surface: [12km, 4km]}) and the usual model sets, modules, turrets (a behaviour with do: turret and ground arcs) and damage. Surface anti-air turrets, shield domes, landing pads (ships launch from them as an arrival), and buildings that are objectives (roles: {colony: {class: mining_colony}}) all use existing constructs.

As built (app 0.6.1)

kind: ground exists: such an object is static and is set down on the terrain wherever it is placed (at the ground height plus a quarter of its collision radius); the environment is set before anything is placed. Positions are ordinary [x, y, z] — the y is replaced — rather than position: {surface: …}. Anti-air is a kind: ground class with beams, a turret_arc and a turret behaviour (the default campaign's dominion_flak). Shield domes and landing pads as arrivals are not built.

Mission types for the surface follow the same format: Defend colony (surface), Raid research outpost, Ground strike, Rescue at the crash site, with location: surface and an atmospheric environment chosen from the map body (environment: body).

docs.title: Campaign events: events: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
Events are how story beats, side missions and reactions happen. An event is a condition plus an action list, checked by the campaign clock.

As built (app 0.10.0)

Built: when, chance, check, do, choices, once, cooldown, and arc: <id> (the step is the event's place in the arc's steps). The actions are the fourteen of script::action::EVENT_ACTIONS — message, news, set_flag, clear_flag, money, score, relation, research, mission (offer now, accept or decline), raid, plan, aggression, victory, defeat — and since app 0.11.1 – 0.13.0 three for presentation, card (a title card), video and play_cutscene. Not built: start_mission with a place and an expiry, offer_mission, reward:, unlock_research, map changes, a priority on message, a chance per difficulty. Keys: Story layer › events; DEV-051.

events:
  alien_message_2:
    arc: {id: doomsday, step: 2}
    when: >
      date >= 2067-03-01 and flag(alien_message_1) and captured(structural_component)
      and research(wraith_examination)
    chance:                                 # per check; empty = certain once `when` holds
    check: daily                            # daily, weekly, monthly, after_battle, on_research
    do:
      - "message(@msg.alien_2, high)"
      - "unlock_research(alien_message_2)"
      - "set_flag(alien_message_2)"
    once: true
  rogue_freighter:
    when: "month <= 6 and not flag(rogue_freighter_done)"
    chance: 15%
    check: monthly
    do: ["start_mission(rogue_freighter, random_outpost_system, 504h)"]   # expires in 21 days
    reward: {money: 250000}                 # applied by the mission's win outcome
Key Meaning when, chance, check When the event may fire: a condition, a probability per check (one value per difficulty allowed), and how often it is checked. do Actions: messages and news, missions (start_mission, offer_mission with accept/refuse), unlocks, flags and counters, money, relation changes, map changes (spawn or remove bases and outposts, reveal locations), plan changes, arc steps, endings. choices Choices for the player (- {text: "@choice.pay", do: ["add(money, -200000)", "set_flag(paid)"]}) — a dialogue box with buttons. arc, once, cooldown Story ordering, single-shot, minimum time between firings.

The original's side missions (smarms, smnova, smraiders, smrecon, smrescue, smrogue: discrete triggers, confirmed by its cheat codes) are each one event plus one mission type; the alien messages, Doomsday shipments, MacArthur and final mission are the doomsday arc.

As built (app 0.9.1 – 0.9.2): backdrops and convoys

Besides planet, an environment's backdrop may be a nebula (color, second_color, density, seed). Convoy battles are built as missions with cargo: the mission key cargo: <role>, the battle query cargo(role), roles with escort: <role>, waves with every:, and the towable/cargo object keys (Missions).

docs.title: Squadrons and flight plans
docs.text: The strategy layer moves squadrons (a group of craft with a size class Small 1–3, Medium 4–6, Large 7–9, Huge 10+), convoys and probes on flight plans across the map. When a squadron's plan meets a player asset or player squadron, or a request is raised, a mission of the matching type is generated, with the squadron filling its role. squadrons: {<id>: …} defines compositions per tech level and difficulty; convoys: {<id>: …} defines freighters, tugs and escorts.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here. Logistics wording aligned with the revised decisions (survey ships; supply-convoy attack point at launch) 1.11.0 2026-11-11 Marked as built: hazards (app 0.5.1) with their explicit keys; environment, environments, terrains and atmospheric flight (0.6.0) with the simplified forces; ground installations (0.6.1). Not built: location/backdrop from the map, speed_of_sound, weather, terrain textures and scattered objects, shield domes, landing-pad arrivals 1.15.0 2026-11-11 As-built notes: campaign events (app 0.10.0) — what is built and what is not; the nebula backdrop and convoy-battle keys (app 0.9.1 – 0.9.2); the format itself unchanged 1.16.0 2026-11-11 As-built note on campaign events: the presentation actions card, video, play_cutscene (app 0.11.1 – 0.13.0); the format itself unchanged

docs.title: Format: space objects and models
docs.text:
Status: design. Extends the ships: and objects: sections of the rules files (rulesets); their existing keys keep their meaning. Mod files are YAML (mod format 2); the examples below use the same form for the planned sections.

Every thing in space — fighter, freighter, station, module, probe, mine, asteroid, debris — is an object class that names a model set. Splitting the two lets several classes share one look (the pirate and the corporate Lightning differ in rules and colours, not geometry), and lets a remaster replace a look without touching a class.

docs.title: Model sets: modelsets: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
A model set is everything needed to draw one object in every state it can be in.

modelsets:
  lightning:
    intact: original:INTTYPEA            # the normal model (all its LODs)
    scale: 1
    textures: {hull: original:inttop}    # optional: retexture one texture slot by name
    # Damage: texture swaps (and optional model swaps) applied as hull integrity falls.
    # (Example: the original has no ship damage textures; mods may add them.)
    damage:
      - {below: 66%, textures: {inttop: inttop_scorched}}
      - {below: 33%, textures: {inttop: inttop_burnt}}
    # Destruction: the model is replaced by debris pieces that fly apart.
    debris: lightning
    destroyed_effect: explosion_medium
    engine_glow: attachments             # or a list of points
Key Meaning intact Model reference: original:<mesh>, a pack OBJ, or another model set (modelsets.<id>). Required. scale Model units → metres. textures: {<slot>: <texture>} Replace the texture a model names <slot> for this set only (faction colours, variants). damage: [{below:, textures: {a: b}, model:}] Below that hull fraction, swap textures (and optionally the model). Levels are checked from the lowest below up; swaps are cumulative from the first level onwards. debris A debris set (below) used when the object is destroyed. destroyed_effect Effect played on destruction (explosion size, sound, flash, shock wave). states Named construction or condition states (stations; below). attach: {<slot>: <model>} Models mounted at the model's attachment points (below). engine_glow attachments (rear-facing attachment points, the Stage 1 rule) or explicit points. lights Blinking/marker lights: {at: [x, y, z], color: [r, g, b], period: 1s}.

docs.title: Debris: debris: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
When an object is destroyed its model is removed and these pieces are spawned at the object's position and orientation, then fly apart and tumble. Debris is also a target type (salvage, collisions) and fades out after its lifetime.

debris:
  lightning:
    pieces:
      - {model: original:X-SHIPA1, offset: [0, 0, -2], speed: [20, 60], spin: [30, 120], life: 20s}
      - {model: original:X-SHIPA2, offset: [1, 0, 1]}
      - {model: original:X-SHIPA3}
      - {model: original:X-SHIPA4}
    chunks: {models: [original:CHUNK1, original:CHUNK2], count: 6, speed: [40, 120]}   # generic rubble
    salvage: human_light_hull       # optional: what tractoring a piece yields
Key Meaning pieces: [{model:, offset:, speed:, spin:, life:}] A named piece placed at offset (model space; default: its own centre), thrown outwards from the object centre (plus the object's velocity) at a random speed in the range, tumbling at a random rate (degrees/second). Ranges are [min, max]; seeded from the battle seed, so replays are deterministic. chunks: {models:, count:, speed:} Generic pieces scattered randomly. salvage Salvage definition if pieces can be tractored.

The original program has exactly this, hard-coded: a wreck table of 28 named sets of up to five chunk meshes (sets with fewer chunks repeat the first), for example UFOARandom → a-shipa2…6, UFOShade → ashadc1…5, XCOMARandom → x-shipa1…4, XCOMBaseRandom → xbasech1,2,3,5,6, XCOMPatton → xkpat1,2,3,5,6, plus generic rubble chunk1…6, chunkf1…2, trichunk, alien corpse parts floating in alien wrecks, and the shokwave shock wave mesh. The interceptor mod writes the table as 28 debris: entries (analysis). The "Random" in the set names is honoured with pick: [3, 5] (choose that many pieces at random from the list).

docs.title: Construction and condition states (stations)
docs.text:
A station looks different depending on what has been built — and in the original each X-COM module has three textures: normal, under construction and destroyed (x-hanger, hang-const, xhngr-brn), alien modules two (normal and -b). States express this:

modelsets:
  xcom_hangar:
    intact: original:XMMOD02             # one generic module mesh, retextured per type
    textures: {xmmod: original:x-hanger}
    states:
      building: {textures: {xmmod: hang-const}}
      destroyed: {textures: {xmmod: xhngr-brn}}

Mesh-swapping stages (planned with logistics). A state may also replace the model and name its own debris (states: {build_25: {model: models/rig_build25.obj, debris: rig_build25}}) — implemented in Stage 2 — so a facility shows distinct construction stages (scaffold, frame, cladding); the strategy layer will choose the stage from build progress.

The engine sets building while a module's build time runs, and destroyed (a module wreck stays attached, unlike a destroyed ship) when its hit points reach zero; damaged-but-working is shown with the HUD's base-view overlay, as in the original.

The hub itself has slots for modules (each with a size requirement: the original refuses "module [size 2] to position 7 [size requirement 1]") and may show or hide overlay faces by condition:

modelsets:
  xcom_base:
    intact: original:XBASE7
    # Attachment slots (the mesh's manipulators) and what each can hold
    slots:
      dock_1: {attachment: 0, size: 2}
      dock_2: {attachment: 1, size: 2}
      turret_1: {attachment: 33, size: 0}
    # Overlay faces of the hub that depend on state (the XMSH overlay flag, low bits = group)
    overlay_groups:
      21: {visible_when: "module(landing_pad)"}
      29: {visible_when: "not module(landing_pad)"}
  • Slots are named attachment points (the original's manipulators; for OBJ models, empties named slot_<name> — see below) with a size class (0 small, 1 medium, 2 large, 3 special, the original's SizeClass). A module class says its size and which model it shows.
  • Overlay groups use the overlay faces decoded in Stage 1 (flag 0x2000_0000) whose low bits may number a group (unconfirmed; XMSH). A model set can show or hide each group on a condition. If the low bits turn out not to be groups, the same key accepts a face list (faces: [4, 5, 6]), authored with the viewer's face selection.
  • visible_when takes a condition.

docs.title: Model references in OBJ
docs.text: For modders' own models: an OBJ object or group named slot_<name> is not drawn; its centre and orientation (first face's normal = forward) become attachment point <name>. Groups named overlay_<group> are overlay groups. Groups named lod<n>_... belong to LOD n (with lod_distances: [..] in the model set). One OBJ can therefore carry LODs, slots and overlays.

docs.title: Object classes
docs.text:
The existing keys stay. Planned keys (those already implemented are marked):

Key Meaning modelset The model set (replaces model; model: <ref> remains as shorthand for a model set with only intact). class Strategic class used by the campaign: interceptor, freighter, tug, probe, mine, outpost, opp, base, module… (free list, defined in the campaign ruleset). mounts Mount points by type: {beam: 4, missile: 3, special: 4} (the original's three mount kinds). loadout Default equipment: {beam: [laser, laser], missile: {xwinder: 4}, special: [ecm]}. systems Damageable systems (implemented: systems: [...] replaces the default list, systems+: [ecm] adds; hit points come from the systems: section). behaviour Behaviour id (behaviours), implemented; per difficulty with variants: {<level>: {behaviour: …}} (implemented). power Power plant output and the beam/shield split rules (the global power: section is implemented). cost, build_time, upkeep Strategy values (see strategy). capturable, salvage Whether a disabled object can be tractored (capturable implemented), and what it yields. cargo What a freighter carries (resources and amounts) for the economy. crew Pilot slots: {pilot: 1} for fighters; capital ships may have more. launches Craft this object can launch (freighter drones, base defence craft, probe launchers).

docs.title: Modules: modules: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
A station module is an object class too (it can be shot and destroyed) plus strategy effects.

modules:
  hangar:
    name: "@module.hangar"
    modelset: xcom_hangar
    fits: {slot: "dock_*"}         # which slots it may occupy
    cost: 250000
    build_time: 10day
    upkeep: {amount: 5000, per: month}
    effects: {hangar_capacity: +4}
    requires: "research(base_modules)"

effects are named campaign variables changed while the module exists (see strategy).

docs.title: Effects: effects: {<id>: …}
docs.text: Explosions, shock waves, shield flashes, engine trails, beam impacts: sprite or particle definitions using images (the original XSPT sprites, or pack PNG sequences), size, duration, light and sound. Stage 2 implements the set the original uses; mods add their own.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: Format: strategy layer
docs.text:
Status: design; implemented in Stage 4 (map, economy, research, bases, ships, pilots) and Stage 5 (relations, strategist). Files in strategy/*.yaml (YAML, the mod format of the implemented rules files). Numbers that vary by difficulty take one value per level ({per_level: [..]}, implemented); any quantity the original computes with a formula takes an expression in the condition language (arithmetic over campaign queries), so the formulas are data too.

As built (app 0.7.0 – 0.7.3)

The built part of this design, with every key, default and error, is on the modding page Strategy layer. Built: start (one start; DEV-046), maps (fixed and generated; free and lane travel), star_classes, research and research_model (mode, rate, switching), items (plus rounds), hulls, base_modules, base_types (limits, template, max_distance in place of a placement expression), raids (the built stand-in for squadrons and the strategist), incomes, expenses, pilots (stats, ranks by experience, salary, recruit fee, pool, healing, survival), scores, flags and economy (delivery, salvage_per_kill), all expressions in the campaign context (script::campaign). Not built yet: bodies, probes and sensors as items, factions and relations, evaluations, resources, markets and factories as sections, storage, salvage tables, capture, designs, fitting rules, training, bravery, injuries by health, strategists. Several keys are simpler than designed (a number where an expression is shown, upkeep as a plain monthly number); see Deviations DEV-046.

As built (app 0.8.0 – 0.9.0)

For the original's own data (app 0.8.0): tech_ids: {<number>: <topic>} translates the numeric Prereq1..3 and TechRequired/TechRequired2 read by inheritance into research(x) prerequisites; economy.cost_scale (the original's money is in thousands) and economy.module_time: days; start.money_from: original:<file>/<key> reads the starting money from the difficulty level's section. Resources and the logistics sections (app 0.9.0): resources, components, recipes, facility_types, research_sites, logistics, and deposits, features, hull components, topic lab, site, start_cost.

docs.title: maps: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
maps:
  frontier:                          # interceptor: generated like the original
    kind: generated
    size: [60000, 60000]             # map units (2D)
    unit_ly: 0.000167                # map unit → light years (so 1.5 ly ≈ 9000 units)
    systems: [30, 45]                # or a table rolled on d100
    star_classes: table:spectral     # d100 table → star class
    bodies: {count: [0, 5], slots: 5, table: bodies}
    names: text:star_names           # pool
    guarantee: "black_hole >= 1"     # the gateway
    travel: free                     # free hyperjumps, or lanes
    hidden: [black_hole]             # not drawn until found
    seed: random                     # or a number for a fixed campaign
  reach:                             # default campaign: a fixed, hand-made map
    kind: fixed
    systems:
      mercury_gate: {pos: [1200, 800], class: yellow, bodies: [planet:rocky, belt:thin]}
      ajax: {pos: [4300, 1500], class: red_dwarf, bodies: [planet:ice, belt:rich]}
    lanes:
      - {between: [mercury_gate, ajax], length: 48h}
    travel: lanes
Construct Covers star_classes: {<id>: …} Visual (sun model, colour, size), d100 range, mineral richness table, hazard (black hole: hidden, swallows probes, battle gravity). bodies: {<id>: …} Planet, moon or asteroid field: size, richness, the backdrop model used in battles in its orbit, what can be built there (OPP, outpost). travel free (any point, range-limited: the original) or lanes (only along lanes: simpler, used by the default campaign). locations: {<kind>: …} Location kinds a mission can happen at: deep_space, system, orbit, base, outpost, opp, gateway, pocket (a separate battle space reached only by story).

docs.title: Sensors and probes
docs.text:
Survey ships (a separate craft from supply ships; range: the launching station's radar range) that report a system's deposits and facility suitability are designed on Logistics. Battle probes (probe: {sensors, jamming}) are implemented (Stations, modules and probes).

sensor keys on bases, ships, outposts and probes give a map range; contacts are visible inside the union of ranges. Probes are object classes with map_range, lifetime, movement (station, roam) and effects (reveal, jam: downlink, hunt).

docs.title: factions: {<id>: …} (extended)
docs.text:
factions:
  corporate:
    name: "@faction.corporate"
    kind: patron                 # player, rival, patron, independent, hostile
    relation: {xcom: funding}    # relation is a per-holding funding share
    funding: {range: [0%, 95%], start: 50%}
    leaves: "funding <= 0%"      # holding lost for good
    names: text:corporations
kind Meaning Interceptor Default campaign player The player X-COM Interplanetary Guard rival A strategic opponent with its own economy, research, plan and AI Aliens Umbral Dominion patron Funds the player; relation per holding or overall Corporations Solar Senate independent Has a relation score; can trade, help or turn hostile Arms dealer, GSC Nebula Cartel, Belt Prospectors hostile Attacks everyone; can be bribed or destroyed by events Kabron pirates, Cult of Sirius Black Comet raiders

Relations are numbers (−100…100) or funding shares, changed by actions (add(relation(x), n)) and by evaluations. Conditions read them.

docs.title: Dynamic relations (optional per campaign)
docs.text:
The original's relations are fixed except for corporate funding. A campaign may instead switch on dynamic relations: every pair of factions has a standing that drifts with what happens, and the standing decides who supports whom and who fights whom, so the player's actions decide their allies over time.

relations:
  dynamic: true                         # false = hostility only from factions' hostile lists
  scale: [-100, 100]
  stances: {hostile: -40, wary: -10, neutral: 20, friendly: 60, allied: 100}   # upper bounds
  # Initial standings (unlisted pairs start at 0); symmetric unless written both ways
  start: {guard-cartel: -10, guard-senate: 30, cartel-senate: -50, "dominion-*": -100}

# How events move standings: who did what to whom
relation_rules:
  defended:
    on: "battle_won and ally_of_victim(asset_owner)"     # you saved their base, convoy or ship
    change: {asset_owner: {base: 15, convoy: 6, ship: 2, other: 8}}
    also: {enemies_of_asset_owner: -3}
  attacked:
    on: "destroyed_by_player or captured_by_player"
    change: {owner: {base: -40, outpost: -25, freighter: -10, fighter: -3, other: -10}}
    also: {enemies_of_owner: 4}
  refused:
    on: defence_request_refused
    change: {requester: -6}
  drift:
    every: 720h                         # a month
    change: {towards: 0, by: 2}         # old grudges fade
Stance Effect in battle Effect in strategy allied Their ships fight on your side; you may call for help They share sensor data, sell at a discount, may fund you, ask you to defend them friendly Their ships help if attacked nearby Trade; occasional requests neutral Ignore you unless attacked Trade at normal prices wary Ignore you; return fire Refuse to trade; no requests hostile Attack on sight; their bases and convoys become targets Raid your convoys; may ally with your enemies

Stance changes fire events (event:on_stance_change with the faction and old and new stances), so a campaign can react with messages, new missions or story steps. Battle hostility is taken from the stances at the moment the battle starts. The interceptor campaign sets dynamic: false to match the original, with corporate funding as its only moving relation; the default campaign sets dynamic: true.

As built (app 0.10.0 – 0.10.3)

relations is built for the player's standing with each faction: dynamic, start (by faction, not by pair), drift (monthly, towards 0) and stances (upper bounds; above the last, allied). Of the stance effects only hostile or not acts: a non-hostile faction's raids stop, and campaign battles make each faction hostile to the player or not by its stance. Not built: pairs between other factions, scale, relation_rules, on_stance_change events, allies in battle, trade and price effects. Keys: Story layer › relations; DEV-051.

docs.title: Evaluations: evaluations: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
The monthly funding review is an evaluation: a period, an expression per holding, and a table mapping the result to changes.

evaluations:
  funding:
    period: 720h                 # a month
    each: outpost_system
    value: "activity(xcom, here) + activity(xcom) / 10 - activity(alien, here) - activity(alien) / 5"
    change:                      # result bands → funding change range
      - {below: -1000, change: [-5%, -20%]}
      - {below: -500, change: [-2%, -10%]}
      - {below: -250, change: [0%, -5%]}
      - {below: 0, change: [0%, -1%]}
      - {equal: 0, change: 0}
      - {up_to: 250, change: [0%, 1%]}
      - {up_to: 500, change: [0%, 5%]}
      - {up_to: 1000, change: [0%, 10%]}
      - {above: 1000, change: [2%, 10%]}
    then:
      new_outposts: {rolls: "sum / 1000", table: {none: [1, 3], one: [4, 7], two: [8, 9], three: [10, 10]}}

docs.title: Economy
docs.text:
Section Defines Interceptor Default resources Something mined, stored and sold Ore (kt) Cosmium incomes A recurring income: source, period, expression Outpost yield × exchange rate × 0.75 × funding Senate stipend per protected colony + cosmium sales expenses Recurring costs Module maintenance, hull upkeep, salaries Same, fewer markets Who sells what, prices, availability, and who buys Outposts sell; the arms dealer buys (and arms the aliens) Senate depot sells; the Cartel buys and sells (and may supply the Dominion) factories Manufacturing capacity and queue rules Outpost technicians (10 + 10/OPP), priorities 10/25/50/100% One shipyard per base deliveries How goods arrive Outpost freighters (100 CSU; lost with cargo) Supply rocket storage Units and limits CSU; cargo module 1000; full = no orders, loot jettisoned Same rule

Logistics (default campaign, planned). Resources with deposits per system, three production facility types (mining facility, research station, manufacturing center), a demand-driven order chain (main base ← manufacturing ← mining) with time-based extraction and recipes, automatic government supply convoys on fixed lanes with the attack point chosen at launch, enemy supply depots, survey ships, site-specific research branches and facility fighter pools are designed on Logistics: facilities and supply lines. A campaign that leaves those sections out keeps the simpler deliveries model above — as interceptor does, by decision, to stay faithful to the original.

Item economy keys go on the items themselves: cost, sell_price, prod_time (0 = bought off the shelf), size (storage), maintenance, requires.

docs.title: Research
docs.text:
research:
  tri_titanium:
    name: "@research.tri_titanium"          # found name / researched name / text keys
    size: 18000                              # work units (the original's TQ)
    level: 1
    requires: "research(wraith_examination)"
    requires_any: []                         # alternative prerequisites
    appears: "salvage(wraith_hull) or captured(wraith)"   # how it becomes available
    unlocks: [items.tri_titanium_armor, hulls.firestar]   # the original's hard-coded yields
    encyclopaedia: "@db.tri_titanium"

research_model:
  mode: download                             # or labs
  rate: "module_count(downlink_std) * 30 + module_count(downlink_hyper) * 35"
  per_base: {topics: 1, max_downlinks: 3}
  switching: lose_progress
  jammed: {when: "probe_near_base(data_jammer)", effect: pause_one_downlink}
  • mode: download is the original (research done elsewhere, bandwidth-limited); mode: labs is the familiar X-COM model (staff in base labs) for other campaigns.
  • Discovery routes: prerequisites, salvage, capture, events (unlock(research: x)).
  • Salvage is salvage: {<id>: …}: per item type, survival chance by difficulty (the original's 13 *Goodies sections), what it yields (items, research topics, score).
  • Capture: a disabled object can be towed or held until victory; its class's capture key gives what it yields.

docs.title: Bases and modules
docs.text:
base_types:
  xcom:
    hub: objects.xcom_hub
    max_bases: 8
    placement: "distance_to_own_base <= 1.5ly"
    cost: "(1500000 + template_cost) * 0.75"
    build_time: "slowest_module + 168h"
    dismantle: {refund: 50%, sell_stock: true, dismiss_pilots: true}
    limits: {shield: 1, sensor: 1, comms: 1, hangar: 3, downlink: 3, weapon: 10}
    templates:
      new: [beam_defence, beam_defence, downlink, shield, sensor]   # best available of each

Production facilities (facility_types: mining, research, manufacturing) extend base types with production roles; see Logistics.

Modules are object classes (objects) with effects: named campaign quantities they add while working (hangar_capacity +3, pilot_capacity +5, heal_rate x2, storage +1000, research_rate +30, base_shield 2000, sensor_range 40000, orders_in_flight, probe_launch, repair_rate x2, ecm 1km), and on_destroyed actions (lose(ships in hangar), kill(pilots in module), lose(stock)). A destroyed module stays as a wreck until repaired or dismantled.

docs.title: Ships and equipment
docs.text:
hulls:
  firestar:                    # strategy data for a ship class (same id as ships.firestar)
    slots: {beam: 4, missile: 3, special: 4, armor: 1, engine: 1, sensor: 1, shield: 1}
    cost: 550000
    prod_time: 18000
    upkeep: {amount: 18000, per: month}
    requires: "research(tri_titanium)"

items:
  graviton_pulse:
    kind: engine               # beam, launcher, missile, armor, shield, engine, sensor, special, probe, mine
    special: {power: 300, endurance: 48h}
    cost: 185000
    requires: "research(graviton_pulse)"

designs:
  lightning_stock:             # named configuration
    hull: lightning
    fit: {beam: [laser_cannon, laser_cannon], missile: [xwinder_launcher, xwinder_launcher], engine: [conversion_drive]}
    auto: best                 # stock designs upgrade to the best available item
    price: "hull + 0.9 * parts"

Loadout rules (fits on items: which slots, minimum sensor for a missile, power draw) are item keys; the Equip Ship screen enforces them.

docs.title: Pilots
docs.text:
pilots:
  stats:
    intelligence: [50, 100]
    accuracy: [25, 100]
    flying: [25, 100]
    aggression: [25, 100]
    bravery: [25, 100]
    psionics: [1, 100]
    stamina: [50, 100]
    health: [6, 15]
  ranks: {rookie: 40%, ensign: 20%, lieutenant: 20%, lt_commander: 15%, commander: 5%}
  rank_up: {experience: [2, 10, 24, 38]}   # thresholds (experienced); other levels via variants
  experience: "kills / missions + missions"
  kill_value: {fighter: 1, freighter: 1, outpost: 10, opp: 5, probe: 5, mine: 0.25}
  salary: "(48000 + modifiers) / 12"
  training: {stats: [accuracy, flying, psionics], per_month: "ceil(0.1 * stat * intelligence / 100)"}
  injury:
    - {health: 5, accuracy: 50%, flying: 50%}
    - {health: 2, accuracy: 25%, flying: 25%}
    - {health: 0, state: unconscious}
    - {below: 0, state: dead}
  bravery: {kill: 5, outpost: 10, base: 25, own_base_lost: -25, flee_below: 10, flee_chance: 50%, flee_check: 30s}
  recruit: {pool: 10, refresh: monthly, fee: "10000 + 24000 + modifiers"}
  names: text:pilot_names
  voices: [m1, m2, m3, m4, m5, f1, f2, f3, f4, f5]

Every formula is an expression, so another campaign can use completely different pilot rules (or leave out the pilots section and have none).

docs.title: Rival strategy: strategists: {<id>: …}
docs.text:
The rival is driven by a strategist: budgets, priorities and an offence ladder, with conditions deciding when it expands or attacks. It replaces the original's hard-coded strategic AI and reads its Think.ini numbers.

strategists:
  alien:
    faction: alien
    income: 100%                                   # of outpost yield
    budget: {plan: 50%, forces: 35%, research: 15%}   # Think.ini ResearchDefault/GoodsDefault/DoomsdayDefault
    period: 360h                                   # 15 days
    aggression:
      start: think:StartingAggression
      up_when: player_passive
      down_when: player_winning
    explore: [probes, patrols]
    expand: {new_base_when: "player_aggressive or lost_base or plan_starved or outposts_exposed"}
    outposts: {monthly_chance: "5% + day / 30 * 1%", max: 16}
    offence: [attack_probe, attack_freighter, attack_opp, attack_outpost, cripple_base,
              destroy_base, decoy_strike]          # ordered by aggression
    defence: [outposts, bases, opps, freighters]   # priority order
    tech: {levels: 3, cost: [800000, 4000000], funded_by: "module_count(data_receptor) * 20000"}   # per week
    cheats: [knows_player_start_area, instant_equipment, outposts_rebuilt]
    build_priorities: think:module_priorities      # the 31 module sections of Think.ini

The strategist launches squadrons on flight plans; when squadrons and player assets meet, a mission is generated.

As built (app 0.10.0)

Only the aggression is built, as a global strategist: section (aggression: {start, min, max, up, down}, calm_after_wins) rather than strategists.<id>: it multiplies every raid's chance, rising each month the player wins fewer than calm_after_wins battles and falling otherwise. Budgets, exploration, expansion, outposts, the offence ladder, defence, tech levels, cheats, build priorities and the Think.ini values are not built. Story layer › strategist; DEV-051.

docs.title: Logistics: resources, facilities and supply lines
docs.text:
Status: planned (design); decisions recorded 2026-11-11, revised the same day (survey and supply separated, supply convoys, construction thresholds). Requirements: Strategy & logistics (R-STR-012 – R-STR-027). A strategy-layer capability for the default campaign (Perils of the Void). The interceptor campaign will not use it: it stays a faithful match of the original (outposts, OPPs and freighter deliveries, Economy); an optional addon could add logistics to it. Everything below is data in YAML rules a modder can change or leave out — every number is campaign-tunable, and a campaign without facility_types, recipes and logistics sections behaves as today. Owners: Stage 4 (economy, facilities, logistics, convoys, surveys), Stage 3 (the two new mission types) and Stage 5 (the rival's depots, third-party convoys).

Already in the engine (Stage 2): the facility and supply-craft objects of the default campaign (rules/logistics.yaml: mining facility, research station, manufacturing center with turret and shield slots; the cargo clipper and cargo pod), their three construction stages with their own meshes and debris, and the construction-defence and convoy-ambush testbed arenas (Testbed). The strategy-layer simulation below is Stage 4.

As built (app 0.9.0, main ff9d8fc)

The core of this design is built — resources, components, recipes, the three facility types, research sites and station-only topics, deposits and features on the map, surveys within radar range with the attack roll at launch, demand-driven orders, automatic convoys of several vessels along the lanes with the ambush point rolled at launch, and saves — with the keys on Strategy layer › Logistics and the runtime on Campaign › Logistics. Differences from this design: placement is fixed rules per role instead of placement: expressions, and the nearest supplier is measured in a straight line (DEV-049); ambushes and attacks on survey ships are auto-resolved. Not built yet: flying convoy_ambush, construction stages on the map and construction strikes, facility fighter pools and escorts, captured cargo and enemy depots, third-party convoys, cargo capacity and facility upgrades. Requirement statuses: R-STR-012 – R-STR-027.

As built (app 0.9.2, main 0d1c522, 146195b): flown ambushes and the supply vessel

With logistics.ambush_mission an ambushed convoy waits for the player, who flies its escort (convoy_ambush) or lets it fight through; a flown escort delivers the share of cargo still aboard. The supply vessel is the cargo clipper with twelve cargo pods and a point-defence laser as modules; grappler tugs with saucer escorts tear pods off and capture them. Captured cargo is lost to the player but not yet stored at an enemy depot (5.11).

docs.title: What the player does
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    BA["main base<br/>orders components (demand)"] -- "order" --> MA["manufacturing center<br/>needs materials for the order"]
    MA -- "order" --> MI["mining facility<br/>extracts resources over time"]
    MI -- "supply ship (auto) with materials" --> MA
    MA -- "supply ship (auto) with components" --> BA
    MI -- "supply ship: materials to begin a project" --> RS["research station<br/>site-specific tech branches"]
    PR["survey ship<br/>within the base's radar range"] --> SV["survey result:<br/>deposits, research site, suitability"]
    SV --> BU["build a facility<br/>(time; 3 construction stages; attackable from 50 %)"]
    EN["enemy"] -. "attack point on the route chosen at launch" .-> MI & MA
    EN -. "25 % attack roll at launch" .-> PR
  1. Survey. A base launches a survey ship to a system within its current radar range; the survey ship reports the system's deposits and whether it suits a mining facility, a research station or a manufacturing center. When a survey ship launches, a 25 % roll decides whether it will be attacked. Survey ships and supply ships are different mission profiles and different craft.
  2. Build. A facility is built in a system that meets its type's requirements. Building takes time and passes through three construction stages; from 50 % the enemy may try to destroy it (a construction-defence mission), at most three times per location.
  3. Demand pulls supply. The main base orders components (for fighters and other technology) from a manufacturing center. An order needs materials; the center orders them from mining facilities. A part cannot be produced until enough materials are in the center's store. This is the familiar "bases produce fighters and parts" model with a supply chain behind it: a basic supply-and-demand simulation in which demand creates orders and orders pull materials along the chain.
  4. Ship. When a delivery is ready, a supply convoy is dispatched automatically along the fixed lanes: several large supply vessels, each carrying an even share of the cargo. Supply ships are provided by the government — the player does not buy or manage them. The position along the route where the convoy will be attacked is chosen at random at launch. A destroyed or captured vessel's share never arrives; the surviving vessels deliver theirs.
  5. Research. Research stations unlock tech branches that ordinary bases cannot research, only in systems meeting their site criteria. Resources are needed only to begin a project; research then continues without further supply.
  6. Defend. Fighters are built at main bases and then transferred to facilities, where they form a separate pool from base hangars; they defend the facility's system and escort its supply ships, and can be moved between facilities.

docs.title: Data model
docs.text: All sections live in the campaign's strategy/*.yaml (the strategy-layer files of Format: strategy layer). Quantities use the implemented units (48h, 2.4km, 40%); conditions and expressions use the condition language with a campaign context (planned, Stage 3–4).

docs.title: Resources and deposits
docs.text:
The set of resources is campaign data: whatever the campaign's tech tree and core construction need. The names below are examples of the form.

resources:
  iron:      {name: "@res.iron", unit: t, bulk: 1}          # bulk: cargo space per unit
  gold:      {name: "@res.gold", unit: t, bulk: 1}
  dilithium: {name: "@res.dilithium", unit: kg, bulk: 0.1, rare: true}
  cosmium:   {name: "@res.cosmium", unit: t, bulk: 1}       # the default campaign's signature resource

maps:
  reach:
    systems:
      ajax:
        pos: [4300, 1500]
        class: red_dwarf
        bodies: [planet:ice, belt:rich]
        deposits:                           # what can be mined, where, how fast, how much
          cosmium: {body: belt, rate: 6/day, reserve: 1800}
          iron:    {body: planet, rate: 20/day, reserve: unlimited}
        features: [nebula, pulsar_near]     # tags for research-site criteria
        hidden_deposits: true               # only a survey reveals them
  • Deposits belong to a system (optionally a body). rate is the base extraction rate of a level-1 mining facility; reserve runs down as it is mined (unlimited allowed).
  • Features are free tags a campaign defines (nebula, pulsar_near, derelict); research-site criteria test them.

docs.title: Components and recipes
docs.text:
What is manufactured is campaign data too — generally the components fighters and other technology are built from:

components:
  hull_plating:  {name: "@comp.hull_plating"}
  ray_emitter:   {name: "@comp.ray_emitter"}
  rocket_motor:  {name: "@comp.rocket_motor"}

recipes:
  hull_plating:
    at: manufacturing_center
    inputs: {iron: 20t, cosmium: 2t}
    time: 24h
    output: {component: hull_plating, amount: 4}
  ray_emitter:
    at: manufacturing_center
    inputs: {gold: 2t, dilithium: 5kg}
    time: 48h
    output: {component: ray_emitter, amount: 1}
    requires: "research(heat_ray)"

hulls:
  comet:
    build_at: main_base                      # fighters are built at main bases …
    components: {hull_plating: 8, rocket_motor: 2, ray_emitter: 2}   # … from delivered components
    time: 120h

A manufacturing center runs up to lines recipes at once; a recipe starts only when its inputs are in that center's store, takes time, and its output waits in the store for shipment. A main base builds hulls and items from components in its own store.

docs.title: Facility types
docs.text:
facility_types:
  mining_facility:
    name: "@fac.mining"
    hub: objects.mining_facility             # implemented object with construction stages
    role: mining
    placement: "survey_known(system) and deposit(system, any) > 0"
    max_per_system: 1
    build: {cost: 400000, time: 240h, stages: [build_25, build_60, build_90]}
    extracts: {rate: "deposit_rate(system, resource) * level", storage: 400t}
    upgrades: {level_2: {cost: 250000, time: 120h, requires: "research(deep_drills)"}}

  research_station:
    name: "@fac.research"
    hub: objects.research_station
    role: research
    placement: "survey_known(system) and research_site(system, any)"
    build: {cost: 900000, time: 480h, stages: [build_25, build_60, build_90]}
    research_rate: 40                        # work units per hour

  manufacturing_center:
    name: "@fac.manufacturing"
    hub: objects.manufacturing_center
    role: manufacturing
    placement: "owned(system) and lane_distance(system, nearest_base) <= 2"
    build: {cost: 1200000, time: 360h, stages: [build_25, build_60, build_90]}
    lines: 2                                 # recipes running at once
    storage: 800t

fighter_pools:                               # fighters assigned to facilities (separate from base hangars)
  per_facility: {mining: 2, research: 2, manufacturing: 4}
  transfer_time: lane                        # moved between facilities along the lanes
Key Meaning role mining, research or manufacturing (engine behaviours); ordinary base_types keep theirs. hub The object class placed on the map and in battles at this facility — its model set has the construction stages. placement A campaign condition over the candidate system (deposit(...), research_site(...), owned(...), lane_distance(...), survey_known(...)). build cost, time, stages (three state names of the hub's model set, in order), requires (research). extracts, lines, research_rate, storage Role parameters. upgrades Levels with cost, time and requirements.

docs.title: Research sites and tech branches
docs.text:
research_sites:
  nebula_lab:
    name: "@site.nebula_lab"
    criteria: "feature(system, nebula) and star_class(system) in [red_dwarf, blue_giant]"
  pulsar_array:
    criteria: "feature(system, pulsar_near)"

research:
  theremin_shielding:
    size: 24000
    requires: "research(force_fields)"
    lab: research_station                    # only research stations can work on it
    site: nebula_lab                         # …and only one at a nebula lab site
    start_cost: {cosmium: 20t, dilithium: 2kg}   # delivered once; the project then runs unsupplied

lab: restricts a topic (or a whole branch, branches: {theremin: {lab: research_station}}) to a facility type; site: further to stations in systems meeting a research site's criteria. start_cost is the materials a station needs to begin the project — they are ordered from mining facilities like any other demand; once delivered, research runs to completion with no further supply. Topics without lab: are researched as today (the campaign's research_model).

docs.title: Orders, supply ships and ambushes
docs.text:
logistics:
  travel: lanes                              # fixed lanes only
  orders:                                    # demand creates orders; orders pull materials up the chain
    main_base:      {from: manufacturing, wants: components}    # for hulls and items in its build queue
    manufacturing:  {from: mining, wants: recipe_inputs}        # for the recipes it must run
    research:       {from: mining, wants: start_cost}           # once, to begin a project
  source: nearest_by_lane                    # which facility fills an order
  dispatch: "order_filled"                   # a supply ship leaves when the order's cargo is ready
  supply_ship:
    object: objects.supply_ship              # implemented: the cargo clipper; a larger convoy vessel is planned
    provided_by: government                  # automatic; not bought or managed by the player
    convoy: {vessels: tbd, cargo: even_share}   # several vessels; each carries an even share
    capacity: tbd                            # TBD: per vessel, set with the tech-tree balance
    escort: {from_facility_pool: true, max: 3}
  ambush:
    position: random_on_route                # where along its route the convoy is attacked, chosen at launch
    attackers: "strategist_force(lane_threat)"
  losses:
    destroyed: lose_cargo
    captured: {cargo: captor, store_at: nearest_supply_depot}   # the enemy stores it
  • Demand-driven. Nothing is shipped speculatively. A main base's build queue creates orders for components; a manufacturing center's recipes create orders for materials; a research station's start_cost creates a one-off order. Each order is filled by the nearest suitable facility; when its cargo is ready, a supply ship leaves.
  • Supply ships are automatic and provided by the government: the player never buys or manages them, but may escort them with the facility's assigned fighters.
  • Supply convoys. A shipment travels as a convoy of several vessels, each carrying an even share of the cargo, so a partly destroyed convoy delivers the surviving share. Single ships would be destroyed quickly; convoys keep escort missions interesting and playable. A supply vessel is reasonably large: a core vessel with several attached cargo containers (a new default-campaign model, planned).
  • Attack position at launch. When a convoy launches, the point along its route where it will be attacked is chosen at random; when the convoy reaches it, a convoy_ambush mission is generated (the player may fly it; otherwise it is auto-resolved). Open: whether every supply convoy is attacked, or only some and at what chance — the user's answer gives the 25 % roll for survey ships only.
  • Losses. A destroyed vessel's cargo is lost. A captured ship's cargo goes to the enemy, who stores it at a supply depot; destroying an enemy supply depot lets the player seize the resources stored there.
objects:
  dominion_supply_depot:                     # the rival's store of captured and mined cargo
    kind: station
    depot: {seize_on_destroyed: true}        # the player takes its stock when it falls

docs.title: Mission types tied to logistics (Stage 3)
docs.text:
missions:
  convoy_ambush:                             # the marked supply ship reaches its ambush point
    location: lane
    generated: "supply_ship_ambush_point_reached"
    roles:
      convoy: {from: supply_ships, behaviour: freighter_run, protect: true}
      escorts: {from: supply_ship_escorts}
      attackers: {from: ambush_force}
      player: {from: launched_craft, optional: true}
    arrivals: {attackers: {distance: 5km, from_role: convoy, ambush: true}}
    objectives:
      win: "destroyed_all(attackers) or retreated_all(attackers) or departed_all(convoy)"
      lose: "destroyed_all(convoy) or captured_any(convoy)"
    outcomes:
      win: [deliver(convoy)]
      lose: [lose_cargo(convoy)]             # or captor stores it (losses.captured)
    auto_resolve: true

  construction_defence:                      # the enemy strikes a facility before it is finished
    location: facility
    generated: "facility_progress(site) >= 50% and construction_attacks(site) < 3 and hostile_targets(site)"
    roles:
      site: {from: target_facility, state: build_stage}   # shown in its construction-stage state
      guards: {from: facility_pool}
      attackers: {from: attacking_squadron}
      player: {from: launched_craft}
    objectives:
      win: "destroyed_all(attackers) or retreated_all(attackers)"
      lose: "destroyed(site)"
    outcomes:
      lose: [lose_facility(site)]
  • Construction attacks become possible once a facility reaches 50 % and happen at most three times per location (construction_attacks); both numbers are campaign data.
  • state: build_stage uses the implemented scenario state: (an object shown in a state has no modules or point defence yet), and protect: true the implemented objective marking.
  • The default campaign's Escort and Convoy raid mission types become these generated missions on the strategy map; the testbed already has both arenas.

docs.title: Survey ships
docs.text:
Surveys are flown by survey ships: a mission profile and a craft distinct from supply ships.

survey_ships:
  survey_ship:
    object: objects.sky_eye_probe            # the battle object used so far (implemented); see Open questions
    launch_from: base
    range: radar                             # systems within the launching station's current radar range
    survey_time: 24h
    attack: {chance: 25%}                    # rolled once, when the survey ship launches
    reveals: [deposits, features, research_sites, suitability]

When a survey ship launches, a 25 % roll decides whether it will be attacked. A survey records, per system: deposits and reserves, features, the research sites it qualifies for, and for each facility type whether placement holds — the suitability shown on the star map.

docs.title: Third-party convoys
docs.text:
Prospectors and the Cartel run convoys with the same entities, with their own movement rules:

third_party_convoys:
  prospectors:
    pattern: expedition                      # base → system under investigation → pause → base
    targets: "unsurveyed_or_rich(system)"
    stay: [48h, 120h]                        # prospecting (in-universe: then home to restock)
  cartel:
    pattern: random                          # random destinations, including empty or uncharted stars
    destinations: any_star

Escorting or attacking them changes relations (the campaign's dynamic relations).

docs.title: Construction stages as model-set states
docs.text:
Each facility hub's model set has three states, one per construction stage, each swapping the mesh and naming its own debris (both implemented in Stage 2):

modelsets:
  mining_facility:
    intact: models/mining_facility.obj
    states:
      build_25: {model: models/mining_facility_build1.obj, debris: mining_facility_build1}
      build_60: {model: models/mining_facility_build2.obj, debris: mining_facility_build2}
      build_90: {model: models/mining_facility_build3.obj, debris: mining_facility_build3}

The strategy layer shows build_25 from the start of construction (0 %), build_60 from 60 % and build_90 from 90 %, and the intact model on completion. These thresholds — 0 / 60 / 90 % — are confirmed by the user (2026-11-11); the stage list in build.stages is the data. The same state is used on the strategy map's 3D view and in battle. The generator (tools/default_assets/) builds the stage models — scaffold, frame, cladding — for the three facilities and the Guard station.

docs.title: Engine pieces
docs.text: Piece Stage What it does Campaign context for conditions 3–4 System and facility queries (deposit, feature, research_site, survey_known, owned, lane_distance, facility_progress, construction_attacks) for placement, criteria, generated. Economy tick (campaign::economy) 4 On the campaign clock: extraction, recipe progress, research, construction progress and stage changes; storage limits stop production when full. Deterministic; unit-tested on synthetic campaigns. Order book (campaign::logistics) 4 Demand → orders → sources along the chain (main base ← manufacturing ← mining; research ← mining once per project); the logistics graph over the fixed lanes for nearest sources and paths. Supply convoys (campaign::convoys) 4 Spawned automatically when an order is filled, as several vessels sharing the cargo evenly; move along lanes; the attack point chosen at launch; delivery of the surviving share or loss; captured cargo to the captor's depot. Shared with the rival's plan shipments and third-party convoys. Mission generation hooks 3–4 convoy_ambush at the ambush point; construction_defence from 50 % (at most three per location); auto-resolve when the player does not fly. Surveys 4 Survey-ship launch within radar range, the 25 % attack roll, survey timer, results per system. Research labs, sites and start costs 4 lab:, site:, start_cost in the research model. Facility fighter pools 4 Fighters built at main bases, transferred to facilities, moved between them. Supply depots 5 The rival stores captured and mined cargo; the player seizes a destroyed depot's stock. Construction states 2 (done) → 4 Mesh-swapping states with their own debris (implemented); the strategy layer selects the stage. Screens 4 (functional) → 6 (skinned) Facility screen (orders, store, queue, assigned fighters), survey overlay, supply traffic on the star map. Saves 4 Stores, orders, build progress, convoys and survey ships in flight with their attack rolls and points, survey results.

docs.title: Decisions (2026-11-11)
docs.text: Question Decision Supply ships Automatic, provided by the government; not purchased or managed. Travel and routing Fixed lanes. Destinations follow each facility's requirements: demand creates orders that pull materials along the chain (main base ← manufacturing ← mining). Resources Campaign data, set by what the tech tree and core construction need (e.g. iron, gold, dilithium); manufacturing produces components for fighters and other technology. Research stations Resources are needed only to begin a project. Survey and supply Different mission profiles and different craft (revised 2026-11-11; the earlier reading "survey ship = supply ship" is withdrawn). Survey range Systems within the launching station's current radar range. Attacks The 25 % attack roll is made when a survey ship launches; a supply ship's attack position along its route is chosen at random at launch. User's words: "25% probability, determined at survey ship launch. attack position on supply ship along route randomly determined at launch as well". Supply convoys Several vessels, each with an even share of the cargo; a partly destroyed convoy delivers the surviving share. Reason: escort missions stay interesting and playable, since single ships would be destroyed quickly. A supply vessel is a core vessel with several attached cargo containers (new default-campaign model, planned). Captured cargo Feeds the enemy, stored at supply depots; destroying a depot lets the player seize its stock. Construction attacks Possible from 50 % construction; at most three per location. Facility fighters A separate pool from base hangars; built at main bases, then transferred; movable between facilities. Third parties Prospector convoys: base → system under investigation → pause → base. Cartel convoys: random destinations, including empty or uncharted stars. interceptor No logistics: it stays a faithful match of the original; an optional addon could add it. Construction stages Three, each with its own mesh and debris (implemented); shown from 0 %, 60 % and 90 % (confirmed).

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
1. Cargo capacity of a supply vessel — still TBD, set by the tech-tree balance (capacity: tbd).
  2. Supply-convoy attacks — whether every convoy is attacked at its chosen point, or only some and at what chance.
  3. Survey ship — its craft (the Sky-Eye probe object or a new model), and where, when and in which mission an attacked survey ship meets its attackers.
  4. Convoy size — the number of vessels per supply convoy.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0. Decisions revised: survey and supply ships are different profiles and craft (the "survey ship = supply ship" interpretation removed); the 25 % attack roll at survey-ship launch; supply-ship attack position chosen at launch; supply convoys with even cargo shares and a larger convoy vessel; construction thresholds 0 / 60 / 90 % confirmed; cargo capacity still TBD 1.14.0 2026-11-11 As-built note (app 0.9.0): what is built, the two differences (fixed placement rules, straight-line nearest supplier; DEV-049), auto-resolved ambushes and survey attacks, and what is not built yet 1.15.0 2026-11-11 As-built note (app 0.9.2): flown convoy ambushes (ambush_mission), the supply vessel with cargo pods and a point-defence laser, tugs and escorts; depots still not built

docs.title: Mod structure
docs.text: Status: partly implemented (Stage 2). kind, parent, targets, format, the active set built from the chosen campaign and its load order, YAML mod files checked against schemas (mod format 2) and <key>+ / <key>- list edits are implemented (see Packs); conflicts, a load-order setting, saves naming their mods, text keys and the other folders and sections below are still design. A pack without kind is an addon. Mod files are YAML; original INI files are still read, section by section, through inherit: original:<file>/<section>.

docs.title: Mod kinds
docs.text:
OpenXcom distinguishes master mods (a whole game: UFO Defense, Terror From the Deep) from mods that change one. OpenInterceptor does the same, with one addition: a campaign can be built on another campaign.

Kind What it is Examples campaign A complete, playable game: a campaign ruleset plus all the content it uses. The player chooses one campaign when starting a new game. interceptor, default, interceptor-remastered addon Changes a campaign: balance, new ships, new missions, replacement art. Applies only when its target campaign is being played. faster-lightning, an HD cockpit library Shared content with no campaign of its own: models, textures, sounds, behaviours that several mods use. Loaded only when something depends on it. common-effects

docs.title: pack.yaml
docs.text:
# yaml-language-server: $schema=../../schemas/pack.schema.json
id: interceptor-remastered
name: "X-COM: Interceptor — Remastered"
version: "0.1"
kind: campaign
parent: interceptor           # this campaign is the interceptor campaign plus my changes
requires_original: true       # inherited from the parent anyway; stated for the launcher
depends: [common-effects]     # libraries loaded before this mod
description: Sharper textures and upgraded models for modern screens.
authors: ...
licence: MIT                  # shown in the launcher; the engine never enforces it
format: 2                     # mod format version this mod was written for
Key Applies to Meaning id, name, version, description, authors, licence all As today; authors and licence are informational. kind all campaign, addon (default) or library. Implemented. parent campaign Another campaign this one extends: the parent's whole content loads first, then this mod's files override and add. Chains are allowed (remastered → interceptor); a cycle is an error. Implemented. targets addon Campaign ids the addon applies to (targets: [interceptor]). An addon targeting interceptor also applies to every campaign whose parent chain contains interceptor. targets: ["*"] applies to all. Implemented (no targets also applies to all). depends all Libraries (or other addons) that must load before this mod. requires_original all true when the mod reads the player's CD. Inherited through parent. format all The mod-format version. The engine refuses newer formats with a clear message. Implemented: the current format is 2 (YAML); a format-1 pack (a folder with pack.ini and INI rules) is refused with a message pointing to the YAML format. conflicts addon Ids that must not be active at the same time.

docs.title: Which mods load
docs.text:
When a game starts (or a save loads) the active set is built from the chosen campaign:

flowchart LR
    C["chosen campaign<br/>interceptor-remastered"] --> P["parent chain<br/>interceptor"]
    P --> L["libraries from depends"]
    C --> A["enabled addons whose targets<br/>match any campaign in the chain"]
    L --> O{{"load order"}}
    P --> O
    C --> O
    A --> O

Load order — later overrides earlier:

  1. Libraries, in dependency order.
  2. The root campaign (end of the parent chain), then each child down to the chosen campaign.
  3. Enabled addons that target the chain, in dependency order, then by a load-order list in settings.yaml, then by folder name.

The order is computed once, deterministically, and written into every save, so a save names exactly the mods (and versions) it was made with. Loading a save with a missing mod is refused with the list of what is missing; with a different version it warns.

As implemented in Stage 2, the testbed launcher shows the scenarios of the active set only, and Tab switches campaign (remembered as game: campaign: in settings.yaml; --campaign on the command line). Libraries and dependencies load first, then the parent chain root first, then the addons — the load-order tie-break is not implemented yet (addons keep folder-name order). A full campaign selection screen is still Stage 4.

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
A mod is a folder. Every folder is optional; files are found by convention (and every file in a rules folder is loaded, in file-name order).

<mod>/
  pack.yaml                 manifest (required)
  campaign/*.yaml           campaign ruleset: difficulty (implemented); game flow, start state, victory
  rules/*.yaml              ships, objects, weapons, systems, factions, flight, power, damage,
                            sounds, cockpits, behaviours (implemented)
  strategy/*.yaml           star map, relations, economy, research, bases and modules, pilots
  missions/*.yaml           mission types, generators, objectives
  events/*.yaml             scripted campaign events
  behaviours/*.yaml         AI and object behaviours (today in rules/*.yaml as `behaviours:`)
  scenarios/*.yaml          testbed arenas (implemented)
  interface/*.yaml          screen layouts, skins, fonts, HUD and cockpit layouts
  text/<language>/*.yaml    every player-visible string; encyclopaedia; messages
  scripts/*.lua             optional scripts (Tier 2, see Behaviours and scripting)
  models/                   OBJ + MTL
  textures/                 PNG/TGA; also re-skins any model texture by name
  images/                   UI art, cockpit art; images/<dll>/<id>.png overrides original images
  sounds/                   WAV (and OGG, Stage 5)
  music/                    WAV/OGG loops and tracks
  video/                    cut-scenes (Stage 5)
  recipes/*.yaml            generated-asset recipes (see below)

docs.title: Ids and overriding
docs.text:
• Every definition has a kind and an id: it is written under its section's key — ships: {lightning: …}, research: {plasma_beam: …}, events: {nova_theft: …}. Ids are lower case a-z 0-9 _ -.
  • Ids are global across the active set. A mod that defines ships: {lightning: …} again overrides it key by key (mappings merge, values and lists are replaced); delete: true removes it, and an empty value (model:) removes one key. Implemented.
  • inherit: <id> (same section) or inherit: ships.<id> copies another definition first (variants); inherit: original:<file>/<section> copies a section of an original INI file, whose keys map to field names by spelling (HitPoints → hit_points). Implemented.
  • List keys can be replaced or edited: beams: [a, b] replaces; beams+: [c] and beams-: [a] edit the inherited (or earlier pack's) list without restating it. Implemented for every list key; systems+ also edits a class's default system list. This matters for addons (adding one research topic's unlock without copying the topic).
  • Difficulty: variants: {<level>: {…}} inside a definition gives only the keys that differ at that level; any number may be {per_level: [80, 100, 120]}. Implemented.
  • Text is never in rules. A rule names a text key (name: "@ship.lightning.name"); the string lives in text/<language>/. A plain value without @ is used as written, so small mods can skip translation tables.
  • Assets keep the Stage 1 rules: pack-relative paths, original: references, and per-asset overrides at the override paths.

docs.title: Generated assets (recipes)
docs.text:
Some content must be derived from the player's own files: an upscaled texture is a conversion of an original texture, so it can never be shipped. A recipe describes how to make an asset; the engine runs it on the player's machine and caches the result.

# recipes/textures.yaml
recipes:
  all-textures-x4:
    kind: upscale              # built-in generators: upscale, mesh-patch, recolour, composite
    inputs: original:*.xtxr    # every original texture
    scale: 4
    method: edge-directed      # built-in, deterministic (see Interceptor Remastered)
    output: "textures/{name}.png"
  • Outputs land in <user data>/cache/<mod id>/<mod version>/ and are treated as if they were files of the mod at their output paths — so they take part in overrides like any file.
  • The cache is keyed by the recipe text, the mod version and the input file's hash; a change to any of them rebuilds. --build-recipes builds everything ahead of time with progress output; otherwise the launcher builds on first use.
  • Recipes are deterministic and in-crate (no external tools), so two players get identical results and a recipe can be unit-tested on synthetic inputs.

Built-in generators: upscale (textures and images), mesh-patch (edits to an original mesh: see Interceptor Remastered), recolour (palette or hue changes: faction colour variants), composite (layer images: decals, damage overlays).

docs.title: Validation
docs.text: --check --campaign <id> loads the active set for that campaign and validates every definition, reference and condition, reporting each problem with its file, line and key path (YAML syntax and schema errors: rules/ships.yaml:12: ships.comet.max_sped: unknown key (did you mean 'max_speed'?); conditions are type-checked at load). A campaign must pass with no addons, and each addon must pass with its targets.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: The original game, system by system
docs.text:
Status: analysis, 2026-11-10. What X-COM: Interceptor does, how it decides it, and where the data lives — the requirements the mod format must meet. Facts are marked V verified (seen in the CD data), D derived (inferred from data, strings or a source), U unknown.

Sources.

  • [CD]: the player's CD. Files used:
    • GameSettings.ini (259 sections)
    • Think.ini
    • MPSettings.INI and NetSettings.ini
    • soundfx.ini
    • Text/LangFile1.txt, with 3,782 keyed strings
    • Text/starcorp1.txt, Names1.txt, news1.txt and short1.txt
    • Animations/mfdanim.mps
    • the Loops/*.wtl music tables
    • strings and constants in Interceptor.exe
  • [G]: X-COM Interceptor Official Strategies & Secrets (Sybex, 1998), the designer-written strategy guide.
  • [UR] UFOpaedia: Research, Background and Hypernews pages.
  • [F]: a GameFAQs walkthrough.

Nothing here reproduces original text or art; names and numbers are cited as facts.

docs.title: Summary: data versus code
docs.text:
The original keeps numbers in data and rules in code.

In data (V) Hard-coded in the executable (V/D) Prices, build times, maintenance, hit points, weapon and missile stats, hull handling, research sizes and prerequisites, module stats and size classes, rank thresholds, salvage chances, sensor tables, mission score values, alien budget priorities, Doomsday defence counts, all text, names, news, sound cue table Star map generation; every mission's composition, waves and objectives; all AI (strategic, financial, tactical, Doomsday, "fluff" encounters, 32 agent classes); the campaign arc (messages, components, final mission); research yields (what a topic unlocks: all Yield keys are 0); the meaning of each score index; funding and evaluation formulas; report and news triggers; the debris table; module meshes and textures; star and planet visuals; limits (85 systems, 20 bases (8 in the UI), 33 modules per base, 8 players)

Consequence: the interceptor mod must express everything in the right-hand column as data. That column is therefore the hard part of the format, and each row has a section below.

docs.title: Campaign arc
docs.text: Element Rule Src Start 1 Jan 2067. X-COM: 1 base, 3 corporate outpost systems nearby, 3 Lightning II, 5 pilots, cargo of 5 Sensor Probes and 10 X-Winders. Aliens: 2 bases, 6 outposts, at least 1 parsec away G (D) Starting base Cargo, Communications, Hangar, 2 laser turrets, Personnel, Probe Launcher, Standard Downlink, Standard Sensor G Story gate chain Alien Message 1 (not before 1 Feb; chance per combat 7/7/5/5/4% by difficulty, or automatic later) → aliens ship Structural Components → Message 2 (≥1 Mar; needs Msg 1 + a captured Structural Component + Wraith examined) → Message 3 (≥1 May; + Spectre examined; Weapon Components start) → Message 4 (≥1 Jul; + Phantasm examined + Weapon Component; Drive Components start) → Message 5 (≥1 Oct; + Drive Component; gateway map) G (D) Doomsday components Built one type at a time. Totals per difficulty: 25/25/25/20/18 components, split Structural/Weapon/Drive (e.g. Beginner 8/8/9, Superhuman 7/6/5). Convoys pass near X-COM space with probability 65→45%. On the three easiest levels, a fully shipped Structural or Weapon type you never captured is granted. All Drive Components delivered = loss G (D) Final preparation Alien Hull Alloys (Super Avenger), Message 5, Dimension Jump Drive, Nova Bomb researched; gateway (a black hole) found by probes; "Summon MacArthur" (arrives in about 1 week) G Final mission I Outside the black hole vs a large fleet. Fail if the MacArthur dies or no Nova-armed Super Avenger survives G, CD strings FINAL1_MACDEAD, FINAL_NOVASGONE Final mission II Inside the "pocket universe": 7 squadrons, a base, maybe mines; Doomsday weapon untargetable; ships rearmed (repaired on low levels). Total victory: Nova Bomb delivered and you return to within 1 km of the MacArthur; partial victory: bomb delivered, you are lost G Defeat Doomsday completed (DD_TOOLATE), last base destroyed (S_LASTBASEDEAD), final mission failed CD V, G Warnings DD_WARNING1..3; MacArthur prompts MAC_PROMPT1..7 CD V

docs.title: Strategy map
docs.text: Element Rule Src Generation Procedural each campaign (universe.cpp); no map file. Star names from a pool of 100. Limits: 85 systems, 2D grid of 60000 units CD V Stars d100 spectral class: red giant 1–2, blue giant 3–6, black hole 7–10, white dwarf 11–13, blue 14–24, white 25–35, yellow 36–70, orange 71–85, red dwarf 86–100. At least one black hole (the gateway). Black holes hidden; probes lost in them G Bodies 0–5 satellites in 5 orbit slots; asteroid fields mostly inner; planet size small/medium/large/huge; mineral richness low/medium/high by spectral class G Locations DEEPSPACE{x,y}, SYSTEM{id,x,y,orbit}, BASE, OUTPOST, OPP{outpost,opp}, DOOM_PORTAL, POCKET, FLIGHTPLAN CD V Travel Free hyperjumps on the 2D map (no lanes). Range limited by engine endurance: 24/36/48 h. Ships stranded without fuel are lost. Ambush chance grows with distance from home G Time Real time, 6 speeds, auto-pause on events; weekly reports (WEEKLY1..40); monthly evaluation G, CD Sensors Rings around bases (long), ships, outposts, probes. Sensor Probe 0.75 ly, 4–6 weeks; Hunter Probe roams, 3–4 weeks. Destroyed base sensor → about 0.25 ly G Orders in flight Need a Communications module at the squadron's base G

docs.title: Factions and relations
docs.text: Party Mechanics Src X-COM The player — Aliens Full strategic opponent with the same rules plus cheats (rough knowledge of X-COM's start, off-the-shelf equipment, outposts always rebuilt). Five races, lore only G, CD Corporations 87 names; each outpost system's corporation sets a funding share 0–95%, moved monthly by evaluation; at 0% it leaves for good. Only source of money, supplies, manufacturing, recruits. Corporate fighters guard outposts; escorts can be hired (10% of an order) G, CD Kabron pirates Hostile; one base. docs.title: Language files (LangFile1.txt)
docs.text:
The original's player-visible text is in plain-ASCII language files (verified):

/ a comment line starts with a slash
KEY_NAME        "The text~second line"

A key, whitespace (tabs or spaces), then the text between the first and last double quote on the line; ~ is a line break; anything else is skipped. formats::langfile reads them from the player's CD at run time when a pack's text file imports: them; the strings become @orig.<KEY> text keys and are never copied into a pack (Text and translation).

docs.title: MPSRC packs
docs.text: Animations/mfdanim.mps is an MPSRC pack: a plain bundle of named files. In the original it holds the cockpit display's animations — 113 Smacker clips (talking heads and small transmissions) — read in-crate by formats::mpsrc since main 319a31b. The layout below is verified on the reference CD's mfdanim.mps (113 entries, all inside the file); the members are Smacker clips.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
All numbers little-endian.

Offset Size Field State 0x00 8 Signature MPSRC followed by three zero bytes verified 0x08 4 count: number of entries verified 0x0C count × 136 Entry table (below) verified … … The members' bytes, at the offsets the entries give verified

Each 136-byte entry:

Offset in entry Size Field State 0x00 128 Member name, zero-padded (for example a clip name ending .smk) verified 0x80 4 size in bytes verified 0x84 4 offset from the start of the file verified

The reader rejects a missing signature, a truncated table, an implausible count (over 100 000) and an entry that runs past the end of the file. Member names are matched without regard to case.

docs.title: References
docs.text:
An engine asset reference names a member after #: original:mfdanim.mps#<member> (Content::read_asset). Such a reference may be used wherever a video is accepted, and as a voice set's face on the comms panel (Radio voices).

The member names fall into groups by prefix (at_, as_, e_, w_ and others); which speaker each group is, is unknown, so the interceptor campaign does not map faces yet.

docs.title: PE resource container
docs.text: The asset DLLs are ordinary 32-bit Windows PE files whose .rsrc section holds the data. Their code is a stub; the engine never runs it. verified

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
1. e_lfanew at 0x3C → PE header; number of sections at +6; optional-header size at +20.
  2. Data directory 2 (resources) gives the .rsrc RVA; the section table maps RVAs to file offsets.
  3. The resource directory is a three-level tree: type → name → language. Each directory has 16 bytes of header, then named + id entries of 8 bytes: a name (high bit set → offset of a UTF-16 length-prefixed string) and an offset (high bit set → subdirectory, else data entry).
  4. A data entry gives the RVA and size of the resource bytes.

Names are stored with surrounding double quotes in these DLLs ("INTTYPEA"); the engine strips them and compares case-insensitively. Language is always 1033 (US English).

docs.title: Resource types used
docs.text:
Type Holds DLLs Count (approx.) XMSH 3D meshes xobjects1, xobjects2 147 + 150 XTXR Textures xobjects1, xobjects2 461 + 338 XSPT Sprite animations (explosions, flak, laser) xobjects2 10 TARG TGA images, numeric IDs Cockpit*, Sprites, Wrappers 170–1,733 per DLL

Each XMSH, XTXR and XSPT resource begins with a 12-byte lowercase name (NUL-padded with 0xCD, the MSVC debug fill) and a 4-byte tag MSH\0, TXR\0 or SPT\0, then a u32 0 and padding to 0x20.

docs.title: In the engine
docs.text: formats::pe parses the tree once per DLL and keeps (type, name) → byte range. The packs VFS exposes each resource as a virtual file, e.g. xmsh/inttypea, so the rest of the engine never knows the data came from a DLL. See Formats layer.
