docs.title: Smacker video
docs.text: Animations/*.smk are RAD Game Tools Smacker files (SMK2/SMK4): the intro, alien transmissions, endings and credits; the cockpit display's talking heads are Smacker clips bundled in Animations/mfdanim.mps (MPSRC packs). The Smacker format is publicly documented. OpenInterceptor decodes it in-crate (formats::smacker, app 0.12.0); the original SMACKW32.DLL is never used. The decoder was checked against all eleven .smk files of the reference CD — every frame and its audio decode (verified).

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
All numbers little-endian.

Part Contents State Header (104 bytes) Signature SMK2 or SMK4; width; height; frame count; frame rate (positive: milliseconds per frame; negative: hundred-thousandths; zero: 10 fps); flags (bit 0: a ring frame follows the last; bits 1 – 2: lines doubled or interlaced); seven audio-track sizes; the size of the Huffman tree data; the four trees' sizes; seven audio-track rate words (rate in the low 24 bits; flags: data present, 16-bit, stereo, compressed); a reserved word verified Frame sizes One u32 per frame (+1 with a ring frame); the low two bits are flags, the rest the size verified Frame types One byte per frame: bit 0 a palette chunk follows; bits 1 – 7 an audio chunk for tracks 0 – 6 verified Trees The four big Huffman trees — mmap, mclr, full, type — packed least-significant bit first verified Frames Each: an optional palette chunk, the audio chunks of the tracks flagged, then the video bitstream verified

docs.title: Huffman trees
docs.text: A small tree has 8-bit leaves: a bit 1 is a node (left subtree, then right), 0 a leaf followed by its 8-bit value. A big tree (16-bit leaves) is preceded by a low-byte and a high-byte small tree and three 16-bit escape values; a leaf's value is a pair (low, high) decoded through the small trees. A leaf equal to an escape instead stands for one of a three-slot cache of the most recent values; every decoded value pushes into the cache. The caches are reset at the start of each frame.

docs.title: Video
docs.text:
The frame is cut into 4 × 4 blocks in raster order. A type value gives the block kind (two bits), a run length (six bits, through a table: 1 – 59, then 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048) and, for solid blocks, the colour (the high byte):

Kind Pixels Mono mclr gives two colours, mmap a 16-bit pattern choosing between them per pixel Full full gives the 16 pixels two at a time; in SMK4, two further modes give half-resolution blocks (pixels doubled) Skip Unchanged from the previous frame Solid One colour for all 16 pixels

docs.title: Palette
docs.text: A palette chunk (its length in units of four bytes, then commands) rebuilds the 256 entries from the previous palette: a byte with the top bit set keeps the next (b & 0x7F) + 1 entries; one with bit 6 set copies (b & 0x3F) + 1 entries from a given index of the old palette; otherwise the byte and the next two are 6-bit red, green and blue, scaled to 8 bits.

docs.title: Audio
docs.text: Up to seven tracks. Each audio chunk in a frame starts with its own length (a u32, itself included). A compressed chunk's body starts with its unpacked size, then a bit for "data", one for stereo and one for 16-bit, then one small tree per byte stream (one or two per channel), the first samples as raw values, and deltas from there (DPCM). Uncompressed chunks are raw PCM; 8-bit samples are unsigned. The engine plays track 0.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here 1.16.0 2026-11-11 The format as decoded in-crate (app 0.12.0): header, tables, trees with the escape cache, block kinds, palette and audio; verified on the reference CD's eleven videos; the talking heads' MPSRC pack

docs.title: TGA images and cockpits
docs.text:
TARG resources and the files in 3DObjects/ are standard Truevision TGA. verified

  • Type 2 (uncompressed true-colour), 16 bits per pixel (RGB555, with an attribute bit), 18-byte header, no image ID. Descriptor bit 5 clear: rows bottom-up.
  • Some wrapper screens are type 10 (RLE true-colour).

docs.title: Cockpits
docs.text:
CockpitA.dll, CockpitB.dll and CockpitC.dll each hold a 640×480 cockpit frame (resource IDs 12000, 12200, 12400) and many smaller parts: gauge needles, MFD and radar elements, damage states. One DLL per player hull (derived: the game has exactly three hulls).

The frame uses cyan, RGB555 0x03DF, as its colour key: those pixels are the window onto space. The engine converts the key to transparent alpha at load.

The frame shows (from the art): a message strip across the top, two round scopes (radar), a centre MFD, four small gauges above it, and two lower dials. What each scope shows (fore/aft or range modes) is derived and refined in Stage 1–2.

docs.title: Other images
docs.text: 3DObjects/ holds reticles (five variants), lens-flare elements, sun and star sprites. SpritesDLL.dll holds ~1,700 small sprites; WrappersDLL.dll the full-screen menus.

docs.title: XMSH meshes
docs.text: Every 3D object (ships, stations, debris, asteroids, nebula billboards, planets) is an XMSH resource. Coordinates are Direct3D-style (left-handed, Y up); the engine converts to its own right-handed frame at load. Units appear to be metres (a fighter has a bounding radius of about 10). All 297 meshes parse with this layout. Rendering three hulls and a saucer with their original textures confirmed positions, UVs and texture binding.

docs.title: File header
docs.text: Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name, lowercase, NUL then 0xCD fill verified 0x0C char[4] tag MSH\0 verified 0x10 u32 0 verified (always 0) 0x20 f32 bounding-sphere radius verified 0x28 f32[6] bounding box min xyz, max xyz verified 0x40 u32 flags; 1 on hulls with a manipulator, 0 on many others unknown 0x44 i32[4] −1 unknown 0x54 i32[4] offsets of up to 4 LOD blocks, −1 = none verified

docs.title: LOD block
docs.text:
All offsets inside a LOD block are relative to the block's start.

Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32 switch distance: use this LOD while closer than this (last LOD: 1e8) derived +0x04 u32 0 — +0x08 u32 vertex count verified +0x0C u32 vertex offset verified +0x10 u32 edge count (includes unused edge 0) verified +0x14 u32 edge offset verified +0x18 u32 texture-name count verified +0x1C u32 texture-name offset verified +0x20 u32 manipulator count verified +0x24 u32 manipulator offset verified +0x28 u32 BSP root node offset verified

docs.title: Vertex — 32 bytes
docs.text: f32 x, y, z, nx, ny, nz, u, v. Vertices are duplicated where UVs differ. verified

docs.title: Edge — 16 bytes
docs.text:
u32 v0, u32 v1, u32 (0xCDCDCDCD), u32 0. Edges are 1-based: entry 0 is unused filler. verified

Some edges have the same vertex at both ends (zero length): about 3% of polygons (1,014 of 33,012 across the CD) contain one, giving a repeated corner such as 11, 24, 24, 9. They are in the original data, not a decoding error, and are harmless — the fan triangulation turns the repeated corner into a zero-area triangle. verified

docs.title: Texture name — 32 bytes
docs.text: NUL-terminated lowercase name of an XTXR resource, 0xCD fill. verified

docs.title: Manipulator — 64 bytes
docs.text:
f32[12] (a 3×4 transform) then two i32. The original program's strings call these XCGEN_MANIP_OBJECT and "dummy" manipulators: attachment points such as gun mounts or engine positions. derived — the meaning of each one per model is not yet known.

On the X-COM base (XBASE7) the 34 LOD-0 manipulators are module mount points: the first i32 (kind) runs 0–50 and the positions sit on the ring and spine. The modules themselves are separate meshes (XMMOD02, XMMODHUB, XLANDPC1–4, GUNTURRET2, SCICENTER02, …), so a station under construction is the base mesh plus whichever modules are attached. derived

docs.title: BSP node — 64 bytes
docs.text:
Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32[4] splitting plane (normal, distance); zero in a leaf derived +0x10 f32[6] node bounding box verified +0x28 i32 front child offset, −1 = none verified +0x2C i32 back child offset, −1 = none verified +0x30 i32 0 unknown +0x34 i32 polygon count verified +0x38 i32 −1 unknown +0x3C — 0xCD fill —

The node's polygons follow immediately after its 64 bytes.

docs.title: Polygon — 40 + 4·n bytes
docs.text:
Offset Type Field Confidence +0x00 f32[4] face plane (normal, distance) verified +0x10 u32 flags (see below); 0 on most polygons derived +0x14 u32 colour, 0xAARRGGBB-like; used when untextured derived +0x18 u32 / f32 0, or an opacity-like float when 0x80000000 is set derived +0x1C f32 small value (≈0.03–0.05) unknown +0x20 u32 texture index into the LOD's name list verified +0x24 i32 edge count n verified +0x28 i32[n] signed edge references verified

A positive reference e walks edge e from v0 to v1; a negative one walks edge |e| backwards, so the polygon's corner is v0 for positive and v1 for negative references. Polygons are convex fans with 3 to 36 corners (most are triangles and quads).

The corner order is counter-clockwise around the face plane's normal (by the right-hand rule, in file coordinates) for 32,893 of 33,012 polygons; the rest are degenerate. The plane normals point outward (every asteroid face does), so faces are one-sided and the original culled back faces. Thin surfaces seen from both sides — shield rings (1ASHA…3SH3C), the Avenger's fin, ALORBOUT — are modelled as two polygons back to back. verified

Texture coordinates may lie outside 0..1 (the Patton CPAT has 564 such corners, ROID100 172): textures tile (Direct3D's default wrap addressing). verified by rendering.

docs.title: Polygon flags (+0x10)
docs.text:
Bits Meaning Count (LOD 0, whole CD) Confidence 0x20000000 overlay: a decal lying exactly on a larger base polygon in the same plane (station panels, alien hull markings) 32 alone, 53 with 0x80000000 derived 0x80000000 translucent? — always with a float 0..1 at +0x18 (0.33, 0.60, 0.65) 569 alone, 101 with other bits derived 0x00200000, 0x00020000, 0x00008000, low 9 bits (0x115–0x11E on station overlays) not decoded — unknown

Evidence for the overlay bit: of 124 same-facing overlapping coplanar pairs, 72 have the flag on the later polygon and 8 on the earlier one. The original drew polygons in BSP order, so the later polygon painted over the base; a depth-buffered renderer must instead be told which one wins — the engine's overlay layers (see Rendering). The opacity float is read but not used yet.

docs.title: Typical sizes
docs.text: A fighter: four LODs from ~310 to ~140 vertices and ~200 to ~35 polygons. The X-COM base: ~2,450 vertices and ~660 polygons at LOD 0.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• The flag at 0x40, and the undecoded polygon flag bits.
  • Whether 0x80000000 really is translucency, and how the float is applied.
  • Whether the low bits on station overlays (0x115–0x11E) select overlays by construction state; they do not match the base's manipulator kinds.
  • What each manipulator means per model (weapon mounts? engine glow? docking?).
  • The float at +0x1C (≈0.01–0.05).
  • Whether the BSP order is needed for correct transparency.

The model viewer's wireframe and face selection (see Testbed) show each polygon's index, flags, layer and UVs, which helps this research.

docs.title: XSPT sprites
docs.text:
Ten animated sprites in xobjects2.dll: blam, blamo_, boom, flak, kaplo_, laser, pop, pow, puff, wip — explosions, flak bursts, hit flashes.

Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name verified 0x0C char[4] tag SPT\0 verified 0x20 u32, u32 frame width, height derived 0x28 u32, u32 centre (hot spot) x, y derived 0x30 f32 frame duration or scale (0.1, 0.15) unknown 0x34 u32 frame count derived 0x38 u32 1 unknown 0x3C u32[] per-frame data offsets derived … per frame: a small header (size, origin), then 16-bit RGB555 pixel runs unknown

The pixel encoding is a run-length scheme still to be decoded (Stage 2). Until then the engine draws procedural explosions.

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: XTXR textures
docs.text:
Palettised textures with 16 shade tables and mipmaps. verified for every size present.

Offset Type Field Confidence 0x00 char[12] name verified 0x0C char[4] tag TXR\0 verified 0x20 u16, u16 width, height (powers of two, 16–256) verified 0x24 u16 0xCDCD — 0x26 u16 0 — 0x28 u16[16][256] 16 palettes of 256 RGB555 colours verified 0x2028 16 bytes unknown unknown 0x2038 u8[] 4 mip levels of 8-bit indices: w×h, w/2×h/2, w/4×h/4, w/8×h/8 verified

Total size = 8,248 + w·h·85/64 bytes.

  • Palette 0 is full brightness; palettes 1–15 are progressively darker (shade tables for the 1998 software renderer). The engine uses palette 0 and lights with the GPU.
  • Rows are stored bottom-up (text on textures reads correctly only after flipping V).
  • Whether an index is transparent (e.g. index 0 or black) is still unknown; no transparent surfaces have been confirmed on hulls.
  • A few 32×32 textures are 15,416 bytes rather than 9,608: 7 KiB more than expected, perhaps animation frames. unknown

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Adopted into Specification 1.0.0 as a normative format page; requirements link here

docs.title: Campaigns requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for campaign choice, difficulty, the three campaigns, story and rivals, and presentation. The normative format is Format: campaign and game flow.

Features: Campaigns. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-CPN-001 One campaign at a time Implemented R-CPN-002 Difficulty levels Implemented R-CPN-003 Default campaign plays without the CD Implemented R-CPN-004 Default campaign content Planned R-CPN-005 Interceptor campaign content Planned R-CPN-006 Interceptor Remastered Planned R-CPN-007 Events and arcs Implemented R-CPN-008 Rival plans and strategist Planned (partly met) R-CPN-009 Dynamic relations Planned (partly met) R-CPN-010 Victory, defeat and endings Planned (partly met) R-CPN-011 Screens and skins Planned (partly met) R-CPN-012 Video and music Planned (partly met)

docs.title: R-CPN-001 One campaign at a time
docs.text:
Exactly one campaign MUST be active, chosen by --campaign, settings.yaml game.campaign or the launcher; the active set MUST be the campaign, its parent chain, the addons targeting it and their dependencies.

Rationale: A campaign is the unit a modder ships.

  • Implements: F-CPN-001, F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::pack::the_active_set_follows_the_chosen_campaign; app::launcher::menu_lists_viewer_and_scenarios_and_wraps; MT-2-12
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Packs, Packs, VFS and rules

docs.title: R-CPN-002 Difficulty levels
docs.text:
A campaign MUST define its difficulty levels; the player MUST choose one in the launcher, with --difficulty or in settings.yaml, remembered per campaign; definitions MUST vary by level through variants and {per_level: …} values.

Rationale: Five levels in interceptor, four in default.

  • Implements: F-CPN-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::rules::difficulty_variants_and_per_level_values; soak::default_campaign_difficulty_scales_enemy_lethality; settings::parses_and_round_trips; MT-2-19, MT-2-20
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Rulesets

docs.title: R-CPN-003 Default campaign plays without the CD
docs.text:
The default campaign MUST load, validate and play with no original data present.

Rationale: Modding first: the engine stands alone.

  • Implements: F-CPN-003, F-MOD-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: check::the_default_campaign_passes; content::loads_original_free_packs_rules_scenarios_and_models; MT-1-19, MT-2-13
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: The default campaign

docs.title: R-CPN-004 Default campaign content
docs.text:
Perils of the Void MUST provide its fixed six-system map, its craft, stations and weapons, the 11 generated mission types (2 on surfaces), the 12-chapter arc, the Dominion as rival and the logistics of R-STR-012 – R-STR-027.

Rationale: The worked example for modders.

  • Implements: F-CPN-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (in progress: rules, scenarios, 9 missions).
  • See: The default campaign, Missions (modding)

Progress (app 0.6.4, main 3866c34, 90653b9)

Nine missions now: defend_station, convoy_ambush, construction_defence, intercept_scouts, and five that use the Stage 3 environments and hazards — colony_defence (moon_surface, protect the ground installation guard_colony), ground_strike (dusk_hills, dominion_flak batteries, a timer to a draw), outpost_raid (orbit, a dominion_outpost, two wingmen), asteroid_hunt (an asteroid field) and pocket_ambush (pocket, a 65 % ion storm, hot-rods). Each has briefing, chatter and debrief text keys, including killed. Strategy layer (app 0.7.1, main 10f7fce): resources/default/strategy/ holds the fixed Reach map, a 12-topic research tree, items, hulls, nine module kinds, the Guard base, the Senate stipend, five raids flying these missions, pilots and scores (Strategy layer). Its texts are plain English, not yet text keys. Two of the nine are on surfaces, as this requirement asks. Soaked with the AI pilot at cadet: colony_defence win at 43 s, outpost_raid win at 99 s; the other three make kills but run past 300 s. Still to come: these are not yet the 11 generated mission types (generation is the strategy layer, Stage 4), and the chapter story missions belong with the 12-chapter arc (Stage 5). Terrain and sky are generated by the environments themselves (terrains: generators and sky: colours), so no separate assets are needed.

Progress (app 0.9.1 – 0.10.3, main 3b19dea – 76bda5c): playtest changes, convoy battles and the serial

From the user's playtest (0.9.1): the pocket environment is a nebula (a nebula backdrop) rather than a planet; the Comet, Meteor and Thunderbolt are bulbous teardrop "bullets with fins" (maximum radius 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.4 m, from 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.6) so they are fair targets; the dreadnought is scaled 1.25. Convoy battles (0.9.2, the user's design): convoy_ambush rebuilt around the clipper's twelve cargo pods, grappler tugs with saucer escorts and a 15-minute draw, flown from the map (R-STR-019). The 12-chapter arc (0.10.1): resources/default/strategy/story.yaml — twelve chapters triggered by progress, the Cartel's choice, side events, the Eclipse Engine plan, dynamic relations, the Dominion's strategist, four endings, an encyclopaedia, and the finale mission eclipse_assault (Story layer). Still to come: the chapters' bespoke special missions — chapters 1 – 11 fly the nearest existing mission (DEV-052); the 11 generated mission types; the Dominion's own logistics (5.11). Not play-tested.

docs.title: R-CPN-005 Interceptor campaign content
docs.text:
The interceptor campaign MUST express every system of the original from the player's data: the 27 mission types, the simulator types and the final mission's two parts, the 71 research topics, the 68 modules, the Doomsday arc and the alien strategist; values that the original keeps in code MUST be recorded as derived.

Rationale: Compatibility; the primary test case.

  • Implements: F-CPN-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (in progress: 26 mission types defined, DEV-041; the strategy layer, DEV-050). content::strategy::tests::original_tech_ids_become_research_prerequisites (synthetic); MT-4-22, MT-4-23
  • See: The Interceptor campaign mod, Coverage matrix

Progress (app 0.6.5, main b1f57ab)

packs/interceptor/missions/missions.yaml defines 26 mission types: the first five and 21 more (original types 3 – 5, 7 – 9, 12 – 14, 16, 18 – 23, 25 – 27, 29 and 30): base, corporate outpost, OPP and science-station defence; freighter convoys against aliens and pirates; deep-space ambush and encounter; the pirate squadron ambush; alien freighter ambushes; attacks on alien mining platforms, outposts and bases; the doomsday weapon. Names, briefings and debriefs are the original's own, by text key; compositions are derived estimates growing with the level (DEV-041). Soaked with the AI pilot at beginner, and at veteran for the hardest.

Open

The original's briefing keys run to 30; types 2, 6, 10 and 17 have no definition. Whether they are real mission types is unknown — the earlier count of 27 (issue #17's "remaining 22") is one more than the 26 now defined. Also not yet defined as their own entries: the simulator types and the final mission's two parts. The strategy layer (below) has not been play-tested: a six-month automatic run researches 4 of 71 topics on one downlink, so the research pace and every DERIVED value need the developer's judgement; the original's per-outpost evaluation, the Doomsday arc and the alien strategist are Stage 5.

Progress (app 0.8.0, main c64d178): the strategy layer

Plan item 4.12 is done as derived. tools/interceptor_strategy.py reads the player's GameSettings.ini and Interceptor.exe and writes packs/interceptor/strategy/references.yaml: the executable's tech-id table (12-byte entries {pointer to the R_ section name, string id, tech id}; derived — 67 of 69 TechRequired values resolve through it, eight Prereq links point to a topic of a higher Level, ids 75 and up are not in it) and inherit: references for 71 research topics, 55 items and 34 X-COM modules (section names and ids only; the values are read from the player's file at load). packs/interceptor/strategy/campaign.yaml authors the rest — a generated Frontier map, downlink research, hulls inherited from Ship_IntType1 – 3, module groups and effects, the X-COM base type, funding, raids flying the original mission types, pilots and scores — with every estimate marked DERIVED (DEV-050). New engine keys for it: tech_ids, economy.cost_scale, economy.module_time: days, start.money_from. Research unlocks are not authored: items, hulls and modules are gated by their own TechRequired. Of the original's 68 modules, the 34 X-COM ones are the player's; the alien ones belong to the strategist (Stage 5).

Progress (app 0.10.2, main 8926d11): the Doomsday arc

packs/interceptor/strategy/story.yaml holds the Doomsday arc — five alien messages with the guide's date, research and plan gates, the summoning of the MacArthur (the original's MAC_PROMPT1 key) and the final mission, whose win now sets doomsday_destroyed — the Doomsday plan (Structural, Weapon and Drive counts by difficulty, convoys passing X-COM space at a chance falling from 65 % to 45 % by difficulty, warnings by the original's DD_WARNING1 – DD_WARNING3 keys, completion = defeat by DD_TOOLATE), the last-base defeat (S_LASTBASEDEAD), a strategist and two of the seven side missions. Estimates are marked DERIVED; the saucer-examination topics in the gates are derived and unconfirmed (DEV-052). @keys now resolve in strategy and story texts; corporate funding weighs the month's score less (an ignored month no longer bankrupts). Still to come: five side missions, the alien strategist from Think.ini, report triggers. Not play-tested.

docs.title: R-CPN-006 Interceptor Remastered
docs.text:
interceptor-remastered MUST declare parent: interceptor and supply ×4 textures, ×2 images and an enhanced X-1A Lightning II mesh patch, all generated by recipes from the player's data.

Rationale: Proof that a mod extends a campaign.

  • Implements: F-CPN-005, F-MOD-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Interceptor Remastered

docs.title: R-CPN-007 Events and arcs
docs.text:
Events MUST have conditions, chances per check, actions, choices, offers and cooldowns; arcs MUST order steps whose state conditions can read.

Rationale: Story.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: implemented (app 0.10.0, main 485d01e)
  • Verified by: campaign::story::tests::arcs_fire_in_order_with_choices_missions_and_cooldowns; script::action::tests::a_text_argument_keeps_its_commas; campaign::tests::the_default_campaign_runs_a_year_with_its_story_and_stays_consistent; MT-5-01 – MT-5-03
  • See: Story layer, Format: missions, environments, events

As built (app 0.10.0)

events.<id>: when, check (daily, weekly, monthly, after_battle, on_research), chance per check, do (actions checked against EVENT_ACTIONS), choices ({text, do}, chosen on number keys), once (default true), cooldown, arc. An offer is the mission(x) action: the player flies it at once or declines. News is news(text). arcs.<id>.steps orders events; a step fires only after the one before it; arc(x) and fired(x) read the state. The format is a simpler subset of the design (DEV-051).

docs.title: R-CPN-008 Rival plans and strategist
docs.text:
A rival MUST pursue plans (stages, budgets, shipments by convoy, visibility, completion, warnings) and be run by a strategist with budgets, aggression, expansion, offence and defence priorities.

Rationale: An opponent with intent.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned — partly met (app 0.10.0, main 485d01e): plans with stages, shipments, completion and warnings; the strategist's aggression
  • Verified by: campaign::story::tests::plans_grow_from_shipments_that_get_through_and_can_end_the_campaign, relations_drift_and_the_strategist_answers_the_player; MT-5-04, MT-5-06
  • See: Story layer, Format: campaign and game flow, Format: strategy layer

As built (app 0.10.0)

plans.<id>: owner, stages ({name, count}), start_when, every and chance for shipment rolls, raid (a shipment is that raid's contact), warnings ({at, do}), complete. A shipment that reaches its destination unopposed adds one component; one intercepted and beaten adds nothing; plan(x) reads the progress. Visibility is the shipment's chance. The strategist is aggression only: strategist.aggression (start, min, max, up, down) and calm_after_wins; it multiplies every raid's chance, rises each month the player wins fewer than calm_after_wins battles and falls otherwise.

Open

Not built: plan budgets and grants if missed, plan_stage(x); the strategist's budgets, exploration, expansion, outposts, offence ladder, defence priorities, tech levels and cheats; the X-COM Think.ini values (DEV-051).

docs.title: R-CPN-009 Dynamic relations
docs.text:
Factions MUST have relations governed by relation rules, drift and stances, with effects in battle and on the strategy layer, and events on stance changes.

Rationale: A living setting.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned — partly met (app 0.10.0 – 0.16.2, main 485d01e, 76bda5c, 563c93f, 6b45fcb): drift, stances, raids and battle hostility follow them; mission outcomes move standings, and a stance change they cause is announced
  • Verified by: campaign::story::tests::relations_drift_and_the_strategist_answers_the_player, mission_outcomes_move_standings (the notice since app 0.16.2); app::flight::tests::campaign_stances_decide_who_fights_whom; MT-5-02, MT-5-05, MT-5-11, MT-6-12
  • See: Story layer, Format: strategy layer

As built (app 0.10.0 – 0.10.3)

relations: dynamic, start (standings −100..100), drift (monthly, towards 0), stances (upper bounds; above the last, allied). Story actions move standings (relation(f, n)); a stance change is announced. Strategy effect: a faction that is not hostile stops raiding. Battle effect (0.10.3): each campaign battle makes every faction with a standing hostile to the player, or not, by its stance (flight::apply_stances, Ruleset::set_hostile, in the battle's own rules). An income may read relation(f) (the default campaign's Senate stipend).

Open

Fixed in app 0.12.1 (main 563c93f): a mission outcome's relation(f, n) now moves the standing (Campaign::battle_result → change_standing). Fixed in app 0.16.2 (main 6b45fcb, #40): a stance change it causes is announced as soon as the strategy screen is back (Campaign::notices) and stops the clock, like a story event's. Not built: relation rules (standings moved by other things that happen in battle), standings between factions other than the player, allied factions fighting at the player's side, effects on prices and trade, stance-change events a campaign can react to (DEV-051).

docs.title: R-CPN-010 Victory, defeat and endings
docs.text:
A campaign MUST define victory and defeat and its endings, including partial victories.

Rationale: A beginning, middle and end.

  • Implements: F-CPN-006
  • Status: planned — partly met (app 0.10.0 – 0.16.14, main 485d01e, 87b04f3, de30c2a): endings and their conditions; an ending's video; a finished campaign shows its ending again; an ending screen
  • Verified by: campaign::story::tests::plans_grow_from_shipments_that_get_through_and_can_end_the_campaign; MT-5-07, MT-6-11, MT-6-26
  • See: Story layer, Format: campaign and game flow

As built (app 0.10.0)

endings.<id> (text, victory) and campaign_end (victory and defeat lists of {when, ending}), checked daily and after every battle, defeats first; the actions victory(x) and defeat(x). The ending stops the campaign and is saved. The default campaign has one victory and three defeats, interceptor one victory and two defeats.

Open

A partial victory is expressible (another ending with victory: true), but neither campaign defines one yet. The ending screen (app 0.16.14) has no image of its own; its music is the strategy screen's, with the good or bad stinger.

As built (app 0.12.1, main 87b04f3)

endings.<id>.video (an asset) plays full screen when the campaign ends that way, before the banner; the interceptor victory plays the original's credits film (original:credits_sm2a.smk). Loading a save whose story has ended sets the screen's ending again, so Campaign: continue shows the ending rather than a stopped map (the question left by MT-5-07).

As built (app 0.16.14, main de30c2a): the ending screen

The ending fills the window over the darkened map: VICTORY or DEFEAT, the ending's text, and the campaign's record (date, final score, battles won, bases and craft), with Credits and Main menu (Enter and Esc: the menu); both save first (#48).

docs.title: R-CPN-011 Screens and skins
docs.text:
Screens MUST be laid out in design spaces with skins (nine-slice panels, buttons, fonts, custom panels bound to queries); menus MUST cover options, difficulty, load/save, credits, endings and campaign and mod selection.

Rationale: Finished presentation.

  • Implements: F-CPN-007
  • Status: planned — partly met (app 0.11.1 – 0.16.14, main 2dd85dd, a7ea7b6, 563c93f, a18a7b4, dcf9563, ac7ae62, 6b45fcb, de30c2a): skins on the menu, launcher and strategy screen; title cards; a main menu with options (graphics: full screen; controls), load/save with slots, credits and an ending screen; the strategy screen's layout as data (screens.starmap, its background drawn) with buttons, lists and modal prompts
  • Verified by: content::screens::tests::a_layout_moves_only_what_it_names; app::widgets::tests::text_wraps_between_words_and_cuts_only_giant_words, lists_keep_the_selection_in_view, grids_and_hits; content::skin::tests::skins_parse_colours_with_fallbacks; app::ui::tests::nine_slices_keep_corners_and_stretch_the_rest; settings::tests::parses_and_round_trips (the default volumes only); app::menu::tests::the_menu_offers_continue_only_with_a_save (Load game and age_text since app 0.16.14), options_show_only_what_can_change (Full screen, Controls), volumes_step_in_quarters_and_stop_at_the_ends; app::credits::tests::the_roll_rises_from_below_and_ends_off_the_top; content::front::tests::menu_and_credits_parse_with_defaults; MT-6-04 – MT-6-06, MT-6-14 – MT-6-16, MT-6-19, MT-6-20, MT-6-22, MT-6-25 – MT-6-27; MT-4-29 – MT-4-33 (the strategy screen)
  • See: Skins, Screen layouts, Format: interface, text and media, Architecture › Presentation

As built (app 0.11.1 – 0.12.1)

skins.<id>: colours (seven roles: background, panel, border, text, dim, accent, highlight), panel: {image, slice} (a nine-slice frame) and font (a TrueType file); campaign.skin chooses one (else the first). app::ui::Ui gives the screens colour, panel and text; the launcher and the strategy screen draw through it. The default campaign has an art-deco skin with a generated gold-framed navy panel; interceptor a palette only. Title cards: the story action card(Title | text), drawn in the skin over the strategy screen; the default serial's twelve chapters open with them (app 0.11.1, main a7ea7b6). Options: settings.yaml audio: {music, effects}, stepped by the launcher's M and V keys (app 0.12.1). Main menu and credits (app 0.14.0, main a18a7b4, plan item 6.2): a campaign with a strategy layer opens on app::menu::MainMenu — Continue (with a save), New campaign, Battles & tools (the launcher), Options (campaign, difficulty, physics, music, effects; Left/Right), Credits, Quit — styled by campaign.menu {title, subtitle, showcase, starfield_seed} and playing the music's menu state (else strategy); app::credits rolls campaign.credits.lines (# headings) then the engine's credits, or plays credits.video (interceptor: the CD's credits film); --credits. Leaving the map, the launcher or a film returns to the menu.

As built (app 0.14.2 – 0.16.0): screen layouts, buttons and prompts

Screen layouts (app 0.16.0, main ac7ae62, content::screens): screens.<id>: {design: [w, h], background, widgets: {<name>: [x, y, w, h]}}. The engine owns each screen's logic and widgets and gives each widget a default place; a pack moves only the widgets it names (a widget name the screen does not have is a load error). Only starmap (the strategy screen) is laid out so far, with the widgets top, map, nav, info and panel in a 1280 × 720 default design space. Unlike a cockpit, a screen stretches its design space to fill the window (x and y scaled separately; text by the smaller factor). Buttons, lists and modal prompts (app::widgets): immediate-mode buttons, button rows and grids, a scrolling ListView, word wrapping and modal prompts with buttons, drawn in the skin; the strategy screen uses them for every action (R-STR-010). Menu option values (app 0.14.2, main dcf9563): a value too long for the room beside its label is drawn smaller (menu::fit_size, never below half size) — the interceptor pack is now named X-COM: Interceptor.

Open

Not built: layouts for screens other than the strategy screen (the main menu, launcher, credits and ending screen are placed in code); custom panels bound to queries, skin sounds; brightness in the menu (it is in settings.yaml); the interceptor screens with the original's wrapper art at 640 × 480 — the WrappersDLL layouts are not mapped (6.7) — now specified, with the original-style multi-screen interface, as Strategy interface R-UI-001 – R-UI-040 (plan item 6.9); custom cockpit instruments bound to queries (the rest of 6.6).

As built (app 0.16.2 – 0.16.14, main 6b45fcb, de30c2a)

screens.<id>.background is drawn (0.16.2): stretched over the window behind the strategy screen's widgets, reported once on standard error when it cannot be loaded. The main menu (0.16.14, #48) gains Load game — the automatic save and three slots with how long ago each was written (menu::age_text), the slots written from the strategy screen's Save — and two options: Full screen (switched at once, remembered as graphics.fullscreen; --windowed overrides) and Controls (the controls screen, back to the menu). The campaign's end is an ending screen (R-CPN-010).

docs.title: R-CPN-012 Video and music
docs.text:
The engine MUST play the original's Smacker cut-scenes and talking heads and image-sequence video for mods, and interactive music with states, segments, switches and stingers.

Rationale: Finished presentation.

  • Implements: F-CPN-007, F-CMP-002
  • Status: planned — partly met (app 0.11.0 – 0.16.2, main 1f183d1, 5163a57, 87b04f3, 76d64d5, 747d1e9, 6b45fcb): interactive music with states, segments and stingers (good and bad too since 0.16.2); the original's Smacker films (transmissions, credits, the opening); the comms panel with faces
  • Verified by: content::music::tests::sets_parse_and_the_state_follows_the_nearest_enemy; audio::music_tests::segments_cycle_within_the_wanted_state; app::comms::tests::the_panel_lasts_the_clip_and_the_signal_moves; the formats::smacker tests (R-CMP-010); MT-6-01 – MT-6-03, MT-6-07 – MT-6-11, MT-6-13, MT-6-21, MT-6-23, MT-6-24
  • See: Music, Cutscenes › Videos, Format: interface, text and media

As built (app 0.11.0 – 0.13.0)

Music (music.<id>: states — cruise, threat, battle, strategy, each a list of segments — stingers, threat_range, battle_range, volume): audio::MusicPlayer plays one segment at a time and changes state only at a segment's end. In a battle the set is chosen by the battle's seed and the state by the nearest hostile (battle, threat or cruise); a decided result plays victory or death; the strategy screen plays the first set's strategy state; other screens are silent. interceptor maps the original's three loop sets from Loops/*.wav by name; the default campaign's music is synthesised (tools/default_assets/music.py). Video: an in-crate Smacker decoder and app::video::VideoPlayer (letterboxed, clock-timed, skip with Enter, Esc or a click), played by the story action video(<ref>), an ending's video, campaign.intro_video and --video; interceptor plays the five alien transmissions (alientrans1 – 5), the credits on victory and animation1 as the opening (derived: which film is the opening). Comms panel (app 0.13.1, main 747d1e9): voice sets gain name and face (a picture, or a Smacker clip — possibly original:<pack>.mps#<member> — looping while the voice speaks) and chatter gains speaker; app::comms::Comms shows the face and name top left for the clip's length plus 0.6 s (at least 2.5 s), animated signal bars when there is no face, and COMMS when there is no speaker. The default campaign has generated CRT portraits for Guard Wing and Colony Control.

Open

Not built: switches as data (the states follow a fixed nearest-hostile rule) and the original's .wtl transition tables (DEV-053); good and bad stingers in the default campaign's music (the engine plays them since app 0.16.2); CD audio tracks; interceptor's talking heads on the comms panel — the clips are read from mfdanim.mps (app 0.13.1) but which clip prefix (at_, as_, e_, w_) is which speaker is unknown, so no faces are mapped; image-sequence video and other video files for mods (MD3, R-MOD-046). Fixed in app 0.14.1 (main 16a9954): a film's soundtrack follows the effects volume, and the default campaign's music WAVs are committed.

As built (app 0.16.2, main 6b45fcb)

The good and bad stingers play on the strategy screen (#49): good for a battle won (as the map returns), research complete and a victory; bad for any other battle result and a defeat (DEV-059). Films and cutscenes skip on a click or a gamepad's Start, A or B as well as Esc and Enter (app::skip_pressed, #65). --check loads every voice and chatter clip, music segment and stinger, and the voice sets' faces (#50).

docs.title: Cockpit & HUD requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for cockpits, views, instruments, the targeting display, the layout editor and visibility.

Features: Cockpit & HUD. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-HUD-001 Cockpit per hull, scaled to the window Implemented R-HUD-002 Views Implemented R-HUD-003 HD and 3D cockpits Implemented R-HUD-004 Anchored 3D-cockpit instruments Implemented R-HUD-005 Radar, shield rings and ship status Implemented R-HUD-006 Gauges, readouts and messages Implemented R-HUD-007 Targeting display Implemented R-HUD-008 Cockpit layout editor Implemented R-HUD-009 Drift display Implemented R-HUD-010 Brightness setting Implemented R-HUD-011 Other craft visible at combat ranges Implemented R-HUD-012 Atmosphere instruments Implemented R-HUD-013 Wide-screen side bands Implemented

docs.title: R-HUD-001 Cockpit per hull, scaled to the window
docs.text:
Each hull MUST have its cockpit (interceptor: A = Lightning II, B = Firestar, C = Super Avenger, DEV-014); a cockpit's design space MUST be scaled as large as fits and centred while the 3D view fills the window.

Rationale: Original cockpits on modern displays (DEV-006).

  • Implements: F-HUD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::layout_scales_by_height_and_centres; MT-1-08
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-002 Views
docs.text:
Views F1–F8 MUST place the camera for the cockpit, chase and external views; the manual chase camera MUST orbit and reset.

Rationale: Original views.

  • Implements: F-HUD-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: app::flight::views_place_the_camera, chase_orbit_responds_and_resets; MT-1-09
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-003 HD and 3D cockpits
docs.text:
A cockpit MAY declare its own design space and HD art, or be a 3D model; a 3D cockpit's field of view MUST widen only on windows narrower than its design.

Rationale: Modding first (DEV-033).

  • Implements: F-HUD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: app::flight::cockpit_fov_widens_only_on_narrow_screens; MT-1-25, MT-1-26, MT-2-14
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpits (HD and 3D)

docs.title: R-HUD-004 Anchored 3D-cockpit instruments
docs.text:
Instruments of a 3D cockpit MUST be drawn in perspective at anchors on the dashboard surface, so they stay in their bezels at any window shape.

Rationale: User feedback (plan item 2.21).

  • Implements: F-HUD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::layout::corners_lie_on_the_surface_with_world_up, rays_pick_the_nearest_surface; MT-2-15
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpits (HD and 3D)

docs.title: R-HUD-005 Radar, shield rings and ship status
docs.text:
Radars MUST place contacts by angle on front and rear scopes in faction colours; the front scope MUST ring the fore shield and the rear scope the aft shield, green, amber, red, blinking when down.

A ship status instrument (ship_status) MUST show the player's craft from above, tinted by the fraction of its hull left (green when whole, through amber, to red), inside a fore arc (ahead) and an aft arc (behind). Each arc MUST have up to three bands, one lit per third of that facing's shield (a facing above two thirds lights three; a facing at or below 2 % lights none), in the same green / amber / red colours as the rings and blinking when the facing is down. A cockpit MAY place it anywhere; the glass HUD MUST show it.

Rationale: Situational awareness; shield state at a glance (DEV-037). The ship status display is a user request after a playtest (app 0.15.1): the round ship display in the X-COM cockpit art showed nothing, and the single shield needle summed both facings. Its look follows the shield display of X-Wing.

  • Implements: F-HUD-003
  • Status: implemented (ship status: app 0.15.1, main bf963b4)
  • Verified by: hud::radar_places_contacts_by_angle, hud::draw::shield_rings_go_green_amber_red_then_blink, hud::draw::tests::ship_status_bands_follow_thirds_of_the_shield; MT-1-35, MT-2-28, MT-2-30, MT-6-17, MT-6-18
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD, Cockpits › The ship status display

As built (app 0.15.1)

hud::draw::draw_ship_status: the arcs are 140° wide, centred ahead and behind; shield_bands(fraction) gives the lit bands and hull_color(fraction) the craft's tint. The default campaign's 3D cockpit and the glass HUD place ship_status where gauge 3 (the summed shield needle) was. The interceptor cockpits A, B and C place it in their art's round display; the rectangles were set by eye (derived), and the layout editor (F12) adjusts them. Gauge 3 remains an instrument a cockpit may still place.

docs.title: R-HUD-006 Gauges, readouts and messages
docs.text:
The HUD MUST show speed, energy, shield and hull gauges, the power settings and system lamps, MFD pages (including Systems) that cycle, and a message line that expires and keeps the newest. Text MUST be fitted to its instrument. Cockpits that do not place the power or systems instruments MUST get fallback panels.

Rationale: The pilot must always know the craft's state.

  • Implements: F-HUD-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::gauges_sweep_and_read_the_ship, power_and_system_readouts, mfd_pages_cycle_and_describe, messages_expire_and_keep_the_newest; hud::draw::lamp_grids_follow_the_panel_shape; hud::glyphs::sizes_snap_down_onto_the_ladder; MT-2-21, MT-2-29
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-007 Targeting display
docs.text:
The HUD MUST bracket the target, show a lead marker where shots will meet it, show lock progress and lock, point to an off-screen target, and mark the selected nav point.

Rationale: Gunnery and navigation.

  • Implements: F-HUD-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::lead_point_anticipates_motion; MT-1-10, MT-1-12, MT-1-17
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpit and HUD, Deviations (DEV-002)

docs.title: R-HUD-008 Cockpit layout editor
docs.text:
F12 in the cockpit view MUST open an editor that drags and resizes 2D instruments, places instruments on a 3D cockpit by ray-picking, and saves the layout as a valid addon.

Rationale: User feedback (plan item 2.22).

  • Implements: F-HUD-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::layout::dragging_and_scaling, saved_layouts_are_valid_rules; MT-2-16, MT-2-17
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Cockpits (HD and 3D)

docs.title: R-HUD-009 Drift display
docs.text:
The speed indicator MUST show forward speed and the sideways (X) and vertical (Y) components of the velocity in the craft's frame; the HUD SHOULD show a flight-path marker where the velocity vector points.

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-006): newtonian flight allows drift the pilot cannot otherwise see.

In the glass HUD's status line this is THR 60% 312 m/s X+45 Y-12: forward speed, then sideways (X, + right) and vertical (Y, + up) drift in whole metres per second, signed. The flight-path marker is a circle with three ticks at the point the velocity vector projects to; with no drift it sits on the crosshair.

  • Implements: F-HUD-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::tests::body_velocity_reads_drift_in_the_ships_own_axes, hud::draw::tests::drift_reads_signed_whole_metres_per_second; MT-3-13
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

Open

How the original cockpits' speed gauge would show three values is not designed: the drift readout is on the status line, which every view shows. The marker's look is settled (above).

docs.title: R-HUD-010 Brightness setting
docs.text:
The player MUST be able to set the picture's brightness in the settings, where 1 means as authored. The setting is graphics: {brightness: …} in settings.yaml, from 0.5 (darker) to 2 (brighter); values outside are clamped. It MUST lift dark tones more than bright ones (a gamma of 1 / brightness on the lit models).

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-007).

  • Implements: F-HUD-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: settings::tests::parses_and_round_trips; MT-3-16
  • See: Settings and data discovery, Settings (user guide)

Where it is set

The settings file only, for now; an in-game options screen belongs to Stage 6 (presentation).

docs.title: R-HUD-011 Other craft visible at combat ranges
docs.text:
Other craft MUST be visible to the player at combat ranges in every cockpit and view. The campaign's rules MUST set the lighting (flight: {lighting: {ambient, sun, rim, distant_dot}}): a rim light outlines hulls seen edge-on, and a craft on the player's radar MUST NOT be drawn smaller than distant_dot pixels — smaller craft are drawn as a dot in their radar colour (the objective colour if protected).

Rationale: User request (F-HUD-007): "it is difficult to see other fighters".

  • Implements: F-HUD-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::rules::tests::builds_typed_definitions_with_inheritance (the lighting keys); MT-3-15
  • See: Rendering, Mod file reference (flight)

Criterion

The measurable part is the minimum on-screen size (distant_dot, 4 px in both packs). Whether a craft is easy to see is judged in play (MT-3-15).

docs.title: R-HUD-012 Atmosphere instruments
docs.text:
In a battle over a ground (an atmospheric environment, R-MSN-008), the HUD MUST show:

  • on the status line, after the speed and flight flags, ALT n VS ±n: the height above the terrain directly below the craft and the vertical speed (+ up), in whole metres and metres per second;
  • in the forward view, an artificial horizon: a level horizon line straight ahead in the camera's compass direction, whatever the craft's pitch and roll, and a pitch ladder with shorter, labelled rungs at −20°, −10°, +10° and +20°.

In space neither is shown.

Rationale: Flight over terrain: the pilot needs to know how high they are, whether they are sinking, and which way is level.

  • Implements: F-HUD-008
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.0, main af003f6)
  • Verified by: hud::draw::tests::the_pitch_ladder_sits_ahead_at_its_angles; MT-3-44
  • See: Cockpit and HUD

docs.title: R-HUD-013 Wide-screen side bands
docs.text:
A 2D cockpit stays centred at its design aspect, filling the screen height. A cockpit MAY define wide: in its pack data: - blackout: true covers the side bands left and right of the art in color (default black); - from (design-space y, default 0) starts the bands lower, so only the sides of the dashboard are covered and space still shows beside the canopy; - left and right name images stretched to fill each band below from, over the colour (extension art made for wide screens). They must be the pack's own art, never original content.

The bands MUST be drawn after the 3D view and the cockpit art, and before the instruments. They MUST NOT change the field of view or the instrument layout.

Rationale: 4:3 cockpit art on wide screens (see F-HUD-009).

  • Implements: F-HUD-009
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: hud::tests::side_bands_cover_the_screen_beside_the_cockpit; the rules test builds_typed_definitions_with_inheritance (keys); manual test on a 16:9 screen

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-HUD-001 – R-HUD-012 (12 requirements; 8 reverse-engineered from the code) 1.1.0 2026-11-11 R-HUD-009, R-HUD-010, R-HUD-011 implemented (app 0.3.1): drift status line and flight-path marker; graphics.brightness 0.5–2 as a gamma; flight.lighting with rim light and distant dots. R-HUD-010 and R-HUD-011 open notes resolved; R-HUD-009 keeps the original-cockpit question 1.8.0 2026-11-11 R-HUD-013 wide-screen side bands 1.11.0 2026-11-11 R-HUD-012 atmosphere instruments rewritten as built and implemented (app 0.6.0): ALT n VS ±n on the status line, the artificial horizon with a pitch ladder at ±10° and ±20° 1.17.0 2026-11-11 R-HUD-005 extended (user request): the ship status display — the craft from above tinted by hull, fore and aft arcs of up to three shield bands (app 0.15.1); renamed Radar, shield rings and ship status. R-HUD-013 added to the summary table

docs.title: Combat requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for weapons, damage, systems and power, special equipment, targeting, AI pilots, stations and the look of damage.

Features: Combat. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-CMB-001 Beam fire and energy Implemented R-CMB-002 Bolt travel Implemented R-CMB-003 Missile lock Implemented R-CMB-004 Missile guidance and damage modes Implemented R-CMB-005 Mines Implemented R-CMB-006 Layered damage Implemented R-CMB-007 Ship systems and repair Implemented R-CMB-008 Power settings Implemented R-CMB-009 Tractor and capture Implemented R-CMB-010 Cloak Implemented R-CMB-011 ECM Implemented R-CMB-012 Point defence Implemented R-CMB-013 Probes Implemented R-CMB-014 Targeting Implemented R-CMB-015 Wingman orders Implemented R-CMB-016 Behaviours as data Implemented R-CMB-017 AI missile discipline Implemented R-CMB-018 Station modules Implemented R-CMB-019 Model sets and damage looks Implemented R-CMB-020 Debris and explosions Implemented R-CMB-021 Shot physics Implemented

docs.title: R-CMB-001 Beam fire and energy
docs.text:
Each beam mount MUST have a cooldown of 1 / rate_of_fire; a group MUST fire only if there is energy for the whole group, otherwise report NoEnergy and hold for 0.5 s; link modes Linked (pairs), Full (all) and Unlinked (one at a time) MUST cycle.

Rationale: The original's gunnery model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::beams_fire_cost_energy_respect_cooldown_and_hit, beams_need_energy, link_modes_cycle_and_change_how_many_fire; MT-1-11
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-002 Bolt travel
docs.text:
A bolt MUST live for range / speed, start at its muzzle with its streak never reaching behind the muzzle, and inherit the firing ship's velocity plus the muzzle's turn velocity (R-CMB-021). Its streak MUST be drawn along its velocity relative to the viewer, so shots from a drifting craft streak straight out of its guns.

Rationale: Shots must look as if they leave the gun.

  • Implements: F-CMB-001, F-CMB-011
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::a_new_bolt_streak_never_reaches_behind_the_muzzle, a_bolt_leaves_with_the_muzzles_velocity_then_flies_straight; MT-1-34, MT-3-14
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-003 Missile lock
docs.text:
A lock MUST build while the target stays inside flight.lock_angle (10° by default, DEV-013) and within the missile's reach for the missile's lock_time, at a speed scaled by the sensors' efficiency and halved while the target's ECM is on; leaving the cone MUST reset it.

Rationale: The original's missile model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::lock_builds_in_the_cone_and_missile_homes_in, lock_is_lost_outside_the_cone_and_dumbfire_works; MT-1-12
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-004 Missile guidance and damage modes
docs.text:
Missiles MUST support the guidance kinds homing, dumbfire, sidestep, parallax decoys, cloaked wait, cluster and doppelganger, and the damage modes normal, bypass shields and enveloping. The proximity fuse MUST fire on a near miss (inside proximity_radius and moving away); a hit inside the target's shape MUST deal impact damage; empty racks MUST be reported and skipped.

Rationale: Every missile of both campaigns.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::guidance::homing_hits_and_dumbfire_misses_an_offset_target, sidestep_still_arrives, parallax_decoys_lure_enemy_missiles, cloaked_wait_sleeps_until_prey_comes_near, cluster_splits_into_submunitions, doppelganger_launches_a_decoy_ship_that_expires, damage_modes; sim::combat::proximity_fuse_fires_on_a_near_miss, empty_racks_report_and_cycle; MT-2-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missiles and mines, Deviations (DEV-010, DEV-036)

docs.title: R-CMB-005 Mines
docs.text:
A mine MUST stay in place and detonate with an area blast when an enemy comes within its trigger range.

Rationale: Original and default-campaign weapons.

  • Implements: F-CMB-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::mines_go_off_when_an_enemy_comes_near; MT-2-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missiles and mines

docs.title: R-CMB-006 Layered damage
docs.text:
Damage MUST strike the fore or aft shield (by the side hit), then armour, then hull; hull at zero MUST destroy the ship and make every ship targeting or towing it let go; a shield facing reaching zero MUST say "FORE/AFT SHIELD DOWN".

Rationale: The original's damage model.

  • Implements: F-CMB-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::damage_layers_and_aft_shield; MT-1-13
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-007 Ship systems and repair
docs.text:
Each system MUST have hit points and a condition: full effect above half, half effect at or below half, stopped at zero until repaired back to 25 %, destroyed for the battle below −destroy_below × hit_points. Damage past the armour MUST strike a random system; repair MUST take the worst system first. A ship whose engines and manoeuvring are out MUST drift disabled.

Rationale: The original's system damage; thresholds are engine values (DEV-029).

  • Implements: F-CMB-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::damage_knocks_systems_out_and_repairs_bring_them_back, systems_can_be_destroyed_beyond_repair, disabled_when_engines_and_manoeuvring_are_out; sim::ai::disabled_ships_drift; MT-2-03
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Rulesets

docs.title: R-CMB-008 Power settings
docs.text:
Beam and shield charge settings A–E and switched-on equipment MUST share power.budget steps; raising one setting MUST take from the other when the budget is full; cycling MUST wrap to A; the pilot MUST be able to transfer energy and move shield points fore and aft within caps; recharge MUST follow the settings.

Rationale: The original's power management, as charge settings (DEV-024).

  • Implements: F-CMB-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::raising_takes_power_from_the_other_setting, cycling_wraps_to_a, balance_caps_and_message, shield_balance_moves_points_forward_and_recharge_follows_power, requests_change_power_and_balance; sim::flight::energy_and_shields_recharge_up_to_capacity; MT-2-01, MT-2-02
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-009 Tractor and capture
docs.text:
The tractor MUST need power, a fitting and a disabled target in range; while it is on, beams MUST be off-line; a ship holding a disabled target when it jumps MUST capture it. An object of a towable class (a cargo container) MUST be towable even when not disabled; tractoring one mounted on a hub MUST tear it off, and a ship jumping while it holds one MUST capture it.

Rationale: Original capture of disabled craft; grappler tugs stealing cargo (the user's convoy design, app 0.9.2).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented (towable app 0.9.2, main 0d1c522)
  • Verified by: sim::systems::tractor_needs_power_a_fitting_and_a_target_in_range, tractor_holds_a_disabled_target_and_captures_it_on_jump; sim::ai::tugs_tow_disabled_enemies_away; sim::tests::a_tug_tears_a_container_off_and_prefers_a_disabled_ship; MT-2-04, MT-4-26
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-010 Cloak
docs.text:
A cloaked ship MUST vanish from enemy sensors beyond detection range; firing beams or a missile MUST drop the cloak with "CLOAK DROPPED".

Rationale: Original equipment; no invisible attacks (DEV-025).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::cloaked_ships_vanish_from_enemy_sensors_beyond_range; MT-2-05
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-011 ECM
docs.text:
While ECM is on, incoming missiles MUST lose their target and enemy lock MUST build at half speed.

Rationale: Original equipment.

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::ecm_makes_incoming_missiles_lose_their_target; MT-2-06
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-012 Point defence
docs.text:
A ship with point defence MUST fire at the nearest hostile missile (decoys included) within range when cooled down and with energy, roll chance on the world's seeded generator, and spend energy per shot.

Rationale: Capital ships and stations defend against missiles (values derived, DEV-038).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::point_defence_shoots_down_hostile_missiles; MT-2-31
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes

docs.title: R-CMB-013 Probes
docs.text:
A sensor probe MUST extend its side's radar to 8 km around it; a jamming probe MUST halve hostile radar range and missile-lock speed within 2.5 km; the radar MUST hide cloaked ships.

Rationale: Original probes given battle effects (derived, DEV-039).

  • Implements: F-CMB-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::probes_extend_radar_and_jam_their_enemies; MT-2-32
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes

docs.title: R-CMB-014 Targeting
docs.text:
The pilot MUST be able to cycle targets forwards and backwards with wrap-around, select the nearest hostile (ignoring friends and protected objectives) and select the most central ship in the sights.

Rationale: Original targeting keys.

  • Implements: F-CMB-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::targeting::cycles_forwards_and_backwards_with_wraparound, nearest_hostile_ignores_friends, in_sights_picks_the_most_central, nothing_to_target; sim::protected_objectives_are_not_picked_as_the_nearest_enemy; MT-1-10
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-015 Wingman orders
docs.text:
Wingmen MUST hold formation slots and obey: formation (ignore my target), attack my target, fire at will, evasive (10 s), retreat (flee and jump out) and status report, given from a comms menu.

Rationale: Original wingman commands.

  • Implements: F-CMB-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::wingman_closes_on_its_slot, orders_switch_wingmen_to_attack, evasive_ends_and_retreat_jumps_out; app::flight::commands_target_and_order_wingmen; MT-1-14, MT-2-08
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-CMB-022 Wingmen keep their distance
docs.text:
A wingman's formation slot MUST come from a named formation (formations:, R-MOD-047): the mission role's formation:, else flight.formation (default vee); wingmen of every wingman role MUST take successive slots of it. The slot MUST lie at least flight.formation_gap (default 3) × the two ships' combined radii from the leader; a closer slot from data is pushed out along its own direction. The wing order Wingmen: next formation (Shift+O) MUST move the player's wingmen into the campaign's next formation, in list order, wrapping.

Every moving AI pilot — wingmen and enemies alike — MUST avoid collisions predictively: it MUST project each other object's path against its own (constant velocities) to their closest approach within AVOID_HORIZON (2.5 s; 1 s for static objects and for its own target, so that firing passes are not broken off), and when the miss would be under 1.5 × the combined radii + 10 m (static objects: the combined radii + 30 m), or the other is already inside twice the combined radii and closing, it MUST steer to widen the miss and ease off if the danger is ahead. A leader MUST ignore its own wingmen (they keep clear of it); static objects and turrets MUST NOT avoid.

Rationale: The user's request (see F-CMB-007): wingmen collided with the player and kept pushing.

  • Implements: F-CMB-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::ai::formation_slots_keep_a_gap_from_the_leader, sim::ai::a_wingman_steers_clear_of_the_leader, sim::ai::collision_avoidance_predicts_the_closest_approach, sim::ai::tests::the_formation_order_cycles_the_campaigns_formations; mission::tests::wingmen_take_successive_slots_of_their_formation; content::formation::tests::shapes_place_followers_behind_and_beside_the_leader, custom_slots_then_a_vee_and_errors; MT-3-62, MT-3-63, MT-4-01
  • See: Formations (modding), Simulation › AI

Formations (MD1, app 0.6.6, main 6d390d7)

Slots come from formations: pack data (content::formation) instead of the fixed side offsets: shapes vee, line_abreast, echelon, box, diamond or a custom slots: list, in units of spacing. Both campaigns ship the five shapes in rules/formations.yaml. An unknown formation is a load error.

From user feedback (app 0.6.7, main c0e2516)

The user's playtest reported wingmen and enemies ramming each other and the player. Avoidance was reactive and for wingmen only; it is now predictive and for every moving AI pilot (ai::avoid_collision). The default guard_station was given hit_points: {per_level: [11000, 8000, 8000, 8000]} and defend_station two raiders at cadet, keeping R-MSN-011's 150 s undefended promise with the AI wasting fewer runs.

docs.title: R-CMB-016 Behaviours as data
docs.text:
AI pilots MUST be driven by behaviour definitions: states using the built-in manoeuvres (idle, circle, patrol, attack, evade, retreat, turret, tow, escort, travel, mine), transitions on conditions, skill (aim, reaction), fire discipline, turret arcs, target preferences (prefer) and systems use (cloak, ECM, power). Any definition MUST accept difficulty variants and {per_level: …} values.

Rationale: Modding first; the original's AI is code, so its behaviours are derived (DEV-031, DEV-032).

  • Implements: F-CMB-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::behaviour::parses_states_transitions_and_skill, reports_mistakes, the_builtin_attack_is_valid, target_preferences_parse_and_reject_unknown_selectors; sim::ai::transitions_switch_states_on_conditions, aim_skill_decides_accuracy, turrets_fire_off_the_nose, escorts_hold_formation_until_a_hostile_comes_close; sim::preferences_pull_the_ai_past_a_nearer_target, sim::ai_pilots_switch_cloak_ecm_and_power_by_condition; MT-2-20, MT-2-27, MT-2-33
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: behaviours and scripting, Behaviours and conditions

Added (app 0.9.2): escort, travel, tow escape

escort flies in formation on the leader the mission gives (escort: on the role) and attacks a hostile within range of the leader or itself; travel flies straight on for range, then jumps; tow takes a towable object when no disabled ship is near, skips a prize another ship is towing, and hauls it escape (default 2.5 km) before jumping.

docs.title: R-CMB-017 AI missile discipline
docs.text:
AI pilots SHOULD launch missiles only when closing on their target, staggered between pilots, each pilot drawing from its own random sequence.

Rationale: Missiles from every enemy at once overwhelmed the player.

  • Implements: F-CMB-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: None recorded.
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (architecture)

Open

No unit test names this behaviour; one should be added.

docs.title: R-CMB-018 Station modules
docs.text:
Modules MUST mount at a hub's attachment points (OBJ slot_<name> groups, original manipulators by index), follow the hub, provide turrets and shield generators, and fall with the hub, leaving wrecks in their destroyed look. Any ship class MAY be a hub: a module MUST NOT collide with its own hub or with another module of the same hub, a craft's collision avoidance MUST ignore its own modules, and the modules still mounted MUST leave by hyperspace with their hub.

Rationale: Base assaults and defences.

  • Implements: F-CMB-009
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::station_modules_mount_follow_and_fall_with_their_hub, sim::tests::cargo_modules_count_until_torn_off_destroyed_or_jumped_away_with_the_hub (a moving hub keeps its speed; modules jump with it), formats::obj::slot_groups_become_attachment_points; MT-2-22, MT-2-23, MT-4-26
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Stations, modules and probes, Deviations (DEV-035)

Open

Damage zones on hubs are not built (Stage 2 deferred list).

docs.title: R-CMB-019 Model sets and damage looks
docs.text:
A model set MUST define the intact model, texture swaps that accumulate with damage levels (by hull fraction), and named states that may swap the texture, the mesh and the debris set; the viewer MUST show every look.

Rationale: Visible damage; construction stages.

  • Implements: F-CMB-010, F-STR-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::looks::swaps_accumulate_with_damage_and_state, texture_keys_ignore_folders_case_and_extensions; app::viewer::looks_cover_damage_states_and_debris; MT-2-25
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: objects and models, Looks

Playtest (app 0.9.1): size

A model set's scale scales its collision shape with it: the default campaign's dreadnought is set to 1.25. The default fighters were rebuilt larger (maximum radius 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.4 m for the Comet, Meteor and Thunderbolt, from 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.6) after the user found them too hard to hit — a content change, no requirement text changed.

Open

Slot size classes, overlay groups and lod<n>_* files are not built (Stage 2 deferred list).

docs.title: R-CMB-020 Debris and explosions
docs.text:
Destruction MUST spawn the object's debris set (pieces with offsets, speed and spin ranges, random picks, lifetimes, seeded) and its effect (fireball size, duration, colour, optional shock wave, sound).

Rationale: Feedback on kills; engine fireballs stand in for sprites (DEV-034).

  • Implements: F-CMB-010
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::looks::debris_and_effects_parse_with_defaults; render::effects::events_create_effects_that_expire, explosion_curve_grows_and_fades; MT-1-13, MT-2-25
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Looks

Open

XSPT sprite explosions, shield flashes, lights and debris collisions are deferred.

docs.title: R-CMB-021 Shot physics
docs.text:
A ruleset option MUST choose how shots move, and the default MUST be physics: a shot MUST leave the muzzle with the craft's velocity plus the craft's turn velocity at the muzzle (angular velocity × muzzle offset) plus its own muzzle speed, and once fired MUST move independently of the craft's orientation.

The option is flight: {bolt_frame: world | ship}. world (the default) is the physics above. With ship, a shot MUST move in its owner's frame for flight.bolt_carry (a time, default 0.3 s), turning with the nose, and then fly straight with its last velocity.

Rationale: User request (F-CMB-011); decision D1.

  • Implements: F-CMB-011
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::combat::a_bolt_leaves_with_the_muzzles_velocity_then_flies_straight, with_bolt_frame_ship_a_bolt_turns_with_the_nose_while_carried; content::rules::builds_typed_definitions_with_inheritance; MT-3-14
  • See: Simulation, Mod file reference (flight)

docs.title: R-CMP-001 Finding the player's data
docs.text:
The original data MUST be found in this order: command line, environment, settings, the user data folder, the development tree; explicit and existing locations MUST win.

Rationale: Works without --data (plan item 1.14).

docs.text:
Original resources MUST be found by name whatever the layout of the player's copy.

  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::vfs::original_data_is_found_by_name_in_any_layout

docs.title: R-CMP-003 PE resources
docs.text:
Resources MUST be read from the original DLLs by type and name, as data; non-PE and truncated files MUST be errors.

docs.title: R-CMP-004 XMSH meshes
docs.text:
XMSH meshes MUST be read with their LODs, signed edge loops, untextured polygons and polygon flags, mirrored into engine handedness with outward winding, triangulated and grouped; overlapping overlay faces MUST be layered by depth bias.

docs.title: R-CMP-010 Smacker video
docs.text:
Smacker video MUST be decoded in-crate for the original cut-scenes and MFD talking heads.

Rationale: Faithful presentation.

  • Implements: F-CMP-002
  • Status: implemented (app 0.12.0 – 0.13.1, main 5163a57, 644b218, 319a31b, 747d1e9) — the decoder, the cut-scenes, and the talking-head clips inside mfdanim.mps
  • Verified by: formats::smacker::tests::small_and_big_trees_decode_with_the_cache, palettes_decode_explicit_kept_and_copied_entries, a_tiny_file_decodes_a_solid_frame, audio_dpcm_8_bit_mono; formats::mpsrc::tests::a_pack_lists_and_returns_its_members; by hand against all 11 of the reference CD's videos with the ignored real_smacker_file_decodes (OI_SMK); MT-6-07, MT-6-08
  • See: Smacker video, Architecture › Formats

As built (app 0.12.0)

formats::smacker decodes SMK2 and SMK4: the four big Huffman trees (built from two small trees each, with the three-slot escape cache reset every frame), mono, full (with version 4's two half-resolution modes), skip and solid 4 × 4 blocks, delta palettes, and DPCM or raw audio, 8- or 16-bit, mono or stereo, on up to seven tracks. Written from the format's public description; SMACKW32.DLL is never used. Bad data returns an error.

Talking heads (main 319a31b, app 0.13.1)

The MFD talking heads are 113 Smacker clips bundled in mfdanim.mps, an MPSRC pack (format), now read by formats::mpsrc; a member is addressed as original:mfdanim.mps#<member> and decodes like any Smacker file. The comms panel (app 0.13.1) can show one as a voice's face. Still open: which clip belongs to which speaker (the at_, as_, e_, w_ prefixes) is unknown, so the interceptor voices have no faces yet.

docs.title: R-CMP-011 Bad data never panics
docs.text:
Every reader MUST return an error with a readable message on bad, truncated or out-of-bounds data, never panic.

docs.title: R-CMP-012 No original content
docs.text:
No original asset may enter the repository or a published build in any form; tests MUST use synthetic data built in the test; original binaries MUST be read as data only and never executed.

Rationale: The player supplies the data (project rule).

docs.title: R-CMP-013 Facts and deviations marked
docs.text:
Facts derived from the original data MUST be marked verified, derived or unknown, and every knowing difference from the original MUST be recorded as a deviation.

Rationale: An undocumented deviation looks like a bug.

  • Implements: F-CMP-004
  • Status: implemented

docs.title: R-CMP-014 Resources folder
docs.text:
Content bundled with the game MUST live under resources/: - The default campaign's pack MUST be resources/default/, with all its assets in open formats (YAML, OBJ, PNG/TGA, WAV), generated by tools/default_assets or written by hand. - resources/xcom/ and resources/xcom-cd/ MUST be git-ignored, MUST contain nothing in the repository, and are where a player places original data. - The engine MUST load packs from resources/ (sub-folders with a pack.yaml; the original-data folders have none and are skipped) and from packs/, which holds the bundled mods such as interceptor. - A mod MUST still override resources, as packs did before. - The app bundle MUST ship resources/default and packs, and never resources/xcom*.

Rationale: it makes explicit what the game provides and what a mod or the player adds; a root game/ folder suggested the game was included.

  • Implements: F-CMP-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: cli::tests::content_dirs_are_resources_then_packs; scripts/check.sh refuses tracked files under resources/xcom* (and the old game/).
  • See: Getting started → Folder layout, Settings and data discovery

docs.title: R-CMP-015 Installed copy or CD copy
docs.text:
When no path is given (--data, OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA, settings.yaml paths.original, <user data>/original), a development checkout MUST look for original data in resources/xcom/ (an installed copy) first, then resources/xcom-cd/ (a CD copy). Both layouts MUST work: original files are found by file name anywhere under the folder.

Rationale: an installed copy is the more likely thing a player still has.

  • Implements: F-CMP-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: settings::tests::original_data_is_found_in_order (an empty resources/xcom is skipped; once it holds files it wins over resources/xcom-cd).
  • See: Settings and data discovery

docs.text:
A controls menu, reachable from the launcher and the pause menu (K), MUST capture keys and gamepad presses and chords, take a captured binding from any other action, clear and reset bindings, and edit device settings (dead zone, invert pitch, stick layout, mouse range and invert).

docs.title: R-CON-005 Gamepad
docs.text:
Gamepads MUST work with sticks, buttons, a dead zone and a modifier layer (holding the left shoulder reaches a second layer that covers every power control); a button used as a modifier MUST do nothing on its own.
