docs.title: R-CON-006 Mouse flight and chords
docs.text:
Mouse flight MUST be a toggle; a Shift chord MUST NOT also trigger the plain key; one-shot presses MUST be carried to the next simulation tick when a frame runs none.

Rationale: Menus usable; no lost presses on high-refresh displays (DEV-004, DEV-015).

  • Implements: F-CON-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::mouse_flight_only_when_enabled, a_shift_chord_does_not_also_trigger_the_plain_held_key, one_shot_commands_and_shift_chords; sim::unconsumed_presses_carry_over_held_inputs_do_not; MT-1-06
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-CON-007 Action catalogue
docs.text:
Each action MUST have, in the one action table (R-CON-001), an id, a display name, a group and a short description, so that the bindings, the controls overlay and the console's catalogue message are generated from it.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-003): one catalogue drives keys, the overlay and the console.

  • Implements: F-CON-003, F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::the_keys_help_lists_every_action_with_its_current_keys, every_action_is_reachable_from_keyboard_and_flight_actions_from_the_pad, input::tests::every_action_has_a_one_sentence_description; remote::protocol::tests::the_idle_catalogue_lists_every_action_with_its_description_and_all_available; app::flight::tests::the_keys_help_shows_descriptions_only_when_the_columns_are_wide_enough; MT-3-18, MT-3-65
  • See: Input and gamepads

As built

input::ACTIONS is the catalogue: each entry has its id (name, the bindings.yaml name), a display name (label), its default keys and pad buttons, and its group. It drives parsing, the defaults, the controls menu and the keys overlay (input::help_rows); and, since C1 (app 0.4.0), the console's catalogue message (remote::protocol::catalogue). Since main bb04952 (app 0.15.1, GitHub #6) every entry also has a one-sentence, player-facing description: the catalogue sends it beside the label (in a battle and idle, through one builder, catalogue_with), the tablet shows it as a small two-line caption under each button and as the button's title, and the keys overlay prints it as a dimmer line under each action when its columns are wide enough, else one line per action (help_layout / help_place, pure and tested). help_rows returns HelpRow {label, description, keys}.

docs.title: R-CON-008 Controls overlay
docs.text:
A key MUST toggle an in-flight overlay listing the actions by group with their current bindings, without leaving the battle. The overlay is the action help, bound by default to ? (Shift+Slash) and Shift+F1; it pauses the battle and lists every action by group with the player's current keys and pad buttons ("unbound" if none). Esc or the help key closes it.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-003).

  • Implements: F-CON-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::the_keys_help_lists_every_action_with_its_current_keys; MT-3-18
  • See: Input and gamepads, Controls (user guide)

Resolved: F1 stays a view key

The request named F1, which selects cockpit view 1 (views F1–F8, an original key). F1 keeps its original meaning, so there is no deviation; the overlay uses ? and Shift+F1 (a Shift chord never triggers the plain key, R-CON-006). F12 is not used for it: F12 opens the cockpit layout editor in custom cockpits (R-HUD-008).

docs.title: R-CON-009 Console server
docs.text:
The game MUST be able to serve the console page and a WebSocket endpoint. The console MUST be off by default, MUST accept connections from the local network only, MUST require a pairing code, and MUST listen on port 8765 by default, with the port changeable in the settings if it conflicts.

Rationale: Decision D2: safe by default.

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: remote::server::only_local_network_peers_are_served, pairing_codes_are_six_digits_and_vary_with_the_seed, serves_the_page_pairs_and_relays_actions_over_a_real_socket; remote::http::parses_a_websocket_upgrade_and_waits_for_the_blank_line, bad_requests_are_errors_and_responses_are_well_formed; remote::ws::sha1_and_base64_match_the_published_test_vectors, frames_decode_masked_wait_for_more_bytes_and_encode, protocol_violations_are_errors; settings::tests::parses_and_round_trips (the console keys); MT-3-19
  • See: Console protocol, Remote console, Tablet console

Resolved (C1, app 0.4.0)

Settings keys: console: {enabled, port} in settings.yaml (default off, 8765), and --console / --console-port N for one run. Local network only: each accepted connection's peer address is checked (remote::server::is_local): private, link-local, IPv6 unique-local and loopback addresses (and IPv4-mapped forms of them) are served; any other connection is dropped without an answer. Pairing code: six digits chosen at start-up, printed in the terminal and shown at the bottom left of the flight screen with the URL until a console pairs (and while the menu is open); three wrong codes close the connection.

As built (app 0.4.7, main c42d773)

Pairing works on every screen. The server's connection thread answers a right code with welcome {version} itself, at once, so the page knows it is paired even when no battle is running (before 0.4.7 only the flight screen answered, and a tablet paired from the launcher waited for ever). The page pairs as soon as the sixth digit is typed (an iPad's number pad has no Enter key), shows Connecting… and its errors (Could not reach the game, a wrong code, Disconnected), and accepts the code in the address (/?code=123456, for a future QR code).

docs.title: R-CON-010 Console protocol
docs.text:
Game and console MUST exchange the JSON messages of the console protocol; the protocol MUST NOT depend on the transport.

Rationale: A later USB serial transport reuses it.

  • Implements: F-CON-004, F-CON-007
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::decodes_console_messages_and_refuses_unknown_ones, the_catalogue_lists_every_action_and_marks_missing_equipment; remote::json::parses_objects_arrays_strings_and_numbers, bad_and_hostile_input_is_an_error, writes_compact_objects_that_parse_back; remote::server::serves_the_page_pairs_and_relays_actions_over_a_real_socket
  • See: Console protocol

As built

Protocol version 1: hello, action, throttle from the console; welcome, denied, catalogue, telemetry from the game. Since app 0.4.7 the server sends welcome {version} the moment the code is right, and the flight screen sends welcome {version, campaign} again during a battle; outside a battle (the launcher) the game sends a catalogue with every action available and an idle telemetry {alive: false, state} twice a second. remote::protocol builds and decodes the JSON text only; the WebSocket framing is in remote::ws, so a serial transport can carry the same text.

docs.title: R-CON-011 Console actions are game actions
docs.text:
An action from the console MUST have the same effect as the bound input for that action from the catalogue; the console MUST NOT offer actions outside the catalogue.

Rationale: One set of actions, however they are triggered.

  • Implements: F-CON-003, F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: remote::tests::held_actions_last_until_released_and_taps_fire_once, remote::protocol::decodes_console_messages_and_refuses_unknown_ones; MT-3-20
  • See: Console protocol, Remote console

As built

Console input joins the frame's RawInput (remote_held, remote_pressed, remote_throttle) through remote::RemoteInput, and Bindings::translate treats a held or tapped console action exactly like a bound key; sim is untouched. Names outside input::ACTIONS are refused by the decoder. A console that disconnects releases everything it held.

A console that sends nothing for 1 s MUST have its held actions released (heartbeat ping every 250 ms), so a dropped connection never leaves an action held. Verified by remote::tests::a_silent_console_lets_go_but_a_pinging_one_keeps_holding.

docs.title: R-CON-012 Console page from web components
docs.text:
The console page MUST be built from custom web components and CSS, with no framework, and served by the game itself.

Rationale: Lightweight, dependency-free web UI (project dependency policy).

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented (C1 page app 0.4.0; the Cockpit layout and tiles in 0.4.11; the target viewport, map and themes in 0.4.14 – 0.5.0)
  • Verified by: remote::server::serves_the_page_pairs_and_relays_actions_over_a_real_socket (the page is served); MT-3-19 – MT-3-23, MT-3-29 – MT-3-32
  • See: Dependency policy, Remote console

As built (C1)

web/console/ (index.html, console.css, console.js) is embedded in the binary and served by the game. It is made of four custom elements (oi-pairing, oi-telemetry, oi-throttle, oi-actions) with no framework and no build step. This is the C1 page; the C2 page (tiles, themes) completes the requirement.

As built (C2 – C4, app 0.4.11 – 0.5.0)

The page now has thirteen custom elements: the C1 four plus oi-mode (the layout switch), oi-hud-strip, oi-shields, oi-display (the display console, with its Target and Map tabs), oi-target-view (hand-written WebGL 1, no library), oi-map (2D canvas), oi-power, oi-tiles and oi-static. Still no framework and no build step.

docs.title: R-CON-013 Console layout
docs.text:
The console MUST show the exterior-view HUD in its top row, a widened display console in the centre, shield rings and shield controls on the left, power sliders on the right, and the other functions grouped logically below. It SHOULD fit an iPad in landscape.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-004).

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.11, main db2f264, as the Cockpit layout of R-CON-026)
  • Verified by: MT-3-29

As built (C1)

The C1 page is a working layout, not the one required here: telemetry cells, a throttle slider, then every action as a button under its group title. The HUD row, display console, shield and power columns come with C2, as the Cockpit layout; the C1 layout stays as All-in-one (R-CON-026).

Open (resolved)

The grouping of the remaining functions: the nine catalogue groups, one tile each (R-CON-018).

docs.title: R-CON-014 Console telemetry
docs.text:
While paired, the game MUST send craft telemetry at 20 Hz and radar contacts at 5 Hz, and events as they happen.

Rationale: Real-time knowledge of the craft's condition.

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented (craft telemetry at 20 Hz since app 0.4.0; radar contacts at 5 Hz and events since 0.4.15, main e2b5012)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::telemetry_reports_drift_and_the_targets_relative_rotation, remote::protocol::tests::contacts_are_in_the_players_axes_and_targets_decode, hud::tests::the_message_log_reports_what_is_new_since_a_count; MT-3-19, MT-3-31
  • See: Console protocol

As built (C1)

Craft telemetry is sent at 20 Hz to every paired console (app::flight::FlightSession::console_frame). Radar contacts (5 Hz) and events were not sent yet in C1: they are the contacts and event messages on the Console protocol page, which came with C4 (below). Outside a battle (app 0.4.7) the launcher sends telemetry {alive: false, state: "launcher"} twice a second, which the page shows as Not flying (launcher).

As built (C4, app 0.4.15, main e2b5012)

contacts (protocol::contacts) is broadcast every 0.2 s by FlightSession::console_frame: every live craft on the player's radar (sim::systems::on_radar), in the player's own axes. Events are the pilot's message log: each new line becomes an event {text}, found with MessageLog::total and MessageLog::since, so the console sees exactly what the pilot's message line shows (system damage, locks, shields, mission results, radio). Fields: Console protocol.

docs.title: R-CON-015 Target viewport
docs.text:
The console's centre display MUST show the current target's model at its true orientation relative to the player's craft. The game MUST send each target class's mesh once, decimated.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-005).

  • Implements: F-CON-005
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.14, main e51eca9)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::tests::model_messages_are_normalised_and_coloured_per_group (textured groups carry a PNG and uvs); formats::png::tests::a_png_has_the_signature_chunks_and_stored_pixels, downscaling_averages_blocks; MT-3-30, MT-3-61
  • See: Console protocol, Remote console

As built (C3, app 0.4.14, main e51eca9)

The display console's Target tab draws the target's model with hand-written WebGL 1 (oi-target-view), flat-shaded, lit from the upper left, turned by telemetry.target.rotation. The game sends model {name, groups} when the target's class changes or a tablet pairs. Decimation is by level of detail: the most detailed LOD with at most 3000 triangles (protocol::MODEL_TRIANGLE_BUDGET; the coarsest if every LOD is larger), normalised to radius 1. No textures are sent: each material group has one colour, the texture's average (protocol::average_color, transparent pixels ignored) or the vertex colour of an untextured group. Messages are built once per class and cached in the flight screen. A video stream of the game's own rendering stays a possible later upgrade (GitHub issue #3).

Textured, from user feedback (app 0.6.7, main c0e2516)

The user asked for the target to look like the craft. Each textured group of the model message now also carries texture, its image downscaled to at most 128 px a side and encoded as a data:image/png;base64,… URL by the new in-crate writer formats::png (stored, uncompressed zlib blocks), and uvs, two per vertex. The page redraws each image onto a 128 × 128 canvas (WebGL 1 repeats only power-of-two textures, and the models' uvs run past 0..1) and samples it; the group's average colour shows until the image loads. Checked in headless Chrome.

Open (resolved)

The decimation budget (3000 triangles, by LOD) is settled; textures are sent since app 0.6.7 (above). Original meshes sent to a device on the player's own network stay on the player's equipment (no redistribution).

docs.title: R-CON-016 3D map view
docs.text:
The centre display MUST toggle between the target viewport and a 3D map view of the battle modelled on TIE Fighter's map.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-006).

  • Implements: F-CON-006
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.15, main e2b5012)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::tests::contacts_are_in_the_players_axes_and_targets_decode; MT-3-31
  • See: Console protocol, Remote console, Tablet console

As built (C4, app 0.4.15, main e2b5012)

The display console's Map tab (oi-map, 2D canvas) beside the Target tab. It draws the contacts around the player: a grid and range rings at a quarter, half and full radar range on the plane at the player's height; a height stalk from each contact to that plane; relation colours (friendly, hostile, neutral, objective); a label with name and range; a tick showing where each contact will be in 2 seconds. Views Behind, Top and Side; drag to orbit, pinch or the wheel to zoom. Tapping a contact, or a row of the list sorted by range, sends target {id}; the game targets it only if it is on the player's radar.

Open

Nav points and orders on the map (the contacts and ranges are in).

docs.title: R-CON-017 Serial transport
docs.text:
The console protocol SHOULD be carried over a USB serial link so a physical panel (Arduino) with lights and buttons can act as a console.

Rationale: User request (F-CON-007), longer term.

  • Implements: F-CON-007
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned (interlude item C5, later).
  • See: Console protocol

Open

Framing, the message subset a microcontroller handles, and pairing over serial.

docs.title: R-CON-018 Function-group tiles
docs.text:
The console MUST present one tile per function group, each a status card for its system group. Tapping a tile MUST collapse the other tiles to their headers and open a full-width control strip for that group; tapping the open group's title MUST collapse the strip so all status cards show; tapping another group's title MUST switch the strip to that group.

Rationale: Many options per function group stay manageable on a tablet (F-CON-008).

  • Implements: F-CON-008
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.11, main db2f264)
  • Verified by: MT-3-29
  • See: Console protocol, Tablet console

As built (C2, app 0.4.11, main db2f264)

oi-tiles in the Cockpit layout: one tile per catalogue group (the nine groups of catalogue), each a status card that also counts the controls not fitted. Tapping a tile opens a full-width strip with that group's buttons and folds the others to their headers; tapping the open title closes it; tapping another title switches. Checked in Chrome over the LAN address; iPad check pending.

docs.title: R-CON-019 Features the craft lacks are disabled, not hidden
docs.text:
Every function group MUST be shown for every craft. A control for a feature the current craft lacks (for example cloak or ECM not fitted, or no missiles) MUST appear disabled: greyed, not tappable and labelled as not fitted; the group's status card MUST show that feature as not fitted. Availability MUST be sent per action in the catalogue message and resent when the craft changes.

Rationale: All function groups are common to every craft by design; only individual features differ (user correction, F-CON-008).

  • Implements: F-CON-008
  • Status: implemented (catalogue and buttons app 0.4.0; the tiles' status cards 0.4.11)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::the_catalogue_lists_every_action_and_marks_missing_equipment; MT-3-21, MT-3-29
  • See: Console protocol

As built (C1)

Availability is sent per action in catalogue and resent when the craft class changes; the C1 page shows an unavailable action's button greyed, not tappable and labelled "not fitted". The group status cards arrive with the C2 tiles (R-CON-018): since app 0.4.11 each card reads, for example, Weapons · 2 not fitted.

Open

Whether a fitted but destroyed system is shown as not fitted or as damaged (read here: damaged, from telemetry).

docs.title: R-CON-020 Console theme from the active pack
docs.text:
The console's visual style MUST come from the active campaign or mod, delivered as a console theme in the theme message; a pack without a console theme MUST get a plain, clearly labelled default.

Rationale: Immersion matching the campaign (F-CON-009).

  • Implements: F-CON-009, F-MOD-001
  • Status: implemented (app 0.5.0, main 0a1c340)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::tests::themes_layer_per_cockpit_and_become_css_variables; MT-3-32
  • See: Console protocol, Console themes, Mod file reference

As built (C2b, app 0.5.0, main 0a1c340)

A rules section console: {theme: {colors, font, corner}, cockpits: {<id>: {colors, font, corner}}} (rules::ConsoleTheme, rules::ThemeLayer; schema files::console_theme). Colour names: bg, panel, line, ink, dim, hot, warn, danger, off. ConsoleTheme::for_cockpit layers the cockpit's overrides on the campaign's base. The theme {vars} message carries CSS variables (--bg … --off, --font, --corner): the base is sent on pairing (from the launcher), and the craft's layered theme with each catalogue in a battle. The page derives every colour from these variables (tints with CSS color-mix). A pack without a console section sends no variables, so the page keeps its own plain, labelled default.

docs.title: R-CON-021 Console theme assets are original-free
docs.text:
Console theme assets MUST be new art made for this project and kept in the pack's own files; the interceptor console theme MUST be styled after the current craft's cockpit overlay (palette and framing cues read at run time, or new art made in the same spirit) without reproducing any original art; every control MUST be clearly labelled. The default campaign's theme MUST follow its retro (art-deco) style.

Rationale: Never reproduce original content (project rule); legibility on a tablet.

  • Implements: F-CON-009, F-CMP-003
  • Status: implemented (app 0.5.0, main 0a1c340)
  • Verified by: remote::protocol::tests::themes_layer_per_cockpit_and_become_css_variables; MT-3-32
  • See: The default campaign, Console themes

As built (C2b, app 0.5.0, main 0a1c340)

Both themes are colours, a font list and a corner radius only: no images, so no art at all is shipped or copied. Default campaign (resources/default/rules/console.yaml): art-deco, brass lines on midnight panels, cream text, amber values, Futura, corner 2. interceptor (packs/interceptor/rules/console.yaml): the page's green instrument look, tinted per cockpit with that cockpit's accent colour, measured from the player's cockpit art (A olive bronze, B steel blue, C red); only the measured colours are written down. Every control keeps its text label.

docs.title: R-CON-022 Keep the tablet awake
docs.text:
The console MUST keep the tablet's screen awake while the page is open and visible. It MUST use the Screen Wake Lock API where the browser allows it and otherwise play a tiny, muted, looping inline video made for the project; it MUST take the lock again when the page becomes visible, and MUST show whether the screen is being kept awake. The server MUST serve the clip with HTTP range requests (206 Partial Content).

Rationale: User request, 2026-11-11: "tablet goes to sleep while page displayed; some function in page needs to keep alive. browser will keep tablet alive during media streaming for video display, so there are some kind of mechanisms in place to prevent sleep. Unclear to what extent this is possible." Safari offers the wake lock only on secure (https) pages, so an iPad on the plain-http console needs the video; iOS Safari plays video only from a server that honours ranges.

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: remote::http::ranges_are_served_as_partial_content; MT-3-26
  • See: Console protocol, Remote console, Tablet console

As built (app 0.4.8, main f1c8be8)

Written as planned and built in the same pass. The clip is web/console/keepawake.mp4 (black, 2 KB), generated with AVFoundation by tools/console_assets/make_keepawake.swift: the project's own output, not third-party. It is started on the pairing tap, again on any tap until it runs, and whenever the page becomes visible. Checked in headless Chrome over localhost (the wake-lock path) and over the LAN address (the video path); not yet on an iPad (MT-3-26).

docs.title: R-CON-023 Button press feedback
docs.text:
Every console button, tap or hold, MUST visibly show that it is pressed: its background MUST fill with the button's border colour and its text MUST turn black. A hold button MUST stay so while it is held; a tap MUST show it for at least 150 ms.

Rationale: User request, 2026-11-11: "Initial test on console works well, better button press feedback needed so that it's clean when user has pressed the button. for the style currently applied, the button should highlight with the border color and text switch to black. Add brief static effects when a craft is hit by weapons fire."

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.9)
  • Verified by: MT-3-27
  • See: Tablet console

docs.title: R-CON-024 Hit static
docs.text:
When the player's craft is hit by weapons fire, the console MUST show a brief static (noise) effect, about 0.4 s long and fading out: lighter when the shields absorb the hit, stronger when the hull is struck. telemetry MUST carry running counts of hits on the player's craft (hits) and of hull hits (hull_hits); the page plays the effect when a count rises.

Rationale: User request, 2026-11-11 (as R-CON-023): "Add brief static effects when a craft is hit by weapons fire."

  • Implements: F-CON-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.9)
  • Verified by: MT-3-27
  • See: Console protocol

Interpretation confirmed by the user (2026-11-11): works well

"A craft" is read as the player's craft, and the effect as appearing on the console (not on the game's screen, and not for hits on other craft). The user, 2026-11-11: "Hit static - correct, works well now".

docs.title: R-CON-025 Keys held at the start of a battle are ignored
docs.text:
Keys, gamepad buttons, triggers and mouse buttons that are held when a battle starts MUST be ignored until they are released; a fresh press of the same input MUST then work normally.

Rationale: User request, 2026-11-11: "When mission is started by pressing enter on the menu or restart prompt, a laser fires immediately at start of mission because of the enter press. that first keypress should be suppressed." Enter (and the pad's A button) both start a mission and fire or burn in flight.

  • Implements: F-CON-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: input::tests::keys_held_when_a_battle_starts_are_ignored_until_released; MT-3-28
  • See: Input and gamepads

As built (app 0.4.10, main 4edc9d7)

input::StartGuard records the keys, pad buttons, triggers and mouse button held on a battle's first frame and filters them out of every later frame until each is let go. It is applied first in the flight screen's frame, right after the devices are read, so the launcher's, the restart prompt's and the debrief's Enter never fires the guns.

docs.title: R-CON-026 Two console layouts
docs.text:
The console page MUST offer two layouts, switchable on the page and remembered per tablet:

  • All-in-one: the C1 layout — telemetry cells, the throttle slider, and every action group expanded as a grid of buttons;
  • Cockpit: the proposal's layout (R-CON-013) — the exterior-view HUD strip on top; the display console in the centre (target data now, the target viewport with C3, the map with C4); shield rings on the left; power sliders on the right; the function-group tiles below, expanding and collapsing (R-CON-018).

Rationale: User request, 2026-11-11: "ipad UI is very different from the design proposal but useful. the page should support two modes, the collected \"all-in-one\" control scheme in the current design, and the version from the proposal PDF."

  • Implements: F-CON-004, F-CON-008
  • Status: implemented (app 0.4.11, main db2f264): the mode switch (remembered per tablet, ?mode=), the Cockpit layout with HUD strip, shield rings and balance, display console (target data; the viewport came with C3 in 0.4.14 and the map with C4 in 0.4.15), power sliders (power {beam, shield, balance}), and tiles that open a full-width strip. Verified live in Chrome over the LAN address via the DevTools protocol; iPad check pending
  • Verified by: MT-3-29
  • See: Stage 3 interlude, Tablet console

R-CON-008 open note resolved: F1 stays the cockpit-view key, no deviation 1.4.0 2026-11-11 R-CON-011: held actions released after 1 s of silence (heartbeat). R-CON-014 status corrected to partial 1.3.0 2026-11-11 Console C1 (app 0.4.0): R-CON-009, R-CON-010, R-CON-011 and R-CON-014 implemented (R-CON-014: craft telemetry; contacts and events still planned); R-CON-012, R-CON-013 and R-CON-019 partial (the C1 page, per-action availability). New R-CON-022 keep the tablet awake (app 0.4.8), implemented. New R-CON-023 button press feedback and R-CON-024 hit static (hits, hull_hits in telemetry), implemented in app 0.4.9; the hit-static interpretation (the player's craft, on the console) awaits the user's confirmation. New R-CON-025 keys held at the start of a battle are ignored (app 0.4.10), implemented; new R-CON-026 two console layouts, All-in-one and Cockpit (C2), planned; R-CON-013 note 1.8.1 2026-11-11 R-CON-026 implemented (0.4.11) 1.9.0 2026-11-11 R-CON-024: the hit-static interpretation (the player's craft, on the console) confirmed by the user: "Hit static - correct, works well now" 1.10.0 2026-11-11 Console C2 – C4 and C2b complete (app 0.4.11 – 0.5.0): R-CON-015 target viewport (0.4.14), R-CON-016 3D map (0.4.15), R-CON-014 contacts and events (0.4.15), R-CON-018 tiles (0.4.11), R-CON-020 and R-CON-021 themes (0.5.0) implemented, with As-built notes and Verified-by lines; R-CON-012, R-CON-013 and R-CON-019 completed by the C2 page (0.4.11); R-CON-015 open note resolved (3000-triangle LOD budget, no textures). R-CON-017 stays planned (C5). No requirement wording changed 1.13.0 2026-11-11 R-CON-015: the target model is textured — PNG data URLs and uvs per textured group (app 0.6.7, from user feedback) 1.17.0 2026-11-11 R-CON-007: the description is built — every action has one, sent in catalogue, shown on the tablet and in the keys overlay (main bb04952, app 0.15.1, #6); the open part of the As-built note removed

docs.title: Flight requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the flight model, speed management, collisions, the arena edge, hyperspace and atmospheric flight.

Features: Flight. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-FLT-001 Newtonian flight model Implemented R-FLT-002 Assisted flight model option Implemented R-FLT-003 Turn rates fall with speed Implemented R-FLT-004 Speed hold Implemented R-FLT-005 Afterburner Implemented R-FLT-006 Vectored thrust (VCT) Implemented R-FLT-007 Arena edge Implemented R-FLT-008 Hyperspace out Implemented R-FLT-009 Collisions Implemented R-FLT-010 Fixed, deterministic tick Implemented R-FLT-011 Atmospheric flight Implemented R-FLT-012 Terrain Implemented

docs.title: R-FLT-001 Newtonian flight model
docs.text:
Under the newtonian model (the default) the simulation MUST treat throttle as thrust, let a ship coast at zero throttle, decelerate it with reverse thrust or a held brake, cap forward speed at the hull's max_speed, and MUST NOT steer the velocity when the ship turns.

Rationale: Space flight with momentum, as the owner asked after the first playtest.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::newtonian_accelerates_to_the_cap_and_coasts, half_throttle_is_half_the_acceleration, reverse_thrust_slows_and_then_backs_up, brake_stops_against_the_direction_of_travel, turning_does_not_steer_the_velocity; MT-1-22
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-019)

docs.title: R-FLT-002 Assisted flight model option
docs.text:
A ruleset MUST be able to select flight: {model: assisted}, in which throttle sets a target forward speed, the ship accelerates towards it and sideways drift is damped.

Rationale: Mods that want arcade handling keep it.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::assisted_model_holds_throttle_speed_and_damps_drift
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Rulesets

docs.title: R-FLT-003 Turn rates fall with speed
docs.text:
Pitch and yaw rates MUST scale with clamp(1 − |speed| / lock_speed, 0, 1); roll MUST NOT be reduced; angular velocity MUST approach the commanded value with the hull's damping.

Rationale: The original's handling: fast ships turn wide.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::pitching_up_raises_the_nose_and_rates_fall_with_speed, yaw_right_and_roll_right_turn_the_expected_way, helpers; MT-1-04
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-004 Speed hold
docs.text:
Match speed MUST set a held forward speed equal to the target's; while held, the ship MUST thrust and brake within its own acceleration towards nose × hold, cancelling drift. Any manual throttle, reverse or brake input MUST clear the hold. AI pilots MUST manage speed through the same hold.

Rationale: Speed management under newtonian flight, with the same limits for AI and player.

  • Implements: F-FLT-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::speed_hold_matches_speed_and_cancels_drift, sim::match_speed_copies_the_targets_speed; MT-1-23
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-020)

docs.title: R-FLT-005 Afterburner
docs.text:
The afterburner MUST raise the speed cap and drain energy while lit; speed above the normal cap MUST bleed off at the hull's acceleration once it stops. Thrust and the afterburner MUST scale with the engines' efficiency (no afterburner at zero).

Rationale: Original piloting function; damage matters.

  • Implements: F-FLT-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::afterburner_raises_the_cap_drains_energy_and_excess_bleeds_off; MT-1-05
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-006 Vectored thrust (VCT)
docs.text:
A hull with VCT MUST be able to thrust sideways and vertically at 0.5 × acceleration under the newtonian model (25 % of max_speed as a slide under the assisted model), scaled by the VCT system's efficiency.

Rationale: Original equipment.

  • Implements: F-FLT-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::vct_thrusts_sideways
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-007 Arena edge
docs.text:
A ship beyond flight.arena_radius (default 60 km; 0 = no limit) MUST be placed back on the boundary with its outward velocity removed and its tangential velocity kept, and the pilot MUST be told "ARENA BOUNDARY" on first arrival.

Rationale: Coasting ships would otherwise leave for ever.

  • Implements: F-FLT-004
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::the_arena_edge_halts_outward_motion; MT-1-24
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-021)

docs.title: R-FLT-008 Hyperspace out
docs.text:
Hyperspace MUST count down flight.hyperspace_time seconds (doubled while the hyperdrive is damaged); pressing the key again MUST abort; on departure the ship MUST leave the battle with any ship it tows as a captured prize, and with the modules still mounted on it. The player jumping out of a mission MUST end it as retreat.

Rationale: Original retreat and capture.

  • Implements: F-FLT-005
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::systems::hyperspace_counts_down_aborts_and_departs, tractor_holds_a_disabled_target_and_captures_it_on_jump; sim::tests::cargo_modules_count_until_torn_off_destroyed_or_jumped_away_with_the_hub; MT-2-07, MT-4-27
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Deviations (DEV-026)

docs.title: R-FLT-009 Collisions
docs.text:
A module and its hub, or two modules of the same hub, MUST NOT collide (they are one craft). Fighters touching (spheres at 60 % of radius) MUST be separated (in proportion to their masses, taken as radius cubed) and, while approaching, MUST exchange an impulse along the contact normal with restitution flight.collision.restitution (default 0.5). A fighter sweeping into a station mesh MUST be backed out and bounced the same way, with the station immovable.

Each impact MUST add spin to the ships involved: - from the glancing (tangential) speed, by friction at the contact point; - and from the angle between the ship's nose and the impact direction, scaled by flight.collision.spin.

A spin above about 0.5 rad/s MUST start a tumble of up to flight.collision.tumble seconds, during which the pilot's turn authority is reduced, so the craft spins out of control and then recovers.

The impact sound (Collision event) and the collision damage (approach speed × 0.1) MUST happen only when two ships first touch, not on every tick they stay pressed together.

Bolts and missiles MUST test the segment travelled each tick so they cannot pass through a target.

Rationale: Solid stations, hits that count, collisions that feel like collisions, and no "hammering" from a ship pushing against another.

  • Implements: F-FLT-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::tests::cargo_modules_count_until_torn_off_destroyed_or_jumped_away_with_the_hub (a hub's modules do not brake it), sim::combat::fighters_bounce_off_each_other_and_stations, sim::combat::a_glancing_hit_sends_a_fighter_tumbling, sim::combat::pressed_together_ships_make_one_impact, sim::collision::segment_sphere_hits_misses_and_inside, segment_triangle_hits_inside_only, shapes_use_mesh_in_model_space; MT-1-15
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation

docs.title: R-FLT-010 Fixed, deterministic tick
docs.text:
The simulation MUST advance at a fixed 60 Hz tick, use seeded random sequences, and have no rendering or input dependency, so the same inputs give the same battle.

Rationale: Testable simulation and repeatable soak runs.

  • Implements: F-FLT-001, F-TST-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::step_advances_time_and_clears_edge_controls, sim::random_is_deterministic_and_in_range, sim::generational_handles_detect_reuse
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Simulation, Architectural design

docs.title: R-FLT-011 Atmospheric flight
docs.text:
In an environment with physics: atmosphere (R-MSN-008), every craft that can move MUST feel, each tick, with ρ = the environment's air_density and g = its gravity:

  • Drag a = −k · ρ · |v| · v, with k = acceleration / atmosphere_max_speed² (never removing more than the whole velocity in one tick), so that full thrust balances drag at atmosphere_max_speed in air of density 1, and a craft without thrust slows down.
  • Gravity g along −Y, except for craft with hover: true.
  • Lift g · ρ · (forward speed / lift)² along the craft's own up, capped at 2g, for craft with lift > 0: at the lift speed the wings carry the weight, slower they sink, and banking turns the lift sideways.
  • Ground: a craft MUST NOT pass below the terrain (R-FLT-012). Touching down at no more than LANDING_SPEED = 25 m/s into the ground while upright (its up within about 45° of the ground's normal) MUST be a landing: the motion into the ground stops and a slide is slowed. Faster, or not upright, MUST be a crash: damage of (impact speed)² × 0.5, a Collision event and a bounce that keeps half the speed.
  • Ceiling: a craft that climbs above the environment's ceiling MUST leave the battle, as by hyperspace (Departed, with the message LEFT THE ATMOSPHERE).

AI pilots MUST pull up to a climb at a speed their wings can fly when below 150 m, or when their vertical speed would take them below 100 m within 3 s. A craft in Simple physics (R-FLT-013) MUST keep its arcade handling (the forces act, but its velocity is still set along the nose). In physics: space none of this applies.

The per-ship values MUST be data on the ship class: atmosphere_max_speed (default 60 % of max_speed), lift (default 120 m/s for fighters, 0 for every other kind), hover (default false) and atmospheric (default true; read and validated, not yet acted on).

Rationale: Surface missions, where a craft must fly rather than drift; the forces are simple enough for a modder to tune with three numbers.

  • Implements: F-FLT-007
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.0, main af003f6)
  • Verified by: sim::env::tests::drag_gravity_and_lift_act_in_air_and_not_in_space, ai_pilots_pull_up_near_the_ground, gentle_touchdowns_land_hard_ones_crash_and_the_ceiling_is_an_exit; MT-3-41 – MT-3-43 (Stage 3 exit: "atmospheric flight feels distinct from space")
  • See: Environments and terrain, Simulation, Format: missions, environments, events

Resolved (1.11.0)

The equations and key names are as above. The design's drag_area (Cd·A) was not adopted: drag is set by atmosphere_max_speed, which a modder can reason about directly. atmospheric: false is reserved for hiding a craft from surface missions once the strategy layer chooses craft (Stage 4).

docs.title: R-FLT-012 Terrain
docs.text:
A pack MUST be able to define terrains as data, terrains: {<id>: {generate | heightmap, size, height, colors, resolution}}, used by an atmospheric environment's terrain:.

  • A terrain MUST be a square heightfield of resolution points per side (default 129, 17 – 257), size metres across (default 30 km), centred on the origin; its heights MUST span height: [low, high] metres (default [0, 1500]). Outside the square the ground MUST continue to the horizon as mirror-image tiles of the field (each neighbour reflected across the shared edge, so heights meet without seams); collision and the drawn ground MUST agree everywhere, and the tiles within the fog distance MUST be drawn.
  • Heights MUST come from exactly one of:
  • generate: {kind, seed}: hills (smooth value noise in five octaves) or craters (a gently rolling plain with bowl-shaped craters and raised rims), deterministic for seed, built once while the rules are read;
  • heightmap: <image>: a greyscale PNG or TGA from the pack (black = low, white = high; the red channel, resampled to resolution), built once when the content loads.
  • The ground height under a point MUST be bilinearly interpolated; its normal comes from the slope around it.
  • The terrain MUST be drawn as a lit mesh coloured from colors: {low, high, slope}: low ground to high ground by height, blended towards slope where the ground is steep, faded into the sky's fog with distance (R-MSN-008).
  • Giving both generate and heightmap, neither, or an unknown kind MUST be a rules error; a heightmap that fails to load MUST be a content error naming it.

Rationale: Surface missions of the default campaign, on ground a modder can generate from a seed or paint as an image.

  • Implements: F-FLT-007
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.0, main af003f6)
  • Verified by: content::environment::tests::environments_and_terrains_parse_and_report_mistakes, generated_heightfields_span_their_range_are_deterministic_and_interpolate (mirrored beyond the edge), render::terrain::tests::terrain_meshes_face_up_and_colour_by_height, tiles_match_the_folded_ground_heights; MT-3-39, MT-3-40, MT-3-60
  • See: Environments and terrain, Rendering, Format: missions, environments, events

Open

Not built yet: texturing with detail maps (texture: {base, detail}) and scattered objects on the ground (objects: {scatter, density}), the rest of plan item 3.5 (ground installations are built: R-MSN-008, app 0.6.1). The terrain's look has been checked only by unit tests so far, not on screen.

From user feedback (app 0.6.7, main c0e2516)

The user's playtest saw the ground end at the field's edge. Heightfield::fold maps any point back into the field (odd tiles reflected), so height_at answers everywhere; the renderer draws up to 7 × 7 tiles around the camera within the fog distance from two meshes, the field and its X-mirror (render::terrain::tile_placement). Static objects spawned over a ground now float one radius clear of it (app 0.6.7, 65141dc).

docs.title: R-FLT-013 Simple physics mode
docs.text:
The player MUST be able to choose simple or realistic physics: in the launcher (key P), or with game: {physics: simple} in settings.yaml. The default is realistic.

Simple applies to the player's craft only: - its velocity MUST always lie along its nose, at the throttle (or speed-hold, afterburner, brake) speed, reached at the craft's acceleration; - sideways and vertical velocity MUST be only what the slide (VCT) thrusters ask for, with no drift left after turning or after a collision.

The choice MUST take effect only when the campaign's difficulty is one of its first three levels. At any higher level the player MUST fly Realistic, and the launcher MUST say so.

AI craft always fly the campaign's own model (flight.model).

Rationale: An easier entry for players used to traditional fighter games, without changing the challenge at higher levels or the AI's behaviour.

  • Implements: F-FLT-008
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: sim::flight::tests::simple_physics_has_no_drift, sim::flight::tests::simple_physics_only_on_the_first_three_levels, settings::tests::parses_and_round_trips

docs.text: Version Date Change 1.0.0 2026-11-11 Bootstrap: R-FLT-001 – R-FLT-012 (12 requirements; 10 reverse-engineered from the code) 1.5.0 2026-11-11 R-FLT-009 revised: impulse with restitution, spin from glancing speed and impact angle, tumble, one impact per contact (flight.collision) 1.6.0 2026-11-11 R-FLT-013 simple physics mode 1.11.0 2026-11-11 R-FLT-011 atmospheric flight rewritten as built and implemented (app 0.6.0): drag from atmosphere_max_speed, gravity, lift capped at 2g, hover, landing below 25 m/s upright, crash damage, the ceiling exit, AI ground avoidance, Simple physics kept; keys atmosphere_max_speed, lift, hover, atmospheric; the open note on equations and key names resolved (drag_area not adopted).
