docs.title: Strategy interface requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for the original-style, multi-screen strategy interface: a campaign's set of full screens and dialogs, built from engine widgets placed by rectangle, linked to one another, and laid out as pack data. The interceptor set follows X-COM: Interceptor's screens at 640 × 480 from the player's own wrapper art; the default campaign has its own set with generated art; the single-grid strategy screen of app 0.16 stays as the testbed layout. The normative format is Format: interface, text and media › Screen sets.

Features: Strategy interface. How to read a requirement: Specification. Plan: Stage 6 › 6.9 Original-style strategy screens.

Source: the user's request, 2026-11-12

"Critically missing from the game and requirements is the strategy UI from Interceptor. The gridded layout currently present is fine for testing, but we need to support the interface style the original game has. It broke up functionality across multiple screens as opposed to a single grid like currently present." — and — "there are additional screens, these are just a subset."

The screens named below come from the user's screenshots of the original (CSD, Interceptor Orders, Bases, Purchase, Pilots, Briefing, Mission debriefing, Launch Mission, Alien Transmission, Options). WrappersDLL.dll holds further backgrounds (research, manufacturing, status reports, UFOpedia, the combat simulator, title screens), which a reverse-engineering pass is mapping. No requirement here depends on that pass's results: a screen the pass has not mapped falls back to the engine's built-in version (R-UI-019).

Requirement Status R-UI-001 Screen sets Planned R-UI-002 Engine screen catalogue Planned R-UI-003 Navigation between screens Planned R-UI-004 Dialogs Planned R-UI-005 Widgets placed by rectangle Planned R-UI-006 Buttons Planned R-UI-007 Toggles and radio groups Planned R-UI-008 Labels and bound values Planned R-UI-009 Lists Planned R-UI-010 Map, minimap, globe and clock Planned R-UI-011 Model views Planned R-UI-012 Text, images and frames Planned R-UI-013 Portraits and grid views Planned R-UI-014 Keyboard and gamepad navigation Planned R-UI-015 Scaling the design space Planned R-UI-016 Localisable text Planned R-UI-017 Screen sets are validated Planned R-UI-018 Two layouts per campaign Planned R-UI-019 A partial screen set still plays Planned R-UI-020 Interceptor screens follow the original Planned R-UI-021 Original art by reference only Planned R-UI-022 The default campaign's screen set Planned R-UI-023 CSD screen Planned R-UI-024 Orders dialog Planned R-UI-025 Bases screen Planned R-UI-026 Purchase screen Planned R-UI-027 Manufacture screen Planned R-UI-028 Pilots screen Planned R-UI-029 Launch mission dialog Planned R-UI-030 Notice, transmission and choice dialogs Planned R-UI-031 Briefing screen Planned R-UI-032 Debriefing screen Planned R-UI-033 Research screen Planned R-UI-034 Hangar screen Planned R-UI-035 Reports screen Planned R-UI-036 Encyclopaedia screen Planned R-UI-037 Options screen Planned R-UI-038 Messages, simulator and title screens Planned R-UI-039 Custom screens Planned R-UI-040 Interface sounds Planned

docs.title: R-UI-001 Screen sets
docs.text:
A campaign MUST be able to define a screen set: entries screens.<id>, each a full screen with its own design space (design: [w, h]), a background image and its widgets. The screens of a set MUST link to one another through widget actions (R-UI-003). A screen set MUST be ordinary pack data: a later pack (an addon, a remaster) MUST be able to replace a screen, add a widget, or move or restyle one widget by naming only that widget, as the layouts of R-CPN-011 do today. The interceptor set MUST use the original's 640 × 480 design space.

Rationale: The user's request: the original "broke up functionality across multiple screens as opposed to a single grid".

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Screen sets, Screen layouts (modding)

docs.title: R-UI-002 Engine screen catalogue
docs.text:
The engine MUST provide each screen's function — its state, its named values and lists, and its commands — under the ids of the Screens table: starmap (the CSD), bases, research, hangar (equip ship), market (purchase), factory (manufacture), pilots, reports, encyclopaedia, messages, briefing, debriefing, simulator, options, and the dialogs orders, launch, notice, transmission and choice. A screen set binds widgets to those functions and MUST NOT need engine code to place, restyle or omit any of them. A screen the campaign does not use (its campaign.systems) MAY be left out of the set. Each function MUST be documented with its values, lists, list fields and commands on the modding site.

Rationale: The engine owns the logic, the mod owns the look — the rule the strategy screens already follow (R-STR-010).

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Screens

docs.title: R-UI-003 Navigation between screens
docs.text:
Widget actions MUST include open(<screen>) (show a full screen, remembering the one left), back (return to the screen left), home (the set's home, starmap by default), dialog(<id>) and close (close the topmost dialog). Esc and the gamepad's B MUST act as close on a dialog and as back on any full screen other than home. Each screen MUST state whether the campaign clock runs while it is shown (clock: runs | paused); dialogs pause it unless they say otherwise. A battle launched from a screen MUST return through the debriefing (when the set has one) to the screen it was launched from.

Rationale: The original moves between full screens from the CSD's buttons and returns to the CSD.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Actions

Open

Whether the original's clock runs on each screen other than the CSD is unknown; the interceptor set records what is found (R-UI-020). The engine's default is paused for every screen but starmap.

docs.title: R-UI-004 Dialogs
docs.text:
A dialog MUST be a screen drawn over another: a rectangle in the design space of the screen beneath (or its own design, centred), a frame, its widgets and optionally a dimming of the screen beneath (dim: 0..1). It MUST be modal — input goes to the topmost dialog — and dialogs MUST stack (a transmission over the orders dialog). The engine MUST raise its own dialogs when the campaign needs the player: notice and transmission for campaign and story notices, choice for event choices and offers, orders when the player selects their craft on the map, launch when a mission is launched. A dialog the set does not define MUST fall back to the engine's built-in modal prompt drawn in the skin (R-UI-019).

Rationale: The original's Interceptor Orders, Launch Mission and Alien Transmission dialogs sit over the CSD.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Dialogs

docs.title: R-UI-005 Widgets placed by rectangle
docs.text:
Every widget MUST have a type from the engine's widget catalogue — button, toggle, label, value, list, map, minimap, globe, lamp, clock, model_view, text, image, frame, portraits, grid_view — and a rect: [x, y, w, h] in its screen's design space. Widgets MUST be drawn in the order listed (later on top) and hit-tested topmost first. A widget MAY carry visible and enabled conditions (the condition language of R-MOD-013) and a tooltip text key. Widgets MUST be drawn from data built once when the screen opens (no per-frame allocation of the layout).

Rationale: Functional components a modder places by rectangle — the same rule as cockpit instruments.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-006 Buttons
docs.text:
A button MUST draw an image per state — up, down (pressed), hover and disabled — or, without images, a face drawn in the skin with a text key. A missing state MUST fall back (hover and down to up; disabled to up dimmed). A button MUST run its action — one action or a list run in order: a navigation action (R-UI-003), speed(<n>) or pause (the campaign clock), a screen command from its screen's catalogue (R-UI-002), or run_for(<duration>) (run the clock for that long, then pause) — when released over it. A button MAY have a hotkey (key) and MAY repeat while held (scroll arrows, quantity steppers).

Rationale: The original's buttons are pictures in the wrapper art with pressed and lit states.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets, Format › Actions

docs.title: R-UI-007 Toggles and radio groups
docs.text:
A toggle MUST draw off and on images (with optional hover and disabled) and be bound (bind) to a boolean screen state or engine value. Toggles sharing a group MUST form a radio group: each has a value, exactly one is on, and the group is bound to a screen state — for example the base overlay (normal, defences, damage), the purchase category, or the clock speed.

Rationale: The Bases screen's NORMAL / DEFENSES / DAMAGE and the purchase categories.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-008 Labels and bound values
docs.text:
A label MUST draw a fixed text key. A value MUST draw a bound value: a named engine value (money, date, time, speed, score, base.name, selected.name, … — the engine's set plus each screen's own, R-UI-002) or a campaign query (query: "plan(eclipse)"), formatted by an optional format text key holding {value}. Both MUST take a font (a skin font), a colour, and an align (left, centre or right; top, middle or bottom), and MUST be refreshed when the value changes, not rebuilt every frame.

Rationale: The CSD's clock, date and money; the purchase screen's cargo and hangar space.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Bound values

docs.title: R-UI-009 Lists
docs.text:
A list MUST show a named list of its screen (source) in columns (each: a bind to a row field, a width, an align, optional header, font and colour), with a row_height. It MUST scroll by the wheel, keys and pad, and by named scroll buttons (scroll: {up, down}) or a scroll bar; it MUST keep a single selection bound to screen state, drawn with a highlight colour or image; it MUST run an activate action on a double click, Enter or A; it MAY name quantity steppers (quantity: {up, down}) that change the selected row's quantity; it MAY use layout: carousel to show one row at a time with previous and next buttons (a dial). An empty list MUST draw its empty text key.

Rationale: The purchase list (size, cost, stores, quantity, up/down), the docked-ships list, the Bases module dial.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-010 Map, minimap, globe and clock
docs.text:
A map MUST show the star map in its rectangle, shape: rect or round (a circle inscribed in the rectangle, or a mask image), with the zoom, pan and picking of the current map; it MUST name a hover box widget that shows what is under the cursor (object, class, owner) and MUST set the selected.* values. A minimap MUST show the whole map with the main map's view marked and centre the map on a click. A globe MUST draw a picture or animation with lamp widgets, each lamp an off / on / blink image bound to a condition or a named alert (alert.contact, alert.base_attack, …). A clock MUST draw the campaign time as text or from a strip of digit images.

Rationale: The CSD: round star map, hover box, minimap, globe with status lamps, clock.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-011 Model views
docs.text:
A model_view MUST render a 3D model from its screen's state in its rectangle — subject: craft, base, item or entry — with the campaign's own meshes and textures, an orbiting camera turned by a rotate pad (named buttons) or a drag, and zoom. On the Bases screen it MUST let the player pick a module slot by clicking it, and draw the overlay chosen by a radio group (normal, defences, damage). Its GPU meshes MUST be built when the screen opens, not per frame.

Rationale: The Bases screen's 3D base view; the craft on the hangar and purchase screens.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets, R-STR-006

docs.title: R-UI-012 Text, images and frames
docs.text:
A text widget MUST draw wrapped text — a text key or a screen's named text (a briefing, an entry, a message) with {variables} filled — in a skin font, colour and alignment, scrolling by the wheel, keys, pad and named scroll buttons when it does not fit. An image MUST draw a fixed picture or a bound one (bind: item.picture). A frame MUST draw a nine-slice or fixed image behind other widgets (a dialog's panel, an info box).

Rationale: The briefing's wrapped text; the purchase screen's item picture and info box.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-013 Portraits and grid views
docs.text:
A portraits widget MUST lay out sockets as a ring (ring: {centre, radius, count, start}), a grid, or an explicit list of points, show one row of a bound list per socket (a pilot's portrait), draw an empty image in an unused socket, keep a selection bound to screen state, and page when the list is longer than the sockets. A grid_view MUST draw a cell grid (cells: [columns, rows]) on which its screen places icons — the briefing's formations, objectives and waypoints, by side.

Rationale: The Pilots screen's ring of portrait sockets; the briefing's formation grid.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Widgets

docs.title: R-UI-014 Keyboard and gamepad navigation
docs.text:
Every screen and dialog MUST be fully usable with the keyboard alone and with a gamepad alone. A focus MUST move between the enabled interactive widgets (button, toggle, list, map, portraits, model view) with the arrow keys, the d-pad or the left stick — to the nearest widget in the direction pressed, or in the screen's focus order when given — and Tab / Shift+Tab and the shoulder buttons MUST cycle it. Enter or A activates; Esc or B is close / back (R-UI-003). Inside a list, up and down move the selection and left and right step the quantity; on a map, the stick pans, the triggers zoom and A selects. The focused widget MUST be visibly marked (the skin's focus image or an outline). Hotkeys (key) MUST work whatever has the focus. Moving the mouse MUST NOT move the focus; a click does. The keys and buttons MUST be interface actions in the one action table (R-CON-001), so they can be rebound.

Rationale: The engine is played with a gamepad from the couch as well as with the mouse.

  • Implements: F-UI-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Focus, Input and gamepads

docs.title: R-UI-015 Scaling the design space
docs.text:
A screen set's design space MUST be scaled to the window uniformly, keeping its aspect ratio, centred, with the rest of the window filled by bands of a colour or an outside image (scale: fit, the default for screen sets) — the rule cockpits follow. scale: integer SHOULD use the largest whole multiple that fits. Images MUST be sampled so they stay crisp (filter: nearest for pixel art such as the original's, linear otherwise), and text MUST be drawn at the window's resolution, not scaled as a bitmap. The testbed layout keeps scale: stretch (as built in app 0.16.0). A mod MAY supply a screen in another design space (a widescreen remaster), and MAY give aspects alternatives chosen by the window's aspect ratio.

Rationale: 640 × 480 art on a 16:9 window must not be distorted or blurred.

  • Implements: F-UI-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Scaling

docs.title: R-UI-016 Localisable text
docs.text:
Every string a widget draws MUST come from a text key or a bound value; widgets MUST NOT carry literal player-visible text. The original's own strings MUST be reached by @orig.* keys. Text too long for its rectangle MUST be drawn smaller (down to half size) and then cut with an ellipsis, so a translation never spills over its neighbours; --check MUST report missing keys.

Rationale: Translation (R-MOD-041); the original's strings are read by reference.

  • Implements: F-UI-006
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Text

docs.title: R-UI-017 Screen sets are validated
docs.text:
Loading and --check MUST reject, with a message naming the pack, file, screen and widget: an unknown screen, widget type, action, screen command, named value, list or list field; a widget without a rect; a radio group with no or two default members; an image that cannot be resolved; a missing text key. A rectangle outside its design space MUST be a warning.

Rationale: Modding first: a mistake in a layout is found before play.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Validating (modding)

docs.title: R-UI-018 Two layouts per campaign
docs.text:
A campaign MUST be playable in either of two layouts: its screen set (the default where the campaign defines one, and so the default for interceptor) and the testbed layout — the single-grid strategy screen of app 0.16 (top, map, nav, info, panel). The player MUST be able to switch between them in Options at any time without losing campaign state; the choice MUST be remembered per campaign (interface.layout: screens | testbed in settings.yaml). A campaign with no screen set MUST use the testbed layout. Both layouts MUST drive the same screen functions (R-UI-002), so whatever one can do the other can. The testbed layout's widgets MUST stay placeable as data (testbed_layout); an existing screens.starmap whose widgets are all plain rectangles naming testbed widgets MUST be read as the testbed layout, with a --check warning.

Rationale: The user: "The gridded layout currently present is fine for testing".

  • Implements: F-UI-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Two layouts, Screen layouts (modding)

docs.title: R-UI-019 A partial screen set still plays
docs.text:
A screen set MAY define only some screens and dialogs. Opening one the set lacks MUST show the engine's built-in version of that function, drawn in the skin (the testbed layout's list or prompt for it, in a full-window panel), and back MUST return to the set. --check MUST list the screens that fall back.

Rationale: A set — and the interceptor mapping in particular — can be built and played one screen at a time; nothing waits for the whole original to be mapped.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Two layouts

docs.title: R-UI-020 Interceptor screens follow the original
docs.text:
The interceptor screen set MUST follow the original: which screens and dialogs exist, how they link, each widget's position, size, images per state, and behaviour — including the clock while a screen is open and the "(5 secs)" variants of buttons. Every layout fact read from the original MUST be marked verified (read from the data and checked against the original running) or derived (inferred), and what is not known as unknown, in the pack data's comments and on the docs site. Coordinates, sizes and resource ids are facts and MAY be in pack data. The set MUST NOT wait on the whole original being mapped (R-UI-019).

Rationale: Compatibility: playing Interceptor should look and feel like Interceptor.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: The Interceptor campaign mod, R-CPN-005

Open

What the "(5 secs)" buttons do is derived from their labels only: the action, then the clock runs five seconds and pauses again (run_for(5s)). Confirm against the original.

docs.title: R-UI-021 Original art by reference only
docs.text:
The interceptor set's art MUST be named by reference — original:WrappersDLL.dll#<id> for a wrapper image, and original:WrappersDLL.dll#<id>@[x, y, w, h] for a part of one (a button drawn into a background) — and read from the player's data at load. No wrapper image, part, conversion, extract or screenshot of one may enter Git, the docs site or a generated file in the repository. When a referenced image cannot be read, --check MUST say so and the campaign MUST fall back to the testbed layout with a message.

Rationale: The project's rule: never commit original content.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-CMP-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: PE resource container

docs.title: R-UI-022 The default campaign's screen set
docs.text:
The default campaign MUST have its own screen set covering every screen and dialog it uses, with art in its art-deco style generated by tools/default_assets, laid out by its own design (not a copy of the original's coordinates); it MUST contain no original content, MUST stay fully playable in it, and MUST pass --check with no original data present. It is the worked example in the modding guide.

Rationale: Modding first: a feature that works only with original data is incomplete.

  • Implements: F-UI-005, F-CPN-003
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: The default campaign, R-TST-012

docs.title: Screens
docs.text: Each screen below is an engine function (R-UI-002). What it MUST offer is listed; where it is drawn, and with what pictures, is the screen set's.

docs.title: R-UI-023 CSD screen
docs.text:
starmap MUST offer: the star map (R-UI-010, round in interceptor) with the hover box (object, class, owner) and the selection; a minimap; buttons to the other full screens (six in the original); a globe with status lamps; the clock, the date and the money; the clock speeds and pause. Selecting one of the player's craft or squadrons MUST open orders; launching a mission MUST open launch.

Rationale: The original's Combat Strategic Display, the hub of the game.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-002

docs.title: R-UI-024 Orders dialog
docs.text:
orders MUST show the selected squadron's ships with their status, and offer the commands Attack (when a target is in reach), Select new destination (the next click on the map sets it), Return to base, and the timed variant of Return to base (R-UI-020).

Rationale: The original's Interceptor Orders dialog.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-003

docs.title: R-UI-025 Bases screen
docs.text:
bases MUST offer: the current base and switching between bases; the 3D base view (R-UI-011) with module slots — choosing a module, then "select a location for the …" a free slot; the overlays normal, defences and damage; a rotate pad; a module dial (R-UI-009, carousel) of the modules that can be built, with cost and time; dismantling; building a new base.

Rationale: The original's Bases screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-006

docs.title: R-UI-026 Purchase screen
docs.text:
market MUST offer: category buttons (a radio group of the campaign's item categories, ships among them); the list of items with size, cost, stores and quantity, and up / down to change the quantity; the selected item's picture and info box; the order's totals against the base's free cargo and hangar space; placing the order; selling where the campaign allows it.

Rationale: The original's Purchase equipment / ships screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-004

docs.title: R-UI-027 Manufacture screen
docs.text:
factory MUST offer: the items the player can make, with cost and time; the manufacturing queue with priorities, moving up and cancelling; progress and the workshop capacity used.

Rationale: The original's manufacturing screen (a WrappersDLL background).

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-004

docs.title: R-UI-028 Pilots screen
docs.text:
pilots MUST offer: the base's pilots in portrait sockets (R-UI-013, a ring in interceptor); the selected pilot's stat panel — the campaign's own stats, which for interceptor are assignment, kills, missions, health, intelligence, stamina, accuracy, flying ability, aggressiveness, bravery, psionics and salary; the docked ships with the pilot assigned to each, and assigning a pilot to a ship; recruiting, training and dismissing where the campaign allows.

Rationale: The original's Pilots screen; stats are data, so a campaign with other stats uses the same screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-008

docs.title: R-UI-029 Launch mission dialog
docs.text:
launch MUST list the base's docked ships, let the player select up to the campaign's limit (5 in interceptor; strategy.launch.max_craft), and launch them or cancel.

Rationale: The original's Launch Mission dialog.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-003

docs.title: R-UI-030 Notice, transmission and choice dialogs
docs.text:
notice MUST show a campaign notice with OK and the timed OK. transmission MUST show a story message — with its film or face playing in a named rectangle when it has one — with OK, the timed OK and allocate new research (open research). choice MUST show an event's text and one button per choice, or Fly / Decline for an offered mission.

Rationale: The original's Alien Transmission dialog; the story layer's notices and choices (R-CPN-007).

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-CPN-012

docs.title: R-UI-031 Briefing screen
docs.text:
briefing MUST show the mission's briefing as wrapped text and its forces on a grid view (R-UI-013) — the ship formations of each side — and offer launching the battle or going back.

Rationale: The original's Briefing screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-MSN-001

docs.title: R-UI-032 Debriefing screen
docs.text:
debriefing MUST show the battle's result: what was recovered, the items gained, the score, the rating and the debrief text, then continue to the screen the battle was launched from (R-UI-003).

Rationale: The original's Mission debriefing screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-MSN-005

docs.title: R-UI-033 Research screen
docs.text:
research MUST offer: the topics available, the current work with its progress, rate and estimated completion, choosing and changing topics, and the capacity used and blocked.

Rationale: The original's research screen (a WrappersDLL background).

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-005

docs.title: R-UI-034 Hangar screen
docs.text:
hangar MUST offer: the base's craft; the selected craft in a model view; its slots and the items fitted, fitting and removing from stores; the pilot assigned.

Rationale: The original's Equip Ship screen.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-007

docs.title: R-UI-035 Reports screen
docs.text:
reports MUST offer the periodic reports in panels (four in the original) — finances, activity, holdings and evaluations — chosen by period.

Rationale: The original's status reports (a WrappersDLL background in four panels).

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-009

docs.title: R-UI-036 Encyclopaedia screen
docs.text:
encyclopaedia MUST offer: the categories; the unlocked entries in the chosen category; the entry's model view or picture, its text and its stats.

Rationale: The original's UFOpedia.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Encyclopaedia

docs.title: R-UI-037 Options screen
docs.text:
options MUST offer the keyboard configuration — the bindings of R-CON-004, drawn in the set's layout — and the game's options (audio, graphics, the layout switch of R-UI-018).

Rationale: The original's Options screen with its keyboard configuration.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-004
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-CPN-011

docs.title: R-UI-038 Messages, simulator and title screens
docs.text:
messages MUST offer the message log and the news; simulator MUST offer the combat simulator's setup (R-MSN-010); a screen set MAY lay out the shell screens (main_menu, load_save, credits, ending) the same way, using the original's title backgrounds in interceptor.

Rationale: The remaining WrappersDLL backgrounds.

  • Implements: F-UI-001
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: R-STR-010

docs.title: R-UI-039 Custom screens
docs.text:
A pack MUST be able to add screens and dialogs beyond the catalogue — composed of the generic widgets, bound to named values, campaign queries and the lists of any catalogue screen, and linked by the navigation actions — for example a relations screen or a chapter recap.

Rationale: The user: "there are additional screens, these are just a subset" — and a custom campaign will want screens the original never had.

  • Implements: F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Format › Screen sets

docs.title: R-UI-040 Interface sounds
docs.text:
A button or toggle SHOULD play a sound when pressed (its own, or the skin's click), and a screen MAY name a music state to play while shown. interceptor SHOULD use the original's interface sounds by reference.

Rationale: The original's screens click and beep.

  • Implements: F-UI-001, F-UI-002
  • Status: planned
  • Verified by: Planned.
  • See: Music (modding)

docs.title: Revision history
docs.text: Version Date Change 1.19.0 2026-11-12 New area page (user request): R-UI-001 – R-UI-040, the original-style multi-screen strategy interface — screen sets and the engine screen catalogue, navigation and dialogs, the widget catalogue, keyboard and gamepad navigation, scaling, text, validation, the testbed layout as a second layout, partial sets, interceptor fidelity and art by reference, the default campaign's set, and the screens and dialogs. All planned (Stage 6.9)

docs.title: Missions requirements
docs.text:
Requirements for missions as data, objectives and outcomes, the debrief, chatter, environments, hazards and mission balance. The normative file format is Format: missions, environments, events.

Features: Missions. How to read a requirement: Specification.

Requirement Status R-MSN-001 Mission roles Implemented R-MSN-002 Arrivals and waves Implemented R-MSN-003 Objectives, timer and outcomes Implemented R-MSN-004 Mission mistakes found on load Implemented R-MSN-005 Debrief Implemented R-MSN-006 Radio chatter Implemented R-MSN-007 Voices Implemented R-MSN-008 Battle environments Implemented R-MSN-009 Hazards Implemented R-MSN-010 Simulator missions Implemented R-MSN-011 Base defence balance Implemented R-MSN-012 Logistics missions Implemented

docs.title: R-MSN-001 Mission roles
docs.text:
A mission MUST declare roles with class lists, counts per difficulty level, faction, AI, behaviour, protect, state, hull, systems and speed; at start roles MUST be placed, counted and faced at the player.

Rationale: Missions as data.

  • Implements: F-MSN-001
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::mission::a_full_mission_parses, mission::roles_are_placed_counted_and_faced_at_the_player; MT-3-01 – MT-3-09
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events, Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-002 Arrivals and waves
docs.text:
A role MUST be able to arrive at a position relative to another (at: {distance, bearing, from, spread}) and when a condition holds (arrive:); a role without arrive: MUST enter at the start; waves MUST repeat a role's arrival. A wave with every: <time> MUST come again that long after it last came, for as long as its when holds. A role with escort: <role> MUST fly in its formation on the newest live member of that role.

Rationale: One place per group (DEV-040). Repeating waves and escorts: the supply-convoy battle's tugs come every two minutes, each with its own squadron (the user's design, app 0.9.2).

  • Implements: F-MSN-001
  • Status: implemented (every: and escort: app 0.9.2, main 0d1c522)
  • Verified by: mission::arrivals_waves_chatter_and_a_win; sim::ai::tests::escorts_hold_formation_until_a_hostile_comes_close; MT-4-26
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-003 Objectives, timer and outcomes
docs.text:
A mission MUST evaluate win, draw and lose conditions and optional objectives in the battle context; lose MUST beat win in the same tick; a timer MUST end the mission with its stated result; outcomes MUST be lists of checked actions with battle or campaign scope. The results are win, lose, draw, retreat and killed. The engine MUST set killed when the player's craft is destroyed, checked before the mission's own conditions; killed MUST take the mission's lose outcomes unless the mission gives outcomes: {killed: …}.

Rationale: Clear, testable results; the debrief must say what actually happened (the player's death is not the objective failing).

  • Implements: F-MSN-001, F-MSN-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::lose_beats_win_and_the_timer_ends_it, the_players_death_is_its_own_result_with_the_lose_outcomes; script::action::actions_parse_and_check; script::battle::ids_match_and_roles_are_checked_names; sim::tests::cargo_modules_count_until_torn_off_destroyed_or_jumped_away_with_the_hub (cargo(role)); MT-4-27
  • Reverse-engineered: yes

Added (app 0.9.2): cargo

The battle query cargo(role) gives the share (0..1) of the role's cargo containers still aboard; a mission's cargo: <role> puts that share at the end into the debrief and the campaign's battle report, where a flown convoy escort delivers it (R-STR-019).

  • See: Missions (architecture), Conditions (script)

docs.title: R-MSN-004 Mission mistakes found on load
docs.text:
Mistakes in a mission file (unknown role, bad timer result, unknown action) MUST be reported on load with where they are.

Rationale: Modders find errors before flying.

  • Implements: F-MSN-001, F-MOD-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: content::mission::mistakes_are_reported_with_where
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-005 Debrief
docs.text:
At the end of a mission the debrief MUST show the result, its text, kills, losses, time, optional objectives and the campaign actions, and MUST offer a retry. The player jumping out MUST count as retreat. For killed the headline MUST be "YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED" and the text MUST be the mission's debrief: {killed: …} if given, otherwise none (never the lose text, which describes the objective).

When the result is decided the verdict MUST be shown at once ("MISSION ACCOMPLISHED", "MISSION FAILED", "YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED" or "MISSION ENDED") and the battle MUST keep running, so its end can be watched; the debrief MUST appear flight.debrief_delay (rules data, a time, default 30 s) after the result, with a countdown, and Enter MUST show it at once. A retreat (the player leaving) MUST show the debrief at once.

Rationale: Closure and feedback.

  • Implements: F-MSN-002
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::the_players_death_is_its_own_result_with_the_lose_outcomes; app::flight::tests::the_debrief_waits_for_the_delay_after_the_result; MT-3-01 – MT-3-11 (the debrief in every mission case), MT-3-17, MT-3-64
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (architecture)

From user feedback (app 0.7.4, main 9295707)

The user's playtest asked to see the battle end: the result is announced (verdict and computer voice) at once, and the battle runs on for flight.debrief_delay before the debrief. flight::debrief_due decides when; the wait is skipped with Enter.

Campaign battles (app 0.7.1)

In a campaign battle the debrief returns to the strategy screen (Enter or Esc), which applies salvage, score, money and flags (R-STR-003, R-STR-010).

docs.title: R-MSN-006 Radio chatter
docs.text:
A mission MUST be able to play chatter lines when their conditions become true.

Rationale: Atmosphere and information.

  • Implements: F-MSN-003
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: mission::arrivals_waves_chatter_and_a_win
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Missions (modding)

docs.title: R-MSN-007 Voices
docs.text:
Chatter and the computer voice SHOULD play recorded or original voice samples. As built:

  • A pack MUST be able to define radio voice sets as data, voices: {<set>: {<line>: clip or [clips]}}, and a ship class MUST be able to name one with voice: <set>; an unknown set MUST be a rules error.
  • When the player gives a wing order (fire at will, attack my target, ignore my target, evasive, retreat), one of the player's living wingmen whose voice has the line MUST play an acknowledge clip; a status request MUST play a status clip; when one of the player's wingmen is destroyed, another MUST play a down clip. With several clips for a line, one is chosen each time.
  • A mission chatter entry MAY name a clip with voice:; it MUST play when the line is said. Voice clips and chatter voices MAY be cue:<Name> references, resolved through the sound cue table like sounds: (app 0.6.7).
  • When the mission's result is decided (since app 0.7.4 that is before the debrief, R-MSN-005), the named sound mission_accomplished MUST play for a win and mission_failed for any other result (the computer voice).
  • A ship without a voice, a voice without the line, or a campaign without these sounds MUST stay silent without error.

The default campaign MUST ship the voice set guard_pilot (synthesised radio clips, used by the Comet, Meteor, Thunderbolt and Victory) and the two mission sounds; the interceptor campaign maps the computer voice from the original's cue table (Comp_MissionAccomplished, Comp_MissionFailed).

Rationale: Atmosphere, and the original's radio and computer voice. Voices are data, so a mod can give its pilots voices without code.

  • Implements: F-MSN-003, F-CPN-007
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.2, main 5bdb47f)
  • Verified by: app::flight::tests::a_wingman_answers_in_its_own_voice, content::rules::tests::builds_typed_definitions_with_inheritance (voice sets and clips); MT-3-47 – MT-3-50
  • See: Radio voices (modding), Audio

Open

The interceptor campaign's pilot chatter clips (the numbered FPilot1xx and MPilotxxx files) are not mapped to voice lines: which line each clip says is not known (unknown), and a wrong mapping would put the wrong words in a wingman's mouth. The user is asked to identify the lines by listening (for example in the launcher's asset browser, Sounds tab) so that packs/interceptor can map them to acknowledge, status, down and later lines. Also open: --check does not load voice clips. (Resolved in app 0.6.7, main 65141dc: cue: references now resolve inside voices: and chatter voice:.)

docs.title: R-MSN-008 Battle environments
docs.text:
A pack MUST be able to define battle environments as data, environments: {<id>: {physics, arena, gravity, air_density, ceiling, terrain, sky, backdrop}}, and a mission or scenario MUST be able to name one with environment: <id>. Without it the battle MUST take place in open space, exactly as before.

  • physics: space (the default) MUST leave the campaign's flight model unchanged; physics: atmosphere MUST apply atmospheric flight (R-FLT-011) over the environment's terrain (R-FLT-012), which it then MUST name.
  • arena, if given, MUST replace flight.arena_radius for battles in that environment (a small "pocket").
  • backdrop: {planet: {color, size, direction}} MUST draw a lit planet disc of that colour and angular size (degrees) in that direction (orbit).
  • backdrop: {nebula: {color, second_color, density, seed}} MUST surround the battle with soft clouds shading between the two colours, as thick as density (0..1), with the stars dimmed behind them; seed MUST choose the pattern, the same for the same seed (a pocket inside a nebula; app 0.9.1).
  • sky: {top, horizon, fog, fog_distance, stars} MUST replace black space with a sky gradient from top (zenith) to horizon, fade distant objects into fog (default: the horizon colour) by fog_distance, and dim the starfield to stars (0–1).
  • An object class of kind: ground (a ground installation: a colony, an outpost, an anti-air battery) MUST be static and MUST be set down on the terrain wherever it is placed, at the ground height plus a quarter of its collision radius. Anti-air is a turret on the ground: a kind: ground class with beams, a turret_arc and a turret behaviour. The environment MUST be set before anything is placed, so this holds for scenario objects and mission roles alike; in space a ground object stays where it is placed.
  • Unknown environment ids in a mission MUST be reported by --check; a scenario with one MUST fail to build with a message naming it. An atmosphere without a terrain, or naming an unknown terrain, MUST be a rules error.

The default campaign MUST ship orbit, pocket (with a nebula backdrop), moon_surface and dusk_hills, and the ground installations guard_colony and dominion_flak (an anti-air battery); the interceptor campaign stays in space, as the original.

Rationale: Variety, and the surface missions of the default campaign. Environments are pack data so a mod can add worlds without code.

  • Implements: F-MSN-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.0, main af003f6; ground installations app 0.6.1, main de417df)
  • Verified by: content::environment::tests::environments_and_terrains_parse_and_report_mistakes, content::environment::nebula_tests::nebula_clouds_vary_stay_in_range_and_repeat_for_a_seed, sim::env::tests::ground_installations_are_set_down_on_the_terrain; MT-3-37 – MT-3-40, MT-3-45, MT-3-46, MT-4-24
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events, Environments and terrain

Open

Ground installations and anti-air batteries were resolved in 1.11.0 (app 0.6.1). Still open: choosing the environment and backdrop from the strategy map's location (location, backdrop: location, environment: body), which needs the strategy layer (Stage 4); scattered objects and detail textures are under R-FLT-012.

docs.title: R-MSN-009 Hazards
docs.text:
A mission or scenario MUST be able to declare hazards:. Each hazard is optional, and all are deterministic for a given seed.

  • asteroids: {class, count, radius, center, spin} (defaults 40, 5 km, origin, 4 °/s): count objects of the given class (an object such as cosmium_asteroid or asteroid), placed uniformly at random in the sphere radius around center. None is closer than 300 m to a craft already placed. Each turns at a random rate up to spin degrees per second. Being objects, they collide, block shots and can be destroyed. Asteroids are scenery: they MUST show on the radar only within radar range (other objects that never move, such as stations, still always show).
  • minefield: {class, count, radius, center, faction} (defaults 20, 2 km): count mines of a mine class (kind: mine, such as space_mine), placed the same way, belonging to faction (default: the class's own).
  • black_hole: {position, pull, radius} (defaults 15 m/s², 400 m): every craft and missile that can move is accelerated towards position.
  • The acceleration is pull m/s² at 1 km, growing with the inverse square of the distance and capped at 20 × pull.
  • A craft that comes within radius metres is destroyed.
  • It MUST be drawn as a black core (a sphere of radius) with a slowly turning accretion ring of glows.
  • AI pilots (other than idle objects) MUST turn away and burn out when inside 4 × radius, or within 10 × radius while heading in.
  • ion_storm: {sensors} (default 40 %): radar range is multiplied by sensors (a fraction, for example 40%), missile locks build at half speed, and the pilot is told ION STORM: SENSORS AT n% when the battle starts.

An unknown class or faction in a hazard MUST be an error: --check reports it for missions, and a scenario fails to build with it.

Rationale: Variety, and the original's battles in asteroid belts and next to a black hole.

  • Implements: F-MSN-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.5.1, main 70d68e2)
  • Verified by: content::hazards::tests::hazards_parse_with_defaults_and_report_mistakes, sim::hazards::tests::asteroid_fields_and_minefields_are_scattered_clear_of_craft, a_black_hole_pulls_harder_when_near_and_swallows_what_crosses_its_radius, ai_pilots_turn_away_from_a_black_hole, an_ion_storm_shortens_radar_range; MT-3-33 – MT-3-36
  • See: Format: missions, environments, events, Missions › Hazards, Deviations (DEV-045)

docs.title: R-MSN-010 Simulator missions
docs.text:
The player MUST be able to set up a simulator mission on a setup screen and fly it. As built, the setup screen (the launcher's Simulator entry) MUST offer:

  • the mission (any mission of the loaded campaign) and the ship (any playable ship, unless the mission fixes the player's class);
  • the environment: the mission's own, or any environment of the campaign;
  • asteroids, a minefield, a black hole and an ion storm, each on or off. Asteroids and mines MUST use the campaign's own classes (the first class whose id contains asteroid; the first kind: mine class); when the campaign has none, the row MUST say so and add nothing;
  • the enemy force, ×0.5, ×1, ×1.5 or ×2, scaling every enemy role's count range and every enemy wave, rounded and never below one. Friendly and objective roles MUST be unchanged.

The choices MUST produce a modified copy of the mission that is flown by the ordinary mission code; with the defaults (own environment, no hazards, ×1) the copy MUST equal the mission. A ship with atmospheric: false MUST be refused in an environment with physics: atmosphere, with the reason shown. Flying again from the debrief MUST fly the same setup. The difficulty level is the launcher's.

Rationale: The original's simulator; practice, and trying a mission in other conditions without editing it.

  • Implements: F-MSN-005, F-TST-004
  • Status: implemented (app 0.6.3, main 1d13b59, c3fb959)
  • Verified by: app::simulator::tests::a_setup_changes_environment_hazards_and_enemy_force_only, ships_that_cannot_enter_an_atmosphere_are_refused_there; app::launcher::tests::menu_lists_viewer_and_scenarios_and_wraps; MT-3-51 – MT-3-54
  • See: User guide › Simulator, Testbed › The simulator

Open

The interceptor campaign's own simulator mission types (R-CPN-005) are separate mission definitions still to be written (plan item 3.11); the simulator screen flies whatever missions a campaign defines.

docs.title: R-MSN-011 Base defence balance
docs.text:
In every base-defence mission, at every difficulty including the lowest, the base MUST survive long enough for the player to engage more than one attacker. Measured with --soak <mission> --soak-pilot idle (the player's craft sits still and does nothing): at the lowest level an undefended base or station MUST hold for at least 150 s.

Rationale: User request (F-MSN-006).

  • Implements: F-MSN-006
  • Status: implemented
  • Verified by: soak::tests::at_cadet_an_undefended_station_holds_for_150_seconds; MT-3-01, MT-3-05, MT-3-12, MT-3-17
  • See: Missions (modding), Manual tests (MT-3-01, MT-3-05)

Finding (app 0.3.1)

Measured with the idle pilot, xcom_base_defense at beginner still had 2 390 of 6 000 hull after 400 s, and the AI pilot won in 75 s with the base untouched. On veteran the mission ended at 15–18 s because the player's craft was destroyed by elerium torpedoes, while the debrief showed the base-lost text. The base was not too weak; the result was mislabelled. The fix is the killed result (R-MSN-003, R-MSN-005), not a change of pack values. Default campaign, defend_station, idle pilot: cadet still running at 400 s; ranger lose at 140 s; space ace killed at 8 s.

docs.title: R-MSN-012 Logistics missions
docs.text:
The convoy_ambush and construction_defence missions MUST be playable: protect the convoy against attackers; defend a facility shown in its construction-stage state. In convoy_ambush the enemy MUST be after the cargo: it wins by capturing a supply vessel or every cargo container, the convoy wins when its vessels have left with cargo aboard, and a battle in which a vessel never reaches its jump point MUST end in a draw after a time limit, delivering what is still aboard.

Rationale: Logistics in battle. The convoy battle was redesigned by the user after playtesting (app 0.9.2): a battle about cargo, not about killing raiders.

  • Implements: F-MSN-007
  • Status: implemented (the convoy design: app 0.9.2, main 0d1c522, 146195b)
  • Verified by: MT-3-02, MT-3-03, MT-4-26, MT-4-27
  • Reverse-engineered: yes
  • See: Logistics, Missions › The convoy ambush

As built (app 0.9.2)

Two clippers with twelve cargo pods and a point-defence laser each (R-STR-017) run about ten minutes to their jump point; grappler tugs come every two minutes from 140 s, each with a saucer squadron in formation on it (breaking off within 1.5 km), tear pods off and haul them 3 km before jumping out; raiders (freighter_raider) go for the clippers. Lose: captured_any(clippers) or destroyed_all(clippers) or cargo(clippers) == 0; win: count(clippers) == 0 and cargo(clippers) > 0; a 15-minute timer ends it in a draw.

Open

Generating construction_defence from the strategy layer is R-STR-019 / R-STR-023 (the convoy ambush is generated since app 0.9.2).

docs.text:
Requirements for packs, rule files, schemas, overrides, extraction, text, the condition language, validation and recipes, and (planned) the Mod Designer, 3D cockpit instrument placement, single-file models, cutscenes, video cutscenes and shared formations (design). The normative structure is Mod structure; every key is in the Mod file reference.

Features: Modding toolkit. How to read a requirement: Specification.
