Five parts (a mod may move them: Screen layouts):

  • Top bar. The date, your funds and the campaign score. In the middle the current base between < and > buttons: orders apply to it. On the right the clock — || pause, then 1h, 6h, 1d and 5d (campaign time per real second; the running speed is outlined) — then Save and Menu (save and go to the main menu).
  • Map (left). Star systems (hidden ones appear when your sensors reach them), lanes, your bases (squares) with their sensor ranges, enemy contacts once detected (red, with their way ahead), and your craft in flight. With a supply chain also your facilities (a diamond beside the system, grey while building, orange when working), supply convoys (gold dots) and survey ships (sky-blue rings). A legend runs along the bottom.
  • Wheel: zoom in and out about the mouse pointer — the point under it stays put.
  • Right or middle drag: pan.
  • Hover: the name of what is under the pointer.
  • Click: select the nearest system, contact, convoy, survey ship or craft in flight (moving things win when they are as close as a system). Clicking a system with one of your bases also makes that base current.
  • Info panel (right, top). What you selected, its details and its actions as buttons:
  • a system without a base: Build (); with logistics, Survey and Build () for each facility allowed there;
  • a system with a base that is not current: Make current;
  • a contact: where it is heading, how many craft are ready at the current base, and Intercept;
  • up to six buttons (app 0.16.1); a system where more could be built shows the first six;
  • a convoy, a survey ship or a craft: what it is doing.

    • With nothing selected it says how to use the map. - List buttons: eleven buttons that open a list in the panel below (twelve with the testbed's Debug list); the open one is outlined. - Panel (right, bottom). The open list (The lists). Rows that are too long end in ...; the selected row is shown in full under the list, with its actions as buttons. Click a row to select it; double-click to do its first action. The wheel, the scroll bar or Up/Down scroll the list. Grey rows are information only. Buttons that cannot be undone — Dismantle, Dismiss and Cancel — work only as buttons: Enter and a double click never do them (app 0.16.10 – 0.16.11).

    Every order answers in a short yellow line at the bottom of the map: Done., or why not (not enough money, not yet researched, the limit for that kind of module, too far from your other bases, no free pilot, …).

docs.title: Prompts
docs.text:
When something needs you, the clock stops by itself and a prompt opens in the middle of the screen with buttons; nothing else can be clicked until you answer.

Prompt Buttons Report — a building or base finished, research complete, a contact detected, a raid struck or driven off by your defences, the monthly report and its rating, a facility completed or lost, a survey's findings, a story message, a stance changed (also by a mission you flew, as soon as the map is back — app 0.16.2), new research possible, a delivery lost, a game loaded from another version of a pack OK (or Enter / Esc) Interception — your craft reached a contact Fly the battle, Auto-resolve (app 0.16.12), Break off (Enter / Esc) Convoy ambushed Fly the escort, Let it fight (Enter / Esc) Construction under attack — a facility being built is struck (app 0.16.4) Fly the defence, Let it be (Enter / Esc) Save game — the top bar's Save (app 0.16.14) Slot 1, Slot 2, Slot 3, Cancel A decision — a story choice One button per option (or the keys 1 – 5) Mission offered Fly it, Decline (Enter / Esc) Title card — a chapter opens Continue (or a click anywhere) The ending screen — the end (app 0.16.14; The story) Credits, Main menu (Enter / Esc: the main menu; both save first)

docs.title: Keys
docs.text:
The mouse does everything; the keys are shortcuts.

Key Does Space Pause, or resume at 1 day a second 1 – 4 Clock speed: 1 hour, 6 hours, 1 day or 5 days a second Tab / Shift+Tab Next / previous list Up / Down Choose a row Enter Do the selected row's first action Left / Right Change the current base 1 – 5 While a choice is offered: pick that option Enter / Esc In a prompt: the first / the last button F5 Save (the automatic save) Ctrl+M, Ctrl+K, Ctrl+B, Ctrl+J Testbed cheats (below) Ctrl+D Show or hide the testbed's Debug list (app 0.16.13) Esc Save and leave to the main menu

Since app 0.16.0 there are no hidden keys: selling (formerly S) and fitting (formerly F) are the Sell 1 and Fit best buttons.

docs.title: The lists
docs.text:
List Rows Buttons on the selected row Bases Each base: system, modules (and how many are building), what it researches. With a system selected that has no base: Build a at with its cost. Under the current base, each module with its state; Store: n of m used (a campaign with storage modules) and Quarters: room for n pilots (app 0.16.10) Select (make it current); Build; on a module Dismantle (half its cost back) Research What the current base researches; every topic that can be researched now, with progress and size; the topics known Research Build Modules the current base can build, with cost and build time; then its modules and their state (building, days left / working) Build Market Items and hulls on sale, with prices and what you have Buy 1, Buy 5 (delivered to the current base after the delivery time), Sell 1 (items, from the current base's store) Factory The current base's production rate; what it can make, with the work it takes; its queue Make 1, Make 5; on a queued job Move up (not the first) and Cancel (app 0.16.11) Hangar Every craft with its base, pilot (and away when out) and fit (standard fit or the items fitted); then your pilots with rank, kills, missions, state and training; then recruits with their stats and the fee On a craft: Assign pilot (the next free, ready pilot), Fit best (the best equipment in its base's store). On a pilot (app 0.16.7): Train / Stop training, Dismiss. On a recruit: Hire (refused when your quarters are full) Contacts Detected enemy flights and where they head Intercept: send the current base's craft that are at home and have a ready pilot Supply With a system selected: Survey it, and Build each kind of facility there (with the cost, and why not when it is not allowed). Then your facilities and what they hold or how long they take to build; on a working research station, the topics it can research; the current base's store of components; how many orders, convoys and survey ships are under way (Supply) Survey; Build; Start (research at a station) Archive The rival's plans you know of, with how far each is built; every faction's stance and standing with you; the rival's aggression and the battles you have won; the encyclopaedia entries unlocked so far (app 0.10.0) — Reports Your funds, score (and this month's), bases, craft and living pilots; then every monthly report, newest first, with its rating (app 0.16.8) — Messages The log, newest first, with dates — Debug (testbed, Ctrl+D) Each story arc's step; every story event, how often it has fired and whether its condition holds now (app 0.16.13) Fire now

Fit best fills every slot of the craft's hull with the best item of that kind in its base's store — beams, missile racks and, since app 0.15.0, shields and armour. In battle the craft flies with the strongest shield fitted and all its armour plates added up, in place of its hull's standard protection (standard fit means the hull's own). In the default campaign every hull has a shield and an armour slot, and you start with three deflector screens and three steel platings in store; research Force fields and Saucer alloys for better ones (app 0.16.1).

Training (app 0.16.7): a pilot in training improves every stat a little each day (in the default campaign 0.4 points, up to the stat's best) and costs money each day (400) until you press Stop training. Dismiss removes a pilot from the roster for good. Quarters: you can keep only as many pilots as your bases house — the Gatehouse houses four, the four you start with, so build Crew quarters (six more) before hiring (app 0.16.10). Defence: each Ray battery gives a base a 15 % chance of driving off a raid that reaches it unopposed (two: 28 %).

docs.title: Interceptions and battles
docs.text:
1. A raid is detected: the clock stops with Contact: , heading for .
  2. Click the contact on the map and press Intercept in the info panel — or select it in the Contacts list and press Intercept. Your ready craft fly to it on the map — along the lanes to the system nearest it, then straight to it (app 0.7.3). Raiders, too, come in along the lanes, and the map draws each one's way ahead.
  3. When they reach it, the clock stops and the Interception prompt asks: Fly the battle, Auto-resolve (app 0.16.12), or Break off (the contact flies on). Auto-resolve rolls the result at once from the strength of your craft there against the raid's — more and better hulls give better odds — and reports Auto-resolved (NN% odds): WIN or LOSE; the result counts like a flown battle's (a win credits the leader with the raid's kills), but your craft and pilots come back unharmed even from a loss.
  4. The battle is the raid's mission, with the first craft's hull as your ship and its fitted weapons, shields and armour (app 0.7.2, 0.15.0). Fly it as usual. When the result is decided the battle runs on until the debrief (Debrief); at the debrief, Enter or Esc returns to the map. Leaving from the pause menu (L or Q) counts as a retreat.
  5. Back on the map, a report gives the result and the kills. The outcome's score and money apply; the leader gains the kills and experience; if you were shot down, the craft is lost and its pilot ejected injured — or was killed. A prize you towed home with the tractor beam is kept when the mission's outcome says so, and can then be researched (app 0.16.3). With the interceptor campaign's music a short sting plays as the map returns — upbeat after a win, darker otherwise (app 0.16.2).

    6. A raid you do not stop strikes its target: a base loses its newest finished module, and the score drops.

docs.title: Supply
docs.text:
Default campaign, app 0.9.0. The Guard builds its craft from components — hull plating, rocket motors, ray emitters — made from mined resources. When you order a hull on the Factory list, the base orders the components it lacks; a manufacturing center makes them from resources it orders in turn from your mining facilities; everything is carried by automatic government supply convoys along the lanes. You do not move the convoys; you decide where to survey and what to build.

  1. Survey. Click a system on the map and press Survey in the info panel (or open the Supply list and choose Survey from ). The system must be within the current base's radar range. The survey ship flies there (a sky-blue ring); when it arrives a message lists the deposits it found, with their rates a day and how much is in reserve (or unlimited), the system's features and any research site (reserves and features since app 0.16.2). A survey ship may be attacked on the way: it fights off the attack or is lost (then survey again).
  2. Build. With a system selected, the info panel offers each kind of facility that may be built there as a button with its cost, and the Supply list offers every kind:
  3. a mining facility needs a surveyed system with deposits;
  4. a manufacturing center must be within two lanes of one of your bases;
  5. a research station needs a surveyed system that is a research site.

    6. The row says why when it cannot be built. A facility takes days to build (a grey diamond on the map) and a message says when it is complete. 3. Make. Queue a hull on the Factory list as usual. Its row waits until the components have arrived; the Supply list shows the base's store and the orders and convoys under way. 4. Research at a station. A finished research station lists the station-only topics of its kind (Research Theremin shielding here); a topic is refused when the station is not on its research site or its prerequisites are not known. The station first orders the topic's start materials; once they arrive it researches on its own.

    Convoys can be ambushed on the way. Since app 0.9.2 the clock stops with the Convoy ambushed prompt, and the convoy waits:

    • Fly the escort — fly its escort, Convoy ambush, with the first ready craft that has a pilot (from any base). Two cargo clippers, each with twelve cargo pods, make for their jump point about ten minutes away. Dominion grappler tugs come every couple of minutes, each with a squadron of saucers flying formation on it; a tug tears a pod off with its tractor beam, hauls it clear and jumps away with it, or takes a whole clipper once raiders have crippled it. Kill the tugs before they get away, keep the raiders off the clippers, and the clippers' own laser helps against missiles. The battle is won when the clippers have jumped with cargo aboard, lost if a clipper is captured or every pod is gone, and a draw after 15 minutes if a crippled clipper never makes its jump. Back on the map, the share of the cargo still aboard is delivered (a loss delivers nothing; leaving the battle early lets the convoy fight on alone).
    • Let it fight — let it fight through alone: each vessel may be lost, a message says how many, and the survivors deliver their share. This is also what happens when no craft is ready.

    What is missing is simply ordered again.

    Construction can be struck (app 0.16.4). From the time a facility is half built, the Dominion may strike it — in the default campaign a 12 % chance a day, at most three strikes per system. The clock stops with Construction under attack:

    • Fly the defence — fly Construction defence with the first ready craft: win, and the strike is beaten off; lose, and the site is destroyed.
    • Let it be — the strike sets the work back by a quarter of its build time. This is also what happens when no craft is ready.

docs.title: The story
docs.text:
App 0.10.0 – 0.10.3. The story runs by itself as the days pass; you meet it as messages that stop the clock, choices, offered missions and, finally, an ending.

  • Messages and news. A story message stops the clock and shows in a report (a chapter of the default campaign's serial, an alien transmission in interceptor); news lines go into the log without stopping it.
  • Choices. A decision lists the options as buttons; click one (or press its number). The clock does not run until you choose. What you choose changes money, relations, flags and sometimes offers a mission.
  • Offered missions. Mission offered names it: Fly it flies it at once with the first ready craft that has a pilot; its result counts like a raid's battle (score, money, salvage, and the story flags it sets). With no ready craft it says so, and the offer is gone.
  • The rival's plan. A rival builds something from shipments that cross the map as contacts: intercept them and win, and the shipment is lost; let one reach its destination and the plan grows. Messages warn you as it nears completion, and the Archive list shows how far it is. If it is completed, you lose.
  • Relations (default campaign). Every faction has a standing with you from −100 to 100 and a stance — hostile, wary, neutral, friendly or allied. Story events and, since app 0.12.1, the missions you fly move them (winning the nebula-pocket ambush lowers the raiders' standing), and they drift back towards neutral each month. A change of stance stops the clock with a report — one caused by a mission as soon as you are back on the map (app 0.16.2). A faction that is no longer hostile stops raiding you and does not attack you in battle; one that turns hostile does. The Senate's stipend grows with its standing.
  • The rival's mood. Sit back and the rival grows bolder — its raids come more often; win battles every month and it grows more careful.
  • The end. When an ending is reached the ending screen fills the window (app 0.16.14): VICTORY or DEFEAT, the ending's text, and your record — the date, the final score, the battles won, your bases and craft — with Credits (the credits roll, then the main menu) and Main menu; both save first. In the default campaign you win by destroying the Eclipse Engine and lose if it is lit, if you lose your last base, or if the Senate turns against you; in interceptor you win by destroying the Doomsday weapon and lose if it is completed or your last base falls.

docs.title: Films, cutscenes and music
docs.text:
App 0.11.0 – 0.13.0.

  • Title cards. Each chapter of the default campaign's serial opens with a full-screen card — the chapter's title and its hook — and the clock stops. Continue (or Enter, Esc or a click) dismisses it; then the chapter's mission is offered as before.
  • Films. In interceptor, each of the five alien transmissions plays the original's transmission film from your data, the victory plays the closing credits, and a new campaign opens with the original's opening film. The film fills the screen (letterboxed); Enter, Esc, a click or the gamepad's Start, A or B skips it, and the map comes back where you left it.
  • Cutscenes. The default campaign opens with a short scene played by the engine itself — a Guard patrol meets a saucer over the Gatehouse — with captions and black bars. Esc, Enter, a click or the gamepad's Start, A or B skips it.
  • Music. Battles play the campaign's music: calm while no enemy is near, tense when one is within radar range, driving when one is close, changing at the end of a musical phrase. A win plays a victory sting, any other result a darker one. The strategy screen has its own music; in interceptor it also plays a short good-news sting for a battle won and finished research, and a bad-news one for a battle lost (app 0.16.2). The launcher and the other testbed screens are silent. Set the music and effects volumes in the launcher with M and V (Settings).
  • Who is speaking. In any battle, when someone speaks on the radio a small panel at the top left shows their portrait and name for a moment (app 0.13.1) — in the default campaign the Guard Wing and Colony Control; voices without a portrait show moving signal bars.
  • The end. An ending with a film plays it first, then the ending screen. Continuing a finished campaign shows its ending again (app 0.12.1).

docs.title: Money and the monthly report
docs.text: Incomes (the default campaign's Senate stipend grows with your bases, your month's score and, since app 0.10.1, the Senate's standing with you) and expenses are paid on their own schedules and logged. Every 30 days the monthly report charges module maintenance, craft upkeep and pilot salaries, shows the month's score, the total and your funds, and a new set of recruits is offered. Since app 0.16.8 the patron also rates the month: in the default campaign the Senate rates it Outstanding (a month's score of 400 or more: a 150 000 bonus), Satisfactory (0 or more), Poor (−300 or more: 50 000 cut) or Unacceptable (150 000 cut). The Reports list keeps every monthly report with its rating. Pilots in training cost money every day. A purchase can be lost on its way when the campaign says so (not in the default campaign) — paid for all the same.

docs.title: Saves
docs.text:
• F5, leaving with Menu or Esc, and the end of a campaign write the automatic save, <user data folder>/saves/<campaign>.yaml (for example saves/default.yaml); Continue loads it. The user data folder is described on Settings.
  • Save in the top bar asks for a slot — Slot 1, Slot 2 or Slot 3 (app 0.16.14) — and writes saves/<campaign>-<n>.yaml. The main menu's Load game page lists the automatic save and the three slots with how long ago each was written (just now, 5 minutes ago, 2 hours ago, 3 days ago) or empty; Enter loads one, Esc goes back.
  • A save records the packs it was played with. Loading refuses a save that needs a pack that is not active, or one whose rules no longer fit it (a mod was changed), with a message. A save made with another version of a pack that is active loads, with a report naming the two versions (app 0.16.2).

docs.title: Testbed cheats and tools
docs.text:
The testbed keeps the original game's own cheat list as debug keys on the strategy screen (app 0.8.1). Each says so in the yellow feedback line.

Key Cheat Does Ctrl+M payday A million more in funds. Ctrl+K knowitall Every research topic known; bases stop researching. Ctrl+B quickbase Every base and module under construction finished now (not supply facilities). Ctrl+J jump to battle With a contact selected on the map (or its row selected in the Contacts list): a ready craft with a pilot is put at it at once, and the Interception prompt appears. Otherwise it says Select a contact first, or no ready craft with a pilot. Ctrl+D debug Shows (or hides) the Debug list (app 0.16.13): Arc serial: step n of 12 and every story event with how often it has fired and whether its condition holds now. Fire now fires the selected event at once — its title card, message, choice or offered mission appear as in play; the story moves on only if it is the next chapter.

Start at a chapter (app 0.16.13): openinterceptor --no-original --strategy --chapter 6 plays a new default campaign forward by itself — researching, intercepting, flying the offered missions automatically — until the serial reaches chapter 6, then opens the map there. It takes a moment; it stops after at most 1500 days or at an ending.

docs.title: Limits in app 0.16.14
docs.text:
• Fitting takes the best items in store; you cannot choose them one by one yet.
  • Facilities have no fighters of their own, and the Supply list is plain text.
  • The info panel shows at most six action buttons; a system where more could be built shows the first six (the Bases and Supply lists offer them all).
  • There is no separate screen per list and no 3D base view yet. The pilots list does not show a pilot's stats, so training is seen only in a save file.
  • Auto-resolve counts your hulls, not their fitted equipment or pilots.
  • Several chapters of the default campaign's serial fly an existing mission rather than their own; allied factions do not yet fly at your side; two of the original's seven side missions are in interceptor. Neither campaign has been played through from start to finish yet.
  • Films and cutscenes cannot be skipped from the tablet console yet (the gamepad skips them since app 0.16.2).
  • The default campaign's music has no good-news or bad-news sting.
  • The interceptor campaign's strategy layer has not been play-tested; its research is slow with one downlink. Reading the code suggests a base without a finished cargo module cannot buy anything (no room in store) — please report it if you see it.
  • Fixed in app 0.9.0: manufacturing now costs money as each unit starts, and the default campaign's salvage topics (Saucer hull analysis, Robot brains) can be started after salvaging the right raid.

docs.title: Cockpit and HUD
docs.text: What the instruments in front of you show. In the cockpit view (F1) they sit in the cockpit's own art or 3D dashboard; in the other views, and for a craft without a cockpit, the same instruments are drawn as a plain glass HUD. Where each instrument sits is the cockpit's choice (Modding › Cockpits); what follows is what each one means.

docs.title: Radar scopes and shield rings
docs.text:
Two round scopes: the front scope shows what is ahead of you, the rear scope what is behind (mirrored, as in a rear-view mirror). A contact's distance from the centre is its angle off your nose (or tail): the rim is 90°. Contacts are in their side's colours, stations drawn larger, your target boxed.

Just inside each scope's rim a ring shows one shield facing: the front scope the fore shield, the rear scope the aft. Green above two thirds, amber above one third, red below, blinking red when that facing is down.

docs.title: The ship status display
docs.text:
App 0.15.1. A round display with your craft seen from above in the middle:

  • The craft is tinted by its hull: green when whole, turning amber, then red as it nears destruction.
  • An arc ahead of it is your fore shield, an arc behind it the aft shield. Each has up to three bands, one for every third of that shield: three lit means more than two thirds left, two more than a third, one a little, none — the facing is down. The bands take the same green / amber / red as the shield rings and blink when the facing is down.

So you can see at a glance which side is exposed: turn the stronger facing towards the enemy, or shift power to the weak one (the shield balance keys, see Controls).

Where it is:

Cockpit Place Glass HUD Beside the gauges, where the shield needle used to be. The default campaign's 3D cockpit The third gauge bezel, right of the MFD. The X-COM cockpits The round ship display in the cockpit art. Its place was set by eye; if it sits off, press F12 in the cockpit view to move it (layout editor).

docs.title: Gauges
docs.text: Round needles: speed, energy, shields (both facings added up) and hull; a needle turns red below a quarter. The default cockpit and the glass HUD show the ship status display in place of the shield needle.

docs.title: The MFD
docs.text: The multi-function display has five pages — Target (name, side, range, speed, its shields, armour and hull, lock state), Weapons (beams, link mode, missile racks with the selected one marked), Status (your shields with their balance, armour, hull, energy and the power line), Systems (each fitted system: OK, on, damaged, out, destroyed) and Nav. The MFD key cycles them (controls reference).

docs.title: Power and systems
docs.text:
• Power: the beam and shield charge settings (B- and S-, A to E), then bars for the fore and aft shields; used/budget in yellow when the power budget is spent.
  • Systems: one lamp per fitted system with a three-letter label — green working, cyan switched on, amber damaged, red knocked out (blinking while being repaired), dark destroyed.

A cockpit that has no place for them shows them as small panels at the top right.

docs.title: The status line and messages
docs.text:
• Status line: throttle, forward speed and drift (THR 60% 312 m/s X+45 Y-12: sideways and vertical slide in m/s), then flags such as BURN, BRAKE, HOLD n, VCT, CLOAKED, ECM, JUMP n. Over a planet it adds ALT (height above the ground) and VS (vertical speed).
  • Message line: the newest message, for a few seconds.
  • In a battle, a comms panel at the top left shows who is speaking on the radio (app 0.13.1).

docs.title: Targeting
docs.text: In the forward views: a reticle; brackets around the target; its name and range; a lead circle where to aim beams; a ring that fills while a missile locks, then a red diamond and LOCK; an arrow at the edge when the target is off screen; a blue diamond on a nav point. A small circle with three ticks is the flight-path marker: where you are actually moving. Over a planet an artificial horizon with a pitch ladder is drawn ahead.

docs.title: Tablet console
docs.text:
The game can serve a control console: a web page that a tablet (or a phone, or another computer) on the same network opens next to your joystick or gamepad. It shows your craft's condition live and offers every control as a labelled button, so nothing depends on remembering shortcuts.

The console has two layouts — All-in-one, every control at once, and Cockpit, laid out like a cockpit with function-group tiles (app 0.4.11) — a Target view that shows your target's model turned the way it faces you (0.4.14), a TIE Fighter-style Map of every radar contact on which you can tap a craft to target it (0.4.15), and a look that follows the campaign and the cockpit you fly (0.5.0). A physical panel over USB (C5) comes later (Stage 3 interlude).

docs.title: Turn it on
docs.text:
The console is off by default. Turn it on for one run:

target/release/openinterceptor --console                 # port 8765
target/release/openinterceptor --console-port 9000       # another port (implies --console)

or for every run, in settings.yaml in the user data folder (Settings):

console:
  enabled: true
  port: 8765          # change it if another program already uses 8765

When the game starts it prints the address and a 6-digit pairing code in the terminal:

console: open http://192.168.1.20:8765 on the tablet; pairing code 123456

The launcher shows the console's status and address too, and in flight the same line (CONSOLE http://… CODE …) is shown at the bottom left of the screen until a tablet pairs, and again whenever the menu (Esc) is open. A new code is chosen each time the game starts.

If the port is taken, the game says so (console: port 8765 is not available …) and carries on without the console; pick another port.

docs.title: Pair a tablet
docs.text:
1. Connect the tablet to the same local network as the computer running the game. The game serves only local-network addresses; anything from the internet is refused.
  2. Open the address in the tablet's browser (Safari on an iPad works). On an iPad, Share → Add to Home Screen gives it a full-screen icon.
  3. Type the pairing code. The page connects as soon as the sixth digit is entered — there is no need for Enter, which an iPad's number pad does not have. It shows Connecting…, then the console.

You can pair from the launcher or during a battle. On the launcher the console shows Not flying (launcher) and every button; they start working when a battle starts.

The address can also carry the code: http://192.168.1.20:8765/?code=123456 pairs straight away (a QR code in the game will use this later).

A wrong code is answered with wrong pairing code; after three wrong codes the game closes that connection (reload the page to try again). The code is remembered for the browser tab, so reloading the page reconnects without typing it again.

If the game cannot be reached the page says Could not reach the game. Is it still running? If the connection drops (the game quits, Wi-Fi drops), the page returns to the code screen with Disconnected. Enter the code to reconnect. Anything the console was holding (fire, afterburner, a turn) is let go the moment it disconnects.

docs.title: Two layouts
docs.text:
The button at the top of the page switches between the two layouts. Each tablet remembers its choice; the address can also choose one (?mode=cockpit or ?mode=allinone).

  • All-in-one: everything at once, described in the next section.
  • Cockpit: laid out like a cockpit (The Cockpit layout).

Both are live all the time, so switching never loses anything.

docs.title: The All-in-one layout
docs.text:
• Telemetry, updated 20 times a second: craft, speed, drift (sideways and vertical speed), hull, energy, shields fore and aft, the selected missile and how many are left, and the current target with its distance.
  • Throttle: a slider from 0 to 100 %. It sets the throttle position directly, and follows the game's throttle when you change it from the keyboard or stick.
  • Every action in the game's action list, as a button, grouped as on the keys overlay (Controls). A console button does exactly what the bound key does:
    • hold buttons (turns, slides, afterburner, brake, fire beams, the chase camera) act while you keep your finger on them;
    • tap buttons (target cycling, missiles, views, power, systems) act once per tap.
  • Not fitted: a feature your current craft lacks — cloak, ECM, tractor beam, the VCT slides, missiles or beams — is shown greyed out and labelled not fitted, never hidden. The list is sent again when you switch to a craft of another class.

Under each button's name a small caption says in a sentence what it does (two lines at most; the full sentence is also the button's tooltip) — since app 0.15.1.

A pressed button lights up — filled with its border colour, its text black — for as long as you hold it, or briefly after a tap, so you can see every press register (app 0.4.9). When your craft is hit by weapons fire, the console flickers with a short burst of static: lighter when your shields take the hit, stronger when the hull is struck.

Several tablets can pair at once; each one's held buttons are tracked separately.

docs.title: The Cockpit layout
docs.text:
• Top: the HUD strip, as on the exterior view's HUD — speed, drift, throttle, hull, energy, the target and its range, and status (beam link mode, BURN, BRAKE).
  • Left: the shield rings, fore and aft, with buttons to balance the shields equally, forward or aft.
  • Centre: the display console, with two tabs, Target and Map.
  • Right: the power sliders for beam and shield charge (A at the bottom). The power budget still applies: raising one may lower the other, and the slider follows what the game allows.
  • Below: one tile per function group (flight, throttle, weapons, targeting, power, wingmen, views, camera, interface). Each tile is a status card; it also says how many of its controls your craft lacks (2 not fitted). Tap a tile to open a full-width strip with that group's buttons; the other tiles fold to their titles. Tap the open title again to close the strip, or another title to switch to that group.

docs.title: The Target tab
docs.text:
The display console's Target tab shows your target's name in its relation's colour (with PROTECT for a craft you must protect), its distance and closing speed, and bars for its hull and fore and aft shields; beside them the target's model, turned the way it is facing as seen from your craft: nose towards you means it is coming at you. The model is drawn in one flat colour per part (the game sends the shape, not its textures), lit from the upper left. With no target the view is empty.

Under the target data, the last four lines of the message log — the same messages as the cockpit's message line.

docs.title: The Map tab
docs.text:
The Map tab is a 3D map of the battle around you, in the style of TIE Fighter's map:

  • you are at the centre; a grid and range rings at a quarter, half and the whole of your radar range lie flat at your height;
  • every craft on your radar is a mark — a dot for a craft, a square for a station — with a stalk down or up to the grid showing how far above or below you it is;
  • colours give the relation: green friendly, red hostile, yellow neutral, blue an objective you protect; your current target is ringed;
  • each label gives the name and range; a short tick shows where the craft will be in two seconds;
  • beside the map, a list of the nearest contacts by range.
Gesture Effect Behind, Top, Side Jump to a view: from behind you, from above (up the screen is your nose), or from the side. Drag with one finger (or the mouse) Orbit the view. Pinch, or the mouse wheel Zoom in or out. Tap a contact, or a row of the list Target it, as if you had cycled to it. Only craft still on your radar can be targeted.

The map shows craft only; nav points are not on it yet.

docs.title: Themes
docs.text:
The console takes its look from the campaign you play, and while flying, from your craft's cockpit (0.5.0):

  • The default campaign: art-deco — brass lines on midnight-blue panels, cream text, amber values, set in Futura (or the nearest font the tablet has).
  • X-COM: Interceptor: a green instrument look, tinted for each cockpit — olive bronze in cockpit A, steel blue in B, red in C. These are colours only, chosen to match each cockpit; no original art appears on the console.

On the launcher the console shows the campaign's base look; in a battle, the cockpit's tint. A mod can set its own (Console themes).

docs.title: Keeping the screen on
docs.text:
While the console page is open, it keeps the tablet's screen from going to sleep (app 0.4.8). Where the browser allows it, it asks for a screen wake lock; Safari allows that only on secure (https) pages, so on an iPad the page instead plays a tiny, silent video, which browsers do not let the screen sleep through. Since app 0.4.11 the video is a small radar-sweep "link" indicator in the bottom-right corner, because iOS pauses videos that cannot be seen. It starts when you pair, and again when you come back to the page. The Tablet cell of the telemetry shows the state:

Tablet cell Meaning screen kept awake (wake lock) The browser's wake lock is holding the screen on. screen kept awake The silent video is playing. tap the screen to keep it awake The browser wants a tap before it plays the video: tap anywhere.

If the iPad still goes to sleep, set Settings › Display & Brightness › Auto-Lock to a longer time or Never while you play.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Symptom Cause and fix The page does not load The tablet is on another network (guest Wi-Fi, mobile data), or a firewall blocks the port. On macOS, allow incoming connections for OpenInterceptor when asked. The address shows this-computer The game could not work out the computer's network address; use the computer's IP address instead. wrong pairing code Type the code currently shown in the game; it changes every time the game starts. The page stays on Connecting… The game is older than 0.4.7, where only a running battle answered: update, or start a battle. Could not reach the game The game has quit, or the tablet is on another network. The tablet goes to sleep See Keeping the screen on; set Auto-Lock as a fallback. Buttons do nothing Check the in-game screen: the battle may be paused or the menu open. The Target view is empty There is no target, or the browser has no WebGL (try another browser). Tapping a contact does not target it It has left your radar range; the list and map update five times a second. The colours do not match the cockpit The cockpit's tint arrives when the battle starts, or when you change to a craft of another class; on the launcher the campaign's base look is shown.

To test the console without a tablet, developers can use tools/console_client.py (Remote console).

docs.title: Controls
docs.text: OpenInterceptor is flown with the keyboard, the mouse or a gamepad. The default keys follow the original game; every action can be rebound. The full table of actions with their default keys and gamepad buttons is on the controls reference.

docs.title: The keys overlay
docs.text:
Press ? (Shift + /) in flight — or Shift+F1 — to see every key. The battle pauses under a panel titled KEYS that lists every action, grouped, with your current bindings: keys first, then gamepad buttons (pad A), or "unbound" if the action has none. Since app 0.15.1 each action also has a one-sentence description of what it does, in a dimmer line beneath it when the window is wide enough for it; on a smaller window the list falls back to one line per action, in several columns if needed.

Press ?, Shift+F1 or Esc to close it; the battle resumes. The pause menu (Esc) has a line pointing to it.

Plain F1 is not the overlay: it selects the cockpit view, as in the original (F1–F8 are the views). F12 in the cockpit view of a ship with cockpit art opens the cockpit layout editor instead.

The overlay is built from the same action table as the bindings file and the controls menu, so it always shows what the keys really do, including your own changes.

docs.title: Simple physics
docs.text:
OpenInterceptor flies Realistic (Newtonian) physics by default: the craft keeps drifting in the direction it was going after you turn, until thrust or the brake changes it. Players used to traditional space fighter games can choose Simple physics instead:

  • In the launcher, press P. The campaign line shows Physics: Simple (P: change) or Physics: Realistic (P: change). The choice is saved in settings.yaml (game.physics, Settings).
  • In Simple, your craft always travels where its nose points, at the speed the throttle sets, with no drift after a turn or a collision. The slide (VCT) keys still move it sideways. Enemy and wingman craft fly as before.
  • Simple is offered only on the campaign's first three difficulty levels. At higher levels the launcher shows Physics: Realistic (always, at this level) and P does nothing.
  • In flight, the HUD's status line shows SIMPLE while it is in use.
Group What is in it Flight Pitch, yaw, roll, the sideways and vertical slides (VCT) Throttle and speed Throttle steps and settings, reverse thrust, brake, afterburner, match speed Weapons Fire beams, fire a missile, link mode, missile choice Targeting Next / previous target, nearest hostile, target in sights Power and systems Beam and shield charge, power transfers, shield balance, tractor, cloak, ECM, hyperspace Wingmen and comms The comms menu and wingman orders, repeat message Views Cockpit, forward, side and rear views, chase and manual chase camera Chase camera Orbiting and zooming the manual chase camera Interface MFD pages, nav points, pause, the menu, mouse flight, the keys overlay (help)

docs.title: Wingmen and formations
docs.text: Your wingmen fly in a formation — a vee unless the mission names another. Shift+O (Wingmen: next formation) moves them into the campaign's next formation: both campaigns have vee, line abreast, echelon, box and diamond, in that order, and the list wraps. The cockpit message says which (WINGMEN: FORM LINE ABREAST), or NO WINGMEN. The other wing orders — Shift+F fire at will, Shift+A attack my target, Shift+I form up (ignore my target), Shift+E evasive, Shift+R retreat, Shift+S status — are unchanged; after evasive or form up the wingmen return to the formation last ordered (app 0.6.6). Formations are pack data (Mod file reference › formations).

docs.title: Rebinding
docs.text:
Open the controls menu from the launcher (Controls (keyboard, gamepad, mouse)) or in flight from the pause menu (Esc, then K):

  • Each action has two key slots and two gamepad slots. Select a cell and press Enter (pad A), then press the new key — hold Shift for a Shift chord — or the new button (hold a modifier button and press a second one for a pad chord). Esc cancels.
  • Delete (pad X) clears a cell, D (pad Y) restores the action's defaults, Shift+D restores every default.
  • A key taken by another action is moved: the status line names the action that lost it.
  • Leaving the menu applies the bindings at once and saves them to bindings.yaml in your user data folder (see Settings).

The device settings at the end of the menu set the stick dead zone, pitch inversion, the stick layout (space, as the original joystick, or aircraft), the mouse-flight range and mouse inversion.

bindings.yaml can also be edited by hand; actions not mentioned keep their defaults, and the names are those in the controls reference:

keyboard:
  fire_beams: [Enter, LeftControl]
  help: [Shift+Slash, Shift+F1]
gamepad:
  fire_beams: [RightTrigger]
options:
  stick_layout: space

A broken file cannot lock you out: it is reported and the defaults are used. Deleting it recreates the defaults on the next run.

docs.title: Mouse flight
docs.text: Press C to fly with the mouse: the cursor's offset from the centre steers (cursor down lowers the nose), the left button fires beams and the right button a missile. Press C again to free the cursor.

docs.title: What you need
docs.text:
• Rust 1.86 or newer (rustup, stable). The project is checked with 1.99.
  • macOS 11+ (Apple silicon) with the Xcode command line tools, or Linux with X11 (Wayland through XWayland) and OpenGL 3. On Debian/Ubuntu install libasound2-dev libx11-dev libxi-dev libgl1-mesa-dev first.
  • Nothing else for the default campaign: everything the game ships is in the repository, in editable formats. Original data is optional: to play the interceptor campaign you need your own X-COM: Interceptor, an installed copy or the CD.

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/bbogovich/OpenInterceptor.git
cd OpenInterceptor
cargo build --release

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
Folder Holds In Git resources/default/ The default campaign, Perils of the Void: everything the game ships, in editable formats (YAML, OBJ, PNG, WAV) yes resources/xcom/ Your installed copy of X-COM: Interceptor (optional; tried first) no, git-ignored resources/xcom-cd/ A copy of your X-COM: Interceptor CD (optional) no, git-ignored packs/ Bundled mods, such as interceptor (which needs your original data). Mods override resources yes <user data folder>/mods/ Your own mods (--mods or settings.yaml paths.mods moves it) no

Content is loaded from resources/ first, then packs/, then your mods; a later pack overrides an earlier one. --packs DIR replaces only the bundled-mods folder.

docs.title: Put your original data in place (optional)
docs.text:
Most players will play the default campaign and can skip this. If you own X-COM: Interceptor, copy an installed copy of the game to resources/xcom/ in your checkout, or the CD contents (the folder with Resources/, ProgramFiles/ and Animations/) to resources/xcom-cd/. If your copy has the CD audio tracks extracted, put them in a CD Audio/ folder inside it. Both folders are git-ignored, and each counts only once it holds files.

You rarely need --data: the engine looks, in order, at --data, the OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA variable, settings.yaml paths: {original: …} in the user data folder, <user data folder>/original, then resources/xcom/ and finally resources/xcom-cd/ in the development checkout (Settings and data discovery). An installed app keeps your original data (or a copy of it), settings.yaml, bindings.yaml and mods/ in the user data folder (a settings.ini or bindings.ini from an earlier build is read once and replaced by the YAML file).

docs.title: Build the macOS app
docs.text:
python3 tools/build_bundle.py            # dist/OpenInterceptor-<version>.app

The app contains the engine, resources/default and the bundled mods in packs/, never original data. The script points settings.yaml at resources/xcom/ (else resources/xcom-cd/, or --data PATH); --install-data clones that data into the user data folder instead, as a real install would. Open the app from Finder. See Packaging.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
# The main menu of the chosen campaign (the original data is found automatically); a
# campaign without a strategy layer opens on the testbed launcher instead:
target/release/openinterceptor

# Only original-free packs (the default campaign, your own mods):
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original

# Choose the campaign (default: the last one chosen in the launcher, else interceptor
# when original data is found, else default):
target/release/openinterceptor --campaign default

# ... at a chosen difficulty level:
target/release/openinterceptor --campaign default --difficulty space_ace

# Open a new campaign's strategy screen directly (a campaign with a strategy layer):
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --strategy

# Go straight to one mission (or scenario) with one ship:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --mission defend_station --ship comet

# How long each playable ship needs to destroy each class (shields, armour, hull, dps):
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --balance --difficulty captain

# Play a mission headless with the AI pilot and print the result:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --soak defend_station --soak-pilot ai --seconds 400

# Go straight to one scenario with one ship:
target/release/openinterceptor --data resources/xcom --scenario flight-test --ship lightning

# ... and start in the chase view:
target/release/openinterceptor --data resources/xcom --scenario flight-test --ship firestar --view chase

# Serve the tablet control console (the game shows the URL and pairing code):
target/release/openinterceptor --console

# Headless validation of every campaign, pack, model and texture; list what loaded:
target/release/openinterceptor --check
target/release/openinterceptor --list

# Render a scenario's starting screen to a PNG and exit:
target/release/openinterceptor --no-original --scenario rocket-vs-saucer --ship comet --screenshot shot.png

# Open the model viewer on one model (ship id or original mesh name):
target/release/openinterceptor --model XBASE7

# Convert the original data to OBJ/PNG/WAV for modding (personal use only):
target/release/openinterceptor --extract ~/interceptor-extracted

# The quality gate (tests, build, checks):
scripts/check.sh

docs.title: Command-line options
docs.text:
Option Meaning --data <PATH> Your original data: an installed Interceptor or the CD. Without it: OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA, then settings.yaml, then <user data>/original, then resources/xcom (installed copy) and resources/xcom-cd (CD copy) in a checkout. --mods <DIR> Folder of user mods (default: settings.yaml paths: {mods: …}, else mods/ in the user data folder). --packs <DIR> Folder of bundled mods (default: packs/ next to the program, or the source tree). It replaces only that folder: resources/ (the default campaign) is always loaded first. --console Serve the tablet control console (settings: console.enabled). --console-port <N> The console's port (default 8765; settings: console.port); implies --console. --no-original Ignore the original data even if available. --campaign <ID> Load this campaign (default: the last one chosen in the launcher, else interceptor when the data is available, else default). --difficulty <ID> Play at this difficulty level, a level id of the campaign (default: the last one chosen, else the campaign's default_difficulty). --scenario <ID> Start this scenario, skipping the launcher. --mission <ID> Start this mission, skipping the launcher (Missions). --strategy Start a new campaign on the strategy screen, skipping the launcher (app 0.7.1; Campaign). Without a strategy layer the launcher opens. The campaign's intro cutscene or film is not played this way. --chapter <N> With --strategy: play the new campaign forward by itself until its story reaches chapter N (its first arc's step N; at most 1500 days), then open the strategy screen there (app 0.16.13; Campaign › Testbed cheats and tools). Ignored without --strategy. --credits Open on the campaign's credits roll (or its credits film), then the main menu (app 0.14.0). --cutscene <ID> Play this cutscene of the campaign, then open the main menu (or the launcher, for a campaign without a strategy layer) (app 0.13.0; Cutscenes). --video <REF> Play this video, then open the main menu (or the launcher) (app 0.12.0): original:<file>.smk from your data (for example original:alientrans1.smk) or a pack path; Smacker files only. --strategy-soak <DAYS> Play the campaign's strategy layer without a window for that many days with a simple automatic player, print one line (date, funds, score, bases, craft, topics, battles, messages) and exit (app 0.8.0; Strategy layer). Use with --campaign. --ship <ID> Player ship for --scenario when the scenario lets you choose. --view <VIEW> Start view: cockpit, forward, left, right, rear-left, rear-right, chase, chase-manual. --model <NAME> Open the model viewer on this model: a ship class id (comet) or an original mesh name (XBASE7). --screenshot <PNG> With --scenario or --model: render the starting screen for --frames frames, save it as a PNG and exit. --frames <N> Frames to run before --screenshot (default 120). --check Validate all content without a window, then exit (status 1 on errors). Every campaign is checked separately, with its own addons; --campaign checks one. --balance Print a balance report and exit (app 0.15.0): for every class of the campaign at the difficulty level — shield per facing, armour, hull, effective hit points against beams from one side (the three added up), and sustained beam damage per second (limited by its energy recharge) — and, for each playable ship, the seconds of perfect beam fire it needs to destroy that class. Real fights take longer (bolts miss, shields recharge); compare the ratios. Use with --campaign and --difficulty. --soak <SCENARIO or MISSION> Play a scenario — or a mission, which then prints its result (soak mission <id> (<level>, <pilot>): <result> after <n> s; <k> kills) — without a window for --seconds (default 60) and report what happened to the player's ship (balance testing); the player is --soak-pilot passive (default: flies at the nearest enemy and never shoots), ai (its class's behaviour) or idle (sits still and does nothing: how long a defended object holds on its own). Use with --ship, --campaign, --difficulty. --language <CODE> Text language: the packs' text/<CODE>/ folders (default en, or settings.yaml game.language). --write-schemas <DIR> Write the JSON Schema files of the mod file types (pack.schema.json, rules.schema.json, scenario.schema.json) for editor completion and checking, then exit. --extract <DIR> Convert the original data to OBJ/PNG/WAV at the paths where mod files override it (Overrides and extraction), then exit. --list List campaigns (* = loaded), packs, playable ships and scenarios, then exit. --windowed / --fullscreen Window mode for this run. Without either, the game starts as settings.yaml graphics.fullscreen says (windowed by default; app 0.16.14); --windowed overrides the setting. --help Usage.

Environment: OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA (default for --data), OI_DEBUG_KEYS=1 (print key names as you press them).

The user data folder (settings.yaml, bindings.yaml, original/, mods/) is ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/ on macOS and $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/) on Linux.

docs.title: The main menu
docs.text:
Since app 0.14.0 a campaign with a strategy layer — the default campaign and interceptor — opens on its main menu: the campaign's title and subtitle over a starfield, a ship turning behind, the campaign's skin and its menu music. Up/Down (or the pad's D-pad) choose, Enter (pad A or Start) selects, Esc (pad B or Back) goes back or, on the main page, quits.

Item Does Continue Loads the campaign's automatic save (shown only when there is one). New campaign Starts a new campaign at the chosen difficulty, after its introduction (Campaign). Load game Shown when one of the three save slots holds a game (app 0.16.14): a page listing the automatic save and Slot 1 – Slot 3, each with how long ago it was written or empty, then Back. Enter loads the chosen one; Esc goes back (Campaign › Saves). Battles & tools The testbed launcher (below): scenarios, missions, the simulator, the viewers. Esc there returns to the menu. Options Campaign, difficulty, physics (on the levels that allow Simple), music and effects volume, Full screen and Controls... (app 0.16.14); Left/Right changes the row (Enter too for Full screen; Enter opens Controls), Esc or Back returns. Changing the campaign or the difficulty reloads and comes back to the options. Everything is saved in settings.yaml (Settings). Credits The campaign's credits roll, then the engine's (Esc or Enter ends it); interceptor plays the CD's credits film instead. Quit Leaves the game.

Leaving the strategy map (Esc), the end of a film or cutscene, the ending screen's Main menu, leaving the controls screen (since app 0.16.14, also when it was opened from the launcher) and Esc in the launcher all come back to the menu.

docs.title: The testbed launcher
docs.text: The launcher (Battles & tools, or the first screen of a campaign without a strategy layer) lists the model viewer, the asset browser and the test scenarios from every loaded pack: Up/Down to choose, Left/Right to pick a ship, Enter to start, Esc to return to the main menu (or to quit, for a campaign without one). In flight, Esc opens the menu (R restart, L back to the launcher) and ? lists every key (Controls). Default controls follow the original game; see the controls reference. Flight is newtonian by default: throttle is thrust and the ship coasts; Z reverses thrust, hold B to brake, M holds the target's speed. New to space sims? Press P in the launcher for Simple physics: the craft always flies where its nose points, with no drift (Controls › Simple physics).

docs.title: The condition console
docs.text: In any mission battle — from the launcher, the simulator, --mission or a campaign — the backquote key (`) opens the condition console along the bottom of the screen (app 0.16.5): type a condition or expression in the battle context — count(raiders), alive(colony) and time > 30s, hull(colony) — and its value shows beneath as you type (= 3, = true), or the error in orange (an unknown role, a typo). The battle is paused while the console is open; Esc or ` closes it and the battle carries on. Looking never changes the battle: even random(p) is evaluated on a copy of the battle's dice. Role names are the mission's own; difficulty level names work as in mission files. A scenario (not a mission) has no conditions: the console says no mission: conditions belong to missions.

docs.title: After a battle: the debrief
docs.text: When a mission's result is decided, the verdict appears at once — MISSION ACCOMPLISHED, MISSION FAILED, YOUR CRAFT WAS DESTROYED or MISSION ENDED — and the computer voice speaks, but the battle keeps running so you can watch it end: the last explosion, your wingmen forming up. A countdown, Debrief in 30 s (Enter: now), shows when the debrief will appear; Enter shows it at once (app 0.7.4). Leaving the battle from the pause menu (a retreat) shows the debrief at once. A campaign sets the wait with flight.debrief_delay (Mod file reference).

docs.title: Documentation site
docs.text:
From the docs worktree (engine-docs/ in the main checkout):

./docs.sh serve     # live preview on http://127.0.0.1:8000
./docs.sh build     # strict build
./docs.sh deploy    # publish to the pages branch (needs a remote)

docs.title: Next
docs.text:
• New to Rust? Start at Learn Rust with this codebase.
  • Want to make a mod? Start at Modding.
  • Want to work on the engine? Read Architecture and Best practices, then run scripts/check.sh.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text: OpenInterceptor keeps the player's choices in settings.yaml in the user data folder. The launcher writes the campaign and difficulty you choose; everything else you can edit by hand while the game is not running. Unknown keys are ignored, and a key left out (or left empty) means the default.

docs.title: Where the files are
docs.text:
Platform User data folder macOS ~/Library/Application Support/OpenInterceptor/ Linux $XDG_DATA_HOME/openinterceptor/ (default ~/.local/share/openinterceptor/)

It holds settings.yaml, bindings.yaml (your keys, see Controls), mods/ (your mods) and optionally original/ (a copy of your original data: an installed copy or the CD).

docs.title: settings.yaml
docs.text:
paths:
  original: /Users/me/Games/XCOM Interceptor
  mods:
packs:
  disabled: [hd-cockpit-test]
game:
  campaign: default
  difficulty: ranger
  language: en
  physics: simple       # or realistic
graphics:
  brightness: 1.2
  fullscreen: false
console:
  enabled: true
  port: 8765
audio:
  music: 70%
  effects: 100%
Key Default Meaning paths.original found automatically Your original data (optional): an installed Interceptor or the CD. --data and the OPENINTERCEPTOR_DATA variable take precedence; without any, the engine looks in original/ in the user data folder, then in a development checkout's resources/xcom/ (installed copy) and resources/xcom-cd/ (CD copy) (Folder layout). paths.mods mods/ in the user data folder Folder of your mods (--mods overrides it). packs.disabled none Pack ids to switch off without deleting them. game.campaign the last chosen, else interceptor if its data is found, else default The campaign to load; the launcher's Tab writes it, --campaign overrides it for one run. game.difficulty the campaign's default level A difficulty level of game.campaign (the launcher's D writes it, --difficulty overrides it). Ignored when another campaign is loaded. game.language en The text language: the packs' text/<language>/ folders (--language overrides it). game.physics realistic simple: the player's craft always flies where its nose points, with no drift, like a traditional space fighter game. Used only on a campaign's first three difficulty levels; higher levels always fly realistic. The launcher's P key switches it (R-FLT-013). graphics.brightness 1 The picture's brightness: 1 is as authored, from 0.5 (darker) to 2 (brighter); values outside are clamped. It lifts dark tones more than bright ones (a gamma), so ships in shadow become easier to see without washing out lit faces. The HUD and cockpit art are not changed. Read when the game starts. graphics.fullscreen false Start full screen (app 0.16.14). The main menu's Options › Full screen switches it at once and writes it here; --fullscreen starts full screen for one run whatever it says, and --windowed starts in a window. console.enabled false Serve the tablet control console (--console turns it on for one run). console.port 8765 The console's port; change it if another program uses 8765 (--console-port overrides it). audio.music 70% The music volume, 0% to 100% (app 0.12.1): battle and strategy-screen music and its stingers. The launcher's M key steps it. audio.effects 100% The volume of every other sound, 0% to 100%: weapons, explosions, voices, the computer voice and cutscene sounds (app 0.12.1), and since app 0.14.1 films' soundtracks. The launcher's V key steps it.

docs.title: Other ways to set them
docs.text:
• The command line overrides paths, game.campaign, game.difficulty, game.language, graphics.fullscreen (--windowed, --fullscreen) and console for one run (Getting started).
  • How bright ships are in a campaign is also the campaign's choice: a modder sets the lighting with flight: {lighting: …} (Mod file reference). graphics.brightness adjusts the result for your screen.

docs.title: Options in the main menu
docs.text: Since app 0.14.0 the main menu's Options page sets the campaign, difficulty, physics and the music and effects volumes with Left/Right (volumes by a quarter, stopping at 0 % and 100 %) and saves them here at once (Getting started › The main menu). Since app 0.16.14 it also has Full screen (On/Off with Left, Right or Enter: the window changes at once and graphics.fullscreen is saved) and Controls..., which opens the controls screen (Controls › Rebinding) and returns to the main menu.

docs.title: Volumes in the launcher
docs.text:
The launcher's line of packs ends with Music 70% (M) Effects 100% (V). M steps the music volume and V the effects volume up by a quarter — 0, 25, 50, 75, 100 % — and from 100 % back to 0 (a value in between, such as the default 70 %, goes up past the nearest quarter: 70 % → 100 %). Each press is saved in settings.yaml at once and takes effect immediately.

Brightness and the console are still set in this file; the controls have their own menu in flight, in the launcher and (since app 0.16.14) in the main menu's options.

docs.title: Simulator
docs.text: The simulator flies any mission of the loaded campaign the way you set it up: in another place, with hazards added, against a smaller or larger enemy force. It is for practice and for trying things out; nothing you do in it counts towards a campaign. (App 0.6.3; requirement R-MSN-010.)

docs.title: Opening it
docs.text: In the launcher, choose Simulator (set up a mission and fly it) — the entry after Controls. The difficulty level is the launcher's: press D there first to change it.

docs.title: Setting up
docs.text:
Row Choices What it does Mission every mission of the campaign The battle to fly. Its briefing is shown under the rows. Ship the ships you can fly Your craft. A mission that fixes your craft shows "(the mission's own)". Environment the mission's own (or open space), then every environment of the campaign Where the battle happens: open space, orbit, a pocket, a planet surface … Asteroids off / on Adds an asteroid field ahead of you. Minefield off / on Adds a minefield ahead of you. Black hole off / on Adds a black hole some 9 km ahead: its pull grows as you near it, and its core destroys what crosses it. Ion storm off / on Cuts your radar range to 40 % and slows missile locks. Enemy force ×0.5, ×1, ×1.5, ×2 Scales every group of enemies and every enemy reinforcement (never below one craft). Your wingmen and what you defend are unchanged. Fly — Starts the battle.

Keys: Up/Down choose a row, Left/Right change it, Enter flies, Esc returns to the launcher.

  • A campaign that has no asteroids or no mines shows "(none in this campaign)" on that row.
  • Some ships cannot fly in an atmosphere. If you choose one with a planet-surface environment, Fly shows "The … cannot enter an atmosphere: choose another ship or environment." and nothing starts.
  • With the mission's own environment, no hazards and ×1, the battle is exactly the mission as the launcher would start it.

docs.title: After the battle
docs.text: The debrief appears as in any mission. Enter (pad A) flies the same setup again — the same mission, ship, environment, hazards and force; Esc or L returns to the launcher. R in the pause menu also restarts the same setup.

docs.title: Ideas
docs.text:
• Fly defend_station on moon_surface to feel how the same fight changes in thin air and low gravity.
  • Add a black hole to intercept_scouts and use its pull to catch the scouts.
  • Try a hard mission at ×0.5 to learn it, then at ×2 once you know it.
